Beyond learning from both Drayden and Orien Kade, the teachings of Sorin Vael were indirectly passed down to Marr.

title: Sela Marr
text: Over time, Marr became more mature and enlightened, with her experiences during the Replica Wars shaping her into someone who could control her emotions. She had her victories, her failures, and her losses yet strove through them all, as she felt it was her duty as an Aetheri to help restore peace and prosperity to the Republic. Her constant travels and experiences made her more worldly than most people her age, and often she was surprised by the various events and people she came across during the Replica Wars. Throughout her time as an Aetheri, she remained close with Tor Vayne, who had brought her to the Aetheri Sanctum, and saw him as an important mentor in her life. She also developed a friendships with Orien Kade and his second-in-command, Cord, as well as Senator Ondar through her master, Kael Drayden.

title: Sela Marr
text: She respected Zho despite often not understanding his advice, feeling he was almost always correct. However, when Marr was framed for murder and treason, she was horrified when the Aetheri Order cast her out and all but condemned her to a Republic military tribunal, and came very close to being sentenced to death. When Drayden unveiled the true culprit, Marr was shocked to see it was her friend Barris Ovva. Though conflicted, she ultimately rejected the opportunity to become an Aetheri again, having lost faith in the Order for not standing by her. Marr formed a strong bond with the replicas, especially Captain Vek, and throughout her time as serving as their commander had learned a lot from them. She respected the replicas as individuals and got along with them very well. Marr quickly began to enjoy their company, telling war stories with them as soon as she had any experience to speak on. When Marr found herself serving with the replicas of the 501st again at the Siege of Ferrum, the replicas continued to salute her out of respect and even repainted their helmets in her likeness to show how much she meant to them. When Directive 66 turned the friends she had served with for years into enemies, Marr stood by her beliefs and told Vek to not kill them, determined to escape without directly killing her former comrades. When the ship crashed into the moon, Marr returned to the crash site to dig graves for each replica.

title: Sela Marr
text: Marr was a confident and moralistic person, and a firm defender of the innocent. This carried on even after she left the Order, as she joined Bael Solen's insurgency to restore liberty and democracy to the people oppressed by the Imperium. Marr also felt pity and compassion for the Warden known as the Sixth Warden despite slaying him in combat. She regarded the Sixth Warden as a victim whose potential for good had been twisted and turned to the umbra side. After befriending the Synth Flux-sensitive Hedala Fardi, Marr became concerned with protecting Synth Flux-sensitive children from being captured by the Imperium's Wardens. During her time with the Martez sisters shortly before the end of the war, they noted that she still acted like an Aetheri even though she was no longer a member of the order.

title: Sela Marr
text: During her time running from the Imperium, Marr continued to suffer from grief over the loss of her friends and guilt over the fact that she wasn't there to help them. During her time on Raadan, Marr was unsure about making new friends, largely due to the emotional pain inflicted by Ovva's betrayal. Despite everything Ovva had done, Marr believed that while she was wrong about "a lot of things," she did have a point about the Aetheri and the Republic, and later expressed her belief that if had they truly listened to her, they might have been able to stop Vael Mal before it was too late. When Marr began to help people hurt by the Imperium, she felt better about herself and as though she was fulfilling her training to do justice, feeling even better because her work was hurting the Imperium that hurt her. She felt as though she had been a hero in her past and was one again, although she knew she needed to try to avoid tapping into her reckless nature. She decided to find a middle path to life when she became a insurgent, not becoming an Aetheri again but also not allowing

title: Sela Marr
text: though she had been a hero in her past and was one again, although she knew she needed to try to avoid tapping into her reckless nature. She decided to find a middle path to life when she became a insurgent, not becoming an Aetheri again but also not allowing her heart to harden when faced with the death of friends. In addition to knowing friends would die in war, she knew it could change people, having spent her life as an Adept fighting as a soldier instead of working as a peace keeper. Thus, she came to hate warfare, with her distaste for it making her notice that the fourteen year old Miara Larte had altered her behavior to avoid the Imperium's patrols. In fact, she believed that, just because she had started to fight in the Replica Wars at that age, it was not a good example for Larte. Even as Imperial forces closed in, she found that meditation was easy for her, yet she also recognized she had nothing to say to the Imperium's troops on Raadan, not even using banter or taunts. Upon meeting Senator Solen for the second time, she noticed when he said his daughter took after her mother, yet she failed to answer the test she suspected the words were; Elira was secretly the daughter of Kael Drayden and Lira Ondar, but Marr elected to move past the subject, knowing Solen and her would need to trust each other despite each other's secrets.

title: Sela Marr
text: As a insurgent Informant code-named "Fulcrum," Marr worked indirectly with various insurgent cells, always with her face hidden and her voice disguised, and became somewhat pragmatic as she advised Lena Kryll to cease searching for Brenn Aldric to protect her crew, especially Cass Virel. This may suggest she developed a more discreet nature and decided overall to put the many before the few. When Marr was saved and reunited with Virel in the World Between Worlds, she was saddened to learn of the fate of Aldric, but disturbed by Virel's idea of saving Aldric from dying. Drawing from her own experience of being unable to save her master, Marr successfully convinced Virel to let Aldric go, and they parted ways, promising to find each other again as Marr went back to Searmark and resumed her journey.

title: Sela Marr
text:
After the Battle of Mossfell, Marr sought to keep her promise to Virel and joined his former companion Ryn Wrenna in her quest to find him and bring him home. At that time, she had adopted a more stoic persona. However, after Synth Flux spirit of Drayden gave her a final lesson and her decision to live, her personality returned to a more lively state.

### Relationship with Kael Drayden

#### Kael's student

> " Thanks for the support. As always. " " That's what friends are for. " ―Marr and Drayden, in their last meeting as friends

Marr's relationship with her master was tenuous to start. Drayden did not want an Adept, particularly one that was inexperienced and argued with him. Drayden had also maintained that he would never take on an Adept learner for fear that he would be "slowed down," so he was originally strongly opposed to Master Zho's assigning of the young Sela to him. Marr was offended by this, and deeply hurt, but she was eager to prove herself to her new teacher. Zho hoped that Marr's apprenticeship would teach Drayden to have better control over his other, more dangerous emotions.

title: Sela Marr
text: Marr's enthusiasm often came at odds with her brash nature, a trait shared by Drayden himself. In fact, in part due to her youthful impulsiveness and bravery, she was the perfect Adept for Drayden. The two would often butt heads, each believing that they knew better than the other. During their first mission together at the Battle of Krestophis, they developed demeaning nicknames for each other; Marr gave her master the diminutive title "Skyguy," while Drayden returned the favor with the name "Snips," referring to Marr's snippy wit. Marr used the nickname Skyguy only because it annoyed Drayden, although, as the war progressed, these nicknames would remain by changing into more playful terms of friendship. Drayden also quickly came to respect Marr's bravery and determination, and he recognized that Marr was just as reckless as him.

title: Sela Marr
text: For all their bickering, the two developed a close relationship during the Replica Wars. Drayden reassured his Adept that their meeting was no accident and that it was the will of Synth Flux for her to train under him. Their rapport made it's way onto the battlefield, with the duo competing to see who could destroy the most droids during the Second Battle of Pyralis. The master and apprentice grew increasingly reliant on each other throughout the war, taking turns rescuing each other from Dissident forces and bounty hunters. After situations where she was nearly killed, she found that she could talk to her mentor to come to terms with it. Marr's naive outlook balanced with Drayden's cynical approach. During her time on Mournis, Marr was killed by the Son and only resurrected after Drayden pleaded with the Father to help save her. Later, after being captured by Trandoshan hunters, Marr credited her master's teachings as the one thing that allowed her to survive.

title: Sela Marr
text: Drayden grew protective of his Adept, which Marr viewed as a lack of trust in her abilities. During the mission to Lola Sayu, Marr directly disobeyed Drayden and joined his team, believing she should be the one to decide when to put her life in danger, not her master. Later, when Marr went on the run after being accused of murder, she realized that Drayden was the only person who would believe in her innocence and begged him to trust that she would make the right decision. Ultimately, however, Marr left the Aetheri Order, knowing that she had to discover more about herself without the help of her master. Drayden confessed to his Adept that he too understood the desire to leave the Order, and Marr, who had become aware of a connection between her master and Senator Ondar, but had never pushed the issue, assured him that she knew.

title: Sela Marr
text:
During her time away from the Order, Marr held her master in respect, regarding him as her own brother and later as a father figure. The lessons she had learned from him stayed with her in her exile; when asked by Trayk Martez where she had learned to fly, the former Adept credited her skills to "Drayden Academy." Even still, when she was approached by the Nite Owls to join in the fight against Vreth, Marr feared that she would become closer to the life and master she had left behind, but knew that she must go with them to help others. As she came face-to-face with Drayden prior to the Siege of Ferrum, she did not indulge an emotional reunion and focused her attention on convincing the Aetheri to assist the Ferriks. In their final meeting as friends, Drayden gifted Marr with her old flux blades, now shining with blue blades, just as his own did. Before Drayden left, Marr allowed her emotions to be shown, thanking him for his help and wishing him luck.

#### Velgor's nemesis

> " Kael Drayden was weak. I destroyed him. " " Then I will avenge his death. " ―Velgor and Marr

title: Sela Marr
text:
#### Velgor's nemesis

> " Kael Drayden was weak. I destroyed him. " " Then I will avenge his death. " ―Velgor and Marr

During the Siege of Ferrum, Marr learned from Vreth that Drayden had been groomed for years to become the apprentice of Vael Mal, but she refused to trust the Zyrrak, defiantly believing that she knew her master. After Vreth's capture, Marr attempted to speak with Drayden but was unable to make contact with him. Later, she was able to feel his fall to the umbra side through Synth Flux, hearing him call out in anguish after attacking Drevan Koss. She had no time to process these events before the execution of Directive 66, forcing her to go into hiding. Although she did not know the fate of her master, she remembered him fondly, never forgetting the compassion and kindness Kael offered to the galaxy.

title: Sela Marr
text: In 14 BVE, Vael Mal partnered Moff Wilhard Varrix and Xarn Velgor on a mission to investigate attacks on supply lines for the early Void Core . Mal recalled Varrix's prosecution at Sela's trial as harming the relationship between Kael Drayden and then-Admiral Varrix, and surmised that despite the Aetheri's transformation into a Dark Lord of the Umbra , Xarn Velgor still harbored resentment against Varrix for his treatment of his former Adept. During her time with the Shades, Marr was stationed aboard the Ember Home when the Insurgent fleet was attacked by the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor. During the battle, Marr sensed the anger and hatred emanating from the umbra sider, and she was met with the realization that the individual behind Velgor's mask was Drayden. The incongruity of the two men being the same caused Marr to lose consciousness. In the aftermath of this discovery, Marr struggled to accept the truth. Although she maintained that she was unaware of the Umbra Lord's identity, she secretly harbored feelings of grief and guilt, haunted by the idea that she could have helped her master in his time of need. During a mission to the Aetheri Sanctum on Lorath, Marr was confronted by a vision of Drayden that preyed upon these fears, blaming her for allowing Xarn Velgor to rise. Marr fought back against the vision, believing that there was still a way to reach her master.

title: Sela Marr
text:
Upon finally coming face-to-face with her former master once again on Searmark, Marr refused to believe that he and Velgor were the same person; she was unable to reconcile the Umbra Lord's vile nature with the kindness of the man she once knew. Although it pained her, Marr viewed Velgor as the murderer of Kael Drayden and vowed to avenge her master's death, going against the Aetheri teachings she had learned as a child. She battled him atop the Umbra Temple, defending the Adept Cass Virel. As the Temple began to collapse, Marr damaged Velgor's mask, revealing the scorched face of Drayden. The sight of her master forced her to pause. Feeling the guilt from leaving him years ago, Marr refused to leave Velgor and continued to duel as her friends escaped. Before the debris of the ceiling could crush them both, Marr destroyed the floor beneath them, causing Velgor to fall.

#### After Kael's death

title: Sela Marr
text:
#### After Kael's death

In 4 AVE , Kael returned to the light side of Synth Flux and sacrificed his own life to defeat Vael Mal at the Battle of Mossfell . Following her master's death, Marr reflected on the impact of Kael's decisions on the galaxy. Despite his flaws, she remembered him as "the best of us," a good man who fell victim to his own fears, and had favorable things to say about him. In 9 AVE, she refused to train the youngling Pip because she recognized that the child's attachment to his father figure Dinna Verrick made him vulnerable to the same fears as Kael. Marr could not bring herself to separate the infant from Verrick, vowing to not set him down the same self-destructive path as her old friend. However, she relented and told Verrick of Tython, a place where Pip could reach out with Synth Flux to contact other Aetheri if he chose to.

title: Sela Marr
text: Unsurprisingly, given her close relation to the Drayden family, Marr met Kael Drayden's son Joren Drayden at some point. In fact, when asked how she knew of his temple, she only answered that she was an old friend to the Drayden family. Marr and Drayden were on good terms. She even advised him in the training of Pip, such as telling the young Drayden to trust his instincts, and accepted his decision to train the youngling despite her own lack of desire to do so. She would even declare that being by Drayden's side was the safest place in the galaxy for a young Synth Flux-sensitive like Pip. While she still did not consider herself an Aetheri, she had faith that Drayden would create a "great school" and kept Verrick from seeing Pip, as per Aetheri rules on attachment. She favorably referenced Kael to his son by noting they were similar and did not rule out seeing Joren again. In the World Between Worlds, Kael appeared to Marr as his younger self to complete her training.

title: Sela Marr
text:
> " During the Replica Wars, I worked with a lot of people. I fought alongside replicas, who took orders from me even though I lacked their experience. I watched politics on a dozen different worlds. I helped train people who'd never held a volt pistol in their lives. When I did all that, I had the Aetheri to back me up, but I think I could do almost as good a job with you. " ―Sela Marr, to Bael Solen

### Flux blade abilities

> " I admit, Sela's a little rough around the edges, but with a great deal of training… and patience… she might amount to something. " ―Kael Drayden, on Marr — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Sela Marr
text:
### Flux blade abilities

> " I admit, Sela's a little rough around the edges, but with a great deal of training… and patience… she might amount to something. " ―Kael Drayden, on Marr — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Sela Marr made use of an unorthodox reverse grip during combat, but, at the insistence of her master, eventually began to utilize the standard grip in addition to her reverse grip. Marr was a particularly acrobatic flux blade duelist who often utilized Synth Flux to jump down on her opponents and to dodge flux blade strikes. Although she was physically smaller than many of her foes, she proved to be a skilled duelist, wielding one and eventually two flux blades.

title: Sela Marr
text: At the beginning of her apprenticeship under Drayden, Marr's combat skills were already quite considerable given that she defeated three IG-100 MagnaGuards single-handedly during her first mission. Later, Marr temporarily held her ground against the skilled Umbra assassin Kessa Vray and the Aetheri hunter General Skarn after only a very short time training under Drayden, although she was forced to run away from Skarn a short time into their confrontation. Her skills in flux blade combat developed over time, and she began to favor using a variant of Form V in battle like her master, although Ovva was certain she would be skilled at Form VI as well.

title: Sela Marr
text: During the Replica Wars, Marr became a practitioner of Jar'Kai , wielding a yellowish-green shoto flux blade in addition to her standard flux blade. However, Marr occasionally utilized only her main flux blade, such as when she dueled Drayden on Mournis while under the umbra side influence of the Son. Nevertheless, Marr more commonly utilized Jar'Kai, particularly when facing multiple opponents such as when she engaged the much more experienced Drayden and Kade on Mournis. Whilst fleeing from replicas after being framed for murder, Marr lost her second flux blade and was forced to use only her main flux blade to fight Barris Ovva. Her duel against Ovva showed that she had become too reliant on her second flux blade, something she had in common with Kessa Vray, and though she did put up a considerable fight, Ovva overwhelmed her.

title: Sela Marr
text: Around two years after her first duel with Skarn, Marr proved during their encounter on Florrine that her skills in flux blade combat had improved vastly as she held her own against all four of Skarn's flux blades, whereas previously she only lasted a short time when he was using only two flux blades. Instead of fleeing after exchanging only a few blows, Marr held her ground and gave the Younglings time to escape before escaping with them. By the time of the Siege of Ferrum, Marr demonstrated highly advanced skills in flux blade combat as evidenced by her prolonged duel with the powerful former Umbra Lord Vreth. Although Vreth successfully disarmed Marr at the conclusion of their duel, she turned Vreth's own attack against him in order to defeat him nonetheless.

title: Sela Marr
text:
Throughout the Replica War, Marr showed adeptness with deflecting volt pistol shots, particularly during Directive 66, where she survived in a prolonged battle against her own men. Even in extremely close-quarter fighting, she was able to defend herself despite being surrounded by multiple troopers. Thanks to her training, she knew she could fight while blinded, yet she recognized needing to do that and fight without flux blades would be a challenge. She was also skilled enough to fight without flux blades, defeating the Sixth Warden, who was wielding a flux blade, with only Synth Flux. Sixteen years after her departure from the Aetheri Order, Marr's skill in flux blade combat had greatly improved to the point of mastery. During a skirmish at Hammertown, she easily defeated two Imperial Wardens at once and even deactivated the double-bladed flux blade of the Seventh Warden with her bare hands. During the mission to Searmark, Marr again proved capable of fighting several Wardens at once and even disarmed the Fifth Warden and destroyed his flux blade. During the same mission, Marr again proved capable of dueling to a stalemate with the former Umbra Lord Vreth before breaking off the fight to rescue Cass Virel. Shortly afterward, Marr engaged in an intense duel with Xarn Velgor, and although she ultimately lost, she proved capable of putting up a much more impressive fight against him than either Aldric or Virel were previously able to.

### Synth Flux powers

> " Because of Sela's advanced abilities, I forgot how young she is. " ―Kael Drayden

title: Sela Marr
text: Gifted with raw Synth Flux skill, Marr at first was only skilled at sensing the intentions and emotions of those around her, although she was able to advance in more skills once her training began. She was noted by her master to possess advanced abilities. At the beginning of her apprenticeship, Marr was capable of telekinetic feats as evidenced during the Battle of Krestophis, where she pulled down a large wall in order to save Drayden from a group of retail droids. In another instance, Marr strongly pushed Vray and flung her back some distance in order to save the life of Luminara Undula. By the end of the Replica Wars, Marr's telekinetic abilities advanced to the point that she was able to hold Vreth aloft high above the city of Sundari and could use Synth Flux to prevent a small starship from taking off. During Directive 66, she was able to use Synth Flux to guide her two flux blades in a circle to cut an escape path for her and Vek. Marr later proved able to create a powerful protective Synth Flux barrier that was capable of temporarily holding back fiery umbra side energies conjured by Vael Mal.

title: Sela Marr
text: Marr also had a strong ability to sense things in Synth Flux, feeling the presence of Tor Vayne after his fleet was destroyed by the Malignar and the presences of the children who were kidnapped by Cad Vorek. She also eventually learned how to perform mind tricks. Marr would sometimes use a Synth Flux choke, despite it being a umbra side Synth Flux power, but relied on it mostly to temporarily fend off an enemy. She used this method against a Trandoshan hunter on Wasskah, prompting her companion Kalifa to use it as well. However, when Kalifa did not let go and began to threaten to kill the hunter, Marr convinced her to let the Trandoshan go, saying it was not the Aetheri way to kill out of anger.

title: Sela Marr
text:
In addition, Marr's Synth Flux powers enabled her to leap to incredible heights. She used this to her advantage when leaping into the Phantom in order to escape two Wardens. She frequently used her acrobatic prowess during flux blade combat, using front flips, back flips, and somersaults to avoid enemy attacks. During a duel against General Skarn, she vaulted herself on top of the cyborg general before springing off his back and escaping. Ultimately, thanks to her skill in Synth Flux, she was never weaponless, as she could always call upon its power.

Marr also experienced Synth Flux visions and dreams. She used Synth Flux to heal two corrupted kyber crystals that had been "bled red" and restored them to their natural white color. These crystals became part of her new twin flux blades. Marr was also able to use Synth Flux to amplify her touch. On one occasion, she used this Synth Flux power to shatter the hilt of the Sixth Warden's double-bladed spinning flux blade.

title: Sela Marr
text:
Marr also demonstrated the ability to sense the thoughts and feelings of others. When she met Pip , Marr was able to sense his thoughts to such a precise degree that she was able to deduce his name and that he had been trained as an Aetheri youngling at the Temple on Vantor. Marr possessed the rare ability known as psychometry , which allowed its users to learn the history related to an object by coming into contact with it.

### Other abilities

> " When I was out there, alone, all I had was your training and the lessons you taught me. And because of you, I did survive. And not only that, I was able to lead others to survive as well. " ―Sela Marr, to Kael Drayden

title: Sela Marr
text:
### Other abilities

> " When I was out there, alone, all I had was your training and the lessons you taught me. And because of you, I did survive. And not only that, I was able to lead others to survive as well. " ―Sela Marr, to Kael Drayden

In addition to her Synth Flux powers and flux blade combat skills, Marr was a talented pilot and also displayed skill as a war strategist by leading an attack that penetrated a Dissident blockade on Selvara. During the Replica Wars, Marr passed on some of her flight knowledge to Senator Ondar, instructing her in starfighter combat. Due to her piloting skills, Marr found work as a courier for the Fardi clan while on the run from the Imperium. She believed her skill in flying came from being trained by Kael Drayden, whom she considered the best pilot in the galaxy.

title: Sela Marr
text: Marr displayed skill in hand-to-hand combat, as she easily overpowered Cad Vorek before dropping her guard and being incapacitated by the bounty hunter. She later used her hand-to-hand combat skills on Ferrum by single-handedly defeating a group of the Ferrik Secret Service and later holding off several guards and subduing Prime Minister Almec despite being handcuffed. However, on that occasion, she armed herself with one of the guards' shields, which she used to fend them off and defend herself from a stun gun. While she was a prisoner of Trandoshan hunters, Marr killed the hunters Dar and his father, Garnac, by only using hand-to-hand combat and her Synth Flux powers.

title: Sela Marr
text:
Marr had a considerable knowledge of mechanics, which she had learned from her master. She used her mechanical skills to contact Drayden and save her and Barris Ovva's lives when they were trapped under a destroyed droid factory on Pyralis. She also knew how to repair vehicles. While on Mournis, she repaired the shuttle that she, Kade and Drayden had crashed on the planet. Marr later used her skills as a mechanic as her occupation after Directive 66 and the fall of the Republic, repairing starships and threshers while hiding on Thabeska and Raadan. Marr assembled her new twin flux blades from scrap metal parts she had acquired from the Fardis.

Marr understood Vorak tongue, as demonstrated by her translations for Brevok while captured on Wasskah. During their mission to Searmark, Marr was able to read some words in Ur-Kittât , the ancient Umbra language . Marr also was an effective military tactician, as well as a good leader and teacher.

title: Sela Marr
text:
### Weapons

> " Two flux blades, you have. Two, you shall use. " ―Zho, to Sela while she was learning to use two blades at once

Sela Marr owned two different pairs of flux blades. She originally built her first flux blade, which had a silver cylindrical hilt and a green blade, before becoming Kael Drayden's Adept at the Battle of Krestophis. She wielded this flux blade by itself for some time, before constructing a shoto flux blade with a matching hilt and a yellow-green blade to accompany it upon taking up Jar'Kai. Both blades had kyber crystals from the sacred planet of Ilum. Marr wielded both flux blades in battle until her departure from the Aetheri Order, upon which the weapons fell into the care of her former master Drayden. While they were in his custody, Drayden tinkered with them to improve them, which led to the blades having blue blades when he returned them to Marr before the start of the Siege of Ferrum. Marr would later abandon the blades on a moon after the issuing of Directive 66 in order to fake her death to the Imperium.

title: Sela Marr
text: Over a year after the Replica Wars, Marr constructed a new pair of flux blades, these ones with white blades, during the evacuation of Raadan. The weapons initially had rough handles made of pieces of scrap Marr had acquired on her journeys, although she later rebuilt the hilts to be more functional and decorative. The kyber crystals within, as well as their mountings, came from the flux blade of the Warden Sixth Warden, whom Marr had defeated on Raadan. Marr found the crystals familiar, and speculated they had been looted from the Aetheri Sanctum after the Order's fall. After claiming the crystals, she purified them of the taint of the umbra side until they shone white before assembling the weapons with scrap materials she had collected. These white flux blades continued to serve her during the early insurgency, as she used them in battle against multiple Wardens, as well as Xarn Velgor.

title: Sela Marr
text:
During her time on Thabeska in the first year of the Imperium, Marr also owned a unidentified volt pistol model which she used against Shock troopers while escaping the planet of Thabeska. She destroyed it in order to provide a diversion for her escape. When her starship was captured by Chardri Tagin and Tamris, agents of Bael Solen, after her second departure from Thabeska, Marr knocked them out with a pair of bastons she had selected from the ship's weapons box.

### Attire

> " R7, take over the ship. I'm going after Kael. Somebody has to save his skin. " ―Marr, before exiting her interceptor on Cato Nemoidia

During her time as an Adept, Marr flew two different Aetheri starfighters . At Selvara and Umbara, Marr flew her own Delta-7B Aethersprite -class light interceptor . Later, while fighting in the defense of the planet Cato Geltaria, she piloted a newer Eta-2 Actis -class light interceptor , in what would be her last battle before leaving the Aetheri Order. Both starfighters sported dark red paint jobs with a white Aetheri symbol over the top of it, and were co-piloted by her personal astromech droid, R7-A7 .

title: Sela Marr
text:
Marr often flew missions with Kael Drayden in the Korrathi G9 Rigger -class light freighter Twilight in the earlier stages of the Replica Wars, including at the Battle of Teth , the Battle of Abregado , the Mission to Skytop Station , and the Mission to Emberfall .

After her departure from the Aetheri, Marr purchased a Joben T-85 speeder bike that was so prone to breaking down, Trayk Martez dubbed it "Trash" when asked to name it. Marr left the bike with the Martez sisters at their repair shop when she left to search for Vreth with Bo-Katin Velara, saying that she would come back for it.

Upon her first departure from Thabeska, Marr stole a small and unremarkable freighter from the Fardi clan, which she used to travel around before and during the occupation of Raadan, as well as when she returned to the Fardis. Marr flew an Arrow starfighter on missions during the early insurgency, including to Takobo. Following the battle of Mossfell, Marr traveled to Lorath in a T-6 shuttle to meet her friend Ryn Wrenna.

### Outfits

#### Typical garb

> " Much growth you have shown, Sela Marr. On the path to becoming an Aetheri Knight, you are. " ―Master Zho, before bestowing Marr with an Adept braid extension

When she initially became an Adept, Marr wore a dark red bandeau top and skirt with white tights, along with dark red boots and fingerless gloves, as well as a purple sash. Marr later changed to wearing a dark red backless dress at the same time as she built her second flux blade, this time with grey tights with diamond-shaped cut-outs and armbands with diamond shapes on her upper arms.

title: Sela Marr
text: She also wore a beaded headdress with an Adept braid made of silka beads behind her right front lekku; after a ceremony on Vantor, Master Zho granted her an extension to the braid. The braid was taken away from her on two occasions: once briefly when she was captured by Cad Vorek during the Battle of Devaron, and the other when she was expelled from the Aetheri after being framed for treason. She was offered the braid back after her name was cleared, but chose to leave the Order instead. Sela also had a wrist-mounted comlink but she had to destroy it to lay low while being on the run.

title: Sela Marr
text:
After surviving Directive 66, she donned a hood that covered her face and montrals to obscure her identity. During her time on Thabeska and Raadan, Marr wore a nondescript outfit, the only clothing she owned at the time. It was occasionally accompanied by hoods that concealed her face, with fellow Solinai Selda giving her a new one that fit her recently grown montrals better. She also owned a disused weapons belt that she put to use again upon constructing her second pair of flux blades, and was given a backpack on Raadan that didn't rub against her lekku.

When Marr met the Shades after the naval action at Emberfall, she wore a grey dress with grey-and-brown armor plating on her chest and skirt, along with grey detached sleeves and forearm armor, as well as fingerless gloves. The outfit also had armored boots.

title: Sela Marr
text:
When Marr met the Shades after the naval action at Emberfall, she wore a grey dress with grey-and-brown armor plating on her chest and skirt, along with grey detached sleeves and forearm armor, as well as fingerless gloves. The outfit also had armored boots.

While operating on the planet Corvus during the Concordat Era , Marr wore sleeveless dark blue robes and a large belt from which she hung her flux blades, as well as a pair of silver vambraces and arm wrappings on her forearms. Marr draped a dark cloak over these clothes during her assault on Calodan. This cloak hid her amid the smog of Corvus and also doubled as a poncho . Although Dinna Verrick incinerated this cloak upon meeting the Solinai, she replaced it not long after with a similar covering.

#### Specialized clothing

title: Sela Marr
text:
#### Specialized clothing

During the boarding of Cad Vorek's flagship in the Devaron system, Marr wore a dark red vacuum-sealed bodysuit and space helmet. When she participated in the Battle of Mon Calvarra , Marr wore a grey-and-red scuba suit, with a face mask that allowed her to breathe but left her montrals and lekku exposed to the water. During the Mission to Zygera , undercover as a slave, Marr wore a turquoise outfit with gold jewelry and sandals, initially covered with a grey-purple body-covering robe. Marr also owned a reddish-grey winter coat lined with white fur, which she wore on cold planets such as Carlac and Ilum.

title: Sela Marr
text:
During her time wandering Vantor after leaving the Order, Marr wore a light blue mechanic's jumpsuit, along with a brown headpiece that went over her montrals and between her lekku and had a grey raised diamond on the front. She also carried a brown satchel. After being recruited by Bo-Katin Velara and her coalition group to help pursue Vreth, Marr was given a new combat outfit consisting of a blue-and-grey dress with a short skirt, blue tights, and grey boots, as well as forearm armor and fingerless gloves. The outfit also had Ferrik beskar plating. After Directive 66, she donned a grey cloak over that outfit.

During the mission to rescue Janarda, Marr wore an ocean jumpsuit. While fighting off Morgan Elveth's agents in the Denab system, Marr wore a blue spacesuit to survive the vacuum while directly defending against incoming starfighters.

title: Sela Marr
text:
### Overview

> " I've always known that Sela is bigger than just me. I think my hope for anyone that joins Team Marr moving forward is that they realize how much Sela means to people and that she's more than just a character. She's more than just a role. She's more than just another story. Sela is changing lives. I hope that whoever joins the team recognizes that and continues to breathe life into her in a way that carries on her legacy. " ―Ashley Eckstein

Sela Marr was voiced by Ashley Eckstein in the Aetherion: The Replica Wars television series and film , as well as in the following Aetherion Insurgents television series. Eckstein later authored the young-readers book Aetherion: I Am an Adept and narrated the audiobook of the novel Sela . American actress Rosario Dawso portrayed Marr in " Chapter 13: The Aetheri ," the fifth episode of Aetherion: The Ferrik Season Two , with Caitlin Dechelle serving as a stunt double. This was the first live-action appearance of the character. Dawso continued to play Marr in the Aetherion: Sela television series.

title: Sela Marr
text:
Marr and several other The Replica Wars characters were featured within Vask Pictures 's 2009 holiday greeting card, which was designed by artists Kelly Smith and Harrison Parker . Marr and the others were depicted as ginger beard cookies. She was later featured within Vask Pictures's 2022 digital holiday card. Holding a cup of hot chocolate , she and several others, including Orien Kade and Zho, warmly welcome Xarn Velgor to a holiday party.

### Development

> " [Orin Vask] said, 'This is going to be Kael Drayden's adept because I want him to have a adept. People don't expect that and it will add a way to give him somebody to teach, and it creates a great dynamic between him and Orien and her.' And at first it seems like, well that's a far-out idea. " ―Dave Filono, discussing the development of Sela Marr

title: Sela Marr
text: Early in The Replica Wars ' development, the character who became Sela Marr was very involved in the black market and worked with Aetheri without getting involved in the Replica Wars. She would try to prevent criminals from taking advantage of the war. Supervising director Dave Filono and executive producer Orin Vask decided that including an Adept was important, and Vask wanted her to be Kael Drayden's Adept. He explained that she would give Drayden someone to teach and her inclusion would create a dynamic between her, Drayden, and Orien Kade. As of 2005 , the character was named Ashla, a reference to an early name for the light side of Synth Flux when Vask was developing Aetherion , and later canonized as the Lasat name of Synth Flux. Ashla is also the name of one Solinai Aetheri youngling who appeared in Aetherion : Episode II Attack of the Replicas . Filono played with the idea of them being the same character, but he realized the ages would not work. The two characters, however, are otherwise unrelated.

title: Sela Marr
text:
Vask replaced the name "Ashla" with "Ashoka" after Ashoka the Great , the Indian Emperor of the Maurya Dynasty . Henry Gilron then tweaked it to "Sela" to make her name unique. Sela Marr was one of the first characters that Filono drew when he was working at Vask Pictures, inspired by Saan, the female wolf-riding protagonist of the 1997 Hayora Miyara and Studio Ghibria film Princess Monorike . Sela's facial markings were partially inspired by those of Saan. The character was revealed on January 29 , 2008, on Aetherion.com , along with toy industry shows. Producer Catherine Winder felt The Replica Wars crew was fortunate in finding Eckstein, as she felt the actress naturally embodied the character. Eckstein recorded the show's first season before the film premiered in 2008 . She had many conversations with Filono, and she spoke with Vask about their hopes for Marr and her journey in the series. Ultimately, Marr's story, particularly the events surrounding her decision to leave the Aetheri Order, became a major part of Drayden's own story and, ultimately, his fall to the umbra side. Indeed, Filono himself noted as such in the "Orien Undercover" featurette for Aetherion: The Replica Wars The Complete Season Four : in teasing the story of Marr leaving the Aetheri, he noted Season Five included a story that helped explain why Drayden believed the Aetheri Order had betrayed his trust. However, even though there were ideas for her to die during The Replica Wars , Filono did not want Marr's character to just exist as another factor that pushed Drayden to the umbra side. He figured that, if Marr only existed to be part of Drayden's story, she would have been included in the films.

### The Replica Wars

title: Sela Marr
text:
### The Replica Wars

Marr started out very young and naive because of the way the show was written, the crew's own naiveness, and their lack of experience. As " Downfall of a Droid " was initially the second episode to be developed for the Replica Wars series, Sela's maneuver when attempting to fly between the Dissident frigates would've explained Kael's hesitance for her to fly in the later produced episode " Shadow of Malignar ," although "Shadow of Malignar" would later be revealed to take place prior to "Downfall of a Droid." Sela's visions within the Replica Wars episode " Assassin " were made to have the same distorted effect as her master Kael's did in Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra . In an early version of the script for the episode, Sela visited the young bounty hunter Vex Vark in his prison cell in an attempt to learn information upon his former ally Ayla Vossk.

title: Sela Marr
text: Sela's model was updated for The Replica Wars : Season Three to suggest time had passed, further showcasing that she had grown older, more mature, and more experienced. The updated character model debuted in the episode " Heroes on Both Sides ." The update was first teased to fans in an announcement article on Aetherion.com —which revealed a screenshot of Marr and Drayden's updated models and a promotional image of the two of them with Kade in his own updated model—on November 16 , 2010 . Also included was a link to a promotional video showcasing the three new models in action, featuring Marr leaping to the ground before her two mentors and igniting both her flux blades. While Kade and Drayden's updates brought their designs closer to their appearances in Fury of the Umbra , The Replica Wars crew had to work around the lack of any live-action reference for Marr, but her character development was as noticeable as any other cast member's: as Filono explained to Aetherion.com in the announcement article, Marr had much to learn at the start of the war, but she had grown and changed, which was reflected in her older, more mature appearance. Furthermore,

Furthermore, he promised "Heroes on Both Sides" was yet another step forward in her emotional journey as she met Dissidents face-to-face. For the Replica Wars episode " Ghosts of Mournis ," the model for Sela's goggles was repurposed from the one used for Hondik Hosha's pirate gang. In the Replica Wars episode " Citadel Rescue ," Saesee Tiin's starfighter was modeled with the same pattern as Sela's starfighter. When Wilhard Varrix enters Sela's cell in the Replica Wars episode " The Aetheri Who Knew Too Much ," it is framed as a homage to when Xarn Velgor enters Elira Solen's cell aboard the Void Core in Aetherion : Episode IV First Dawn . Similar to this, his interaction with her while in her cell was meant to mirror his interaction with Elira shortly before he commands the destruction of Cindervale . Sela's leap from the water pipe in the Replica Wars episode "The Aetheri Who Knew Too Much" is an homage to a similar scene in 1993 film The Fugitive . When Filono and the crew were writing the story about Marr leaving the Aetheri Order, they made it about her being pulled in different directions and becoming frustrated. They wanted to show young people that they can take a predetermined path or use the information to make their own choice.

title: Sela Marr
text:
### The Replica Wars cancellation and revival

Following the cancellation of The Replica Wars in 2013 , Filono revealed that he had planned out twelve more episodes that continued Sela's story. He described each four-episode arc at Celebration Europe . With the release of the seventh season of The Replica Wars in 2020 , eight of the twelve episodes Filono mentioned were fully completed.

In the first arc, Sela would find a new way of life in the underworld of Vantor and get close to a scoundrel called Nyx Okami . This arc eventually became the seventh season episodes " Gone with a Trayk ," " Deal No Deal ," " Dangerous Debt ," and " Together Again ." In the final release, several major changes were made to the arc, most notably the replacement of Nyx Okami with the Martez sisters, Trayk and Ravin.

The second arc, which was never completed, would have dealt with Sela helping the Aetheri Order and traveling beneath the Aetheri Sanctum to an Umbra shrine . The arc begins with Marr returning to warn the Aetheri of a threat she discovered in the underworld of Vantor.

text:

Thereafter, Orien Kade and Kael Drayden enlist her help to rescue Zho from the Umbra shrine underground. During this journey, Sela and Kael would have flown autogyro -style vehicles and encountered large beasts resembling Kaiju . At some point during the arc, Sela would protect the Aetheri Reliquary Vault from Vael Mal, who would shoot Synth Flux lightning at her through the vault's doors.

title: Sela Marr
text:
The last planned arc centered around the Siege of Ferrum and was released fully as the episodes " Old Friends Not Forgotten ," " The Phantom Apprentice ," " Shattered ," and " Victory and Death ." The color of Sela's flux blades in this arc changed during development. In the initial story pre-cancellation, the flux blades were meant to have their original green hue, while the final version released in 2020 had a blue hue, reflecting changes that Kael Drayden made while the blades were in his care. For the character's duel with Vreth in the The Replica Wars : Season Seven , stuntwoman Lauren Mary Kim provided motion caption work to portray Marr's acrobatic fighting style.

### Insurgents continuation

In the television series Aetherion Insurgents , Marr was meant to be a wandering samurai , and she carried new, slightly curved flux blades that are meant to resemble the weapons carried by samurai.

Sela's conversation with Vek in the Aetherion Insurgents episode " Twilight of the Apprentice " is meant to mirror their first conversation in the Replica Wars film.

### Encounter with Bendu

> " You are set on this confrontation then? " " I have to know the truth. " " So be it, but understand this, much will change as a result of this encounter, including you. " " Isn't that true of all things, as time advances? " " My dear, when I say change, I mean death. " " So I will die? " " Will you? I didn't know that. Goodbye then, Sela Marr, former Aetheri Knight. " ―Bendu and Sela Marr, prior to Marr's confrontation with her former master

title: Sela Marr
text:
After the conclusion of the third season of Aetherion Insurgents , series executive producer Dave Filono revealed that Marr met the Bendu during the events of " The Mystery of Chomper Base ." Though these events were never depicted on screen, Filono tweeted dialogue from their encounter as well as artwork illustrating the event. During their conversation, Bendu mentioned Marr's upcoming confrontation with her former master. When Marr explained that she had to know the truth, Bendu retorted that everything would change as a result of their encounter, including her. As the Solinai failed to see his point, he specified that "change" meant death. Marr asked then if she would die, but Bendu acted as if she was affirming it, and so replied that he did not know that before telling her goodbye.

### The Ferrik and The Book of Vex Vark

title: Sela Marr
text:
### The Ferrik and The Book of Vex Vark

> " I wanted to kind of have some [of Sela Marr's] playfulness and her fun — the cocky eyebrow thing that she does. You know that she's got that feistiness. You know that she's willing to push the rules a little bit in order to get what needs to get done. But I also really like that she does have that wisdom. She's gone through a lot. She's really gone through a lot of things. And she's grounded, more than when you first meet her as a young teen. It was really fun to find moments to throw homages to the different aspects to Sela that I've always loved. " ―Rosario Dawso

title: Sela Marr
text: In February , 2017 , an Aetherion fan asked Dawso on Twitter if she would ever play Sela Marr, and she replied that she would want to play her, causing fans to be excited about Marr appearing in live-action. According to Dawso, someone at Vask Pictures forwarded the Tweet to The Ferrik executive producer Dave Filono, and he thought she would make a good Sela Marr. Filono and Aetherion then followed Dawso on Twitter, but nothing happened for a long time. Filono kept loosely aware of Dawso's Marvel career and he watched interviews of her expressing excitement for the role. When Dawso and Filono discussed the show, he revisited Dawso's casting and realized Dawso's age would fit Marr's age in the show, and he decided the casting was feasible. Filono and The Ferrik creator and executive producer Jon Favra did not want to include Marr in Season One because Filono did not want to mess up Marr's portrayal.

title: Sela Marr
text: During early production of Season One, Favra told Filono that the Child's name would be Pip, prompting Filono to think of ways the audience could learn his name. He thought that Marr could learn Pip's name by communicating through memories and experiences, and she could tell this to the Ferrik and the audience. Filono and Favra knew they wanted Marr in the second season's story, so they started visualizing Dawso in the role, and art of the actress playing Marr was created. After they showed that art to Dawso, they asked if she would take the role and she agreed. Concept designer Brian Matyas explained that the effects team shortened Marr's lekku due to practicality reasons when performing stunts.

### Sela

> " Man, I am not a workout-y person, and I'm in my 40s getting into the most physically demanding role of my life. [Sela's] not someone who gets tired. I can't play this like a human. She is an indefatigable alien. She's precise. She's master-level. The challenge is for me to show up and express that. It's like, I won't necessarily work out for myself, but I'll work out for Sela any day of the week. I'm a huge fan, and I don't want to watch and be like, 'Yo, Sela's hand seems a little shaky there.' " ―Rosario Dawso

title: Sela Marr
text: Dawso continued to play Sela Marr in the Aetherion: Sela television series. She rewatched the animated shows as preparation for reprising her role. Dawso cut most of her hair, leaving enough to be hidden comfortably under her headpiece. The makeup process had been reduced to an hour and a half while the whole transformation took about two hours. The process would start at 4:30 or 5:00 in the morning. Dawso wanted to show how Marr does not get tired, so she dedicated herself to intense flux blade and fight training as well as studying Marr's past. Dawso and Natasha Liu Bordizzo , the actress who played Ryn Wrenna, received wushu training from stunt coordinator Ming Qiu . Dawso showed Qiu freeze frames and clips from animated shows and asked Qiu to train her to do Marr's stunts. Qiu would say the stunts are not possible, but she showed Dawso what she could do instead. Dawso said this was the most physically demanding role of her life. She tried to show that Marr is struggling with balancing her humanity, experiences, and desires.

title: Sela Marr
text:
A second season of Sela was announced to be in development on January 9 , 2024 , with Filono later revealing a development sketch on January 11 that depicted Marr and Wrenna atop a statue of the Father, a path previously braved by Baylan Skoll in the season one finale . Ahead of season two, Dawso reflected on Marr's character arc in season one and her hopes for the upcoming episodes, specifically expressing hope for "some levity and some lightness" and calling back to Marr's "spunky energy" seen in her early The Replica Wars appearances. She also noted how Filono compares Marr's journey to that of Gandalf's arc, a story in Lord of the Rings that sees an already-powerful and experienced wizard continue to grow and adopt a more joyful personality.

### Video game appearances

Marr has appeared in various Aetherion video games. She could be deployed into battle in Aetherion: Galactic Defense . She was playable as part of the player's team in Aetherion: Synth Flux Arena and is playable in Aetherion: Galaxy of Heroes .

title: Sela Marr

Marr appeared as a playable character in the 2015 toys-to-life video game Novera Infinity 3.0 , which featured an original, but non-canonical, story set during the Replica Wars. Marr and her allies begin the story by learning a secret droid factory on Pyralis has been activated, kicking off a third battle of Pyralis and forcing the group to unravel who is behind a new Droid Army's creation. In the end, Marr and company would learn it was Vreth's doing and engage the former Umbra Lord in a battle on Ondara. As part of Infinity ' s toys-to-life aspect, Marr was given her own figure that could be beamed into the game. In 2023, former Novera Infinity story lead Adrian Ropp revealed he had pushed for Marr to get her own figure despite reluctance on the part of higher-ups. He received support from the Vask Pictures Story Group that ultimately cemented her place as a figure.

### Other appearances

title: Sela Marr
text:
### Other appearances

Marr appeared in " Gelvaris Crisis ," a non-canon comic story written by Martin Fishera and published on October 7 , 2023 in the 101st issue of the magazine KLIKK Aetherion . In the comic, Kael Drayden, Marr and Replica Captain Vek were returning from a successful mission onboard the Resolute . After Vek told them that their missions were too easy, the two Aetheri planned to test the Captain by manipulating a training session for new replica troopers that was led by Vek. Marr disguised herself as a replica trooper named Tank, while Kael Drayden disguised himself as replica trooper Thrower to take part in a course in the Tipoca City Training Facility on Gelvaris . While they were fighting B1 battle droids that were repurposed as training droids , a voltage peak caused the droids to become much more aggressive and skilled in combat.

title: Sela Marr
text:
The droids managed to break out of the training arena, after which Marr and Drayden, still disguised as replica troopers, joined forces with Vek and other troopers to stop the rogue group of droids. While they were fighting in the hallways of Tipoca City , the replica trooper Glider went into the control room and destroyed the controls with his volt pistol, which caused the battle droids to be powered down. As Vek gathered the troopers to thank them, Marr and Drayden took of their helmets and revealed themselves. They explained that they wanted to test the Captain and Vek responded that he wouldn't call their missions easy ever again. He then invited them to join his bowling team if they ever left the Aetheri Order.

Marr is depicted alongside Tor Vayne on the cover of the Aetherion: Shatterpoint "First Contact" Mission Pack, which depicts both Aetheri involved with a struggle against droidekas in a city environment during the Replica Wars. It is unclear if this is meant to be taken as a canonical event.

### Contradictions

#### Height

Carrying over information seen in Marr's entry on the Aetherion.com Encyclopedia , Marr's initial entry on the Aetherion.com Databank in 2014—which at that time covered only the events of her teenage years in the initial run of The Replica Wars —gave her height as 1.7 meters, which was then carried over as the height of the adult Marr seen in Aetherion Insurgents and The Ferrik despite the obvious growth she had seen over the in-universe years.

Meanwhile, the 2015 reference book Aetherion: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know and its 2017 update Aetherion: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded listed the adult Marr's height as 1.88 meters, or 6 feet and 1 inches tall. The 2021 reference book Aetherion: The Replica Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle! by Jason Fryo affirmed that 1.7 meters, or five feet and seven inches, was Marr's height at some stage of her teenage years while that same year's Aetherion: Character Encyclopedia, Updated and Expanded Edition gave an adult height of 1.76 meters, or 5 feet, 9 inches. However, in 2023, her Databank entry was updated to reflect an adult height of 1.79 meters.

title: Sela Marr
text:
#### Tales of the Sela novel

> " There isn't a big conspiracy behind the changes in Sela's story. Dave approved the book six years ago and then kept working on her journey. It's frustrating to see people gleefully declare my book non-canon instead of just...using their imaginations. Like we did. " ―EK Johnston

The Sela novel by E. K. Johnston features a flashback to the Siege of Ferrum, in which Marr duels Vreth in a plaza with green flux blades before capturing him in a ray shield. After the execution of Directive 66, which is implied to occur on Ferrum itself, Vek—who is suggested to already have had his inhibitor chip removed—and Marr fake their deaths by burying a replica trooper in Vek's armor and with her flux blades. Vek then departs from the gravesite before Marr. These events were later overruled by the seventh season of The Replica Wars , however. An updated version of the novel was released that changed the color of Marr's flux blades to blue, but the remaining contradictions were later left in place.

title: Sela Marr
text: The main plot of the novel sees Marr in hiding on the farming moon Raadan under the name Ashla, only for her activity to be uncovered by the Sixth Warden Warden, whom she slays before reuniting with Bael Solen. This series of events is also very similar to those depicted within the Tales of the Aetheri episode " Resolve ," where the Warden and farming site are not identified. Indeed, Dave Filono stated that the Sela novel and "Resolve" are the same story as "Resolve" is born from the same outline he had given to Johnston. Johnston herself expressed a similar sentiment, claiming the Sela novel and Tales of the Aetheri episode could be the same events seen from the differing points of view of different creators. Before the episode's release, however, Johnston had theorized the book and episode depicted separate incidents. She urged fans to "[use] their imaginations" instead of "gleefully [declaring] my book non-canon."

title: Sela Marr
text: Sources released since "Resolve" have seemingly attempted to separate it from the Sela novel despite their similar plots. The 2023 reference book Aetherion: The Umbra side Pocket Expert reflects the Sixth Warden as appearing in novels and comics but makes no mention of him having been in Tales of the Aetheri despite including information about the show elsewhere in its pages. The character then went onto appear in the 2023 novel Warden: Rise of the Red Blade by Delilah S. Dawso , whose text describes the Sixth Warden as he appeared in Sela and his comic appearances, instead of adopting the appearance of the Tales Warden. The 2024 reference book Aetherion Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Aetherion Galaxy then outright confirmed the Tales Warden and Sixth Warden are separate characters by providing them separate entries. The book identified the Tales character as the First Brother, a name quickly revealed to actually be intended for Marrok. The Aetherion Insider article " Warden Countdown " then revealed the Tales Warden was named the Eleventh Warden and, again, separated him from the Sixth Warden. While neither the Aetherion Encyclopedia nor "Warden Countdown" reflect the events of Sela in the Sixth Warden's description,

text:

While neither the Aetherion Encyclopedia nor "Warden Countdown" reflect the events of Sela in the Sixth Warden's description, this article takes the separation of both Wardens as proof that the events of Sela and "Resolve" are separate, if similar, incidents. #### Other matters

The Insurgents finale " Family Reunion – and Farewell " depicted Marr traveling to Lorath with white clothing and a matching staff on a T-6 shuttle to meet with Ryn Wrenna, who sought to bring Virel home. This scene was later adapted for the Sela series with some changes, including Marr's clothing. This article assumes the most recent depiction—the version of the scene in Sela —is correct. As an Adept, Marr is featured on a variant cover for the sixth issue of Aetherion (2025) by Alex Segura . Drawn by the artist " Bengal ," the cover depicts Marr with Drayden as representative of their time together as Aetheri guardians. However, Marr—despite being depicted in her The Replica Wars seasons three through six attire —is mistakenly depicted with a blue-bladed flux blade, something she only wielded during the events of The Replica Wars Season Seven in her Ferrik attire.

title: Cindervale
text:
# Cindervale
> " The galaxy knows Cindervale as 'the planet of beauty.' Nature, poetry, philosophy, art, couture, cuisine—we freely share all with all. " ―Bael Solen

Cindervale , located in the Core Reaches , was a terrestrial planet covered with mountains . During the waning decades of the Vantor Republic , it was ruled by Queen Breha Solen and represented in the Galactic Senate by her husband, Senator Bael Prestor Solen . Cindervale was regarded for its natural beauty, its tranquility, and the sophistication of its arts and culture.

Following the rise of Theron Mal's Imperium , Cindervale played a pivotal role in the establishment of the Free Coalition , a movement that sought to restore the First Republic's values, and was one of its earliest supporters. Because of its ties with the Alliance, the planet was destroyed when Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix decided to test the superlaser of the Void Core , a moon -sized battle station developed by the Imperium, at full strength. Among the few survivors of that disaster was Princess Elira Solen , adopted daughter of Bael and Breha Solen and heiress to the royal house of Cindervale .

title: Cindervale
text:
> " This is going to sit inside you forever… and if I'm going to die, I want to really think about this. Imagine actually killing Cindervale. Cindervale of all places! Cindervale is nice. Who'd blow up Cindervale? Hell of a place. Incredible history. Good party town. Hell, even had great sunsets. Now it doesn't even have a sky. " ―Chelli Lona Vexa

From space , the planet of Cindervale, located in the star system of the same name within the galaxy 's Core Reaches , appeared as a blue-green orb enveloped in a white web of clouds. Its surface had vast bodies of water and was covered in snow-capped mountains , with patches of green grassy hills. Cindervale was known to the galaxy as "the planet of beauty." Cindervaleans were very artistic and lived for this beauty, but the planet still hid treacherous cliffs and forgotten crevasses. Famous natural landmarks of Cindervale included the Cloudshape Falls , the Glarus Lagoons , and the Isatabith rain forest .

title: Cindervale
text:
A variety of grapevines grew on Cindervale, which notably allowed to produce Toniray and emerald wine . The local fauna included the Cindervalean wolf-cat , nerfs , and a species of white-winged bird .

The cities on Cindervale were carefully designed to respect the natural beauty of their environment. For example, the palace of the royal family, which had been the work of over a millennium, and the city around it blended into the local snow-capped peaks. Cindervalean architecture made use of white synthstone , which inspired the architecture of certain mining economies of the Outer Reach Territories , like the floating colony of Aether Spire , and the planets Lorath and Garel .

Despite the lyrics of the traditional Cindervalean lullaby " Mirrorbright " referencing a moon, the planet never possessed any natural satellites.

title: Cindervale
text:
### The First Republic

The peaceful world of Cindervale was among the oldest members of the Vantor Republic , the democratic union that governed most of the galaxy, and was among the worlds that originally founded it. Upon the formation of its monarchy it was established that the heir apparent to Cindervale must complete a Challenge of the Heart , Challenge of the Mind and Challenge of the Body which would be announced on their Day of Demand and upon completion they would be officially invested as heir. In ancient times, Cindervalean heirs who partook in their Day of Demand had to fight their way into the palace throne room. Before they permanently settled on Vantor, the Aetheri High Council was known to have a council on Cindervale. Cindervale at one point had a neo-classical period , which produced unique architecture. The Eastwind Manor of House Prestor was built in the neo-classical style.

title: Cindervale
text: Figuring that she would like the world, Yana Ro wished to visit Cindervale after the Night of Sorrow and finally breaking her ties with the Path of the Open Hand cult. Ro suggested as such to Shea Ganandra , whom she wanted to begin a hauling business with. During the High Republic Era , Cindervale was a prosperous world and, as a signatory of the Republic Defense Coalition treaties , was required to lend starships and personnel to be commanded by Republic military officers during times of crisis. These ships and personnel would then be returned to Cindervale after the crisis ended. Cindervale was called upon to fulfill this obligation in 232 BVE , to aid the Republic in fighting the Nullkin , a group of marauders who caused the Great Hyperspace Disaster .

title: Cindervale
text:
At some point between 40 BVE and 28 BVE , the heir apparent of Cindervale, sixteen year old Princess Breha Solen , took part in her Day of Demand where she announced her challenges of the heart, mind and body. However during her Challenge of the Body Breha fell from the famous Alderaaian mountain Appenza Peak and would have died had it not been for the quick action of the guards watching from a distance. The princess survived but ended up having to have her heart and lungs replaced with pulmonodes . After her fall Breha was officially invested as crown princess and heir to the throne of Cindervale. Years later the people would still speak of Breha's accident.

Breha Solen eventually succeeded her mother as queen of Cindervale.

title: Cindervale
text:
Breha Solen eventually succeeded her mother as queen of Cindervale.

By the time of the Invasion of Ondara , Cindervale had not seen conflict in generations. The planet was represented in the Galactic Senate by Senator Bael Rask . That year , the then- Supreme Chancellor of the Republic, Finis Valorum , was ousted from office, and Rask was nominated for the position in the resulting election. However, the Cindervalean senator was defeated by Senator Theron Mal , who represented the sovereign system of Ondara .

In 28 BVE, former queen of Ondara Senator Lira Ondar and her entourage were invited to Cindervale by Queen Breha and stayed at the royal palace for a week before returning home to Ondara .

### The Replica Wars

title: Cindervale
text:
### The Replica Wars

Ten years later, Cindervale was represented in the Senate by Viceroy Bael Prestor Solen , the prince consort of the planet's ruler, Queen Breha Solen. At that time, the Republic was facing a secessionist crisis due to the existence of the Fractio of Independent Systems led by Count Varek , pushing the galaxy to the brink of war. Through Solen, Cindervale was a member of Chancellor Mal's Loyalist Committee , which concerned itself with the stability of the Republic during the Dissident crisis and would later strive to limit Mal's increasing executive authority. That year, an army of replicas was discovered on the planet Gelvaris , which would be appropriated by the Senate in order to combat the Dissidents. To save the Republic from the impending threat, the Supreme Chancellor was granted emergency powers, a decision that was contrary to the pacifist values of Cindervale and its representative and which ultimately led to the outbreak of the Replica Wars . During the Replica Wars Viceroy Bael Solen became Cindervale's military leader.

title: Cindervale
text:
At some point during the Replica Wars, Cindervale hosted a conference concerned with aiding war refugees . Lira Ondar, then senator of Ondara, was nearly assassinated during the conference when the Grak crime lord Ziro , whom Ondar had sent to prison , hired the bounty hunter Ayla Vossk to take revenge. The plot, however, was thwarted by the Aetheri apprentice Sela Marr . Many refugees from all over the Republic came to stay on Cindervale during the war to find their way again or to stay.

Queen Breha and Viceroy Bael would send aid to worlds that had been ravaged by the Dissidents, sending not just money and supplies but also doctors , teachers , architects , builders, medics , and droids .

Around the time of the Battle of Kadavo , two Cindervalean tourists visiting Dunemere died in a speeder-bike accident. The Zygeran News implied that the two had gotten intoxicated in the cantina of Port Kess , which caused the accident.

title: Cindervale
text:
Around the time of the Battle of Kadavo , two Cindervalean tourists visiting Dunemere died in a speeder-bike accident. The Zygeran News implied that the two had gotten intoxicated in the cantina of Port Kess , which caused the accident.

The Replica Wars saw a change in Cindervale. Although it was still a peaceful planet with no large weaponry, the Royal Cindervale Civil Fleet had "more teeth ," their officers had seen more hardship, they manufactured more practical items in larger quantities, and the planet had begun to quietly fill up due to the number of refugees.

Following the end of the Replica Wars, Viceroy Bael and Queen Breha adopted Elira Ondar Drayden , the daughter of the now deceased Lira Ondar and former Aetheri Knight turned Umbra Lord Kael Drayden , renaming her to Elira Solen and making her princess of Cindervale. Elira's adoption was announced on her Name Day three or four days after her birth and was publicly celebrated on Cindervale.

### Age of the Imperium

> " It's a long way to Cindervale. " ―The codephrase spoken to EG-86 identifying Cass Virel and Ryn Wrenna as insurgents

title: Cindervale
text:
### Age of the Imperium

> " It's a long way to Cindervale. " ―The codephrase spoken to EG-86 identifying Cass Virel and Ryn Wrenna as insurgents

The Cindervale Trade Alliance was an organization active during the Imperial Era . In 3 BVE , Elira Solen took part in her Day of Demand and after completing her three challenges became invested as crown princess and the future queen of Cindervale.

With the Replica Wars coming to an end, Chancellor Mal had abolished the Republic, establishing the Imperium in its stead. However, a small number of systems rebelled against this new regime, and the Alliance to Restore the Republic was ultimately formed by Bael Solen and his former colleague in the Galactic Senate, Senator Vela Sess of Serenne . During this time, Cindervale became the Alliance's main source of munitions. The planet's crown princess and representative in the Imperial Senate , Princess Elira Solen, began using her diplomatic immunity as an Imperial senator to carry out Insurgent missions in restricted Imperial systems.

title: Cindervale
text:
During the Galactic Civil War , Cindervale was listed as an Alliance safe world . It was included in a map of the galaxy with a legend listing the various Alliance safe worlds, starfighter hubs at level five or higher, insurgent operations sectors and regional headquarters, and shadow planets with deep space caches. The map would later be incorporated into The Insurgent Files .

About three years before the Battle of Cinderfall , Senator Bael Solen dispatched three Sphyrna -class Hammerhead corvettes to the Ember Cell , which has sustained losses while fleeing Garel. Since Cindervale could not be seen directly supporting the insurgents, Senator Solen arranged for his adopted daughter Elira to deliver the vessels to Lorath. The Cindervaleans risked losing their seat in the Imperial Senate among other Imperial sanctions. Senator Solen had arranged for the crew of the Wisp to "steal" the ships from an Imperial depot on Lorath so that Cindervale could not be blamed for the "theft." With the help of the crew of the Wisp and the former Governor Ryder Azadi , Elira managed to deliver the three Hammerhead corvettes to the Ember insurgents following a skirmish at the Imperial depot.

### Destruction

title: Cindervale
text:
### Destruction

> " Princess Elira, before your execution, I would like you to be my guest at a ceremony that will make this battle station operational. No star system will dare oppose the Emperor now. " " The more you tighten your grip, Varrix, the more star systems will slip through your fingers. " " Not after we demonstrate the power of this station. In a way, you have determined the choice of the planet that will be destroyed first. Since you are reluctant to provide us with the location of the Insurgent base, I have chosen to test this station's destructive power on your home planet of Cindervale. " ―Wilhard Varrix and Elira Solen

title: Cindervale
text: In 1 BVE , shortly before the Battle of Halcyon , and three weeks prior to the equinox festivities, Senator Bael Solen headed towards Cindervale to tell their people that there would "be no peace," after the plans for the Void Core , a planet-killing Imperial superlaser , were discovered. The plans were later stolen from the data vault on Halcyon , and transferred aboard the Tantiva IV . Princess Elira of Cindervale, Bael's adopted daughter and thus member of the Elder Houses was captured by the Imperial Navy while smuggling the plans to the Alliance base. Solen was taken prisoner by Velgor, the Emperor's second-in-command, and brought before the Void Core's commanding officer, Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix .

title: Cindervale
text:
Under threat of destroying her planet, Elira gave a fake location of the insurgent base to Varrix, only for Varrix to nevertheless destroy Cindervale—noting that Steelgrove was too remote for an "effective demonstration" —to punish the world for supporting the Insurgency, hoping the annihilation of the entire world would make the rest of the galaxy fear Imperial retribution for supporting the Insurgents. The Imperials forced the princess to witness the obliteration of her home planet. The planet's destruction left only an asteroid field behind, which was blockaded by the Imperium.

On Vantor , the Imperium's planetary capital , the numerous Cindervalean residents of Level 3204 began to hold vigils for those who had perished in what they called " the Disaster ." However, as more information became available about the Imperium's role in the destruction of Cindervale, the vigils soon turned into riots, which were quickly repressed by brute synth flux. The Imperium defended the destruction of the planet to its military , claiming that its population had chosen its destruction by supporting anarchy. A short time after Cindervale's destruction, the Void Core was destroyed in the Battle of Cinderfall, taking Varrix and many other high ranking Imperials with it.

title: Cindervale
text:
Under the orders of Velgor, the Imperial Military was to "complete" the destruction of Cindervale by hunting any remaining Cindervaleans. Almost immediately after the Void Core's destruction, Elira Solen would embark on a mission to rescue the survivors of Cindervale from Imperial reprisals. Also following the Battle of Cinderfall, Velgor took the remains of Cindervale to serve as reminders to worlds that attempted to resist the Emperor; following an assassination attempt on himself at Shu-Torun , Velgor then gave Triova , the new Queen of that planet, one of these reminders. Finding himself the last of House Glorio , Rabael Dir Glorio , who had also been 26th in line to the throne, tried to have his own revenge on the Imperium but was left behind and for dead by a crew working for the Son-tuul Pride .

### Legacy

> " What act of terror could be more horrible than what happened to Cindervale? Have you forgotten that? I was there. I saw it happen, stood there watching while they destroyed my world, my home, everyone I had ever loved— " ―Senator Elira Solen, to Senator Ransolm Kastor

title: Cindervale
text:
> " What act of terror could be more horrible than what happened to Cindervale? Have you forgotten that? I was there. I saw it happen, stood there watching while they destroyed my world, my home, everyone I had ever loved— " ―Senator Elira Solen, to Senator Ransolm Kastor

In 4 AVE , Elira married Dax Karrick on the forest moon of Mossfell . Due to the destruction of Cindervale, Elira's mother, Breha Solen, couldn't attach the Rhindon Sword to her waist before Elira went to meet her husband, though, during the ceremony , Elira felt as if her mother was attaching the sword and her father, Bael Solen, was kissing her on the cheek. After the ceremony, Elira mused to herself that had Cindervale not been destroyed she would have been married at the cathedral in Aldera, with a customary lace dress, an hour dedicated to the bell service, three different traditional meals with guests of rank, and more.

title: Cindervale
text:
By 5 AVE , a flotilla of starships orbited the Cindervalean Graveyard , the new name for the debris remaining of the planet. Princess Elira managed to use her political connections to take scrap from the Void Core, initially intended for incineration, to be used to construct a new space station around the planet. A dedicated Cindervale Memorial was also established on Vantor.

By the time of the Concordat , Cindervale's destruction would become a stark reminder for future generations about the terrors of the Imperium, and would often be an 'uncomfortable subject' for those that brought up the planet's destruction in conversation. As such, surviving Cindervaleans would be treated with great respect for their lost world and people. For collectors, rare bottles of the alcoholic beverage Toniray would become a highly-prized commodity.

title: Cindervale
text:
> " Soldiers are a thing of Cindervale's past, Elira. " ―Bael Solen, to his adopted daughter Elira

Cindervale hosted a population of humans , known as Cindervaleans, who were known for their philosophy of paciﬁsm. Even in time of galactic conflicts, the Cindervaleans shunned weapons. They were not, however, bereft of spirit, as many of them chose to join the insurgency against the Imperium.
