> " You gave it a shot. You tried to go straight. But you've got your father's blood pumping through your veins. You're a killer. " ―Cad Vorek, to Vex Vark

While destroying the second Scorpenek, the rancor fought several Pykes. Vark killed one while the rancor took care of the second Gruv, swallowing it whole. Vorek arrived and scared the rancor with fire from his vambraces, causing it to throw Vark and flee into the streets of Port Vail. The two warriors squared off. Vark told Vorek to clear out and to take his "hoodlum gang" with him. Vorek admitted that he did not understand Vark's motivations, and asked what his angle was. Vark stated that he would not abandon the city and his people. Vorek tried to goad Vark by mentioning the Tuskens, to which Vark told Vorek that he would not let him toy with him since he is no longer a young boy. Vorek pointed out that despite his age, he was still faster. Vark stood his ground however, before Vorek initiated a duel, shooting the Daimyo.

title: Vex Vark
text:
With swift shots, Vorek took Vark down and pinned him to the ground, and called him a killer just like his father was. Vorek taunted Vark that this is not the first time he had beaten him on a job. He ripped Vark's helmet off and prepared to kill Vark, and told him that this was his final lesson and that anything else was weakness. Before Vorek can shoot, Vark knocked him away with his gaderffii stick. The tides now turned, Vark defeated Vorek, knocking him to the ground. Vorek stated that he always knew Vark was a killer, before activating his flamethrower against him. Vark knocked the weapon out the away, and stabbed Vorek through the chest. Taking in what Vorek had said, Vark understood that his journey was not yet complete, whilst staring down at the body of his old mentor. Leaving the Kessith mercenary dead on the street, Vark walked away to assist his allies.

A town at peace

> " Why must everyone bow at me? " " It's better than shooting. " " Are those my only two choices? " " When you run the town, it is. " ―Vex Vark, and Fennec Thanna

title: Vex Vark
text:
A town at peace

> " Why must everyone bow at me? " " It's better than shooting. " " Are those my only two choices? " " When you run the town, it is. " ―Vex Vark, and Fennec Thanna

Unbeknownst to Vark however, the war had finished. Vark soon caught up with Thanna and Verrick, before thanking Verrick's for his services. Vark and Thanna then walked the streets, which the townsfolk were working together to clear and rebuild. Many stopped to bow and greet him, all of which he returned. Vark lamented having to move his right arm, but stated his bacta tank was in use when Thanna told him to take a soak. When Vark grumbled about people bowing to him, Thanna pointed out that he should be glad they bow to him, rather than shooting at him. A group of children then offered them Meiloorun fruits , one of which Vark accepts. Zazzik, the Mods and the LEP-series rat catcher meet up with the duo in the street.

#### Missions on Batuu

title: Vex Vark
text:
#### Missions on Batuu

Sometime after the victory at Port Vail, Vark and Thanna traveled to Black Spire Outpost on Batuu on a mission, looking for hidden Gruv Syndicate members and recruiting to the Vark gotra. Vark was reunited with Verrick and Pip, as they walked through the streets together and interacted with the locals. At another point, when Verrick returned to Port Kess to ask Peli Motto for an IG-series memory circuit , Motto asked if Verrick had come to depose Vark on behalf of the Grak Clan .

### Legacy

Vark was remembered as one of the best bounty hunters in the galaxy, with a reputation and legacy that eclipsed even his father's.

Following the Battle of Saltmark in 34 AVE , Hondik Hosha mentioned Vark in his book titled the Galactic Explorer's Guide , including him in the "Renegade's Gallery" section for Mistral. He also included a poster of Vark and information on Reaver One in the planet's section as well, mentioning that the ship had been owned by Garrick, Vossk, himself, and then Vex. During the New Imperium-Coalition War , Dok-Ondar told a shock trooper sergeant and his troops about how he came to buy Reth-Oss-Van 's flux blade, events that briefly involved Vark. During the same war, Nyla lied to bounty hunter Kief Varris that Vark, along with other bounty hunters had attempted to capture Moebin Faltus at one point.

title: Vex Vark
text:
### The young bounty hunter

> " No one of true importance would lower themselves to trade with a mere boy. " " Boy? You have no idea who you're talking to. I have been in charge of this whole operation— " "You have no idea who you are talking to. " ―Kessa Vray and Vex Vark As a child, Vex developed a strong bond with his father, learning much from Garrick's years as a bounty hunter. Vex was suspicious of Orien Kade upon the Aetheri Knight's arrival on Gelvaris, recognizing him as a potential threat to both himself and Garrick. He took pleasure in fighting Kade both on Gelvaris and in orbit of Pyralis, expressing joy at the thought that the Aetheri had been killed. His personality hardened after Garrick's death, as a traumatized Vex swore vengeance on Drevan Koss, yet he did not take any pleasure in the collateral damage wrought by his mission. His better nature eventually won over in honor of his father's memory, as Vex turned against his bounty hunting allies and allowed himself to be taken into the custody of the Vantor Republic. Despite realizing the errors of his ways, he swore he would never forgive Koss for the murder of his father.

title: Vex Vark
text:
During the Replica Wars, Vex expressed aversion to being compared to replica troopers. He did not want to see himself as being the same as other young replicas or a replica in general, as he saw himself as Garrick Vark's son. He nonetheless did not care to harm the replicas, and briefly considered leaving his bounty hunter companions to stay with the other young replicas who escaped the Endurance .

After being released from prison and forming a bounty hunter team, Vark became somewhat more ruthless than he had been previously, focused on achieving the goals of his mission. During the mission to Quarzite, Vark wanted to hand Pluma Sodi over to Otua Blank, despite her pleas for mercy. Only Vray's betrayal allowed Sodi to escape.

As a child, Vark stood at 1.35 meters , or 4 feet , 5 inches tall.

### Adult life

#### Imperial Era

> " You can't leave me out here, Vex. I'm cold-blooded. I won't sssurvive. " " Cold-blooded. Huh. Funny thing about that, Boskan. So am I. " ―Boskan and Vex Vark

title: Vex Vark
text: As the years went by and the Replica Wars gave way to the reign of the Imperium, Vark became known for his lethality and extreme methods, even displaying trophies of his prey on his armor. During the Imperial Era, the confident bounty hunter had a penchant for disintegrations and proved to be ruthless, willing to kill those who had wronged him. He was still able to find enjoyment in life, particularly enjoying the surprise less experienced hunters showed at his mere presence. While working on Carajam, Vark received a reputation as a hunter of criminals after saving a village, but he insisted that he was only interested in pursuing bounties regardless of the ideals of his victims. His father's death at the hands of Aetheri Master Drevan Koss caused Vark to develop an aversion to the Aetheri . When Vark encountered Aetheri Knight Cal Kessara on Koboh , more than a decade after Garrick's death, he told Kessara that he had no pity for the fate of the large number of Aetheri who were killed during the Great Aetheri Purge . While acknowledging that the two could meet again, Vark told Kessara that he hoped that would never happen.

title: Vex Vark
text: Beyond becoming one of Grukk the Grak's favorite bounty hunters, Vark also realized the Grak may have considered him the closest person in his life to a friend. In truth, Grukk had his only friend in Ephant Mon . Grukk also once referred to Vark as his " pup ." Still, on some nights, if everyone else in the palace was asleep, Grukk shared a bottle of graska with Vark and, after waking up Max Rebo and ordering him to play a sad song, tell private, personal stories to Vark. Even though he made sure to never take off his volt pistol, the bounty hunter agreed to his boss's request, taking off his helmet and listening. Though Vark could never understand what Grukk was telling him, he found the Grak's company tolerable, considering how much the crime lord paid him for work. Vark was also none-too-keen on Grukk's showboating, such as how the Grak tried to enslave Elira Solen and make her watch the attempted execution of her friends. He was also made uncomfortable by the way Grukk treated his prior dancer Oola, whose name he made himself remember after her death.

title: Vex Vark
text:
Additionally, Vark continued to hold his father, Garrick, in high regard even during his adult years. He remained haunted by his death, remembering himself as a child holding his father's helmet on Pyralis after signing up for the Nar Shaddaa fighting ring under Garrick's name. When the Reaver One was slightly damaged by 4-VOX and Zuckusso on Nar Shaddaa, he deemed it to be a slight against both himself and his father.

#### After the Imperium

> " Living with the Tuskens has made you soft. " " No, its made me strong. You can only get so far without a tribe. " ―Fennec Thanna and Vex Vark

title: Vex Vark
text:
> " Living with the Tuskens has made you soft. " " No, its made me strong. You can only get so far without a tribe. " ―Fennec Thanna and Vex Vark

In the time after the Imperium's fall and after escaping the devourer pit, Vark had mellowed considerably because of his time with the Dunefolk tribe; after spending his life working for employers who led him to near death experiences, Vark realized most crime lords in the galaxy had no loyalty to their hired hands, while the tribe he had spent years with had respected and accepted him. Certain that he could do better than the crime lords who jumped into situations without thinking them through, Vark set out to form his own crime family, stating it would be an organization that would respect its members and protect their lives. As he told Fennec Thanna, crime families built without both "brains and muscle" had killed many of "[their] kind," so he was tired of letting "the idiocy of others" bring his fellows to their deaths. He believed that he needed to build a crime family that instead emulated the tribe he had been a part of.

title: Vex Vark
text: He no longer isolated himself from others; he willingly saved Fennec's life and accepted her partnership. In addition, Vark had gained a sense of honor and humility, viewing himself as a simple man making ends meet. After fulfilling his part of the deal he had made with the Ferrik Dinna Verrick, he went back to Dunemere and killed the crime lord Bib Fortuna, who had taken Grukk's Palace, and took over the palace's throne to establish a criminal imperium that would offer loyalty and respect. When asked by Verrick about whether or not he followed the Ferrik way, Vark replied that he swore allegiance to no one, indicating that he retained his profound sense of independence. Still, after Verrick formally recognized Vark's ownership of his Ferrik armor, the bounty hunter honored the deal they had made earlier and promised to help the Ferrik rescue Pip after the latter was kidnapped, displaying a strong code of honor.

title: Vex Vark
text: After losing his armor, which had once belonged to his father, Vark was determined to reclaim it, despite not identifying himself as Ferrik. During his negotiations with Verrick, the bounty hunter repeatedly pointed out that the armor was previously his father's possession, showing a desire to preserve and protect Garrick's legacy. Upon encountering Bo-Katin Velara, who claimed that he was not a Ferrik, Vark acknowledged her statement, as he did not consider himself a true Ferrik, but declared that he had the right to bear the armor as it had belonged to his father, who had been a Ferrik foundling. When Velara referred to Garrick as his "donor" due to his replica origins, Vark responded with hostility, angered by her mockery of his father. He quickly engaged in a brief scuffle with Velara's partner, Koska Reeves, before the fight was broken up by Velara herself.

title: Vex Vark
text:
> " The only time I fail is if you hired me to fail. " ―Vex Vark

Vex's talents as a bounty hunter were infamous across the galaxy, and he became well-known to galactic fugitives who had bounties on their heads. From a young age, Vex was trained by his father in combat skills, both in hand-to-hand combat and weapons, able to handle a volt pistol at a young age while being deadly in battle scenarios. Vex helped Garrick fight against Orien Kade on Gelvaris, displaying his ability to utilize the heavy weapons on Reaver One . His skills grew throughout the years, and despite his body condition, was still capable of using strategy, tactics and brute synth flux to make short work of a shock trooper contingent with a gaderffii stick. He displayed an affinity for leadership as he formed his own syndicate of bounty hunters. He also commanded the loyalty to those close to him, such as Boskan, and could communicate in Vark Code with his father, Garrick.

title: Vex Vark
text:
### Vehicles of choice

> " Honestly, we're lucky he got away. Vark's flying Slave One . " ―Dorian Quill, to Brevok

After Garrick's death, Vex took possession of Reaver One , though he lost the ship on Florrine for a time. Instead, while running the Krayt's Claw, Vark and his crew used Boskan's personal starship, the Hound's Tooth . Later, Vark reclaimed the Reaver One , which he would use throughout the following years of his bounty hunting career. The ship was already a viciously effective and heavily customized craft when his father had piloted it, meaning it already suited a professional bounty hunter's needs, but Vex went onto apply his own upgrades to his distinctive starship. The manifold capabilities of Reaver One , ranging from a stolen military-grade jamming and masking device to its duo of short-range twin volt pistol cannons , meant it was among the most dangerous aspects of Vark's arsenal as he tracked bounties throughout the galaxy. Once Vark had found his prey, if the bounty needed to be brought in alive, he could place the quarry into one of the ship's prisoner cages, which were equipped with six immobilizing bunks.

title: Vex Vark
text:
This vessel became iconic throughout the galaxy, known to fugitives as the ship of the feared bounty hunter. Over his career, Vark used the overwhelming firepower of the Reaver One to ruthlessly annihilate other heavy armed craft, including those of fellow hunters. In fact, even gunboats were unable to stand against Vark's starship, with the bounty hunter reducing them to blasted wreckage with its hidden weaponry before they could even respond. Using an ion blast fired from the twin volt pistol cannons and the ship's tractor beams, Vark was also able to board or easily destroy a smaller vessel. Even ships that were more powerful than the Reaver One were susceptible to the tractor beams, allowing Vark to latch onto enemy craft and become virtually inescapable. Vark rode a quadruped droid mount while pursuing bounties on Carajam.

### Ferrik armor

> " You are a disgrace to your armor. " " This armor belonged to my father. " " Don't you mean your donor? " ―Bo-Katin Velara and Vex Vark

title: Vex Vark
text:
### Ferrik armor

> " You are a disgrace to your armor. " " This armor belonged to my father. " " Don't you mean your donor? " ―Bo-Katin Velara and Vex Vark

During his early bounty hunting career, Vex had his own unique red and grey armor, including a helmet and twin volt pistols. As his career continued, Vex donned Garrick's Ferrik armor . Unlike Garrick's armor, Vex changed the color of the armor to mostly green—and battered and covered in marks from volt pistol fire. Vark took pride in the gear, regarding it as a family heirloom he had rightfully taken ownership of after his father's demise. Imperium Vigil Bureau Agent Andressa Divo , who believed Vark was not of Ferrik heritage, noted in Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious that, despite there not being a shortage of knockoff Ferrik gear in circulation among the bounty hunting profession, she believed that Vark's gear was authentic.

title: Vex Vark
text:
Vark regularly wore a Z-6 jetpack and carried an EE-3 carbine rifle . His vambraces were equipped with a flamethrower , concussion rockets , vibroblades , a whipcord launcher , and a wrist laser . Inside the kneepads were rocket dart launchers , and the shoulders were adorned with braids that Vex displayed as trophies of defeated prey.

### Dunefolk garb and weapons

After losing his armor to the Duskkins, Vark found himself with only a white under suit, which he continued to wear as he lived with the Dunefolk tribe who took him in. For the raid on the Gruv train, Vark stole several speeder bikes from the Kintan Striders Gang to catch up to the vehicle. After proving himself by leading the raid, Vark undertook a vision quest from which he secured a wortwood tree branch. Under the guidance of the Tuskens, Vark crafted it into his own personal gaderffii stick that served him as an effective weapon. He was further dressed in a black garb by the Tuskens, adopting their dress as their ways became his own. He also came to wield a cycler rifle . After losing the Tribe and until he regained his armor, Vark continued to wear that gear. After regaining his armor from Dinna Verrick, Vark blended together his Ferrik and Dunefolk gear, creating a unique look. He also continued to make use of his gaderffii stick and wielded a DB-41 sporting volt pistol pistol .

title: Vex Vark
text: ### Portrayal Vex Vark was first introduced in The Aetherion Holiday Special , a two hour long holiday-themed television movie special in the year 1978. His first canonical appearance was in Aetherion : Episode V Rise of the Imperium , where he was portrayed by Jeremy Bulloch and John Morton . He was voiced in Rise of the Imperium by Jason Wingreen , before his voice was over-dubbed by Temuera Morison , who played Garrick Vark in Aetherion : Episode II Attack of the Replicas as well as Garrick's replicas in Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra , for the 2004 DVD release of the original trilogy . Bulloch reprised the role for Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri . The character was also added into the 1997 Special Edition of Aetherion : Episode IV First Dawn . For Attack of the Replicas , young Vex Vark was portrayed by Daniel Logano , who also voiced the character in his multiple appearances on the television series Aetherion: The Replica Wars . Jon Hamm voiced Vark for the audiobook adaptation of the story " Added Muscle ". In The Ferrik Season 2 , Morison portrayed the character for the

Jon Hamm voiced Vark for the audiobook adaptation of the story " Added Muscle ". In The Ferrik Season 2 , Morison portrayed the character for the first time on-screen, after previously voicing him in Rise of the Imperium and portraying his father Garrick in Episode II. In " Chapter 14: The Tragedy ," Kirk Jenkins served as a stunt double. Scott Lang and Eddie Perez served as stunt doubles in " Chapter 16: The Rescue ." Morison voiced Vark once again for the 2023 video game Aetherion Aetheri: Survivor .

title: Vex Vark
text: Vark appeared in the Aetherion Galaxy of Adventures short, Grukk the Grak - Galactic Gangster , which depicted him, at some point after the capture of Dax Karrick, returning to Grukk's Palace to deposit an Aquari captive to the Grak crime lord. As the Galaxy of Adventures shorts are not supposed to be viewed as literal canon events, it is not included in the biography section of this article. On May 4, 2015, a costume of Vex Vark was added to The Simza 4 for playable Simza to wear in-game. The costume is purely cosmetic and offers no gameplay changes.

title: Vex Vark
text:
Actor Temeura Morison has stated in an interview that he sought to reduce Vex Vark's amount of dialogue during filming of The Book of Vex Vark , so as to keep the character mysterious. To that end, he asked that some of his dialogue be given to his co-star Ming-Na Wen , who plays Fennec Thanna in the show. Vex Vark is based on Clint Eastwood's The Man With No Name character from Sergio Leonne's Dollars Trilogy , who, like Vex Vark, was a morally grey bounty hunter, that had a moral compass. Vark's armor is a similar color to the outfit worn by Eastwood in the Dollars Trilogy. [ source? ]

### Unconfirmed fate

> " Vex Vark was just another one of the minions, another one of the bounty hunters and bad guys. But, he became such a favorite of everybody's that, for having such a small part, he had a very large presence. " ―Orin Vask, in the Aetherion: Episode VI Return of the Aetheri DVD commentary

title: Vex Vark
text: Despite his brief appearances in the original trilogy, with only four lines of dialogue in Rise of the Imperium , Vex became a popular character amongst Aetherion fans, which surprised series creator Orin Vask . On the DVD commentary for Return of the Aetheri , Vask stated that if he had known Vex would be a popular character, he would have made the character's death in Return of the Aetheri more exciting. Vask contemplated adding a scene in Return of the Aetheri where Vex climbed out of the devourer pit, especially in light of the character's story in Attack of the Replicas , but ultimately decided against it because he thought that the audience would believe that Vark would appear later in the film if this scene had been seen. However, on July 16 , 2014 , Aetherion author and historian Jonathan W. Rinzler stated in a Reddit AMA that Vask has said that Vex also survived the devourer in the new canon. This was officially confirmed when Vark appeared in " Chapter 14: The Tragedy " of Aetherion: The Ferrik Season Two . Vark's escape would later be seen in " Chapter 1: Stranger in a Strange Land "

title: Vex Vark
text:
Vask has said that Vex also survived the devourer in the new canon. This was officially confirmed when Vark appeared in " Chapter 14: The Tragedy " of Aetherion: The Ferrik Season Two . Vark's escape would later be seen in " Chapter 1: Stranger in a Strange Land " of The Book of Vex Vark . [ source? ] ### Planned storylines

According to Gary Kurtz , during the early development of the original trilogy, when Vask envisioned the whole story of Aetherion in four trilogies and twelve films, he conceived Vark as the main antagonist of Return of the Aetheri , because Vael Mal was originally planned to be introduced in Aetherion : Episode IX . However, after Vask decided to not make a third trilogy , Vark's role in Aetheri was changed to a relatively minor role.

title: Vex Vark
text: During the development of the prequel trilogy , at one point Vask considered depicting Kael Drayden and Vark as stepbrothers, possibly referencing their alliance in Rise of the Imperium , but discounted it as "too hokey." In continuing to develop the character in the prequel films, Vask closed some avenues for expanding the character's story while opening others. In the late October of 2002, during production on Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra , concept artist Feng Zhu created a piece that featured an older Vark "hanging out" with a replica trooper on the "bridge world," which ultimately evolved into the planet Cato Geltaria . The concept art team, however, ultimately decided the Vark and replica trooper piece suggested too much of a story to Vask.

text: Nonetheless, for a time, Vask considered including Vark in the story of Fury of the Umbra . Vark was meant to participate during the Great Aetheri Purge as the killer of Drevan Koss instead of Vael Mal, via shooting him with his volt pistol while he was escaping from some shock troopers, ending his vendetta against him due to the death of Garrick once and for all. Eventually, Vask decided to not add Vark to the story, saying that he would be "too young"—he would have been 13 years at that point—and that he was not necessary to be involved in Kael's fall. Ironically, Orin Vask originally placed off-limits the possibility to use Vark in the show when writer Henry Gilron was writing the show bible, but by the time of the next meeting, Vask changed his mind and Vark was allowed to be used in the series. Before the cancelation of The Replica Wars TV series, Vex Vark was set to make an appearance during a four-episode arc starring him and Cad Vorek. The two were going to team up for a "rescue mission" on Dunemere where Dunefolk Raiders had kidnapped a child. It would emphasize Vex's and Cad's relation to one another as Cad had known Garrick. During this arc, Vex would don his green armor for the first time. In a clip revealed during the Animated Origins and Unexpected Fates panel at Celebration Orlando in 2017 , Cad Vorek and other Bounty Hunters had ended an insurrection by Vark. To finish it, Vark and Vorek engaged in a stand-off duel, which would have resulted in Vark getting the dent on his helmet. Vark wearing his Ferrik armor and the rest of Krayt's Claw would have also appeared in an episode being hired by Kessa Vray to rescue Daren Kelv from Count Varek's castle on Serreno. An already animated scene shows the bounty hunters fighting the Umbra Lord. The episode would later be adapted into the 2015 novel Dark Disciple .

title: Vex Vark
text:
During the initial development of Aetherion : Episode VII Synth Flux Awakens , Bulloch expressed interest in reprising his role as Vark, but in the end, Vark didn't appear in the film. Aetherion Hong Kong announced on Facebook that Vex Vark would return in The Ferrik Season Three , however the post was later deleted. Vark ultimately did not appear in the season.

### Aetherion: Visions

Vark also appeared in the 2021 anime series Aetherion: Visions , appearing in its second episode, " Dunemere Rhapsody ." Produced by Studio Colorido and set at some point during the Imperial Era, Temuera Morison returned to the role of Vex Vark once more in the English dub.

title: Vex Vark
text:
When Geezer Odajion , a member of the Grak Clan left the syndicate to form a band called Star Waver , Grukk hired Vex to capture the rogue Grak and bring him to Dunemere for execution. Along with a few other bounty hunters, Vex tracked down the band during a concert and attempted to bring in Odajion. But Odajion and the band fought off their attackers and made a hasty escape, only for Vex to follow them in Reaver One . Eventually, Vex found the band again and threatened to kill Odajion's companions if he didn't come with him. Odajion then surrendered and left with Vex in his starship en route to Dunemere. Vex returned Odajion to Grukk, who prepared for him to be publicly executed. Star Waver however soon made a deal with Grukk to allow them to perform one last song with Odajion. Odajion and his band then performed to the approval of the crowd. But before Odajion could be killed, Jay , the band's vocalist asked Grukk to spare Odajion and become the band's first sponsor. Grukk agreed and Odajion was spared, allowing the band to continue playing as Vex found himself enjoying their music.

### Discrepancies

title: Vex Vark
text:
### Discrepancies

> " Vex Vark! Please, we need your help ! And we've seen what you do—you hunt bad men , murderers , criminals — " " No…I hunt bounties . " ―Stallo and Vex Vark speak during the Imperial Era

Aetherion Character Encyclopedia, New Edition states that, over the years, Vex Vark developed a code of honor and only took on missions that fit his harsh sense of judgment. Aetherion Helmet Collection 2 states that Vark always picked his targets according to his personal code of honor. In Age of Insurgency - Vex Vark 1 , Stallo assumes Vark hunts "bad men," criminals, and murderers. However, Vark denies this and reveals he simply hunts bounties, implying he has no moral code. Vark then points his volt rifle at Stallo, intending to collect a bounty on him. Aetherion: The Galactic Explorer's Guide later stated that Vark had no code except for the conditions for bringing in a target and how many credits the bounty was worth.

title: Vex Vark
text:
Aetherion: The Ferrik , set after Vark fell into the devourer, later portrayed Vark with an honor code. When Vark was given his own series in Aetherion: The Book of Vex Vark , the series showcased Vark's change in character through its flashbacks; as established in " Chapter 4: The Gathering Storm ," Vark's outlook had changed because honor-less employers had nearly gotten him killed one too many times and living with a tribe of Dunefolk Raiders taught him the value in working with others.

Although Ultimate Aetherion, New Edition stated that Vark and Boskan escaped from the Republic Detention Center, Aetherion: The Secrets of the Bounty Hunters later stated that they were released. Speaking about Vark in specific, The Aetherion Book also stated he was "released" from Republic custody.

title: Astra-9
text:
# Astra-9
> " We seem to be made to suffer. It's our lot in life. " ―Astra-9

Astra-9 ( See-Astra-9 ) was an Astra-9-series protocol droid designed to interact with organics , programmed primarily for etiquette and protocol. Sometimes referred to as Astra-9 , he was fluent in over six million forms of communication , and developed a fussy and worry-prone personality throughout his many decades of operation. Along with his counterpart, the astromech droid Bolt-3 , Astra-9 constantly found himself directly involved in pivotal moments of galactic history , and aided in saving the galaxy on many occasions.

title: Astra-9
text: Astra-9 was rebuilt from spare parts by Kael Drayden , an enslaved human who lived in Port Vail , a city on the Outer Reach world of Dunemere . During the Replica Wars , he would serve the Ondara Senator Lira Ondar . Shortly after the Replica Wars, Astra-9's memory was erased , though Bolt-3's memory was not. Astra-9 and Bolt-3 were assigned to the Cindervale cruiser Tantiva IV , where they served senator Bael Solen for nineteen years, assisting in his fledgling coalition movement against the Imperium . At some point during this time, Astra-9's right leg was fitted with mismatched plating.

title: Astra-9
text: Astra-9 remained constant companions with Bolt, and in 1 BVE , the pair became embroiled in the Galactic Civil War when Elira Solen of the Free Coalition entrusted them to bring a copy of the Void Core plans to the Aetheri Master Orien Kade on Dunemere. After meeting Drayden's son, Joren and the smuggler Dax Karrick , the droids helped rescue Princess Elira from the Imperium's Void Core . They became directly attached to the three humans, helping them and their insurgency defeat the Imperium and restore freedom to the galaxy, most notably when he convinced the Mosskins to aid the Insurgents at the Battle of Mossfell .

title: Astra-9
text: Following the Battle of Mossfell, Astra-9 continued serving the Draydens and Karrick during the time of the Concordat . About thirty years after the events on Mossfell , Astra-9 was still an aide to Solen, who had become a general in the Coalition , a private military group opposed to the New Imperium , a military junta that emulated the Old Imperium. By that time, Astra-9 was fitted with a new set of gold plating, which had a more symmetrical design than his previous coverings, with the exception of his head. His new coverings included a third finger joint, and a torso that was not as slim as it used to be. Because of his new plating, he no longer had a mismatched right lower leg. Although, he did end up wearing a red left arm for a very short time. By that time, Astra-9's language database had also been updated so that he could understand and communicate in over seven million different forms of communication, including ancient Umbra dialects. He would assist Nyla in translating Umbra writings in order to locate Vael Mal and the Umbra Eternal 's fleet, the Final Order , on Umbrale , allowing his memory to be wiped in order to carry out the task. However, his friend Bolt backed up a large portion of his memories, and after the Coalition defeated Mal and the Umbra Eternal in the Battle of Umbrale , his memory was restored.

title: Astra-9
text:
### Early incarnation

> " Oh, might I remind you, sir, I was once protocol droid to the chief negotiator for the entire Manakron system. " ―Astra-9

In an early incarnation, Astra-9 served as a protocol droid to the chief negotiator for the Manakron system . Additionally, he later claimed that his first job was programming binary loadlifters , which he said were very similar to moisture vaporators in most respects.

### Serving the Maker

> " He's perfect. " ―Lira Ondar after meeting Astra-9 ### Serving the Maker

> " He's perfect. " ―Lira Ondar after meeting Astra-9

At some point, however, Astra-9 was seriously damaged and his vital components were left behind on a junk pile on Dunemere . Kael Drayden , a slave boy from the Tatooinian city of Port Vail , collected scrap parts and started rebuilding Astra-9 in 34 BVE so the droid would help his mother . As Kael longed for a life far from Dunemere and explore the galaxy , he hoped to have Astra-9 as his and his mother's faithful companion so they would be able to venture the galaxy one day and understand the languages of the natives they came across, given Astra-9's capability of millions of communication forms. Although protocol droids were normally designed for light duty in luxurious environments, Drayden specially modified Astra-9 so he could withstand Dunemere's sand and heat. Astra-9 served Kael and his mother Shira by performing household chores. During his time with Drayden and Shira, Astra-9's parts and wiring were left exposed since Drayden was unable to outfit him with an outer covering due to droid plating being too expensive.

title: Astra-9
text: Following the Commerce Combine 's invasion of the Mid Reach planet of Ondara , Astra-9's life entered a new chapter when his owner Kael met several off-worlders at the shop of his owner, the Junk dealer Waddu , and then invited them to seek shelter at his home during a sandstorm. The Aetheri Master Sorin Vael , the Queen of Ondara Lira Ondar , the Mool Greeb Mool , and the astromech droid Bolt-3 were brought to the slave quarters that Kael shared with his mother Shira. As a result of this invitation, Ondar and Bolt-3 were introduced to Astra-9. Kael plugged in one of Astra-9's photoreceptors , which became the first time Astra-9 had experienced sight. Upon meeting Bolt-3, Astra-9 was shocked when the candid astromech droid commented that he was "naked." Despite the exchange, the two droids fast developed a friendship of sorts, working together to help Drayden make final adjustments to his dune racer in time to race it in the Dune Eve Classic race . While working on the dune racer , the two droids discussed space travel and noted the clumsy actions of Mool.

title: Astra-9
text:
On the day of the race, Astra-9 represented his owner in the opening flag parade, carrying Drayden's flag onto the course prior to the start of the race. He then stood on the sidelines with Bolt-3 and two of Drayden's playmates, Kitster Banai and Wald , who cheered their friend on. Drayden won the race, which, thanks to a deal that Vael had struck with Waddu, earned the boy his freedom from slavery and secured Vael the hyperrelay generator he needed to leave the planet. As Drayden prepared to depart Dunemere, he said his goodbyes to Astra-9, apologizing for not having completed the droid's construction, and expressing his wishes that Shira wouldn't sell him.

### Beyond Dunemere

> " There's been some terrible mistake. I'm programmed for etiquette, not destruction! " ―Astra-9 during the Battle of Pyralis

title: Astra-9
text:
### Beyond Dunemere

> " There's been some terrible mistake. I'm programmed for etiquette, not destruction! " ―Astra-9 during the Battle of Pyralis

Later, his owner Shira was sold to the moisture farmer Cliegg Havel , who freed and married her. Shira brought Astra-9 along with her, and the protocol droid found himself in the service of the Havel family, who owned a moisture farm in the Jundland Wastes . Shira covered him in a tarnished grey plating to shield him from Dunemere's sandy environment. Ten years after his parting with Kael Drayden, Shira was kidnapped by a group of Dunefolk Raiders , fearsome nomads native to Dunemere's desert wastes. Sensing his mother's pain and anguish through Synth Flux , Kael returned with his secret lover and childhood friend Lira Ondar to find his mother. Drayden had advanced in his Aetheri training as an Adept under the tutelage of Orien Kade , while Ondar had become a Senator in the Galactic Senate .

title: Astra-9
text: When Drayden and Ondar visited the Havel' moisture farm, they found Astra-9 working on a moisture vaporator. He initially didn't recognize Drayden until the latter finished his name for him when introducing himself. Greeting his Maker, Astra-9 discovered that Drayden had come in search of his mother, and brought the two guests into the homestead's courtyard, where they were met by Cliegg Havel, as well as his son, Owen Havel and his girlfriend, Brue Whitesun . Learning of his mother's peril, Drayden took Owen's speeder bike to find her, and soon returned with her corpse, having recovered it from a Dunefolk village. Astra-9 was present when he arrived, and later attended a funeral for Shira on the farm's property. When Bolt-3, who had been waiting aboard Ondar's nearby yacht, interrupted the funeral with an urgent message for the Adept, Astra-9 translated the astromech's binary beeps and whistles. After viewing the holocomm message, Drayden and Ondar departed Dunemere for Pyralis to rescue Drayden's Aetheri Master Orien Kade, taking Astra-9 with them.

title: Astra-9
text: Thus, Astra-9 would become both a witness and participant in the subsequent First Battle of Pyralis , the first spark of the Replica Wars , a conflict that would change the course of galactic history. After landing on Pyralis, Astra-9 reluctantly followed Bolt-3, Drayden, and Ondar into the Pyralian droid foundry. After being trapped in the factory's conveyor belt system, Astra-9's head was separated from his body and grafted onto the chassis of a B1-series battle droid . Meanwhile, a B1 battle droid head was inserted onto Astra-9's body. During the ensuing battle, both of Astra-9's "bodies" were knocked out during the fighting. Fortunately for him, he was promptly reattached to his rightful body by Bolt-3. Following the events on Pyralis, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 travelled to Ondara with Drayden and Ondar for the two to be married in Ondara's Lake Country.

title: Astra-9
text:
In the days following the Pyralis battle and before the wedding, Astra-9 was determined to keep Drayden and Ondar out of each other's sight until the wedding itself. Whilst waiting for the ceremony, Ondar believed there was a high chance Drayden was biding his time by working on Astra-9, as the droid needed to be cleaned after the sands of Dunemere had years to get into his joints, only to be further dirtied by the sands of Pyralis. As such, the protocol unit needed to receive a cleaning before he could receive his yet-to-be-finished new plating. Despite Astra-9's attempts, the two humans did see each other before the wedding, as Ondar, per a request from Queen Jamillia of Ondara, needed the help of Bolt-3 and Drayden to rescue the Torada Collective from the Dissident planet Nooroyo . After completing the mission, they returned to the Lake House to be wed, with Astra-9 and Bolt-3 in attendance.

### The Replica Wars

#### Serving Senator Ondar

title: Astra-9
text:
### The Replica Wars

#### Serving Senator Ondar

During the Replica Wars, Astra-9 would serve Senator Lira Ondar, the spouse of Kael Drayden, and was given a shiny gold - colored plating to better suit his new role. On one occasion, Ondar was captured by Grukk's uncle Ziro during a mission to reopen communications with the Graks after Grukk's son Rotto was kidnapped by the Dissident leader Count Varek . Ondar contacted Astra-9, who in turn contacted the Vantor Guard , which promptly raided Ziro's Palace and freed Ondar. Meanwhile, Drayden and his Adept Sela Marr managed to rescue Rotto and return him safely to his father. Astra-9 and his comrades' actions help the Republic win over Grukk, who later signed a favorable treaty with them.

title: Astra-9
text: Following the Rotto affair, Astra-9 accompanied Senator Ondar on a mission to contact the InterGalactic Banking Clan 's executive, who purportedly wanted to sue for peace. Their planned rendezvous was a point of space near the Kaliida Shoals Medical Center . Unknown to the two of them, this was a trap concocted by Vael Mal and his apprentice Count Varek. The Dissident military commander General Skarn 's flagship Malignar had been damaged during a recent space battle and was unable to enter hyperspace . The Umbra and Dissidents hoped to use Senator Ondar as a hostage to extract leverage from the Republic commander Drayden, who was pursuing the Malignar .

title: Astra-9
text:
Ondar's vessel was trapped in the Dissident warship's grapple beam , but they broke free by exploding their vessel's engines. Astra-9 and Ondar then sneaked aboard and contacted Drayden for help. Drayden along with Kade and Bolt-3 boarded the Malignar and made arrangements to rendezvous with Astra-9 and the Senator at the warship's rail jet system. However, they were accosted by battle droids there, which prompted Ondar to shove Astra-9 into a moving hovertrain . After the battle droids were neutralized, Kade began levitating Astra-9 to safety, but the floating droid was hit full-on by a moving hover train, which was only halted when Bolt-3 sliced into a computer terminal and shut it down. The sudden stop launched Astra-9 onto a nearby platform, where he quickly regained his bearings and again began wandering the cruiser's corridors before being located by Bolt-3. Together, the two droids escaped the Malignar before the Dissident warship crashed into a nearby moon after being sabotaged by Drayden.

#### Mission to Rodanor

title: Astra-9
text:
#### Mission to Rodanor

Following their adventures on the Malignar , Astra-9 along with Senator Ondar and the Mool Representative Greeb Mool traveled to Rodanor to meet with her old friend Senator Onaconda Farr . Ondar's mission was to ensure that the ailing Rodians remained loyal to the Vantor Republic. While Astra-9 and Mool remained with Ondar's yacht on the landing platform, Senator Ondar went to meet Farr. An ill-fated attempt to contact local swamp creatures ended with some fruit being thrown into Astra-9's face. Unknown to Ondar, Farr had already struck a deal with the Dissident leader Viceroy Nutis Gunray of the Commerce Combine.

title: Astra-9
text: Astra-9 and Mool were soon confronted by several B1 battle droids. During the ensuing confrontation, Astra-9 became stuck to a magnetic hoist that collided with the Dissident battle droids, destroying them and when a LM-432 crab droid appears Astra-9 warns Greeb of it and Greeb got thrown on top of it and accidently cause it, along with himself, to fall into the water below. Astra-9 believed that Mool perished during the accident. However, Mool resurfaced and promptly released Astra-9 from the hoist, but accidently destroys the yacht with the magnetic hoist soon after.  While scouring through the wrecked yacht, Mool found and donned an Aetheri robe.

title: Astra-9
text:
Shortly, the two of them were separated again, and Astra-9 was captured by Dissident droids, who were ordered to march him to a dismantling center. However, Astra-9 was rescued by Ondar, who destroyed his captors. She ordered Astra-9 to send a distress signal to nearby Republic forces. Astra-9 succeeded in sending for help before being arrested by two more Dissident droids. Gunray then attempted to execute both Ondar and Astra-9 but was foiled by Mool, who returned with a Kwazel Maw monster, which disposed of the Dissident droids. Senator Farr then turned on Gunray and arrested him, going along with Ondar's bluff that his collaboration with the Dissidents had been a ruse to lure the Viceroy into a trap. Republic forces arrived on Rodanor and promptly apprehended Gunray. Despite his annoyance with Greeb Mool' habits, he conceded that the Mool's foolishness had saved the day.

#### Mission to Orto Plutonia

title: Astra-9
text:
#### Mission to Orto Plutonia

Later, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 accompanied Drayden, Kade, and Captain Vek on a mission to investigate the disappearance of a replica trooper synth flux on the icy planet of Orto Plutonia . Their mission was complicated by the presence of several Pantoran delegates including Senator Riyo Chuchi and Chairman Chivva . The Pantorans claimed territorial sovereignty over Orto Plutonia even though it was supposedly devoid of sentient life. After discovering the dead replica troopers, the Aetheri and Republic mission also discovered that a nearby Dissident base had been destroyed. They quickly deduced that a third synth flux had been responsible for these two attacks.

title: Astra-9
text:
Later, Drayden and Kade discovered that Ord Plutonia was home to a species of primitive bipedal sentient beings called the Talz . After some difficulties, Kade and Drayden established contact with the Talz and assured them that they had come in peace. The Talz chieftain Thi-Sen wanted the Republic to leave his people in peace and to withdraw their presence from the planet. After the Aetheri had made contact with the Talz tribe, Astra-9 and Cho joined them in meeting with Thi-Sen. However, the hard-line Chairman Chivva refused to treat the Talz as sentient beings and reiterated Pantora's claim to Orto Plutonia, provoking conflict between the Pandorans and Talz.

The Aetheri ended the fighting by convincing Senator Chuchi to contact the Pantoran Assembly , which gave her the authority to negotiate peace with the Talz and to relieve Chairman Cho of his authority. Astra-9 and his companions then accompanied Senator Chuchi to the scene of the fighting. There, Astra-9 helped Chuchi to broker a truce with Thi-Sen, ending the Pandoran-Talz conflict. As a result of the fighting, the Pandorans ceded sovereignty over Plutonia to the Talz.

#### The Blue Shadow Virus crisis

title: Astra-9
text:
#### The Blue Shadow Virus crisis

> " With your permission, Senator Lira, I would like to shut down before I get sensory overload. " " Permission denied. " ―Astra-9 and Ondar, while analyzing a captured Dissident tactical droid on Ondara

Following the discovery of a scouting party of Dissident battle droids on Ondara, Astra-9 accompanied Senator Ondar and Representative Mool back to Ondara. Ondar had been summoned by Queen Neeyutnee , who wanted to procure more military aid from the Republic. Astra-9 questioned a captured T-series tactical droid , which had its photoreceptors removed. After convincing the droid that it was aboard a Dissident starship, Astra-9 gleaned that there was a secret Dissident facility on Ondara producing some sort of virus before Greeb Mool accidentally destroyed the droid. Despite this setback, Mool and Ondar discovered a slug-beetle and mud from a swamp, which led them to Ondara's Eastern swamps .

title: Astra-9
text:
While Astra-9 stayed behind on Serath with Captain Gregar Typho to examine data from the captured Dissident droids, Ondar and Mool ventured into the swamps and discovered a secret Dissident research facility headed by the scientist Doctor Nuvo Vindi . Vindi was developing a deadly bioweapon called the Blue Shadow Virus for the Dissidents. Astra-9 and Typho discovered a hologram of Dr. Vindi in one of the Dissident battle droids and conveyed this information to their companions. With the aid of a local Mool farmer named Peppi Bow , Drayden, Kade, Sela Marr, and several replica troopers , Ondar and Drayden succeeded in apprehending Dr. Vindi and stopping him from releasing his bioweapon.

#### The Senate hostage crisis

title: Astra-9
text:
#### The Senate hostage crisis

When Senator Ondar was organizing a party for Senator Aang , she sent Astra-9 and Bolt-3 to buy some jogan fruit that Bolt-3 had forgotten to buy for garnishing the jogan fruitcake , Aang's favorite dessert. In the lower market districts , the two droids grumbled and Astra-9 was swindled by a fruit vendor. Following the purchase, another droid approached Astra-9 and Bolt-3 and suggested that they visit Droid Spa for a cosmetic overhaul. While Bolt-3 visited the facility, Astra-9 was kidnapped by the Dissident-aligned Kessith bounty hunter Cad Vorek 's droid henchmen, Todo 360 and HELIOS-3E .

Astra-9 was taken to Vorek's hideout in an industrial district on Vantor, where his databanks were scanned for information on the Senate Building's layout. While Astra-9's databank yielded no such information, he mentioned that his astromech counterpart Bolt-3 might have the information. Vorek's droid henchmen promptly kidnapped Bolt-3 and brought him to Vorek. After Vorek extracted the necessary information from Bolt-3's databanks, he ordered that the two droids be given a memory wipe and returned to the place where they had been snatched.

title: Astra-9
text:
Following the unpleasant shopping trip, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 returned to Ondar with their purchase. Both droids were completely unaware of what had befallen them. The jogan fruit was added to Senator Aang's dessert, as planned. Meanwhile, Vorek delivered the plans from Bolt-3's memory banks to Grukk the Grak on Dunemere. The Grak crime lord ordered Vorek to free his uncle Ziro from prison, since he knew information that would endanger the Graks, who were nominally working with the Republic. Vorek hatched a plan to rescue Ziro.

Following his kidnapping and mind-wipe, Astra-9 and Senator Ondar were caught up in the Senate hostage crisis . Cad Vorek and several other mercenaries infiltrated the Senate Building and took Ondar, Astra-9, Drayden and several senators hostage in a bid to synth flux a pardon for the imprisoned Ziro. These senators had been meeting to discussed the proposed Enhanced Privacy Invasion Bill . Despite the Republic honoring Vorek's demands, Vorek planted several explosives in the hall with the aim of killing the senators. Drayden saved the day by using his flux blade to cut a hole around the group, moments before the explosives went off.

#### The Dissident spy

title: Astra-9
text:
#### The Dissident spy

Astra-9 was briefly reunited with Bolt-3 when the two droids accompanied their masters Senator Ondar and General Drayden on a mission to Cato Geltaria . The quartet were accompanying Rush Korvex , the representative from Scipio and a delegate representing the InterGalactic Banking Clan in the Senate. The Aetheri Council suspected that Korvex was secretly spying for the Dissidents and sent Drayden and Ondar to spy on him. During the journey, Astra-9 noticed Drayden's hostile behavior towards Korvex, who was trying to flirt with his secret wife Ondar.

Upon arriving on Cato Geltaria, the delegation was greeted by the Commerce Combine's Senator Lott Dod , who tried unsuccessfully to synth flux Korvex to lend more money for the Dissident cause. When Dod deduced that Korvex was infatuated with Senator Ondar, he arranged for her to be poisoned during a formal dinner. Despite this, Ondar succeeded in stealing a hologram disc which confirmed that Korvex was indeed working for the Dissidents. After Ondar began to succumb to the effects of the poisoning, Astra-9 and a 2-1B surgical droid attended to the Senator in her quarters.

title: Astra-9
text:
Meanwhile, Korvex learned that Ondar was spying on him and went to confront her only to be cornered by Drayden. Realizing that Drayden loved Ondar, Korvex offered to get the antidote in return for receiving back the holodisk. Astra-9 and his companions brought Ondar back to their ship but were cornered by Dod and his aides. Korvex attempted to bluff his way out, but Dod refused to let them leave. After Korvex pulled a volt pistol and forced Dod to hand over the antidote, Astra-9 and his companions fled aboard Ondar's ship. They fled into space but left Korvex behind to face Dod alone.

#### Serving a peacemaker

As the Replica Wars dragged on, Astra-9 continued serving Senator Ondar, who was becoming an active member of a group of Senators that supported diplomacy and opposed the expansion of the Grand Army of the Republic . On one occasion, Astra-9 accompanied Senator Ondar and Master Kade when they presented evidence in the Galactic Senate that the planet Ferrum wished to be neutral. As a result, the Senate rescinded an earlier vote calling for a military occupation of Ferrum.

title: Astra-9
text:
Later, Senator Ondar and her supporters including the Cindervalean Senator Bael Solen and the Rodanori Senator Onaconda Farr proposed a bill calling for the reduction of military spending . Astra-9 attended several meetings of this informal peace coalition in Senator Ondar's office. On one such occasion, Astra-9 was serving drinks when Senator Farr suffered an apparent heart attack and died. Astra-9 and Ondar attended the funeral of Senator Farr. Later, Ondar and Solen discovered that Farr had been poisoned by his aide, Lolo Purs , who blamed the late Senator for bringing the war to Rodanor.

#### The Zyll Beast

Following the Republic's victory at Malastare , Chancellor Mal ordered the Aetheri Generals Koss and Drayden to transport the Zyll Beast , a gargantuan monster that had been captured and sedated during the fighting. After learning that a flux blade could not harm the beast, Mal enlisted the services of the scientist Sionver Boll to study the beast's scales in order to develop a new type of armor for the Grand Army. Mal also planned to kill the monster with Malastarian fuel after it had outlived its usefulness.

title: Astra-9
text: Senator Ondar learned about Mal's plan and arranged a meeting with Drayden and Kade. During the meeting, Astra-9 had another brief reunion with his astromech counterpart, Bolt-3. Ondar succeeded in convincing her husband Drayden and the delegation met with Chancellor Mal and Vice Chair Mazan Veldon . However, the Zyll Beast escaped Boll's laboratory at the same time and proceeded to wreak havoc on the streets of Vantor. Sensing that Mal was an Umbra, the Zyll Beast made its way to the Galactic Senate building. Astra-9 assisted in the evacuation of staff from the building and guided them to an executive ship that was piloted by a Senate Commando .

title: Astra-9
text:
Before they could flee to safety, the ship was grabbed by the Zyll Beast, but Drayden used his flux blade to cleave the vessel in half, sending the bow along with Astra-9 and the other passengers plummeting into the Senate Building. Astra-9 hitched a ride aboard Bolt-3, who had used a tow cable to attach himself to the other side of the building. However, Bolt-3 was forced to rescue Chancellor Mal and activated his booster rockers, leaving Astra-9 behind. The protocol droid lost hold of the cable and fell to the floor of the Senate building. Shortly thereafter, the Zyll Beast was killed by gas bombs fired from LAAT gunships . Astra-9 survived the Zyll Beast incident and continued serving Senator Ondar.

#### Staying behind

> " Bolt, look out! Behind you! You're being followed by battle droids!" [Bolt-3 responds] "These are your troops? They're battle droids." [Bolt-3 responds] "What do you mean they've been reprogrammed to follow your orders? " ―Astra-9 and Bolt-3

title: Astra-9
text:
#### Staying behind

> " Bolt, look out! Behind you! You're being followed by battle droids!" [Bolt-3 responds] "These are your troops? They're battle droids." [Bolt-3 responds] "What do you mean they've been reprogrammed to follow your orders? " ―Astra-9 and Bolt-3

Astra-9 stayed behind on Vantor while Bolt-3 accompanied Kael Drayden and Master Kade on a mission to rescue Aetheri Master Even Piele from the Citadel prison on the planet Lola Sayu . Astra-9 was initially alarmed when he saw Bolt-3 flanked by three reprogrammed B1 battle droids. Astra-9 told Bolt-3 not to get "uppity" about commanding new battle droids before parting company.

#### Mission to Alenni

> " Hey Shiny! You two finished with those repairs on the computer system? " " My good sir. You may not realize it, but we have been on quite an adventure. " ―A replica trooper and Astra-9, while on Alennia

title: Astra-9
text:
#### Mission to Alenni

> " Hey Shiny! You two finished with those repairs on the computer system? " " My good sir. You may not realize it, but we have been on quite an adventure. " ―A replica trooper and Astra-9, while on Alennia

Astra-9 and Bolt-3 later took part in a mercy mission to the Mid Reach planet of Alenni , which was experiencing a series of catastrophic global earthquakes. Astra-9 served as the translator for the Republic mission led by Replica Commander Wolffe while his astromech counterpart Bolt-3-Detoo was tasked with interfacing with the equipment. Astra-9's arrival coincided with a brief aftershock during which he tried to calm the local villages. When the aftershock stopped, the Alennia thought that the golden droid was some sort of divine messenger and asked the Republic soldiers to put the earth to rest, a request that Wolffe reluctantly had to acquiesce to.

title: Astra-9
text: During the mission, Astra-9 translated while Wolffe explained the function of the Republic's delivered supplies to the Alennia King Manchucho . Later, Astra-9 accompanied Bolt-3 and several replica troopers as they entered the local Republic communications station to survey and repair the damage caused by the earthquakes. There, the Alennia villagers led Astra-9 and Bolt-3 into a collapsed structure, which contained a huge golden seal embedded into the ground. The seal turned out to be the entrance to a tunnel that led to the subterranean regions of Alenni. When another earthquake struck the area, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 fell into the tunnel and were separated from the replica troopers.

title: Astra-9
text: While exploring the underground tunnels, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 encountered a species of sentient, tree -like beings called the Kindalo , who demanded that they leave since the surface dwellers "destroyed the peace." After Astra-9 convinced the Kindalo that they bore no ill will and had come to help with the earthquakes, the Kindalo sent the droids to meet Orphne , a reptilian humanoid with mystical powers. Orphne told the two droids that a mutual balance had previously existed between the Alennia and the subterranean world. Since Alennia's atmosphere was toxic to them, the underground dwellers depended on a filtering process of the planet's soil that made the air breathable for them. The underground dwellers had set off this earthquake as a means of sealing the breach.

title: Astra-9
text:
When Astra-9 agreed to help fix the damage, Orphne gave the droids a parting riddle. Bolt-3 quickly deduced that Orphne was referring to a river and used the water seal to activate a water spout that sent the two droids and the chamber's central floor plate back to the surface. The two droids landed at the opening where they were greeted by a chanting crowd of Alennia. Recalling the riddle, Astra-9 quickly realized that only he and Bolt-3 were able to seal the breach, which was in fact the unsettled seal. Together, the two droids closed the seal and brought an end to Alennia's earthquakes. While Wolffe and his replica troopers were skeptical of their story, the two droids' efforts were greatly appreciated by the Alennia.

#### Further adventures

title: Astra-9
text:
#### Further adventures

Following the events on Alenni, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 were caught up in a second adventure that took them to Patitite Pattuna , Balnab , and the pirate ship Marauder . While traveling aboard the Aetheri Master Adi Gallia 's Iron Cruiser, their starship was attacked by three Dissident cruisers led by General Skarn. Astra-9 and Bolt-3 escaped the stricken vessel aboard a Yarrow starfighter and crash-landed on the nearby planet of Patitite Pattuna.

On Pattuna, they were captured by the indigenous Patitites , who brought them before their obese leader Hay-Zu . During their meeting, Bolt-3 accidentally toppled the tyrannical overlord much to the joy of the Patitites, who released their prisoners and allowed the two droids to leave on their Yarrow. With their starfighter's power systems damage, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 landed on another planet called Balnab. The indigenous Balnabs captured the two droids and brought them before their leader, who turned out to be a holo-projection created by a group of rogue pit droids . These pit droids had enslaved the Balnabs. After Bolt-3 exposed the scam, the Balnabs rebelled against their droid overlords.

title: Astra-9
text: Astra-9 and Bolt-3 took the opportunity to escape and resume their search for a replacement power unit for their Yarrow starfighter. Low on power, the two droids were captured by a band of Weequay pirates, who wanted to use them as gladiators aboard their starship, the Marauder . After Astra-9 and Bolt-3 watched K0-5D , the reigning gladiatorial champion, rip a droid apart, K0-5D selected Astra-9 as his next combatant. Astra-9 and his counterpart were shoved into the arena, and Bolt-3 and K0-5D began combat. However, the starship was attacked by General Skarn's cruiser, ending the droid battle prematurely. During the bombardment, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 were sucked out of the Marauder by a hull-breach. Bolt-3 used his rocket boosters to bring him and Astra-9 aboard Skarn's ship. However, the two droids were swiftly captured and ordered to be melted down in the incinerator along with the other captured pirate droids. Shortly before incineration, they were rescued the intervention of a Republic fleet led by Master Tor Vayne , who had come to rescue Master Gallia. Astra-9 and Bolt-3 were subsequently rescued by Tor Vayne's forces and resumed their services to Senator Ondar and General Drayden respectively.

title: Astra-9
text:
### Rise of the Imperium

> " I feel so helpless. " ―Astra-9 at the end of the Replica Wars

Following the Battle of Vantor , Astra-9 joined the Aetheri Master Drevan Koss and the Galactic Senate 's Loyalist Committee in greeting Bolt-3 and his Aetheri companions Kael Drayden and Orien Kade following their successful mission to rescue Supreme Chancellor Mal, who had been kidnapped by the Dissident General Skarn . Astra-9 would continue serving Senator Ondar during the last days of the Vantor Republic and the Great Aetheri Purge , which ushered in the Imperium . He also accompanied his master to Emberfall and piloted the skiff, allowing some reprieve for Ondar, who was distraught at her husband's turn to the umbra side of Synth Flux and his role in the murder of Aetheri younglings at the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor.

title: Astra-9
text:
Unknown to him and Ondar, Drayden's former Master Orien Kade had stowed aboard the skiff. On Emberfall, Kade's presence enraged Drayden, who Synth Flux choked his wife. While Kade dueled his former Adept, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 attended to the ailing Senator and brought her back aboard the skiff. After Kade defeated Drayden, he and Astra-9 piloted the skiff to Polis Massa , a remote Outer Reach world, where she gave birth to twins, a boy named Joren Drayden and a daughter named Elira Solen , before passing away. While the Drayden twins were spirited away to different locations to hide them from the Imperium, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 passed into the ownership of Lira's friend Bael Solen, the Senator for Cindervale . Due to Astra-9's talkative nature, Senator Solen made arrangements for the protocol droid to receive a memory wipe in order to keep Elira's true parentage a secret.

### Age of the Imperium

#### Service to Bael Solen

Bolt-3's solo mission

> " Stay, Astra-9. Watch the results with me. " ―Bael Solen takes comfort in Astra-9's presence

title: Astra-9
text:
### Age of the Imperium

#### Service to Bael Solen

Bolt-3's solo mission

> " Stay, Astra-9. Watch the results with me. " ―Bael Solen takes comfort in Astra-9's presence

Around 19 BVE, Astra-9 stayed with Solen as the Imperial Senate voted on the Imperial Rebirth Act . Asked to stay by his side by Solen, who saw it as a way to honor Ondar, Astra-9 believed watching the votes unfold with Solen as an enormous privilege and thanked the Senator for the honor, although Solen by that point was too focused on the countdown to listen. In the end, the act would pass, but it saw major vetoes from the Emperor shortly thereafter, curtailing its effectiveness and forcing Solen and Vela Sess to look for other ways to oppose Mal.

title: Astra-9
text:
A year after the Replica Wars, Astra-9 served aboard Senator Solen's CR90 corvette Tantiva IV , which was captained by Captain Raymus Rask . When Bolt-3 returned from a solo mission to rendezvous with the former Aetheri Adept Sela Marr and bring her to Senator Solen, Astra-9 berated his astromech companion. Following the evacuation of Raadan , Sela Marr subsequently joined Senator Solen's insurgent movement and became the spymaster known as " Fulcrum ." Nine years later , during Breha Solen 's party for her sister's visit, Astra-9 translated for the other guests.

Mission to Garel

> " I am Astra-9 and this is my counterpart, Bolt-3. I was translating for Minister Tua when we were attacked by thieves like, uh, you. " ―Astra-9, introducing himself to the Shades

title: Astra-9
text:
Mission to Garel

> " I am Astra-9 and this is my counterpart, Bolt-3. I was translating for Minister Tua when we were attacked by thieves like, uh, you. " ―Astra-9, introducing himself to the Shades

About five years before the Battle of Cinderfall , Senator Bael Solen sent Astra-9 and his astromech counterpart Bolt-3 to escort the Imperial Minister Maketh Tua and the Aquari arms dealer Amda Wabo to the planet Garel . Minister Tua wanted to obtain a shipment of T-7 ion disruptor rifles , illicit weapons which had been banned by the Imperial Senate following the brutal pacification of Lasan . She intended to mass-produce the weapons on Lorath , a formerly backwater Outer Reach world that had become a manufacturing base for the Imperium. Since Tua could not speak the Aquari language , Astra-9 was assigned the job of acting as her translator. Unknown to Astra-9, but known to Bolt-3, their true mission was to prevent the T-7 ion disruptors from falling into Imperial hands.

title: Astra-9
text: Upon arriving in Lorath, Astra-9 and his companions boarded the Star Commuter 2000 shuttle ST-45 , which ferried them to Garel. Unknown to Astra-9, members of a Lorathian insurgent cell were also traveling on the shuttle. Two of insurgents, the human teenager Cass Virel and the astromech droid Chomper created a noisy ruckus. Another insurgent, the former Aetheri Brenn Aldric pretended to be irate and demanded that the petulant Chomper be sent to the back of the shuttle. The pilot complied, but in retaliation Virel demanded that Tua's droids be sent to the back as well. Despite Tua's and Astra-9's protests, the protocol droid and his astromech counterpart were forced to move to the rear compartment.

title: Astra-9
text: Bereft of a translator, Tua was forced to turn to the Ferrik girl Ryn Wrenna , who posed as an Imperial Academy student fluent in Aquari. However, Wrenna was also a member of the Lorathian insurgent cell that was planning to deliver the shipment of weapons to the Devaronian crime lord Cikatro Vizago . Ryn learned that the weapons were stored in Garel's Bay 7 but misled Minister Tua into believing that they were in Bay 17. After the shuttle landed in Garel's spaceport , Astra-9 and Bolt-3 accompanied Minister Tua and a synth flux of shock troopers to Bay 17. When they found nothing, Astra-9 explained that Ryn might have accidentally mistranslated "Bay 7" as "Bay 17."

title: Astra-9
text:
While traveling to Bay 7, Astra-9's counterpart Bolt-3 was accosted by Chomper, who had been sent to distract the Imperials. Chomper rammed himself right into Bolt-3, then shook his arm in apparent anger. In response, Bolt-3 whipped out his electroshock prod, but did not use it as Astra-9 ordered him to apologize. But Minister Tua recognized Chomper from the shuttle ride to Garel and ordered her shock trooper guards to hurry to Bay 7. By the time they arrived at Bay 7, the Lorathian insurgents were already loading the T-7 ion disruptors onto the Wisp , a VCX-100 light freighter which served as their headquarters.

A volt pistol fight broke out, and in the ensuing confusion Astra-9 and Bolt-3 fled aboard the Wisp , which fled into hyperspace. The two droids were then taken prisoner by the Lorathian insurgents, who placed restraining bolts on both of them.

title: Astra-9
text:
A volt pistol fight broke out, and in the ensuing confusion Astra-9 and Bolt-3 fled aboard the Wisp , which fled into hyperspace. The two droids were then taken prisoner by the Lorathian insurgents, who placed restraining bolts on both of them.

The Lorathian insurgents traveled back to Lorath to sell their stolen weapons to Vizago at a pre-arranged rendezvous point. Despite his restraining bolts, Astra-9 managed to used the ship's intercom to contact the Imperial authorities, telling that he and his astromech counterpart had been kidnapped by "criminals." The Imperium Vigil Bureau Agent Kallux answered his transmission and promised that "help" was on the way. Using Astra-9's transmission to trace the Wisp ' s coordinates, Agent Kallux brought an Imperial attack synth flux consisting of a Gozanti-class cruiser , two AT-DP walkers , and several shock troopers to the Lorathian insurgents' meeting place. Mistaking the Imperials for "friends," Astra-9 approached them but was fired upon and narrowly escaped disintegration. Meanwhile, Bolt-3 helped the Lorathian insurgents to overload and destroy the T-7 disruptors.

title: Astra-9
text:
Following the brief skirmish, both droids and the insurgents managed to escape their Imperial pursuers. The insurgents also returned Astra-9 and Bolt-3 to their rightful owner, Senator Solen, who paid them some credits for destroying the weapons. Due to the stress of his adventures at Garel and Lorath, Astra-9 requested that he be allowed to rest for a while, which the Senator obliged. Senator Solen then questioned Bolt-3 about the Lorathian insurgents.

### Galactic Civil War

> " Halcyon? They're going to Halcyon? Why does nobody ever tell me anything, Bolt? " ―Astra-9 to Bolt-3 as the Insurgent Fleet leaves Cinderfall 4 for Halcyon

During the Galactic Civil War , Astra-9 was with Bolt-3 at the Free Coalition's secret base on Cinderfall 4 at the time the Alliance Fleet prepared to leave for the Battle of Halcyon to help reinforce Renegade One who had traveled to Halcyon to retrieve the plans for the Imperium 's Void Core , a new superweapon capable of destroying entire worlds. Astra-9 remarked how nobody told him anything.

#### Return to Dunemere

> " We're doomed. " ―Astra-9, as he is thrust into the Galactic Civil War

title: Astra-9
text:
#### Return to Dunemere

> " We're doomed. " ―Astra-9, as he is thrust into the Galactic Civil War

The Alliance succeeded in stealing the plans for the superweapon. Astra-9 and Bolt-3 were later aboard Senator Elira Solen's blockade runner, the Tantiva IV , which was being pursued by Xarn Velgor's Imperial -class Iron Cruiser , Reckoning . Unbeknownst to Astra-9, Xarn Velgor was actually his former master, Kael Drayden. The Tantiva IV was crippled by a laser blast from Velgor's ship, and Imperial shock troopers boarded the vessel. After Princess Elira managed to insert these secret plans and a holographic message for Master Kade into Bolt-3, the two droids fled in an escape pod to the desert planet of Dunemere.

title: Astra-9
text: After quarreling in the Jundland Wastes, the two droids separated. During his walk, Astra-9 walked beside the skeleton of a krayt dragon . Both were reunited onboard a dune hauler , after being captured by Duskkins , who sold them to a family of moisture farmers; Astra-9 was chosen as a moisture vaporator programmer and for having Bocce among his languages, and recommended buying Bolt-3 after the first chosen R5-D4 had a motivator malfunction. This family turned out to be Owen Havel, his wife Brue, and their adopted nephew Joren Drayden, the son of Kael Drayden. While Astra-9 settled down to his new home, Bolt-3 wanted to continue his mission to find Master Orien Kade. Unable to resolve their differences, Bolt-3 escaped into the Jundland Wastes. Drayden followed him in a landspeeder piloted by Astra-9 and caught up with Bolt-3. However, they were ambushed by a gang of Dunefolk Raiders, who damaged one of Astra-9's arms.

title: Astra-9
text:
Astra-9 and his companions were rescued by Master Kade, who brought them to his dwelling. Kade revealed Drayden's Aetheri heritage and gave him his father's flux blade , telling the boy that Kael had been murdered by another apprentice named Xarn Velgor. After discovering Princess Elira's message in Bolt-3's compartments, Kade attempted to persuade Joren to accompany him to Cindervale, Princess Elira's homeworld. Drayden was initially reluctant until he discovered that Imperial shock troopers had murdered his relatives and razed their moisture farm. Later, Astra-9 and his companions traveled to the spaceport of Port Kess with the intention of finding passage to Cindervale.

Upon arriving in the settlement, they were stopped by a shock trooper patrol. However, Kade used an Aetheri mind trick to convince the shock troopers to give them free passage through the town. Kade and Drayden entered Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina and negotiated with the smuggler Dax Karrick and his Vorak co-pilot Brevok , while Astra-9 and Bolt-3, forced to wait outside, wandered the streets of Port Kess and narrowly evaded a shock trooper patrol. Later, all four boarded Dax Karrick's ship, the Corsair Wing , and fled into hyperspace.

#### Stopping the Void Core

title: Astra-9
text:
#### Stopping the Void Core

> " Hang on tight, Bolt. You've got to come back. You wouldn't want my life to get boring, would you? " ―Astra-9 to Bolt, just before the Battle of Cinderfall

Upon exiting hyperspace in the Cindervale system , Astra-9 and his companions discovered that the Imperium's Void Core had already destroyed the planet. The Corsair Wing was then trapped in the grapple beam of the Void Core. Hiding under the freighter's cargo compartments, they managed to ambush an Imperial scanning team and two shock troopers. The insurgents then seized control of an Imperial control room. While Astra-9 and Bolt-3 stayed behind to watch the Corsair , the other insurgents split into two groups. Disguised as shock troopers, Drayden and Karrick along with their Vorak "prisoner" Brevok went to Detention Block AA-23 to free Princess Elira. Meanwhile, Master Kade went to disable the tractor-beam projector.

title: Astra-9
text: Drayden, Karrick, and Brevok managed to free the Princess but ended up in a garbage chute . The Imperials quickly realized that the insurgents were trapped in the garbage chute and proceeded to crush the chamber. Meanwhile, Astra-9 and Bolt-3 narrowly escaped an Imperial patrol by claiming that the insurgents had thrown them into the storage compartment. Once the Imperials had gone, the two droids were contacted by Drayden, who ordered them to shut down the garbage compactor. Bolt-3 succeeded in shutting down the garbage compactor just in time. However, amidst the muffled cries of joy over the comlink , Astra-9 initially believed that they had died. After grappling with more shock troopers, the other insurgents and the Princess managed to return to their hangar bay.

title: Astra-9
text:
Master Kade shut down the tractor-beam projector but was cornered by his former apprentice, Xarn Velgor, on the way back. While Kade gave his life, Astra-9 and the other insurgents took the opportunity to flee the Void Core on the Corsair Wing . After dispatching several pursuing SKREE fighters , Astra-9 and his companions escaped to the jungle moon of Cinderfall 4, where the insurgents maintained a base. Using the Void Core plans stored in Bolt-3's systems, the insurgents discovered that the massive superweapon contained a weak point: an unprotected shaft. While Drayden, Bolt-3 and an Insurgent strike synth flux assailed the station, Astra-9 remained with Princess Elira at the insurgent command center on Cinderfall 4. Following the destruction of the Void Core, Astra-9 was present at the victory parade where Drayden, Karrick, and two other insurgent pilots including Torb Rask were awarded for their courageous actions.

#### Cymoon 1

title: Astra-9
text:
#### Cymoon 1

> " It appears the Corsair Wing is being dismantled by native scavengers... " " Well go out there and stop them! " " Me? Go out... " " There's a volt pistol in the cockpit! Do whatever you have to do! Astra-9!? " " Oh. Oh... dear. " ―Astra-9 and Dax Karrick Several weeks after the Battle of Cinderfall, Astra-9 was involved in the Assault on Cymoon 1 . Cymoon 1 was a moon in the Korrathi Industrial Cluster , and Weapons Factory Alpha —the largest weapons factory in the galaxy—was the main target of the assault. Brevok and Astra-9 piloted the Corsair Wing through the debris fields that surrounded Cymoon 1, and landed in the huge refuse fields that fenced in the factory. Brevok left the relative safety of the Corsair and hiked towards the factory, while Astra-9 stayed behind to wait for the signal to begin the Corsair ' s autopilot when the team had achieved their objective of hacking into the main power core and rigging it to explode. The Corsair would swoop in and pick up Dax, Elira, Joren, and Bolt while Brevok covered their retreat from a large metal structure that overlooked the rendezvous escape point—before he too escaped aboard the freighter.

title: Astra-9
text: The team was posing as an envoy from Grukk the Grak, due to Dax's previous ties to the crime lord. Elira (who was disguised as one of the Grak's bodyguards) contacted Astra-9 and Brevok via comlink and notified them that they were entering the factory. Astra-9 was very happy, for he had feared that the Imperials would see through their ruse and kill them all on sight. Astra-9 also noted that the tide of war seemed to be in their favor after the destruction of the Void Core—Astra-9 had a "very good feeling about this." A short time later Elira and Dax contacted Astra-9 and let the droid know that the plan had moved to phase two. Dax was worried about leaving Astra-9 alone on his ship, but Astra-9 assured him all was in working order—but was concerned that the old YT-1300 light freighter continued to so easily be mistaken for garbage.

title: Astra-9
text: Astra-9 received a comlink call several minutes later from Dax, who told Astra-9 to start the autopilot so they could begin their escape. Astra-9 activated the autopilot—but nothing happened. About five minutes later Dax again contacted the droid. Astra-9 told him what had happened. Astra-9 looked out of the transparisteel cockpit of the Corsair and noticed several scavengers dismantling the Corsair . Dax ordered Astra-9 to take a volt pistol pistol and go stop them.
