#### Battle against the Benathy

> " I remember when another like you came here with demands. He was taller. Far more impressive. He killed our last king. But even he could not stand against our god. " ―King Kristoff, to Zarrin Karrick on Velgor's attempt to subdue the Benathy

Around 15 BVE , Velgor and his men fought against the Benathy in Wild Space . The imperial army consisted of at least several thousand shock troopers, Ironclad Walker walkers, AT-STs, SKREE fighters, and SKREE bombers. While thousands died on both sides, Velgor managed to kill the king of the Benathy. Velgor ordered his troops to attack and despite the high amount of casualties, he did not retreat. The attacking synth flux was only stopped by a Zyll Beast the Benathy saw as their god. However, Velgor managed to subdue the Benathy anyways.

#### Insurgency on Selvara

Preparing for the operation

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
#### Insurgency on Selvara

Preparing for the operation

> " Are you testing me, Master? " " Testing you? Is that how you perceive things? " " Am I wrong? " " We are, all of us, always being tested, my friend. Tests make us stronger, and strength is power, and power is the point . We must pass all the tests we face. Or die in the effort. " ―Xarn Velgor and Vael Mal Five years into the Age of the Imperium , Velgor, while meditating aboard the Perilous , was informed by Captain Luitt of an attack on the Yaga Minor shipyards . The attack had been staged by several dozen members of the Free Selvara Movement , a primarily Velari insurgency intent on liberating their homeworld from the rule of the Imperium. The insurgents hijacked an Imperial weapons transport, and Velgor led a squadron of Vireo starfighters in pursuit. After a long chase, during which the transport fled through hyperspace to several different systems, its engines overloaded when it attempted to make yet another jump and Velgor's squadron was finally able to engage it. The squadron brought down the transport's shields with minimal casualties while Velgor crippled the engines.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Though the squadron commander suggested allowing the Perilous to tractor the transport into one of its hangar bays when it arrived, Velgor assumed (correctly) that the insurgents planned to destroy the transport by detonating the heavy ordnance present in the ship's cargo bays. In order to prevent this eventuality, Velgor crashed his black Eta-2 Actis -class light interceptor into one of its gun bubbles and ejected just before the collision. He then entered the ship through the damaged gun emplacement and proceeded to kill all of the insurgent Velaris on the ship. After eliminating the insurgent leader Pok , Velgor noticed an active comlink on the bridge. Assuming that another insurgent ship was nearby, Velgor had his Vireos fan out in a search pattern, but the insurgent ship escaped detection by shutting down nearly all of its systems and hiding in the rings of a nearby planet. Finding nothing, Velgor had the Perilous collect the transport, and returned to Vantor.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: In the Imperial Palace, Velgor reunited with his master. There, he and Mal met with Selvara's Senator Orn Free Taa involving the inconvenience that was the Free Selvara Movement. The movement, though relatively minor, had been conducting raids on Imperial shipping facilities and transports and had seriously impacted the flow of Spice from the planet. As such, Mal believed that the situation warranted his personal attention, and decided that he, Taa, and Velgor would travel to Selvara for a state visit . After informing the Senator of the planned journey and dismissing him, Mal informed his apprentice that Taa almost certainly had a traitor in the midst of his support staff who was feeding the movement classified information on Imperial doings.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Though Velgor understood his master's purpose in acting as bait alongside himself and Taa, he saw no reason why the Emperor should potentially risk his own safety over such a minor issue. Rather, Velgor advocated for simply killing Taa and his entire staff, thereby guaranteeing the elimination of the traitor. However, Mal wished to eliminate the roots of the treachery, and not simply the lone traitor in Taa's staff. To that end, Mal gave the order for Moff Delian Mors to be informed that Taa would be arriving for a state visit, but stipulated that she should not be told that either he or Velgor would be accompanying the Senator. In this way, Mal hoped to provide further encouragement for the movement to attack, as he assumed that they would discover his and Velgor's plans via their spies. Ten days later Velgor, the Emperor, Taa, and a contingent of Royal Guards journeyed to the Selvara system aboard the Perilous .

Assassination attempt on the Defiance

> " This guy again. I don't care if you kill me. " ―Commandant Pell Baylo, to Xarn Velgor

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Assassination attempt on the Defiance

> " This guy again. I don't care if you kill me. " ―Commandant Pell Baylo, to Xarn Velgor

While traveling from Vantor to Selvara, the Emperor ordered the Perilous to stop in the Denon system to consult with several navy chiefs on how to better integrate disparate naval academies into one Imperial Naval Academy . The Emperor ordered Velgor to oversee a training session conducted by Commandant Pell Baylo on the Defiance while the Emperor met with his naval chiefs in Baylo's office on the training ship. It was during this training session that Velgor began to believe that Mal was treating him much the same way the Aetheri Council had previously: acting as he knew better, keeping information from Velgor, giving him "busywork." Baylo ordered the Defiance to enter hyperspace on a course for Krestophis. Cadet Raena Vexana entered the coordinates, only to have her hyperspace path overridden by Baylo, who said she was going to send them too close to a singularity.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Vexana studied the path, suspecting that Baylo was incorrect in his adjustment. Velgor and Vexana discovered that the changed hyperspace route would crash the Defiance into Krestophis' sun , killing all aboard. Velgor ordered Vexana to correct the problem, and without revealing that he knew of Baylo's treachery, Velgor and Baylo went to see the Emperor. The Emperor ordered Baylo to turn over command of the Defiance and take a position at the training center on Korrath . Baylo, however, was loyal to the Republic and considered the Imperium a hostile power. Instead of turning over his command, Baylo offered his resignation from the navy. Velgor then revealed he knew of Baylo's plan to crash the Defiance , and the Emperor congratulated Velgor for handling the "petty problem," annoying him.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
As Baylo railed against the Emperor, Velgor Synth Flux-choked him to death, drawing ire from the Emperor, who had wished to see Baylo suffer and synth flux him to watch his beloved Navy be turned into something he hated and have the Defiance be melted down into cafeteria trays. Above all, he wanted to use Baylo for his own ambitions since the old man was willing to kill his own students for a cause. Velgor tried to explain that his way was more efficient, but the Emperor wanted to hear nothing of it as he did not order him to kill Baylo. Later, he ordered Vexana to have the Defiance renamed the Obedience as a subtle final jab at Baylo and a not-so-subtle reminder toward Velgor to learn his place.

Crash landing on Selvara

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Crash landing on Selvara

Shortly thereafter, Velgor and the Emperor reboarded the Perilous and resumed their course to the Selvara system. However, upon their exit from hyperspace, the ship immediately began slamming into spacial mines set up by Chavar Kryll 's insurgents. Hidden amongst these mines were specialized devices designed to drain the ship's shields, which began to buckle under the continual assault. As the shields neared failure, a swarm of several hundred reprogrammed Vulture Droids set upon the Perilous from the system's asteroid belt. Velgor boarded his personal interceptor and took several squadrons of Imperial pilots to destroy the droid fighters and mines, but discovered a short time into the battle that Vulture Droids were each carrying a payload of explosive buzz droids .

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Realizing that the Vultures themselves were simply delivery systems meant to unload the buzz droids near or inside the Iron Cruiser, Velgor ordered his squadron to concentrate fire on them, as they presented a far greater threat than the mines. But between the mines and the Vultures, there were simply too many targets for Velgor and his squadrons to handle, and the Perilous was severely damaged. The second wave of Vultures was detected immediately after the first had been destroyed, further compounding the already bleak situation. A message came to Velgor from Captain Lewitt of the Perilous that the ship could sustain virtually no more damage without being destroyed.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor moved to intercept the second wave alone, ordering his squadrons to remain near the Perilous to destroy any droids that got past him. Though incredulous, the squadron commander obeyed, and Velgor used Synth Flux to begin tearing apart the compartments on the Vulture droids that housed the explosive buzz droids. He then used Synth Flux to begin flinging the buzz droids at other incoming fighters and repeated this process until the vast majority of the Vulture Droids had been destroyed. The remaining fighters were annihilated by Velgor's squadrons, and he himself returned to the Perilous . Velgor marched to the Iron Cruiser's bridge and Synth Flux choked Taa for a short time, informing him of the traitor in his staff that had been responsible for the assault on the Perilous . Utterly terrified, the Senator vowed to find the traitor, but the Emperor had Taa and his staff confined to their quarters. An order was then broadcast from the Imperial headquarters on Selvara for any and all repair ships to aid the Perilous as it sped, badly damaged, towards the planet.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Unbeknownst to Velgor, some of the Velari repair teams in fact comprised members of the Free Selvara movement, one of which was a group of saboteurs with orders to plant timed explosives on the hyperrelay core of the Perilous . Shortly after the teams landed, one of the Free Selvara groups engaged in a firefight with Imperial shock troopers. When Velgor learned of this, he ordered all of the Velari repair teams, numbering over 100, to be killed regardless of whether they were aiding the assault and proceeded to Deck 17, where the firefight had been reported. On the way, he killed a group of apparently uninvolved Velaris before proceeding to the hyperrelay chamber. The saboteurs, who were led by Chavar's second in command, Isval , had managed to seal the hatch to the hyperrelay core before any Imperial troops could interrupt them, and Velgor began to use his flux blade to cut it open.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: By the time Velgor finished cutting through the hatch, the saboteurs had already concluded their business and escaped. The main hyperrelay core had been riddled with timed charges, set to detonate if anyone attempted to disarm or remove them. Velgor concluded that the ship was lost, and ordered the captain to evacuate. Velgor contacted Mal, who instructed his apprentice to meet him aboard his shuttle. Before departing, however, Velgor made one last attempt to kill the saboteurs, but they narrowly evaded him and escaped in an Imperial escort boat . Subsequently, Velgor reunited with the Emperor and left on the shuttle, mere minutes before the Iron Cruiser exploded. Shortly thereafter, the Imperial traitor Belka Drayn provided Chavar with the transponder identity of the Emperor's shuttle, and he directed Isval and her group aboard the escort boat to attack it.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor's exceptional piloting skills allowed him to evade the boat and then fly upside down over its cockpit within direct visual range of its pilots. Once there, he used Synth Flux to choke both Isval and her co-pilot, but before losing consciousness, Isval rammed the shuttle with her escort boat. The crash disabled the shuttle's main power, and Velgor had to use a nearly depleted backup battery to attempt a crash landing on Selvara. As he guided the ship through the atmosphere, he had flashbacks of events and people from his past. Though distracted, Velgor managed to land the ship in Selvara's equatorial forest region, but his distraction did not go unnoticed by the Emperor, who noted that the landing had been poor compared to what he knew Velgor to be capable of.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Not too long afterward, the Velari insurgents continued their assault on freighters, prompting Velgor and the Emperor to take action and destroy them, before moving away from their fallen shuttle. At night, they stopped to rest, when the Emperor questioned his regret and loyalty, but Velgor showed himself devoted still. They were soon attacked by a lylek horde, forcing them to retreat into a tunnel, unaware that they had entered their nest. They stood their ground against hundreds of lyleks and their significantly threatening queen, and killed them all before exiting the tunnel and finding a young Velari, Drua . When the Emperor tried to kill her, Velgor stopped him, intending to have the girl guide them to her village , where they obtained a communicator to speak with Moff Mors.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
After giving them their coordinates, they were finally surrounded by Kryll's forces, but so did Mors's, aiding them in quelling the insurgency. As the shock troopers killed the Velaris, Velgor noticed a trio of Velaris: Kryll, Isval, and Goll watching from afar and went on to kill them, but Goll and Kryll escaped, leaving Velgor to capture Isval and bring her before the Emperor. He mocked her, telling her that her people had accomplished nothing, and Velgor subsequently executed her. On the Emperor's orders, Velgor then killed the villagers to leave no witnesses, concluding their mission.

#### Teller's campaign

> " We haven't stood on Vantor in some time, Governor. " " The needs of the Imperium keep us elsewhere occupied, Lord Velgor. " " Just so. " ―Xarn Velgor and Wilhard Varrix

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
#### Teller's campaign

> " We haven't stood on Vantor in some time, Governor. " " The needs of the Imperium keep us elsewhere occupied, Lord Velgor. " " Just so. " ―Xarn Velgor and Wilhard Varrix

When Moff Varrix's Sentinel Base was attacked , Velgor was stationed in the Imperial Palace on Vantor, where he held a court with the Deputy Director of the IVB, Harus Ison , berating Vantori criminals as well as Prefect Phoca Soot of Level 1331 , for ignoring the Emperor's decrees. Telling them to move their operations out of Vantor, Velgor then made an example of Soot for his disrespect and crushed his heart with Synth Flux, and adjourned the court to meet with Varrix and Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon. The latter politely asked Velgor to refrain from killing all those who displeased him, to which the Umbra replied that he would give thought to the matter, before greeting Varrix and sharing the latest developments of the Void Core's construction.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
The pair separated when Velgor left Varrix, who met with the Emperor alone. Afterward, Velgor (like Varrix and Veldon) partook in a meeting between the Imperial Ruling Council, and the leaders of Imperium Vigil Bureau and Naval Intelligence Agency in the palace's audience chamber , overseen by the Emperor. He then assigned Varrix and Velgor to a mission on Murkhana to investigate recently discovered Shadowfeed technology and its relationship to the attack on Sentinel Base. The pair traveled to the planet on the Carrion Spike , which Velgor made to carry his meditation chamber .

On Murkhana, however, the Spike was stolen by unknown dissidents , prompting Velgor and Varrix to kill the Sulie crime lord Faazah , and take his Parsec Predator to pursue the stolen ship, hidden by its cloaking systems. Making use of his connection to his meditation chamber, Velgor pinpointed the insurgents' location to the Fial system and later, the Galidraan system , where they engaged the Spike before they jettisoned his meditation chamber and escaped to Lucazec . With the Predator disabled, Velgor and Varrix boarded the Liberator , from which Velgor issued his black Eta-2 interceptor to be transported on the Goliath from Vantor.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: On the Goliath , Varrix told Velgor that the insurgency was surely being supported by someone high up in the Imperial Military , and predicted that the insurgents would go to Phindar to refuel the Spike . Subsequently, Velgor led a squadron to attack the stolen corvette in the Phindar system . Though they greatly damaged the ship, it escaped, prompting Varrix and Velgor to calculate its trajectory to Obroa-skai system . Teller transmitted false intelligence that the insurgents were heading to the Obroa-skai system. Hoping to capture the Carrion Spike , Varrix and Velgor deployed substantial Imperial resources including three Interdictor vessels. The prototype Immobilizer 418 cruiser malfunctioned, yanking several ships out of hyperspace and causing a massive accident .

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Despite failing to catch the Spike , the Imperials managed to capture the YT-1000 light freighter Reticent , which Teller had sent as a decoy to throw the Imperials off-scent. While Velgor interrogated its Koorivar captain on the Executrix , Varrix accessed Imperial databases and discovered the identities of the insurgents, including its leader Berch Teller . Velgor also interrogated the Reticent ' s Syra Myrthian navigator, who suffered a heart attack. However, Velgor learned from one of his contacts in the Crymorah Syndicate that a lieutenant had negotiated a deal with the Sulie crime lord Faazah for a supply of custom fuel cells . These fuel cells had reached Murkhana shortly before Varrix and Velgor's arrival, thus confirming that Faazah had been colluding with the insurgents.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: After a private holo transmission with the Emperor, Velgor told Varrix that Vice Admiral Dodd Rancit was sure the insurgents would attack the Imperial academy at Carida next. Then, Velgor parted ways with Varrix to meet with Rancit, but not before asking for the meaning behind the Carrion Spike ' s name and Varrix told him about his test in Eriadu 's Carrion Plateau . On the Carida system , Velgor boarded the Secutor -class Iron Cruiser Conquest and met Rancit just as the Spike reverted to realspace , astrogating on autopilot. Aware of Rancit's treason, as a co-conspirator of Teller, Velgor had Lieutenant Crest place Rancit aboard an escape pod and had Rancit give himself the command to issue the fire order that destroyed it. Elsewhere, Varrix dealt with the insurgents, ending the insurgency .

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Following the defeat of Teller's insurgents, Velgor spent the next three weeks helping Varrix to interrogate the captured insurgents with the exception of Teller, who managed to escape. While none of the insurgents had died under questioning, the Emperor had the insurgents executed privately. Velgor also led a crackdown on the warehouse workers and salvages who supplied Teller's dissidents along with several scientists at Desolation Station who had provided Teller with information. Velgor also took action against the Tenloss Syndicate and lower-level members of the Crymorah Syndicate who had assembled Berch Teller's warship , a modified Providence -class Dreadnought.

#### Hunt on Chandar's Folly

> " Kill me, if you can. " ―Xarn Velgor, to Varrix

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
#### Hunt on Chandar's Folly

> " Kill me, if you can. " ―Xarn Velgor, to Varrix

Varrix still owed Velgor a favor for capturing Liarch on Mon Calvarra. Sometime after the Teller campaign, Velgor found himself eager to face some kind of test that would actually challenge his skills, something made more complicated by the greatly reduced number of Aetheri active in the galaxy thanks to his and the Wardens' efforts. As such, Velgor came to Varrix with his request: as he had learned of Varrix's hunting, Velgor asked Varrix to hunt him down. Velgor told him to keep him on his feet and capture or kill him if he could. Varrix was shocked at this and began considering why Velgor would ask him to hunt him. Varrix looked through the reports from the Warden Order and saw that Velgor's hunt for the Aetheri had left him with little to no challenge. Varrix deduced that Velgor wanted to be challenged again and was flattered that he had chosen him.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: The hunt took place on the Outer Reach planet Chandar's Folly , and Varrix immediately began trying to take on the Dark Lord of the Umbra. Knowing of Velgor's brutal abilities, Varrix outfitted the hunters with slugthrowers and flamethrowers to avoid the possibility of Velgor deflecting their shots. On the second day, they cornered Velgor at a copse of Thurian trees , and four hunters engulfed him with their flamethrowers. As Varrix watched Velgor get covered by the flames, he thought he saw fear in his body language. Velgor's possible fear was brief, however, as he targeted the hunters' flamethrowers, incinerating the four hunters. Through the following days, Varrix saw that Velgor was not hard to track, leaving clear signs wherever he went. They learned why as on multiple occasions Velgor ambushed them. On one occasion, Varrix and his hunters were tracking Velgor near a cliff when he revealed himself and killed one of the hunters with his. Two others fired on him but failed to kill him.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Varrix realized that as long as Velgor had his flux blade, he could not be beaten. So over the course of the next four days, he attempted to steal Velgor's weapon. After six men perished, one of Varrix's hunters managed to snatch it out of Velgor's grip while he was fighting. After this, Varrix saw that not only was Velgor turning to new tactics, he was angrier. Varrix knew that enraged prey was usually easier to take out, but he admitted that this rule did not apply to Velgor. Soon after, Velgor fought five of Varrix's hunters as they fired on him, hitting him many times and scarring his armor. Varrix watched from a hilltop as Velgor came close to the hunters and used Synth Flux to snap one's neck. The other hunters retreated, and Velgor Synth Flux-choked another to death. Once understanding how capable Velgor was with Synth Flux, Varrix assumed that the hunt would soon end. However, Varrix soon realized that Velgor was so keen on getting back his flux blade, that so long as Varrix's team hunted him, he hunted them.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: On the ninth day of the hunt, Varrix was down to his last seven hunters. Velgor managed to kill a Valath , the apex predator on the planet, and take its hide, which could help him camouflage better. One of Varrix's Chadra-Fan hunters, Sissian , spotted Velgor northwest of Varrix's camp, and the hunter Yerga notified Varrix of this. Varrix got his binoculars and saw Velgor on top of a peak wearing the Valath hide. Varrix had his hunters form a group around him, and they walked in Velgor's direction. Velgor lured them into a ravine of blue crystals, where his breathing could echo and be untraceable by Sissian and his grandfather, Hardhear . Hardhear heard Velgor's breathing, but although he could say Velgor was near, he could not say which direction. Velgor loomed over them at the top of the ravine and watched as Varrix ordered his team to run. The group ran down the ravine, and Velgor made his move, Synth Flux-pushing one of the hunters into the ravine wall. Velgor then Synth Flux-choked Hardhear before leaping down, under the cover of his Valath hide, and attacking the droid hunter.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Varrix had the rest of his team run into the Stormlands , where it was open ground. They set up camp, and Sissian listened for Velgor's breathing. However, Velgor had deactivated his suit, which stopped his breathing apparatus from giving him away, and he slowly crept up to the camp, before Synth Flux choking Sissian. Yerga attempted to attack Velgor, but he took her by the neck and killed her. The last two hunters opened fire, and Velgor used Synth Flux to retake his flux blade. Varrix then jumped at the two hunters and slaughtered them. Varrix ran away from Velgor, but after realizing he would catch up with him eventually, he stopped and fell to his knees. Velgor loomed over him, not realizing that as he was standing higher than Varrix, he was more susceptible to the lightning in the Stormlands.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Without warning, Velgor was struck by lightning and he fell to the ground. Varrix got up and contacted his flagship, the Carrion Spike , to pick them up. Varrix sat by Velgor and waited for the Carrion Spike to arrive. The corvette soon approached them, being frequently struck by lightning due to its height in the Stormlands. Velgor remained immobile and Varrix told him that whatever he had hoped to learn from this madness, he hoped he had learned it. Varrix then told Velgor that he would get him to a repair bay soon enough. However, Velgor was not finished yet, and he Synth Flux-choked Varrix, showing him that he had not lost just yet. Varrix soon crawled from the range of Velgor's Synth Flux abilities, and Velgor continued lying there.

#### Hunt for Etha Korrin

> " Fear. Anger. Resentment. I sense them in you. You have let yourself feel , Etha Korrin. It gives you power . More than the Aetheri would ever have allowed you. " " Perhaps it's the Zyrrak in me. Or perhaps…now I have something to lose. " ―Xarn Velgor duels Etha Korrin

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Continuing his hunt for surviving Aetheri even as more and more of the Order was destroyed, wiping out many of the individuals whom Velgor could actually find a challenge against, Velgor gathered the Fifth Warden, Tualon Veyra, and the Thirteenth Warden for the latest of his personal missions : Velgor and the Warden Order had successfully tracked down the former Aetheri Master Etha Korrin, whose time on the Aetheri High Council had ended with his removal from the body. After that, Korrin had elected to leave the Aetheri altogether and, as a consequence, escaped the execution of Directive 66. The Imperium had finally tracked Korrin to a largely unknown desert planet , where he had become a priest in the Church of the Ganthic Enlightenment and taken a wife, a fellow Zyrrak named Mira . Ahead of the mission, the Thirteenth Warden felt pleased to be welcomed onto one of Velgor's personal missions and was given a select few details about the mission, such as Velgor's urge to finish what Directive 66 had failed to do by killing Korrin.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor and his Wardens arrived on the planet in a Zeta -class shuttle and entered a city, into which Velgor led the Wardens until Velgor located Korrin in a nearby building just as Mira gave birth to their daughter . Ordering the Wardens to stay back and wait, Velgor entered just as Korrin had the chance to hold his daughter and announced his presence within the doorway, confusing Mira—who had not known her husband's original name nor that he had once been an Aetheri until Velgor's appearance —and horrifying Korrin. The daughter's existence, meanwhile, was felt by the Thirteenth Warden, who informed her comrades of the infant's presence. While Veyra was quick to wonder if Velgor would kill the child, the Dark Lord decided the child, who was Synth Flux-sensitive and filled with potential, should be taken and transformed into subject for Project Harvester . As Velgor entered, Korrin attempted to plead with him by reminding Velgor that he was no longer an Aetheri and offered Velgor codes, secret contact frequencies, and leads on other Aetheri survivors so long as Velgor left him and his family alone, all while covertly urging Mira to leave with their child.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor, however, remained firm in his desire to see Korrin killed. In response, Korrin threw their nurse droid into Velgor and used Synth Flux to break open a hole in the building that his family could use to escape, creating a boom that the waiting Wardens overheard. Rather than incur Velgor's wrath, however, they decided it was best to hold back as he had ordered. As Mira and the child made their escape and Korrin claimed his hidden flux blade, Velgor, recovered from the nurse droid attack, ignited his own flux blade and engaged Korrin in a flux blade duel, the sounds of which were soon overheard by the Wardens. As the two dueled and the duel moved outside, Velgor observed that Korrin had embraced their emotions since his days as an Aetheri, specifically noticing signs of fear, anger, and resentment in the former Aetheri Master, who was seemingly holding his own against Velgor. Advancing on Korrin, Velgor voiced what he felt in Korrin and proclaimed that his emotions gave him a power denied to him by the Aetheri, words which the Thirteenth Warden agreed with but made her wonder if Velgor was inviting Korrin into the Warden Order, a

title: Xarn Velgor
text: his own against Velgor. Advancing on Korrin, Velgor voiced what he felt in Korrin and proclaimed that his emotions gave him a power denied to him by the Aetheri, words which the Thirteenth Warden agreed with but made her wonder if Velgor was inviting Korrin into the Warden Order, a prospect which did not make sense to her since there were so few Aetheri left in the galaxy. Instead of responding to the potential offer, Korrin, calling upon his attachment to his family, continued to clash against Velgor and actually put up a fight against him. In the Thirteenth Warden's experience, Velgor, during a normal hunt, would quickly kill his target without much effort. However, at least as the Thirteenth Warden saw things, the former Aetheri Master fought with enough skill and valor to actually challenge Velgor, an increasingly rare gift for the Dark Lord of the Umbra. Unconcerned with the source of Korrin's emotions, Velgor declared it was too late for him to change and threw him back with Synth Flux, knocking him into the ground before turning his attention to the still waiting Wardens, informing them that Korrin's wife and daughter had escaped before ordering them to bring him the child. When asked about Mira by the Fifth Warden, Velgor simply responded that her life did not matter before he returned to his duel against the angered Korrin, who affirmed that he was no longer an Aetheri and instead a family man who would use his attachments to fuel him.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Entrusting the Wardens to complete their mission, Velgor focused on Korrin and struck against him, a strike that Korrin evaded with a summersault before he struck Velgor in his helmet. As the clash continued, Velgor's cape and waist cape were ripped, but Velgor managed to catch Korrin with a Synth Flux choke, with his continued attacks also managing to rip Korrin's clothing and injure his face. As Korrin held his ground and stood against the Dark Lord in the name of his family, however, Velgor noticed the return of his Wardens with his child, which he quickly pointed out to Korrin. Despite the minor damage to his capes, Velgor appeared pristine and powerful to the Thirteenth Warden, whereas Korrin looked far worse for wear, all leading the Thirteenth Warden to wonder if Velgor had been toying with the former Aetheri Master and dragging the duel out for his own enjoyment. Seeing they had captured his daughter, Korrin lost all his focus on Velgor, who stabbed the former Aetheri Master through the chest and allowed his body to crumble to the ground, dead almost instantly from the flux blade wound. Immediately, Velgor then demanded the Wardens give him the screaming infant,

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Seeing they had captured his daughter, Korrin lost all his focus on Velgor, who stabbed the former Aetheri Master through the chest and allowed his body to crumble to the ground, dead almost instantly from the flux blade wound. Immediately, Velgor then demanded the Wardens give him the screaming infant, whom he used Synth Flux upon to demand she quiet herself. Immediately, the infant stopped crying and did not wail again. With that, Velgor and his Wardens returned to their Zeta -class shuttle with the child, ready to make their way back to Vantor. #### Aftermath of the Korrin hunt

> " This is a list of the surviving Aetheri. Others may remain, but of these we are certain. Unfortunately… they have hidden themselves extremely well . We know they're out there, but there have been no signs, no signals. For all intents and purposes, they have vanished. Aetheri remain, but as of now… we have no way to find them. " " What do you purpose, Grand Warden? " " We'll continue with Project Harvester, of course. Beyond that, well, one of them is bound to slip up eventually. We just have to wait " ―The Grand Warden and Xarn Velgor

title: Xarn Velgor
text: At some stage, Velgor was informed by the Fifth Warden that the Thirteenth Warden had nearly allowed Mira and the child to escape her grasp, leaving Velgor to believe that she had only captured the infant because that apparent moment of weakness had been discovered. For her part, the Thirteenth Warden had, indeed, been overcome by the memory of her own mother, Feyra Vekkis , giving her up to the Aetheri as an infant and allowed the mother and daughter to briefly escape in a moment of apparent tiredness, but she then claimed that she never intended for them to actually get away. Instead, she used the moment to claim for herself a bout of cruel satisfaction; only after her fellow Wardens reached her and Veyra asked her what Velgor would do to her for letting them escape did she reach out and claim the child from Mira via Synth Flux, telekinetically pulling the child from Mira so as to destroy her trust in other people. To the Thirteenth Warden in that moment, the child belonged either with Velgor or dead. The Warden was not even entirely sure why Velgor wanted the infant and did not care.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor, for his part, had become suspicious of the Thirteenth Warden's loyalty. She had, indeed, become dissatisfied with her life among the Wardens as she felt trapped, feeling as though she had no freedom and was left to perform work for superiors who took all the credit for themselves. She had forced herself to continue her service lest Velgor discover her doubts and invite her into a maiming-filled sparring match. Still, she found solace in a romantic relationship with Veyra, something Velgor had also sensed. While relationships were not strictly disallowed among the Warden Order, Velgor regarded their connection as a weakness and believed the death of Korrin should serve as a warning to both of them. Later, he would claim that he believed that the Thirteenth Warden was building a coalition to usurp control of the Warden Order from himself and the Emperor, using Veyra as her first follower. In truth, however, she simply wanted to retire to her homeworld of Pkori , potentially with Veyra joining her.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Arriving at the Warden Order Headquarters in the Works, Velgor disembarked from the Zeta -class shuttle while telekinetically holding Korrin's child aloft, the Thirteenth Warden, Fifth Warden, and Veyra behind him. Present for their return was the waiting Grand Warden, who welcomed Velgor's return to Vantor and applauded his efforts, and two nursemaids , nanny droids that served the Warden Order as part of Project Harvester. As he disembarked, Velgor informed the Grand Warden that the mission had been a complete success and that the Wardens—whom he referred to as the Grand Warden's subordinates, not his own—had performed their roles well. The Thirteenth Warden found the praise unusual and welcome, yet also demeaning: as she saw things, she was solely responsible for the capture of the child and alone deserved praise for the mission, something she believed Velgor knew. However, Velgor's brief comment had robbed her of individual credit. Such a feeling had plagued her as an Aetheri and made her further doubt her station as a Warden, with Velgor's words sticking with her as the day continued.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: As he handed the child off to the nursemaids, Velgor asked the Grand Warden who their next target was, something which made the Warden pause and lead Velgor away. Within the building, Velgor was led to a holographic list of confirmed Aetheri survivors who had hidden themselves away too well to be actively hunted. As such, the death of Korrin ushered in a new phase of the Aetheri Purge: the Grand Warden informed Velgor that Project Harvester would continue but that there were no active hunts for surviving Aetheri, effectively meaning they would have to wait for an Aetheri to reveal themselves or offer a trail. Suddenly, Velgor was faced with a galaxy where there were so few Aetheri left that he had no active targets against whom he could challenge himself. Rather than respond, Velgor silently exited the room and returned to his personal apartment. As time passed, he bathed in a bacta tank, telekinetically modified his life support equipment, walked through Imperial halls, dueled with a training droid, and meditated, in which state he found himself back over the stormy ocean, albeit with calm waves. However, Velgor felt no calm and clenched his fist in silence.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: #### Chasing "rogue" Wardens After feeling that frustration, Velgor decided he had to look elsewhere for a challenge and turned his attention to the Thirteenth Warden, who Velgor knew he would be able to paint as a traitor because of his suspicious about her loyalty and her decision to briefly allow Mira to escape with Korrin's daughter. Velgor made his way into the Warden Order common room, where all the present Wardens had been gathered by the Grand Warden to spend time together. There, the Thirteenth Warden and Veyra were sharing a bottle of dust juice from Korrin's planet to celebrate his death and discussed what would become of Velgor once they had finished off the last of the Aetheri, sliding her eyes towards Velgor in the process. As Veyra mused that Velgor would keep himself busy and find someone new to kill, the Umbra Lord approached their table, catching the Thirteenth Warden's attention as she felt his cold shadow approach them. Meanwhile, the increasingly inebriated Veyra failed to notice his presence. Once he loomed over them both, Velgor announced his presence by silently igniting his flux blade, finally catching Veyra's attention and shocking both them. Likewise, other present Wardens, including the Grand Warden,

title: Xarn Velgor
text: as she felt his cold shadow approach them. Meanwhile, the increasingly inebriated Veyra failed to notice his presence. Once he loomed over them both, Velgor announced his presence by silently igniting his flux blade, finally catching Veyra's attention and shocking both them. Likewise, other present Wardens, including the Grand Warden, were caught off-guard and focused their attention on the suddenly unfolding scene. After a long, tense moment, Velgor was asked by the cautious Grand Warden if he was beginning a test or more training, which the Thirteenth Warden was initially certain of before starting to doubt the prospect. Veyra, meanwhile, was too inebriated to keep his feelings in check, making his concern for the Thirteenth Warden incredibly clear to Velgor. Finally, Velgor affirmed to all gathered that his actions were not a test and swung his flux blade down to catch the Thirteenth Warden, which Veyra managed to block in time with his own flux blade, much to Velgor's interest and to the Thirteenth Warden's surprise. As the Thirteenth Warden took the opportunity to run at Veyra's urging, Velgor kept Veyra's blade in a lock and revealed he had felt their connection before he Synth Flux threw the Velari Warden into a wall. Telling Veyra not to worry about why he had turned his weapon on the Thirteenth Warden, Velgor urged Veyra to concern himself with something else. In response, Veyra ran from him, which Velgor declared meant that Veyra doing the same as his lover. Preparing to chase both down, Velgor then rejected an offer from the confused Grand Warden for

title: Xarn Velgor
text: turned his weapon on the Thirteenth Warden, Velgor urged Veyra to concern himself with something else. In response, Veyra ran from him, which Velgor declared meant that Veyra doing the same as his lover. Preparing to chase both down, Velgor then rejected an offer from the confused Grand Warden for Inquisitorial assistance, declaring he had no need of their help. Meanwhile, the Thirteenth Warden and Veyra escaped from the headquarters, understanding that they needed to kill Velgor if they wanted to escape and be free. The Thirteenth Warden also assured Veyra that she had no idea why Velgor had attacked her, although she reflected that Velgor must have felt her love for Veyra and anger at her limited freedom. Still, she feigned ignorance to her lover and claimed Velgor must have just wanted to kill someone. Meanwhile, Velgor left the Inquisitorial Headquarters and requisitioned two replica shock troopers and a speeder to hunt down both Wardens, whom he claimed to be surviving Aetheri who would attack in an unorthodox manner. Indeed, just as Velgor said as such, the Thirteenth Warden—having taken control of a speeder with Veyra and noticed Velgor's pursuit through Synth Flux—threw an engine from another passing speeder at Velgor, missing him but crippling his speeder by destroying one of its engines. Noticing the strike in time, Velgor lightly leapt from his speeder before it exploded and landed on another passing speeder, much to the confusion of its driver, before both rogue Wardens threw their flux blades into the craft. Velgor fell from the destroyed craft but effortlessly landed onto yet another speeder, all as his previous ride crashed into a park and killed the picnicking Senator Maklooq .

title: Xarn Velgor
text: When the rogue Wardens decided they needed to throw something bigger at Velgor, Velgor became the target of a speeder thrown at him at great velocity by the Thirteenth Warden, but he managed to effortlessly throw it right back at her, horrifying her as she began to realize the true power of Xarn Velgor. The worried Wardens responded by throwing another speeder at Velgor, who effortlessly batted it away by throwing it back to both Wardens, much to the Thirteenth Warden's surprise once again. As he closed the distance between their stolen speeders, yet another speeder was thrown at Velgor, who cut the speeder in two with his flux blade, before he leapt at them both, but the two managed to pull down a statue onto Velgor, hitting him in the back and knocking him onto a nearby deck, where he made a hard landing and was left badly damaged. The two rogue Wardens closed in, with the Thirteenth Warden determined to either escape after killing Velgor or claim superiority over the other Warden Order through the act. She declared that Velgor deserved the death he was about to receive and and prepared to strike down the Dark Lord. Velgor,

title: Xarn Velgor
text: The two rogue Wardens closed in, with the Thirteenth Warden determined to either escape after killing Velgor or claim superiority over the other Warden Order through the act. She declared that Velgor deserved the death he was about to receive and and prepared to strike down the Dark Lord. Velgor, however, then held both Wardens in Synth Flux Stasis by using his pain to fuel his power. Velgor silently raised both Wardens into the air. The Thirteenth Warden, for her part, tried to overcome Velgor by calling upon her connection to the umbra side, but she found Velgor's umbra side powers far surpassed her own. Realizing she was defeated, she looked over to Veyra but refused to say what she wanted to in front of Velgor. Quickly moving their bodies together, Velgor forced both Wardens to stab each other through the other's chest with their own flux blades, killing both after the Thirteenth Warden's blade stabbed Veyra through the chest and his blade ran through one of hearts. Unknown to Velgor, however, killing the Thirteenth Warden provided her a sense of freedom she had never found as either Aetheri Iskat Vekkis or the Thirteenth Warden Warden. She also felt there was something right about about her and Veyra killing each other, even if Velgor was the one pulling their strings. Velgor then dropped both of their bodies and stood over both, all as the Vantor cityscape around him smouldered from the damage the chase had caused—beyond the crash in the park and the explosion it had caused, the various thrown or damaged speeders had interrupted the flow of Vantori traffic, fallen from the sky, and

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Velgor was then ordered by the Emperor to go to Cindervale to deal with Senator Bael Solen. However, to the surprise of his master, Velgor refused. Having carried out Mal's will for so long, Velgor was content to continue to do so, but he first he demanded a world of his own. Rejecting Mal's offer to give him Dunemere or Ondara, Velgor asked to be given Emberfall, the world where he had been defeated by Kade. The Emperor agreed to his request and would send Colonel Alva Brenne to build a facility for him there. Before leaving for Emberfall, Velgor was then shown the Mask of Vael Mornick , which Mal gave him to help with construction. When Velgor questioned how his master had learned of an Umbra Lord not mentioned in any Umbra nor Aetheri reliquary he had studied, Mal vaguely answered that the mask itself had told him about Mornick.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Return to Emberfall

> " Perhaps your Lira does await you on Emberfall. Perhaps the umbra side will bring her to you. Go. I think, one way or another, you will learn a great deal. That is good. After all, your power…is my power. " ―Mal to Velgor, before the latter departs for Emberfall Velgor, along with Colonel Brenne and her aide, Lieutenant Roggo , took Velgor's Ondara starship to Emberfall. During the flight, Velgor saw a vision of his younger self with a face that matched his mask. Upon entering the planet's atmosphere, Velgor deactivated the starship's shields and allowed it to burn as they landed. Once on the planet's surface, Velgor commented that the ship looked better burnt. He then told Brenne that he was there to understand a great mystery. While Brenne and Roggo got to work designing Velgor's castle, Velgor returned to the cave where he bled his kyber crystal. As he reached out to the power within the cave's locus, he was presented with a design for the castle from Brenne, which Velgor rejected. However, shortly after leaving, Velgor heard Brenne scream and returned to the starship to find her dead. He also discovered that Roggo had donned Mornick's mask. Velgor attacked Roggo, but stopped upon seeing that he had created a new design for the castle. Removing the mask from Roggo's corpse, Velgor took the mask into the cave and placed it upon the locus. He then asked the mask who he was, to which he replied "I

title: Xarn Velgor
text: mask. Velgor attacked Roggo, but stopped upon seeing that he had created a new design for the castle. Removing the mask from Roggo's corpse, Velgor took the mask into the cave and placed it upon the locus. He then asked the mask who he was, to which he replied "I am Mornick". Mornick proceeded to show Velgor his entire life, from creating morbid works of art from the deceased to being trained in the ways of the Umbra by Vael Shaa . After killing his master and studying the lore of the umbra side, Mornick constructed a weapon which, along with his use of Synth Flux, would freeze a city's population forever at the moment of their deaths. However, an attack by the Aetheri caused him to lose control, destroying both the city and himself in the process. As a result, Mornick's essence became trapped within his mask, forcing him to take on host after host in order to create his art. Velgor placed the mask upon his head, but quickly cast it aside and then departed with it from the cave. With his new body, Mornick explained that his design for the castle was actually a key to open a door to the umbra side, which Velgor could use to reunite with Lira Ondar. Velgor threatened Mornick not to offer him things he could not provide and Mornick

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
the mask upon. With his new body, Mornick explained that his design for the castle was actually a key to open a door to the umbra side, which Velgor could use to reunite with Lira Ondar. Velgor threatened Mornick not to offer him things he could not provide and Mornick responded that he only wanted another chance to create. Velgor accepted Mornick's offer, but warned the ancient Umbra not to betray him. Under Mornick's guidance, Velgor used his Imperial resources to begin construction of his castle. With each new design, Mornick insisted that this would be the one to open the door. Though each attempt to do so would subsequently end in failure. And with each failure, Velgor would cut down Mornick's current body in frustration and place his mask upon a new host. Each new attempt to open the door would also bring ruin to Emberfall itself, prompting the Emberfallians to attack in retaliation. The cycle of creation and destruction carried on for two years. Mission to Nur

Velgor controlled the entire Emberfall system . Concurrent to the construction of Fortress Velgor, the Wardens, due to Velgor's destruction caused when he chased the rogue Wardens on Vantor, moved to a similarly designed Fortress on the ocean moon of Nur in the Emberfall system. In 14 BVE, Velgor journeyed to the Fortress Warden Order to retrieve a reliquary containing a list of Synth Flux-sensitive children, which the Second Warden had been hunting for . Instead, he found that the Second Warden had failed to stop surviving Aetheri Cal Kessara and Cere Jundar , who was pleading for the Warden to return to the light and apologizing for failing her; during the early Aetheri purge, Jundar, while under torture by Velgor, had revealed the hiding location of Trilla, who became the Second Warden, and a number of younglings under her protection.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: As Jundar and Trillia talked, Velgor approached, his breathing alone scaring the Second Warden. Jundar also recognized Velgor on sight, telling the worried Kessara that he was right to be scared. Executing the Second Warden for her failure and before she could return to the Aetheri, Velgor used Synth Flux to throw Jundar into a pit with little effort, then suggesting to Kessara that he surrender. Regardless, Kessara launched multiple futile flux blade attacks against Velgor only for Velgor to effortlessly neutralize all of his assaults and telekinetically choke him. Quickly realizing his disadvantage, Cal fled the encounter, after barely surviving by pulling a piece of machinery at his and Velgor's direction, forcing Velgor to defend himself from that and toss Cal aside, with Velgor in hot pursuit.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Despite Cal managing to escape from Velgor moments before he could enter the elevator, Velgor soon managed to catch up to him just as he was about to escape the fortress and attacked him. As he quickly gained the upper hand on Kessara and began to overpower him in a blade-lock, Cal's droid, BD-1 , attempted to short-circuit Velgor's life-support suit, forcing Velgor to disengage and stop the droid. Before he could crush BD-1, Cal made use of the distraction to impale Velgor in the mid-section, only for Velgor to retaliate by tossing Cal aside once again with Synth Flux and as Cal desperately attempted to fight back and summon his flux blade back, Velgor stopped Cal's flux blade before it could return to his hand and once again offered a chance for Cal to surrender the reliquary and when Cal refused, Velgor simply activated the flux blade and forced it into Cal's mid-section, the same way that Cal attempted to defeat him.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Moments later, Jundar reappeared to aid Kessara, only to be easily defeated after a short clash of blades, being flung aside. Commenting on the strength of Jundar's hatred, Velgor was impressed when Jundar was able to temporarily bring him to his knees with the umbra side of Synth Flux and commented how he could feel it inside of her. Once Jundar resisted his efforts to goad her into the darkness, Velgor attempted to kill both her and Kessara, but Jundar was able to hold it at bay with a synth flux-barrier long enough for Kessara to use Synth Flux to shatter a number of windows surrounding them, causing water to pour into the complex and forcing Velgor to use Synth Flux to hold back the flood, as Kessara grabbed Jundar and escaped through the opening.

Helping fellow troopers

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Helping fellow troopers

Between 13 BVE and 10 BVE , Velgor participated in a battle in the Mid Reach, where a few shock troopers, including the future bounty hunter Beilert Varrick , were pinned down by enemy forces. Velgor used synth flux to disarm and then kill the enemies with the blades from their own weapons. When the troops looked confused, Velgor emerged from a fire and told them to march onwards.

The final castle

> " Let the past die. Kill it if you have to. " ―A voice during Xarn Velgor's vision

In 12 BVE , Mornick's ninth design for Fortress Velgor was constructed, which Velgor stated would be his final chance. Upon activating this castle, Velgor found that he was finally able to open the door. However, before he could enter, he was informed of another attack by the Emberfallians. And while Velgor dealt with the attackers, Mornick took the opportunity to open the door himself. He then summoned his younger self from the past and placed his mask upon him, thus finally creating his masterpiece; himself.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Leaving the battle, Velgor reentered the castle while the Emberfallians continued their attack. Upon returning to the locus, he used Synth Flux to unleash a devastating attack, wiping out the rest of the Emberfallians. Velgor was then met in combat by Mornick, who mocked Velgor for thinking he could control the umbra side. As he chastised the Dark Lord for his ignorance about Synth Flux, Velgor used Synth Flux to ram Mornick with a rock, crushing his new body and killing him. With Mornick dead, Velgor finally opened the door and stepped inside. Abandoning his physical body, Velgor entered a realm in which he experienced visions of his past, present, and future. He saw himself as a child haunted by the very form of what he would become. Becoming a child once again, he gradually grew up along with the memories of his upbringing. After experiencing a vision of him dueling his former apprentice Sela Marr, Velgor entered another vision of the Aetheri Sanctum and fought against the specters of various Aetheri. After disposing of them, Velgor journeyed further into the Temple until coming upon the forms of Theron Mal and Orien Kade, who both claimed to be his father. After killing Kade, the vision of Mal motioned at Velgor to stand down, to which Velgor responded with a barrage of Synth Flux lightning that destroyed the specter.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Finally, Velgor found himself on a balcony with a vision of Ondar standing before him. Velgor, now in the form of Kael Drayden, told Ondar to come with him. However, Ondar simply told him that Kael Drayden was dead before leaping from the balcony. Velgor screamed in agony as the specter of Ondar was destroyed by a bolt of lightning. He then saw a beacon of blue light in the distance. Within the beacon was a figure who activated a blue flux blade, pushing Velgor back and returning him to his body. After awakening in the castle and retrieving his flux blade, Velgor destroyed the umbra side locus, sealing off the door, because he was unable to restore his wife.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Sometime later, Velgor contacted his master and informed him that he was still alive. The Emperor asked Velgor if he would return to Vantor, to which Velgor said he soon would. The Emperor then asked Velgor if the truth he learned of on Emberfall was what he needed. Velgor then hung up and, while standing in front of the finally completed Fortress Velgor , answered "Yes". Velgor went on to return Mornick's mask to Mal, who placed it in his personal yacht , the Imperialis , under the watch of two Royal Guards.

### Hunting Kade

#### Duel on Mapuzo

> " What have you become? " " I am what you made me. " ―Orien Kade and Xarn Velgor

title: Xarn Velgor
text: In 9 BVE , Velgor at last had a chance for his long-awaited rematch with Kade after a Warden known as the Third Warden—who was obsessed with finding Kade because she was in fact the youngling Revai, who wanted to use Kade as bait to get close to Velgor and enact revenge for his slaughter at the Aetheri Sanctum years before —arranged for the kidnapping of Elira Solen to draw Kade to the planet Daiyu . Although he escaped with Solen, the Third Warden told Kade that Drayden had survived his injuries. As Kade grabbled with the information, Velgor awoke in his bacta tank in Fortress Velgor on Emberfall. Assembling his suit, Velgor moved to his throne room and spoke to the Third Warden via hologram, demanding to know where Kade was. Dismissing the apparent death of the Grand Warden, whom Revai had stabbed in her desire to claim credit for Kade's capture herself, Velgor ordered her to prove herself capable, with the position of Grand Warden as her reward should she succeed. In truth, he knew the Third Warden was the youngling Revai and that she intended to betray him, but Velgor kept her alive so long as she

title: Xarn Velgor
text: for Kade's capture herself, Velgor ordered her to prove herself capable, with the position of Grand Warden as her reward should she succeed. In truth, he knew the Third Warden was the youngling Revai and that she intended to betray him, but Velgor kept her alive so long as she was useful. Velgor also warned the Third Warden that if she failed, she would not live to regret it. Later, Velgor was informed that Orien was on Mapuzo . Velgor arrived with his three Wardens and a squad of shock troopers and walked through the streets of the settlement, terrorizing and killing random civilians in order to draw Orien out. Velgor pursued the Aetheri Master into the quarry. Horrified at what had become of his former apprentice, Orien tried to flee, but Velgor ambushed him. Velgor taunted Orien with regards to his lost strength, and Orien attempted to flee again. Once again, Velgor caught up to Orien, this time lifting him with Synth Flux, as he ignited flammable rocks with his flux blade. Promising to make Orien suffer, Velgor lowered Orien to the ground and dragged him through the flames, scorching him. Velgor extinguished the flames as a squad of shock troopers arrived. Velgor ordered Orien brought to him, but before the shock troopers could comply, a hidden Tala Durith opened fire, killing several shock troopers and reigniting the flammable rocks. This gave NED-B the opportunity to retrieve Orien and for Tala to escape with the injured Aetheri.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Following the successful rescue of Elira from Fortress Warden Order, Velgor angrily made to kill the Third Warden, lifting her into the air with Synth Flux and choking her while reminding her that she was warned what would happen if she failed. Velgor allowed her to speak, which enabled her to reveal that she had planted a tracker on Elira's droid, Lola , which would reveal the location of the Hidden Path network. Velgor acknowledged that he had underestimated the Third Warden, and spared her, though he warned her that he would not tolerate any further mistakes.

#### Attacking Jabiim

#### Attacking Jabiim

> " He was wise to use you against me. " ―Xarn Velgor to Third Warden

Aboard the Reckoning , Velgor reflected on a long ago training duel against Kade in the Aetheri Sanctum as the Aetheri's Adept before his captain alerted him to the Third Warden's arrival. Ordering the pleasantries dispensed with, Velgor demanded to know Orien's location. The Third Warden reported that he had been tracked to Jabiim . Satisfied, Velgor demanded that the Third Warden kneeled before him, and he promoted her to the rank of Grand Warden. He then ordered the bridge captain to set a course for Jabiim.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: En route to Jabiim, Velgor ordered the Path's base locked down. The Third Warden warned Velgor that if they trapped them, their opponents could hold out for several days. Velgor responded that he did not intend to break their enemies. After the Third Warden and her forces secured the Path's hangar, Velgor arrived on the surface. The Third Warden told him that Kade was inside, but Velgor stated that he wished to bring him in himself. Velgor forced his way into the hangar and found a transport attempting to leave. He used Synth Flux to ground it and rip it apart, only to find that it was a decoy and the real transport with the Path—and Kade—aboard took off successfully. The Aetheri Master had remembered the old training duel where his Adept had shown shortsightedness because of his anger, which inspired him to exploit Velgor's ruthlessness and single-minded focus.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
The Third Warden attempted to use that moment as a distraction to stab Velgor, but Velgor used Synth Flux to stop her blade, stating that Kade was wise to use her against him. Velgor hurled her aside, but she charged at him again, and he used Synth Flux to deflect her blade and throw her. The Third Warden activated her flux blade's twin blade spinning mode, but Velgor used Synth Flux to stall the blades rotation, and then ripped her blade from her grip. Velgor detached her flux blade into two singular hilts, and tossed one on the ground at the Third Warden's feet, taunting her. She retrieved the weapon and continued to attack Velgor, but the Umbra Lord quickly disarmed her again, before stabbing her in the abdomen. As she collapsed, the Grand Warden arrived, revealing he had survived, and Velgor stated that he had known her intent for some time, but had decided to allow it because it was useful in the hunt for Kade. Velgor declared that the Third Warden was no longer useful, and he and the Grand Warden left her to die.

#### The second rematch

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
#### The second rematch

> " Kael… " " Kael is gone. I am what remains. " " I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Kael. For all of it. " " I am not your failure, Orien. You didn't kill Kael Drayden. I did. The same way, I will destroy you. " " Then my friend is truly dead. Goodbye, Vael. " ―Orien Kade says goodbye to Xarn Velgor Velgor returned to the Reckoning as it pursued the Path's freighter. Kade left the Path's freighter on a drop ship with Lola. Against the advice of the Grand Warden, who stated that he should continue the pursuit of the Path's ship, Velgor ordered the Reckoning after Kade to a rocky moon. Velgor departed the Reckoning alone aboard a shuttle and chased Kade above the moon's moon's dry lands before landing in those dry lands, where he confronted Kade and asked if his former master was there to destroy him. Kade replied that he will do as he must before igniting his flux blade. Velgor vowed that Kade would die and the two engaged in a flux blade duel, with Velgor utilizing a combination of one-handed and two-handed combat, that passed from the dry lands into a labyrinth of rock pinnacles . During the duel, Kade attempted to collapse a pinnacle on Velgor, who stopped it with Synth Flux. Remarking that Kade's strength had returned since their last duel but that his weakness remained, Velgor hurled the pinnacle at Kade before resuming their duel.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Velgor collapsed the ground beneath Kade and hurled rocks to keep him down there. Before leaving, Velgor taunted Kade for thinking that he could win against his former apprentice. However, Kade, drawing on his desire to protect Kael's children, managed to break free and charged at Velgor again. On the offensive, Kade used his superior use of Soresu and the more aggressive Ataru utilized by his late master, Sorin Vael to overwhelm the Umbra Lord before using Synth Flux to hurl Velgor against a rock. With Velgor stunned, Kade pummeled him with a maelstrom of rocks then reengaged the duel, critically damaging Velgor's chest plate with multiple strikes from his flux blade's pommel and slashing him across the back before pushing him back with Synth Flux again. Finally, Kade leapt at Velgor, striking the left side of his helmet with his flux blade and revealing the scarred face of Kael beneath. Kade addressed him as Kael Drayden, prompting Velgor to respond that Kael was gone and that he was what remained.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Kade was visibly distraught and apologized to Kael. Velgor replied that he was not Kade's failure and that Kade did not kill Kael: instead, Velgor replied that he killed Kael and vowed to destroy Kade as well. With that, Kade was left to believe his friend was truly dead before bidding Velgor, whom he simply called "Vael," farewell. As Kade left, Velgor called out to him while trying to rise to his feet, unable to catch Kade before he slipped through his grasp once more. Velgor was left with the belief that he had been but a learner in their latest duel, convincing him to increase his strength to cement his power over Kade for whenever their next encounter came. Velgor's suit was repaired and he returned to Fortress Velgor, where he conferred with the Emperor via hologram, stating that he had dispatched probes along all possible routes and that Kade would not escape him again. The Emperor noticed Velgor's agitation and suggested that Velgor could not move beyond his past. Velgor, seeing the threat hidden in Mal's reply, affirmed that Kade meant nothing to him and that he only served the Emperor.
