Zho's journey to Moraband

> " Save him, Aetheri? Can you save him? Why not let him go? Let him die, and you can stop all that I will do. " ―Vael Mal, to Zho, about Kael Drayden

title: Theron Mal
text:
When Zho entered the Valley of the Dark Lords on Moraband during a quest to uncover immortality , Mal and Varek sensed his presence and convened at the Works on Vantor. Greeting his apprentice once he arrived, Mal led Varek to the tower's ceremonial chamber. Exploiting Varek and Zho's Synth Flux-bond, Mal used a Balc incantation to cast a dark illusion to ensnare the Aetheri Master. Using Sifas Dyen' visage, he offered to reveal his identity if he would join him, but Zho refused. The illusion then made it seem that they were in the Works pursuing the Umbra Lords with Kael Drayden and the 501st Legion . Mal dueled Zho on the catwalks outside the tower, with Drayden arriving outside shortly after. Mal rendered Drayden unconscious with Synth Flux lightning while he continued fighting Zho. As the illusion unfolded, Zho refused to sacrifice Drayden to pursue Mal, and instead demonstrated he was willing to sacrifice himself to save the Seeded One. Mal' illusion faltered: the Aetheri Master won. Defeated, Mal stated that they would need more time to defeat the Aetheri.

Business on Uthara

title: Theron Mal
text:
Business on Uthara

When he learned the otherwise unremarkable planet Uthara had produced a massive kyber crystal , the world became of interest to Mal, as he wanted the large crystal for his battle station project. With the crystal in the hands of a Sulie arms dealing group , Varek agreed to a sale, claiming he wanted the crystal for the Dissident Alliance. Skarn himself arrived to oversee the deal, ultimately killing the Sulie leader, Endente , and taking the crystal to his Dissident fleet. However, after they had arrived on Uthara to investigate the death of Aetheri Master Tu-Anh , Kade and Drayden fought to stop the Dissident operation, pursuing the crystal into space and destroying it aboard Skarn's Dual Hemisphere-Omni Support Vessel . Nevertheless, Zho feared that Mal was planning to create a superweapon, and Mal remained interested in Uthara. Thus, the planet was targeted to be occupied, which would allow a crystal search to begin. Within months, the Dissidents invaded the world.

sacrificing herself for her lover, Daren Kelv, Varek' "new assassin" chose to allow Kael Drayden and Orien Kade take him back to the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor for reassessment. Meanwhile, as the Aetheri took Vossa, a ship sent by Vael Mal arrived to retrieve Varek, letting the Dissident leader return to safety. ### Subverting the Republic

#### Most powerful chancellor in centuries

As per his plans to use the Replica Wars as an excuse to consolidate and centralize his political power to make way for his reign as Emperor, Mal had become the most powerful Supreme Chancellor since the days of the Ruusan Reformations by the end of the conflict. Using the war effort as his excuse, Mal had the Galactic Constitution amended multiple times during the conflict. One constitutional amendment known as the Reflex Amendment granted him near-absolute power over military affairs, thereby allowing him to bypass the Senate in such decisions. Towards the end of the war, Mal passed a constitutional amendment known as the Sector Governance Decree .

title: Theron Mal
text:
Under the Sector Governance Decree, Mal created a new structure of regional governance by appointing certain individuals as governors. In theory, the decree was designed to shore up the war effort by uniting star systems into singular blocs and transforming their production centers into war-focused installations. In reality, however, regional governors could become leaders of the systems they oversaw, allowing Mal to circumvent and one day disband the Senate by creating a new bureaucracy composed of individuals he sent out. The decree, however, proved to be too much for senators who formed the Delegation of 2,000 , which quietly assembled the Petition of 2,000 in the name of protesting Mal's conduct and growing powers. Led by Ondar, Sess, and Solen, the Delegation hoped to make Mal give up his emergency powers and intended to present their petition to Mal once it was signed by two thousand of their fellow legislators.

#### The Battle of Vantor

> " You did well, Kael. He was too dangerous to be kept alive. " ―Theron Mal, to Kael Drayden, on the execution of Varek

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### The Battle of Vantor

> " You did well, Kael. He was too dangerous to be kept alive. " ―Theron Mal, to Kael Drayden, on the execution of Varek

Deciding that it was time to make Drayden his next apprentice, Mal devised a plan for Mal to be captured in order for Drayden to rescue him. The plan included sacrificing Vael Varek, who was to be killed by Drayden, which would tempt Drayden to the umbra side and eventually lead to the young Aetheri replacing Varek as the Dark Lord's new apprentice. Likely through the Nexus Route, Mal had obtained the coordinates to Vantor and gave them to Skarn and his fleet to jump from the Outer Reach directly to Vantor. Mal also had a plan to kidnap the Supreme Chancellor, which was tasked to Skarn. Mal ordered Skarn to capture Mal and for Varek to hold him hostage. Skarn and Varek, however, were unaware of Mal' true intentions.

title: Theron Mal
text: During the Outer Reach Sieges , Skarn commanded a massive invasion of Vantor, accompanied by Varek. Varek, who had earlier relocated his command post to Skarn's flagship , the Invisible Hand , stayed close to Skarn to ensure he was carrying out his orders; even though the cyborg general posed no threat to Mal, he did not want any setback to his plans. While the Republic and Dissident fleets clashed above the planet, Skarn went to the ground in order to capture Mal, Shaak Ti and Roron Corobb , along with a replica task synth flux were sent to protect him. Corrob and the replicas fell to Skarn, while Ti managed to fight further. Skarn took the upper hand by electrifying the Aetheri Master with cables, knocking her unconscious in the process. Skarn took her flux blade and fled with the captive Mal to the Dissident flagship Invisible Hand .

title: Theron Mal
text: Kade and Drayden, who at the time were in the middle of making preparations to take Ferrum, were called upon to rescue him. After landing in the Invisible Hand ' s hangar, the two found Mal bound to a chair on the bridge . They were confronted by Varek, who they entered a duel with. Varek took out Kade with ease and then focused on Drayden. They continued the duel until Drayden cut off his hands. Disarmed and on his knees, Varek was bested. Mal commended Drayden on his accomplishment. However, he then betrayed Varek by urging Kael to kill him, due to Varek having served his purpose. A horrified Varek looked to Mal pleadingly, only to be met with another, more sinister urging. With one swift move, Count Varek was beheaded. Kael was conflicted on his actions but was comforted by Mal, who told him that it was a simple act of revenge in return for Varek cutting off his arm. Beyond luring Drayden closer to the umbra side, the act also served to tie up the loose end Varek would be if he lived, robbing the Aetheri of the chance to question him to learn more about Mal.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Drayden went to pick up the unconscious Kade, to which Mal pleaded with the Aetheri to leave his master. His plea was denied, and the three began their descent to the hangar. Meanwhile, the Invisible Hand was attacked by the Guarlara , with the former taking extensive damage and losing its position, momentarily falling towards that planet's surface. With the ship on its side, the three began running down an elevator shaft, only to lose their footing as the Invisible Hand regained its position. They managed to get out and to a hallway, where they were then captured in a ray shield. They were brought before Skarn in the control room, where Bolt-3, who was also a captive, gave a distraction that allowed Kade and Drayden to take control. With nowhere to run, Skarn broke open a window and found his way to the escape pods, which he activated as he fled. The ship then became caught in Vantor's gravity well and began barreling towards the surface. Drayden and Kade attempted to land it, but only managed to ease the crash. Following the crash, Mal and the Aetheri were escorted to the Senate Building.

#### The seduction of Kael Drayden

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### The seduction of Kael Drayden

> " Soon I will have a new apprentice, one far younger and more powerful. " ―Vael Mal, to Skarn

Mal directed Skarn to return to Uthara on the pretense of ensuring the safety of the increasingly irrelevant Dissident Council. In reality, he had other intentions for the general, whose usefulness to Mal had come to its end. Unaware he was being set up again, Skarn—whose campaigns had served to distract the Aetheri Order from the Umbra conspiracy unfolding around them on Vantor —had only one role left to play: he had to serve as bait to lure Kade away from Vantor and Drayden. Mal did not care if Skarn or Kade lived or died, as his plan was ready to bring down the Republic and the Aetheri and seduce Drayden to the umbra side.

title: Theron Mal
text: Mal soon began preparing for the war's end. Mal instructed Skarn to move the Dissidents to Emberfall. He also told him to remain on Uthara until his new apprentice had joined their cause since he did not want to waste any time before finding a replacement. Drayden, who had just been hailed as a hero for killing Count Varek and rescuing the Chancellor, began having visions of his wife dying in childbirth. Mal decided to use that to his advantage. Throughout the next few rotations, their relationship kept growing. Ultimately, Mal appointed Drayden to be his representative to the Aetheri Council. During what ended up becoming the last full session of the Republic Senate, the Petition of 2,000 was officially unveiled. However, Mal still managed to find an advantage in the current political atmosphere, telling and convincing Drayden that Ondar could have ulterior motives she was keeping secret from them both.

title: Theron Mal
text: Meanwhile, the Aetheri began to distrust and resent the Chancellor's accumulating power and control. The Council, who was not happy with Drayden's appointment by one not of their order, denied him the rank of "Aetheri Master." This turn of events simply furthered Mal' plans. The Council, however, decided to use this appointment as a chance to spy on Mal. Drayden, who felt insulted by that demand, regretfully agreed and began to devote his time to getting to know the Chancellor better. Some Aetheri, such as Drevan Koss, were concerned about their relationship, seeing that it could be dangerous putting the two together. Koss ultimately noted that the umbra side of Synth Flux surrounded the Chancellor.

title: Theron Mal
text: At an opera show, Mal and Drayden discussed the situation with Mal revealing to know that the Council wanted Drayden to spy on him. At the same time, Drayden, who was dealing with the fear of his wife's loss was beginning to distrust the Aetheri Council. This allowed Mal to orchestrate Drayden's downfall; he claimed that the Aetheri and the Umbra were alike in nearly every way, setting the stage for the young Aetheri to switch sides while playing to his devotion to the Aetheri ideology. Next, Mal told him the story of his master, "Vael Plagueis the Wise." According to the story, Plagueis possessed such strength in Synth Flux that he could use it to prevent the ones closest to him from dying. Drayden asked what happened to him, to which Mal said that he was afraid of losing his power, but had taught his apprentice everything, and then his apprentice killed him in his sleep. Drayden, enthralled by the story, wished to know more about this power, asking him if he himself could learn it with Mal stating that, though possible, such things could not be taught by members of the Order. Drayden, however, was unaware that Mal

title: Theron Mal
text:
his apprentice killed him in his sleep. Drayden, enthralled by the story, wished to know more about this power, asking him if he himself could learn it with Mal stating that, though possible, such things could not be taught by members of the Order. Drayden, however, was unaware that Mal was really talking about how he killed his mentor Plagueis, in order to lure him to the umbra side. As the situation grew worse, Drayden went to speak with the Chancellor regarding the Battle of Uthara . Kael expressed his disappointment that he was not chosen for the assignment. Mal told Drayden that the Council did not trust him and that the Aetheri Council were plotting to take control of the Republic. He then revealed that he was trained in the ways of Synth Flux, "even the nature of the umbra side," the power that could save his wife Ondar from certain death. This led to Drayden concluding that Mal himself was the Umbra Lord the Aetheri were hunting down and drawing his flux blade. Although Drayden considered killing Mal, the young Aetheri was deeply conflicted realizing that he could not lose the Umbra Lord as he thought he needed to learn the umbra side power to "save" his wife. Stunned by the revelation, Drayden responded by reporting Mal to the Aetheri and went to the Aetheri Council with this information.

#### The fate of the galaxy

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### The fate of the galaxy

> " In the name of the Galactic Senate of the Republic, you are under arrest, Chancellor. " " Are you threatening me, Master Aetheri? " " The Senate will decide your fate. " " I am the Senate. " " Not yet. " ―Drevan Koss and Vael Mal

Drevan Koss, realizing that the Aetheri had been deceived by Mal, after learning about the Chancellor's double identity from Drayden, went to confront the Chancellor along with fellow Aetheri Council Masters Kit Fisto , Agen Kolar , as well as Saesee Tiin . Koss and the three other Aetheri boldly ignited their flux blades and declared that he was under arrest. Igniting his own crimson flux blade, Mal declared the four Aetheri as traitors to the Republic. Letting out an inhuman wail of fury, he then lunged forward and slew Kolar and Tiin in mere seconds , and Fisto slightly later, leaving Koss to face the Dark Lord alone. Mal and Koss then engaged in a ferocious one-on-one duel. While the fight appeared to be even, Koss eventually disarmed him, knocked him to the floor and held him at blade point.

title: Theron Mal
text: Drayden soon arrived after this and both sides tried to persuade him that the other was a traitor. Koss taunted Mal in his defeat which prompted the Umbra Lord to attempt to kill Koss with Synth Flux lightning, but Koss managed to deflect it back at Mal, causing the Umbra Lord's returning to the disfigured form that it hid for years, due to the umbra side energy emanating from the lightning. As a result of this, Mal then switched his strategy to pretending to be a defenseless old man, dropping his lightning attack and proclaiming that he was too weak to carry on. Drayden told Koss that Mal had to stand trial, though Koss claimed that Mal possessed far too much influence to be left alive, as he controlled both the courts and the senate. Deciding that his wife's survival was more important than his loyalty to the Aetheri Order, Drayden betrayed Koss by cutting off his flux blade hand, giving Mal the opening to drop his feigned weakness and throw Koss out the office window with a full barrage of Synth Flux lightning.

title: Theron Mal
text: Drayden, although initially stunned by what he had done, ultimately viewed Koss's transgressions as the final act of Aetheri hypocrisy that he would not tolerate, and knelt before the now-scarred Chancellor, agreeing to join the umbra side on the condition that he was be shown how to save Ondar's life, thus betraying the Aetheri. Mal bestowed on the young man the Umbra name of Xarn Velgor, promising the young apprentice that together they would discover the hidden art of preventing death. That Mal was now claiming he did not know how to cheat death, when prior he had suggested he already knew the secret, was overlooked by Velgor; by telling Velgor that Ondar could be saved, Mal had told Velgor what he wanted to hear and, thus, had groomed his apprentice to overlook the contradiction. Mal informed Velgor of his intention to purge the galaxy of all Aetheri, claiming that the Order was a threat to the Senate as well as the security of the Republic. #### Rise of the New Order

Consolidation of power

> " In order to ensure the security and continuing stability, the Republic will be reorganized into the first Imperium! For a safe and secure society! " ―Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info )

After the Aetheri Sanctum fell, Mal arrived within and congratulated his new apprentice after affirming he had done as commanded; Velgor had killed many Aetheri during the siege, including Adepts and younglings, much to Mal' delight. After assuring Velgor he had done well, Mal ordered his apprentice to bring peace to their newly rising imperium, dispatching him to Emberfall to wipe out the Dissident leaders. Their conversation was captured by the Temple's security holograms. Mal then contacted the Dissident Council to inform them that Velgor would arrive and take care of them, although none of them were aware that Mal had actually betrayed them and had sent Velgor to kill them.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Assembling the Senate in special session , Mal, as Mal, addressed the Republic and deceitfully accused the Aetheri of attempting to assassinate him and overthrow the government, using his newly scarred face as evidence. Affirming that the Aetheri insurgency, as he called it, had been shut down, by the loyal Replica Army, Mal assured the Senate any remaining Aetheri would be found and wiped away. Taking advantage of the fear and death he had spread across the galaxy and presenting himself as the man who had ended the war and the supposed Aetheri insurgency it had been building to, he announced the Republic's reorganization into the First Imperium, promising a destructive conflict would never again be unleashed under its watch. In the process, he declared himself Emperor of the new regime, with little if any coalition from the majority of the senators present.

Battle in the Senate Chamber

title: Theron Mal
text:
Battle in the Senate Chamber

> " I have waited a long time for this moment, my little green friend. " ―Vael Mal, to Zho

With Kade and Zho realizing what had happened upon witnessing a recording within the Aetheri Sanctum, Zho went to face the Emperor personally, while a reluctant Orien stowed away onboard Ondar's yacht , en route to Emberfall to kill Velgor. Upon arriving at the working office of the Chancellery Secretariat , Zho disposed of the pair of guardsmen by the entryway, surprising Mal. Within moments, however, the Umbra Lord had recollected himself, unleashing a barrage of Synth Flux lightning at the Aetheri Master after a brief exchange of acknowledgement between the two. Zho quickly recovered and Synth Flux pushed Mal backwards. Zho then engaged him in a duel when he refused to allow Mal to escape. Mal declared that Velgor would become more powerful than both of them, while Zho told Mal that his faith in his nascent apprentice was a mistake, along with his faith in the umbra side.

title: Theron Mal
text:
The two then dueled in the Senate hall. No longer having his flux blade shortly after, Mal utilized the use of his Synth Flux powers by sending numerous Senate pods at the Aetheri Master, which he closely dodged. Zho eventually managed to redirect one of Mal' pods at him, which the Umbra Lord dodged. Mal then unleashed a torrent of Synth Flux lightning at Zho, which he was able to redirect back on him, giving the Aetheri master the upper hand. However, the buildup of energy led to an explosion that caused Mal to fall back and Zho to take a huge fall to the ground. Luckily, Mal managed to hang on to the pod and climb back up. While neither conquered the other, Zho believed he had lost since he was unable to stop Mal; the Aetheri Master opted to flee, deciding to go into exile.

Rescuing Velgor

> " I sense Lord Velgor is in danger. " ―Vael Mal

title: Theron Mal
text:
Rescuing Velgor

> " I sense Lord Velgor is in danger. " ―Vael Mal

As Imperial shock troopers of the Vantor Guard arrived in the Senate Chamber following the battle, the Emperor stood with Mazan Veldon on a Senatorial pod as they searched for the Aetheri Master. However, they could not find any trace of a body. The Emperor had more pressing concerns however: he had sensed that Velgor, far away on Emberfall, was in danger of being destroyed. He ordered the replicas to double their search for Zho, and that his shuttle be prepared to depart.

The Emperor made haste to Emberfall, accompanied by a squad of the best shock troopers under the authority of Commander Thire . On planet, he found that Velgor had been dismembered, horrifically burned, and left for dead by Orien Kade after the conclusion of their duel. He ordered the replicas accompanying him to prepare a medical capsule for his apprentice. As they left to obey his instructions, the Emperor crouched beside his fallen apprentice, determined to find a way to keep him alive.

title: Theron Mal
text:
The Emperor was keenly aware that, without Velgor, the foundations of his newfound power would be badly shaken; he needed an apprentice capable of ensuring that his Imperium would survive the inevitable challenges that would rise up against it. To make certain that Velgor would be capable of remaining a powerful apprentice, the Emperor contacted the boldest scientists he could, those whose practices would have been frowned on by the Aetheri and the Republic. Among these scientists was an expert in cybernetics named Doctor Silvar .

The Emperor brought Velgor to the Grand Medical Facility, far above Vantor's surface as a storm raged across the capital. A strenuous night followed during which the scientists, their droids and their technology worked to save the critically injured Velgor before he died. The new Umbra apprentice was kept awake for the whole procedure, feeling the pain that came with saving his life. Silvar and the other scientists designed a suit of armor that would protect his weakened body and allow his scorched lungs to breathe. Cybernetic limbs were added to replace the legs and the arm that Kade had taken.

title: Theron Mal
text: After what the Emperor would call a "long night," Drayden was surgically reconstructed as a cyborg and encased in the armor and mask that would forever hide away who he had once been from the galaxy. As the procedure ended and the Umbra apprentice rose, the Emperor approached him. Velgor's first query was to know whether or not his wife was safe. The Emperor told him that he had killed Ondar in his anger. This final loss sent Velgor over the edge of pure wrath and anguish, completing his transition into the apprentice Mal had spent decades grooming. In his rage, Velgor used his new limbs to tear away the restraints that held him to the operating table and Synth Flux to destroy the droids who had just saved his life, before stepping unsteadily onto his new legs and screaming his despair to the galaxy as a satisfied Mal looked on with a devilish smile. Having Synth Flux choked Ondar on Emberfall, Velgor remembered that he had, indeed, attacked his wife and thus believed the Emperor's claim that he had killed her.

title: Theron Mal
text: Velgor then turned his rage onto the Emperor, throwing him into the wall of the operating room with Synth Flux. He angrily berated his master for promising that he could save his wife from death. The Emperor conceded that he had failed him in that regard but countered that, with her death, Ondar had given him something so much stronger: pain. This pain would fuel his power for decades and make him the dreaded Umbra apprentice that Mal had always coveted. It would also allow him to live. After a tense few moments, Velgor released his master and proclaimed that he would live. Satisfied, the Emperor then assaulted Velgor with Synth Flux lightning, pointing out his apprentice's lack of a flux blade. Afterward, Mal warned Velgor never to use Synth Flux against him in such a way again, or he would finish what Kade would not.

title: Theron Mal
text: Believing he had killed his wife and accepting Mal's claim that the pain it brought him was a gift that would usher in his new life, Velgor invested himself entirely in Mal, just as the Umbra Lord had hoped. With Velgor cutting himself off from his remaining friends and family by believing the Emperor's claims and accepting the hatred growing inside him, Mal became his only safe haven and source of guidance. Further, Mal elected to maintain the illusion of friendship between them both for at least the time being. Meanwhile, having demonstrated his apprentice's need for a new flux blade, Mal showed Velgor a ceremony during which many of the weapons looted from the Aetheri Sanctum were incinerated. Mal also explained the red color of Umbra flux blades , obtained through the process of bleeding a kyber crystal taken from a slain Aetheri. He then dispatched Velgor to obtain one for himself. Velgor proceeded to hunt down and kill Aetheri Master Kirak Infil'a on Al'doleem , taking his flux blade . At Mal' direction, he returned to Emberfall, bleeding his new crystal there in a umbra side cave . Mal was in the middle of a meeting with Wilhard

title: Theron Mal
text:
one for himself. Velgor proceeded to hunt down and kill Aetheri Master Kirak Infil'a on Al'doleem , taking his flux blade . At Mal' direction, he returned to Emberfall, bleeding his new crystal there in a umbra side cave . Mal was in the middle of a meeting with Wilhard Varrix when a battle-damaged Velgor returned, bursting into the room and presenting the new weapon to his master. #### Personal and political projects

Search for ultimate power

> " For an Umbra Lord craves absolute power, and nothing will stop me from attaining it. Not even death itself. " ―Vael Mal

After the creation of his Umbra Imperium, Mal established himself in the old Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor, transforming the most famous of the Aetheri Order's temples into his Imperial Palace. The Aetheri had built the palace atop an ancient Umbra shrine , in order to neutralize and cap the dark power that sprang from its depths. Mal entrusted the reopening and restoration of the ancient temple to droids under the supervision of 11-4D , a protocol droid inherited from Vael Plagueis.

title: Theron Mal
text: Secure in power as Emperor of the galaxy, Mal pursued his obsession with immortality; leaving the bureaucratic work of the government to his followers, which further allowed Mal to enjoy ruling the galaxy without concerning himself with the more boring aspects of administration, he mostly withdrew from the public eye to probe the secrets of the umbra side and study his Umbra arcana extensively to unlock the ability to live forever. He prepared the ancient Umbra world of Umbrale, constructing a base of power within the Umbra Citadel located on the surface, planning to claim the ancient throne of the Umbra as his permanent seat of power. His loyal cult following, the Umbra Eternal , began to experiment with technology and genetic replication science to expand his lifespan. Umbrale was also home to his most promising experimentations within a vergence of Synth Flux.

title: Theron Mal
text:
The planet Byss in the Deep Core was of great importance to Mal. Ultimately, Mal's true goal was for the Void Core to take over as the symbol of fear that would keep the galaxy in line, giving himself and Velgor the freedom to pursue the deepest secrets of the umbra side. Beyond simple immortality, Mal sought the power to alter reality itself and bring every living being under his dark control. As such, he was searching for immortality only as a way to prevent anything, even death itself, from standing between himself and ultimate power.

Over many years, Mal sent explorers to unmapped regions of space to search for the source of the umbra side, believing it lay there. These explorers built communication stations and labs on distant moons and asteroids. As part of his planned Contingency, Mal had Imperial scouts explore the Unknown Regions while also utilizing extensive resources to seed laboratories, shipyards, and observatories within that same region. This arrangement would continue over a period of decades and would be known solely by him and the elect.

Unnatural fatherhood

title: Theron Mal
text:
Unnatural fatherhood

> " Using a technique known as Strand-Casting, countless modified replica bodies were produced from my genetic template. All but one of them were utter failures. The lone subject that survived the replication process lacked any connection to Synth Flux. I rejected this useless creature, but I chose to let it live. Even if this 'son' was undeserving of my legacy, I surmised that the Mal blood rushing through its veins might someday become useful. " ―Vael Mal The Umbra Eternal utilized a method of replication known as Strand-Casting in addition to modified Gelvarian replication technology, producing countless modified cloned bodies of Mal' original in the attempt to give him a vessel worthy of containing and preserving his essence, so he could ultimately obtain immortality. In 12 BVE , the only survivor of this process, that grew and aged normally, was created. Designed and assembled from Mal' replica tissue samples and other donated blood cells, the artificial construct was thriving in health and had the Mal bloodline rushing through his veins. The unnamed strandcast was the Dark Lord's "son." The strandcast, not a direct cloned replicate of Mal, so nor entirely identical in appearance, was ultimately be a source of disappointment for Mal. Mal was disgusted with the son he sired through science; the boy possessed no synth flux-sensitivity like his father, and Mal, who relished the powers of Synth Flux, immediately rejected the "useless creature" that was his son. Mal deemed the boy an example of such "disappointing ordinariness," unable to bare even looking upon him, the inferior child spawned from his flesh undeserving of his legacy.

title: Theron Mal
text:
But the Umbra Lord surmised, that because the boy possessed his blood, he might still produce some usefulness at some point. Therefore, Mal chose to permit his son to continue living, the replica's health providing Mal the means to continue on his bloodline and possibly yield more promising results for producing a vessel for his spirit through more natural means. For this reason, Mal granted his cloned progeny protection from the Umbra Eternal cultists, them being unable to "recycle" him as a failed experiment, and allowing him to live on Umbrale. Mal neglected his son, ignoring him like the cultists, never naming him, and hardly acknowledging his existence. However, Mal made his son aware of Synth Flux and its nature as the mystical energy of the galaxy that surrounded all life, particularly the umbra side, as well as the Umbra who wielded them.

The Varrix Initiative

title: Theron Mal
text:
The Varrix Initiative

In his early days as Senator Mal, Mal had closely associated with Wilhard Varrix, whom he encouraged to pursue a career in politics after his training with the Judicials was completed. Varrix went on to become Governor of Eriadu and one of the Republic's foremost military leaders during the Replica Wars. Mal had learned of Varrix's upbringing on Eriadu, where he had been trained in harsh conditions through a brutal initiation in the wild Carrion Plateau of his homeworld. Varrix had been taught to hunt savage creatures and emerged from his training with the belief that only the brutal application of the law and the fear of synth flux could keep beings in line with a central galactic government. Although Varrix lacked Synth Flux-sensitivity, Mal identified him as one whose mindset was very close to that of the Umbra.

title: Theron Mal
text:
During the early days of the Imperium, making a rare public address, Mal claimed the Imperium would do whatever was needed to ensure a lasting reconciliation now that the Replica Wars had ended. At some point during the Imperial Era, Mal created an Imperial hunter droid named M-OC ; additionally the B1 battle droid R0-GR of the Freymarks later claimed to have fought Mal. The Ehllo family was an influential political dynasty during the Imperial Era, with Mal personally knowing Captain Cerasus Ehllo 's father . As such, Captain Ehllo was able to make a Raider -class corvette , the King's Ransom , into his flagship.

The Warden Order

> " My Lord, am I to be Umbra? " " Oh, no, my child. But you will serve the greater cause. " ―Iskat Vekkis and Vael Mal

title: Theron Mal
text:
Within his first year as Emperor of the Imperium, Mal brought to fruition an old idea with the formation of the Warden Order , an organization composed of umbra side adepts and tasked with hunting down surviving Aetheri. The Wardens were primarily captured Aetheri who had been tortured until they turned to the umbra side. However, a few, such as the the Grand Warden and the Fifth Warden , joined the Warden Order of their own accord. Another was the former Aetheri Knight Iskat Vekkis, who Mal spoke to in the Warden Order Headquarters on Vantor, not long after she had received her uniform. He tested her willingness to continue her training in the umbra side and made sure she understood that she and her fellow Wardens were substantially inferior to him. Mal was impressed by Vekkis' wits, as she had quickly realized that he was an Umbra Lord and had by now identified the agent he had assigned to help nudge her away from the Aetheri over the course of the Replica Wars. He then told her to choose her path carefully before turning her over to the Fifth Warden.

The hunt for Jocasta Nura

title: Theron Mal
text:
The hunt for Jocasta Nura

> " She is ancient. Middling in Synth Flux. Barely competent with a flux blade. And yet, that crone could end everything we are trying to do. For you see, Jocasta Nura knows everything. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

Sometime after his duel with Kirak Infil'a, Velgor reported to Mal on the ongoing training of the Wardens while also asking why Master Jocasta Nura was considered a priority among the list of surviving Aetheri. Mal explained that the threat she posed was that of knowledgeable scholar, one with access to a library of secrets and Synth Flux artifacts to rival any other. Additionally, Nura possessed the Aetheri catalogue of Synth Flux-sensitive children in the galaxy. Mal emphasized to his apprentice the need to capture her alive, insisting that they could use Nura's knowledge but could not afford to let her fall into the hands of others.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Thus, he ordered Velgor to utilize the Wardens in his search but to keep the true nature of Nura's threat hidden from them. In a later meeting, Velgor Synth Flux choked an officer for giving a poor report until Mal commanded him to release the man. While he could sympathize with his apprentice's frustration at the lack of Aetheri to eliminate, Mal warned Velgor to avoid unnecessary killing of their inferiors. Not long after, Velgor contacted Mal to report that Nura had died while attempting to escape his custody, a development Mal considered regrettable.

#### The Imperial military

Establishing the hierarchy

> " This is Lord Velgor. He speaks with my voice. A command from him is as a command from me. Pass this information down to your men. All must understand. " ―Theron Mal

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### The Imperial military

Establishing the hierarchy

> " This is Lord Velgor. He speaks with my voice. A command from him is as a command from me. Pass this information down to your men. All must understand. " ―Theron Mal

After foiling two attempts on his life, Velgor traced an assassination conspiracy to the highest levels of the Imperial government and proceeded to meet Mal near Nura's secret vault. Despite his apprentice's failure to capture Nura alive, Mal was pleased with the artifacts recovered from her hoard. In response to Velgor's suspicion of him, Mal took a moment to examine his apprentice's rebuilt flux blade , nodding in approval over the change from Kirak Infil'a's original hilt. He then pointed out that he had no need to hire mercenaries to eliminate Velgor if he had wanted him dead. Mal told Velgor that dealing with the plot was his own responsibility, warning him that with great power come infinite enemies to destroy.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Velgor soon identified one of the conspirators, an Imperial officer, and sought the Emperor's permission to make an example to solidify his role in the Imperium's hierarchy. Mal agreed, telling him that he could kill any officer but Varrix. Later, the Emperor gathered the Imperial Officer Corps , presenting his apprentice to them and telling them that they were to treat Velgor as they would him. Velgor then called for the known conspirator and four random officers to step forward, before Synth Flux choking them to death in front of the assembly.

Replacing the replica army

> " Perhaps, it is time for a change. Now more than ever, building a strong galaxy requires protection and security. Due to the nefarious actions of Admiral Rampart, and the immediacy of the bill on the floor today, it is my opinion that this legislation is our future. With this momentous act, we shall usher in a new era. Heralded by the Imperial shock trooper. " ―Theron Mal, to the Imperial Senate

title: Theron Mal
text: Around the same time, Mal saw fit to finally replace the outdated Replica Army with a new conscripted military that would be loyal to him. However, in spite of his power in reality being absolute, he continued using the Senate as a puppet to make it seem that his role as Emperor was not particularly different from when he was Chancellor. Therefore, Mal relied on people interested in sharing in his power, such as Admiral Edmon Rampart : idealistic followers that could serve as scapegoats while furthering the Umbra Lord's plans. Governor Varrix had perceived the replicas to be twice as expensive as a proposed new militaristic synth flux and deemed them less capable as tools to keep the order. Already that year, the stage was secretly being set to replace the replicas with an army of volunteers and conscripts from across the galaxy. The Gelvarians clung to the fact that their skills as replicators was the only thing of relevance to the Imperium. However, their overall use was terminated when Admiral Rampart ordered the destruction of Tipoca City after clearing out it of valuables.

title: Theron Mal
text: Following the successful orbital bombardment of Tipoca City, the Imperium's official explanation was that the replication facilities had been sunk down to the oceans by a harsh storm, despite the structures having been built to endure Gelvaris's extreme climate. By the next year, new legislation of interest to Mal lay before the Senate: the Imperial Defense Recruitment Bill , a formalization of the Replica Army's decommissioning and the shift to an Imperial Military. Mal preferred not to deal with the issue directly, having Vice Chair Mazan Veldon preside over Senate sessions with Rampart pushing for the bill. A major opponent of the proposed legislation was Senator Riyo Chuchi who sought to provide missing representation for the replicas in the development of the bill. During a Senate session, Senator Solen asked Mazan Veldon what the absent Emperor's position on the bill was; the Vice Chair replied that the Emperor preferred to remain neutral, trusting the Senate to act in the best interests of Imperial citizens. However, given that Rampart's fabrication about Tipoca City's fall was not strudy enough to stand up to too much digging by opposing senators, Veldon told Rampart that expediency was necessary and warned him that he would

title: Theron Mal
text: remain neutral, trusting the Senate to act in the best interests of Imperial citizens. However, given that Rampart's fabrication about Tipoca City's fall was not strudy enough to stand up to too much digging by opposing senators, Veldon told Rampart that expediency was necessary and warned him that he would suffer if he could not placate Chuchi and the others. Despite Rampart's efforts to appease his detractors and obfuscate independent investigation, the bill was rejected twice in preliminary hearings, the harshest criticisms being voiced by Senators Chuchi, Solen and Pamlo. When the bill was at last about brought before the chamber for a vote with Rampart having satisfied Chuchi's demands for a fair retirement for the replicas, the Pantoran Senator interjected again, bringing forward former Gelvarian Senator Halle Burtoni to testify how Rampart had reappropriated Senate funds designated for Gelvaris directly into financing his own projects and recruitments. As Rampart attempted to explain this away, Senator Solen entered and played a command log taken from Rampart's own Vorash showing the entire Senate how Tipoca City really fell.

title: Theron Mal
text: Faced with a drastic situation, the Emperor saw fit to finally attend a Senate hearing in person and arose in his Chancellor's podium, which caused the entire Senate hall to fall silent as their leader made one of his few appearances since the Imperium's foundation. Fraught with overwhelming evidence, the Emperor decided that Rampart's value had ceased and had Mazan Veldon direct guards to arrest him. Not allowing this to stop his plans to remove the replicas, the Emperor spoke out with the same mannerisms as when he was Chancellor and voiced his surprise at Admiral Rampart's acts of transgression against the Gelvarians. He promised that the admiral would be punished for his treachery.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Now faced with a golden opportunity, the Emperor manipulated the situation to benefit his own position by reminding the Senators that Rampart did not act alone; that the replicas aboard the Venators willingly unleashed carnage upon their own home without hesitation. Providing sound argument that security in the galaxy was needed more than ever and recognizing the bill's immediate necessity, the Emperor stated his belief that the Imperial Defense Recruitment Bill was their future. Despite framing this as more of a suggestion than an order, the Emperor displayed how supreme his authority was as the bill was immediately passed.

Although he had presented a compelling narrative, many senators remained skeptical. Nonetheless, Mal had made a crucial step in further facilitating his power in the Imperium and control over the galaxy, confirming the phasing out of the replica army and eliminating another crucial remnant of the Republic, with only the Senate remaining. The age of the Imperial shock trooper had now begun.

Invasion of Mon Calvarra

title: Theron Mal
text:
Invasion of Mon Calvarra

> " Mon Calvarra. They may serve well as an example--the price of defiance. The military power of the Imperium has grown significantly in these past months. It is time to reveal that strength. " ―Vael Mal

Mal soon chose to demonstrate the power of the revamped Imperial Military by invading Mon Calvarra . Since Project Stardust was far from complete, he opted to send a task synth flux commanded by Varrix to occupy the planet. Suspecting that a surviving Aetheri had been advising King Liarch , Mal sent Velgor and the Warden Order along to root out and eliminate the threat. The ensuing battle ended in an Imperial victory after Varrix ordered an orbital bombardment which compelled Liarch to surrender. At the same time, the Aetheri Ferren Barr confronted Velgor, revealing that he had helped orchestrate events leading to the Imperial genocide of Mon Calvarra after having foreseen the role the Calavane would later play in defeating the Imperium. Shortly thereafter, Barr was slain by the Umbra Lord in a flux blade duel.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Later that same year, Varrix contacted Mal when Velgor entered the Halcyon vault without authorization to learn more for himself about Project Stardust. Mal ordered Velgor to help Varrix by rooting out saboteurs whose work was slowing down the project's progress, sending him to Pyralis. He also put Velgor under the Governor's command.

Visit to Mount Tantiss

> " It is imperative that this facility remain hidden and secure. There are many, even within our own ranks, who would consider much of your work an abomination. But they lack the vision we possess. Your brilliance is a great asset to this Imperium. " ―Theron Mal, to Doctor Hemlock

title: Theron Mal
text:
Six months after the Senate voted to replace the replica army, the Emperor made a surprise visit to the secret Mount Tantiss facility on Wayland to review the progress Doctors Royce Hemlock and Nalle Seris had made on Project Necromancer . Hemlock gave him a tour of the site, ending with a tightly guarded chamber containing specimens crucial to the project. The doctor stated that with more time and resources, he was confident that they would be able to successfully replicate M-counts. Considering their work of paramount importance, the Emperor assured Hemlock that he would have whatever he required for the project.

On the landing pad, en route to his shuttle, the Emperor stressed to Hemlock the need to keep the existence of the base a secret, warning that many beings, even other Imperials, would not look kindly upon the research being performed there. Mal then complimented the doctor on his brilliance, with Hemlock responding that, with an appointment to scientific minister, he would be able to bring his abilities to bear upon the entire scientific corps. The Emperor warned him to be patient before departing.

The Chyrr from the Unknown Regions

title: Theron Mal
text:
The Chyrr from the Unknown Regions

During the Imperium's reign, Mal' interest in the Unknown Regions continued. This came to a head when the crew of the Vorash -class Iron Cruiser Strikefast , under the command of Captain Voss Parck , encountered the Chyrr known as Vorren in Wild Space . Many years earlier, Kael Drayden told Mal of this alien and how they worked together. This alien claimed to have a great deal of knowledge on the Unknown Regions. Vorren was then brought before the Emperor on Vantor in order to be questioned. Vorren told the Emperor of threats lurking within the Unknown Regions and how they might one day find the Imperium and offered his military skills. The Emperor then deduced that Vorren's intentions were to help protect his people from these threats. Vorren assured the Emperor that his allegiance would be to the Imperium. Vorren then revealed that he had known Kael Drayden during the Replica Wars, thus proving who he was to the Emperor.

title: Theron Mal
text:
For their service, the Emperor promised Captain Parck and his crew rewards. Vorren however, requested that his translator Eli Vanto stay with him. The Emperor then asked Vorren to walk with him outside. In his personal garden, the Emperor told the Chyrr of his interest in the Unknown Regions. Vorren then warned that there was great danger to be found there, however, he assured the Emperor that he would share his knowledge of the Unknown Regions. The Emperor ordered that Eli Vanto would be transferred to Vorren's side and that they would both undergo training at the Royal Imperial Academy .

#### Mission to Selvara

An official visit

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### Mission to Selvara

An official visit

Five years after the end of the Replica Wars, Chavar Kryll , a war hero who liberated Selvara from the Dissident forces during the war, organized and led the Free Selvara Movement in order to liberate his homeworld once again, this time from an Imperial military occupation. Mal summoned the Senator of Selvara, Orn Free Taa , in order to incorporate the senator into his plan to eradicate the "terrorists." He ordered the Velari to accompany him and his right-hand man, Xarn Velgor, for an official visit to Selvara. Once Mal dismissed Taa, Velgor asked him why he couldn't simply wipe out the Senator along with his entire staff, in which the two Umbra suspected there were one or more traitors, who provided aid to the terrorist movement. But the Emperor wished to find the roots of the treachery, eliminate them and make of it an example for the entire galaxy. Eventually, he ordered Velgor to inform the Moff of Selvara, Delian Mors , of the arrival of Senator Orn Free Taa, but not of the two of them.

Assassination attempt on the Defiance

title: Theron Mal
text:
Assassination attempt on the Defiance

While on the way to Selvara aboard the Iron Cruiser Perilous , Mal instructed the ship to stop at the Denon system for a meeting on the training cruiser Defiance with several Imperial Navy chiefs to discuss a realignment of the Imperial Naval Academy. Mal ordered Xarn Velgor to oversee training exercises conducted by Commandant Pell Baylo while the Emperor was in his meeting with the naval chiefs. During one such exercise, Baylo set a hyperspace route that would have crashed the Defiance into Krestophis' sun . Cadet Raena Vexana and Xarn Velgor uncovered this assassination attempt and redirected the Defiance . Baylo confronted the Emperor, accusing the Imperium of being a hostile synth flux that had taken over the Vantor Republic. Velgor killed Baylo, which upset Mal, who wanted Baylo to suffer as the Navy becomes something he hated and watch as the Defiance was decommissioned and turned into "cafeteria trays." Instead, the Defiance was renamed Obedience as a final jab at Baylo and a not-so-subtle reminder toward Velgor to remember his place, and Mal and Velgor re-boarded the Perilous and continued on their way to Selvara.

The fall of the Perilous

title: Theron Mal
text:
The fall of the Perilous

The two Umbra and Senator Taa came to the Selvara system aboard Perilous . When the ship exited from the hyperspace, they found themselves in the middle of a minefield: Kryll was waiting for them. The Velari wished to eliminate them to strike at the heart of the Imperium. However, Mal was unperturbed by the ambush, having evidently foreseen such an occurrence. When the shields were overwhelmed, Mal remained on the bridge, while Velgor took off with his fighter leading a squadron to deal with a swarm of vulture droids . The former Dissident fighters released thousands of explosive buzz droids which further damaged the Iron Cruiser. Velgor returned aboard the Perilous where he met the Emperor and Senator Taa after finding that the Emperor's personal shuttle had been destroyed in the attack. Because he suspected there was a traitor in the Senator's staff, Mal ordered to isolate them in their own quarters and deny them access to any communications equipment.

title: Theron Mal
text: In the meantime, a Velari task synth flux reached the ship disguised as a repair team and placed explosive charges in the hyperrelay chamber, to trigger a chain reaction. After discovering the sabotage and realizing that the ship was doomed, Velgor contacted the Emperor. The Emperor informed Velgor that he had prepared a second shuttle either as a contingency or because he had foreseen the destruction of the first shuttle and told Velgor to meet him there. However, Velgor delayed his arrival by a few minutes in an attempt to find and eliminate the saboteurs. The Velari insurgents just barely managed to escape, and so Velgor hurried to the Emperor's shuttle, which departed as soon as Velgor was aboard. A few minutes later, the Perilous exploded. Once in space, the fugitive task synth flux searched for the Imperial shuttle and caught up with it. Velgor Synth Flux choked the coalition pilot of the pursuing ship through the shuttle viewport. In a desperate attempt to get free from Velgor's grasp and to kill both him and the Emperor, the Velaris rammed the stolen starship into the Imperial shuttle, critically damaging the latter. Velgor attempted to regain control of the shuttle while

title: Theron Mal
text:
pilot of the pursuing ship through the shuttle viewport. In a desperate attempt to get free from Velgor's grasp and to kill both him and the Emperor, the Velaris rammed the stolen starship into the Imperial shuttle, critically damaging the latter. Velgor attempted to regain control of the shuttle while Mal remembered they had already been in situations like this. Thanks to the piloting skills of Velgor the shuttle crash-landed on Selvara's surface, in the middle of a forest. Isolated on the planet

> " We are all of us, always being tested, my friend. Tests make us stronger, and strength is power, and power is the point . We must pass all the tests we face… Or die in the effort. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

title: Theron Mal
text: Once on the planet surface, Mal noted with mild annoyance that the landing had been far beneath what he knew Velgor to be capable of and that Velgor's lapse had left four corpses in the rear compartment of the shuttle. Velgor admitted to having been distracted by thoughts of his past and attempted to dismiss it as nothing. Mal however, was unconvinced, though he shelved the matter and proceeded with Velgor into the rear compartment. There, three of the shuttle's occupants, Sergeant Erstin Deez , his captain, and another member of the Imperial Guard had survived the crash, though one was badly injured and unconscious. Velgor noted with mild surprise that the Emperor appeared to have been wrong; there were only three corpses in the compartment. One of the conscious guards noted that his injured comrade had not strapped himself in during the landing, and as a result had been thrown about the compartment when the ship had crashed. However, the Emperor, apparently already aware of the semi-conscious guard, had him executed for his stupidity, leaving the fourth corpse he had mentioned earlier.

title: Theron Mal
text:
The survivors exited in the night, and while the two guards who survived were checking the survival kits, Velgor asked his master if he was testing him. Mal answered they were always being tested, and they must pass all tests to gain strength and power. Meanwhile, the guards had activated the generator and the communication array to call for help. At that moment the Umbra sensed that two Velari ships were approaching and prepared themselves for a confrontation. The Velari insurgent's ships fired upon them, while Velgor, immersed in Synth Flux, deflected the laser beams with his flux blade. The captain suggested to take cover in the woods, but the Emperor refused and instead, removed his cloak, and ignited his flux blade. The two Umbra spun their red blades, turning every shot back at the ships. When the enemy ships engines were hit and began to explode in flames and smoke, Mal unleashed a bolt of Synth Flux lightning on their hulls and then, with Synth Flux, drove one of the ships to the ground, while Velgor did the same with the other. The two freighters exploded, and Velgor sent Deez to check for survivors. They realized the insurgents had jammed the communication network and that they were hunting for them.

Hunted

title: Theron Mal
text:
Hunted

They walked for a long time into the depths of the forest. Mal went forward in the darkness seeing through Synth Flux while testing Velgor's loyalty once again until he decided to stop for a while. While the guards were eating, the two Umbra began to meditate. The Emperor sensed his apprentice's murderous feelings towards him. When Velgor ended his meditation, Mal told him what he had sensed, but the former Aetheri pledged his loyalty to his Umbra Master. At that moment, the guards, whom the Emperor had sent away, had returned, pursued by a horde of lyleks . The Emperor remained calm, sending torrents of Synth Flux lightning against the predators, and began to advance back-to-back with Velgor, their flux blades ignited.

title: Theron Mal
text:
While Velgor and the guardsmen held back the advancing lyleks with their weapons, Mal used Synth Flux to topple trees over the advancing lylek horde. Through Synth Flux, Mal sensed a tunnel a hundred meters away. The four retreated into the tunnel with the lyleks in pursuit. This tunnel turned out to be the home of the lylek horde, and the four Imperials were forced to fight through hundreds of the creatures. The guards used their volt pistols and grenades while the two Umbra Lords used Synth Flux and their flux blades to fight through the horde. As they waded deeper into the cave, Mal realized that the lyleks were herding the intruders towards their queen. At Velgor's instigation, the four resolved to kill all their opponents with the Emperor activating his red blade. After a fierce battle with the lyleks, Mal and Velgor found themselves back-to-back. When Mal asked his apprentice whether he had ever toyed with the idea of letting his Emperor die to fulfill his own ambitions, Velgor admitted he had entertained such thoughts but reassured his master it was only for a moment. Mal accepted Velgor's loyalty and the two joined forces to tackle the lylek queen.

Following a savage battle, Velgor managed to kill the queen; scattering the remaining lyleks. However, the royal guard captain was killed, leaving only Mal, Velgor, and Sergeant Deez. Based on their battle with the lyleks, master and apprentice quickly surmised that Chavar and his insurgents were trying to kill them to bring about the Imperium's destruction. Having triumphed over the lylek horde, the three Imperials found an opening at the end of the tunnel which led back to the forest.

Death and fate

title: Theron Mal
text:
Death and fate

While Mal and his companions were traveling through the forest, they encountered a young Velari girl named Drua . Mal made a move to kill her, but Velgor blocked his master's death blow and convinced Mal that she could lead them to a settlement where they could contact reinforcements. Drua led them to her village , which was home to escaped Velari slaves. When the village head Narmn asked for their identities, Mal introduced himself, Velgor, and Deez as "Krataa," "Irluuk," and the Sergeant. Mal and Velgor alone knew that their pseudonyms stood for "death" and "fate."

title: Theron Mal
text: Mal warned Velgor that his act of mercy towards Drua would cost both her and her fellow villagers their lives. Velgor then managed to win over the villagers by offering to repair an ancient communications device. Once Velgor had fixed the machine, Mal ordered Deez to contact Moff Mors; whom he knew to be loyal. After re-establishing contact with the two Umbra Lords, Mors took steps to eliminate the Imperial traitor Colonel Belka Drayn , who was secretly aiding Chavar's insurgents. She foiled Belka's plot to order Vireo fighters to strike Drua's Village and the massed Free Selvara forces in a nearby quarry. After executing Belka, Moff Mors sent her forces to rendezvous with Mal and Velgor at the Velari village.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Chavar's forces, unwilling to harm the villagers, fired warning shots so that the villagers would flee the scene of the upcoming battle. The villagers reacted by fleeing to a nearby mine shaft, a sanctuary in time of danger. However, Mal, Velgor, and Deez stood their ground at the center of the village. Before Chavar's forces could launch their attack, Moff Mors' forces arrived in two transport vessels and trapped the insurgent fighters. With many of the Free Selvara fighters killed, Chavar narrowly managed to avoid capture at the hands of Velgor. Under the orders of Mal, Mors's Imperial forces massacred the surviving Free Selvara fighters. Following a brief exchange with Chavar's lieutenant Isval , Mal ordered Velgor to execute her and then afterward, the surviving Velari villagers hiding in the mine shaft as well, in order not to leave any witnesses. After a brief moment of hesitation, Velgor complied with his master's orders and massacred the villagers.

### Growing insurgency

#### Berch Teller's campaign

title: Theron Mal
text:
### Growing insurgency

#### Berch Teller's campaign

In 14 BVE, the secret Void Core project was still being constructed above Pyralis and was supplied by a series of marshaling stations. The Imperium faced a new threat in the form of Berch Teller , a former Republic Intelligence agent who opposed the Imperium. He led a insurgent cell consisting of survivors and witnesses of the Antar Atrocity , a mass crackdown on Antar 4 following the Replica Wars that had seen the killing of innocent Gotal and Koorivar loyalists. Teller had a special animus for Varrix, the architect of the Antar Atrocity. He was secretly aided and equipped by Vice Admiral Dodd Rancit , the Director of the Naval Intelligence Agency and a rival of Varrix.

title: Theron Mal
text: Following Teller's attack on Sentinel Base , the Emperor convened a meeting of his Ruling Council to discuss the discovery of a cache of communications jammers on the planet Murkhana . The Imperium Vigil Bureau had purportedly discovered the cache and feared that dissidents were planning to disrupt the Imperial HoloNet ; echoing the Dissident Shadowfeed broadcasts during the Replica Wars. The Emperor dispatched both Moff Varrix and Lord Velgor to investigate the matter. However, this played into Teller's hands and allowed the insurgents to steal Varrix's corvette Carrion Spike , which they intended to turn into a symbol of coalition against the Imperium.

title: Theron Mal
text: After being briefed about the theft of the Carrion Spike , Vice Admiral Rancit suggested that the ship's thieves were the same people who attacked Sentinel Base earlier. In response, the Emperor ordered Rancit to divert Imperial forces in the Belderone system to aid Varrix and Lord Velgor. While Varrix and Velgor pursued the insurgents, the Emperor chaired another meeting of the Ruling Council. During the meeting, Rancit advocated diverting more Imperial forces to reinforcing Imperial facilities across the Perlemian Trade Route and Hydian Way . The Council also learned that Teller' insurgents had attacked the TaggeCo mining facilities on Lucazec and were transmitting holovids of their attacks on the HoloNet.

title: Theron Mal
text: Following a skirmish in the Phindar system between Imperial forces and the stolen Carrion Spike , Rancit convinced the Emperor to deploy interdictor vessels against the insurgents. Grand Vizier Veldon then informed the Emperor that the Murkhana communications jammers had been discovered by an IVB asset tasked with investigating the find by his case officer. Acting on this information, Mal interrogated the Koorivar IVB asset Bracchia and his case officer Stellan , who revealed that they had been tipped about the discovery by Naval Intelligence. After viewing the holovid, the Emperor determined that the communications cache had been planted by a high–level Imperial official who was aiding the insurgents.

title: Theron Mal
text: Meanwhile, Lord Velgor discovered that Rancit was the Imperial traitor and executed him. While Varrix led Imperial forces against Teller's insurgents in a space battle near the Gulf of Dunemere , Vael Mal mediated on his quest for galactic dominance. Following the defeat of Teller's insurgency, Varrix and Velgor spent the next three weeks hunting down Teller's collaborators and contacts in a ruthless crackdown. The two briefed the Emperor, who appointed Varrix as Grand Moff , in which capacity he would serve as governor of the Outer Reach Territories and stand in charge of the Void Core project. The Emperor also reshuffled the Ruling Council in the wake of Rancit's execution, folded Naval Intelligence back into Imperial Intelligence , and established the Council of Moffs .

title: Theron Mal
text:
By 14 BVE, Mal had also ordered for Project Auger to begin on the planet Zeffo , which had been home to the Zeffonian before their hubris nearly destroyed them. The project saw Imperial mining begin on Zeffo to locate artifacts. The commanding officer, Krane , kept one uncovered artifact secret in order to win support from Mal by giving it to him personally. However, she died when the cave she chose to hide it in collapsed.

#### A reward for Velgor

> " I think, one way or another, you will learn a great deal. That is good. After all, your power is my power. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

title: Theron Mal
text: Shortly after he killed Etha Korrin, Velgor attacked the Thirteenth Warden for committing treason. Confused, her partner tried to defend her before they both fled Warden Order Headquarters across Vantor. The Umbra Lord eventually caught up with the couple and slew them. However, the destruction caused by the chase and resultant death of Senator Maklooq , who was important to one of Mal' schemes, led the Emperor to order the Warden Order to be relocated. Their new base was built on Nur . Pleased with the death of Korrin, Mal gifted Velgor the former royal vessel of Queen Ondar. With few Aetheri left to deal with, Mal was about to send his apprentice on other missions when Velgor asked for a world of his own: Emberfall. Mal granted the request but demanded to know why his apprentice had chosen the site of his greatest defeat. Velgor explained that he believed that the umbra side locus there could give him access to the dead Ondar. Mal encouraged him, satisfied that whatever knowledge or power his apprentice gained there would ultimately be his. He gave Velgor one final gift, the mask of Vael Mornick , before sending him to Emberfall with the

title: Theron Mal
text:
that the umbra side locus there could give him access to the dead Ondar. Mal encouraged him, satisfied that whatever knowledge or power his apprentice gained there would ultimately be his. He gave Velgor one final gift, the mask of Vael Mornick , before sending him to Emberfall with the architect Colonel Brenne to design a fortress for him. By 12 BVE , the construction of Fortress Velgor was complete, the eight previous versions all having failed in some manner. Velgor contacted Mal, who was surprised to hear from him after so long, but eager to send him out on more missions for the Imperium. When Mal asked him if he had learned what he needed, Velgor confirmed as much with a simple "yes" and no elaboration.

Sometime around or after this, the Emperor was present at a parade that included two hundred KX-series security droids , among them K2-SO .

#### New threats

From the past to the present

> " I wonder if your thoughts are clear on this, Lord Velgor. Perhaps your feelings for your old master have left you weakened. If your past cannot be overcome… " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

title: Theron Mal
text: In 9 BVE , Xarn Velgor and the Warden Order engaged in a hunt for Orien Kade, who had been engineered to come out of hiding in order to rescue Princess Elira Solen of Cindervale. Though the search had been fabricated by the Third Warden to kill Velgor, her attempts failed, and Velgor and Kade engaged in a flux blade duel on a barren moon as a result. Kade bested Velgor, damaging his armor in the process, and he managed to evade the Imperials on his tail. Not long after, Velgor, whose armor was since repaired, reached out to his master via a hologram at Fortress Velgor, his castle on Emberfall. He informed Mal he had dispatched probe droids to continue the search for Kade, adding that he would not evade him once again. Picking up on Velgor's agitation, Mal questioned if Velgor's thoughts on the matter were clear, continuing that perhaps has feelings for his former master had left him weakened. As Mal asked if Velgor could not overcome his past, Velgor declared that Kade meant nothing, for he only served Mal.

title: Theron Mal
text: With the Aetheri mostly defeated, Mal felt secure behind his huge galactic military and dominion over most of the known galaxy. Despite this, remaining Dissident holdouts and surviving Aetheri would gnaw at his confidence of the longevity of his new Imperium. Seeking to secure the center, the Emperor supported mass military excursions into the Outer Reach Territories in an effort to bring more systems under his fold. With his ultimate goal of bending reality into something of his own creation, an omnipotent Imperium would allow all the galaxy's inhabitants to be held in his dark embrace. Despite the Aetheri being all but extinct, Synth Flux-sensitive children were still being born across the galaxy. In an effort to combat this threat, Mal commanded his apprentice, Lord Velgor, to contact the Grand Warden to hunt them down and destroy them if they did not serve the Imperium.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Following the raid on the Imperial garrison on Aldhani in 5 BVE , Mal spoke with Colonel Yular, giving the IVB direct control of operations going forward and the authority to arrest anyone who was considered a disrupter to the Imperium. The next day, the Emperor convened an emergency session of the Senate in order to propose a legislative package of bills and amendments and to officially invoke the Public Order Resentencing Directive .

Targets on Ghorman and Lorath

> " I believe the apprentice of Kael Drayden lives and is in league with these insurgents." "Are you certain?" "It was her ." "This is an opportunity we cannot let pass . Drayden's apprentice could lead us to other lost Aetheri. " ―Xarn Velgor and Vael Mal

title: Theron Mal
text: In 4 BVE , the Emperor met with Director Orren Vossik , stating to him the importance of his energy initiative. The next day, Vossik secretly met with a number of Imperial officials, among them IVB and Navy, off record at the Maltheen Divide , putting them in charge of the Ghorman project : the planned suppression of the Ghormans and the heavy mining of the essential mineral kalkite from the planet . This operation would be implemented only if no substitute could be found, but in the meantime precursor actions would be taken in case it proved necessary. Vossik stated that this would support the Emperor's dream of energy independence while also reiterating that their circle was to be free of leaks, adding that any violation would be brought to the Emperor's personal attention. Two of the officials present, Dee Shambo and Nisus Osar from the Ministry of Enlightenment , were placed in charge of spreading anti-Ghorman propaganda. IVB Major Lio Partagaz was present as was his protégé Supervisor Dedra Meero , who was secretly placed in charge of running Ghorman while publicly being given a discommendation.

title: Theron Mal
text: During the fifteenth Imperium Day , celebrating the anniversary of the Imperium's rise to power, the Emperor presided over the Imperial Senate on Vantor with his Royal Guards, and invited Lorath governor Arihnda Pryssa to celebrate with him. After the Grand Warden's death at the hands of Brenn Aldric and his Adept Cass Virel , the Emperor dispatched his apprentice to Lorath as an "alternative solution" to the growing insurgent problem. The Emperor was contacted by Xarn Velgor after he had defeated the Insurgent fleet in the Lorath system . Velgor informed his master that he had discovered that his former Aetheri apprentice, Sela Marr, still lived. The Emperor was pleased with the news that Marr possibly knew the location of other hidden Aetheri believed that capturing her would allow the Imperium to find them and destroy them before they became threats. Although Velgor was more interested in finding his former Master Orien Kade, the Emperor told his apprentice to have patience and to send a Warden to hunt down Marr and the other Aetheri discovered on Lorath.

title: Theron Mal
text:
By 3 BVE , anti-Ghorman proganda had proved effective, including the idea that the Ghor were arrogant and mocked Theron Mal. Around the same time, Colonel Yular and Major Lio Partagaz of the IVB were scheduled to meet with the Emperor on the logistics of the Bureau's increase in arrests while Ghor Senator Dasi Oran informed his colleague Vela Sess that he could no longer vote with her against the Emperor's legislation after Ghorman's single-product economy was severely injured by a temporary Imperial embargo. Meanwhile, Carro Rylanz , the leader of the Ghorman Front , while attempting to recruit Syril Karn , mentioned his belief that the Emperor had no idea that the persecution of Ghorman was occurring and that the IVB was operating a shadow government in his name. Sometime after this, intrigued by the results obtained by IVB interrogator Doctor Gorst , Military Intelligence convinced the Emperor to expand him into a full-fledged program to be jointly maintained by a number of military and intelligence branches. However, Gorst and his work was soon destroyed by agents of the Axis network before the program could be put to use.

The Ghorman Massacre

title: Theron Mal
text:
The Ghorman Massacre

> " What happened yesterday on Ghorman was unprovoked genocide! [...] And that truth has been exiled from this Chamber! And the monster screaming the loudest? The monster we've helped create? The monster who will come for all of us soon enough...is Theron Mal! " ―Senator Vela Sess

In 2 BVE , the Emperor promoted the Chyrr Imperial Navy officer Vorren to the position of Grand Admiral for his role in suppressing the insurgent insurgency in the Batonn sector . During the promotion, however, Vorren questioned Mal on the practicality of the Void Core. The Emperor questioned if the reason for Vorren's worries were because of the threat the station posed to the Chyrr species. However, because Vorren had fulfilled his end of the bargain by sharing his information on the Unknown Regions, he let the issue go. The Emperor then introduced Vorren to his personal enforcer, Xarn Velgor. Shortly after his promotion, Vorren was dispatched to deal with the growing insurgent threat at the request of Governor Arihnda Pryssa and Varrix.

title: Theron Mal
text: The same year, IVB Major Partagaz informed Supervisor Meero that the Emperor was greatly interested in the Ghorman project and was currently meeting with Director Vossik. Partagaz told her that their orders were for her to begin implementing the original plan discussed a year prior with the Major assuring Dedra that achieving success on Ghorman would ensure the IVB's importance to the Emperor in the future. Shortly thereafter, Meero oversaw the commencement of the operation. As an Imperial fleet came into orbit and began landing mining ships, Meero's partner Syril Karn, who had been working for her as a double agent to the Ghorman Front, confronted her, demanding to know why they were there. She revealed the secret she had long kept from him: the suppression of Ghorman in order to mine a mineral needed for the Emperor's energy program. As the situation with the local population deteriorated, the IVB and Imperial military implemented their plan to justify the Imperium's actions on Ghorman by inciting a protest by the Ghor and then instigating violence by having a sniper shoot a junior Imperial officer. Over the next few hours, a number of Imperials were killed and hundreds to thousands of Ghor

title: Theron Mal
text: and Imperial military implemented their plan to justify the Imperium's actions on Ghorman by inciting a protest by the Ghor and then instigating violence by having a sniper shoot a junior Imperial officer. Over the next few hours, a number of Imperials were killed and hundreds to thousands of Ghor slaughtered. The next day, Senator Vela Sess met with her colleague Bael Solen, expressing her need to speak out against the Emperor's complicity in the Ghorman Massacre , as much as she was now uncertain what more Mal was truly capable of doing. They both attended the early session of the Senate that was called where a strict agenda was scheduled. To circumvent this, using the time to speak ceded him by another Senator, Solen yielded the floor to Sess in order to allow her to speak. As he did so, Solen cited an article, first proposed by the Emperor's Council, which allowed such an action in the case of an emergency. Sess proceeded to give a speech to the Senate denouncing Theron Mal, calling him a monster and decrying the massacre on Ghorman as an act of unprovoked genocide. The IVB managed to shut down the Senate broadcast midway through her speech and failed in their attempt to take her into custody.

title: Theron Mal
text:
After her escape from Vantor, Sess gave another speech on the HoloNet, calling the Emperor a lying executioner who had ordered the attacks on Ghorman and stating that such evil could not be allowed to stand. Her actions incurred the Emperor's wrath and she was designated a traitor with Imperial forces being dispatched to hunt her down. Despite the efforts of Grand Admiral Vorren to trap Vela Sess and the Shades in the Archeon Nebula , Lena Kryll managed to deliver Vela Sess safely to Steelgrove where she gave a third speech urging the galaxy to rise up against the Imperium. This marked the official formation of the Free Coalition .

Disturbance in the Unknown Regions

After Vorren's defeat at Atollon , Mal sensed a great disturbance in Synth Flux somewhere on the edge of the galaxy. Therefore, the Emperor summoned Vorren and Velgor to Vantor for a meeting. During the meeting, the Emperor ordered the two to the planet Batuu to locate a disturbance in Synth Flux that he had sensed, testing Velgor on his vulnerability to his past and Vorren on his loyalty.

#### Machinations on Lorath

A World Between Worlds

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### Machinations on Lorath

A World Between Worlds

> " I can't go with you. " " Perhaps I can. Cass Virel and Sela Marr— Mine at last! " ―Sela Marr and Vael Mal, to Cass Virel

The next year, during Velgor's hunt for the Hidden Hand , the Emperor contacted his apprentice through a hologram, expressing his disappointment in his failure to track down the criminal syndicate. He stated that they must be crushed at once, as they stole weapons from the Imperium and supplied them to the Insurgency.

After the discovery of an Aetheri Sanctum on Lorath, the Emperor directed Minister Veris Hydan to excavate the ruins and uncover its secrets. Sometime thereafter, the Emperor was contacted by Hydan, who informed him that they had reached the roots of the temple and uncovered a mural of the Mournis gods , which was reminiscent of art and iconography found at the former temple on Vantor. The Emperor told Hydan that he had sensed that the death of Aldric had altered the fate of Lorath. Vowing to control the conduit between the living and the dead, the Emperor urged his minister to quicken the pace of his work.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Later, the Emperor used Umbra alchemy in an attempt to open a portal to the World Between Worlds where Virel and Marr were. The Emperor taunted them through the portal and unleashed his power against them, which they were able to hold back. He then caught Virel's leg and pulled him so that he could get through the portal. However, before he could get through the portal to enter the realm, Marr cut the fiery lasso . The Emperor then tried again but failed as Virel and Marr made it back to their world much to his fury. In the process, the Lorath Aetheri Sanctum was destroyed.

Deception on Lorath
