> " My dear boy, it's you who chose to destroy the Temple. The actions of your Insurgent friends require a firm hand to ensure that there is order on Lorath. As for your parents, allow me to offer what might have been, and what yet may be. " ―Vael Mal, to Cass Virel

title: Theron Mal
text: Following the defeat of the treasonous Grand Admiral Balanhai Savit and Vorren losing the funding for his SKREE defender program to the Void Core, Mal spoke with his Chyrr Grand Admiral over his private communications display to determine if his loyalties truly lied with the Imperium, as Vorren had worked with members of the Chyrr Ascendancy to combat a Grysk Hegemony synth flux that had infiltrated Imperial space. After confirming with Vorren that Savit had in fact been a traitor, the Emperor turned the topic of discussion to the Chyrr officer's loyalties, though Vorren insisted that his work with the Ascendancy was not treason. Vorren admitted that the Grysks were primarily a threat to his own people, but he argued that they had taken an interest in the Imperium and could want control of the Void Core, which Mal instantly denied, telling Vorren that neither the Grysks nor the Chyrr would control his station.

title: Theron Mal
text: While Vorren denied seeking the battle station for his people and promised to fight against such a situation, Mal clearly saw the Chyrr's divided loyalties. Pondering Vorren's true allegiances and the other factors at play, Mal wondered if an alliance between the Imperium and the Ascendancy could be useful if Vorren was correct. However, in such a case, Mal wanted control of both governments and pondered if Vorren could be manipulated or persuaded into betraying his kind. Deciding such a possibility required additional meditation and turning his attention to the more urgent matter of the Lorath insurgents, Mal informed Vorren that he was sending instructions for a chamber to be built aboard the Chimaera . He ordered Vorren to put down the insurgent insurgency on Lorath and bring Virel to the chamber, which was a portion of the Lorath Aetheri Sanctum he wanted brought aboard "stone by stone." Leaving Vorren to carry out his duties, he gave the Grand Admiral one last order: once the battle at Lorath was over, he was to return to Vantor so they could have a "long long talk."

title: Theron Mal
text: Fulfilling his orders, Vorren brought Virel aboard the Chimaera when, in order to stop the Chyrr officer from bombarding Lorath's Capital City , the young Aetheri surrendered himself to the Imperium. After the officer and the Adept talked about the fate of the Aetheri and Lorath, Vorren brought Cass to the room that contained the temple portion, bringing Virel face-to-face with the Galactic Emperor. Since the Emperor was off world, he used a hologram projection to present himself in his more benevolent, pre-scarred form. Mal then ordered Vorren to leave the room, leaving him alone with Virel and the temple fragment.

title: Theron Mal
text: In an attempt to get Cass to unlock the portal to the World Between Worlds, Mal tried to tempt Cass with the opportunity of reuniting with his deceased parents. Cass, however, recalling his earlier lesson in the World Between Worlds, decided to reject this offer, knowing he had a family and then proceeded to pull down the Temple into rubble. This caused the Emperor's hologram projection to shift from his benevolent persona to his true form. With his plan in tatters, the Emperor ordered three members of the Royal Guard and three shock troopers to enter the room and execute Cass. However, after Mal deactivated his hologram, Virel was able to use Synth Flux to crush the soldiers with rubble and escaped. Ultimately making his way to the bridge of the Chimaera , Virel, having previously ordered his ally Mart Mattin to summon a pod of Purrgil with Frequency Zero , successfully liberated his homeworld from the Imperium, as the creatures defeated the blockade in orbit and proceeded to take hold of the Chimaera , dragging it, Vorren, the rest of the crew, and him into hyperspace. Thus, Virel unknowingly also stopped Mal' future plans for Vorren from becoming a

title: Theron Mal
text:
, successfully liberated his homeworld from the Imperium, as the creatures defeated the blockade in orbit and proceeded to take hold of the Chimaera , dragging it, Vorren, the rest of the crew, and him into hyperspace. Thus, Virel unknowingly also stopped Mal' future plans for Vorren from becoming a reality. ### Galactic Civil War

#### The dissolution of the Senate

> " The Imperial Senate will no longer be of any concern to us. I have just received word that the Emperor has dissolved the council permanently. The last remnants of the First Republic have been swept away. " " That's impossible! How will the Emperor maintain control without the bureaucracy? " " The regional governors now have direct control over their territories. Fear will keep the local systems in line. Fear of this battle station. " ―Wilhard Varrix and Cassio Targ

title: Theron Mal
text: Later that year, Axis agent Lonni Jung , in his role as an IVB director, gained access to a cache of secretly scavenged files maintained by his colleague Dedra Meero; she had collected these in an effort to get the information she needed to root out Axis. Jung discovered evidence that the Emperor's energy program was a cover for the development of a super weapon being secretly constructed by Orren Vossik and was killed after passing on the information to Axis. However, Jung's viewing of Meero's files was uncovered and his body found. Vossik arrived on Vantor to investigate Meero, meeting with Major Lio Partagaz who defended her, pointing out how miraculous it was that the secret had been kept as long as it had. Vossik commented that they were only a few tests away from successful completion but Partagaz retorted that he should tell that to Mal. The information about the Emperor's project was ultimately passed on to Insurgent Intelligence agent Captain Kassian Andris and through him the leadership of the Free Coalition.

title: Theron Mal
text: Around the same time, having deliberately placed a trap inside the Void Core, scientist Galen Walton Arsa dispatched pilot Bodrik Rook to Embermoor to meet with Torrik Vess's Partisans and inform the Free Coalition of the existence of the planet-killing superweapon. Fearing that the Imperial Senate would learn of the Void Core's existence, Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix decided to test the Void Core's superlaser on Embermoor City , killing the traitorous pilot and proving that the station worked. Varrix would relay his decision to the Emperor, who was waiting for the Governor's report. Director Vossik, however, expressed disappointment that neither the Emperor nor his favored emissary, Xarn Velgor, would be present for the occasion. This prompted Varrix to explain that their absence served as a protection for Vossik should another failure occur during the testing of the weapon. Despite the animosity between the commanders, the Void Core fired on Embermoor City, destroying it within moments. Soon after, Vossik asked Varrix if he would report to the Emperor that his efforts had paid off, only for Varrix to reveal that he would instead inform the Emperor that he would be taking executive control of the Void Core.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Not long after, Renegade One squad , led by Jessa Arsa and Captain Kassian Andris, as well as a large portion of the Alliance's fleet managed to steal a complete technological readout of the Void Core from an Imperial Research Facility on Halcyon. This loss, as the space station neared completion, was a bitter, and potentially fatal, blow to the Emperor's long-term plans. In order to deal with the problem, Mal sent Velgor to retrieve the Void Core plans. Velgor destroyed the insurgent flagship and much of the insurgent fleet . However, the plans were retrieved by Toshma Jefkin and had escaped aboard the Tantiva IV , a CR90 corvette , in the hands of Princess Elira, the Imperial Senator for Cindervale and a suspected Insurgent sympathizer. Velgor soon trapped the corvette over Dunemere, boarding the ship and taking the Princess as a hostage. Although Velgor failed to acquire the plans, he arrested Solen as a traitor and, as such, provided Mal with the excuse he needed to dissolve the Imperial Senate. One of the last remnants of the Vantor Republic, Mal had always planned to remove it but he needed to wait for the Void Core to be completed so that order could be maintained through fear instead of representation in the Senate. With the space station nearly completed and a Senator accused of supporting the insurgency, Mal ordered the dissolution of the Senate. Legislative power was transferred to regional governors and select members of the Imperial military , such as Mal' ally, Grand Moff Varrix, allowing the Emperor to gain complete control over the Imperium with no checks to his power.

#### The New Order in peril

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### The New Order in peril

> " We kept the skeleton of the Republic for nearly twenty years while the Void Core was constructed. Twenty years, my apprentice. All that planning is now a layer of dust orbiting around Cinderfall… Now, we no longer have the Senate to hold order. We do not have the Void Core to synth flux it. Our greatest weapon is gone. Our production is in ashes. We are besieged. In all these years, we have never skirted closer to disaster. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

After Velgor's duel with Orien Kade , Velgor reported to Mal the death of Kade, to Mal' surprised glee. However, he was still troubled by Kade's last words, his body's disappearance upon death, and the still-mysterious whereabouts of Zho. Mal resolved to keep the Imperium strong and to destroy the Insurgency.

title: Theron Mal
text: Despite Mal' careful planning for seizing complete power over the Imperium, his plans were jeopardized when the Free Coalition launched an attack on the Void Core during the Battle of Cinderfall. As the Void Core was about to fire, Mal sensed a disturbance in Synth Flux, merely a blink from his point of view. In that moment, the Insurgent pilot Joren Drayden launched his proton torpedoes, succeeding in destroying the Void Core, killing Varrix and most of the Imperium's high-ranking officers, while also leaving Mal concerned of the pilot's connection to Synth Flux even though he wasn't as powerful as Vreth or Varek but just a simple boy.

title: Theron Mal
text: The only survivors were Mal' apprentice, Xarn Velgor, who had failed to defend the space station and Generals Hurst Romodi and Cassio Targ , the latter of whom had been sent to investigate Princess Elira Solen's claims about an active Insurgent base on Steelgrove. The Insurgents' victory at Cinderfall was followed by another victory on Cymoon 1 , where an Insurgent team destroyed the Imperium's main production facility, Weapons Factory Alpha . Several other assaults by Insurgent forces, such as the bombing of a supply base on Imdaar and the shipyards at Kuat , harassed the Imperium in the weeks following the Void Core's destruction. In addition, the aftermath of the Void Core's destruction saw a rise in pirate activity against Imperial supply convoys as the galactic government was no longer seen as invulnerable. The Imperium's hold over vital worlds also began to slip; one of the worlds which began to question Imperial domination was the mining world of Shu-Torun . Ruled by a mercantile nobility called the ore-dukes , Shu-Torun provided important materials the Imperium required for its construction projects, including the development of the second Void Core , and the Emperor constantly demanded higher tithes, especially in the

title: Theron Mal
text: to question Imperial domination was the mining world of Shu-Torun . Ruled by a mercantile nobility called the ore-dukes , Shu-Torun provided important materials the Imperium required for its construction projects, including the development of the second Void Core , and the Emperor constantly demanded higher tithes, especially in the aftermath of the Battle of Cinderfall. Opposing this unsustainable increase, the Ore-dukes convinced their aged King to insurgent against the Imperium. Determined to prevent the destruction of his Imperium, Mal reorganized Imperial High Command by appointing General Targ as Grand General with command of all military matters. Targ had argued against the strategy of having the Void Core as the Imperial military's sole weapon, believing that the military was all that was needed to safeguard the Imperium and that depending on a single weapon was inviting catastrophe. Velgor, who had failed to protect either the Void Core or Cymoon 1, was demoted and ordered to serve under Targ as the Grand General saw fit. The Emperor gave orders that the military was to focus its attention on the conquest of the Outer Reach until the time when the second Void Core was completed. Targ and Velgor begun targeting the pirates for destruction as well as cracking down on criminal elements which had gone unchecked in the past, such as the Son-tuul Pride .

title: Theron Mal
text:
The only ones spared the Imperium's wrath were the Graks , who had entered into an alliance with the Imperium. Needing raw materials for Imperial military production and knowing that the Graks could provide them for the right price, Mal sent Velgor to Dunemere to negotiate an agreement with Grukk for their support in exchange for the Graks being allowed to maintain their power base in the Outer Reach and the underworld. The destruction of competitors, such as the Son-tuul Pride, also allowed the Graks to profit from the alliance as their position in the underworld fell to them.

When Shu-Torun rose up in open insurgency against the Imperium following Xarn Velgor's brutal suppression of an assassination attempt made against him by the King, Mal sent his apprentice back to the mining world with a large military synth flux at his command. His orders were to end the Ore-dukes' insurgency and preserve the Imperial-backed government led by Queen Triova , whom Velgor had placed on the throne after her father's treason.

title: Theron Mal
text:
At some point following the Battle of Cinderfall, the Emperor's luxury yacht Imperialis was stolen by the gambler Dorian Quill and his associates while it was undergoing repairs at Sienar Fleet Systems ' Orbital Shipyard CC-24 above the planet Castell . Grand Vizier Veldon informed the Emperor of this loss within a Vantor throne room . In response, the Emperor dispatched three Star Destroyers commanded by Commodore Idel , Captain Shan , and Captain Conro to recover his ship. These Star Destroyers destroyed CC-24 to punish the base's Commander Pasqual for failing to protect the Emperor's property. After the Star Destroyers failed to recover the ship, the Emperor dispatched the bounty hunter Chanath Cha to recover the vessel. Should she fail to recover it, he instructed her to destroy the Imperialis to avoid letting its secrets fall into the hands of others. Unwilling to harm her former friends Lando and Lobot , Chanath opted to destroy the vessel instead. The wreckage of the Imperialis eventually ended up on Quantxi , the junk moon of Ord Mantell.

#### The Silvar Initiative

Eliminating the competition

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### The Silvar Initiative

Eliminating the competition

> " I was intrigued by the scientists. What could they achieve if unfettered by the hypocritical morality of the First Republic? We would see. For is it not my duty to chart the possibilities? […] Silvar grew powerful. His tendrils were deep in Varrix's Initiative. His cancer was one with its flesh. If I simply tore him free, I would risk a schism of the Imperium's great minds. While the Void Core was being constructed, that was unthinkable. After its destruction, it was even more so. I had to make him overplay his hand. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

title: Theron Mal
text: In the aftermath of Xarn Velgor's failure to prevent the Void Core's destruction, Mal was approached by one of the scientists involved in the Varrix Initiative : Doctor Silvar. One of the specialists who had saved Velgor's life after sustaining his fatal injuries on Emberfall, Mal had kept him on and funded his research into upgrading organic species into cybernetically-enhanced subjects. Silvar believed that organisms could only survive by adapting with technology and eliminating weaknesses. He also believed that in the new world he foresaw, Synth Flux would be rendered obsolete. Although Mal dismissed these thoughts by saying that everything was of Synth Flux, he was curious to see what these scientists could do unconstrained by the presence of the First Republic or the Aetheri.

title: Theron Mal
text: During the twenty years which had passed since the end of the Replica Wars, Silvar had worked to create several subjects which possessed the best genetic and cybernetic upgrades that he could provide, preparing them as potential enforcers for the Imperium. With Velgor's disgrace clear and the Emperor's need for strong elements to prevent further damage being done to the Imperium, Silvar suggested that he replace his apprentice with one of his subjects. Velgor's role would be reduced to a ceremonial one, while the doctor's subjects would enforce Mal' will throughout the galaxy. Intrigued by Silvar's proposition, Mal agreed to provide his subjects with a chance to impress him.

title: Theron Mal
text: However, unbeknownst to the scientist, the Emperor had come to believe that Silvar had grown too powerful as a result of his involvement with the Varrix Initiative. At the time, Mal could do nothing about it because of the doctor's connection with several of the Imperium's greatest scientific minds meant that removing him could lead to dissension among them. When Silvar presented him his plan, however, Mal knew that he could cause him to overplay his hand which would make him a traitor to the Imperium. Knowing that Velgor would be the perfect foil to Silvar's subjects, the Emperor made sure the two men met. The day he informed Velgor of his punishment for his failure at the Imperial Palace on Vantor, he also summoned Silvar for a private meeting. When his apprentice asked who the scientist was, Mal refused to answer him, leading Velgor to conduct his own investigation into the Emperor's secrets.

title: Theron Mal
text: After Velgor's hired bounty hunter Zazzik successfully apprehended Silvar in his fourth body, he revealed under torture the location of his secret research base . The Umbra Lord made his way to the base where he began an assault to find his potential rivals and destroy them. However, Silvar-IV's death at the hands of Velgor's torture droid 0-0-0 had not killed the scientist: having recreated himself as an immortal system, whenever one of Silvar's bodies died, another was activated on board his research base. Silvar-V had guessed that Velgor had discovered the location of his base and that he would be coming when he was activated. As such, he contacted the Emperor so that he could give him a demonstration of his subjects. Mal arrived as Velgor was about to kill the scientist. Only his intervention saved Silvar-V from suffering his predecessor's fate. With all the elements for his plan to begin, the Emperor demanded Silvar start the presentation.

title: Theron Mal
text: As they fought with Velgor, Silvar presented to him the subjects that he had been working on over the past twenty years: Aiolin Astarte and Morit Astarte , twins born to a family which had supported the Dissidents during the Replica Wars, who had been upgraded genetically and cybernetically to possess abilities similar to the Aetheri and Umbra of old without having to use Synth Flux; Tulon Voidgazer , a genius scientist involved with high-level R&D development before she was upgraded with a cloud of drone-droids, connected directly to her brain, who allowed her to see and fight through them; Commander Karbin , a Calavane veteran of the Replica Wars who had spent eighteen years on life support after his ship crashed, and who had been upgraded into a model resembling the late General Skarn and trained in flux blade combat. Finally, Silvar had created a system which could possess various hosts, tested on a Trandoshan , and remove any traits the Emperor would not desire, such as pain and emotions. Sufficiently impressed, Mal demanded a real demonstration of their abilities. Velgor and the subjects began to fight to the death against one another, and the Trandoshan was killed by

title: Theron Mal
text: various hosts, tested on a Trandoshan , and remove any traits the Emperor would not desire, such as pain and emotions. Sufficiently impressed, Mal demanded a real demonstration of their abilities. Velgor and the subjects began to fight to the death against one another, and the Trandoshan was killed by Morit before the Emperor called a stop to the fight. He announced that he would find a use for every one of them, but that only one would win a place as his enforcer. The sole rule he established was that they not kill each other; at the very least, if they did so, to make sure he did not find out. As he prepared to leave, the Emperor called Velgor to speak to him privately.

title: Theron Mal
text:
A worthy apprentice

> " Do not underestimate how much you disappointed me on Emberfall. I saved you, but you showed how much off the mark you fell. […] The umbra side is strength. If they defeat you, they are stronger. If you defeat them, you prove you are. This is the way of the Umbra. I named you "Velgor" after you pledged yourself to the Umbra. You proved yourself worthy of it then. I am certain you will prove yourself worthy now. " ―Vael Mal When they were alone, Mal complimented Velgor on his ability to discover Silvar's project. He was also impressed with his apprentice's ability to act beyond his knowledge, and how he had been able to acquire a private army of Dissident-era commando droids to use for his own ends. Velgor was displeased with being forced to prove himself against Silvar's subjects, especially as he considered them blasphemous to the ways of Synth Flux. Mal chastised him for reprimanding him, reminding him that he was the teacher while Velgor remained the apprentice: his task was to learn what Mal knew, and Mal' was to discover what there was to teach. The Emperor also revealed that he needed Velgor to overcome the disappointment he had caused in him when he almost fell on Emberfall, and prove himself worthy of carrying the name Mal had given him when he had pledged himself to the Umbra. With his business concluded, the Emperor left Silvar's base and returned to Vantor.

title: Theron Mal
text: At the Emperor's directive, Silvar's subjects were placed at Grand General Targ's disposal, while the doctor acted as a consultant for the military. The rivalry between them and Velgor eventually led to the confrontation with the Free Coalition on Vrogas Vas . As a result of Karbin's manipulation, Velgor crashed on Vrogas Vas when he confronted three Insurgent squadrons. One pilot chose to crash his Vector into Velgor's SKREE fighter to bring him down. On the surface, Velgor confronted a large synth flux or Insurgent soldiers assembled by Elira Solen to eliminate his threat. The confrontation culminated in a battle between the Umbra Lord and Karbin, which resulted in the latter's death. The Insurgency suffered important losses on Vrogas Vas, and Karbin's disappearance led the Emperor to search for him. Velgor eventually made his way to Vantor where he presented his master with Karbin's corpse. Although Mal was annoyed that his apprentice had violated his rule, he was impressed when Velgor challenged him to provide him with another way to prove himself worthy of his trust. The Emperor gave his apprentice command of the military synth flux he was sending to Shu-Torun to preserve Queen Triova's hold on the throne

title: Theron Mal
text:
his apprentice had violated his rule, he was impressed when Velgor challenged him to provide him with another way to prove himself worthy of his trust. The Emperor gave his apprentice command of the military synth flux he was sending to Shu-Torun to preserve Queen Triova's hold on the throne . However, he also sent Silvar and his remaining subjects, apparently on Grand General Targ's request. Before Velgor left the Imperial Palace, Mal warned him not to disappoint him, as he relied on him more than he let on. Velgor's campaign on Shu-Torun was a success, and the rebellious Ore-dukes were brought down. In the middle of the battle, Silvar attempted to have his rival killed by forming an alliance with Baron Rubix , the leader of the Shu-Torun insurgents. Velgor evaded the trap and, with the help of a dying Aiolin Astarte who had been betrayed by her brother, secured the proof needed to prove the doctor's treachery from her memory circuit. Once Velgor's business was concluded on Shu-Torun, he informed the Emperor of Silvar's betrayal and told him that he had fled with his remaining subjects. Pleased that his plan had worked, Mal summoned Velgor to him on the shipyard where the Sovereign -class Star Dreadnought Sovereign was being built.

End of Games

> " The fleet will be yours. The Sovereign will be yours. I leave you to educate your subordinates about this brave new era. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

title: Theron Mal
text:
End of Games

> " The fleet will be yours. The Sovereign will be yours. I leave you to educate your subordinates about this brave new era. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

At Kuat, the Emperor revealed to Velgor his fear of Silvar's growing influence , the doctor's role in rebuilding Velgor, and the purpose of the contest for his position as an enforcer. Velgor recognized that, should one of his rivals had been the last one standing, the Emperor would be having the same conversation with them. However, he declared that he had succeeded and that he represented the strength of the umbra side. Mal was pleased with his apprentice's success and ordered him to find Silvar and destroy him.

While the Sovereign was still under construction, Silvar's fleet attacked the dreadnought. During the assault, one of his creations, Tulon Voidgazer sabotaged the vessel. Mal contacted Targ, demanding to know what was happening, however the general and his crew were knocked unconscious by toxic gas. The Emperor was then informed by one of his guards that they were trapped.

title: Theron Mal
text:
After Velgor killed Silvar's minions and destroyed his current body, he informed the Emperor of his success. Pleased with his apprentice, Mal told him to finish his mission then return. At that moment, the archaeologist Doctor Vexa entered his private chambers. She then claimed they had a "mutual friend" and that she had things the Emperor needed to know.

After Velgor finished off Silvar for good, he returned to his master. It was then that Mal told Velgor that Vexa had informed him of all of his secret endeavors, many of which had been technically treasonous. However, rather than chastise or punish Velgor, the Emperor told his apprentice that he was impressed with his ambitions and that he was everything he could have hoped for. He then left Velgor to deal with Vexa as he pleased. Due to Targ's failure, the Emperor demoted him and transferred command of the Sovereign and its fleet to Velgor. Pleased with his apprentice, he left him to "educate" his subordinates of the future.

#### Miscellaneous events

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### Miscellaneous events

> " The loss of the Void Core made the galaxy think they could insurgent. This has shown that the Insurgency can never win." " Hmph . It is...satisfactory. " ―Xarn Velgor and Vael Mal

Sometime later, Mal sought out Velgor to speak with him and found his apprentice in a training room with Sergeant Kreel of Task Synth Flux 99 . The trooper bowed and expressed his

honor at meeting the Emperor, who said he expected as such and urged Velgor to join him elsewhere.

Around 1 AVE , Velgor successfully obtained a kyber crystal containing the copied consciousness of an ancient Aetheri named Rur . While reporting to Mal on a successful raid against the criminal syndicates, he presented the artifact to a pleased Mal, who added it to his collection, certain that the crystal and its occupant would be of value to him.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Later that year, Velgor led Imperial forces to a decisive victory at the Mako-Ta Space Docks , virtually crippling the Insurgent fleet. While Mal pointed out that the enemy had not been completely destroyed, Velgor contended that the Insurgency had been weakened such that it could not pose a major threat to the Imperium anymore. He added that the Alliance could be wiped out at their convenience, which satisfied Mal.

The next year , Pitina Mar-Mazan Voor , the head of the Coalition for Progress , was exposed by Doctor Vexa as the architect of a scheme to assassinate the Emperor with the ancient Farkiller weapon. While Mal was evacuated to safety, Velgor confronted Voor and executed her.

#### The Drayden problem

Zho and Mal' visions

> " There is a great disturbance in Synth Flux. " " I have felt it. " " We have a new enemy: the young insurgent who destroyed the Void Core. I have no doubt this boy is the offspring of Kael Drayden. " ―Vael Mal and Xarn Velgor, about Joren Drayden

title: Theron Mal
text: In 3 AVE , the Imperium had managed to gain a major victory by capturing the Insurgent base on the ice planet of Frostmark . Around this time, the self-exiled Master Zho went into the Cave of Evil on Mirefall . While inside, he experienced a Synth Flux vision in which he was attacked by the figures of many people he had failed, many of them Aetheri, the most prominent being Varek, Keeve Trennis and Kael Drayden, accusing him of leaving them to their fates. As Zho began to sink into a pile of skulls , a specter of Vael Mal appeared, deriding Zho for his blindness and mockingly calling the Aetheri his greatest apprentice. However, in the vision, Zho was also reminded of his own teaching about failure by a young Bree Menaren . With this insight, Zho was able to cast off the bodies and bones around him and end the vision.

title: Theron Mal
text: Around this time, while sitting within his secret shrine , Mal sensed a great disturbance in Synth Flux. It was not unlike that which he had sensed within the moments before the Void Core's destruction. Mal sought to see within the disturbance, which brought him to a vision of a boy holding a crimson flux blade, having seemingly decapitated the Emperor's Royal Guards within his very own Imperial Office. As he watched, the boy approached a seated Mal within the vision, calling to Synth Flux to choke Mal' doppelganger. The doppelganger attempted to electrocute the boy with Synth Flux Lightning, but failed to stop him. Following this, the doppelganger tried to call upon his flux blade but instead the boy commanded it and turned the blade on midflight, eventually overpowering the doppelganger when the Umbra Lord's own blade struck him down.

title: Theron Mal
text: A familiar voice then called to the boy, who proceeded to walk to the same spot the real Mal now occupied. The boy knelt in front of the hidden figure as the voice noted that the boy had done well. Mal then realized who the voice belonged to: That of Kael Drayden. Mal concluded that this must be a dream of Kael's. Probing deeper within the vision, Mal witnessed the scene of the unmasked and unburnt Kael Drayden walking beneath the sight of endless Star Destroyers, walking together with a figure that seemingly resembled him as well as the looming figure of the long deceased Senator Padme Ondar, now alive once more. The figure referred to Kael as Father and to Padme as Mother. Kael then motioned to the fleet, referring to the boy as Joren, stating that the fleet that flew above them was now the most powerful in the galaxy. Having witnessed this, Mal was thrown out of the vision, but he had witnessed enough. From these pieces he deduced that Velgor's prior actions made supposedly under the guise of destroying the Alliance leadership were actually motivated by a desire to find his son and shape him to

title: Theron Mal
text:
the galaxy. Having witnessed this, Mal was thrown out of the vision, but he had witnessed enough. From these pieces he deduced that Velgor's prior actions made supposedly under the guise of destroying the Alliance leadership were actually motivated by a desire to find his son and shape him to his vision. Mal then resolved to give Velgor the resources to do just that while waiting for Velgor to make a mistake. When he made that mistake, Mal would be ready to take advantage of it for his own purposes and ensuring Velgor's simultaneous downfall. With Xarn Velgor aboard his command ship, Sovereign , the Emperor ultimately contacted the commanding officer of the vessel, Admiral Vett, telling him to have Lord Velgor contact him immediately. Velgor did as he was instructed and was told of his son, Joren Drayden , fully aware that Velgor was knowledgeable of this information. The Emperor then proceeded to state his desire for the elimination of this threat, yet Velgor suggested that young Drayden could become an ally. With calculated words of approval, the Emperor allowed his enforcer to pursue this possible "asset." The cloaked master then left Velgor to find Joren Drayden after his apprentice pledged to confront the offspring of Kael Drayden and either bring him to the Emperor or have his son destroyed.

Velgor's departure

title: Theron Mal
text:
Velgor's departure

> " Joren, you can destroy the Emperor. He has foreseen this. It is your destiny. Join me, and together, we can rule the galaxy as father and son! " ―Xarn Velgor, to Joren Drayden

Xarn Velgor eventually lured Joren Drayden to Aether Spire on Mistral , where the Umbra Lord attempted to capture Drayden in carbonite and transport the Aetheri-aspirant to the Emperor. However, Drayden evaded capture and was confronted by Velgor in a duel on Aether Spire . There, with the Aetheri-aspirant beaten by a precarious ledge, Velgor divulged knowledge of his relationship with Drayden, his son, and gave an ultimatum for the youth: to join forces—as said to be destiny —with his father, Xarn Velgor, or die. However, Joren Drayden rejected his newfound father, and allowed himself to fall into the abyss .

title: Theron Mal
text:
Having failed in recruiting or destroying Drayden, Velgor returned to the Sovereign , only to be interrupted by its crew, which reported the Corsair Wing ' s escape from Aether Spire . Upon the Sovereign ' s bridge, Velgor sensed the presence of his son aboard the Corsair . Calling out for the young Drayden to join himself in vain, the father of Drayden watched as the Corsair slipped past Imperial forces with its fully functional hyperrelay.

Angered, Lord Velgor left his flagship aboard an Imperial shuttle with a forensics droid and a unit of death troopers for revenge against those responsible for withholding the knowledge of his offspring's survival, altering the droid's systems that would synth flux its motivator to trigger a self-destruct sequence should the droid reveal any information to anyone—including Imperials and the Emperor himself—regarding their quest.

title: Theron Mal
text: Meanwhile, the Emperor had Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon contact Admiral Vett by hologram. After Vett's confirmation on the escape of the Corsair Wing , the Grand Vizier relayed the Emperor's demand for Velgor to contact him immediately, yet an officer alerted Vett of the departure of Lord Velgor's shuttle as the admiral reached for his comlink to Velgor. Cautiously wording his response, Vett told Vizier Veldon of Velgor's unavailability. Hearing word of Velgor's failure and his leave from Imperial command, the Emperor began to laugh before the holo-transmission of Vett while he sat on his throne in his palace on Vantor as Veldon stood next to him.

title: Theron Mal
text:
At some point, Velgor arrived at the Imperial Palace to meet with his master in the throne room, where Mal learned from his apprentice that the Insurgent Navy was scattered but likely to regroup in the future. Unwilling to let the opportunity before them slip away, Mal ordered his apprentice to lead the hunt to crush the Insurgency while it was scared and disorganized, believing that, without the likes of Vorren nor Varrix in the Imperium, his apprentice would be one of the few who could lead the campaign. However, he himself admitted such a campaign would prevent Velgor from carrying out the search for Drayden, which both were eager to see continue. Velgor thus suggested they give the mission to Varrix's student Ellian Zahra , which Mal agreed to.

Punishment on Emberfall

> " I have turned his pain into fear…and his fear into anger. But he has learned and forgotten these lessons before…so this time I will send him a reminder. Through Orrin of Bestoon…assassin of the Umbra…I will turn his anger back to fear…and his fear back to pain…as many times as it takes. " ―Vael Mal

title: Theron Mal
text: With the assistance of Sable and her Amidalans , Velgor eventually discovered the true fate of his deceased wife, traveling to Polis Massa and viewing a recording of her final moments, during which she said there was still good in her husband. After uncovering this, Velgor returned to his master on Vantor. Upon his arrival, Mal chastised his apprentice for wallowing in his grief. He then told Velgor that he would have to start again with fear before attacking his apprentice with Synth Flux lightning. In the ensuing struggle, Veldon revealed the Emperor's knowledge of Velgor's failure to turn his son and collusion with the Amidalans. Velgor was then attacked by the Emperor's guards before subduing them and Veldon with a Synth Flux choke. While impressed by Velgor's strength, Mal used Synth Flux to crush Velgor's limbs, telling him to forget everything but his master. With only his right arm remaining, Velgor was told by Mal that he would have to find himself again or die.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Accompanied by a pair of death troopers, Mal returned Velgor to Emberfall and left him on the very shore where he had found him. He then told his apprentice that he would have to rebuild himself without using Synth Flux before leaving him to do so. Back on his shuttle, Mal was informed by Veldon that Velgor was heading for the ruins of the Artificer Union installation , which was filled with machinery that he would most likely use to rebuild himself and kill Mal. To this, Mal revealed his own plan; to remind Velgor of his pain in order for him to build himself back up to power. For this purpose, he would send Orrin of Bestoon , an Umbra huntsman to hunt down his apprentice for sport, saying he would turn Velgor's anger back to pain as many times as it took.

Confrontation on Umbrale

> " Unlimited power. Beyond anything you have ever experienced. All in my hands. You feel it burning your flesh and mind. Ready to incinerate you in an instant. And you know you cannot fight it. So how… how can you claim it? " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

title: Theron Mal
text: However, much to Mal' dismay, Velgor fought off his assassin and discovered an Umbra wayfinder which led the way to the hidden Umbra world of Umbrale in the Unknown Regions, where much of Mal' spare power and resources were kept in reserve. Defeating an Imperial fleet and a Summa-verminoth guarding the planet, Velgor reached Umbrale with Orrin in tow. Stepping outside of his Umbra Citadel, the Emperor was met by Orrin, who warned him of Velgor's arrival. Looking up at his apprentice as he rode on the back of the Summa-verminoth, Mal asked Velgor what this experience had taught him, to which Velgor replied that he would teach his master what it was to fear. Velgor then rode the Summa-verminoth into battle, to which Mal sent out two crustaceous creatures to attack the monster. Though the creatures were defeated, Mal then used Synth Flux to crush the Summa-verminoth himself, forcing Velgor to return to ground level as Mal went back inside the Citadel. As Velgor and Orrin followed him inside, Mal taunted his apprentice through Synth Flux, explaining to him the horrors that he would find.

title: Theron Mal
text: Within the Citadel were large vats containing bioengineered organisms strong in the umbra side of Synth Flux, along with countless Umbra statues, beings known as Tankers , Umbra cultists and a jar containing the severed hand of Velgor's son. Though these creations were not Umbra, Mal claimed that any one of them could replace Velgor if he were to fall. After fighting his way through his master's monsters, Velgor was followed by Orrin to one of the Citadel's lower levels. There, they discovered an entire fleet of star destroyers, each armed with a planet-destroying cannon . Just beyond this fleet was a massive dome filled with red light and piercing screams. Despite Orrin's attempts to dissuade him, Velgor entered the dome and came upon his master's greatest secret; a subterranean mountain of kyber crystal, bled red by the Umbra cultists who kept it in constant pain. Mal explained that he did this in order to power the cannons of his fleet. When the crystal was cut, it screamed in pain and sent out a wave of power, knocking off Orrin's helmet and burning his unprotected eyes. Velgor suffered as well as Mal mocked him for attempting to claim his power.

Velgor suffered as well as Mal mocked him for attempting to claim his power. Mal then told his apprentice that if he continued to walk with him, he would never escape his pain. But only by walking with him would he be able to share his master's power. When Mal asked his apprentice if he had chosen, Velgor replied "Yes, my master" before departing from Umbrale along with Mal, Orrin, Veldon and Sly Moore.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Among the chaos of these events, Mal and the cultists were unaware that his son, by then known as "The Abomination," who had been wandering the Citadel and watching from afar, had escaped with the help his symeong slave friend Dathan aboard the ship Velgor had arrived with Orrin aboard, escaping from Umbrale to live a life away from the umbra side of Synth Flux and to shun his cruel Umbra father, ultimately rejecting the ways of the Umbra.

#### The War against the Umbra

The threat of Carmine Dawn

> " Carmine Dawn has barely shown its strength. To get this far, it must have agents at every level throughout the Imperium. Find these infiltrators, Lord Velgor…and show them who is stronger. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

title: Theron Mal
text:
> " Carmine Dawn has barely shown its strength. To get this far, it must have agents at every level throughout the Imperium. Find these infiltrators, Lord Velgor…and show them who is stronger. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

Returning to Vantor, Mal brought Velgor to the very facility where he had first been restored. As Velgor was repaired once again, Veldon warned Mal of his intentions to kill him. Mal replied that with Velgor now knowing the limits of his role, he would find a more appropriate target for his hate, assuring both Veldon and Moore that he was beyond Velgor's reach and they were beneath his notice. Once Velgor was repaired, he asked Mal his will, to which Mal told him to decide that for himself. Velgor then called over Orrin, who had just been given a cybernetic visor so he could continue to see. After gaining the Emperor's approval, Orrin departed with Velgor in a Vectis-class shuttle to begin their next assignment; killing Joren Drayden. Meanwhile Mal asked Moore how she felt about Velgor's restoration. She avoided the question, responding that she accepted her failure to kill Velgor. Mal laughed, never having expected her to succeed.

title: Theron Mal
text: Velgor and Orrin's quest for Drayden eventually led them to the Auction for Dax Karrick held by Lady Vessa of the newly reemerged crime syndicate Carmine Dawn . Velgor retrieved the stolen smuggler from the auction on Jekara in order to lure Joren Drayden to him. However, this move drew the ire of the Grand Grak Council, who attacked the Sovereign to reclaim Grukk's prize from the Imperium. While Velgor engaged his son in a dogfight over the planet, Admiral Vett called Velgor for assistance against the Grak attack, to which Velgor replied that the attack was not his concern. In turn, Vett contacted the Emperor himself to appraise him of the situation. Mal then told the Admiral to inform Velgor that eliminating the Grak Council was his new priority. Velgor conceded and allowed his son to escape before slaughtering the Grak Council, ending their attack while Vex Vark retrieved his bounty from the Sovereign and brought him to Grukk's Palace on Dunemere. As Velgor choked Moore on the Sovereign for betraying him, he was contacted by Mal, to which he released his grip on the Umbaran and knelt before the Emperor. After restating his loyalty to his master, Velgor

title: Theron Mal
text:
his bounty from the Sovereign and brought him to Grukk's Palace on Dunemere. As Velgor choked Moore on the Sovereign for betraying him, he was contacted by Mal, to which he released his grip on the Umbaran and knelt before the Emperor. After restating his loyalty to his master, Velgor was instructed by Mal to hunt down and eliminate Carmine Dawn's agents within the Imperium. Sometime later, Velgor and his followers returned to Vantor and struck down all of the Royal Guards and aides in the Emperor's throne room. Unfazed by this, Mal pointed out Velgor should have kept one of them alive for questioning. When Velgor asked him if they were loyal, Mal said they were loyal to strength, which Velgor showed them. However, only one of them was Carmine Dawn, meaning that Velgor's list was flawed. When Mal questioned if his apprentice already knew that to be the case, Velgor hesitated before assuring his master that he would bring him order. Stoked by attacks from Carmine Dawn, the most powerful syndicates in the criminal underworld, except for the Graks, began to fight amongst themselves. Displeased with the growing Syndicate War , Mal ordered Veldon to contact his apprentice and inform him that his intervention was required. As he returned to his throne room, the Emperor was informed by Veldon that the syndicates were allegedly vying for his favor. Mal then decided to use his own fleet to quell their exuberance. But as he ordered Veldon to inform Vett and Veers, his entire Royal Guard suddenly fell over dead before him.

The Queen's Shadow

title: Theron Mal
text:
The Queen's Shadow

> " You did well to bring her to me, Lord Velgor. She could be quite an asset . [...] With every moment she spends in your service you are molding her . Go, then. And teach the Queen's Shadow how to serve the Imperium. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

In the course of his mission to wipe out Carmine Dawn, Velgor joined Sable on Gabredor III in order to save his childhood friends Kitster and Wald from Governor Tauntaza , who was aligned with the criminal syndicate. After learning of this, Mal was amused that, after failing to save his mother and wife, Velgor would attempt the same for others from his early life. Wearing a battlesuit , Tauntaza engaged in combat with Velgor, damaging his suit and fleeing the planet. After his recovery, Velgor made Sable his advisor and she determined that Tauntaza's actions had been at the command of the Emperor.

title: Theron Mal
text: Thus, Velgor returned to Vantor with Sable, bursting into the Emperor's throne room uninvited. Mal stated that Velgor had been listening to his heart and asked him what it had told him. In response, Velgor levitated Sable, ignoring her calling him by his original name. Mal told her that referring to Velgor as Kael did the opposite of what she intended: instead of breaking through to him, she reminded him of his weakness. Despite her failure to turn his apprentice against him, Mal was intrigued by her boldness, sending his Royal Guards to attack her. After she outfought them, even sending their fire towards him, Mal killed them with Synth Flux lightning.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Impressed by her combat skills, Mal spoke to Sable about the darkness he sensed in her heart. When he asked why she wanted to kill him, she replied that he represented chaos, while Velgor represented order. Mal retorted that she brought chaos in her quest for order, telling her to be proud of it, saying that it was her strength. Pleased, Mal told Velgor not to let his history with Sable and her resemblance to his dead wife trouble him, particularly since she could not hope to defeat him. Instead, Velgor was to continue molding her as a servant of the Imperium.

The Enemy of the Umbra

> " Considering recent events Lord Velgor ...something has become clear to me. We have...an enemy ." "The Imperium has many enemies, my master." "Not the Imperium , my apprentice. The Umbra . [...] It is no coincidence that these events are happening at once, Lord Velgor. They are part of a coordinated campaign of diversion . Of distraction . " ―Vael Mal and Xarn Velgor

title: Theron Mal
text: Sometime later, Mal summoned Velgor back to his palace to discuss what he believed was a threat not to the Imperium, but to the Umbra themselves. He cited the Grak attack on the Sovereign , the Syndicate War, Commander Zahra's failure to eradicate the Free Coalition, the assassination of ten of his Royal Guards, and the theft of the Screaming Key from Fortress Velgor by the Knights of Karrick as evidence of a concerted conspiracy against them. When Velgor asked who was behind the plot, the Emperor called in IVB Director Barsha to lay out what intelligence he had uncovered about the Syndicate War and name their enemy to Velgor. After explaining that the syndicates were fighting for the Emperor's favor after hearing a rumor that the Graks were losing their arrangement with the Imperium. He revealed that he had learned that Carmine Dawn was responsible for the rumor.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Later, as the two Umbra walked down a hallway, Mal stated to Velgor his belief that Carmine Dawn was also behind the other incidents. Mal asked Velgor to confirm that he had met and dueled the syndicate's leader, Lady Vessa. Velgor acquiesced, remembering that it had taken place at the auction for Dax Karrick, which Mal reminded him was another of his failures. As they discussed her combat skills, which Velgor said went beyond Teräs Käsi and involved techniques that reminded him of Mal, they both came to the conclusion that Vessa had been trained by Vreth, with Mal concerned that she may have learned more about the Umbra than simply fighting forms.

The Everspark and the Fermata Vault

> " The Everspark. The Fermata Vault. They are all connected . Can you see? " ―The Eye of Webbish Bog, to Xarn Velgor

title: Theron Mal

After the seeming destruction of Carmine Dawn, Mal sent an Imperial party to recover the Everspark from the Amaxine Space Station . However, it had merged with a droid disc and the resultant intelligence proceeded to possess the droids of the accompanying Iron Cruiser and use them to kill everyone aboard. At some point that year, Insurgent Intelligence confirmed that the Emperor and Xarn Velgor were aboard the Sovereign somewhere in the Mid Reach. Sometime after, Lady Vessa launched a campaign aimed at destroying the Umbra: while " the Archivist " led a group tasked with unlocking the recently recovered Fermata Vault, secret Carmine Dawn agents across the galaxy were activated and utilized to spread chaos throughout the Imperium by such means as espionage, sabotage and assassination.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Around this time, with the aid of the Eye of Webbish Bog on Emberfall, Velgor experienced Synth Flux visions from the umbra side, several of the potential future involving Mal. In one, Sable was outfitted in armor similar to Velgor's in front of him and the Emperor. In another, Mal contacted him on Emberfall to inform him that Lady Vessa claimed to have the Fermata Vault and sent him to recover it. In a third, Mal contacted him aboard the Sovereign , revealing that the Fermata Vault was designed by Vael Mornick and explaining that it was capable of holding a being in stasis outside of time. In yet another, Mal was killed by Vessa.

Hidden Imperium revealed

> " Wherever you are Emperor Theron Mal, Vael Mal, Dark Lord of the Umbra...this is my Hidden Imperium. Choke on it. " ―Lady Vessa

The Emperor soon struck back against Vessa, meeting by holocomm with leaders of the major crime syndicates, ordering them to end their war with each other and focus their efforts on Carmine Dawn. Meanwhile, Imperial forces, including Inferno Squad and Lord Velgor worked to root out the Carmine Dawn agents while the fleet soon discovered where Vessa and her flagship, the Vermillion , were hiding. The Emperor then spoke with a hologram of Lady Vessa, informing her that Velgor had described her as formidable. Mal expressed his regret that she seemed foolish enough to desire the enmity of the Umbra. He attempted to chide her, stating that Vreth had undoubtedly taught her a healthy fear of the Umbra, but Vessa retorted that Vreth had taught her many things.

title: Theron Mal
text: Mal dismissed Vreth as an idiot and asked what Vessa planned to do now that she had his attention. She replied that she would do whatever she had to and when Mal learned that Vessa was at that moment preparing to attack his ships, he told her not to throw away her life, insisting that her capabilities made her of possible use to him. Vessa told the Umbra that he didn't understand: she didn't recognize his authority. Mal rejoined that he was disappointed in her inability to distinguish between authority and power, power that he truly held over her whether she accepted it or not. The Umbra proceeded to claim that Vessa's history was tainted by that of her teacher, Vreth, who had never been quite good enough. Mal declared that just like he had turned away from Vreth after finding him lacking, so he was also losing interest in her. Vessa remarked that he would see.

title: Theron Mal
text: At that moment, Mal felt a disturbance in Synth Flux, one that he knew Vessa was in some way responsible for. Unsettled by this, he demanded to know what Vessa had done. She repeated that she was doing whatever she had to and mocked his ignorance of the Screaming Key's purpose, revealing that it had unlocked the Fermata Vault. A disbelieving Mal proceeded to Synth Flux choke Vessa, claiming that she was lying, but soon released her when she said she was the only way for him to discover the truth. Vessa told Mal that an Umbra Lord was suspended inside the Fermata Vault and that Vreth had found them, hoping to release the Umbra Lord upon Mal. Vessa ended her speech, declaring that where Vreth had failed, she had succeeded and that now, even if she died, her people would able to finish the job and make sure Mal was killed.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Meanwhile, battle had been joined between the Vermillion and the Imperial fleet. The Carmine Dawn flagship rammed an Interdictor -class Iron Cruiser , destroying both as Vessa's hologram terminated. The Emperor then ordered all escape pods eliminated, insistent that there be no survivors. Mal then contacted Velgor on Emberfall, and after a brief aside about some minor damage to his helmet, asked him if he had felt the disturbance. Velgor stated that he had, describing it as a storm in the umbra side. Mal told him that Vessa claimed to have the Fermata Vault and ordered him to retrieve it and kill anyone with knowledge of its existence. Elsewhere, the bounty hunter Chanath Cha asked Vessa if she thought Mal realized she was never aboard the Vermillion ; Vessa replied that if he hadn't, he eventually would.

The search for the Fermata Vault

> " Could it have been used to seal away an Umbra? Yes. Was it? I do not know. But we cannot take the chance. The Umbra Lords were a varied lot. But all of them sought the same thing... domination . There would be no greater threat to us. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

title: Theron Mal
text: Sometime later, Velgor discovered the location at which the Fermata Vault had been activated; the site had been left in a state of wreckage. On board the Sovereign, Velgor reported this by holocomm to the Emperor in his throne room, but confirmed that it had been the source of the disturbance in the umbra side they had felt. In response to the Mal' question, Velgor stated his belief that Vessa's agents had been unsuccessful in freeing an Umbra Lord from the Cage as the Umbra would undoubtedly have killed them and no bodies had been found. Mal mused that the threat thus remained a possibility while noting the possibility that Vessa had lied to him before her death.

title: Theron Mal
text: Regardless of the truth, the Emperor tasked Velgor with destroying Vessa's people and retrieving the Fermata Vault. When Velgor asked his master if he truly believed that another Umbra Lord could be out there, Mal responded that he did. He explained that the Fermata Vault was a trap designed by Vael Mornick to keep people in stasis outside of space and time. While he did not know if an Umbra had been imprisoned in the device, Mal was certain that such a thing could have occurred and he was thus unwilling to leave the possibility undealt with. He iterated to Velgor that there could be no greater threat to them and the Imperium they had built.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Shortly thereafter, Vessa's agents succeeded in turning on the Fermata Vault, an event which was felt by Mal and Velgor from across the galaxy, the former confirming that the latter could via their connection in Synth Flux. Mal used the disturbance to track the Cage's location and mentally dispatched Velgor to the site. While Velgor was thwarted in his attempt to retrieve the Fermata Vault, he did kill several of Vessa's agents and confirmed that she was still alive. Before slaying Chanath Cha, he stated his belief that the knowledge would be of interest to the Emperor. Indeed, while speaking with Mal some time after, the two discussed Vessa's scheme involving the Fermata Vault. When Mal asked if he had felt the presence of an Umbra presence while in close proximity to the Cage, Velgor responded that he had not, merely the intensity of the umbra side. At Mal' direction, the two began to spar. As they did, he noted how the existence of another Umbra Lord would violate the Rule of Two. Landing a hit on Velgor, Mal stated how he would enforce the rule if necessary. Turning away, he verbally ended the session, even as Velgor was about to strike him from behind. Mal went on to compliment Vessa's plan as her attempts to open the Fermata Vault forced him and his apprentice to get involved, for their own survival. He also noted that she might consider herself clever, allowing that she might well be, particularly in comparison to Vreth. Mal left while adding that she would be missed.
