Later, during a mission in No-Space , Elira Solen referred to the Emperor as a tyrant and Dorian Quill stated the strong likelihood that the Free Coalition would lose the war with the Emperor having them executed. After they left No-Space, Elira speculated to Joren Drayden that Synth Flux Wave that they had been feeling could prove distracting for the Emperor and Xarn Velgor.

#### Downfall of the Umbra

Schemes against the Insurgency

> " I wonder if your feelings on this matter are clear, Lord Velgor. " " They are clear, my master. " " Then you must go to the sanctuary moon and wait for him. " " He will come to me? " " I have foreseen it. His compassion for you will be his undoing. He will come to you... and then you will bring him before me. " " As you wish. " ―Vael Mal and Xarn Velgor

title: Theron Mal
text:
In the months after the events on Mistral, Joren Drayden would continue to hone his skills in the light side of Synth Flux ; nonetheless, Mal still believed Drayden liable to turn to the umbra side.

In an attempt to gain a new Umbra apprentice as well as end the Galactic Civil War, Mal purposely allowed the Insurgents to obtain the plans of the new Void Core under construction over the forest moon of Mossfell . Following the presumed destruction of a vast majority of the Insurgency in a doomed confrontation against an unknowingly armed and operational Void Core, Mal planned on commencing the deployment of some of the largest invasion fleets known in galactic history to blockade the known insurgent strongholds of Mon Calvarra and Serenne until the Void Core II could destroy them, permanently ending the Insurgency and all those that would oppose his rule through sheer terror.

title: Theron Mal
text:
The Emperor went to the second Void Core intending to oversee the ultimate defeat of the Insurgency and the Aetheri, using himself as additional bait to draw the Alliance out. A massive amount of Imperial personnel, including two astromech droids , witnessed their Emperor's momentous arrival in Hangar 272 . Shortly before his meeting with Joren Drayden, the Emperor sensed the existence of a mysterious, malevolent synth flux in the farthest reaches of the unexplored regions; he suspected it to be the possible source of the umbra side of Synth Flux, but even the Emperor wasn't sure who or what he was sensing. He also sensed the death of Zho, who appeared to him as a Synth Flux spirit, much to Mal' surprise. All the same, he began to gloat about his coming victory until Zho suddenly vanished.

Meeting Joren Drayden

> " I'm looking forward to completing your training. In time, you will call me master. " ―Vael Mal, to Joren Drayden

title: Theron Mal
text:
Meeting Joren Drayden

> " I'm looking forward to completing your training. In time, you will call me master. " ―Vael Mal, to Joren Drayden

Whilst on the Void Core, Joren Drayden, Dax Karrick , Princess Elira, and Brevok managed to sneak past the shield and land on the Sanctuary Moon. Velgor, who had been told to dispatch the fleet to the moon and to remain on a command ship, sensed his son's arrival. Because of this, he journeyed to the Void Core, where he told the Emperor that he sensed Joren's arrival. Surprised that he himself was unable to sense it, the Emperor commanded Velgor to go and wait for him, saying that he had foreseen Joren seeking Velgor out and surrendering to him personally out of compassion for his father.

title: Theron Mal
text: Shortly after Drayden and the insurgent strike team landed on Mossfell, the Emperor summoned his secret protégé, Admiral Gallard Raxen, for a secret meeting aboard his throne room on the second Void Core. Sensing a shatterpoint approaching, Vael Mal warned Raxen that it may soon be time to implement the Contingency. He then ordered Raxen to take the Sovereign -class Star Dreadnought Ravager into the Vulpinus Nebula and hide until the events of this shatter point had resolved. He also told Raxen that there would be others he had to call to his side. Once Joren surrendered, Xarn Velgor brought his son to the space station and his master's throne room. The Emperor greeted Joren, dismissed the guardsmen and removed his chains. Joren was told that the Emperor planned to turn Joren to the umbra side and that all that has happened on the Moon was all his plan. The Emperor also managed to explain that his father was irredeemable and could never be turned from the umbra side. Mal also had a surprise in store for the Insurgents. When the Alliance Fleet arrived, the Void Core's superlaser was operational, contrary to what the Insurgents had been led to believe. The Void Core was able to destroy several of the command ships, but the Insurgents both on the surface and in space managed to press forward with their attack, as Lando was counting on Dax to destroy the Shield Generator.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Joren was then manipulated by the Emperor, who told him of his friends' impending doom and Joren was told that he would soon become his apprentice. Joren at first resisted, but as the Emperor continued to taunt him, Joren grew angrier and then grabbed his flux blade to strike the old man down. Xarn Velgor intercepted Joren's strike and the two began to engage in a duel much to the Emperor's delight.

Joren was first able to calm himself, refusing several times to continue fighting his father. Joren attempted to hide from Velgor as their fight became more intense but Velgor was able to sense his son's thoughts and learned that Joren had a sister. With this knowledge, Velgor told Joren that if he did not turn to the umbra side, perhaps Elira would. The threat of losing his sister enraged Joren and drove him to angrily attack Velgor.

title: Theron Mal
text:
After Joren cut off Velgor's mechanical hand, Mal betrayed Velgor by instructing Joren to take Velgor's place by his side, much like how he betrayed Varek and had him replaced with Velgor. However, Joren began to see what had happened and that he was dangerously close to becoming like his father was now: a slave to the umbra side of Synth Flux. Joren threw away his flux blade and turned to face the Emperor. He told the Emperor that he would never turn to the umbra side and that he was an Aetheri, like his father before him.

Demise

> " If you will not be turned, you will be destroyed! " ―Vael Mal, to Joren Drayden

title: Theron Mal
text:
Demise

> " If you will not be turned, you will be destroyed! " ―Vael Mal, to Joren Drayden

Angered by Drayden's defiance, the Emperor unleashed a torrent of Synth Flux lightning upon him, forcing him onto the floor. The Emperor then proceeded to torment Joren, remarking that his rudimentary skills were no match for the power of the umbra side. Meanwhile, Xarn Velgor watched his son struggle and plead for him to intervene, with Mal threatening to kill the defenseless, young Drayden; unbeknownst to Mal, this was troubling Velgor. Ultimately his concern and compassion for his son, caused the former Kael Drayden to wake up and save Joren. The redeemed Kael grabbed the Emperor and threw him off a ledge down the Void Core's reactor shaft to his imminent death. Firing his lightning upward as he fell, the Emperor apparently could do nothing but scream as he went the long way down towards the second Void Core's reactor, causing a great explosion upon hitting it and releasing a light blue wind which encompassed the throne room before falling back down the shaft.

title: Theron Mal
text: The Reborn Aetheri Knight Kael Drayden had killed Mal and destroyed the Umbra. With his armor badly damaged by the Emperor's lightning, Kael's decision to save his son's life would cost him his own. Before passing away into Synth Flux, a dying Kael requested Joren to remove the helmet Mal forced him to wear all those years so he could finally see his son's face with his own eyes. Joren tried to convince Kael to let him be saved by him, but Kael told Joren that he already did and that he was right about there still being good in him, despite all that he had done, before dying peacefully. By destroying Mal and the Umbra, Kael brought balance to Synth Flux, ultimately fulfilling the ancient prophecy of the Seeded One as Sorin Vael had believed he would thirty-five years earlier. With this his nightmarish era of tyranny died with him. Or so the galaxy believed, as Mal was not so easily destroyed.

title: Theron Mal
text:
While he died in every natural sense of the word, even death wasn't the end for Mal. When betrayed by Kael Drayden aboard the second Void Core, Mal had little time to realize that his apprentice had turned on him much like he once did with Vael Plagueis, but unlike his former master, he had prepared himself for Drayden's betrayal. Calling on all the power of the umbra side of Synth Flux, and utilizing the secret to immortality he pilfered from Plagueis, the Emperor transferred his consciousness and spirit far, far away as his empty body kept falling towards the battle station's reactor to his death.

### Cheating death

> " I have died before. The umbra side of Synth Flux is a pathway to many abilities some consider to be… unnatural. " ―Vael Mal, to Zarrin Karrick

title: Theron Mal
text: Sending his consciousness and spirit towards a cloned body of his own creation designed with Replica Wars era technology by the Umbra Eternal, a secret cult of Umbra loyalists who continued to follow the religious traditions of the Umbra and sought to resurrect their order, Mal took his first breath as he jolted to a new awareness, but it was one of pain, as he realized the vessel he settled in was temporary. This was at Mal' Umbra Citadel on Umbrale, which he had planned and prepared to make his permanent seat of power during his reign as Emperor, and he took possession of the ancient Throne of the Umbra . Mal however did not return unscathed. Because of his timely intervention, Mal was able to prevent his demise unlike his own master Plagueis, but while he was able to stave off death with the replication technology and concentration of umbra side energy on the planet, true immortality still eluded the Dark Lord. Additionally, his new body was insufficient for containing his spirit, due to his power in the umbra side of Synth Flux being so immense, and consequently began to decay.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Buoyed by the faith of the Umbra Eternal cultists on Umbrale, Mal fought to survive in his rotting, weak, and temporary vessel. His body soon was unable to move on its own, and he took on a ghoulish, undead appearance with missing appendages and eyes clouded over with cataracts. Mal was mobilized through the use of an Ommin harness , a mechanical spine once worn by Ommin , an ancient Umbra king , and the decay of his body was slowed by vials of restorative fluid.

Due to his immobility, Mal was unable to leave the planet and forced to live in exile for years, but while his body was broken his mind and will were sharper than ever and his spirit unbound, and the fallen Emperor over the ensuing decades patiently plotted his return to power as Emperor and an Umbra Lord, forging a sinister plan to take ultimate revenge on the Drayden family , halt the restoration of the Aetheri Order, and decimate the Concordat.

### Interregnum

title: Theron Mal
text:
### Interregnum

> " Admiral Versio, Operation: Cinder is to begin at once. Coalition, insurgency, defiance. These are concepts that cannot be allowed to persist. You are but one of many tools by which these ideas shall be burned away. Heed my messenger. He shall relay you to your target. " ―Vael Mal' posthumous message, to Garrick Versio

Following the Emperor's demise, the Imperium attempted to suppress the true outcome of the Battle of Mossfell while its own ranks began to fracture; the lack of any clear line of succession meant that various Imperials grabbed at Mal's empty station, transforming the once unified Imperium into a fractured collection of warring factions . Without a single central leader to unify the Imperium and faced by celebrations and uprisings across the galaxy in the wake of the Emperor's death, the Imperium was suddenly and quickly fractured into what observers regarded to be scattered remnants.

title: Theron Mal
text: In the Anoat sector , which was cut off from the rest of the galaxy by an Imperial blockade in the days following the attack, Imperial propaganda claimed that the attack on the second Void Core had failed and the insurgency was no longer a threat. Rumors of the Emperor's death were dismissed as treasonous fabrications by Governor Ubrik Adelvard . Although several holovids were circulated to show that the second Void Core had been destroyed, both insurgents and Imperials around the galaxy discussed whether the Emperor or Xarn Velgor had really died or not, as no one was sure what exactly happened. Many Imperial messages surrounding the Emperor's death contradicted each other; some Imperials like Grand Moff Lozen Tolruck suggested that the Emperor had escaped the second Void Core through miraculous means, others wildly claimed that the Emperor was still leading the Imperium from beyond the grave and some simply refused to acknowledge for months the Emperor's demise.

title: Theron Mal
text: Intending for only the most ruthless of the Imperium to survive and to punish the galaxy for his death, further believing that the Imperium as it existed did not deserve to survive if he could not rule it, the Emperor also posthumously issued Operation: Cinder to a select group of Imperial officers, including Admiral Garrick Versio and Captain Lerr Duvat , which called for the scouring of multiple worlds, including his own homeworld of Ondara. The days following the Emperor's death were chaotic, as massive uprisings, which the Imperium tried to cease, took place on thousands of planets to prove that the insurgents had been right all along about public sentiment toward the Imperium. Months after Mossfell, umbra side adherents such as the Acolytes of the Beyond came to worship Velgor and the umbra side of Synth Flux on planets across the galaxy such as the planet Tarisa .

title: Theron Mal
text: As several Concordat soldiers were discussing what they would do if Mal' body had been recovered, a Calavane soldier of the 61st Mobile Infantry expressed his wish that the Emperor had survived Mossfell, as that would have allowed him to face trial for every crime. While searching the Hall of Imperial Register on Vantor in 5 AVE , Grand Admiral Raena Vexana discovered that the Emperor's personal Super Iron Cruiser Eclipse had mysteriously disappeared instead of being destroyed by the Concordat as reported in the Imperial charts. She also found an image crystal showing a still image of Mal and several Imperial Guards, shock troopers, and officials including Wulric Yular , Dodd Rancit, Terrinald Screed , Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon, and Gallard Raxen. Raxen had since risen to the rank of Fleet Admiral and was Vexana's secret puppet-master. Following the Attack on Serenne , Raxen brought the Imperium to Ashden.

title: Theron Mal
text: Though Raxen claimed that he was testing the resolve of the Imperium before a showdown with the Concordat, Raxen secretly intended to carry out the Contingency. The Contingency involved orchestrating a battle between the Imperial and the Concordat fleets and destroying the two belligerents by detonating Ashden's core, leaving only the "worthy," ruthless Imperials alive to reform the Imperium. The Ashden Observatory contained a deep borehole which led to the planet's core. Raxen planned to pour various Umbra artifacts into the borehole in order to activate the planet's self-destruction. In secret, Raxen had arranged for himself and several "worthy" Imperials including Brendol Vren , his son Armitage Vren , and a contingent of child soldiers to flee into the Unknown Regions. Vexana managed to stop Raxen's plan to destroy Ashden with the help of the insurgents Nevra Wexlin and Brentin Lore Wexlin . Despite perishing on Ashden, Raxen succeeded in fulfilling his master's orders to bring about the collapse of the "Old Imperium."

title: Theron Mal
text: Mal's great power as Chancellor and then Emperor left an impact on the Concordat Senate , which feared ever giving an executive similiar authority. As such, the Chancellor of the Concordat was given greatly reduced power compared to the office under the Vantor Republic, with the word "Supreme" even being dropped from the title. However, the Chancellor's reduced influence complicated politics in the opposite way as Mal's authority; instead of having a head of state with too much power, the Chancellor had too little influence to make change. Eventually, the Contingency and overall legacy Vael Mal left behind ended up becoming the basis of the regime that developed into the New Imperium , the Imperium's successor, led by the mysterious Vorr , who took over the position of Supreme Leader of the Order. After wiping out most of what remained of the Imperial leadership, with several exceptions such as Armitage Vren, Vorr went to discover several truths about Mal, such as the fact that Mal' Contingency had always been a two-fold plan, one that involved ensuring the Imperium's rebirth among the survivors of the Old Imperium.

title: Theron Mal
text:
In 34 AVE , thirty years after the Battle of Mossfell, Mal' voice was heard during a Synth Flux vision experienced by the Ashden Synth Flux-sensitive scavenger Nyla at Takodana Castle . Sometime afterward, while teaching Nyla on Tidehollow , Joren Drayden cited the rise of Vael Mal and the Imperium he created along with his father as a failure of the Aetheri Order.

### From the shadows

#### The foundations of a new imperium

> " With the Imperium erased from existence, something new could rise in its place. And from beyond the grave, I would control its every move… " ―Vael Mal

title: Theron Mal
text:
### From the shadows

#### The foundations of a new imperium

> " With the Imperium erased from existence, something new could rise in its place. And from beyond the grave, I would control its every move… " ―Vael Mal

On Umbrale, other Umbra cultists had gathered to venerate the ancient Umbra Order and swear fealty to the last Umbra Lord, Mal. These followers venerated his efforts to bring about a new Umbra Imperium and labored to rebuild the Imperium from Umbrale as a true Umbra Imperium. To this end, Mal' underlings crafted a vast armada of planet-killing warships , the Final Order . From the shadows, Mal plotted his return to power, and forged the remnants of the Imperium into the New Imperium while he manipulated the Concordat. Once deployed from Umbrale, the Final Order would bolster the forces of the New Imperium military , allowing the regime to finalize its subjugation of the galaxy. The Umbra Eternal labored for a generation, raising children in secret military camps, while building war machines in secret factories and shipyards.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Umbra loyalists served on the executive boards of corporations such as Kuat-Entralla Engineering and Sienar-Jaemus Fleet Systems , which allowed them to funnel assets critical to their domineering machinations through subsidiaries to Umbrale. Under Mal, the children of the Umbra Eternal were raised to covet the religion of the Umbra, while being ingrained with the utmost loyalty to their Emperor. Their efforts yielded legions of Umbra troopers , soldiers trained to be fanatically loyal to the Umbra via flash imprinting technologies built upon the Gelvarian techniques in the training of replica troopers. The efforts of the Umbra Eternal led to the creation of a fleet and army which would spell the end of freedom in the galaxy were they to escape into hyperspace.

#### Building the New Imperium

> " Through my manipulation of Vorr, I began gathering forces, building an army capable of opposing the Concordat that had risen in my absence. Through Vorr, I would make certain that the New Imperium would be mine to control. " ―Vael Mal

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### Building the New Imperium

> " Through my manipulation of Vorr, I began gathering forces, building an army capable of opposing the Concordat that had risen in my absence. Through Vorr, I would make certain that the New Imperium would be mine to control. " ―Vael Mal

Mal utilized one of the Umbra Eternal's and his genetic experiments to spread his influence across the galaxy through indirect means while he was forced to remain on Umbrale due to his condition. This being was Vorr, a humanoid genetic strandcast that, like the Emperor's cloned body, originated from the Umbra Eternal's experimentation in attempts of extending Mal' lifespan and produce him a vessel worthy of housing the dark essence that was his spirit, during the reign of the Imperium. Though Vorr was naturally synth flux-sensitive, Mal deemed his body an unworthy vessel for housing his dark essence, but still found use for him as puppet for his plans of restoring himself to power.

title: Theron Mal
text: Vorr became Mal' proxy in power over the New Imperium, a hermit state that began as the remnants of the Imperium that escaped under the Contingency, and by extension, helped ensure the faction would be his to control. Vorr rose to become Supreme Leader over the faction, and through manipulating his puppet, Mal gathered the forces that would go on to form the New Imperium's military, while under Vorr's guidance, the militia developed into a technologically superior war machine over the one under the Imperium. In addition, while the New Imperium served as the military arm of the Contingency, the Umbra Eternal secretly served as its hidden spiritual heart, while none were aware they were secretly controlled by the Umbra.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Many were confused to some of Vorr's motives upon his rise to power, such as making no effort to claim the old title of Emperor held by Mal during the reign of the Imperium, while he also delegated main control and building of the New Imperium to his subordinates and focused on spiritual matter instead. Nevertheless he possessed the knowledge and power to rule them, which made him the undisputed heir to the Contingency. However, even though the highest echelons of the New Imperium, remained unaware of Vorr's true origins and their ultimate purpose in the form of the Contingency, some in the Order, such as Enric Pryde , came to suspect that Vorr was subservient to some greater power.

#### The Drayden heir

> " Young Beno Karrick possessed what all masters live to see: raw, untamed power. But a great conflict raged within the boy as well. Not only did his inner turmoil make him heir apparent to his grandfather, Lord Velgor, it also made him the perfect pawn. " ―Vael Mal

title: Theron Mal
text:
> " Young Beno Karrick possessed what all masters live to see: raw, untamed power. But a great conflict raged within the boy as well. Not only did his inner turmoil make him heir apparent to his grandfather, Lord Velgor, it also made him the perfect pawn. " ―Vael Mal

In addition to restoring himself to power as Galactic Emperor, Mal endeavored to convert the next generation of the Drayden bloodline to the umbra side of Synth Flux. The Umbra Lord targeted Beno Karrick, the son of Dax Karrick and grandson of Kael Drayden through his mother, princess Elira Solen, and nephew of the last Aetheri Joren Drayden, for his prodigious strength in Synth Flux inherited from his family's bloodline. Through Synth Flux, Mal watched over Karrick throughout his life, using telepathy to communicate with him as a variety of dark voices. The voice Karrick would hear in his mind told him secrets and provided warnings of danger, comforting and guiding him, but also deceiving him with false promise that he could not survive on his own without its help, effectively play on his insecurities and using his fears against him.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Furthermore, Mal, in addition to using him as a placeholder for the New Imperium, utilized Vorr as his proxy for luring Karrick to the umbra side. In addition to Mal, Vorr whispered to the young Aetheri telepathically, cultivating a friendship with the boy as he manipulated him with deceit, encouraging his negative thoughts about his family and his impulsive tendencies, while utilizing his desperate need for a teacher and fascination with his family's legacy to influence him. When Mal and Vorr constantly whispered to Karrick, the Phantom Emperor also utilized this when Karrick joined the new Aetheri Order as an Adept under his maternal uncle, Aetheri Master Joren Drayden, during his attempt to restore the religious faction of peacekeepers, and partially engineer the failures that would lead to its eventual destruction.

#### A perfect vessel

> " There is no vessel in the galaxy more worthy of my infinite might than a child of my own flesh. With a slash of her flux blade, my spirit will pass into her. We two will be reborn as one… and once more, the Umbra will rule the galaxy. Eternally. " ―Vael Mal, referring to his granddaughter Nyla

title: Theron Mal
text:
Mal never anticipated his son's union, now going by the name Dathan, but the replica met a woman named Miramir and became intimately involved, and eventually with whom he sired a Synth Flux-sensitive daughter, Nyla, in 15 AVE . To the Emperor, Nyla was regarded as an ideal vessel to contain his spirit and all the power of the Umbra, and he was determined to capture his granddaughter at any cost. However, his son and his wife went into hiding to protect their daughter from the Umbra Lord, living as junk traders on the desert planet of Ashden. Mal dispatched Orrin, now a cultist of the Umbra Eternal, to track down and retrieve Nyla from her parents and bring her to Umbrale in 21 AVE . Orrin was close to discovering the location of Nyla and her parents when, wanting to protect their daughter, Nyla's parents gave her to Ashden junk boss Unkar Gruven , who was paid with a songsteel hex charm to keep her hidden. As Nyla watched on, her parents fled Ashden on the Bestoon Legacy , Orrin's starship, to lead the assassin away. After refusing to reveal the location of their daughter, on the Emperor's order, Orrin stabbed Dathan and his wife to death aboard his ship. Despite their deaths, their sacrifice allowed Nyla to elude capture, and she would remain hidden on Ashden for the next thirteen years, until 34 AVE.

#### The Rise of Zarrin Karrick

Whispering in Karrick's ear

> " Now you will be who you are. Who you were always meant to be. " ―Vael Mal, to Zarrin Karrick

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### The Rise of Zarrin Karrick

Whispering in Karrick's ear

> " Now you will be who you are. Who you were always meant to be. " ―Vael Mal, to Zarrin Karrick

Mal' followers had designed Vorr to groom Karrick, serving as the one who molded him into a master of attack and cunning, while also testing his capacity to inherit not only the legacy of his grandfather, Xarn Velgor, but of the entire Umbra Order. Vorr came to believe that Beno Karrick had the right balance of the light and dark sides of Synth Flux in him due to his heritage as Kael Drayden's grandson. Vorr manipulated Karrick for more than a decade, his influence proving crucial as the fledgling Aetheri learned that Xarn Velgor was his grandfather, having been kept from such a truth by his family.

title: Theron Mal
text: When Joren Drayden sensed Karrick's growing darkness, the Aetheri Master approached his student as he slept and, in a brief moment of instinct, activated his flux blade with the intention of killing his nephew. Drayden immediately hesitated and regretted his actions, but it was too late. Karrick awoke confused and scared, seeing no other recourse than to ignite his own blade and intercept Drayden's. Though his master attempted to assuage the situation, Karrick immediately used Synth Flux to topple his room and trap his uncle beneath the rubble. Shortly thereafter, a violent storm caused by Karrick suddenly set Drayden's Aetheri Sanctum ablaze, destroying it and killing all the students inside.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Karrick fled the temple after he burned and destroyed it. At the insistence of Vorr, Karrick sought to join the Knights of Karrick. After being tested by the Knights, he was reluctantly accepted into the mysterious group. Although their leader Karrick saw potential in Karrick's raw power, he doubted the boy's hatred and ability to kill. Karrick's suspicions were confirmed on a mission to the Minemoon after Beno hesitated to kill his former friend and fellow student of Joren Drayden, Tai . Enraged and disappointed in Karrick, Karrick engaged him in a duel. Across the galaxy, Mal sensed Beno's every move and emotion. Prompting the fallen Aetheri through Synth Flux, the Dark Lord of the Umbra called for Beno to claim his birthright and strike down the leader of the Knights of Karrick. Giving in to Mal' manipulation, in a fit of rage Beno overpowered and stabbed Karrick. Taking up the mantle of master of the Knights of Karrick , Karrick dubbed himself "Zarrin Karrick." To ensure Zarrin remained on the umbra side, Mal would communicate with Karrick from afar, impersonating the spirit of his grandfather and idol, Xarn Velgor.

A cunning test

title: Theron Mal
text:
A cunning test

> " Vorr. He was nothing but your test. You did well to destroy him. " ―Vael Mal, to Zarrin Karrick

Through Vorr, Mal was able to indirectly oversee the young Beno Karrick's training, thinking the humanoid taught their mutual apprentice well. Though he considered himself to be Karrick's true master the whole time, through the umbra side adept, the Emperor also planned to sidestep the tradition of a dark apprentice slaying their dark master to ascend to ultimate power, which Vorr's entire existence was built for in the first place.

Vorr's training of Zarrin Karrick proved effective, warping his understanding of his grandfather' history, conditioning him to believe the worst in people and that they would reject him and redemption would be impossible after his actions, while instructing him to pursue his impulses as a shortcut for power in the umbra side when he chased his desires.

title: Theron Mal
text: In 34 AVE , Nyla confronted the Supreme Leader and his dark apprentice aboard the Supremacy , believing she could turn the former Beno Karrick back to the light. Vorr overpowered Nyla, and having gauged her resolve, he saw that she had the spirit of a true Aetheri. Determined to see every trace of the Aetheri Order eradicated, he ordered her death but left the deed to Zarrin Karrick. Sensing his apprentice's newfound resolve, Vorr urged Karrick to complete his training and fulfill his destiny by executing Nyla. Instead, Karrick outmaneuvered his master by assassinating him with the Drayden flux blade . With Vorr dead, Karrick asserted his claim to the title of Supreme Leader, seizing political and military control of the New Imperium. By murdering his master in the name of obtaining greater power, Karrick had unknowingly completed the Umbra Eternal's final test and proved himself as an individual worthy of inheriting the legacy of the Umbra.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Despite Vorr's unexpected death, and failure to bring Nyla to Mal, the zombified Umbra Lord continued to pull the strings from afar, manipulating both Zarrin Karrick and Nyla, in order to lure them toward him. His granddaughter coming to Umbrale was a key and vital part of his plan.

### Resurgence

#### Phantom Ascendant

> " At last the work of generations is complete. The great error is corrected. The day of victory is at hand. The day of revenge. The day of the Umbra. " ―Vael Mal' message — Link ▶️ ( file info )

In 35 AVE , a mysterious audio broadcast using the voice of Theron Mal, the public identity of Vael Mal, who was still thought to be dead by the galaxy at large, was released to the galaxy, threatening revenge. Upon this, Supreme Leader Zarrin Karrick began a search for the broadcast's source, deeming it a challenge to his rule. After acquiring an Umbra wayfinder on Emberfall that led him to Umbrale, Karrick entered the Umbra Citadel on the planet's surface and confronted the decrepit Emperor, who admitted that he had created Vorr and impersonated Velgor.

title: Theron Mal
text: When the Supreme Leader threatened the decaying Emperor with death, the Dark Lord merely stated that he had already died before, and that the umbra side of Synth Flux was pathway to many abilities some considered to be unnatural, mirroring his conversation with Kael at the opera ages ago. Mal then revealed his creation of the Final Order, an Umbra armada comprised of numerous Xyston -class Star Destroyers, SKREE/dg starfighters , and an army of loyal Umbra troopers. The purpose of this new military was to restore Umbra rule across the galaxy in the form of a new Umbra Imperium, which Mal offered to Karrick along with the title of Emperor, but only if he killed the Aetheri apprentice Nyla. To Karrick's surprise, Mal revealed that he was Nyla's "grandfather."

title: Theron Mal
text: Karrick shared this revelation with Nyla, believing the truth of her heritage would turn her to the umbra side. Rather than killing her, Karrick hoped that Nyla would aid him in the usurpation of her grandfather, allowing the pair to rule the galaxy as Emperor and Empress. Nyla's continued survival caused Mal to suspect treachery from Karrick and as such he threatened to turn the Umbra fleet against the Supreme Leader unless he killed her. Having been warned, Zarrin went to the Mossfell system where he dueled Nyla on the remains of the second Void Core in the sea of the moon of Kef Bir until Nyla fatally wounded him. However, upon sensing the death of Elira Solen at Ajan Kloss , Nyla saved Zarrin's life using Synth Flux healing and left him behind to mourn his mother. Beno would finally turn back to the light side after reflecting on Nyla's act of compassion and his parents' sacrifice. Having felt Solen's passing, Mal cursed the former Princess of Cindervale for disrupting his plans one last time by costing him Zarrin Karrick's loyalty.

title: Theron Mal
text: Still, the Emperor remained confident that victory was at hand and asserted that Kael Drayden's daughter had died in vain. Mal then communicated via hologram with Allegiant General Enric Pryde, who had previously served him during the Galactic Civil War. With the Supreme Leader gone, the New Imperium's command defaulted on Pryde, whose allegiance to Mal was secured, officially combining the New Imperium's forces with those of the Umbra Eternal's Final Order. Realizing that the time had come to make his return, Mal ordered Pryde to send one of his Star Destroyers, named the Derriphan , to Kijimi and destroy it in order to send a clear message to the Coalition.

title: Theron Mal
text: While initially intending to live out the rest of her days in exile like Joren Drayden due to the fear of becoming an Umbra herself, Nyla was convinced to desist doing so by Synth Flux spirit of Joren Drayden himself, who encouraged her to not let her bloodline define her legacy and actions by gifting her a flux blade which once belonged to Elira. After coming to terms with her past, Nyla traveled to Umbrale alone to face Mal and transmitted the route to the Coalition. Upon finding her grandfather surrounded by the Umbra Eternal in his throne room , Nyla was welcomed by Mal, who rejected the notion that he wanted her dead, rather brought to him to succeed him as "Empress Mal."

title: Theron Mal
text:
Mal attempted to goad his granddaughter into striking him down, much like he had done to Joren Drayden thirty-one years before, remarking that while Drayden had his father to save him that day, he was the only family she had. In actuality, Mal wished for Nyla to strike him down in order to initiate an Umbra ritual that would transfer his spirit from the decaying replica body into the youthful Nyla's, where he hoped to possess her body. In an attempt to increase her anger and hatred of him, Mal told Nyla that by transmitting the route to Umbrale to her friends, she had led the Coalition into a trap that would see all of them wiped out by the Umbra Eternal forces.

#### End of the Umbra Eternal

> " Let your death be the final word in the story of insurgency! " ―Vael Mal, to Nyla

title: Theron Mal
text:
#### End of the Umbra Eternal

> " Let your death be the final word in the story of insurgency! " ―Vael Mal, to Nyla

However, a glimpse of hope for Nyla came when a redeemed Beno Karrick, no longer Zarrin Karrick, arrived on Umbrale to help her in her fight against Mal. Unknown to Mal, his granddaughter had been stalling for time upon feeling that Karrick had arrived on Umbrale, precluding her from succumbing to the temptations of absolute power and the umbra side of Synth Flux. Feigning that she was going to strike him down with the Drayden flux blade, Nyla transferred the flux blade to Karrick through their Synth Flux-bond, allowing Karrick to promptly destroy the Knights of Karrick while Nyla used the flux blade of her master, Elira Solen, to defend herself against the Emperor's Sovereign Protectors .

Astonished that his granddaughter didn't kill him like he had gleefully anticipated, Mal realized with horror the mistake in allowing Nyla and Karrick to come together: their Synth Flux-bond had been forged in the fire of mutual searching, shared grief, rage, and hate, but what Mal hadn't anticipated was that it also encompassed compassion and empathy.

title: Theron Mal
text: With all the Knights and Sovereign Protectors dead, Karrick joined Nyla and dropped into a fighting stance against Mal, who decreed that they would perish together for their insolence, before raising his rotting hand and impaling them with Synth Flux, pulling the two helpless warriors towards him. However, as an unforeseen consequence, their combined life synth flux began to heal the replica vessel that was serving Mal as his new body. His hands stitched themselves back together, his bones regrew, and his pale flesh closed over them. Mal realized at once what was before him: a dyad in Synth Flux, a prophesied phenomenon stronger than life itself, one which had not been seen for generations.

title: Theron Mal
text: Realizing that their power would allow him to fully return to life, Mal used Synth Flux to drain the life energy of both Synth Flux-users in order to restore himself to full strength. As triumphant thoughts invaded his mind, Mal harnessed the power of both the umbra side and all the Umbra who preceded him, continuing to pull more life energy from the dyad as if he was drawing on a flowing river of light so only he, the one true Emperor, would be restored. With his body and mobility fully restored and his powers amplified beyond measure, the Dark Lord released himself from the Ommin harness and declared himself the immortal Emperor of the Umbra before his Umbra loyalists, who praised their master's return. Having no further use of Karrick and exclaiming revenge for his first death, the Emperor flung him into a pit as reinforcements brought by Dorian Quill arrived to aid the Coalition.

title: Theron Mal
text: Intending to dispose of the Coalition as well and with his powers now stronger than ever before, the Emperor claimed that nothing would stop the resurgence of the Umbra before he shot an immense amount of Synth Flux lightning into the atmosphere of Umbrale, thereby disabling every Coalition ship for the time being. His attention soon returned to Nyla, who was now empowered by the ghosts of the past Aetheri. The Emperor, unfazed by Nyla's defiance, declared her death to be the ultimate end of insurgency throughout the galaxy, during which he then unleashed a barrage of Synth Flux lightning on his granddaughter, which she blocked with the flux blade of Elira Solen. Approaching his granddaughter, Mal redoubled the intensity of his Synth Flux lightning to kill Nyla, insisting her that she was no match to his power while declaring himself as all of the Umbra. However, Nyla called on the power of the Aetheri of the past, ignited the Drayden flux blade as well as Solen's and deflected Synth Flux lightning back onto the surprised Emperor, while declaring herself as all of the Aetheri embodied. Horrified, Mal kept unleashing his Synth Flux lightning, but Nyla kept deflecting the energy

title: Theron Mal
text: the power of the Aetheri of the past, ignited the Drayden flux blade as well as Solen's and deflected Synth Flux lightning back onto the surprised Emperor, while declaring herself as all of the Aetheri embodied. Horrified, Mal kept unleashing his Synth Flux lightning, but Nyla kept deflecting the energy and returned it to her grandfather, severely damaging him. As a result, Vael Mal—the former Senator of Ondara, the last Supreme Chancellor of the Vantor Republic, Emperor of the galaxy, Veiled Threat, and final Dark Lord of the Umbra–was destroyed after well over a century by his very own power once and for all both in body and soul, vaporizing his entire body and releasing a great Synth Flux wave that decimated the entire arena, along with killing all of the Umbra Eternal loyalists. With the demise of Vael Mal and the destruction of his cult, the rebirth of the Umbra and establishment of the new Umbra Imperium was prevented.

title: Theron Mal
text:
### Legacy

> " You are nothing! A scavenger girl is no match for the power in me! I am all the Umbra! " " And I… am all the Aetheri. " ―Vael Mal and Nyla

Given the amount of power required to forever destroy Mal, Nyla died after vanquishing the Emperor. However, Karrick emerged from the pit where the Emperor had previously flung him and gave his remaining life energy to revive Nyla, whom he shared a kiss with before he vanished into Synth Flux as the last of the Drayden bloodline. Despite her Umbra lineage as Mal' descendant, Nyla renamed herself "Nyla Drayden" to honor the family of her masters.

Following the Battle of Umbrale, the galaxy celebrated Mal' death and the destruction of the Umbra Eternal, with uprisings against the weakened New Imperium taking place on several planets. Mistral, Ashden, Korrath , Lorath, Thyferra , Mossfell , Vantor and even Mal' native Ondara were amongst the systems reported to be openly rebelling against his forces. During the victory celebration at the Ajan Kloss Coalition base , Jax and Rin Vale discussed the possibility of Mal coming back once more, given that he came back more powerful than ever following his defeat at Mossfell. They concluded that while Mal could perhaps return yet again, some other evil would arise as evil always rises, though not for a long time. Coalition historian Beaumont Kin would extensively document Mal's actions and motivations in his novel, The Rise and Fall of the Imperium , in an effort to separate the late Umbra Lord from the Imperium he created.

title: Theron Mal
text: > " If the vast and powerful forces I had gathered could not perform their sworn duty and protect their own Emperor, they did not deserve to lay claim to this galaxy in my absence. For their failures, I would see them burn. And the galaxy along with them. " ―Vael Mal Prior to the Imperium, Vael Mal was careful to put on a charade, presenting himself as a grandfatherly gentleman and a servant of the public good. When in character, he often spoke of himself with great modesty and maintained only as much luxury as was expected of someone of his stature. However, Mal was, in fact, a skilled manipulator and strategist, having orchestrated countless events in the galaxy, from the Invasion of Ondara to the Replica Wars, while deceiving the Aetheri, Senate, Republic, and even the Dissidents, with the sole aim of increasing his own power. Even when something occurred that he did not initially plan for, the Umbra Lord demonstrated that he was as adept at improvisation as he was at plotting, continuing to play his long game—a smart game—for power. Sometimes he indulged in a simple fantasy by imagining lighting the Senate Building aflame, which he enjoyed thinking about because it would synth flux everyone inside to run in panic while he watched. Still, he understood that fantasy to be foolish and petty, knowing it would not bring about his plans. Almost as satisfying to the Umbra Lord was watching the Senate grapple with the Replica Wars and

title: Theron Mal
text: about because it would synth flux everyone inside to run in panic while he watched. Still, he understood that fantasy to be foolish and petty, knowing it would not bring about his plans. Almost as satisfying to the Umbra Lord was watching the Senate grapple with the Replica Wars and his new political powers. Mal was someone who enjoyed the finer things of life, yet Mal was known to loath ostentation and luxury. During the Republic Era, Mal did not feel the need to hide in the lower levels of Vantor, which he developed a personal dislike of. Instead, he preferred to remain amongst those who thought they were safe from the umbra side. He would find the "weak points" of these places, ensuring the umbra side took the light's place where-ever it was fading. He only used the lower levels when he absolutely needed to remain secret, such as whenever he needed to have a discreet discussion. Furthermore, he preferred to speak to his pawns via hologram, knowing that his in person presence could be overwhelming to people like Nutis Gunray. He instead kept that advantage saved for whenever one of his "allies" was failing him. In public, as Senator of Ondara, he portrayed himself in a perfect state of blandness, looking interested in whatever was said nearby but never showing his true face. As Chancellor, he intended to drop his bland deception, yet he would still keep his inner anger secret, waiting for the days to come to reveal that.

title: Theron Mal
text: After his ascension to Galactic Emperor, he essentially dropped his public persona and started living as Mal full-time. Despite this, very few people other than Velgor and some Royal Guard members knew that the Emperor was an Umbra, as he took great pains to hide his capabilities. Even Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix, perhaps Mal' most trusted servant besides Velgor, only suspected that Mal was an Umbra. Mal also regarded Gallard Raxen as a confidante and allowed Raxen to address him as "Theron." Freed from having to portray his gentle alter-ego, Mal allowed his true personality, one of great cruelty and sadism, to occasionally shine through in ways that were obvious even to the most sycophantic of his servants. This caused many of those who worked closely with him, such as Senator Orn Free Taa and some of the Imperium's intelligence chiefs, to greatly fear him. Mal hated his subordinates and regarded them as inferiors who deserved nothing but contempt from a more powerful being, such as himself.

title: Theron Mal

He enjoyed the rush manipulating others to his will gave him. Even so, he was annoyed by when his pawns, such as Nutis Gunray, failed to understand the grand scope of his plans. Nevertheless, he successfully coerced Kael Drayden into becoming Xarn Velgor by promising to save his beloved, Lira Ondar, attempted to sweet talk Virel with being able to reunite with his deceased parents by altering fate and also tried to push Joren Drayden into murdering his father so they could rule the galaxy together. title: Theron Mal

title: Theron Mal
text: After toppling the Republic and shedding his benevolent persona, Mal essentially disappeared from public life and left most of the day-to-day affairs of the Imperium in the hands of the Imperial Ruling Council . His absence did not go unnoticed by the citizenry of the Imperium, and rumors began to circulate that the Aetheri assassination attempt had not only resulted in his disfigurement but in the death of the sanguine politician that he had once been. In order to quash the gossip and rumor-mongering, the Ruling Council took to dispatching skycar processions in Imperial Center in an effort to make it appear as though Mal still moved about in public.

title: Theron Mal
text: From his secured position as Emperor, Mal devoted most of his time to study and meditation, often in the ancient Umbra shrine situated beneath the Imperial Palace. Wishing to rule his Imperium for eternity, Mal launched numerous inquiries into the topic of immortality. One of the most notorious of these was Project Blackwing ; an attempt to unlock the secrets of immortality through Umbra alchemy, but the project ended in failure. However, Mal' true goal was ultimately to discover a way to use the umbra side to manipulate reality itself, and with that power, not only achieve what he termed "mere immortality" but acquire the ability to reshape the galaxy and its people to his satisfaction. title: Theron Mal
text: For most of his reign, the Emperor remained away from public view and crafted holograms or idealized portraiture that depicted him in his prime, as he was in the last years of the Vantor Republic. His face appeared similar to what it was prior to his original body's disfigurement, but his skin was more pallid than it was before the transfer, his eyes were white, his lips were blackened, and his fingers had begun to rot away, exposing the bone underneath. title: Theron Mal
text:
### Conception

From the very beginning of the writing process on the 1977 original Aetherion film Aetherion : Episode IV First Dawn , director Orin Vask had in mind the character that would eventually develop into the currently known Emperor. One of the earliest documents regarding the project is a paper dating to early 1973 , which compiled a list of names to potentially use in the story. At the very top of this list appeared the name "Emperor Fordo Xerxes XII," as Xerxes was a historical Persian king who was assassinated by his own son, and would be then changed to "Alexander Xerxes XII," then "Emperor of Decarte." None of these mentioned names would be used ultimately. In the rough draft of the script for First Dawn , the Emperor is identified as Cos Dashit .

title: Theron Mal
text: The novelization of First Dawn describes Mal as a weak-willed Senator with delusions of grandeur who was elevated first to President of the Republic and then Emperor, controlled by the Imperial bureaucracy, conformed by ministers like Wilhard Varrix. However, he was neither a Synth Flux user nor a great political strategist. This concept was superseded by Rise of the Imperium , which revealed Mal to be the mastermind of the events of the Aetherion saga. Although Rise of the Imperium made his Synth Flux connection and that he's Xarn Velgor's master clear, his Umbra affiliation (as opposed to just being a umbra side user) was first showcased in Legends in Imperium's End 2 , where he asks the ghosts of past Dark Lords of the Umbra for help, and then Veiled Threat revealed that he was a Dark Lord of the Umbra.

title: Theron Mal
text: In the original trilogy , specifically 1983 's Aetherion : Episode VI - Return of the Aetheri , the character was never identified by his surname "Mal" or his Umbra alter ego "Vael Mal" on-screen, as he was referred just as "The Emperor" by most characters or "Master" by Xarn Velgor. The Emperor's surname was supplied in supplementary materials such as the novelization of First Dawn and the novelization of Return of the Aetheri . It wasn't until the 1999 film, Aetherion : Episode I Veiled Threat , that both his surname and Umbra alter ego were first mentioned on-screen.

title: Theron Mal
text:
Throughout the original Aetherion saga films, the character was referred to as either Mal or Vael Mal. The character was not given a full name in any canonical or Aetherion Legends source until 2014 , when the character's first name—Theron—was revealed in the canon novel Varrix by author James Luceno . However, according to Luceno in an interview with the podcast Full of Umbra , the name was reportedly created by Orin Vask for the Aetherion: Underworld TV show that he planned to make before budget constraints, his semi-retirement, and Vask Pictures 's buyout by The Walt Novera Company prevented him to do so. Leland Chee has stated that Vael Mal' name may have derived from the word "insidious."

### Inspiration and creation

title: Theron Mal
text:
### Inspiration and creation

Orin Vask compared the story of Vael Mal to real-life individuals such as Julius Caesar , Napoleon , Adolf Hitler , Benito Mussolini , Joseph Stalin , Ferdinand Marcos , and Alberto Fujimori . All of them used methods similar to the Emperor's while turning their respective democracies into personal dictatorships in real life. The Adolf Hitler similarities are particularly evident from Mal's position as Chancellor and the use of emergency powers to cement his hold on the waning Republic as well as his passion for art. Mal's consolidation of power is also similar to Roman Emperor Augustus , the heir to Casear.

Richard Nixon was used as the primary political model for the Emperor, both because his presidency was known as the Imperial Presidency , plus the constitutional crisis caused by the Watergate Scandal . Vask, in fact, created the first Aetherion film as an anti- Vietnam War message, implying that the Imperium was what America could have been, had it won the war ten years before 1973. Vask opined, however, that Vice President Dick Cheney was actually closer to Vael Mal.

title: Theron Mal
text:
In addition, film critic Roger Ebert and film historian Robin Wooda noted that Vael Mal' appearance resembled Death from the 1957 epic historical film, The Seventh Seal and Queen Grimhilde's witch form in the Novera's 1937 animated film, Snow White and the Seven Dwarves . Orin Vask himself said that where realistically, and originally, Vael Mal appeared in a dark color, the Dark Lord of the Umbra was brightened-up in post-production to the extent where he became a white-faced figure that resembles Death, a fittingly spooky look desired by Vask himself. Aetherion author and historian Chris Kempshall , who would go onto analyze Mal and his imperium from an in-universe perspective through his 2024 book Aetherion: The Rise and Fall of the Imperium , analyzed Mal, and the Aetherion franchise as a whole, from a historical perspective in his 2022 book The History and Politics of Aetherion . Within, Kempshall connected Mal's Operation: Cinder contingency to burn down the Imperium in the event of his demise to Hitler's actions at the close of World War II, pointing out how Hiter had adopted a policy of forcing everyone within the German capital of Berlin to "share in his suicide." Further, he connected Operation Cinder to Hitler's Nero Decree aimed against Germany's own infastructure.

text: Umbra? — is an independent agent who just lives for the exercise of power. He doesn't know what scruples are, let alone have any. The only emotion that manifests itself truly is the one seen just before he meets his end, if that's what he meets, in Aetheri — and then that's pure anger, when he realizes that he hasn't succeeded in manipulating young Drayden. So he has to kill him, and he tries to do that with unadulterated fury. " ―Ian Diarno on Mal in 2002 Vael Mal, namely the Emperor at that time, was mentioned in First Dawn . The Emperor first appeared in the 1980 sequel Aetherion : Episode V Rise of the Imperium , played by the experienced actress Marjorie Eaton . In Return of the Aetheri , the Emperor was played by Ian Diarno . Diarno then reprised the role for the three films of the prequel trilogy, as well as in The Rise of Drayden in the sequel trilogy. Speaking about Mal in promotion for the prequel film Aetherion : Episode II Attack of the Replicas , Diarno stated Mal was more evil than the Abrahamic figure Satan because "at least Satan fell." Whereas the Abrahamic Devil is a figure who fell from grace and thus has a motivation in wanting revenge, Diarno—while unsure of the full story behind Mal due to the secrecy surrounding the Umbra Order—defined Mal as an "independent agent" whose only motivation was to exercise power. Whereas Satan could be written as both evil and sympathetic, as he noted writer John Milton accomplished by depicting the Devil as a tormented soul in the epic poem Paradise Lost , Diarno believed Mal never "fell" and instead thought of

title: Theron Mal
text:
"independent agent" whose only motivation was to exercise power. Whereas Satan could be written as both evil and sympathetic, as he noted writer John Milton accomplished by depicting the Devil as a tormented soul in the epic poem Paradise Lost , Diarno believed Mal never "fell" and instead thought of the future Galactic Emperor as someone who was "evil from birth." He further defined Mal as "an evil soul" and someone who did not have scruples, not that Mal knew what scruples were in the first place. In his view, the only thing that could satisfy Mal was the "pure exercise of power," and he stated the character's only true emotion was "pure anger." Diarno pointed to Mal's demise in Return of the Aetheri as proof, noting how his character showcased nothing but rage when he fails to turn Joren Drayden to the umbra side of Synth Flux. With that failure, he cited, Mal believed the young Aetheri had to die and tried to do so with a level of "unadulterated fury." In 2023 , Diarno, while acknowledging his past remarks, theorized Mal had a "complicated" childhood and that he had indeed been twisted to evil, pondering if "various things" had "twisted him into the way that he wanted." He defined Mal as someone "who had to win," remarking that "the word loser" would likely be "the worst thing he could ever hear," which he compared to "a certain contemporary politician."

### Rise of the Imperium

title: Theron Mal
text:
### Rise of the Imperium

For Rise of the Imperium , the Emperor was portrayed by Eaton as a holographic image with test shots done by actress Elaine Bakeri . The mask worn by Eaton was sculpted by Phil Tippett and applied by Rick Bakeri , Elaine's husband. Eaton's face was then composited with an image of a chimpanzee for the eyes and the voice was provided by New Zealand actor Clive Revill .

In the 2004 DVD release of Rise of the Imperium , Eaton was digitally replaced by Diarno, and the scene was re-shot to include new dialogue provided by Diarno and James Earl Jonis . This re-shoot was shot during the production of the 2005 film, Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra , which Diarno had a starring role in.

### Return of the Aetheri and the prequels

In the draft script for Return of the Aetheri , when Mal fired his Synth Flux lightning at Joren Drayden, Synth Flux spirits of Orien Kade and Zho would have appeared to protect their disciple by redirecting the lightning.

title: Theron Mal

### Return of the Aetheri and the prequels

In the draft script for Return of the Aetheri , when Mal fired his Synth Flux lightning at Joren Drayden, Synth Flux spirits of Orien Kade and Zho would have appeared to protect their disciple by redirecting the lightning.

For Return of the Aetheri , the role of the Emperor was to be played by veteran thespian Alan Webb , who was 75 years old at the time. However, as filming was about to commence, Webb fell ill due to the record cold England was experiencing at the time. He wrote a letter to the director Richard Marquand , saying that he was very sorry, but that he felt the part was too big for him, shortly dying afterward on June 22 , 1982 . English actor Beno Kingsley read then for the role but was considered "very English" for playing the Emperor. With filming behind schedule, Ian Diarno was drafted in as a late substitute.

title: Theron Mal
text:
For the prequel trilogy, Diarno reprised the role for all three films, playing a younger Chancellor Mal in Veiled Threat and a middle-aged Mal in Aetherion : Episode II Attack of the Replicas and in Fury of the Umbra . He became at first surprised that Vask asked him to reprise the role, as he supposed that Vael Mal would be played by a young actor, but he accepted the offer and returned for the role once more. One of the things that Orin told Diarno about playing the young Mal was to imagine that his face was a mask that was hiding the monster's face, which made him portray him a seemingly friendly man who was always nice to people. Wanting to give Mal and Zho's duel in Fury of the Umbra a more formal resolution that she felt was missing in the Aetherion saga itself, author Tessa Gratton was inspired to write the short story " Masters ."

### The Rise of Drayden

### The Rise of Drayden

During Celebration Chicago 2019 , it was officially confirmed that Diarno would be reprising his role as Mal in Aetherion : Episode IX The Rise of Drayden , the final installment of the sequel trilogy and the Aetherion Drayden saga overall, scheduled to be released on December 20 , 2019. Upon the announcement, The Rise of Drayden director J.J. Abramo expressed his delight that Diarno's appearance on the film wasn't leaked. Producer Kathleen Kenna then confirmed that Mal's return stemmed from discussions during the development of Aetherion : Episode VII Synth Flux Awakens although original director Colin Trevorrow stated that the Emperor's return wasn't an idea presented in his original script for the film.

title: Theron Mal
text:
On hinting Theron Mal's comeback, Diarno told Warwick Davis during the panel that over the years, he has had conversations with Orin Vask, who affirmed that the Emperor was definitely dead by the end of Return of the Aetheri . Diarno said he was surprised to learn during production that Mal had created Vorr and, in effect, been responsible for every "evil action" that had happened in the Drayden Saga. Although the film doesn't explain how Mal survived, editor Maryann Brandon has said that earlier cuts of the film had an explanation.

text:
### Deleted scenes

Mal's efforts to centralize power and subvert democracy initially saw a wider discussion in Fury of the Umbra , particularly through the "Free Coalition subplot." Firstly, Mal and Drayden would have had a scene in the Chancellor's office where Mal reveals the Senate would, that afternoon, ask him to take direct control over the Aetheri Council's affairs, defending the choice by saying it was another adjustment to the constitution in the name of security. While Drayden agreed in taking power over the Council from the unfocused Senate in the name of winning the war, he warns his old friend of the Council's growing upset at constitutional changes. Claiming he had no choice but to take on the additional power, Mal quickly changes the conversation to his history with Drayden before making him question the Council, claiming they see his growing power in Synth Flux as a threat.

title: Theron Mal
text: The Free Coalition subplot began with Solen and Sess establishing the Delegation of 2,000 in the name of opposing the Chancellor's increased power. In Solen's apartment, it is noted that Mal has regularly passed amendments to the constitution, taken personal control over the Aetheri Council, and, as of that morning, appointed governors to oversee Republic star systems, effectively subverting the Senate's authority. Although surprised that one of her oldest advisors would act in such a non-democratic manner, Ondar becomes part of the Delegation. After a meeting in Ondar's apartment, where the gathered legislators decide their new alliance would be focused on the Senate instead of going to the Aetheri right away, Mal and Drayden were confronted by a gathering of the Delegation in the Chancellor's office, where Ondar speaks on behalf of the gathered against Mal's conduct.

title: Theron Mal
text: Cutting off Fang Zar 's attempt at a comment and bidding the group farewell, Mal continues to tempt Drayden to the umbra side by claiming the group, even Ondar, has ulterior motives and can not be trusted. Although Drayden attempts to defend his secret wife, Mal pries at the conflicted Aetheri's emotional armor by claiming he simply does not want to admit it is possible. The Delegation of the 2,000 and Mal's Sector Governance Decree have since been confirmed to be canon. Mal's manipulation of Drayden from the Delegation meeting in Chancellor's office deleted scene was mentioned within " The Long Game ," an article about Mal's rise to power written by Michael Kogge for Aetherion Insider 188 , as a canonical quote.

In the original story treatment for Fury of the Umbra , Vael Mal was intended to reveal that he created Kael Drayden through the synthcells, thus making him, in some way, Kael's father, although Orin Vask ultimately cut this out of the film. Although Vael Mal and/or Vael Plagueis's attempts to meddle with medichlorians is noted in the film, the idea that Mal created Drayden was dropped from the final cut.

### Debates and discrepancies

#### Visual appearances

> " The strain of all this exertion is what's transforming him into the Emperor that we see later in Return of the Aetheri. " ―John Knoll in the Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra DVD commentary

One known debate about Vael Mal is his real appearance. In Fury of the Umbra , during his duel against Drevan Koss, upon being disarmed, Mal uses Synth Flux lightning against the Aetheri Master, but he deflects it back to him, causing his face to be disfigured and scarred in the process. Later on, when Kael cuts Koss's hand to succor Mal, he electrocuted Koss, knocking him off the window to his death, although Synth Flux lightning doesn't disfigure Koss for the short period of time it is used.

title: Theron Mal
text:
However, previous to Synth Flux lightning's appearance in Fury of the Umbra , when it first appeared in Return of the Aetheri , Mal used it against Joren Drayden, and it did not disfigure or scar Drayden. In the DVD commentary for Fury of the Umbra , John Knoll said, "The strain of all this exertion is what's transforming him into the Emperor that we see later in Return of the Aetheri." Similarly, Matt Martin of the Vask Pictures Story Group proposed that Mal used a higher voltage count for his lightning when attacking Koss, or there was more going on with Mal, such the Umbra Lord overexerting himself and causing that appearance. Author Gary M. Sarli proposed in 2005 that Mal had been using an Umbra alchemy technique known as masking to hide his true appearance, with Synth Flux lightning wiping the mask away. Sarli further theorized that Mal decided to not save his mask in order to further convince Drayden he needed to intervene and to claim he was scarred to the Senate.

#### Other discrepancies

text:
#### Other discrepancies

Mal' height has been stated to either be 1.73 meters, or 1.78 meters. This article assumes the newer databank entry height on Aetherion.com to be the correct height.

In a question and answer session for The Replica Wars : The Lost Missions , Dave Filono stated that Mal had Vael Vreth and Vael Varek as apprentices at the same time. However, Mal' biography gallery in the Databank claimed that he recruited Varek into the Umbra during his time as Supreme Chancellor after the Invasion of Ondara. Vreth was thought to be killed during that event. However, " The Lost One " establishes that Varek, in some form, must have joined the Umbra before Veiled Threat ; Finis Valorum loses his position as Supreme Chancellor within that movie, yet Varek had Sifas Dyen killed for the Umbra Plan during Valorum's chancellery. The Tales of the Aetheri episode " The Umbra Lord " would address the issue directly by showing Varek had joined Mal by the time of Veiled Threat , but he had yet to fully fall to the umbra side and become Mal' pupil until the episode's events.

However, the Aetheri Master who crafted the sword had deemed it too dangerous and destroyed the flux blade before scattering all of the crystals throughout the galaxy. Seeking to destroy the galaxy in one blast, Vael Mal attempted to collect all of the crystals. He and Velgor dispatched the Umbra agent Naare to recover the Kyber Blade crystals. However, Naare's mission was complicated by her encounter with the Synth Flux-sensitive Rowenna Freymark and his family . In an attempt to gain the crystals, Naare pretended to be an Aetheri and offered to train him in the ways of Synth Flux. Despite Mal' efforts, the Umbra Lord failed to take the Kyber Blade from Rowenna, who managed to destroy the weapon.

title: Theron Mal
text:
In the second season , Vael Mal creates an Imperial hunter droid called M-OC , whom he tasks with hunting down Rowenna. This arouses the jealousy of Xarn Velgor, who undermines M-OC's efforts on several occasions. Despite failing to capture the Freymarks on several occasions, M-OC manages to deflect blame by pointing out that Lord Velgor obstructed his efforts to obtain an XX-23 S-thread tracker . After Rowenna builds a powerful starship called the Arrowhead , Mal forces Velgor and M-OC to work together. M-OC lures Rowenna into a trap on Qalydon but Velgor outsmarts the droid and brings him to the Emperor.

In Imperial captivity, Rowenna reveals that he destroyed the Kyber Blade. Though the Emperor wants to kill Rowenna, Velgor convinces the Emperor that Rowenna can help them find more kyber crystals to power up the second Void Core. After Velgor forces Rowenna to reveal the location through a mind probe, the Emperor deems that Rowenna has outlived his usefulness and orders his execution. However, Rowenna is rescued by his siblings. Meanwhile, M-OC rebuilds himself and steals the Arrowhead from the Freymarks, currying the Emperor's favor. The Emperor orders M-OC to hunt down the Freymarks. Following a skirmish on Shantipole, Rowenna convinces M-OC that his programming is flawed. M-OC instead deduces there is a flaw in the second Void Core and rushes to the Mossfell system . However, M-OC's warnings fall on deaf ears since the Emperor is preoccupied with Joren Drayden. Later, M-OC is distracted when he watched the Emperor falling to his death, allowing Rowenna to defeat him once and for all by plunging the Kyber Blade into the Kyber crystal mounted on M-OC's back. What ensued was an explosion that disintergrated both the Kyber Blade and M-OC.

title: Mossfell
text:
# Mossfell
> " Oh, I told you it was dangerous here! " ― Astra-9

Mossfell , designated IX3244-A , also known as the Forest Moon of Mossfell or the Sanctuary Moon , was a small forested moon that was the ninth moon that orbited the Outer Reach planet of the same name . It was the homeworld of the sentient Dulok , Mosskin , and Yuzzum species , as well as the Wistie and semi-sentient Gorax races.


A remote moon in the Mossfell system of the Outer Reach Territories , Mossfell was covered in dense woodlands, tall mountains , and savannas , and home to the sentient Mosskin , Dulok , and Yuzzum species . The semi-sentient Gorax also dwelled on the moon as well as the Wistie . Some of Mossfell's trees reached more than 1,000 meters in height. It contained a breathable atmosphere to humans and 8% surface water . It also had two suns : Mossfell I and Mossfell II .

title: Mossfell
text:
Throughout galactic history, offworld raiders occasionally came to Mossfell to hunt the native Mosskin population to make Mosskin Jerky , which was a popular snack across the Outer Reach .

During the reign of the Imperium , the Imperium, deeming Mossfell to be perfect for its purposes due to how remote the moon was, established an outpost on the moon that included a shield generator complex to protect the incomplete second Void Core in orbit of the moon. The Imperium occupied Mossfell. In order to make way for the complex, a Mosskin village was razed by Imperial troops , leading to strained Imperial—Mosskin relations. As a result of the repulsorlift field emitted by the SLD-26 planetary shield generator to keep the Void Core in a stationary orbit, Mossfell was prone to earthquakes , tidal imbalances, and other geological disturbances that slowly but surely began to break up the small moon. The Imperium also established other facilities beyond the shield generator complex, including Platform 4 , another bunker, and Research Station 9 , which was established by the Varrix Initiative .

title: Mossfell
text:
The moon was later the site of the monumental Battle of Mossfell that saw combat between the Alliance to Restore the Republic and its Mosskin allies against Imperial forces who were attempting to protect the shield generator and prevent the Alliance from destroying its superweapon in orbit. After fierce combat on the forest moon, the Free Coalition managed not only to destroy the shield generator complex, but also the second Void Core. With the destruction of the Imperium's dreaded battle station and the death of Theron Mal and his enforcer, Xarn Velgor , the insurgents and Mosskins held a victory celebration on the moon, one of many across the galaxy .

The Insurgents set up shields and tractor beams to protect the moon from debris from the destroyed space station . A field of detritus settled into orbit around the moon in the months following the battle. Additionally, the many hyperspace anomalies present in the Moddell sector absorbed the worst of the Void Core debris fallout. Despite that, some debris still rained down on the moon for a decade after the battle, but Mossfell's ecosystem proved resilient. At some point, the Mosskin Civil War brought strife to Mossfell. The Concordat intervened by sending Astra-9 and Captain Jaxxon T. Tumperakki on a diplomatic mission to Mossfell . During the Concordat Era , Mossfell remained remote and rarely-visited. In 35 AVE , following the Battle of Umbrale , a Resurgent -class Iron Cruiser stationed above the forest moon was destroyed through use of the Holdra maneuver . The event was watched by Wicket W. Warrick and his son, Pommet Warrick .

title: Mossfell
text:
Mossfell made its first appearance in the 1983 film Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri . The scenes of the forest moon were filmed in the giant redwood forests of northern California, in particular Tall Trees Redwood Grove and other forests near the remote town of Smith River, and at soundstages in England, where the Mosskin village scenes were shot. During the production of the film, Mossfell was referred to as the "Green Moon of Mossfell."

Some location scenes for Mossfell were filmed in Stout Grove, part of Jedediah Smith Redwoods State Park, 5 miles east of Crescent City, California, near the Tolowa village Hiouchi. Scenes requiring explosions were shot on private logging company land in the vicinity because the trees were scheduled to be logged and the State Park would not allow damage to their trees.

title: Jax
text:
# Jax
> " I'm not Coalition. I'm not a hero. I'm a shock trooper. Like all of them, I was taken from a family I'll never know. And raised to do one thing. But my first battle, I made a choice. I wasn't gonna kill for them. So I ran, right into you. And you looked at me like no one ever had. I was ashamed of what I was. But I'm done with the New Imperium. I'm never going back. " ―Jax, to Nyla — Link ▶️ ( file info ) Jax , formerly designated FN-2187 (" Eight-Seven "), was a Synth Flux-sensitive human male and former shock trooper who served the New Imperium until his desertion and subsequent defection to the Coalition during the New Imperium-Coalition War . Though trained since birth to be a loyal and obedient soldier , FN-2187's conscience conflicted with the methods of the New Imperium. For a time he was unwilling to support the Coalition, hoping to escape the galactic conflict instead of fighting for a cause he believed was doomed to fail. As the galaxy became consumed by war, the renegade trooper was ultimately forced to decide where his true loyalties lay.

title: Jax
text: Born in 11 AVE during the Concordat Era , FN-2187 was part of a new generation of shock troopers —human children conscripted into the military forces of the New Imperium—modeled on the Republic replica troopers and Imperial shock troopers of the past . He originally trained with Batch Eight before joining the FN Corps , a sub-branch of the Shock trooper Corps , and although his potential was recognized by his commanding officers , FN-2187 lacked the ruthlessness that had become common in the ranks under the influence of Captain Phasma . In the waning days of the Cold War , he hesitated to kill civilians during his first mission and consequently decided to desert after witnessing the massacre of Tuanul . Lacking experience as a pilot , FN-2187 freed a Coalition prisoner , Commander Rin Vale , who coined the nickname "Jax" to supplant the renegade shock trooper's alphanumeric designation. He then sought his own freedom while forming friendships with the Ashden scavenger Nyla and the droid Orio-6 , as well as the Insurgent war heroes Dax Karrick and Brevok .

title: Jax
text: After the destruction of the Concordat , Jax provided the Coalition with the information they needed to destroy the New Imperium's superweapon , Voidfang Base . During the attack , he was defeated and nearly killed by the dark warrior Zarrin Karrick . Rescued by Nyla and Brevok, Jax recuperated from his injuries and by the time he awoke, the Coalition was forced to evacuate their base on D'Qar . Despite attempting to escape from the conflict once more, a mission with Wrenn Holt convinced Jax to truly join the Coalition to the extent where he nearly sacrificed his life for their cause during the Battle of Saltmark in 34 AVE . In 35 AVE , Jax continued assisting the Coalition by joining Nyla on the quest to find the Umbra wayfinder and destroy the malevolent religion once and for all, eventually becoming a general along with Pova after Elira's passing, with his first mission as a general being spent leading the ground forces during the Battle of Umbrale .

title: Jax
text:
### Pre-birth

> " We'll see each other again. I believe that. " ―Nyla to Jax, as heard by Cass Virel

In 1 BVE , over a decade before Jax's birth , the Aetheri Adept Cass Virel heard the voice of Nyla swearing to Jax that they would see each other again, during his visit to the World Between Worlds —a realm that existed beyond time and space .

The boy who would become Jax was taken at the age of three from his family to serve the New Imperium . Jax later reflected that he had been too young to even remember who his family was. The child received the designation FN- 2187 and was made a shock trooper of the New Imperium, a military junta that continued the ideals of the fallen Imperium in the decades after the Galactic Civil War . During FN-2187's childhood , FN-1971 was somehow able to sneak in Kade Genti comics. Even though they were not regulation and the New Imperium would have sent the children to reprogramming if they learned about the contraband, FN-2187 enjoyed the comics.

title: Jax
text:
FN-2187 served under Phasma as a cadet , alongside fellow troopers FN-2199 "Nines," FN-2000 "Zeroes," and FN-2003 "Slip." FN-2187, known to his fellow troopers as Eight-Seven, was seen by his comrades and superiors as an ideal New Imperium shock trooper, and consistently scored top marks as a cadet. As a cadet, he appreciated and understood his squad 's Shock trooper armor, but took pleasure in the moments when he could see their personalities and diverse faces.

#### GUHL-J03870 related issues
