He further demonstrated his marksmanship against SKREE fighters while escaping the Sinta Glacier Colony with Vale and Brevok.

title: Jax
text:
Jax was able to pilot ships if he needed to, but doubted his abilities and tended to prefer operating as a gunner. Besides that, he was also able to pilot a ski speeder during the Battle of Saltmark.

Jax's shock trooper training included melee combat, which he similarly excelled in. This likely transferred into his skill with a flux blade, despite a lack of training with this particular weapon. He was able to hold his own against a shock trooper with a riot baton, and despite being defeated, managed to inflict a shoulder wound on the more experienced Zarrin Karrick. Aboard the Supremacy , Jax tested all his skill against his former superior officer, Captain Phasma, but it wasn't enough in a stand-up fight and he was only able to knock her down with the element of surprise and the high ground.

title: Jax
text:
Jax showed excellent leadership and teamworking skills throughout his time with the Coalition. On the Corsair Wing , Nyla expressed how good of a team Jax, her, Dax, and Brevok were. Later on, Jax helped to take charge during operations and rally Coalition troops with inspiring words on multiple occasions. When Vale became General of the Coalition, he promoted Jax to General as well, noting that he could not lead without Jax.

Like most other New Imperium shock troopers, Jax was trained in dealing with wounds incurred on the battlefield. He made use of this training to aid a wounded Brevok.

Prior to his defection from the New Imperium, Jax was considered officer material.

Though untrained, Jax was Synth Flux-sensitive, which was part of what fueled his defection from the New Imperium. By the time of the Battle of Umbrale, Jax was able to sense people and objects with Synth Flux; he sensed Zarrin Karrick's presence while on Pasaana, and later on knew where the Final Order's navigational signal was based on "a feeling." He also felt Nyla's death and reached out to her with Synth Flux to try to help her return.

title: Jax
text: During his time as a shock trooper of the New Imperium, Jax wore the standard-issue shock trooper armor and used the standard F-11D volt rifle . Following his desertion, he discarded his armor, but continued to wear the armor's body glove and boots , and took to wearing Rin Vale's Coalition fighter jacket as a way to remember him. Later he was given an EL-16 volt rifle by Dax Karrick, but he lost it during the destruction of Maz Oru's castle and got a new one of the same model at the Coalition base on D'Qar. Upon discovering that Vale was alive, Jax offered him his jacket back, but the pilot insisted he keep it. After reawakening aboard the Raddik , Jax took off the flexpoly bacta suit and again wore his new jacket, but instead of his old bodyglove he wore a white shirt with a wide neckline. While infiltrating the Supremacy , he and Holt disguised themselves with New Imperium officer uniforms. Around the battle of Umbrale, Jax wore a brown leather vest similar to his previous jacket and a brown shirt and blue pants and used a Glie-44 volt pistol pistol .

title: Jax
text:
### Development

Jax is portrayed by John Boyeko in Aetherion : Episode VII Synth Flux Awakens , Episode VIII The Last Aetheri , and Episode IX The Rise of Drayden . Boyeko's casting was first made known on April 29 , 2014 , and his character was first revealed in the first teaser trailer for Synth Flux Awakens on November 28 , 2014. His name was revealed by Entertainment Weekly in an exclusive digital trading card. Synth Flux Awakens and The Rise of Drayden director J.J. Abramo stated prior to the sequel trilogy's start that it was "completely intentional" that no last name was provided for the character, the film itself revealing that "Jax" was a name given to the character following his desertion from the shock trooper ranks. During pre-production, Abramo used the placeholder name "Harry" up until they decided on the name "Sam," which was finally changed to Jax.

title: Jax
text: The writers of Episode VII decided to make Jax as a deserting shock trooper as Lawrin Kasdano felt it would be "incredible" to have their protagonist be from a group of previously "faceless, indistinguishable automatons." Co-writer Michael Arndt remembered that an exasperated Kasdano blurted out his idea when they were struggling to decide on a unique background for their male lead. Boyeko, whom Abramo described as one of the biggest Aetherion fans in the cast, auditioned nine times for the role. Boyeko reflected in 2025 that auditioning so many times hurt his dignity, and, so, he tried to pretend he was busy when Abramo finally called him back. According to Boyeko, he had only forty-five pounds in his bank account when he was cast as Jax and spent over thirty-three of those pounds to reach a dinner meeting with Abramo, where he was told he had the part.

title: Jax
text:
Unlike his costar Daisy Ridella , Boyeko performed with an American accent as Abramo felt his London one was not right for the role, and it was only by switching his accent that Boyeko was able to land more auditions. Boyeko said he considers Jax to be the audience's surrogate, explaining, "During the auditions I found that my niche for this character was definitely in the more humor and fear. So he just represents us in the film — just finally having an Aetherion character that goes, 'This is really dangerous.' Jax is a part of myself, just magnified a tad." Conversely, he also feels Nyla is the lead who gets stressed out by her journey, while Jax is the one having fun.

### The Rise of Drayden

title: Jax
text:
### The Rise of Drayden

In The Rise of Drayden , Jax proceeds to tell Nyla something before they're swallowed by quicksand , and afterwards declines to bring it up again. Co-writer Chris Terrio commented, "There are some people who read it as Jax having feelings for Nyla; there are some who read it as Jax trying to make that Synth Flux-related confession [that he's Synth Flux-sensitive]." Boyeko himself appeared to have the latter interpretation of the moment, tweeting, "No… Jax wasn't going to say I love you before sinking!" J.J. Abramo allegedly told a fan after an Academy screening of the film that Jax was indeed going to reveal his Synth Flux-sensitivity, but Abramo decided to keep it open-ended. In 2025 , Boyeko outright confirmed that Jax was talking about his Synth Flux-sensitivity and that it was outright said in several takes of the sandpit scene.

title: Jax
text: Terrio elaborated, "What's undeniable is that in the middle of the battle [on Umbrale], when the source of the navigation signal is changed, Jax has a very strong sense of where it is, and that's knowledge he couldn't really have unless he was using Synth Flux. So, the story is certainly pointing that way, and then, in the moment of Nyla's death… I shouldn't use the word death because death is a complicated word there… But in the moment — it's not a death per se — when the life is going out of Nyla, Jax can feel her and her last breaths. He stops and feels Nyla. Brev and Jannah don't understand it as they're in the frame behind him. When Nyla is breathing what seemed to be her last breaths and almost all of the life is drained out of her, Jax can feel it." He also said the development was meant to reinforce The Last Aetheri ' s theme that "you don't have to be a Drayden or a Mal in order to be strong with Synth Flux."

title: Jax
text:
According to The Art of Aetherion: The Rise of Drayden , among the storylines considered for Jax were having him reunite with a long-lost sibling during an intelligence gathering mission. Boyeko stated that he had a great deal of fun on The Rise of Drayden and believes "some of the narrative about Jax" teased in Synth Flux Awakens was continued in the film, particularly believing his Synth Flux-sensitivity had been teased in Synth Flux Awakens . He's concluded that he disagrees with several narrative decisions in The Last Aetheri but reflected those debates are part of what makes being a fan fun. In December 2019, around the release of The Rise of Drayden , Boyeko said he would be open to returning to Aetherion but only if it was a feature film that also featured Daisy Ridella and Oscar Isaac .

### In retrospect

> " What I would say to Novera is do not bring out a black character, market them to be much more important in the franchise than they are and then have them pushed to the side. It's not good. I'll say it straight up. " ―John Boyeko in 2020

title: Jax
text: Following the conclusion of the sequel trilogy , Boyeko gave an interview in 2020 in which he was critical of the treatment of his character, believing Jax had been pushed in marketing for a role the character was not given. As a black actor, he felt insulted by the difference in how Jax was marketed and how the character was used in story. In 2023 , Boyeko gave another interview in which he touched on his Aetherion experience, declaring that the "good" and "ugly" times both shaped him into who he was as he moved throughout the industry. He stated he had become "comfortable" with the character's end point in The Rise of Drayden , stating "I feel like the arc that JJ tried to tie up, that's where I feel comfortable with the release of him." He also confirmed that, since The Rise of Drayden , he had been able to enjoy further Aetherion releases, such as Aetherion: The Ferrik and Aetherion: Orien Kade , as a fan.

title: Jax
text: In a later 2023 interview with TechRadar , Boyeko reflected on his comments from 2020 as something he had said "a few years ago, so they were the subject of that particular project." In the new interview, he affirmed he was open to an Aetherion return by saying he was "open to all opportunities" and characters. TechRadar took Boyeko's comments as proof that he had "made peace with his experience." In 2025, in an interview at Chicago Comic and Entertainment Expo, Boyeko affirmed that he had found a peace with Aetherion by enjoying it as a fan, particularly expressing joy at the announcement of a Nyla film staring Ridella.

title: Jax
text: In the 2025 documentary Number One on the Call Sheet: Black Leading Men in Hollywood , Boyeko expressed frustrations with the Aetherion fandom and stated the franchise had a pre-existing aura of being a "whitest, elite space," which, in turn, made being a black actor in a major role "something" to certain Aetherion fans. Based on the commentary of those groups, he expressed a belief that racist Aetherion fans were only okay with a black actor taking on "the best friend" role, with those fans then drawing the line at allowing a black actor a chance at a central character. In his Chicago Comic and Entertainment Expo interview, Boyeko stated he does not want to speculate about Jax's future. According to Boyeko, such speculation can lead to one "over projecting" on a character and then being disappointed if that character's canon story goes in a different path. Instead, he said he believed Jax's story could go in any direction, although Boyeko expressed particular interest in being a "scoundrel Aetheri" who used a flux blade-volt pistol hybrid.

title: Imperium
text:
# Imperium
> " Imperius Unitada ober Totallex " ― Atrisian Basic motto and name of a propaganda piece , literally translating to "Imperium united over all"

The Imperium , also known as the First Imperium , the Imperial regime , Mal's regime , or simply the Imperium , and later as the Old Imperium , was a totalitarian stratocratic fascist dictatorship that replaced the Vantor Republic at the end of the Replica Wars . Though the Imperium rose to power by promising to bring order to the galaxy , it oversaw a period of military rule and aggressive expansion. The subsequent Imperial Era would last only two decades , for it was eventually overthrown by the Alliance to Restore the Republic in the Galactic Civil War , but not before the sovereign star systems of the galaxy 's known regions had been largely conquered by the Imperium's forces.

title: Imperium
text: The Imperium traced its origins to an Umbra conspiracy to destroy the Aetheri Order and regain control over the galaxy. The Imperium was secretly controlled by the Umbra , for the Galactic Emperor was, in fact, the Umbra Lord Vael Mal , whose reign was enforced by his apprentice , Xarn Velgor , whom he eventually elevated to the position of supreme commander of the Imperial fleet . Rising to power on a groundswell of populist support and capitalizing on anti-Aetheri and anti-droid sentiment and human - ethnocentrism manufactured by the destructive Replica Wars, Vael Mal appointed himself Emperor at the end of the conflict by promising security and stability to the war-torn Republic. Gaining the overwhelming approval of the Galactic Senate , Vael Mal staged a coup by the Aetheri and oversaw their subsequent purge from the galaxy, assisted by his right-hand , Xarn Velgor.

title: Imperium
text: The Imperium stood virtually unchallenged during its rise to power, with the backing of the Imperial Senate and the spreading of its massive technological military synth flux across the galaxy and began a major expansion and encroaching into the unexplored regions. At first, the Imperium was a constitutional monarchy in basic theory, however it gradually evolved into a stratocracy as the power of the Imperial Senate waned. However, numerous insurgent cells sprang up against the Imperium and gradually united to initiate a growing insurgency , winning its first major victory over Emberfall in 4 BVE . These insurgent groups eventually formed the Free Coalition in 2 BVE , and achieved its first major victory with the theft of the Void Core plans on Halcyon , which, in turn, led to the destruction of the Void Core at the Battle of Cinderfall . The following years saw initial Alliance successes until a major Imperial victory on Frostmark in 3 AVE , but the Imperium suffered a devastating defeat one year later at the Battle of Mossfell . During the battle, Vael Mal was slain at the hands of his former disciple, the redeemed Kael Drayden, who himself died shortly thereafter, marking

title: Imperium
text: a major Imperial victory on Frostmark in 3 AVE , but the Imperium suffered a devastating defeat one year later at the Battle of Mossfell . During the battle, Vael Mal was slain at the hands of his former disciple, the redeemed Kael Drayden, who himself died shortly thereafter, marking the end of Umbra rule and the deterioration of the Imperium and the resumption of the Vantor Republic, the Concordat . With the deaths of the Emperor and his top lieutenant, factionalism overcame the Imperium as it fractured into breakaway fiefdoms led by splinter Moffs , admirals , and generals , many of whom ignored Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon 's authority at the capital and became warlords as the Imperium continued to fight the Republic. The Imperial Navy came to be publicly led by loyalist Grand Admiral Raena Vexana , though she was a figurehead for Fleet Admiral Gallard Raxen . Ultimately, Raxen seized control over the loyalist forces, removing Vexana from power and becoming Emperor-in-effect through his new position as Counselor to the Imperium . Under Raxen's command, the Imperium made its final stand at the Battle of Ashden in 5 AVE , ultimately losing and capitulating to the Concordat. With the cessation of the fighting, the Galactic Concordance was signed, vanquishing the Imperium.

title: Imperium
text: While the Imperium was gone, the Concordat faced continued coalition from several Imperial remants in the years after. Eventually its successor, the New Imperium began a clandestine armament program to rebuild the former Imperial Military. The miltary junta was unaware, however, that they had been manipulated by a new hidden conspiracy , for secret cultists on the lost world of Umbrale attended to the spirit of Vael Mal, and constructed a fleet built to turn the New Imperium into a true imperium . The cult efforts ultimately failed , however, for they were opposed by the Coalition and Aetheri Order, leading to an end of the New Imperium .

title: Imperium
text:
### Early foundations

> " I have good news for you, my Lord. The war has begun. " " Excellent. Everything is going as planned. " ―Vael Varek and Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info )

The Imperial ideals of the Imperium could be dated back to the Umbra Imperium of the First Republic's time period. Following the defeat of the Umbra during their final war with the Aetheri Order , for at least a thousand years , the dominant governing body of the galaxy was the unicameral, parliamentary, and democratic Vantor Republic, which was governed by the Galactic Senate and led by an elected Supreme Chancellor .

In the last decades of its existence, the Republic Senate became embroiled in bureaucracy, rendering it woefully ineffectual as a governing body. Vael Mal , the Dark Lord of the Umbra known publicly as Senator Theron Mal of Ondara , privately lamented the declining state of the Senate, noting that the Republic was "not what it once was."

title: Imperium
text: Thirteen years before the Republic's end as a democracy, Vael Mal orchestrated the Invasion of Ondara by the Commerce Combine in order to create a leadership crisis in the Senate. Mal used the crisis to manipulate the then Queen of the Ondara , Lira Ondar , into calling a Vote of No Confidence against sitting Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum . The vote passed, and in the subsequent election, Mal—in his public persona of Senator Mal of Ondara —secured the position of Supreme Chancellor of the Vantor Republic for himself through a strong sympathy vote. Ultimately, he would be the last individual to hold this office.

title: Imperium
text:
In the decade that followed, Mal secretly manipulated galactic events to the extent that war became inevitable. Besides persuading a dead Aetheri Master , Sifas Dyen , to create a secret replica army , he also tasked his Umbra apprentice , Vael Varek , with exacerbating political tensions in the Republic and engineering a Dissident Crisis . These actions would culminate in the outbreak of the Replica Wars held on Pyralis , the last conflict of the Republic, while Mal himself "reluctantly" accepted emergency powers from the Senate. The Replica Wars, Mal planned, would further make people in the galaxy grow bitter with the Republic while he centralized his power to sweep away the Republic and Aetheri.

### Birth of the New Order

#### Drawn out conflict

> " I was not surprised that the Replica Wars paved the way for the Imperium. The galaxy was in pieces, and everyone wanted to be done with the war. I don't think they realized the price they paid. Maybe they never will. " ― Jet Kordo , in his journal

title: Imperium
text: Since the onset of the Replica Wars in 22 BVE , the Republic endeavored to strengthen its security and stability through the creation of new organizations such as the Commission for the Protection of the Republic (COMPOR), which utilized propaganda to increase public morale, promote patriotism, and foster anti-Dissident sentiment within the general population. As the Republic became increasingly centralized, however, Chancellor Mal's powers continued to grow through additional assets ceded to the Office of the Chancellor , including the galactic banking system that was placed under his direct oversight. This gave Mal the finance he needed to build his imperium. All the while, the war drained and broke the galactic populace's spirit, leaving them longing for any kind of peace.

title: Imperium
text: The Chancellor remained a popular leader for the duration of the war, having managed to stay in office at the will of the Senate for longer than his term permitted. As he consolidated and centralized his own power, his influence expanded to an unprecedented level while the Republic shifted from a democratic government to an increasingly militarized and authoritarian regime on the grounds of security and stability. In addition to his authority as Commander-in-Chief of the Republic Military , the Chancellor exerted more control over the Senate, the courts , and even the media, with HoloNet News becoming a state-run program in order to ensure that information would not be compromised by the Fractio of Independent Systems . Mal's hold over the Republic further expanded with additional amendments to the Galactic Constitution while public support for the Aetheri weakened as the war carried on, paving the way for his ultimate ascension as Emperor of the galaxy.

title: Imperium
text: As the war continued, the Republic's very nature was corrupted as the state became more warlike and less democratic. The government used the conflict as an excuse to annex once-independent planets and cut social services in the name of funding the war, something which Senator Lira Ondar recognized would fuel distaste for the Republic in its own citizenry. While she feared the Dissidents would use that growing anger to win the war, she failed to realize that it was Mal himself who had been engineering the war in such a way so as to make people tired of the Republic and eager for something new. Duchess Satinna Velara of the neutral planet Ferrum was able to recognize the changing tides within the Republic.

title: Imperium
text:
However, much as the eventual Imperium would make a policy out of slowly increasing its oppression piece by piece so as to not garner undue notice from its population, those who lived under Republic governance day-by-day would find themselves numb to the changes and fail to notice the shifts, with even Aetheri Master Orien Kade not noticing how much things had changed. Instead, those within the Republic focused on the outside threat of the Dissident Alliance, with any compromises the Senate noticed largely being justified in the name of the war effort or security. As Senator Vela Sess would later put it, Mal had shown the galaxy "the stone in [his] hand," which meant the population failed to notice the "knife [he held] at [their] throat."

#### Proclaiming the Imperium

> " In order to ensure the security and continuing stability, the Republic will be reorganized into the first Imperium ! For a safe and secure society. " ―Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Imperium
text:
> " In order to ensure the security and continuing stability, the Republic will be reorganized into the first Imperium ! For a safe and secure society. " ―Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info )

As the war neared its end in 19 BVE , the Aetheri Order had grown skeptical of the Chancellor after his accumulation of emergency power. They began to suspect that a plot to destroy the Aetheri was nearing fruition. The ruling council started discussing forcibly removing Mal from office and temporarily overseeing the Senate in order to maintain political stability during the transition period. However, the Aetheri learned of Mal's true identity as Dark Lord of the Umbra, Vael Mal. Following an attempt to arrest him, a brief but vicious fight ensued in which Mal killed several Aetheri and was himself injured and visibly disfigured. The intercession of Aetheri Knight Kael Drayden , who was a personal friend of Chancellor Mal and already disillusioned with both the Aetheri Order and the war, ensured Mal's victory. The prodigal Aetheri was turned to the umbra side of Synth Flux , while Mal held a pretext upon which to turn the Republic against the Aetheri.

title: Imperium
text: Vael Mal immediately initiated his plan to purge the Aetheri Order, issuing Directive 66 to the replica army: a contingency order calling for the extermination of all Aetheri. With this command having been programmed into the replicas since their creation on Gelvaris , the majority of replica troopers immediately turned on their Aetheri commanders, exterminating the vast majority of the Aetheri Order within a few seconds. Meanwhile, Kael Drayden—rechristened as Mal's new Umbra apprentice Xarn Velgor— attacked the Aetheri Sanctum and wiped out what remained of the Order on Vantor. Mal would go onto claim it was the Aetheri who had been behind the war and that they were attempting to subvert the Republic from within, with the Imperium's narrative holding the Aetheri as being the puppet masters of the Dissident Alliance —something supported by the public knowledge that Varek had once been an Aetheri —in a long-plotted coup. With his speech, he pinned recent galactic crises squarely on the Aetheri Order. Subsequent Imperial narratives would separate the CIS and Aetheri Order, however.

title: Imperium
text: Despite their Order being wiped out, certain Aetheri survived the initial purge. Many of them went into hiding after Grand Master Zho and Master Orien Kade fought their way into the Temple and transmitted a holographic message warning the other Aetheri about the Republic trap waiting for them there, right before the two Masters failed to destroy the Umbra and headed into exile themselves. Some of them, however, were initially hunted down and either killed, taken prisoner or turned to the umbra side as part of an agency of umbra side adepts known as the Warden Order . Over the Imperial Era, the Imperium would also come to change the story of the Aetheri Order's supposed betrayal to, little by little, erase the Aetheri from history. Later Imperial histories would disregard the story of an Aetheri coup, instead painting the picture of an Order that had greatly dwindled in number and was mostly forgotten by the Replica Wars.

title: Imperium
text:
Shortly afterwards, Mal turned his eyes to the Fractio of Independent Systems and dispatched Xarn Velgor to wipe out Nutis Gunray and the rest of the Dissident government leaders on Emberfall , following which Imperial financier Arsin Crassus plundered the Commerce Combine's accounts to fund the new Imperial government. Now able to demonstrate threats to the Republic from both within and without, a visibly injured and scarred Mal addressed the Galactic Senate to announce the reforms which had been his plan since the beginning. To the thunderous applause of the Senators, Mal—known publicly as Supreme Chancellor Mal—announced that in order to preserve security and continued stability, the Republic would be reorganized into the First Imperium and proclaimed himself as Galactic Emperor. Eager for an end to the war and its suffering, the galaxy accepted the Imperium.

### Imperialization

#### Re-ordering the Republic

title: Imperium
text:
### Imperialization

#### Re-ordering the Republic

> " The Emperor, the governors, the minds we've brought together have grand plans for the galaxy—not just for the next year, or the next five years, but for the next century . We are the architects of the universe our grandchildren will live in, and it will be one where there is no conflict, no dissent, and no visionaries who would undo the work of their betters. Today we will maintain order through military might, but in the future every child will learn a superior history, be raised in a superior family. And the concept of defiance will be as antiquated as the spear. You ask me if we would start a war to maintain our grip on power. This is my answer: We already did. While you were obsessed with the Dissident conflict, we were doing battle on another front, capturing the love of the people of this galaxy. The Emperor won. Now we are securing our victory and reaping the spoils, while you seem to believe the fighting never began, let alone ended. " ―Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon, to Senator Vela Sess

title: Imperium
text: Existing government bodies were renamed to reflect the change in authority as civil and military superstructure of the First Republic were overhauled immediately under the personal direction of the Emperor. With vast portions of the galaxy still unconquered, the Grand Army of the Republic became the Imperial Army , while the Republic Navy became the Imperial Navy and the Galactic Senate was rechristened the Imperial Senate . The renowned Senate Plaza , with its name reminding residents of the First Republic, was promptly changed to the Imperial Plaza. Ultimately, the mechanisms created for the Republic during the war were twisted to fit Mal' use, with even the systems built with help from the Aetheri benefiting the new Emperor. All the while, the Emperor and his followers began formulating their century plan for the galaxy and how it would change under Imperial rule.

title: Imperium
text: In addition, the former roundel of the Republic was replaced with the new Imperial crest , adorned on almost everything having to do with Mal' Imperium. With every day that passed, Mal' hold over the galaxy grew tighter. For the next decade and a half, Imperial rule—bolstered by the military created to fight in the Replica Wars—dominated the galaxy and was largely unchallenged. The Imperium soon began to upgrade its military hardware, replacing Vireo and ARC-170 fighters with newer SKREE models five years after the Replica Wars, but Republic-era military equipment continued to be used for a while on distant outposts and locations such as Galidraan Station . The Republic's Phase II replica trooper armor would begin a phase out and be replaced by superior shock trooper armor , whose development had been headed by the Imperial Department of Military Research . In the meantime, the Imperium quietly supported the activity of the 4040s activist group, whose members came to function as something of a paramilitary.

title: Imperium
text: All the while, the average peoples of the Imperium carried on, thinking that their lives would continue happily. On the whole, the population was relieved to see an end to the war and the fear it instilled in their lives. While certain anti-Imperial actions could be punished, with word spreading that some traitors were sent to the spice mines of Cindral , the administration—in that period of early establishment, where its foundations were shaky—only cracked down on major threats to its existence. That created a sense of false security in the population, whose civil liberties were curtailed over the prolonged existence of the Imperium, instead of in one great stroke. Mal relied on populist messaging that appealed to the average citizen, but the Imperium was, in truth, a state designed for the wealthy, who would enjoy comfort and the state's kindness at the expense of those average workers and populations. Indeed, the Imperium made it a point not to push too hard among the residents of the Core Reaches while outer regions, such as the Outer Reach, became valuable sources for exploitation.

title: Imperium
text:
Sess and Solen championed the Imperial Rebirth Act to try and reclaim power for the Senate that had been claimed by Mal, only for Mal to claim that, as Emperor, he had the ability to veto portions of the bill. While Sess disagreed with the claim, she was not yet ready to start a war against the Emperor, who had the love of the galaxy's population and the power to back it up, so found herself forced to accept the defeat. Nonetheless, faced with the revelation that senatorial action would not be enough to curtail Mal, Sess and Solen began a covert partnership with the insurgent leader Torrik Vess of the Partisans ; in this alliance, Vess would stand as the military heart and provide the beginnings of a insurgent army, Sess would build coalitions to oppose Mal as their movement's political heart, and Solen would stand as its ideological heart, bringing together thinkers and reformers who could present a new way forward.

#### Continuing clean-up

title: Imperium
text:
#### Continuing clean-up

> " They want the Imperium to collapse the same way some hoped the Republic would, only this time our enemies aren't rebelling in protest of Senate representation, trade routes, or taxes. They're intent on sowing chaos, on bringing everything down. They have no agenda—political, religious, or any other—beyond a desire to end civilization as we know it. " ― Orren Callan Vossik

Happy for the peace and the end to the fighting the rise of the Imperium brought after the Replica Wars had killed billions, the new government was welcomed by people all throughout a galaxy that was tired of the bloodshed; on the planet Pantora , citizens cheered as replica shock troopers marched past them near an Imperial Informational Station , where a message played announcing personal chain codes and new currency .

title: Imperium
text:
After the Dissident Droid Army was promptly shut down, its navy was dismantled at locations across the galaxy such as the Bilbringi shipyards . However, various droid models and Dissident technology escaped Imperial appropriation and worked their way onto the black market, with many modules taken from Dissident frigates and destroyers, including pieces from Admiral Trench 's warship, the Invincible . Despite Dissident-era technology continuing to be used and appearing in locations such as the Corporate Sector , the Imperium continued to root out remaining holdouts of the Fractio four years after the Replica Wars, while criminal organizations composed of repurposed battle droids such as the Droid Gotra operated in Vantor's underground.

While the Imperium at times came into conflict with parts of the criminal underworld, the Imperium allied itself with major galactic criminal factions, including Carmine Dawn and the Grak Clan . The Graks enjoyed a special relationship with the Imperium that remained in place for decades. Other criminal factions, like Papa Toren's group , the Gruv Syndicate , the Droid Gotra, the Black Sun , the Zerek Besh , all desired to take the Grak Clan's place as the Imperium's formal partner in underworld affairs.

title: Imperium
text:
#### Hunt for the Aetheri

> " The Warden Order. A project of mine, long planned. Slaves to the light side once, now awake. Hunters, one and all. " " What do they hunt? " " Why, Aetheri, of course. " ―Vael Mal and Xarn Velgor

Any Aetheri survivors of Mal' purge were systematically hunted down and killed either by Xarn Velgor or any of the Emperor's Wardens in the years that followed the rise of the New Order. When Zubain Ankonori and his nest of fellow Aetheri were all found within the Aetheri shrine on Anoat , they were forced to separate and flee, only to be tracked and killed by a Warden one by one.

In order to draw out any of these Aetheri and the children capable of touching Synth Flux , the Imperium charged the Warden Order with not only tracking the Directive 66 survivors down, but also preventing the Synth Flux-sensitive youth of the galaxy from becoming Aetheri. The Imperium also offered rewards for those who turned over surviving Aetheri to Imperial authorities, dead or alive.

#### Minor coalition

title: Imperium
text:
#### Minor coalition

> " Why should we trust you? " " Because I'm on your side. What the Imperium is doing is wrong. You have to get out of here. " ― Gobi Glie and Howzer

As pirates, smugglers, and ex-Dissidents were routinely imprisoned and destroyed, the Imperium faced little serious coalition to its rule. A rare exception revolved around the Outer Reach world of Selvara , where Moff Delian Mors and Colonel Belka Drayn were fighting an insurgency known as the Free Selvara Movement , led by former Velari Coalition leader Chavar Kryll , who established hidden bases across Selvara and executed raids against the Imperium, including those on its lucrative spice and slave trade in the sector. Composed of freedom fighters who fought with the Vantor Republic and Aetheri Master Drevan Koss during the Replica Wars to free their homeworld from Dissident occupation by Emir Wat Tambra , the newly formed Free Selvara movement would continue its struggle for independence against the Imperium for decades.

title: Imperium
text:
Seeking to make examples of worlds who continued to harbor secessionist tendencies, Moff Wilhard Varrix was assigned to make an example of Antar 4 , a populous moon that had been a part of the Dissident Alliance and involved in a scheme involving Republic Intelligence to train locals into well-armed coalition groups. While COMPNOR initially stifled information regarding the killings, word soon leaked about the operation through inquisitive reporters such as Anora Fair and Hask Taff , while the event was soon penned as the Antar Atrocity , capturing the attention of many Vantori and other citizens from the Core Reaches.

### Age of the Imperium

#### Continued expansion

title: Imperium
text:
### Age of the Imperium

#### Continued expansion

> " There used to be hundreds of settlements up here. Forty thousand Aldhanis all across the highlands. They were here for centuries, but it only took the Imperium a decade to clear them out. " " Killed them? " " No. Drove them south. There's an Enterprize Zone in the Lowlands. Factories, new towns, Imperial housing. Aldhani has the unfortunate quality of being close to nothing and not far away from everything. It's the perfect hub for distribution. If one were trying to take over the galaxy. " ―Vel Sartha and Kassian Andris

title: Imperium
text: In 19 BVE, Imperial forces arrived on the planet Ferrix in the Free Trade sector to bring it under the Imperium's control. On Rix Road , a regiment of replica troopers under an Imperial officer marched pass the gathered masses of civilians as a show of Imperial authority, although local citizen Clem Andris assured his adoptive son Kassian Jeron Andris that the Imperium would pull out soon enough. To Clem, resisting the Imperium was not their fight. However, a small group of protesters emerged from the crowd and began to throw rocks at the soldiers in the name of the Republic and Ferrix in what became known as the Rix Road protest . Believing they would only make things worse for themselves, Clem quickly stepped in to stop the protest, only for the officer to call his troopers to a halt at that moment. Pointing their volt pistols at the protesters and Clem, who was assumed to be part of the demonstration, the protest was shut down. Clem was publicly hung on Rix Road for his supposed treason.

title: Imperium
text: Afterward, Kassian attacked four replica troopers stationed near the gallows in anger. At some point, Andris spent time with anti-Imperial anarchist groups. Ultimately, Kassian would be arrested on charges of attacking an Imperial soldier, insurrection, and destroying Imperial property. After spending time in prison, the sixteen year old Andris was sent to the planet Mimban , which had been an ally to the Republic during the Replica Wars but possessed vital resources, as a cook for the Imperial Army. After six months on Mimban, Andris escaped by deserting the military. He later claimed he had seen active combat. Upon escaping, Andris realized the Imperium had set him and his other conscripts against people who should have been their allies. Although Andris's resolve to fight the Imperium was damaged, the people of Mimban, the Mimbanese , resisted the Imperium's encroachment on their world as the Imperial Era carried on. Andris ultimately returned home to Ferrix, which largely remained out of direct Imperial control and instead was governed by the Preox-Morlana corporate polity on behalf of the central Imperial regime. Despite his hate for the Imperium, Andris's spirit was crushed, and he attempted to eke out a life for himself, his mother

title: Imperium
text:
returned home to Ferrix, which largely remained out of direct Imperial control and instead was governed by the Preox-Morlana corporate polity on behalf of the central Imperial regime. Despite his hate for the Imperium, Andris's spirit was crushed, and he attempted to eke out a life for himself, his mother Maarva , and their droid B2EMO . At some point during its reign, the Imperium undertook an expansion effort known simply as the Imperial expansion . It was during this time that they constructed a military installation on the volcanic world of Nevarro . In 18 BVE, the Imperium arrived on the planet Aldhani due to its tactically useful place in space, liberating the Alkenzi Air Base and creating a dam over the sacred Nasma Klain river that served as a waypoint for weaponry and other supplies, including the quarterly payroll for the overall sector. Beginning an occupation, the Imperium displaced the local population of Dhanis over the course of the next ten years. Forcing the Dhani to the southern Lowlands , the Imperium established an Enterprise Zone of new Imperial housing and offered work in factories . To discourage Dhanis from traveling to the sacred Valley of Caves , the location of the Aldhani dam, to view the revered celestial event known as the " Eye of Aldhani " that happened every three years, the Imperium established an Imperial viewing festival in the Enterprise zone in 15 BVE .

#### Designing the ultimate weapon

title: Imperium
text:
#### Designing the ultimate weapon

> " You look at the history of any sentient species and what do you find but tableaux of violence and slaughter. It's finger painted on the ceilings of caves and engraved into the walls of temples. Dig a hole deep enough on any world and you'll find the skulls and bones of adults and children fractured by crude weapons. All of us were fighting long before we were farming and raising livestock…Violence is hardwired into most of us and there's no eliminating the impulse—not with an army of shock troopers or a fleet of Star Destroyers. That's why we've embarked on a path to a different solution. We have a chance to forge a peace that will endure longer than the Republic was in existence. " ―Orren Callan Vossik

title: Imperium
text: Having inherited the Republic Special Weapons Group , a top secret group headed by Professor Sahali tasked with top secret project and ordered by Mal to construct the deadly battle station from it's predecessor state, the Imperium reformed the Weapons Group into the Imperial Military Department of Advanced Weapons Research in which the Ultimate Weapon project was assigned and split into several smaller projects, with Project Celestial Power , a subproject tasked with the development of a superweapon for the battle station, being publicly presented as an initiative to fulfill Theron Mal's dream of sustainable energy independence to transform the Imperial economy and solidify Imperial authority. Lieutenant Commander Orren Callan Vossik , an Imperial officer who had been involved with the failed attempt at the Battle Station's construction, and had held an administrative post at the Institute of Applied Science on Vantor screening scientists for expertise on energy manipulation, materials science, and theoretical physics, was placed in charge of the program. Around this time the the outer rings were completed, with the Emperor performing an inspection shortly after, during which Vossik had the focusing array for what would eventually be the laser dish installed.

title: Imperium
text: In charge of the program, Vossik had the B'ankora relocated from the B'ankor Refuge on Vantor to allow the construction of a new research complex at the site, and seeing potential for the battle station's weapon in the crystallographer Galen Walton Arsa Kyber crystal research, offered the crystallographer a spot in the project, convincing him that the project was tasked with bringing sustainable energy to worlds ravaged by the replica wars, which Galen accepted. As Galen made progress on his research on Kyber crystals, Vossik began attempting to weaponize Galen's research at secret facilities on worlds such as Hypori and Malpaz , all while Galen and his family grew suspicious of Galen's work.

title: Imperium
text:
Despite Project Celestial Power being hit with a major accident when a facility on Malpaz exploded during a weaponization attempt and destroying the planet's capital city , Vossik eventually succeeded in weaponizing Galen's research with the successful test of prototype duel-laser weapon into a set of Black holes known as the Hero Twins . Yet despite the successful test, the project was once again set back when the team tasked with designing the full superlaser questioned their work and realized who's research was being used, forcing Vossik to "relocate" them. Not long after, Galen discovered the Imperial coverup and massacre, which all but confirmed something was wrong. With this information, Galen decided to run away with his family to Lah'mu , making Project Celestial Power stall until Vossik could locate the crystallographer. Grand Moff Varrix used the opportunity to give himself an overseeing position of the Ultimate Weapon Project, often stealing credit for Vossik's work and causing a bitter rivalry between him and Vossik.

#### Spread of the Imperium

title: Imperium
text:
#### Spread of the Imperium

> " For the first time in one thousand generations our sector governors will not be working solely to enrich Vantor and the Core Reaches, but to advance the quality of life in the star systems that make up each sector-keeping the spaceways safe, maintaining open and accessible communications, assuring that tax revenues are properly levied and allocated to improving the infrastructure. The Senate will likewise be made up of beings devoted not to their own enrichment, but to the enrichment of the worlds they represent. " ―An excerpt from the Varrix Doctrine As the Imperium grew, Mal moved closer to his ultimate plan of ruling the entire galaxy and unlocking the secrets of the Umbra Masters who had come before him. With the near extermination of the Aetheri Order and the Imperium swelling in size and strength, the Emperor ultimately planned to possess the powers of the umbra side to reshape reality itself into something of his own creation, and an omnipotent Imperium would allow all the galaxy's inhabitants to be held in his dark embrace. As Emperor, however, he largely disappeared from public life, leaving his public addresses to become more and more rare.

title: Imperium
text: While, in public, the Imperial system of sector governance was designed to improve and uplift life across the whole of the galaxy, the truth of the Imperium and its New Order was that it enforced a form of supposed "natural hierarchy," which uplifted life in the Core Reaches at the expense of those who lived further out across the stars. Planets at the edge of the galaxy suffered under Imperial rule while their resources and wealth were extracted and shipped towards the Core, particularly Vantor, which prospered under Imperial rule. Imperial leadership and their wealthy contemporaries enjoyed luxurious lifestyles. As most planets were ecologically devastated over the Imperial Era, rampant industrialization and mass-production eroded local culture and ecological health. People saw their children drafted into Imperial service, while corrupt governors and magistrates often exploited local populations on worlds such as Jelucan , Devaron and Tangenine . In 18 BVE , the Imperium conquered and occupied the planet Yar Togna , leading to much of its population fleeing as refugees in a mass exodus. At some point, the Mid Reach uprisings were launched by monarchies that refused to obey Mal's will. The revolts ended up as a series of chaotic conflicts that ended in Imperial victory: through the actions of Imperial Starfighter Pilots , the monarchies were forced to submit to the Emperor.

title: Imperium
text: Only a year after its founding, the Imperium had already begun to enforce itself in the Outer Reach. Worlds that did not fall to the Imperium's quick expansion, which installed an oppressive Imperial presence instead of simple bases, became homes to crime lords. In its effort to establish itself in the Outer Reach, in addition to using fear, the Imperium withheld food to make populations endure hunger. While the Imperium turned a blind eye to various abuses, it still maintained a policy of zero corruption and maintained its high standards of conduct, resulting in numerous Imperium Vigil Bureau (IVB) officials actively hunting down corrupt and negligent officials, even resulting in investigations by Lord Velgor himself. Despite this, many citizens were content with the geopolitical situation in the galaxy, believing that strict measures were necessary to maintain order and stability after the destructive Replica Wars. Many also believed that the Imperium, while not the best, was better than anarchy and chaos.

title: Imperium
text: Despite its seemingly endless expansion, such as on Raadan , where Imperial forces arrived to harvest food , which destroyed the quality of the moon's soil and led to a growing oppression. This angered the people of Raadan to the point where they staged an uprising after weeks of planning, with the help of ex- Adept Sela Marr and the forces of Imperial Senator Bael Solen in secret. A major turning point against the Imperium's advance into the Outer Reach occurred in 11 BVE , with Imperial forces commanded by Captain Raena Vexana engaging in a small skirmish in the vital Inner Reach system of Gorse .

title: Imperium
text:
This event saw the meeting of later insurgent Lena Kryll and Aetheri survivor Brenn Aldric , who were confronting efficiency expert Count Denetrius Vidian and his aggressive methods of extracting thorilide —a vital component in the construction of pulse lance batteries and thus essential for the expansion of the Imperial fleet. The Gorse Conflict ultimately ended with the transferring of local thorilide mining operations to Imperial-aligned Baron Lero Danthe , while Kryll and Aldric departed on the heavily modified VCX-100 light freighter Wisp , and would become essential to the eventual formation of the Free Coalition .

Meanwhile, more and more worlds within the Imperium began to realize its true intentions: After various massacres on Thornwood and increasingly brutal tactics, such as the Imperium committing genocide on the Lasat homeworld of Lasan , a growing number of citizens of the galaxy began to insurgent against Imperial dominion. At least nine years after the proclamation of the New Order , the Korrathi Coalition fought the Imperium from its headquarters on the planet Korrath . The Imperium would also end the independence of many galactic, sector and planetary governments in its early conquests.

#### Theft of the Carrion Spike

title: Imperium
text:
#### Theft of the Carrion Spike

> " You hear so many rumors. People are here one day, gone the next. And no one has laid eyes on the Emperor in months. Veldon, Dangor, and the rest of the Ruling Council have taken to dispatching processions of Imperial skylimos to maintain an illusion that the Emperor still moves about in public. You know they commissioned an enormous statue of the Emperor for the Senate—I mean, Imperial Plaza? So far, the thing looks more terrifying than majestic. " " Isn't that the idea, Nils? " ―Admiral Nils Tenant and Moff Wilhard Varrix discuss the Imperialization of Vantor

title: Imperium
text: In 14 BVE , after Mal had spent months on end out of the public eye, members of the Ruling Council, including Mazan Veldon and Ars Dangor, arranged for skylimos to move about Imperial City , creating the illusion of Mal moving amongst the populous. Furthermore, the ongoing Imperialization of the galaxy and even Vantor at that time resulted in, as Admiral Nils Tenant observing, personnel being "here on day, gone the next." Around the time, an enormous statue of the Emperor—which was regarded by Tenant as more terrifying than beautiful—was erected in Imperial Plaza, with Varrix arguing to Tenant that it was supposed to be scary, not majestic.

title: Imperium
text: Meanwhile, various survivors of the Antar Atrocity and other malcontents joined together under the leadership of the former Captain Berch Teller, who organized them into a insurgent cell intent on stalling the development of the Emperor's newest weapon under construction at Pyralis. After stealing the Carrion Spike , an advanced starship based on a prototype stealth corvette used during the Battle of Krestophis during the Replica Wars, the insurgents wreaked havoc across numerous star systems including Lucazec , Galidraan III and Nouane , all while transmitting holovids of their attacks on Imperial HoloNet frequencies, increasing anti-Imperial propaganda across thousands of Mid and Outer Reach star systems before the Imperium was able to shut down the communications grid.

title: Imperium
text: After lengthy fleet redeployments and the discovery of a mole within the Imperial ranks, Varrix, aboard the Imperial -class Iron Cruiser Executrix , disabled the insurgent warship and captured the dissidents after a brief battle and timely arrival of Star Destroyers Compliant and Enforcer . To reward Varrix's skill, the Emperor promoted him to the newly created rank of Grand Moff and gave him command of the Executrix as well as oversight of the Outer Reach Territories, all while the recent attacks on Imperial facilities were made to look like an elaborate plot to root out insurgent cells. The Imperium had effectively dealt with a potentially disastrous situation, rooted out a traitor and kept details regarding the development of its superweapon at Pyralis a mere rumor.

title: Imperium
text:
The Emperor's long-term plan was to allow what he called the "skeleton of the Republic" to remain in place until the Void Core was completed; this included maintaining the Senate to make the systems believe that they still had a part to play in the government. However, upon the superweapon's completion, the Emperor planned to dissolve the Senate and grant its legislative and administrative powers to the military-industrial complex. The Void Core would also provide order to the galaxy, as part of Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix's doctrine of terror , by making its inhabitants too afraid to defy an Imperial command and stand against the Imperium.

#### Outer Reach expansion

> " Good news has come to the citizens of Lorath. The Outer Reach planet has been granted the coveted opportunity to participate in the new Imperial Registration Program. " ― Alton Kastle , on the HoloNet News

Around fourteen years into Mal' rule as Emperor, the Imperium had continued its expansion into the Outer Reach. Worlds like Jelucan saw occupation and development, leading to rampant pollution and industrialization to support the Imperial war machine. One such world that was developed was Lorath , which joined the Imperial Registration Program seeking protection and economic opportunities whereby local citizens would find work in the local Sienar Fleet Systems facilities. Ostensibly this was to grow the local economy, but was in fact secretly part of a much larger five-year plan involving numerous Outer Reach worlds that was overseen by the Imperial Outer Reach High Command , a subdivision of Imperial High Command which was in charge of the Outer Reach Territories .

title: Imperium
text:
But the Imperium did not fully control the Outer Reach and often utilized its worlds instead as testing grounds for new biological weapons and as a source of cheap labor. Lorath's industrial importance soon came to the fore for the Imperium as the Emperor planned to further expand Imperial dominion over the Outer Reach Territories and beyond. In order to maximize the worth of newly occupied systems, worlds such as Lorath soon bore witness to Imperial authorities relocating farmers away from their farmlands to mine for Imperial purposes, leading to the development of re-settlement camps such as Tangletown and Lorath re-settlement camp 43 , known by the residents as "Tarkintown" after the Governor of the Outer Reach. The Imperium also limited the HoloNet across the Outer Reach, leading many dissatisfied systems to view the embargo as a part of the conquest of the Outer Systems. This aggressive dislocation of persons and high tax rate eventually led to the development of a small and localized, albeit serious upheaval against the Imperium on Lorath.

reevaluated, all outstanding fines and levies ordered to be pain in full immediately, and all offenses towards the Imperium, both direct and indirect, to be treated as a class one offense under the Imperial Penal Code . The related information was communicated to the IVB Board by Yular directly the same day that the acts passed. #### Lorath insurgency

> " We are getting reports of unrest all over Lorath. There are whispers from Emberfall. Some people see the Imperium as weak. Vulnerable. " " Not to worry, Agent Kallux. The Emperor has sent an alternative solution. " ―Alexsandr Kallux and Wilhard Varrix

By 5 BVE , separate insurgencies across the Imperial territories had formed but were of little consequence, though the Emperor did foresee a new threat rising against the Imperium—the children of Synth Flux. But the Imperium overall did not fear that the various insurgent cells could unite and form a more potent menace against the Imperium and its interests in the Outer Reach. Imperial Military command maintained a list of known Insurgent sympathizers on several Outer Reach worlds, including Lorath, but most of them were not arrested due to their having powerful allies in the Senate, a known hotbed of corruption and decadence.

title: Imperium
text:
Among these cells on Lorath were the Shades , who manned the Wisp . When rumor of the discovery of Aldric' Aetheri identity and his duty on leading the Shades began to emerge, the Imperium sent the Grand Warden to track him down. The Aetheri survivor was to be taken to Xarn Velgor's fortress on Emberfall, yet in 4 BVE , in a daring battle over Emberfall that marked the first major insurgent victory in the Galactic Civil War, the Wisp crew rescued Aldric and joined with a growing insurgency.

The insurgents, commanded by Sela Marr, were part of a larger insurgent movement across the entire galaxy which included several cells, led by Marr and Imperial Senator Bael Solen, and purposely kept in darkness about the existence of one another to prevent information leaks and Imperial crackdowns. Following rumors of an Imperial defeat over Emberfall, spontaneous riots and unrest on several Imperial worlds occurred. The size of the insurgency had also caused concern in the higher ranks of the Imperium. With the Grand Warden's death, the Emperor sent his loyal enforcer, Xarn Velgor, to quash the threat to the Imperium's reign.

title: Imperium
text: Following the events on Emberfall, Lord Velgor imposed a complete lockdown and blockade of the planet as a disillusioned Minister Tua contacted the Shades to defect to the insurgency, with IVB agent Alexsandr Kallux using this to lure the insurgents back to Lorath and to capture them, but Tua was killed during the escape attempt. This prompted Kallux to frame the insurgents for her murder and send Imperial forces to search for them. The insurgents evaded arrest by hiding in the Imperial Complex only to be met by Xarn Velgor and a duel; however, the insurgents escaped in a stolen shuttle . Velgor ordered Kallux to raze Lorath re-settlement camp 43, known as Tarkintown, to punish the locals for accepting help from the insurgents.

title: Imperium
text:
After breaking the Imperial blockade, Velgor attacked the Ember Cell fleet that had been sent from the Solen-Marr alliance of insurgent cells, who had come to the aid of the Shades and inflicted high casualties on it, forcing both insurgent cells to retreat into hyperspace . With this, the Imperium's operations had been a success and while remaining a threat to the Imperium even after pushing the insurgents off-world, order had nevertheless been restored on the vital world of Lorath and caused a major setback to the insurgency.

#### Further insurgent activity

> " Send a probe to investigate. All leads must be pursued. " ―Alexsandr Kallux

In the aftermath of the victory on Lorath, Admiral Konstantine and the Imperial Navy continued to securing the Outer Reach and also hunting for these insurgents. He was accompanied by Agent Kallux, who also had experience dealing with these insurgents during the revolt on Lorath who had traveled to the desert planet of Seelos to make contact with several retired replica troopers: Vek, Wolffe, and Gregor and hoped to win them over to their cause but Wolffe who distrusted the insurgents sent a coded transmission that was picked up by the Relentless .

title: Imperium
text: Agent Kallux led a ground assault with three Ironclad Walker walkers . Konstantine remained aboard the Relentless to render air support to Kallux' forces. However, the replicas and insurgents joined forces and put up a fierce fight and immobilized Kallux Ironclad Walker walkers. The admiral, however, had been unable to render air support because Lord Velgor had ordered him to rendezvous with his shuttle in space, but instead of meeting Velgor, Konstantine received another Warden known as the Fifth Warden . When Konstantine raised his concerns that the diversion might have compromised Agent Kallux' mission, the Warden merely replied that his struggles were of no concern to him and pledged to stop the insurgents himself.

title: Imperium
text: The insurgents later helped deliver relief supplies to the famine-stricken planet Ibaar , which was being blockaded by an Imperial fleet. The Imperium had doubled the Ibaarians' work quotas and reduced their rations, creating a famine. The first attempt failed and ended with the destruction of the CR90 corvette transporting the supplies. Still, the insurgent network persisted, and the insurgents broke through the blockade with the help of a Blade Wing prototype starfighter , which destroyed one of the Arquitens -class command cruisers . This enabled the insurgents to deliver supplies to the Ibaarian coalition, which subsequently distributed the supplies. While searching for a missing patrol in the Del Zennis system , Commander Savren, Cass, and several other insurgents were captured by an Imperial Interdictor , a prototype warship equipped with gravity well projectors capable of dragging ships out of hyperspace. In response, Brenn, along with Vek and Chomper, staged a rescue mission which ended with the destruction of the Interdictor, dealing a serious blow to Imperial forces.

title: Imperium
text: Lacking a permanent base, one insurgent group—the Ember Squadron—hid in several spaceports scattered across the planet Garel , but the Imperium learned of the insurgent presence there and sent a fleet to crush them with most retreating. Following the losses on Garel, Imperial Senator Solen sent his adopted daughter Princess Elira Solen of Cindervale to deliver three Sphyrna -class Hammerhead corvettes to the Insurgency. Since the Cindervaleans could not be seen directly supporting the Ember insurgents, Bael arranged for Elira to deliver the vessels to Lorath, where in secret the insurgents would "steal" the ships. However, the local Imperial commander Yogar Lyste had fitted the Hammerhead corvettes with gravity locks , but this failed when the insurgents stole the vessel during a skirmish with Imperial forces.

title: Imperium
text:
With the Imperium hunting down the insurgents throughout the Outer Reach Territories, the insurgents decided to create a new route through the Lorath sector . Ryn identified the Concord Dawn system as a viable route that the insurgents could use. The system was home to the Ferrik Protectors , a Ferrik faction that was led by Fen Raun , a veteran of the Replica Wars. Commander Savren sent Ember Leader Lena and Ryn on a mission to negotiate safe passage through the Concord Dawn system with Raun. However, Raun had already aligned the Protectors with the Imperium and attacked Lena's mission, seriously wounding Lena and killing at least one Ember Squadron pilot. In retaliation, Ryn and Brenn infiltrated the Protectors' camp on the third moon of Concord Dawn and destroyed their Fang-class fighters. The insurgents also captured Raun, who agreed to give the insurgents safe passage through the Concord Dawn system in return for keeping his capture a secret from the Imperium.

#### Showdown on Searmark

> " The power within will soon serve the Emperor. " ―Xarn Velgor

title: Imperium
text:
#### Showdown on Searmark

> " The power within will soon serve the Emperor. " ―Xarn Velgor

Eventually, a Warden called the Eighth Warden was sent to seek a shadow on Searmark , within the depths of the Umbra Temple on the planet's surface. At the same time Brenn, Cass and Sela from the insurgency arrived and immediately recognized him as the former Umbra Lord Vreth, to who also the Wardens confirmed was alive and after the death of the three Wardens, Vreth turned on his Aetheri allies and blinded Brenn. The insurgents' problems were further complicated by the arrival of Xarn Velgor, who had come to take the secrets of the temple for himself. The Aetheri removed the reliquary from the temple's obelisk, which triggered an implosion that damaged much of the temple. While the two Aetheri escaped on the Phantom with Chomper, Sela stayed behind to hold back Velgor. The Imperial mission to Searmark was a partial failure, as both the Aetheri and Vreth escaped, but Aldric was blinded in a duel against Vreth while Cass began exploring the umbra side, and the insurgency Aetheri leadership was broken.

title: Imperium
text:
But the insurgent cells continued working on growing and expanding as the Shades conducted a raid on Naraka prison and set out to Reklam Station , where the Imperium was dismantling thousands of Republic-era Yarrow starfighters . Imperial security forces failed to prevent both the destruction of the station and the theft of five Yarrows, which were transferred to General Jan Dodonna 's unit . Meanwhile, all the increased insurgent activity led Governor Arihnda Pryssa of the Lorath sector to request the aid of the Seventh Fleet to deal with the Ember Group, which was granted by Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix and led by Grand Admiral Vorren, who was promoted for wiping out the insurgent presence in the Batonn sector . While Agent Kallux was concerned about the high civilian casualties, Pryssa justified Vorren's actions on the grounds that there were no more insurgents there and was given control over the efforts to destroy the growing insurgency before it could become a true threat to the Imperium's reign over the Outer Reach by setting out a strategy.

#### Wider engagements with the insurgents

title: Imperium
text:
#### Wider engagements with the insurgents

> " I will start my operations here, and pull the insurgents apart piece by piece. They will be the architects of their own destruction. " ―Mitth'raw'nuruodo

En route to provide supplies to Teralov , a squadron of Arrows and a transport were attacked by an Imperial Arquitens -class command cruiser that dispatched three SKREE interceptors led by Captain Vult Skerris , which quickly wiped out the insurgent convoy. Reeling from this loss, the Ember insurgents dispatched the former Imperial cadet Ryn Wrenna to infiltrate the Skystrike Academy to extract the disillusioned cadets Torb Rask , Hobbie , and Rake Gahree , in which the insurgent and defectors would be able to escape from the Imperium's grip. Later, the insurgents, along with the Free Selvara movement led by Chavar Kryll, went on a mission to Selvara, where they learned that Vorren—who had studied the tactics used by the insurgency and now had direct command of Imperial forces—had made military advances led by Captain Slavin in the Tann Province .

title: Imperium
text: The Shades undertook a supply run to the Agamar to obtain proton bombs from a Dissident transport ship. However, they were captured by a Dissident holdout led by the super tactical droid General Kalani . The droid general wished to end the Replica Wars on his own terms, and challenged the insurgents to a battle that would decide the victors, but Imperial forces suddenly arrived and attacked the Dissident ship. The insurgents and Dissidents came to the conclusion that the Imperium was the real victor of the Replica Wars, and decided to unite in order to escape the Imperium. While the Imperial Viceroy, Gar Saxon , discovered that the insurgents were using the Concord Dawn system to avoid Imperial sector patrols. Saxon destroyed the Protectors' encampment on the third moon of Concord Dawn in an attempt to lure Fen Raun back.

title: Imperium
text: The Imperium had planned to impose martial law on the planet Mykapo which insurgents made efforts to evacuate insurgent sympathizers. Upon arriving, the flotilla encountered a light freighter , which was engaged in a dogfight with an Imperial advance patrol calling themselves the Iron Squadron . Vorren, who was aware of this Insurgent presence in the system, dispatched a light cruiser to assess the situation, placed under the command of Admiral Kassius Konstantine in order to test the officer's questionable capabilities. The admiral crippled the Iron Squadron's freighter, prompting the crew with the exception of Mattin to escape aboard the Phantom II with the Shades. The insurgents returned with reinforcements from Ember Squadron to rescue Mattin. During the skirmish, Konstantine's cruiser was badly damaged, and most of his forces were destroyed. The insurgents fled into lightspeed just as the Chimaera arrived in the system.

title: Imperium
text: Soon after, the insurgents returned to Lorath and began an infiltration of the Imperial Armory Complex to obtain the blueprints for a prototype SKREE fighter . However, their mission coincided with a visit by Grand Admiral Vorren on behalf of Imperial High Command, who was investigating the high rate of sabotage within the factory. The insurgents, however, escaped the factory with sensitive Imperial information with the help of the now disillusioned Agent Kallux, who had become an informant for the insurgency. As a result of this insurgent attack, Vorren realized that the Imperium had a traitor among their ranks. Following this, there was an increase of the Imperial Navy presence such as capital ships in and around Lorath as part of Imperial orbital defenses. Beyond the Lorath system, rebellious activities increased, such as on Pyralis, where Captain Brunson responded to a triggered proximity sensor and discovered the Shades vessel Wisp on the planet who had saved both Torrik Vess after his Partisans scout team was killed. Hoping to earn herself and her crew promotions, she attempted to destroy the insurgents using SKREE bombers and rocket troopers , and finally by trapping the insurgents in an underground cavern in attempt to

title: Imperium
text: on the planet who had saved both Torrik Vess after his Partisans scout team was killed. Hoping to earn herself and her crew promotions, she attempted to destroy the insurgents using SKREE bombers and rocket troopers , and finally by trapping the insurgents in an underground cavern in attempt to bury them alive. When she used her cruiser to block their escape, this backfired, as the Wisp fired two proton torpedoes , resulting in the destruction of her ship with the insurgents who recovered images of the poison canisters that were used for the sterilization of Pyralis in order to show the Imperial Senate and rally more systems to their cause.

title: Imperium
text: Vorren later dispatched several E-XD-series infiltrator droids to search the Outer Reach for insurgent bases. However, Kallux used the insurgent identity Fulcrum to warn the base's Chief of Security Gara-Zev Orrelios about the threat. As a result, he and his fellow insurgents Chomper and AP-5 stopped the infiltrator droid EXD-9 from infiltrating the insurgent base on Atollon . They turned E-XD9 into an improvised bomb that destroyed an Iron Cruiser. Despite their efforts, Vorren narrowed the search for the insurgent base to 94 systems. The Imperium lost a local ally in the form of Viceroy Gar Saxon, the Emperor's Hand and puppet ruler of Ferrum . Gar Saxon was defeated during a duel with the insurgent Ryn Wrenna on the planet of Krownest . Saxon's death triggered a power vacuum among the Ferriks. Ryn then joined forces with her mother, Ursa Wrenna , and the former Protectors' leader Fen Raun to reunify the Ferriks.

title: Imperium
text:
Continuing his investigation into the insurgent mole, Grand Admiral Vorren began screening the Imperial sector command staff within the Lorath sector with the help of Imperium Vigil Bureau Colonel Wulric Yular , a veteran of the Replica Wars. Vorren summoned several Imperial officials including Agent Kallux, Lieutenant Yogar Lyste, Captain Brunson, and Commander Brom Titus for questioning aboard his flagship, Chimaera . After learning that Vorren was intercepting Kallux' transmissions, the Shades and Vek mounted a mission to rescue Kallux. During the course of the mission, Kallux joined forces with the insurgents to delete the planet Atollon, which hosted Chomper Base, from Vorren's database. However, Kallux elected not to escape with the insurgents and instead framed his colleague Lyste as Fulcrum. Vorren learned of Kallux' deception but kept this information secret since he hoped to manipulate Kallux into uncovering the Ember insurgent base.

#### A united foe

title: Imperium
text:
#### A united foe

With full-scale insurgency on the horizon, Imperial Senator Vela Sess would openly betray the Imperium by seeking to unite the various rebellions cells into one organization. She began by firstly publicly condemning the reign of Theron Mal after the Ghorman Massacre which led to Commander Vult Skerris leading the effort for her capture in the Archeon Nebula . However, the mission ended in failure, and she was able to escape. This led to her broadcasting a speech to insurgents across the galaxy over Steelgrove , which led to the formation of various insurgent cells into the alliance to restore the Vantor Republic and, along with her resignation from the Imperial Senate, the beginning of a true united insurgency.

### Galactic Civil War

#### Insurgency Rising

Battle of Atollon

title: Imperium
text:
### Galactic Civil War

#### Insurgency Rising

Battle of Atollon

Soon after its founding, the Free Coalition pressed on with the planned operation on Lorath by stealing clearance codes from the Imperium Vigil Bureau station on Killun 71 to allow their forces to mount a successful attack on the Imperium. However, the planned insurgent attack on Lorath did not go forward thanks to Vorren, who had discovered the location of Chomper Base, the headquarters of the Ember Group. Vorren's fleet blockaded Atollon and inflicted heavy casualties on insurgent forces. Vorren launched a ground assault after an orbital bombardment. Meanwhile, Cass, who had escaped the fighting, enlisted the help of Clan Wrenna .

title: Imperium
text:
In response, Governor Pryssa dispatched Jumptroopers, but these reinforcements failed to stop the Ferriks from destroying the last Interdictor cruiser. Despite Vorren storming Chomper Base, the insurgents and Imperials were attacked by an angry Bendu , an enigmatic being that was living on Atollon, who used his Synth Flux powers to devastate the insurgent base before being subdued by Vorren. The surviving insurgent and Ferrik forces fled the battle as the Imperium wiped out the Ember Squadron; however, the Imperium was still unaware of the true scale of the Free Coalition. Nonetheless, the routing at Atollon was seen as proof by the insurgents that they were not yet ready for open war with the Imperium.

Ferrik Civil War

title: Imperium
text:
Ferrik Civil War

Meanwhile, civil war raged on Imperial-occupied Ferrum, with the Free Coalition setting out to rescue Ryn's father and Imperial prisoner Alrich Wrenna from Governor Tiber Saxon . Clan Wrenna rescued Alrich with the help of the insurgents. In response, Saxon unleashed the Arc Pulse Generator known as the Duchess against the Clan Wrenna forces, killing many. Ryn led the Ferriks and insurgents on a mission to infiltrate Saxon's Iron Cruiser, which was above Sundari and were ambushed by Imperial forces, which resulted in the Ferriks and insurgents' success in destroying the weapon and Saxon's flagship. While not pursuing an agenda of open war, the insurgents continued their campaign and mounted successful raids on both Jalindi and the Faos Station . The Imperium failed to stop both the Partisan and Spectre efforts, resulting in the loss of Commander Brom Titus and Captain Slavin. On Lorath, the Imperium Vigil Bureau conducted a successful raid against a suspected insurgent cell allied with the Shades. However, the efforts of the Lorath insurgents and their allies brought about the Liberation of Lorath , with Vorren going missing when Virel forced himself and the Grand Admiral into hyperspace aboard the Chimaera . At some point, a prisoner uprising was launched within the Cherridan Imperial labor camp , but it was put down in a brutal fashion. A failure for the Imperium, however, came when an assault on the Winter's Edge shock trooper garrison ended in success for the enemy.

#### The Ultimate Weapon

Destruction of Embermoor City

> " There is no Void Core. We're informing the Senate that Embermoor was destroyed in a mining disaster. " ―Xarn Velgor

title: Imperium
text:
#### The Ultimate Weapon

Destruction of Embermoor City

> " There is no Void Core. We're informing the Senate that Embermoor was destroyed in a mining disaster. " ―Xarn Velgor

A local insurgency was carried out by Vess's Partisans on the desert moon of Embermoor , an Imperial protectorate , in the ancient streets of Embermoor City as part of their larger campaign against the Imperium. Unknown to many of them, Director Orren Vossik and Grand Moff Varrix had decided to test the capability of the Imperium's new superweapon -equipped battle station , the Void Core , by firing its superlaser at the city using a single- reactor ignition. At least 3% of Embermoor's Imperial forces were presumed destroyed in the blast as well, having been unable to evacuate. The Imperial casualties included such forces as JN-093's squad , who had been assigned to check possible insurgent hiding spots outside the city, leaving them unable to get to the extraction point in time. The Imperium subsequently fabricated a cover story for the Imperial Senate that Embermoor was destroyed in a mere mining disaster.

Battle of Halcyon

title: Imperium
text:
Battle of Halcyon

A group of insurgents under the callsign Renegade One had captured the blueprints for the Void Core, which had just been completed after nearly two decades of work on Halcyon . They infiltrated the planetary shield in a stolen Zeta -class Heavy Cargo Shuttle and waged a guerrilla assault on the base's outskirts, drawing away Imperial forces, while the insurgents could access the Citadel Tower .

However, they received support from the Alliance Fleet under Admiral Raddik , whose forces engaged the Imperial Star Destroyers above Halcyon and aimed to destroy the Shield Gate . Renegade One transmitted the stolen plans to the fleet above, but by the order of Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix, they along with Director Orren Vossik were eradicated by a low-powered blast from the arrived Void Core that destroyed the Citadel and surrounding area. By then, the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor's forces had destroyed the insurgent ships that did not manage to retreat, but he failed to get the plans back as they were transported to Imperial Senator and Princess Elira Solen on the Tantiva IV .

Reveal of the Void Core

title: Imperium
text:
Reveal of the Void Core
