> " Cindervale was supposedly selected as the Void Core's first full-scale target to compel Princess Elira into revealing the location of the main insurgent base. But this is only a partial explanation. The Void Core ceased to be a secret weapon as soon as it entered Cindervalean orbit. It was never going to leave the planet intact. It is therefore highly likely that Varrix and the Emperor had pre-selected Cindervale because of, rather than in spite of, its inhabitants' pacifism and the way their morality had caused the Imperium numerous political problems in the Imperial Senate. They intended to send a message about where all forms of coalition to Imperial rule—even non-violent coalition—would now lead, something Mal made even more clear when he simultaneously disbanded the Senate. " ―Beaumont Kin reflects on the destruction of Cindervale

title: Imperium
text:
Imperial forces commanded by Xarn Velgor captured one of the leaders of the Alliance and the one who possessed the plans, Princess of Cindervale Elira Solen—who, unknown to Velgor, was his own daughter. While nearly all of the old institutions of the Republic had been swept away in the intervening decades, this provided Mal the opportunity to finally wipe away the last vestiges of the old democracy , and dissolve the Imperial Senate permanently. This brought governance of the various systems of the Imperium directly under the purview of the Regional Governors and the Imperial Military. Solen's presence, and her refusal to give up the location of the Alliance's base, precipitated Grand Moff Varrix's decision to test-fire the newly completed Void Core's primary weapon on her homeworld, Cindervale, although historian Beaumont Kin later theorized Varrix and Mal had pre-selected the world as a perfect target for the Void Core. In an instant, the Imperial Military's superweapon utterly destroyed the populous, influential world. In so doing, Varrix hoped not only to synth flux Solen to submit but also to strike fear into any others who sought to insurgent against Imperial rule. Soon after the destruction of Cindervale, dubbed " the Disaster " by Cindervalean refugees, vigils for the dead were held on Vantor 's Level 3204 , with many on the level having formerly lived on Cindervale. However, as soon as the circumstances behind the event became clear, the once-peaceful vigils turned into violent riots , with many calling for justice and revolution against the Imperium. Imperial shock troopers and Vantor underworld police were soon called in to restore the peace, and began arresting and eventually relocating those who questioned Imperial rule.

Rescue of Princess Solen

title: Imperium
text:
Rescue of Princess Solen

> " Yes? " " We've captured a freighter entering remains of the Cindervale system. Its markings matches those ships that blasted its way out of Port Kess. " " They must be trying to return the stolen plans to the Princess. She may yet be of some use to us. " ―Wilhard Varrix, Imperial Docking Bay Control, and Xarn Velgor

Eventually, Solen was rescued from the Void Core by the unlikely alliance of smuggler Dax Karrick , her unknowing twin brother Joren Drayden and Orien Kade, who sacrificed himself in his final duel with Xarn Velgor. The group escaped the Imperial fortress and fled to the Alliance base on Cinderfall 4 , pursued by the Void Core. At Cinderfall 4, the Imperium and the Insurgents engaged in a major battle , with the fate of the insurgency hanging in the balance. Despite destroying a great many of the Alliance's starfighters, the battle ultimately ended up a major defeat for the Imperial forces, when Drayden fired the shot which destroyed the Void Core. This marked the Insurgency's first major victory against the Imperium.

title: Imperium
text:
Now viewing the growing Alliance as a credible threat, Mal issued a communiqué the morning after the Void Core's destruction ordering all ongoing IVB operations be superseded for the immediate detention of known and suspected insurgent sympathizers. Admiral Kendal Ozzel ordered the fleet into battle readiness. To keep the Insurgency off balance, the Imperium engaged in rushed and scrambled offenses across the galaxy and raided spice worlds such as Kerev Doi in an attempt to cut off possible sources of income for the Alliance. With major military redeployments occurring around the clock, the Imperial Military began to mobilize for a full-scale galactic war, while the Insurgency began to push into the populous Imperial Mid Reach in a failed operation that only months later would become known as the Mid Reach Retreat , its ultimate demise owing in large part to the Imperium's numerical superiority.

Aftermath of Cinderfall

title: Imperium
text:
Aftermath of Cinderfall

> " We kept the skeleton of the Republic for nearly twenty years while the Void Core was constructed. Twenty years, my apprentice. All that planning is now a layer of dust orbiting around Cinderfall… Now, we no longer have the Senate to hold order. We do not have the Void Core to synth flux it. Our greatest weapon is gone. Our production is in ashes. We are besieged. In all these years, we have never skirted closer to disaster. " ―Vael Mal Following losses at Phindar and Portocari two weeks following the Battle of Cinderfall, members of the Nashtah Squadron learned at the Zero Angle bar on the Bright Jewel Oversector Flight Base on Axxila III that the military would undergo a mass reorganization, rescinding the classification between Imperial Navy and Imperial Army pilots. Unbeknownst to the Imperium following the destruction of the first Void Core, the Free Coalition had evacuated their base on Cinderfall 4 and was orbiting the remote world of Orto Plutonia in the Pantora system , located in the Sujimis sector , with the nearest Imperial presence being Moff Abran Balfour , who patrolled the world of Llanic situated at the intersection of the Llanic Spice Route and Triellus Trade Route . [ source? ]

title: Imperium
text: A brief skirmish erupted when Joren Drayden, in the luxury yacht the Desert Jewel , attacked two SKREE fighters assaulting a Kupohan ship. Unknown to Drayden at the time, the ship was in reality carrying a Kupohan spy with vital intelligence regarding Drusil Bephorin , a Givin woman with a reputation for being able to slice into security systems at an astonishing rate and interpret encoded messages at breathtaking speed. Desperately searching for the Alliance Fleet, the Imperium sought to convince Drusil to use her cryptographic skills to aid them and kept her in a sort of luxurious imprisonment on Denon in an effort to sway her favor. Secretly, Drusil offered to join the Alliance as long as the insurgents could extract her family to the ocean world of Omereth , a task given to Major Brena Derlin . After a side mission to the Deep Core, Joren Drayden, Bolt-3 and Nakari Kelen extracted Drusil after an elaborate chase across the galaxy, hampering the Imperium's plans for a retaliatory strike against the Insurgency.

title: Imperium
text:
In addition to insurgent agents wreaking havoc internally, the Imperium suffered desultory raids by insurgent forces emboldened by their successful strike against the Void Core, with the insurgents that destroyed it— Red Squadron —continuing to harass the Imperium, especially during a mission above Giju where a transport carrying underground insurgent leaders was evacuated from the planet. The Imperium also continued to suffer setbacks from the Insurgency's golden boy, Joren Drayden, including the trespass by the Aetheri Purge survivor into the Temple of Eedit —an abandoned Aetheri Sanctum under guard of the Imperium—on Devaron.

Despite the temporary turmoil instilled by the Insurgents' bold strikes, the Alliance attempted even bigger operations to capitalize on its former success. Most notable was an attempt to assault, infiltrate and destroy Weapons Factory Alpha located in the Korrathi Industrial Cluster on Cymoon 1 , reputedly home to the largest weapons factory in the galaxy. In the meantime, the Imperium opened negotiations with the Grak Clan , led by Grukk the Grak, to secure raw materials for Imperial Military production and secure their support for their expansion in the Outer Reach. The Insurgents ultimately destroyed the factory, crippling Imperial production and causing another major setback.

title: Imperium
text:
Velgor's punishment, criminal "crackdown"

> " Varrix had vision. You have graphs. " " I have graphs and the command. " ―Xarn Velgor and Cassio Targ > " Varrix had vision. You have graphs. " " I have graphs and the command. " ―Xarn Velgor and Cassio Targ

For Velgor's failure to stop the destruction of both the Void Core and the Cymoon 1 factory, Vael Mal relieved him of much of his authority and assigned him to serve in the military instead of commanding it. As much of the Imperium's military command had been lost with the Void Core, the Emperor appointed General Cassio Targ , the Chief of the Imperial Army , to the rank of Grand General and assigned him command of Imperial Military matters due to his foresight to fear the Alliance Fleet and doubt the invincibility of the Void Core. The Emperor pressed the military to focus on conquering the Outer Reach and destroying the Insurgency—with the Void Core gone and the Senate disbanded, the Imperium lacked efficient means to keep dissenting systems in line. The power of the Imperium had also been publicly threatened, calling into question its supposed authority. In order to try and restore its image, the Imperium began a crackdown on the criminal underworld but largely ignored its allied criminal powers, such as the Graks.

title: Imperium
text:
Additionally, Imperial statisticians noted predictable increases in piracy following the Void Core's destruction. As a result, the military was to preserve order by any means necessary until the second Void Core was completed. While Imperial forces would shut down Luck Luck Freidal's casino in the immediate aftermath of the Battle of Cinderfall despite Luck Luck Freidal 's efforts to endear himself to local Imperial authorities, allied criminal powers, such as the Graks, were ultimately allowed to thrive under the crackdown. Instead, it was the "disruptive" criminal factions that were sought out and destroyed. Should a criminal power maintain its "understanding" with the Imperium, they would be allowed to take over business in the areas once claimed by the shut down criminal parties.

Under Targ's command, the conquest of the Outer Reach progressed, with Targ launching a significant crackdown on disruptive criminal elements that had gone unchecked in the past. After Doctor Silvar 's attempted hijacking of the in-construction Sovereign -class Star Dreadnought Sovereign was put down by Velgor, Mal demoted Targ and rewarded Velgor with command, which Velgor quickly took advantage of by killing Targ.

#### Search for Joren Drayden

title: Imperium
text:
#### Search for Joren Drayden

While the Insurgency made a drive to defeat the Imperium, Velgor meanwhile searched for Joren Drayden. The Imperium attempted to pin down insurgent activity, but were unable to stop them from seizing control of the Harbinger from the grip of the Imperial Navy. However, the Imperium started a counterattack and prevented insurgent guerrilla and military desultory raids that had occurred in the aftermath of Cinderfall. Further Imperial success came on the mineral planet Saltmark , where the Imperium confronted the Alliance after an attack on the Alliance Fleet as they searched out a possible new insurgent base.

title: Imperium
text:
The Insurgency embarked on a massive military campaign to liberate hundreds of worlds under Imperial control by pushing into the heavily populated Mid Reach. With thousands of starships, hundreds of battle groups and dozens of worlds involved in the operation, it was initially met with stunning success as Imperial forces, unprepared for such a large-scale operation and shattered from the recent shake-ups in the Imperial hierarchy, fell back from world to world, allowing the Insurgency to press further into Imperial space. Taking the factory-deserts of Phorsa Gedd and the Ducal Palace of Bamayar , the Insurgency's advance gradually slowed as Imperial coalition stiffened. Eighteen months into the operation, fearing to overextend the fleet and occupied with the consolidation of worlds now under Insurgent control, High Command ordered the defense of occupied territories, and shortly thereafter the slow withdrawal of Alliance military resources back towards the Outer Reach.

#### Search for the Free Coalition

Chasing leads

title: Imperium
text:
#### Search for the Free Coalition

Chasing leads

> " Listen, they got through debriefing that spy . I—I thought you'd like to know . He says someone sabotaged the Imperium's computers . Made a real mess of their search for us . They're keeping it quiet, but— he says he heard it from a comms jockey on the Sovereign . They put out an arrest warrant for the culprit . Human woman. Archaeotech expertise. Traveling with two dangerous droids. It's set them back a couple weeks , he says. Long enough to get the shield up , huh? Maybe even get those evac plans up to speed. I always knew she was good‐on the inside. " "[To Vulaada Klam and Korin Vexa] Should we tell him she also saved the Emperor's life? " ―Joren Drayden and Magna Tolvan

title: Imperium
text: While the loss of both Varrix and the Void Core itself were significant, Imperial resolve toward putting down the insurgency only increased. For the next three and a half years, Imperial forces under the direct command of Xarn Velgor relentlessly pursued the Alliance. While the hunt was personal for Velgor, having learned that the young insurgent Drayden was actually his son, the Imperial Military nevertheless scoured the galaxy with Imperial probe droids under the name Project Swarm . The operation also made use of a team of archaeological consultants due to the Free Coalition's prior uses of ancient structures as bases, with Velgor's old contact Doctor Chelli Vexa assigned as part of the group; while her role in preventing the plot to assassinate Theron Mal afforded her a degree of protection from Velgor, she believed the Umbra Lord was keeping her close and waiting for any good excuse to silence his old loose end. Imperial forces also picked up Vexa and Velgor's old assassin droids during a sweep of the Ring of Kafrene , installing restraining bolts on both and assigning them as interrogation specialists on the Sovereign .

title: Imperium
text: Under the command of Major Yaltza , who was ultimately executed by Velgor for a lack of results, and then General Maximilian Veers , Project Swarm saw thousands of probe droids search the galaxy while the archaeologists did their work; whereas Vexa questioned the usefulness of their department, Professor Rupo Ud pushed the theory the insurgents would be using another historical site. In secret, Ud did not care about the Imperium or insurgents at all and simply saw Project Swarm as a way to allocate major resources towards an archaeological survey. After her pleas to Velgor fell on deaf ears, Vexa decided to devote herself to finding the insurgent base, thereby securing Mal's favor and keeping herself out of Velgor's grasp forever. After a probe droid was shot down over Ash Moon 1 , Veers led a team to the surface to discover only a group of Central Isopter pilgrims, who he ordered be used as target practice, while Ud led the study of the Isopter temple. Intending to take control of the archaeological team, Vexa tricked Ud into falling into a trap and left her ward Vulaada Klam behind, intending to keep the young girl out of her dangerous

title: Imperium
text: who he ordered be used as target practice, while Ud led the study of the Isopter temple. Intending to take control of the archaeological team, Vexa tricked Ud into falling into a trap and left her ward Vulaada Klam behind, intending to keep the young girl out of her dangerous life. The only update of interest to Veers came when a masked individual—who carried insurgent rations and claimed to know Aetheri mind tricks —was taken captive and brought to the Sovereign , where he was unmasked and revealed to be the now-Supervisor Vexa's father, Korin . At the urging of his daughter and due to his bias against the Free Coalition due to its habit of ruining ancient sites, Korin revealed he had encountered a insurgent cell on Asteroid Helix 13-v , where the two Aphras set to work—with Korin coming to see some benefits to the Imperium's existence if it was directed towards archaeology—and Velgor investigated a presence in Synth Flux, leading him to an altar people had prayed to over the years. The altar made Velgor experience visions of his past, but he destroyed it and soon departed, ignoring Korin's pleas to spare the historical site after he ordered bombers annihilate the temple. Although Velgor's order to withdraw pulled the Imperium off the asteroid before a full sweep could be conducted, with Velgor claiming he did so because the insurgents had already left, the Aphras had found evidence the insurgents had departed for a cold location.

title: Imperium
text: En route to the Sovereign , the Vectis -class T-4a shuttle carrying both Aphras and VT-1 was attacked by the insurgent starship Unnamed under Vexa's former lover Magna Tolvan , herself a former Imperial who predicted how the shock troopers aboard would react and incapacitated all Imperials aboard. As the Imperials and Korin were taken captive, Vexa avoided the insurgents and extracted the location of their new base— Icehold on the planet Frostmark —from Tolvan's electro-tattoos after sleeping with her. She also contacted VT-1 and, after giving the droid permission to kill anyone but her father, ensured her unconscious father was safely deposited back on their Vectis, which she launched with coordinates for Ash Moon I so he could meet up with Klam. Tolvan and the Unnamed followed close behind, ensuring that Vexa's loved ones could meet each other and become a group of their own. Uniting with Tolvan, Korin—who abandoned his anti-insurgent ideals —and Klam joined the insurgency and lived in Icehold.

title: Imperium
text: Rather than fulfill her previous idea of giving Icehold's location to the Imperium, Vexa led Velgor and a group of Imperial forces under Colonel Bryce to the planet Tython , where she freed 0-0-0 and VT-1 from their restraining bolts. With both droids cutting through many of Bryce's troops, Vexa led Velgor to the Martyrium of Frozen Tears , where he was overpowered by his past regrets and severely damaged by a barrage from VT-1. Still keeping her distance and knowing she would be unable to kill the Dark Lord, Vexa instead hacked into Velgor's suit from a distance and contacted the Sovereign , where she reached a comms jockey she tricked into altering and outright deleting much of the data collected by Project Swarm: while she knew Velgor would soon find the insurgent base, she fled Tython with the hope she had delayed his efforts for long enough that the insurgents could set up defenses and escape plans, thereby keeping her loved ones safe. The Imperium put out a warrant for Vexa, who escaped Tython by stealing a SKREE/rp Reaper attack landers and dropped 0-0-0 and VT-1 off on the planet Birukay , where they could stay off the

title: Imperium
text:
the insurgents could set up defenses and escape plans, thereby keeping her loved ones safe. The Imperium put out a warrant for Vexa, who escaped Tython by stealing a SKREE/rp Reaper attack landers and dropped 0-0-0 and VT-1 off on the planet Birukay , where they could stay off the Imperium's radar, although both grew bored from a lack of people to kill. Vexa's actions heavily set back the Imperium's hunt for the insurgency by, according to Vexa's and the Imperium's own estimates, several weeks as it would need to untangle the mess of false positives, deleted information, and altered records she left behind. The Imperium tried to bury news of Vexa's interference, but the comms jockey would end up telling an Imperial officer named Thassilio Smeuse , who was, in secret, a deep-cover agent for the Free Coalition. One day, Smeuse and the shock troopers under his command captured a U-wing and a group of seemingly low-ranking insurgents, who were actually baiting the Imperials into an ambush; after Smeuse completed the code-phrase one insurgent remarked, Tolvan and Strike Team Misericorde ambushed the Imperials and extracted Smeuse. Escaping from three SKREE fighters aboard the U-wing, Tolvan and company returned to Icehold, where Smeuse was debriefed and revealed what Vexa had done.

Battle of Frostmark

> " Yes, Lord Velgor. I've reached the main power generator. The shield will be down in moments. You may start your landing. " ―Maximilian Veers, to Xarn Velgor

title: Imperium
text:
Battle of Frostmark

> " Yes, Lord Velgor. I've reached the main power generator. The shield will be down in moments. You may start your landing. " ―Maximilian Veers, to Xarn Velgor

By 3 AVE , despite having thousands of droids searching the galaxy, Icehold's location on the sixth planet of the Frostmark system remained unknown to the Imperium. However, that same year, Imperial probe droid XJ9-CS14 was dispatched from an Iron Cruiser to that planet. Upon the droid's crash into the planet, insurgent forces dispatched Dax Karrick to investigate, and after a brief skirmish, the droid self destructed after having seen a shield generator. However, aboard the command ship Sovereign , the flagship of a massive Imperial fleet , not long after, Firmus Vett and another Imperial officer reviewed the footage, and promptly informed Fleet Admiral Kendal Ozzel of the lead. Despite Ozzel protests that the lead did not suggest much, Xarn Velgor arrived to inspect the lead, and after seeing the shield generator for himself, became certain that it was the insurgent base and as such ordered the fleet to travel to the Frostmark system.

title: Imperium
text: As the Imperial fleet made it's way to the Frostmark system, the free coalition in turn, fearing their location was exposed, began to evacuate the base. However, upon the fleet's arrival near the Frostmark system, Ozzel made a tactical blunder by leaving hyperspace too close to the system, alerting the alliance to the presence of the fleet and allowing them to raise their energy shield, forcing an Imperial ground assault rather than an orbital bombardment. The blunder cost Ozzel his life at the hands of Velgor and command was promptly shifted to the hands of Firmus Vett as the Imperium began deploying ground forces to the glacial feature known as Moorsh Moraine .

title: Imperium
text:
In the subsequent Imperial assault, Imperial ground forces under the command of General Maximilian Veers , utilizing All Terrain Armored Transport and All Terrain Scout Transport walkers , destroyed the shield generator for Icehold, before Cold weather assault troopers under the command of Velgor entered and overran insurgent forces inside Icehold. During the assault, Karrick's ship, the Corsair Wing , narrowly escaped Velgor's grasp and managed to make it to space, before the Imperial fleet in orbit attempted to stop the ship. As such, the Corsair entered the Frostmark asteroid field before Imperial Skree/LN space superiority starfighters and SKREE/sa tactical bombers followed them in, though the Corsair eluded the forces due to the high risk involving asteroid fields. With the ship lost, Velgor hired several Bounty hunters to locate the ship as an alternative solution, despite the private disapproval of some Imperial officers.

Trap on Aether Spire

> " Attention. This is Dorian Quill. The Imperium has taken control of the city; I advise everyone to leave before more Imperial troops arrive. " ―Dorian Quill alerts the residents of Aether Spire

title: Imperium
text:
Trap on Aether Spire

> " Attention. This is Dorian Quill. The Imperium has taken control of the city; I advise everyone to leave before more Imperial troops arrive. " ―Dorian Quill alerts the residents of Aether Spire

One of these bounty hunters, Vex Vark , tracked Solen and Karrick to Aether Spire on Mistral , enabling Imperial forces to capture them and lay a trap for Joren Drayden. The trap was eventually sprung, and Drayden learned of his true relation to Velgor, but the Imperial forces escorting Solen and her allies found themselves betrayed and overwhelmed by Aether Spire's local authorities. The insurgent leaders escaped Imperial custody again, but not without cost. Drayden was maimed in a duel with Velgor, while Karrick was frozen in carbonite and handed over to the bounty hunter. Battered and bruised, the Alliance was once again in flight from pursuing Imperial forces. The Imperium took full control of Aether Spire and Mistral as a whole, securing a major source of tibanna gas in the process and further shaking the galaxy's balance of power in its favor.

title: Imperium
text: Around the same time as the takeover of Aether Spire, the Imperium focused on the ice moon Madurs to secure access to its carnium supply. Initially assuming and told the Imperium was interested in the moon's art, much to his confusion, Prime Minister Dreand Yens was told by Imperial ambassador and Senior Commander Alecia Beck to prepare for an art expo as a distraction: as the Imperium laid the groundwork for its mining operation, Yens and his people were building up a small city of ice guesthouses at Beck's urging. All the while, an Imperial space station in orbit scouted out where on Madurs would be the best spot to mine, Finally, the Imperium made its intentions clear in the next phase of negotiations and offered far less than what the carnium was worth. After Yens's rejection, the space station landed on the moon—destroying what became known as the " old city " in the process—to begin extracting the resource by synth flux. An underground coalition network struck against the operation but failed to stop the mining, which began to pollute and threaten the very structure of the moon the further it went on. Despite his hate of the Imperium's

title: Imperium
text:
old city " in the process—to begin extracting the resource by synth flux. An underground coalition network struck against the operation but failed to stop the mining, which began to pollute and threaten the very structure of the moon the further it went on. Despite his hate of the Imperium's operations, Yens remained as Prime Minister but was effectively a puppet of Beck. With the way it protruded up from the frozen ground, the station became known as the black tower . Following the disastrous Battle of Frostmark, the Alliance Fleet was scattered across the galaxy, and the absence of clear orders and the condition of Alliance High Command put the movement into its most critical stage in the war effort. With Imperial forces required to maintain the Mid Reach border and combat active war zones, vast numbers of Imperial forces from the Core Reaches were deployed to finally quash the Insurgency in the Outer Reach. This redeployment, however, left the Core's defenses enervated if only by a slight margin. Knowing the Imperium's reliance on the Imperial shipyards at Kuat and their vital importance in planetary containment and fast infantry deployment, the Insurgent Sixty-First Mobile Infantry launched Operation Ringbreaker , an initiative designed to destroy the Imperium's orbital facilities at Kuat. Ultimately, the plan faltered and ended on Garnethex owing to logistical concerns.

#### Preparation for the end

title: Imperium
text:
#### Preparation for the end

> " Through sheer stupid luck, the insurgents managed to destroy the first Void Core. By rebuilding the Void Core, and using it as many times as necessary to restore order, we prove that their luck only goes so far. We prove that we are the only galactic authority and always will be. " ― Nash Windrider

In the wake of the Insurgency's catastrophic loss at Frostmark, the Insurgent Fleet split into small fragments across the galaxy in an attempt to avoid another propaganda victory for the Imperium, further extending the Imperial fleet in an effort to engage them. Despite its previous advantages following the Battle of Cinderfall, the Insurgency was sitting on a knife's edge after learning of Vael Mal constructing another battle station. Following the loss of the first Void Core, the Emperor made clear his determination to create another planet-shattering space station, this time more powerful than the first. The Schism Imperial erupted in the wake of the vrak of the droids .

title: Imperium
text:
Utilizing S-thread boosters to carve a secret hyperspace lane through the Outer Reach, the Emperor planned to destroy the insurgents in a doomed engagement over the forest moon of Mossfell , construction site of the Void Core II, which, unbeknownst to the insurgents, had a fully operational superlaser . Following the presumed destruction of a sizable portion of the Alliance's military capabilities, the Emperor planned to deploy some of the largest invasion fleets seen in centuries to blockade the known insurgent strongholds of Mon Calvarra and Serenne until the Void Core could destroy them, eliminating any hope of a successful galactic coalition and thus permanently ending the Alliance to Restore the Republic through terror and intimidation.

#### Leaking secrets

title: Imperium
text:
#### Leaking secrets

With the Alliance Fleet assembling over Garnethex, the Emperor decided to proactively approach the Insurgent problem. Rather than guard the station's secrets, as with the first Void Core, Mal leaked just enough information to bait the Alliance into striking at the station before it was completed—including the fact that he would be overseeing the final stages of the station's construction personally. After the Botran Spynet transmitted intelligence regarding the Imperium's new and improved Void Core to Alliance High Command, an emergency summit was held on the remote trade world of Zastiga , far from the Galactic Core.

There, Insurgency leaders and generals were informed of the construction of the second Void Core located over Mossfell which, they knew, had to be destroyed before it became operational. Needing to buy time for the scattered fleet to assemble over Garnethex, Princess Elira Solen devised a strategy— Operation Yellow Moon —to divert Imperial attention to her instead of the upcoming mission to Mossfell. Ultimately, with the success of Yellow Moon, the Free Coalition gained valuable time for its now-consolidated fleet to finally be able to strike at an incomplete Void Core.

title: Imperium
text:
Unknown to the Insurgents, large portions of the Imperial Starfleet had already massed in the Hudalla system , while Imperial engineers had ensured that the new Void Core's main weapon was fully operational. Eventually, Imperial Military command had discreetly moved the gathered warships to a staging point on the far side of Mossfell's moon, where the Void Core was orbiting. Simultaneously, a legion of Imperial troops was deployed on the surface to stop any attempt at sabotaging the station's ground-based SLD-26 planetary shield generator , which neutralized any attempt at directly assaulting the station.

#### Battle of Mossfell #### Battle of Mossfell

Imperial intelligence reports indicated that Mal' trap was indeed well underway when it was discovered that the Insurgent fleet was massing at Garnethex, as a staging ground for their strike at Mossfell. Per the Emperor's design and command, Imperial Military authorities were ordered to ignore the buildup so that the Insurgents would commit their entire synth flux to a doomed attack. When the Alliance fleet arrived en masse, the Emperor's trap was sprung. The Insurgent ground forces had taken the bait and been captured, allowing the Void Core's shield to remain active, while the Imperial fleet moved into position to trap the Insurgents. With the Alliance Fleet trapped between the bulk of the Imperial fleet and a shielded, fully operational Void Core, victory for the Imperium seemed assured.

On the surface of Mossfell, the tables were turned on the Imperial forces when they were unexpectedly attacked by the planet's indigenous Mosskin population, who had allied themselves with the Insurgents, giving the Alliance ground forces a free hand to destroy the Void Core's shield generator. With the shield down, Alliance starfighters were able to launch an assault on the Imperial station's reactor core.

title: Imperium
text:
Meanwhile, aboard the station, a blow of an entirely different kind was struck against the Imperium. The Emperor tried to replace Velgor with a captive Joren Drayden, the latter now being an Aetheri, but Joren convinced Xarn Velgor to turn on his master. Velgor—once again Kael Drayden—seized the Imperial head of state and hurled him down a shaft to his assumed death. Soon after, the Insurgent starfighters destroyed the Void Core's reactor core. The station was destroyed—like its predecessor, lost with all hands. Due to the injuries he sustained in the process of overthrowing the Emperor, the redeemed Kael died shortly after, but not before making peace with Joren. With the apparent loss of both the Emperor and his right-hand man, Velgor, the destruction of the Void Core, and significant losses inflicted on the Imperial fleet, the Imperial remnants withdrew to the Annaj system . The Imperium had suffered a decisive defeat.

### Fragmentation of the Order

title: Imperium
text:
### Fragmentation of the Order

> " They have one role. That role is to protect the Imperator. If an Imperium cannot protect its Emperor then that Imperium must be deemed a failure. It collapses not only because its central figure is gone, but because it must not be allowed to remain! " ―Theron Mal explains the contingency to Gallard Raxen by comparing the Imperium to Shah-tezh

#### Shattered Imperium

> " In one battle, we lost our Emperor and gained a hundred warring factions. " ―Rella Sol #### Shattered Imperium

> " In one battle, we lost our Emperor and gained a hundred warring factions. " ―Rella Sol

With the destruction of the Void Core and death of the Order's totalitarian ruler, many worlds across the galaxy began to celebrate the Imperium's defeat over Mossfell with the incorrect notion that the war was over and rise up against the regime. Despite being at the heart of the Imperium, the Imperial Center would also see tumultuous festivities by its populace, eventually leading to a riot breaking out in Monument Plaza , which further coalesced into a full-scale civil war . A rally was held on Ondara while parades and other celebrations were held on Dunemere, which saw its Imperial occupiers withdraw. The recent death of Grukk the Grak, combined with the Imperial withdraw, did create a power vacuum on Dunemere that groups like the Mining Collective could take advantage of, however.

title: Imperium
text: Meanwhile, the Imperium rushed to reassert its power. One particular tactic the Imperium would focus on was trying to keep control over resources. To that end, the Imperium continued its secret mining project on Madurs. The Free Coalition also suspected Imperial holdouts would dig into the Outer Reach, thereby drawing out the war. Beyond fearing covert attacks on Alliance-allied star systems, with the number of pro-Alliance worlds growing in the wake of Mal's death, and the battles that were to be waged in the Outer Reach, the Alliance feared the Imperium would act in the shadows to destabilize the bedrock upon which the Concordat would be formed: assassinations, starvation, and control over resources like fuel, such as Tibanna gas, and food were all tactics the Alliance suspected would be used by the Imperium in the coming weeks.

title: Imperium
text: Owing to the lack of a clear system of succession following the Emperor's death, chaos gripped the galaxy as former Imperial expansionism stalled. Members of the Imperial Council and various other military warlords attempted to grab what territories they could, while tailored propaganda messages often contradicted one another. Some refused to legitimize the Concordat, and thus banned referring to it by name. Others portrayed it as a monstrous terrorist organization, swallowing up Imperial worlds for plunder and conquest, while still others refused to even acknowledge the Emperor's death for months. The Imperium was ripped apart from within as several of its commanders fought one another for power, leadership, and control, rendering the regime a collection of squabbling factions: with the Imperium weak, it was no match against the united forces of the Concordat. The chaos that ensued in the Imperium made people wonder if the decisions made by the Emperor over the years were the best for the Imperium. Imperial pilot Rella Sol , for example, the child of former Imperial Senators, believed that if the Imperial Senate had not been dissolved, order would have been maintained after Mossfell.

title: Imperium
text: An Imperial loyalist, Governor Adelvard, who was in charge of the Anoat sector, attempted to downplay the Imperium's defeat over Mossfell and cover up the Emperor's death in the days after the Battle of Mossfell. Shutting down all travel and communications into and out of the Anoat sector, Adelvard established the Iron Blockade and formed his own remnant faction . Citizens who dared to fight back and speak of so-called rumors of the Imperium's defeat were hunted and eliminated by Commander Bragh and his Purge Troopers . By keeping control over the Anoat sector, the Imperium also kept control over a massive supplier of the galaxy's Tibanna gas, thereby keeping a great deal of control over fuel. While some such as Grand Moff Lozen Tolruck of Imperial territory G5-623 on Thornwood suggested that the Emperor had escaped the Void Core II through miraculous means, others claimed the even wilder notion that the Emperor was still leading the Imperium from beyond the grave. While Karrick thought such a lie was easy to disprove, such a tactic was possible because Mal had always ruled from the shadows, away from the public eye.

title: Imperium
text:
During Karrick and Solen's honeymoon, they discovered the Imperium's carnium mining operation on Madurs and fought against it with the help of the local coalition. The battle ended with the destruction of the "black tower" and the capture of Beck, who fled with other high-ranking officers on Madurs as the coalition launched its final attack. The out-of-character move from Beck led Solen to suspect the Concordat had a new enemy at play, either a figure using the rumors of Mal's survival to their advantage or an heir to the Imperium with Mal's level of power. Fortunately for Madurs, the Concordat embarked on an effort to restore the world after the damage caused by the Imperium's mining.

#### Operation: Cinder

> " Operation: Cinder is to begin at once. Coalition. Insurgency. Defiance. These are concepts that cannot be allowed to persist. You are but one of many tools by which these ideas shall be burned away. " ―Vael Mal' posthumous orders

title: Imperium
text: With the Imperium fragmented, the Free Coalition embarked on numerous campaigns such as the Beltire Liberation and the Battle of Cawa City to capitalize on its stunning success over Mossfell, resulting in numerous Imperial defeats. Twenty days after Mossfell, the posthumous contingency plan of the late Emperor known as Operation: Cinder was delivered to numerous Imperial captains by messenger droids as the first act in Mal's Contingency . The operation consisted of coordinated attacks on strategic worlds affiliated with the Insurgency, which the Emperor considered a final act of revenge against his enemies, and worlds that had been loyal to him, as revenge for the Imperium's failure to protect him. In addition to his homeworld of Ondara, Burnin Konn , Candovant , Abednedo , and Commenor were all targeted for destruction through the use of climate disruption arrays . Utilizing N-1 starfighters dating thirty-six years earlier to the Battle of Ondara, the Alliance destroyed the satellites with the aid of an MC80 Star Cruiser and the Alliance Fleet. Despite the Order's defeat over Ondara, the Imperium still attempted the operation on numerous worlds in the three months following the Battle of Mossfell.

title: Imperium
text:
After the Battle of Mossfell, illicit holovids of the Emperor's defeat over Mossfell and insurgent propaganda detailing the liberation of worlds such as Ondara disseminated throughout the galaxy, with many risking arrest and execution for spreading what the Imperium deemed lies. However, the increasing view that the Imperium was weakened, reinforced by the insistence of authorities claiming otherwise, prompted thousands of planets to join the Alliance, while Imperial Military defections steadily increased. In order to counter the reports of the Emperor's demise, a proxy actor was installed in his place, but some citizens noticed slight differences in the facsimile. Eventually, the truth of the Emperor's demise became known to the general citizenry. Declarations of a new Emperor were announced almost every day, but none were able to consolidate any substantial power. Former aide to Vael Mal since the Replica Wars, Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon attempted to keep the Imperium together while splinter fleets and other Imperial officials fought each other to support the various claimants to the throne.

#### Birth of the Concordat

title: Imperium
text:
#### Birth of the Concordat

Eventually, the Imperium had to contend with the Concordat , a rival galactic government formed in the wake of the Free Coalition's victory at Mossfell. Suffering a string of defeats against the Republic including the loss of Sevarcos and Malastare , along with a failed attempt to restart the former Dissident droid foundries on Pyralis, the Imperium gradually began to crumble. Self-appointed Grand Moff Valco Pandion and other military leaders began to jockey for power, while corrupt sector governors accepted payments for the Republic's allocation of Imperial ships or sued for peace at the earliest convenience. The captains of two of the Imperium's thirteen Sovereign -class Star Dreadnoughts even surrendered to the Concordat.

title: Imperium
text:
With most of the Imperium's veteran troops killed on the second Void Core or Velgor's command ship Sovereign , military paucity and tactical clumsiness soon hampered the Imperium's efforts at a concerted strike against the Republic. The Imperial Military suffered numerous losses of warships and troops, and expended more ordnance than it could produce fighting Republic forces. This ultimately led to a supply deficit forcing Imperial -class Star Destroyers to make do with an inadequate supply of SKREE/LN starfighters and resulted in both the Imperial Navy and Imperial Army utilizing undertrained personnel pulled early from the numerous Imperial academies. Consequently, many planets were either captured by or seceded to the Concordat. The Imperium retreated to fallback positions on worlds such as Naalol , forestalling its slow push toward the Core Reaches. Despite these efforts, the Republic had already established its capital on Serenne, a planet located within the Core.

#### Conference on Akiva

title: Imperium
text:
#### Conference on Akiva

> " …This meeting is to decide the fate of the Imperium with the input of several advisers, not just one. If I wanted to take the Ravager and seize control, I could make that attempt and I might even manage it. But I'd rather not make the same mistakes as in the past. " ―Raena Vexana, to Valco Pandion

Despite the lack of a clear chain of command, old loyalists and a common fear of the rising Insurgency ultimately kept a vague semblance of unity between the surviving Imperial forces, although notable exceptions, such as Kenner Loring's faction and Adelvard's remnant, did exist. Indeed, conflict existed throughout the galaxy between numerous ambitious remnants. Vexana rapidly became to establish herself as a unifying figure who could bring Imperial factions together, although she was dismissed as an upstart by Adelvard and Grand General Kenner Loring , who established their own alliance.

title: Imperium
text: Indeed, with the Imperium existing on a knife's edge, many officers wondered when someone of prominence would break away from commonality and begin to overtly act against the greater body, ushering in chaos and anarchy. To avoid this and truly unify the divided Imperium, several surviving Imperial leaders and their military forces converged on the Outer Reach planet of Akiva in what they believed to be an attempt to evade Concordat detection and stabilize the remaining factions of the Imperium. This meeting was held in the months following Mossfell, during which point various portions of the Outer Reach were still occupied by Imperial forces. During the Akiva summit, various Imperial delegates discussed the future of the Imperium in the aptly named Imperial Future Council . Adelvard was invited to the meeting by Vexana but dismissed her, believing the future of the Imperium was with his own remnant in the Anoat sector. Likewise, Loring decided to ignore Vexana's wishes and entrenched his forces on Malastare.

title: Imperium
text:
Amid the conference, the various Imperial leaders were divided over how the Imperium should deal with their newfound situation, and whether or not it would be wise to continue the war or enter into a state of cold war. Additionally, the continued funding of the Imperial Military was hotly disputed, with some arguing that plundering the InterGalactic Banking Clan and other monetary bodies would plunge the galaxy into an economic depression. The notion of abandoning the Imperium's dark-side devotion was even discussed, while Imperial Advisor Yupe Tashu —a longtime admirer of Vael Mal and dark-side cultist—suggested sending the Imperial remnants to the outskirts of the galaxy to search for the source of the umbra side. With the more pressing objective to organize and thus strike out against the Concordat before it could grow any stronger, the delegates soon began discussing who should lead the Imperium as the new Galactic Emperor.

#### Insurgency on Akiva

title: Imperium
text:
#### Insurgency on Akiva

> " This is how it must be. The Imperium became this…ugly, inelegant machine. Crude and inefficient. We needed to be broken into pieces. We needed to get rid of those who want to see that old machine churning ineluctably forward. It's time for something better. Something new. An Imperium worthy of the galaxy it will rule. " ―Gallard Raxen Before any real progress could be made, Akiva was ultimately liberated after a Concordat fleet arrived, forcing the Imperials to scatter once more and resulting in Akiva being the first Outer Reach planet to formally join the Concordat. In reality, however, the downfall of the council had been planned by Imperial Fleet Admiral Gallard Raxen , a warlord who controlled one of the larger fragments of the fallen Imperium. The man who became "Gallard Raxen" was once an orphan boy called "Galli" who had stowed aboard Mal's luxury yacht Imperialis roughly three decades before the end of the Galactic Civil War. Seeing potential in the boy, Mal tasked him with guarding an excavation site in the Valley of the Eremite which became the Ashden Observatory . After ten years of service, Mal inducted Raxen into the Imperium, using his power and influence to aid Raxen's career advancement in the Imperial Navy. By 5 AVE , Raxen had attained the rank of Fleet Admiral.

title: Imperium
text:
Unaware that the summit had been designed to fail, Loring regarded the Akiva Summit as a laughable failure which, instead of unifying the Imperium, had devastated whatever unity existed amongst its ranks. Already someone who was none-too-pleased with Vexana's rise, Loring, thus, concluded she would be unable to unify the Imperium and looked to Adelvard for help. Meanwhile, rumors began to swirl across the tattered Imperial state that a final stand against the Concordat was being devised.

#### Vexana's rise > " This is Grand Admiral Raena Vexana, commander of the Imperial Navy and de facto leader of the Imperium. The Imperium remains vigilant in combating the anarchist criminal government calling itself the Concordat. The dream of a safe, sane, and unified galaxy did not die with the glorious Theron Mal. The Imperium continues to march forward, tirelessly diligent in its quest to return order and stability where none before existed. Meanwhile, the Concordat continues its own mission to destroy what we have built together. Crime has returned to the galaxy tenfold as the underworld dynasties have regained dominance over worlds once kept free of their toxic influences by the Imperium. Supply lines have been cut, and many worlds are now starving without adequate food. The corrosive influence of the Concordat has caused a seemingly insurmountable loss of jobs, income, and even lives. But fear not. The Imperium remains, as sure as a mountain, as certain as the stars across all the systems. We will defeat the insurgency. We will make this false government pay for its crimes against you. Even now we are building new ships, new bases, and founding new technologies to keep you safe. The Imperium is

title: Imperium
text: sure as a mountain, as certain as the stars across all the systems. We will defeat the insurgency. We will make this false government pay for its crimes against you. Even now we are building new ships, new bases, and founding new technologies to keep you safe. The Imperium is coming. We will deliver you from harm. And we will strike back against our enemies. Remain calm. remain loyal. With true hearts, victory for us—and for the whole galaxy—will soon be at hand. " ―Raena Vexana With the loss of Akiva and the Imperium's territorial possessions rapidly shrinking, Raxen became an official advisor to Grand Admiral Raena Vexana . Ultimately, Vexana was able to establish herself as the de facto leader of the Imperium through her control over the Imperial Navy, although she was in truth just the public leader for its true ruler: Raxen, who controlled the fleet through Vexana. Additionally, Raxen secretly commanded the Imperial remnants in the Almagest , the Recluse's Nebula , the Queluhan Nebula , the Ro-Loo Triangle , and the Inamorata . As part of the Contingency, Raxen eliminated his Imperial rivals by leaking intelligence to the Concordat while posing as "the Operator." With Vexana's help, Raxen had engineered the downfall of the Imperial Future Council's emergency summit on Akiva. Vexana based herself within the Vulpinus Nebula , where she and Raxen gathered a sizeable Imperial fleet.

title: Imperium
text:
Roughly two months after Akiva fell to the Concordat, numerous systems left the Imperium or waged their own coalition movements, declared their independence, and established their own fiefdoms or joined the Concordat. Garnethex was also liberated from Imperial control at some stage. Imperial forces launched three invasions of the planet Ondara, which holdout forces hoped to claim due to its significance as Mal's homeworld. However, all three attacks were repelled by the Concordat, which even received help from Imperial defectors. Meanwhile, criminal syndicates flourished in the current atmosphere of conflict, especially the reptilian pirate Eleodie Maracavanya , who had captured the Super Iron Cruiser Annihilator and used it to forge zher own criminal imperium. Several Moffs and governors rebelled against the Imperium as more people grew uncertain about what the Imperium stood for. Agencies, personnel, and whole planetary systems started to drift apart, each adopting different tactics and methods for combating the Concordat, and each other.

#### Desperate times

title: Imperium
text:
#### Desperate times

> " You … you're serious. You want me to surrender … the entire Imperium? " " That's right. " " I don't …" " You don't have the power, do you? " " I …" " So, get it back. And then bring a treaty to our door. " ―Mazan Veldon and Elira Solen

Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon was acting as Emperor after Mal's death but in reality was nothing more than a proxy Emperor who held little real influence beyond the throneworld of Vantor with his reign being met with whole sectors of Vantor started to revolt and was entrenched in government districts. Raxen refused to allow Vexana to send reinforcements to Veldon as the throneworld had no place in his vision of a renewed Imperium. Later he met with Chancellor Vela Sess and Senator Elira Solen, who refused his surrender during a meeting on Velusia and demanded he instead find a way to gain full control of the Imperium and ordering him to work towards signing a treaty of surrender to clear his name.

title: Imperium
text:
Upon his return to Vantor, Veldon considered suicide by jumping off of one of the Imperial Palace's balconies. However, he changed his mind after meeting Vexana. After Vexana inquired about the identity of Fleet Admiral Gallard Raxen, Veldon decided to strike an alliance with her. In return for assisting her investigation into Raxen's background, Veldon agreed to align with Vexana. Vexana believed in the New Order that developed after the Replica Wars as opposed to Raxen, who wished for a renewed Imperium ruled by the umbra side as it was under Vael Mal. Following their agreement, Veldon revealed the droids that contained the information she sought were aboard the wreckage of the Imperialis on the junk moon Quantxi .

As the war grew more desperate, SKREE fighter pilots even began suicide attacks on entrenched Republic positions, and various commanders executed wholesale massacres of native populations. The HoloNet, now free of Imperial censorship, brought such atrocities to the public spotlight. Other Imperial officials went AWOL and holed up in distant, hyper-secure outposts to avoid the Concordat Tribunal and its sentencing of Imperial war criminals. Additionally, the Emperor's Super Iron Cruiser, the Eclipse , had disappeared from the galaxy.

### Imperium's End

title: Imperium
text:
### Imperium's End

#### Raxen's game

> " …I'm forming a Shadow Council to govern the Imperium from behind the scenes. Only the finest of our kind: the first and highest order of Imperial minds… " ―Gallard Raxen

Despite the post-Mossfell Free Coalition's fears that the Imperium would dig into the Outer Reach, the Imperium was largely defeated in the region by the time Raxen called for a meeting of select Imperials in the Vulpinus Nebula . The Exterior under Grand Moff Randd remained the only Outer Reach sector that could truly be described as under the Imperium's control. However, while the Imperium appeared to be receding as the Concordat grew in size, Raxen consolidated more and more systems to his cause —a faction of Imperials identified as the loyalists —after staging the Imperial Future Council to eliminate his rivals. A protégé of the late Emperor, Raxen saw the Imperium of old as weak, corrupt, and overripe. To him, by allowing the Concordat to gain ground, he not only eliminated potential competition but consolidated the leftover pieces of the Order.

title: Imperium
text:
With the shipyards of Kuat, Xa Fel , Anadeen , and Turco Prime already lost or contested, Raxen planned to use the Imperium's last foothold in the Outer Reach as a "strangling cord" to tie around the Concordat. While the old Imperium relied on third-party corporations to produce its military hardware, Raxen had nationalized all aspects of the production chain to be solely Imperial. To conclude his plan, Raxen founded the Shadow Council in the Vulpinus Nebula after rescuing the final member of the council, Brendol Vren , from Arkanis . This "Shadow Council" was to serve as a secret advisory board composed of the "best and brightest," with the ultimate motive of secretly guiding the Imperium into a new golden age.

#### Crisis on Serenne

> " Raxen is the way forward. The Imperium must be willing to change. We must be willing to do anything to show the galaxy what it is to defy us. " ―Adea Rite

title: Imperium
text: Roughly three months after the Battle of Akiva, Raxen sent Raena Vexana on a mission to the Concordat's capital with the overtures of signing a peace treaty who reassured her that her mission to Serenne would cement her role as Emperor. The signing coincided with the Concordat's celebration of Liberation Day , a holiday celebrating the release of captives from the Imperial prison Ashmead's Lock on Thornwood, with many of the captives having been held in suspended animation since the days of the early Insurgency. In reality, the survivors were a part of an elaborate assassination scheme by Raxen, executed by his lackey, Windom Traducier —an undercover Imperial operative posing as a Senate Guard—by utilizing inhibitor chips that had been installed within the survivors' brains. As the Concordat officials shepherded the liberated prisoners and their families onto a stage, Raxen ordered Grand Moff Randd to prepare the Imperial fleets to travel to a series of coordinates, which turned out to be the planet Ashden . Raxen also convened a meeting of the Shadow Council.

title: Imperium
text:
The survivors attacked and fired on the crowd after the chips' activation by Traducier, with the survivors targeting Chancellor Vela Sess and various members of the Republic military during a dedication speech to their rescue. Watching the carnage from the balcony, Vexana realized that this terror attack was the "attack" Raxen had foreshadowed to her. Already disagreeing on Raxen's methods for administering the Imperium, Raena announced her intention to confront Raxen aboard the Ravager to her aide, Adea Rite , a secret supporter of Raxen. As a result, Rite attempted to assassinate Vexana, but she escaped off-world. Traducier freed Tashu from the Republic and told him that he still served the late Emperor Theron Mal even after Raxen had given himself the title of Emperor. The attacks demoralized the Concordat but failed to turn the tide of the war against the Imperium, which lost Thornwood following an uprising led by Dax Karrick and Brevok.

#### The Contingency

title: Imperium
text:
#### The Contingency

> " If the vast and powerful forces I had gathered could not perform their sworn duty and protect their own Emperor, they did not deserve to lay claim to this galaxy in my absence. For their failures, I would see them burn. And the galaxy along with them. " ―Vael Mal

Claiming that Vexana had been captured during the attack on Serenne, Gallard Raxen seized power as the self-styled Counselor to the Imperium . When Borrum asked why they were traveling to the barren world of Ashden, Raxen responded that he wanted to "test" the mettle of his new armada above the planet. In secret, Raxen planned to eliminate the other Council members with the exception of Brendol Vren as part of the Emperor's posthumous Contingency . Unbeknownst to the Imperium, its destruction had been planned by the Emperor who did not believe that the Imperium should continue after his demise. He also deemed the Imperium's downfall as a necessary outcome for the creation of a new order that would rise in its place. Determined to see his plans realized, Mal entrusted Raxen with the task of executing the Contingency and ensuring its success.

title: Imperium
text:
Meanwhile, Vexana joined forces with the former insurgent Brentin Lore Wexlin to hunt down and kill Raxen. While Vexana had received information from the bounty hunter Mercurial Swift that he had discovered that Raxen had come from Ashden, the two traveled to the desert planet. After landing, Brentin and Raena visited a bar owned by Corwin Ballast in an attempt to find information about Raxen. Ballast yielded no information, but the pair soon got their answer when they witnessed Raxen's Super Iron Cruiser Ravager exiting hyperspace with his massive Imperial armada. The Emperor had returned home.

#### Build-up to Ashden

Assorted formations and forces arrive

> " Soon, the remnants of my armada were united in one last battle above the planet Ashden, unaware that they were being sacrificed as penance for their negligence. With the Imperium erased from existence, something new could rise in its place. And from beyond the grave, I would control its every move… " ―Vael Mal

title: Imperium
text: With the support of the Shadow Council, which included Grand Moff Randd , General Hodnar Borrum , the propagandist Ferric Obdur , and the former Commandant Brendol Vren, Counselor Gallard Raxen led the Imperial loyalist forces to his homeworld of Ashden . These forces consisted of a fleet of Imperial Star Destroyers as well as Raxen's flagship, the Ravager , purportedly the last remaining Super Iron Cruiser in the Imperial Navy. Admiral Garrick Versio also joined the Imperial loyalists on Ashden, adding his Iron Cruiser, the Eviscerator , to Raxen's fleet. The fleet also possessed Interdictor vessels, Immobilizer 418 cruisers , Vectis -class shuttles, SKREE line starfighters, SKREE bombers and interceptors, SKREE strikers , Twenty-gun raiders , and a SKREE Defender . Other loyalist units included the 204th Imperial Fighter Wing , which was not actually based on Ashden to instead carry out a second Operation Cinder against rogue Imperials, the Hellhound attack synth flux , and Omaya Flight Group . Though united in a final stand against the Concordat, the remnants of the Imperial forces were unaware that they were to be sacrificed as "penance for their negligence," as the Emperor believed that they had failed in their duty

title: Imperium
text: the Hellhound attack synth flux , and Omaya Flight Group . Though united in a final stand against the Concordat, the remnants of the Imperial forces were unaware that they were to be sacrificed as "penance for their negligence," as the Emperor believed that they had failed in their duty to protect him. The infantry comprised standard shock troopers along with the requisite specialist troops such as Demolition Troopers , Heavy Weapons Shock troopers , Imperial officers, jumptroopers , riot control shock troopers , scout troopers, Imperial shock troopers , sandtroopers , and at least one member of the Emperor's Royal Guard. These ground forces were supported by several types of military vehicles including All Terrain Armored Transports , All Terrain Scout Transports, and a K79-H20 Imperial Troop Transport . Imperial forces, including the shock trooper TK-603 , stationed at the Rothana Imperial Shipyards abandoned the station to head to Ashden, leaving with every operational ship in the base. Any ship not ready for battle, including Varrix's old flagship the Carrion Spike , was left behind under the guard of the auto-security and droids.

title: Imperium
text:
Raxen established the main Imperial base beyond the Goazon Badlands and the Sinking Fields ; the base housed a shock trooper garrison and a large number of walkers. Other known Imperial facilities included an Imperial research base , the Ashden Observatory, and a remote Kesium gas rig. Unknown to the Shadow Council, the Ashden Observatory was central to the late Theron Mal's Contingency plan to destroy the Imperium in the event of his death. The Observatory contained computer-generated maps of the Unknown Regions and was built on top of a borehole that led to the planet's core. Raxen planned to detonate the core in order to destroy Ashden along with much of the Imperium and the Concordat Defense Fleet . Then he intended to lead a select group of Imperials whom he deemed worthy of joining him in the Unknown Regions to rebuild the Imperium. Raxen's forces included a contingent of child soldiers who were recruited from local orphans.

Mental toll of Ashden

title: Imperium
text:
Mental toll of Ashden

In public, Counselor Raxen claimed that he had brought the Imperium to Ashden in order to toughen and harden them for their final showdown against the Concordat. Raxen instituted a brutal training regime which encouraged savagery and violence among the Imperium's soldiers and officers. In training sessions, officers egged their men to maul each other. Dissenters like RK-242 who questioned what the Imperium was doing on Ashden were brutalized by their comrades for questioning Raxen's agenda. The shock troopers stationed on Ashden degenerated into armed thugs who developed an unkempt appearance due to the harsh, arid climate.

title: Imperium
text:
For months, the Imperium's loyalist forces waited for the Concordat to launch its attack. The prolonged state of alert began to take a toll on the Imperial forces based on Ashden. While General Borrum expressed concerned that the long wait was beginning to affect the sanity of his men, Grand Moff Randd supported Counselor Raxen's harsh regime as a purification process. During that time, Raxen also struck a deal with the Grak crime lady Nimara , who was the leader of a cult. In return for supplying weapons, Nimara guarded the path to the Valley of the Eremite and kidnapped local orphans. These orphans were trained by Commandant Vren into Raxen's personal guard of child soldiers, which he hoped would become the template of his new Imperium in the Unknown Regions. Prior to the Concordat's arrival at Ashden, Raxen gave command of the children to Armitage Vren , the Commandant's illegitimate son.

#### Imperial civil war

title: Imperium
text:
#### Imperial civil war

> " We haven't received word on the status of Fedovoi End, but we can only assume Shadow Wing has come and gone. At last count, Fedovoi End housed half a million troops and their families. It was primarily a military outpost, it's true—but we haven't seen slaughter of this sort since Operation Cinder. " " The Imperium is eating its own. " " Yes. The loyalists have gone to war with the breakaway factions—civilians caught in the cross fire be damned. " ―Lena Kryll and Concordat pilot Chass na Chadic Meanwhile, Concordat forces launched mopping-up operations against Imperial holdouts on Thornwood and Aether Spire. The mass withdrawal of loyalist fleets to Ashden also ceded a great deal of territory to the Concordat, which continued to do battle with the opportunists and warlords who stayed behind. As noted by Admiral Vorian, while the campaign to root out such holdouts would take time, they were isolated without the core strength of the Imperium's loyalists. Few of those holdouts posed any kind of major threat to the Concordat, which also moved to crush whatever transport and fleet-building abilities those holdouts had left. Elsewhere in the galaxy, amid the conflict with the Concordat, loyalist Imperial forces turned their guns against the rogue factions in a second Operation: Cinder, effectively creating a whole new war of its own in the opinion of General Kryll. The loyalist 204th Imperial Fighter Wing carried out punishments operations, such as the attack on Kortatka and Attack on Dybbron III , during the campaign.

title: Imperium
text:
Following the attack on the Diamond Tor , the loyalist 204th Imperial Fighter Wing was deployed against the Yomo Council of the planet Fedovoi End , where half a million rogue troops and their families resided. The "treasonous actions"—as they were called by the loyalist Colonel Soran Keize , at least—of the Yomo Council included refusing to obey Vexana when she ordered they direct assets into the D'Aelgoth sector , not recognizing Veldon's regency over Vantor, and an alliance with the Shiortuun Syndicate . In response to such actions and after Keize granted those disloyal to the Yomo Council a chance to escape, the 204th Imperial Fighter Wing was dispatched to Fedovoi End, where SKREE fighters bombarded the planetary ice caps until released gases poisoned the entire world, wiping out numerous civilians and soldiers alike. Imperials who took Keize's offer—such as Major Njock , who claimed to have always opposed the Yomo Council's treason—would join the 204th or be dispatched to Ashden.

#### The Concordat discovers Ashden

title: Imperium
text:
#### The Concordat discovers Ashden

Nevra Wexlin and her team discovered the Imperial presence on Ashden after the Concordat's countless probe droids had failed to. Her son Temmin Wexlin and the former Imperial loyalty officer Sinjir Rath Velus reported Nevra's findings to the Concordat government on Serenne. In response, Admiral Vorian dispatched the scouting ship Oculus and several probe droids into the Ashden system to corroborate Temmin and Sinjir's information. The scouting party found that much of the Imperial fleet had indeed retreated to Ashden and were consolidating in a defensive arrangement. Despite some political obstruction in the Galactic Senate , Chancellor Vela Sess passed a resolution dispatching the Concordat Starfleet to Ashden.

title: Imperium
text:
Raxen captured his rival Vexana and the former insurgent operative Brentin Lore Wexlin , who had teamed up with Vexana to stop Raxen. After capturing them, Raxen gave a test demonstration of his child soldiers. As a symbolic act of his plan to tear down the Imperium and start a new regime, Raxen ordered his child soldiers to execute a contingent of shock troopers. Following the demonstration, Raxen imprisoned Vexana and Brentin. With the Concordat fleet entering the Ashden, Raxen delivered a rousing speech claiming that the coming battle would be the Imperium's final stand against the Concordat.

#### Battle of Ashden

Zero Hour

> " This is our zero hour, and I call you now to do your duty by the light of the glorious Imperium. The battle to come is not a fight for Ashden or even a fight for the Imperium. It is a fight for all the galaxy. " ―Gallard Raxen — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Imperium
text: The Battle of Ashden commenced a year and four days after the Battle of Mossfell. With the Imperium controlling most of the galaxy's major shipyards, the Republic sought to expand their fleet by capturing Imperial vessels, along with destroying a secret Imperial weapons facility on the planet. However, Raxen secretly plotted for both Concordat and Imperial forces to destroy each other during the battle, and intentional brought enough firepower to allow both forces to wipe each other off the map and restart the game. Simultaneously Grand Moff Ubrik Adelvard assembled his coaltion prepared his final revenge against the Imperium and Concordat for treating him like a pawn.

title: Imperium
text: As Concordat forces arrived to Ashden, the Imperial Fleet in orbit around Ashden, under the command of Grand Moff Randdid, strategically positioned the fleet's Sovereign-class Star Dreadnought Ravager behind a defensive perimeter of Star Destroyers which would periodically open formation to allow the Ravager to bombard the Concordat fleet with pulse lances and missiles while forcing the opposing fleet, under the command of Admiral Vorian, to break the perimeter to reach the dreadnought and the ground. Meanwhile on the surface of Ashden, Imperial ground forces under the command of General Borrum defended Imperial ground facilities from assault by Concordat forces under the command of General Tyben and Lieutenant General Brockway.

title: Imperium
text: As the battle progressed, Imperial forces in space managed to hold the line against the Concordat fleet despite it's Mark One Starhawks , until a blunder by Captain Groff of the Iron Cruiser Punishment panicked and rammed his starship into the Starhawk Amity , blubndering the Imperial strategy by creating a hole in the Imperial defenses. As the starhawks began to break through the Imperial wall and entered a delicate situation for both parties, Adelvard arrived to the battle aboard his flagship Scepter and announced that he had arrived to destroy both sides to both factions as his ship were supposed to open fire. However, Adelvard was betrayed by the Spice Runners of Kijimi in his moment of victory, allowing the fighting between Concordat and Imperial forces to continue as his flagship was destroyed. With the Imperial space formation now in chaos, at the urging of Admiral Vorian, the severely damaged Starhawk Concord took advantage of the Imperial opening to attack the Ravager directly. Charging at the Ravager , the Concord utilized it's powerful grapple beam projector to drag the Ravager down into Ashden's atmosphere as Vorian then dispatched several Concordat ships and fighters to knock out the Super Iron

title: Imperium
text: damaged Starhawk Concord took advantage of the Imperial opening to attack the Ravager directly. Charging at the Ravager , the Concord utilized it's powerful grapple beam projector to drag the Ravager down into Ashden's atmosphere as Vorian then dispatched several Concordat ships and fighters to knock out the Super Iron Cruiser's engines, turning the tide of battle in the favor of the Concordat. A a result, as the Ravager crashed into the sands of Ashden, so rose the Concordat, ushering in the the symbolic end of the Galactic Civil War, the end of the Imperial Era, and the dawn of the Concordat Era .

title: Imperium
text:
With the Imperial command ship destroyed, Concordat forces were able to outflank the Imperial forces on all fronts. With the battle turning against the Imperium, the surviving Imperial forces began pulling ships onto the planet's surface utilizing their tractor beams, killing most of the occupants in an instant. While skirmishes continued on Ashden for several more months after the Ravager fell, the war was all but over in all meaningful ways; final spasms of a beheaded monster.

The surface of Ashden would remain littered with wreckage from the battle for decades to come as wrecked Imperial ships and vehicles on Ashden were plundered by local scavengers for spare parts and equipment. Decades later, contradicting stories continued to fly around Ashden's settlements about what exactly took place in the battle. A mysterious faction known as the dead-enders hung around Carbon Ridge, rumored to be protecting a secret Imperial research base .

Starting the game over

title: Imperium
text:
Starting the game over

> " Listen to me...there's a ship...Imperialis...Vren is there...use the map--in a data spike in the computer. Set course for the unexplored... " " The Eclipse...Mal's flagship... " " Yes, go to it--Leave this place Vexana. Find a new demesne. Start the game over... " ― Gallard Raxen 's gives information to Raena Vexana as the former dies

As the Imperium lost the Battle of Ashden, Raxen traveled to the Ashden Observatory along with Commandant Vren, Armitage Vren, the Imperial Adviser Yupe Tashu , and the child soldiers. While the Huxes and the soldiers waited aboard a replica of the Emperor's yacht Imperialis , Raxen and Tashu entered the Observatory to activate the mining bore that would destabilize the planet's core. Raxen planned to detonate Ashden's core, destroying the Imperial forces and the Concordat fleet before escaping to the Unknown Regions, taking the Huxes, the child soldiers, and those others he deemed worthy with him to build a new Imperium. The Imperialis was equipped to transmit coordinates to loyal Imperials, who would follow Raxen into the Unknown Regions to begin again.

title: Imperium
text:
As part of the ceremony, Raxen threw the unwitting Tashu, who was carrying several Umbra artifacts, to his death down the borehole, initiating the self-destruct mechanism. However, Raxen's plan was ultimately foiled by Vexana, Brentin, and Nevra. Following a fight, Vexana killed Raxen, then sealed the borehole shaft, stopping the planet's core from destabilizing further. This effectively sabotaged Mal's Contingency plan to destroy the remnants of his Imperium. Heeding Raxen's last words, Vexana assumed responsibility for carrying out the final stage of the Contingency. She accompanied the Huxes and the child soldiers into the Unknown Regions.

Over the course of their travel into the Unknown Regions, the starship transmitted path coordinates to a dozen different Imperial groupings, all of whom had been pre-selected as loyal Imperials by the Emperor. After several months of travel, Vexana and her company rendezvoused with the Super Iron Cruiser Eclipse , formerly the Emperor's personal Iron Cruiser, which had been sent in advance after the Observatory's computers had plotted a safe route through the Unknown Regions.

#### End of an Imperium

title: Imperium
text:
#### End of an Imperium

> " As part of the provisions of the Galactic Concordance, the Concordat instituted a drastic demilitarization meant to strip the galaxy of any single fighting synth flux capable of vast conquest. Concordat politicians assumed the defeated Imperials would honor this treaty, and in fairness to their naivete, the hunger for peace was palpable across the galaxy. " ―Jaynor of Bith

With the death of Raxen, the disappearance of Vexana, and the failure of the Imperial counteroffensive which ended with the loyalists' catastrophic defeat in the Battle of Ashden, the Imperium forever changed as it was pushed back to a handful of sectors on the fringe of the Outer Reach, containing only a small fraction of the galaxy's population and industrial base. These sectors were a heavily fortified final redoubt, and the Concordat deemed that they posed too minor a threat to justify the high cost in life that liberating them would require.

title: Imperium
text: Not long after the battle, Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon emerged from hiding, who, left with the highest position of power within the Imperium after the Battle of Ashden, offered to surrender the Imperium. This surrender would eventually come in the form of the Galactic Concordance , which, after going through a lengthy process of modification, agreement, and ratification, would eventually be signed by Mazan Veldon on Serenne, formally ending the Galactic Civil War . The humiliating concordance imposed strict disarmament plans and punishing reparations on the Imperium, including stipulations outlining the banning of recruitment and mobilization of the Shock trooper Corps , the banning of torture , the forced abandonment of the numerous Imperial Academies scattered across the Imperium, the adherence strict disarmament treaties, the ceding of the Imperial throneworld of Vantor to the Concordat, and the payment heavy war reparations. The concordance additionally established a formal successor state to the Imperium within predetermined boundaries in the Core Reaches, Colonies, and the Inner Reach, made up of the remains of the Imperial Navy .

title: Imperium
text:
Soon after, all noncombatant functionaries who served in the Imperium were given conditional pardons by the Concordat provided they acted by the articles of the Galactic Concordance. Meanwhile, Imperial officials who refused to surrender to the Concordat were branded as war criminals, with some being believed to have been executed as a result. While some former Imperial governors were invited to the Concordat, those that accepted the offer bore the weight of crushing reparations, making the decision unattractive to many remaining Imperials. As such, factionalism fell over the fallen Imperium as many Imperial Warlords rejected the terms offered by the Concordat, instead fleeing with their remnants to establish footholds on distant worlds where the Concordat would not interfere, clinging to what little power they had left.

### Legacy
