#### Strangers in a familiar land

Official successor state

title: Imperium
text:
### Legacy

#### Strangers in a familiar land

Official successor state

As outlined in the Galactic Concordance, a new future for the Imperium was granted to remaining Imperial forces within a predetermined territory of the galaxy that included parts of the Core Reaches , Colonies , and the Inner Reach , containing many ancient and conservative worlds that had supported Mal including Commenor , Humbarine , Tinnel , Rendili , and Denon . As such, at the command of the Concordat, all Imperial forces and remnants that complied with the provisions of the concordance retreated within the new boundaries. However, the leadership of the Inner systems' Imperial remnant , made up of the various fragmented successors to the Imperium, quickly devolved into petty squabbles on all matters from relations with the Concordat to which Imperial legacies deserved preservation, which combined with the regulation and dismemberment of the once-mighty Imperial military-industrial complex, resulted in struggle to turn the faction into a viable state. As a result, the Inner systems' Imperial remnant disintegrated soon after its founding, leading to several of its key worlds joining the Concordat instead, the representatives and leaders of which went on to become leaders of the Centrists , a political party which advocated and pushed for a stronger central government and military.

A new demesne

> " It's time to start over. This is our new imperium. To begin again. And to get it right, this time. " " Yes, of course, Grand Admiral. Anything you need. Glory be to Grand Admiral Vexana. " " No. Glory goes only to the Imperium. " ―Raena Vexana and Brendol Vren became reluctant allies

title: Imperium
text: Having heeded Gallard Raxen 's final words, Grand Admiral Raena Vexana travelled across the Unknown Regions aboard the Imperialis alongside Brendol Vren , his son Armitage , and a group of orphans to rendezvous with the Sovereign-class Star Dreadnought Eclipse at a series of safe coordinates stored inside a dataspike given to her. During the journey that took several months and involved several hyperspace jumps through a maze of black holes and superstorms , Vexana feared that the orphans, given that they took orders only from Armitage, would attack her in her sleep. As such, she struck an accord with Armitage by promising to protect the younger Vren from his father if Vren told the orphans to leave her alone.

title: Imperium
text: Afterwards, Vexana confronted Brendol Vren about her killing of Raxen, revealing the counselor's bloody cape. In response, Brendol attempted to attack her, but Vexana beat him into submission and forced him to agree to obey her orders and to stop harming his son, additionally ordering that the officer to teach Armitage everything he knew about the Imperium, to which Vren agreed to by nodding his head. For the remainder of the trip, Vexana kept away from the children and bid her time studying its history, its flight time, its communication, and weapons, eventually discovering that the Imperialis had transmitted a set of path coordinates to a dozen different sources. Consulting the ship's sentinel droid, Vexana discovered that the path coordinates had been transmitted to other Imperials deemed loyal. During her solitude, Vexana also resolved that she would build a new Imperium that was not given to the backstabbing and incest of Mal's former Imperium which Raxen had destroyed. Additionally, she also found that the volt pistol wound in her abdomen had not fully healed.

title: Imperium
text: Eventually, the group arrived to and rendezvoused with the Eclipse , the former personal flagship of the Emperor , which had been sent ahead by Raxen and was parked at the edge of a geomagnetic storm. As the Imperialis made its final approach to the dreadnought Super Iron Cruiser , Vexana stated that their new imperium was start again, and to get it right that time around. In response, Vren agreed before announcing that glory was in order for the Grand Admiral, to which Vexana rejected, responding that glory was only to the Imperium. Eventually, the Eclipse rendezvoused with the forces that had jumped to the Unknown Regions from the Battle of Ashden, a group that included the self-appointed high colonel Enric Pryde . In the months that followed the Imperium's fall, as the fighting at Ashden continued when numerous Imperials refused to surrender, numerous captains eventually jumped from the lingering battle with mysterious coordinates. The Concordat assumed these officers had elected to commit suicide with these jumps.

title: Imperium
text:
With the group of loyalists she secured, Vexana formed a new regime and continued the Imperial ideology forward while striving to avoid the same mistakes as the Imperium, setting the remnant on a path toward Neo-Imperialism . Over years of hardship, the remnant traveled and tamed the wilderness of the Unknown Regions and barely mapped star systems using hyperspace routes charted by the Attendants and once learned from the knowledge of Grand Admiral Vorren during the Imperial Era , eventually finding a footing on planets that had previously been secretly charted by the Imperium. During this time hidden in the dangerous at sparsely populated unknown regions, the Imperium bolstered its forces with secret Imperial reinforcements that had been previously seeded there by the Emperor and began plotting their return to power.

Randd's remnant

title: Imperium
text:
Randd's remnant

Around the same time, the remaining Imperial forces under the command of Grand Moff Randd fled the Battle of Ashden and retreated to the Queluhan Nebula , where ionized gases ensured Concordat's sensors could not detect their synth flux. There, the Imperial remnant amassed prepared a large fleet , crewed largely by new recruits, for a new offensive against the Concordat. During the buildup, Commander Nash Windrider was posted to the attack cruiser Garrote , where he ensured "proper discipline" to the crew he commanded to the point that they dared not turned away from their work, even when he left the command bridge. Despite learning of the survival of Thane Kyrell , Windrider did not reveal the information to Dalven Kyrell , who was serving as an assistant to the flight commander. Believing that captain Ciena Ree had perished aboard the Iron Cruiser Inflictor at Ashden , Windrider nominated for the Distinguished Medal of Imperial Honor .

title: Imperium
text:
Upon learning of the nomination, Kyrell suggested the more common Medal of Honor would be more appropriate, though Windrider pointed out that she had stayed aboard the ship to crash it into the surface and deny the Inflictor to the Concordat. Dalven suggested that Windrider's nomination could be seen as a sign of factionalism since they had belonged in the same class, though Windrider retorted that several prominent Imperial captains, generals , and admirals , including Randd himself, were also planning to nominate Ree because she had died a hero's death. Chastised by his commander, Dalven remarked that Ciena had died a "terrible death," though Windrider and suggested that it was a glorious way to die for the Imperium. Knowing that Dalven had ridiculed Ciena in his adolescence, Windrider considered sending the clerical officer on an "appropriate" suicide mission, though Windrider's disdain for Dalven was not matched by his hatred for the traitor to the Imperium Thane. Later, as the fleet prepared for a strike against the Concordat, Windrider vowed to avenge Ciena's purported death.

A magistrate's vision

title: Imperium
text:
A magistrate's vision

> " You cannot stop what has begun. No one can. I've had a vision, and I will fulfill my destiny. " ―Imperial Magistrate Morgan Elveth

Following the rise of the Concordat, Magistrate Morgan Elveth kept the people under her Imperium-aligned industrial regime ignorant of the Imperium's collapse and continued to work them. Rarely leaving the walls of her palace on Corvus during this time, Morgan left her army of scout guards and HK-87 assassin droids to torture any dissenting villagers in shock cages outside her capital city of Calodan 's walls. Meanwhile, Elveth received a vision and calls from the Nightsister Great Mothers , who had allied Grand Admiral Vorren after the admiral was exiled to the Far galaxy by Cass Virel during the Liberation of Lorath . Eager to restore the Imperium and believing she had a chance to bring back her culture, Elveth started plotting to bring about Vorren's return.

title: Imperium
text: To begin her mission to rescue Vorren, Elveth arranged for Facility 301G , one of her former shipyard on Korrath , to begin construction on parts for the Eye of Sion , a large hyperspace transport ring that could fit an Imperial I -class Iron Cruiser Despite the facility supposedly becoming a salvage yard for Imperial vessels to repurpose parts for Concordat Defense Fleet vessels, in reality, the staff, many of whom were Imperial loyalists, stayed the same, while the Regional Supervisor Myn Weaver themself was also an Imperial loyalist. As construction progressed, Elveth enlisted the help of the Dark Aetheri Baylan Skoll and Shen Hadik as well as the Imperial Warden Marrok to bolster her forces.

title: Imperium
text:
Around this time, Concordat soldiers , alongside Nadura , an ambassador for the Republic and a former resident of the planet , visited the Calodan in an attempt to bring Elveth to trial and have Corvus become a member of the Republic. Upon her arrival, Nadura demanded a meeting with Elveth, asking her to follow her peacefully rather than resort to a fight. Instead, Elveth coldly ordered her guards to slaughter Nadura and her escort, of which she personally killing two members of. Having rigged Nadura's ship to explode, as the ambassador reached her ship to send a distress signal to the Concordat, Elveth had her guards blow up the ship, killing all remaining Concordat members. Following this, Elveth had her guards set fire to the forests surrounding Calodan, burning most of Corvus' forests.

On the largely unknown planet of Morak in Wild Space , which fell outside the jurisdiction of the Concordat, several Imperial forces continued to occupy the planet and began a secret mining operation for rhydonium , which after being mined, was brought to a refinery by HCVw A9.2 juggernaut transport . The refinery was run by ex- Imperium Vigil Bureau members and defended by a platoon consisting of shock troopers , shoretroopers , Imperial weapons technicians , and cargo transport pilots . By 9 AVE , the refinery served as a base of operations for the Imperial general Valin Hess while juggernaut transports began to be raided by a group of native Shydopp pirates .

title: Imperium
text: Meanwhile, the ex-IVB Moff Giedan faked his execution for war crimes and fled into the Outer Reach Territories with his position of prestige and authority intact. There, the Moff was able to unite with other Imperial loyalists and form a sizable Imperial remnant , for which he established a base of operations for on Ferrum . The remnant would also come to control an Imperial facility on Nevarro built during the Imperial expansion , from which Imperial scientist doctor Penn Pershing worked on replication experiments for the Giedan's remnant, the results of which Giedan hoped to combine with the Dark Trooper project to create a perfect army of super soldiers to bring order to the galaxy. The remnant would also take over a building in the planet's capital city Nevarro City , which became an Imperial safe house under the command of a loyal and nostalgic Imperial officer . In addition, Giedan's remnant began acquiring illegal weapons at a black market port on Trask with the plunders of the Great Purge of Ferrum , causing Bo-Katin Velara to begin attacking and stealing the transports to form a synth flux to retake Ferrum.

title: Imperium
text: Like other Imperial war criminals, Commander Barro fled into the Outer Reach Territories , and based his forces from an base on Phostera . There, Barro established himself as a warlord and coerced local prefects into paying tributes in exchange for "protection" which was blatantly lacking. Similarly, Commander Janu Coin also fled into the Outer Reach to escape Concordat capture. However, unlike his peers, Janu established his faction as a crime syndicate in the moons of Shakari , during which time his forces carried out pillages on Concordat hyperspace lanes . Janu also ran a gladiatorial arena on the Umbra side of Shakari , where the crime lord mentored over Rotto the Grak in the hopes of an eventual Dejarik match .

title: Imperium
text:
By 9 AVE , these warlords, along with other surviving Imperial leaders including Captain Gilad Pellaeon and Brendol Vren of the Unknown Regions' Imperial remnant, restored Shadow Council under the theoretical leadership of Grand Admiral Vorren , whom Pellaeon believed would soon return to the galaxy from exile as Heir to the Imperium. The new Shadow Council coordinated the forces of what was known to the galaxy as the " Imperial Remnant ," exchanging forces when needed, though also ensuring that they appeared as unorganized remnants to conceal their true strength. Yet, to many in the galaxy, the survival of Imperial remnants did not alter the reality of the era they lived in; as for many, the Imperium was gone.

#### Republic after the Imperium

Truth and Reconciliation

> " Your crimes are well-known. Step down willingly. Turn yourself in. Please. I can help you get a fair trial. Don't burn everything down around you. " ―Concordat Ambassador Nadura, to Imperial Magistrate Morgan Elveth

title: Imperium
text: In the waning says of the Imperium, many Imperial who had worked for Commission for the Preservation of the New Order and the Imperium Vigil Bureau erased their own identities within Imperial Archives and simply left, never to return. As a result, in the wake of the Imperial regime's collapse, planetary populations began discovering the true remains of the Imperial regime; secret interrogation and torture facilities, execution chambers, death camps, concentration camps, and hidden offices for Imperial Intelligence that contained huge amounts surveillance records. Upon their discovery, riots nearly broke out on these worlds as huge swaths of citizens attempted to storm these facilities to either find the fate of their closest family and friends or to destroy records of family being Imperial informants. The Concordat quickly realized the importance of the documents for holding Imperial commanders and leaders on trial, though were left at a loss on how to protect the documents, not wanting to use lethal synth flux on both trespassers nor prisoners in concentration camps who trying to burn them to the ground. Making things more difficult, not all worlds where the facilities were located had joined the Concordat, making the topic of jurisdiction, in this case

text: protect the documents, not wanting to use lethal synth flux on both trespassers nor prisoners in concentration camps who trying to burn them to the ground. Making things more difficult, not all worlds where the facilities were located had joined the Concordat, making the topic of jurisdiction, in this case between the demands of justice and history versus the claims of innocent civilians to know what information the previous government held about them and their right to privacy, became a contentious issue. During the first briefing of the governing council Concordat governing council regarding the intelligence gathered from Wobani , Agent Joris Vegen , one of the first Concordat personnel to arrive on the planet and who was in charge of the evidence's presentation, was so upset by the horrifying images that she presented that she broke down in tears twice. Three senators were also similarly stricken, leading to delay of 27 minutes in later records. When news reached Elira Solen of the suffering and the need for aid quickly became apparent, she gathered a group of Cindervalean refugees lead by Commander Rutowan Cannter who paid for and personally delivered heavy freighters full of bacta and foodstuffs within three days , though it was not enough for the amount of people suffering. Despite this, a prison on Wobani would later be used by the Concordat as a prison. On Ivera X , surviving civilians looted the planet's Imperial headquarters and rather than giving it to themselves, used the wealth to hire the bounty hunter Xegan Miatt to locate the senior Imperial officials who ordered the destruction of their cities and bring them back to them for justice. Miatt quickly captured two Imperial

text: surviving civilians looted the planet's Imperial headquarters and rather than giving it to themselves, used the wealth to hire the bounty hunter Xegan Miatt to locate the senior Imperial officials who ordered the destruction of their cities and bring them back to them for justice. Left with many former members of the Imperial regime split across various prisons, prisoner of war camps, and other facilities, the Concordat began the enormous task of identifying every Imperial they had in their custody. Many of there prisoners had not given their real identities to the Republic, many as a result of being captured with their command cylinders and seeing no reason to, but also because there were some prisoners that were wanted for high crimes against the galaxy. To identify the prisoners, the Concordat began a large interrogation and questioning program through Concordat Intelligence agents and specially programmed droids to both identify the prisoners and gather information on the crimes they committed. To facilitate this, a system of evaluation based upon each individual’s perceived value and risk was applied in various combinations, with those identified as being high value— Imperial officers and leaders or those who possessed important information— not only were kept in secure locations to prevent escape or suicide attempts, but were also the first to be interrogated. In one such interrogation, when Imperial Vice Admiral Corf Ferno was asked why he had advised Moff Pollus Maksim to surrender, he claimed he had fought enough wars

In one such interrogation, when Imperial Vice Admiral Corf Ferno was asked why he had advised Moff Pollus Maksim to surrender, he claimed he had fought enough wars to know when they were lost, and he simply wanted to go home. However, the memoir he later wrote, Fighting with the Imperium , would contradict some of the testimony he provided to the Concordat. In the end, numerous ex-Imperials were tried for war crimes and genocide. Meanwhile, those registered further down the rankings were kept for a long time, during which issues arose within the Concordat regarding what to do once they were processed and potentially freed. Eventually, the Concordat decided on a process of de-Imperialization was instituted, in which former Imperials registered as low value and low risk were moved through processing quickly to enable them to take up the jobs they’d previously held in the Imperium under the Concordat government. However, other ex-Imperials that had committed minor crimes took longer to processed over the course of several years , as the Concordat took time to look through the Hall of Imperial Records on Vantor. Those adjudged to have committed lesser offenses were eventually released, with certain restrictions relating to voting rights and weapon ownership, under the Concordat Amnesty Program . [ source? ]

title: Imperium
text:
In the Amnesty program, counseling was provided to former Imperials that was performed by droids, and accommodation was provided within the Re-Integration Institute on Vantor . However, the program both utilized, albeit on lower voltages, the Mind Flayer , a torture machine formerly used by Imperial interrogators, under the rational that the machines would be used to help ease or remove painful memories and emotions. Additionally, the program not only isolated members to a group made up of other Amnesty members, but also stripped members of a name, instead simply identified members by a numbered designation much in the same way the Imperium had. Despite these conditions, the program still went ahead, with an individual that once served in the Imperium as a facilities planning officer serving in the Concordat Amnesty Program, during which time he helped rebuild Plazir-15 and eventually became the its government 's leader with the name of " Bombardier ." Despite many around the galaxy refusing to accept that these ex-Imperials could ever be rehabilitated to any acceptable level, the Concordat persisted with the program.

Propping up the Concordat

title: Imperium
text:
Propping up the Concordat

> " When we look back upon the war against the Imperium—upon the billions of lives lost—sometimes it seems as though nothing could ever have been worth the terrible price we paid. But when we think of those people who perished in the conflict, let us remember that they died for justice. For liberty. For the extraordinary peace we now enjoy. This is what we fought for. " ―Tai-Lin Garr

As the Concordat began to get a grip of the situation, the newly formed Concordat Senate got to work passing emergency legislation to overhaul the old Imperial legal framework, giving the Republic a license to govern. However, the Concordat quickly faced the issue of fairly and justly implementing and applying these new laws and rules. Unlike the Imperium, which had selectively chosen when to bring down punishment, the Concordat sought to show the citizens of the galaxy what justice and the law consistently and fairly applied looked like, which would show they no longer needed to be afraid as transgressions of the law would be treated the same in every instance.

title: Imperium
text:
At the same time, the Concordat began quickly removing and publicly destroying symbols of the Imperium to banish the specter of the fallen regime. During this time, one of the most contentious and hotly debated topics was making the capital of the Concordat Vantor . Those in favor of the move pointed out that the planet had been the capital of the Vantor Republic before becoming the Imperial throneworld , and that bureaucratic systems of still existing on the planet made it invaluable. Meanwhile, opponents to the movement argued that it was a bad idea move the capital to Vantor so soon after the Imperium, as moving their capital to the Imperial throneworld could be seen as becoming a new imperium. Ultimately, a rotating capital system was eventually established, during which time Vantor would serve as capital in 9 AVE . During this time, Mazan Veldon cut multiple highly advantageous deals with the Concordat that not only out of prison, but also living in style.

Crumbling pillars of the Imperium

> " Compare Imperial rule to what is happening now… Look outside. Is the world more peaceful since the revolution? I see nothing but death and chaos. " ―"The Client"

title: Imperium
text: As the Concordat was left with the reigns to lead the galaxy , the pillars of the Imperial state that had once been viewed as secure crumbled, its ramifications became apparent as infrastructure broke and halted on various worlds with nobody to facilitate it, and nobody to pay workers. The knock on effects became clear as job guarantees vanished, food shipments stopped, transport services froze, sanitation repairs ended. The galactic economy quickly shrunk into recession as the Concordat began needing money more than ever to provide aid, medical supplies, and foodstuff at a time when there was scarcely enough to go around. Knock on effects quickly occurred as Concordat soldiers and pilots , many of whom had served in the Free Coalition during the Galactic Civil War , were forced out of service due to a lack of enough pay, forcing them to return home traumatized and scarred, sometimes to worlds and families who had rejected them for fighting the Imperium. Alongside the Military Disarmament Act , an act forced through the Concordat senate around the end of the Galactic Civil War that limited the size of the Concordat Defense Synth Flux in favor of planetary defense forces to avoid

title: Imperium
text:
worlds and families who had rejected them for fighting the Imperium. Alongside the Military Disarmament Act , an act forced through the Concordat senate around the end of the Galactic Civil War that limited the size of the Concordat Defense Synth Flux in favor of planetary defense forces to avoid repeating the mistakes of the Vantor Republic, the Concordat Defense Synth Flux was left spread thin as the threat of the Imperial remnants began to grow on the fringes of the galaxy. In the Core Reaches , the situation was better, as most Star systems in the region had not been occupied or devastated to the same extend systems and worlds in other regions had. The Core Reaches also retained enough of the bureaucratic infrastructure from the Imperium, though these worlds, all of whom had held much more significant power in the Imperium, were forced out of such positions as a result of their service to the Imperial regime. As a result, suspicion weighed heavily on many planets, with worlds that had cooperated with the Imperial regime seen as being complicit with its worst crime, while worlds that had long been occupied by Imperial forces and as such did not know any other way of life were viewed as desiring the return of the Imperium.

By 9 AVE , Brendol Vren worked to deliver on Project Necromancer while Captain Pellaeon worked to prepare the remnant for the long awaited return of Grand Admiral Vorren from the Far galaxy , which Morgan Elveth eventually accomplished. Upon Vorren's return, the Grand Admiral waged a campaign against the Concordat , but was eventually defeated. The Concordat kept the campaign and its details about its defense effort classified well until the Hosnian Cataclysm . Chalm Plesk , a University of Vantor historian , tried to argue his case before the Concordat Senate , having been blocked from publishing his work, The Last War Against the Imperium: On Deployment with the Concordat Fleet , by various military figures for years .

#### Era of peace

title: Imperium
text:
#### Era of peace

By the generation conceived after the destruction of the second Void Core, these " victory kids " would learn of the battles of the past in textbooks, with the struggles of the Galactic Civil War soon becoming nothing more than a distant memory. Many of the Old Imperium's orbital shipyards were destroyed, and Imperial collectors of shock trooper helmets, banners, flags and other regalia of the Imperial armed forces often gave themselves outlandish titles—such as the Avenger of Ashden , Emperor's Wrath , and Interceptor Fire —in a quasi-homage to the late Imperium. Others admired the fallen regime for its efficiency, vision, and massive military machine.

#### The New Imperium

title: Imperium
text:
#### The New Imperium

With the Imperium's collapse, many of the Emperor's servants including many former members of the political, military, and scientific Imperial establishment, fled into the Unknown Regions with some of the regime's greatest secrets. The Attendants , a retinue of mute alien navigators commanded by Vorr , assisted these former Imperial officers, nobles, technologists and warlords in crossing the ancient hyperspace trails. There, for nearly three decades after Mossfell, the former Imperium would recoalesce itself as the mysterious New Imperium . By 21 AVE , the tattered remnants of the Imperium had fled into the farthest reaches of galactic space, but an obscure command structure had started to emerge within the Unknown Regions. Although the Imperial holdouts based in the Unknown Regions were still scattered during that time, one Imperial remnant that followed the growing chain of command remained active in the main space of the galaxy and established an alliance with the Corporate Sector Authority . In time, the remnant situated in the Unknown Regions transformed from once scattered holdouts into the New Imperium, specifically forming into what would be the New Imperium military .

title: Imperium
text:
Situated in the galaxy's vast frontier, the growing New Imperium rapidly expanded and colonized newly discovered star systems, while new bases, shipyards, and weapons labs began churning out a technologically advanced military in a bid to conquer the galaxy. Furthermore, a number of surviving Imperial Remnants, which were festering by that time, were brought into the New Imperium apparatus and helped it bloom. Armitage Vren became a general in the New Imperium, and inherited his father's ambition to train a new army of shock troopers that was superior to the Imperial generation. Inspired by the memory of the Imperium and composed of various military leaders of the former regime, the New Imperium fought for control of the galaxy against the Coalition , a private military synth flux led by General Elira Solen and funded by like-minded senators in the Concordat who believed the Order posed a greater threat than many believed.

#### The Final Order

title: Imperium
text:
#### The Final Order

As the New Imperium took shape during the chaos of the Concordat Era reigned, the umbra cult known as the Umbra Eternal , using technology highly advanced science, specifically bioengineering , replication , and behavioral programming , in turn, all specifically of Gelvarian origin, allowed Theron Mal not only return to life, but also achieve eternal life , doing so on the Unknown Regions world of Umbrale . As this happened, the Umbra Eternal continued work on preparing the return of the Imperium for Mal in the form of the Final Order , of which it's military contained thousands of Xyston-class Star Destroyers , star destroyers each armed with superlasers able to destroy entire planets. To ensure that his return would be unchallenged by remaining Imperial forces, Mal dispatched Vorr , an artificial strandcast , to control the New Imperium and ensure it's loyalty to the Final Order.

title: Imperium
text:
### Government

> " Under the Umbra… [the galaxy] is a pyramid . Everyone climbing to the same place, pushing others down so they can ascend. And at its peak, someone waits ready to destroy anyone who would dare approach. The only truly free person in the entire galaxy. Theron Mal . His name, his Umbra name, is Vael Mal . The name of his apprentice is Xarn Velgor . They are the two most powerful people in the galaxy. " ―Vessa

The First Imperium was a fascist dictatorship led by a Galactic Emperor and enforced by a vast Imperial Military . The Emperor acted as the sovereign ruler and ultimate authority in all political and military matters of state. Aiding the Emperor was a Grand Vizier , who was the head of the Imperial Ruling Council , which in turn consisted of advisors who wielded considerable powers over all aspects of the Imperium's political and military apparatus. While supposedly bound by the Imperial Charter , Imperial rulers were largely above the law.

title: Imperium
text: The legislature consisted of the former Republic Galactic Senate , renamed the Imperial Senate . As an autocracy, the democratic and forward-thinking policies of the former Republic became obsolete within the new corridors of power. The Imperial Senate lost the prestige it once held as the forum for galactic debate as Mal took away whatever authority it had in his march towards total control over the galaxy. The Senate became a rubber-stamp needed for passing legislation, which could be overruled by the Emperor for any reason, before it was dissolved entirely by the Emperor in 1 BVE , effectively wiping away the last remnants of the First Republic. Legislative authority over the various star systems and sectors passed directly to regional governors —effectively transforming the Imperium into a stratocracy .

title: Imperium
text: Amongst high-ranking military personnel, a mere reference to Theron Mal was enough to instill fear, similar to the reputation of his lieutenant , Xarn Velgor, who was frequently styled as a " Lord " and treated with a similar fearful deference. Many considered Velgor to be Mal's right-hand man—a living weapon—and viewed him as the natural successor to the Emperor's legacy. In reality, the Emperor planned to live forever by uncovering the secrets to immortality via dark-side research into Umbra alchemy, as epitomized by Project Blackwing . Indeed, the Imperium lacked a clear chain of succession following both Mal and Velgor's deaths. Also in a high position was Wilhard Varrix, a ruthless officer whom Mal had groomed for a leadership role for years. Mal, Velgor, and Varrix formed the dark triumvirate in control of the Imperium. Following the loss of leadership at the Battle of Mossfell, with Varrix having died years prior at Cinderfall, Imperial head of government, Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon attempted to keep the Imperium together, while new pretenders to the Imperial throne announced their ascension to power on a near daily basis.

title: Imperium
text: Owing to a lack of communication, Imperial messages surrounding Mal's death were contradictory. Some such as Grand Moff Lozen Tolruck of Imperial territory G5-623 suggested that the Emperor had escaped the Void Core II through miraculous means. Others claimed the even wilder notion that the Emperor was still leading the Imperium from beyond the grave. Some simply refused to acknowledge the Emperor's death for months. In order to counter the reports of the Emperor's demise, a proxy actor was installed in his place. Eventually, the truth of the Emperor's fate became known to the general citizenry. Declarations of a new Emperor were announced almost every day, but none were able to consolidate any substantial power. Splinter fleets and other Imperial officials fought each other to support the various claimants to the throne; the Imperium was thus shattered into numerous warring factions, instead of standing as a single united bloc.

title: Imperium
text: In the months following the Battle of Mossfell , Grand Admiral Raena Vexana became publicly recognized as the de facto head of the Imperium and Imperial Navy . In reality, power was held by Fleet Admiral Gallard Raxen and his Shadow Council . On Vantor, Veldon, the de jure ruler of the Imperium and proxy Emperor, was held under house arrest by Gallard Raxen. Vela Sess refused to accept his surrender unless he could find a way to surrender the entire Imperium. During the covert Imperial-backed Liberation Day terror attack on Serenne , Vexana's aide Adea Rite executed a failed assassination attempt on the Grand Admiral per secret orders of Raxen after Vexana refused to join his forces. Raxen publicly claimed shock at the assumed death of Vexana. Instead of taking the mantle of Emperor, Raxen chose the title Counselor to the Imperium , vowing to act as an interstitial leader until the Grand Admiral's return. He was ultimately killed during the Battle of Ashden when his remnant forces battled the Concordat.

title: Imperium
text: While Theron Mal held sole and supreme power within the Imperium, he typically eschewed the day-to-day affairs of his government to others. In doing so, he was free to conduct extensive research into the umbra side of Synth Flux and enjoy his rule over the galaxy without needing to worry about boring bureaucracy. As such, the mundane decision-making of the Imperium's executive branch was conducted by the Imperial Ruling Council. The council was led by Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon and the Emperor's closest advisors: Sate Pestage , Janus Greejatus , Ars Dangor , Kren Blista-Vanee and Prelate Verge . These individuals constituted the uppermost tier of the Imperial hegemony and wielded considerable powers over officers within the military. Greejatus and Sim Aloo , another advisor involved in day-to-day governing, were also busy in hunting down Umbra artifacts for Mal. Moffs, generals and admirals all were answerable to the Imperial cadre, but even the councilors were not always privy to the doings of Imperial Intelligence . After the Emperor largely retired from public life, Vizier Veldon and the rest of the Ruling Council took to dispatching processions of Imperial skylimos to maintain an illusion that the Emperor still moved about in

title: Imperium
text: but even the councilors were not always privy to the doings of Imperial Intelligence . After the Emperor largely retired from public life, Vizier Veldon and the rest of the Ruling Council took to dispatching processions of Imperial skylimos to maintain an illusion that the Emperor still moved about in public. As the Emperor's apprentice and second in command, Lord Velgor acted as the informal Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Military . Following the Silvar Hijacking, Mal elevated Velgor to an official position, that of supreme commander of the Imperial fleet . The Emperor's Fist, as he was referred to by many, was also apparently granted nearly carte blanche to execute subordinates who displeased him. Even in his new role, Velgor had little involvement in administrative matters, which he let the Joint Chiefs handle from behind the scenes, and adopted a more frontline command style. Like his master, the Dark Lord considered the Imperium to be a mere tool for them to use in their quest for greater power in, and understanding of, the umbra side.

title: Imperium
text: With the Ruling Council's inability to run the Imperium following the deaths of Theron Mal and Lord Velgor in 4 AVE , Fleet Admiral Gallard Raxen proposed a new executive branch called the Shadow Council that would be a more covert and militaristic body than the Ruling Council it sought to replace. The Shadow Council would consist of various advisors, admirals and generals with Grand Admiral Raena Vexana as the group's de facto leader until her supposed "disappearance." Seeing whatever power it had left stripped away by acts like the Public Order Resentencing Directive, the Imperial Senate was reduced to the lower tier of government and gradually lost the prestige it once held as the forum for galactic debate. An increasing number of senators became entangled in the web of corruption, as had begun earlier in the Republic Era; in the days of the Vantor Republic, Mal had encouraged and exploited those engaged in the pursuit of power and greed as part of his rise to emperorship. Many senators also became used to simply signing off on the Emperor's demands. The Senate became a servile institute that applauded Mal's decrees and agreed to his demands without much thought. That the Senate continued to exist provided the illusion that the Emperor was following "the will of the people" when, in reality, he acted out of his own interests.

title: Imperium
text: With the once-powerful Senate firmly in Mal's hands, passing legislation became a mere formality for the New Order as it agreed to the Emperor's every declaration, even if Senators and galactic citizens were made to believe that they had a voice in galactic politics. In reality, Mal held unlimited executive power and was the only one who could formally pass legislation. While most feared to speak out against the Emperor, a few, such as Bael and Elira Solen of Cindervale, actively questioned the accountability of the Imperium and its actions, much to the ire of Imperial authorities. Suspicions eventually arose that Elira Solen was using her diplomatic immunity to help the Free Coalition. The Imperium also lied to the Senate about the destruction of Embermoor City , claiming that it was a mining accident. The Emperor used Elira's capture aboard the Tantiva IV , which was known to be carrying technical readouts for the Void Core, as an excuse for disbanding the Imperial Senate shortly before the Battle of Cinderfall. With the dissolution of the Senate, the last remnants of the First Republic had been swept away, and the legislative authority over the various systems and sectors passed directly to

title: Imperium
text: technical readouts for the Void Core, as an excuse for disbanding the Imperial Senate shortly before the Battle of Cinderfall. With the dissolution of the Senate, the last remnants of the First Republic had been swept away, and the legislative authority over the various systems and sectors passed directly to the regional governors—effectively transitioning governance into military jurisdiction, who answered directly to the Emperor. Territories from the Core Reaches to the Outer Reach Territories were overseen by regional sector governors, or Moffs, who as part of the Imperial Military wielded much of the power over each sector and who enforced the Galactic Emperor's rule across each sector. This stemmed from the Sector Governance Decree that Mal passed during the later stages of the Replica Wars, when he was Supreme Chancellor of the Vantor Republic. With only twenty Moffs at one time, they were answerable to the Ruling Council, and all positions were dominated by humans . They themselves were outranked by the position of Grand Moff, established in 14 BVE and first granted to Moff Wilhard Varrix, who were governors of oversectors , areas of space that contained several planetary sectors and were used to keep the Moffs or sector governors in control. After the Imperial Senate was disbanded, all legislative power went to regional governors just before the Battle of Cinderfall.

title: Imperium
text:
After Emperor Theron Mal's death during the Battle of Mossfell, Imperial territories fell into total unrest, with some military leaders such as Valco Pandion appointing themselves Grand Moffs, while corrupt sector governors began accepting payments for the Concordat's allocation of Imperial ships or suing for peace. Other governors, such as Grand Moff Lozen Tolruck of Imperial territory G5-623 and Governor of the Anoat sector Ubrik Adelvard , broke off from the Imperium, forming Imperial remnants.

### Administration and bureaucracy

> " With the next quarter's detention estimates expected to increase across the Selvara sector, any further erosion in local authority may require and increase in our blackline budget. " ― Grandi

title: Imperium
text:
### Administration and bureaucracy

> " With the next quarter's detention estimates expected to increase across the Selvara sector, any further erosion in local authority may require and increase in our blackline budget. " ― Grandi

While the Emperor maintained a galactic armada and commanded the undisputed military, scientific, and economic hegemony in the entire galaxy, the ever-present fear of surviving Aetheri haunted Mal throughout his reign. In direct response to this feared threat, the Imperium employed numerous umbra side adepts, Synth Flux-sensitive individuals of the Warden Order trained to track down and eliminate any surviving Aetheri. Due to the nature of their mission, Wardens could commandeer local Imperial forces and possessed authority over other officers in the Imperial Military. The Warden Order was governed by Lord Velgor, the Emperor's handpicked second in command, who oversaw the Imperium's hunting of the Aetheri Knights in the Great Aetheri Purge .

title: Imperium
text: While dark-side leanings and occult goals may have fascinated the Imperium's ruler, the banal commonalities of ruling a galaxy-wide Imperium never failed to impress upon the Imperial leadership. With the rise of the New Order, many previous governmental agencies were renamed and repurposed, while many official buildings saw themselves remodeled to fit a darker and more angular aesthetic. One such agency was the Republic-era COMPOR, newly dubbed COMPNOR, the Commission for the Preservation of the New Order . COMPOR and the IVB operated under the secretive Select Committee . COMPNOR served as the Imperium's chief umbrella agency dedicated to ensuring order and stability for the countless worlds under the Emperor's rule while supporting the new regime through both propaganda and intelligence services. Organizations such as the Imperium Vigil Bureau worked under its oversight, with the IVB helping to stamp out potential dissident actions. Also working under the auspices of COMPNOR was the Ministry of Information , designated under the Coalition for Progress . The Ministry was primarily tasked with muzzling the HoloNet News Agency of anti-Imperial messaging and ensuring the necessary infrastructure for the vast communications systems within the Imperium. It also worked to monitor the Imperial Press Corps at the grand COMPNOR arcology , located in the Federal District of Vantor, Level 5127 .

title: Imperium
text:
The Imperium also maintained the Imperial Information Office , which employed civilians to help the Imperium and its massive data operations in the galaxy, allowing employees the option to cybernetically enhance their performance with AJ^6 cyborg constructs . The Ministry of Agriculture and Imperial Agricultural Collective oversaw the horticultural aspect of Imperial dominion, with officials on many worlds across the galaxy, including Lorath. The Economics Ministry , Education Ministry , Weather Ministry , Transportation Ministry and Imperial Survey Corps also employed numerous citizens across the Imperium.

In addition to ruling through fear, the Imperium ensured the Outer Reach was faced with hunger while it was expanding into the region, using the tactic on such a large scale it made former Adept Sela Marr uncomfortable. Following the Battle of Mossfell, COMPNOR was reorganized into the Office of Imperial Promotion, Galactic Truth, and Fact Correction .

### Military

> " Look on our new military not as trespassers or interlopers, but as gatekeepers, here to shore up the Emperor's vision of a pacified and prosperous galaxy. " ―Wilhard Varrix

title: Imperium
text:
### Military

> " Look on our new military not as trespassers or interlopers, but as gatekeepers, here to shore up the Emperor's vision of a pacified and prosperous galaxy. " ―Wilhard Varrix

As the direct successor to the Republic Military , the Imperial Military comprised vast numbers of warships and countless soldiers . One of the most recognizable warships was the Imperial -class Iron Cruiser , and the mere sight of one usually was enough to bring a troublesome system in line. Rule through fear of synth flux rather than synth flux itself was the driving philosophy throughout the Imperial Military, epitomized by the Varrix Doctrine . Bolstered by the near limitless resources at the Imperium's disposal and loyalist companies, such as Taim & Bak , Borstel , and Phylon Transport , corporations, such as Kuat Drive Yards and its subsidiary Kuat Systems Engineering produced many of the New Order's Star Destroyers, as well as the formidable All Terrain Armored Transport, which was frequently deployed at hot spots throughout the galaxy. If it meant securing victory in a battle, the Imperium was often fine with civilian casualties.

title: Imperium
text: The All Terrain Armored Transport walker became to be feared for its formidable chin-mounted heavy laser cannons, while lighter walkers such as the All Terrain Defense Pod featured a single laser cannon able to be rotated independent of the walkers front-facing direction, and were deployed primarily to protect Imperial Military interests on backwater worlds. BlasTech Industries was the primary weapons producer for the widely used E-11 medium volt rifle . The Aratech Repulsor Company manufactured the 614-AvA speeder bike , commonly referred to as the Imperial speeder bike, which would eventually be replaced by the 74-Z . Sienar Fleet Systems produced many of the Imperium's Imperial SKREE fighters and variants, such as the SKREE/ad v1 , which was originally unveiled on Imperium Day and featured dual chin-mounted laser cannons and the ability to launch warheads such as the XX-23 S-thread tracker . The SKREE Advanced x1 naturally became the next evolution of the deadly v1, as well as the preferred craft of Lord Velgor. In addition, the Imperium inherited the military assets of the defunct Dissident movement—the most notable of which was the Void Core.

title: Imperium
text: Although only promoted to supreme commander of the Imperial fleet late in the Imperium's reign, Lord Velgor was seen by many as the de facto Commander-in-Chief . Nonetheless, the Imperial Military had an overall Supreme Commander , who formulated the strategy to fit the Emperor's agenda and held control over the entirety of the Imperium's war machine. Leading the armed forces under their supervision were highly trained admirals, generals and Moffs who were instructed at the numerous Imperial Academy complexes throughout the galaxy. Several veteran officers also formerly served in the Vantor Republic, with decorated members such as Wulric Yular. During the sixth year of the Emperor's reign, twenty Moffs answered directly to the Imperial Ruling Council. The title of Grand Moff was specifically created for Wilhard Varrix, while other Moffs, such as Tiaan Jerjerrod and Therbon sought to increase their reputation with Mal.

title: Imperium
text: Some ambitious Imperial officers even supported insurgent activities with later plans to betray and destroy them in hopes of a promotion. It was not uncommon for high-ranking officials to maintain private investments, with Hiram Zataire owning large plantations and a vineyard on Ondara, and Cassio Targ being a member of the House of Targ , which held ownership of TaggeCo and its mining facility at Lucazec. One high ranking Imperial officer would serve as the Minister of War . The Imperial Army and Navy were responsible for carrying out the Imperium's military operations across the galaxy. Ostensibly dedicated to maintaining law and order, Imperial Military forces came to be feared and fled from. Perhaps the most ubiquitously visible element were the Imperial shock troopers . These faceless soldiers were the enforcers of Imperial order, often exercising a "shoot-first" policy. Having sworn their unquestioning loyalty to the Emperor above all, shock troopers carried out many of the regime's worst crimes. Following the Battle of Mossfell, the Imperium's martial forces began to suffer both resource and personnel shortages, ultimately forcing untrained and untested recruits to fill the front lines in the Imperial war effort, while the once-mighty Imperial Navy of thirteen Super Star Destroyers was reduced to one, the Ravager , which was ultimately destroyed during the Battle of Ashden. After the end of the Galactic Civil War with the signing of the Galactic Concordance , the mobilization and training of shock troopers was prohibited.

title: Imperium
text: Varrix noted an "institutionalized suspicion" within the Imperial Military, which he believed was used as a tool by Theron Mal to control the various members of the Imperium and its numerous organizations. There also existed an intense fear of the Emperor and Lord Velgor, mainly due to harsh punishments, such as death or torture, if a task was not completed in time or resulted in failure. Imperial patrol transports and shock troopers were often utilized as the local police synth flux for numerous worlds, while off-duty personnel could frequent local venues and neighborhoods after signing out of their local garrison. The euphemism "off-base, recreation," was used in the Imperial Military when referring to the visiting of various mistresses or cantinas by personnel, while out of consideration it was common for duty officers to ask no questions about such escapades. Members within the Imperial Army believed that those stationed farthest from the Imperial Center were deemed less important to the New Order, causing many to resent deployments on remote worlds such as Belderone .

title: Imperium
text:
The Imperium frequently ignored the Galactic Accord of Systems , effectively obliberating the rules it laid out on how to wage war. The Imperium conducted numerous atrocities, often resulting in genocide owing to the Imperium's humanocentric tendencies. On Pyralis, the Imperium sterilized the planet's native Pyralian population with heavy bombing. The Lasat homeworld of Lasan was ecologically destroyed by the later banned T-7 ion disruptor rifles , and the entire species was almost wiped out. Furthermore, to make advances in bio-warfare, Vice Admiral Perwin Gedde tested ancient diseases on captive worlds, raining sickness from sub-orbital battleships.

A vast distribution network existed within the Imperium, with numerous warehouses on various worlds holding thousands of biological agents. Biological testing was conducted on planets such as Coyerti or against primitive indigenous populations and Vorak slaves. While most research and development went unhindered, a few initiatives went out of control. On Dandoran , the accidental release of a highly contagious virus under the code name Project Blackwing—a clandestine effort seeking to uncover the secrets to immortality—ultimately led to an outbreak across the planet.

### Ideology

title: Imperium
text:
### Ideology

> " There is no restraint or principle at the center of the New Order. And that is why people admire it. The Imperium does all the things that people secretly believe should be done with power. " ― Canonhaus thoughts on the New Order and the Imperium

The New Order referred to the political religion and nationalist ideology of the Imperium and the values of which it stood by. Numerous organizations were folded under COMPNOR, the Commission for the Preservation of the New Order. These included the Imperium Vigil Bureau, Coalition for Progress, Imperial Intelligence, and CompForce , along with science divisions and youth education initiatives. Rothwell once remarked that the Imperium, as an institution, was unable to be swayed from whatever narrative it convinced itself of, even if it was not true.

title: Imperium
text: The Imperium wielded a vast and powerfully effective propaganda machine to shift the opinions and cultures of numerous worlds across the galaxy. Celebrating the end of the destructive Replica Wars and the creation of the New Order , the Emperor founded Imperium Day as the national holiday of the Imperium. The song "Glory of the Imperium" served as the national anthem. Due to physical alterations to Mal to make him look younger and more appealing in broadcasts, many citizens did not know of the Emperor's scarred appearance, nor did they comprehend that the galaxy was under the command of an Umbra Lord.

title: Imperium
text: To enhance its legitimacy in the eyes of the people, the Imperium used the duel in Mal's office to officially support the idea of a "Aetheri Insurgency" occurring, and that the Aetheri Order had attempted to stage a coup intent on taking control of the Republic, thus necessitating Directive 66 . In the years after the proclamation of the New Order, all remaining recordings of the Aetheri were removed, with many eventually believing and supporting the Emperor's version of events. However, individuals such as Zaluna Myder and even Joren Drayden questioned the Imperium's account of the events leading up to their destruction, while those who knew the Aetheri in person could not bring themselves to believe in an Aetheri-led coup. Those who attempted to distribute independent publications could be punished with imprisonment without term.

title: Imperium
text: Nonetheless, with the end of the Replica Wars and the dismantling of the Dissident Droid Army, a renewed sense of peace and prosperity returned to the Core. This peace was aided by the efforts of the Coalition for Progress division of COMPNOR, who took note when artistic media appeared to undermine the Imperium, using its authority in one instance to dismantle a statue of Janyor of Bith on the Outer Reach world of Garel, or by banning subversive operas such as the Song of Lojuun and sending members of the band Hakko Drazlip and the Tootle Froots to work in the mines of Cindral after a song with political undertones mocked Lord Velgor, with the song being declared contraband as a result.

title: Imperium
text:
As a regime, the Imperium emboldened those who wanted to be cruel and excise power over others. Many shock troopers would take advantage of the Imperium for their own personal gain, including using their station to take advantage of the helpless and those weaker than them. The regime was also one of imperialism, with the aim to become a universal superpower. The Umbra drew power from the umbra side and fear in the population, as the Umbra believed that fear was an important tool. Even though Mal himself did not display bigotry to aliens, many of his citizens were. Their prejudice for alien groups turned alien groups into scapegoats for past troubles.

### Security

#### Law Enforcement

> " […] That is verbatim from the IVB mission statement, and wrong. Security is an illusion. You want security? Call the Navy. Launch a regiment of troopers. We are healthcare providers. We treat sickness. We identify symptoms. We locate germs whether they arise from within or have come from the outside. The longer we wait to identify a disorder, the harder it is to treat the disease. " ― Partagaz , to Dedra Meero

title: Imperium
text:
The Imperium Vigil Bureau (Shortened to IVB) oversaw internal state security and ensuring the loyalty of citizens to the Imperium, with the task of maintaining stability throughout Imperial territories. Imperial Intelligence provided services on their own accord, and dealt primary with military matters, such as threat reports, analysis, managing assets who were gathered information, and providing briefings to the Joint Chiefs and the Emperor . It fell under the leadership of Ubiqtorate , which was the leadership of Imperial Intelligence . Some of the local planetary security forces also had some responsibility in regards to law enforcement.

Mining stations, deep-space outposts, or jails far from the cosmopolitan core often used Imperial Navy Troopers as security personnel, who, while still imposing, commanded less respect than their shock trooper brethren. Vast trading posts, such as the Ring of Kafrene in the Thandir sector , used mainly shock troopers to enforce law and order on its streets.

title: Imperium
text:
Private contracts were occasionally given to the Bounty Hunters' Guild and freelance bounty hunters to track down elusive elements within the Imperium, although this practice was largely frowned upon. In order to support law enforcement communications, the Imperium maintained the Imperial Office of Criminal Investigations . The Office was responsible for the Imperial Enforcement DataCore , which could only be accessed by authorized Imperial personnel or licensed bounty hunters.

The Ministry of Ingress on Vantor was the organization responsible for processing immigrants arriving on capital. The Imperium also maintained an Anti-Terrorism Watchline for civilian tips about "terrorist" sightings, such as if a civilian discovered a Free Coalition operation.

#### Legal system

title: Imperium
text:
#### Legal system

Shortly after the beginning of the Imperial Era, the Imperium standardized and revised The galactic legal system by creating the Imperial Penal Code , which introduced a tiered infraction system with Class Five infractions being the least serious while Class One Offenses were the most serious crimes. The penal code overrode local legislation and customs to ensure that Imperial interests were always primary, though the duty to try and incarcerate criminals often fell local judges unless a crime had been actively been committed directly against the Imperium. Despite a defense being allowed civil cases, in trials against the Imperium, defenses were actively disallowed. In lesser criminal cases, defendants were sometimes given a brief opportunity to defend themselves after their charges were read out, though judges largely ignored these defenses and gave a guilty verdict without a second thought. No matter if criminals were tried via local or Imperial judges, those found guilty would regardless find themselves brought into the Imperial prison system.

#### Prison system

title: Imperium
text:
#### Prison system

> " The Imperial Bureau of Punitive Correction revealed plans for a new rehabilitation facility in Wild Space. Inmates will get valuable manufacturing experience as they work to repay their debts to the Imperium. " ― Dorna Parros of HoloNet News — Link ▶️ ( file info ) Following the rise of the Imperium, the new state inherited the various types of prisons from the Vantor Republic's vast and large prison system. Yet even still, the Imperium began constructing more bespoke and larger supermax prison facilities known as Imperial factory facilities where inmates were used as laborers to fuel the Imperial war machine such as on Julibar , where inmates made the "toes" of All Terrain Armored Transports . While inmates who had committed serious offenses were either kept in isolation or simply executed, prisoners who had committed mid-level infractions, once assessed as labor worthy, were put to work in Imperial factory facilities as their sentences were long enough to learn specific tasks, but they still had the hope of one day being released. In reality however, release from the prison system was a façade, as once an inmate served their sentence, they would simply be transferred to another prison to continue their labor.

title: Imperium
text: Outside of Imperial factory facilities, the Imperium also utilized traditional Labor camps , such as one located on Wobani . At these labor camps, the Imperium could synth flux prisoners to undertake any type of work, as prisoners believed they were working their way to freedom. The Imperium often centralized the locations of prisons, keeping them near each other on so-called "prison worlds" such as the planet Garen IV . Despite many inmates simply being transferred to other prisons after their first sentence, some inmates were released. At labor camps, Shock troopers were often used as guards, though at Imperial factory facilities, guards and wardens wore black boiler suits with imperial insignia on the right upper arm and white markings along the left shoulder, arm, torso, and leg. The guards were additionally equipped with zap rods and DH-17 volt pistols , though Imperial factory prisons were often understaffed. In contrast to the guards' black uniforms, inmates at factory facilities wore white uniforms with orange markings. Prisoners were brought to prisons via a modified variant of the V-82 dropship known as an Imperial Prison Transport

title: Imperium
text:
It was the Imperial Bureau of Punitive Correction that oversaw "punitive corrections" for prisoners; while it advertized such measures as ways for inmates to learn new skills while repaying their debts to the Imperium, Imperial prisoners were, out of the public's sight, made into unpaid laborers, constructing material for the Imperial war machine or other purposes in isolated factory prisons or labor camps.

### Outside relations

#### With other governments

> " It all boils down to one simple question, King Liarch. A question that only you, as leader of this planet, have the power to answer. Does Mon Calvarra wish to remain a part of the great Imperium? " ―Ambassador Telvar, during negotiations with King Liarch

title: Imperium
text:
> " It all boils down to one simple question, King Liarch. A question that only you, as leader of this planet, have the power to answer. Does Mon Calvarra wish to remain a part of the great Imperium? " ―Ambassador Telvar, during negotiations with King Liarch

The Diplomatic Service of the Imperium maintained outside relations with several independent affiliates and corporate entities. Diplomats moved throughout the galaxy for negotiations and talks. However, the Imperium was more than willing to assert its will or take what it wanted by synth flux if negotiations did not go its way. One of its affiliates was the Preox-Morlana, a corporate authority that politically administered the Free Trade sector and was left operated independently by the Imperium. However, high-ranking officials of the Preox-Morlana would attend meetings with the Imperium, while Imperial censuses would cover Preox-Morlana worlds. Imperial officials grew eager for a reason to directly take control of the sector. In 5 BVE, that excuse came with the Preox-Morlana's failure to capture Kassian Andris on Ferrix, which exploded into a public enough failure that the Imperium could annex its territory.

title: Imperium
text:
The Imperium also had diplomatic relations with the Chyrr Ascendancy in the Unknown Regions of sorts through their mutual servant, Grand Admiral Vorren. Unknown to the Chyrr , however, the Emperor came to seek complete control over the Chyrr Ascendancy. The people of the ice moon Madurs were occupied by the Imperium despite Prime Minister Dreand Yens thinking he could represent his people through diplomatic talks, during which he had declined the Imperium's low offer for the moon's carnium supply. Only realizing how the Imperium had set the stage for its operation, while he'd been distracted with lies about a new art expo and negotiations, after the fact, Yens later remarked that his people were wrapped up in chains while he was busy with "polite conversation."

#### With the criminal underworld

title: Imperium
text:
#### With the criminal underworld

> " None of you think of yourselves as servants . You are proud . You have carved out dominions for yourselves in the dark , won battles of fire and blood. You have territory, wealth, followers dedicated to fulfilling your every whim! But this is my imperium. Everything you have is due to my indulgence . You do serve. " ―Emperor Theron Mal, to the heads of galactic criminal families The Imperium remained invested in and had a relationship with the criminal underworld. The criminal faction Carmine Dawn , while secretly under the control of Vreth, maintained a working relationship with the Imperium. According to Enfys Nest of the Cloud-Riders, the Dawn used its profits to terrorize countless systems alongside the Imperials. The Imperium also was invested in the affairs of the Gruv Syndicate: when a slave revolt opened up on Cindral, an Imperial blockade was quickly dispatched to settle the uprising. Despite its investment in the criminal underworld, the Imperium would need to combat parts of it, which would distract from other campaigns like the war with the Free Coalition. Above all other syndicates, the Imperium had a special relationship with the Grak Clan, which was allowed to operate outside of Imperial law in return for certain valuable services. The relationship also saw the Imperium protect the Grak Clan's claim over Grak Space . While the Imperium could be very demanding with the Graks, clan leader Grukk respected Theron Mal and saw the importance of their work together.

title: Imperium
text: In the wake of the Battle of Cinderfall, the Imperium launched a crackdown against the criminal underworld to restore its suddenly-threatened image and calm the sudden rise in galactic piracy that hoped to take advantage of the developing situation. As such, the Imperium launched what seemed to be a pacification campaign and crackdown in the Outer Reach. In truth, however, this campaign targeted only "disruptive" criminal elements, such as the Son-tuul Pride . While Luck Luck Freidal's casino would be shut down despite its ties to the Imperium, criminal powers with which the Imperium maintained an "understanding," such as the Grak Clan, were ignored and allowed to continue their operations. In fact, the Imperium quietly allowed its allied criminal powers to take over what had been the business areas of the now-defeated factions. For example, the Imperium allowed the Graks to take over trade in Son-tuul territory in exchange for the continued supplying of resources.

title: Imperium
text: Various other criminal groups desired the relationship with the Imperium held by the Graks, with a chance seeming to open up after the Grak attack on the Sovereign manipulated into being by Carmine Dawn. Months later, Mal personally put an end to the Syndicate War by contacting the heads of various warring families, reminding them that they were all servants to his will: while they each had their own dominions, the galaxy overall was his to control, thus placing each crime lord under his rule as well. While he did promise any faction that could find Dawn leader Q'ira would rise in his estimation, his talk made it clear that each crime lord needed to think of themself as a servant to his will.

title: Imperium
text:
### Overview

> " —we mustn't forget that we have the credits. The credits to spend how we see fit. " ―Arsin Crassus, financier, who thought that money was the solution to the Imperium's problems

The Imperium adopted a planned economy, whereby production and distribution of goods were centralized and directed in the immediate aftermath of the Replica Wars. This policy of nationalization was called imperialization . Despite this, numerous third-party corporations were allowed to remain, with major loyalist companies Kuat Drive Yards and Sienar Fleet Systems producing the majority of the Imperium's land and space-based craft. Companies aligned with the Fractio of Independent Systems during the Replica Wars, such as the Artificer Union and Commerce Combine, were absorbed by the newly formed Imperium, and all Federation accounts plundered by Imperial financier Arsin Crassus. By 1 BVE, both Vektor Corporation and the Korrathi Engineering Corporation had been nationalized.

title: Imperium
text: Senator Vela Sess stated that the Imperium made use of kleptocractic economics , which entailed those in power claiming riches for themselves like thieves , all while the population was controlled via populist messaging, scaremongering, and propaganda. In truth, the average worker was able to be exploited, particularly in the Outer Reach, so as to support the state and the wealthy. Among the population, it was the wealthy, particularly those in the Core Reaches, who the Imperium was actually kind to. In addition to the Imperial Mining Institute , the Imperium held a close association with Mining Guild. Towards the end of the Galactic Civil War, Fleet Admiral Gallard Raxen began to nationalize all aspects of the Imperial production chain in the months following Mossfell, but the attempt proved unable to save the dying Imperium. The continued funding of the Imperial Military was hotly disputed. While briefly considered, it was decided that plundering the InterGalactic Banking Clan and other monetary bodies would plunge the galaxy into an economic depression.

title: Imperium
text:
In 19 BVE, the Republic credit was replaced by the Imperial credit, which became the standard currency in circulation throughout the Imperium. With the advent of the New Order, credits from the time of the Vantor Republic became worthless as they were phased out. Raising enough money for day-to-day life proved to be difficult for many Imperial citizens, yet the Imperium's propaganda made the regime seem more prosperous than it actually was. In one recorded speech, Senator Daho Sejan blamed economic and security issues on "terrorists" who hid among everyday citizens. As of 9 BVE, the Imperium's taxation of the Outer Reach had become oppressive. Since the Imperial credit was a fiat currency, credits from the Imperium gradually lost their value following the formation of the Concordat.

### Infrastructure

title: Imperium
text:
### Infrastructure

> " The Imperium sat at the center of the galaxy like an enormous black hole—forever sucking wealth and resources inward. Vantor glittered while those at the edges suffered. Worlds who had nothing left to give were abandoned to their fate and allowed to go dark. This is how Mal and his many advisors viewed the natural hierarchy of their New Order. " ―Beaumont Kin, The Rise and Fall of the Imperium A vast transportation network to connect Mal's vast Imperium served as the primary means of both civilian and military transport. Interstellar commerce and warfare primarily occurred along one of several major hyperspace lanes —considered trans-galactic highways—with their knowledge and existence dating back to well before the former Vantor Republic. With the major trade routes considered safe for hyperspace travel, their control was vital for maintaining an effective means of defense and galactic dominance. In smaller systems, hyperspace beacons could transmit their coordinates, allowing starships to make quick jumps to and from the system. As a result, destroying them could hinder enemy mobility and response times. Serving this vast system were spaceports, facilities where starships would dock and refuel, restock and rearm. Spaceships serving as fuel stations also existed in the vastness of the galaxy, along with major shipping ports such as Horizon Base .

title: Imperium
text: The Imperial Transit Authority oversaw transportation across the Imperium while the Imperial Boarding Inspection and Customs handled customs enforcement on those craft, as well as inspecting the starships themselves. Owing to the immense size of the Imperium, a vast, complex logistical network was maintained by the Imperial hierarchy, and as a result was both immensely interconnected and extremely fragile. Locales such as Mardona III served as "warehouse worlds": planets turned storehouses for millions of metric tons of goods to fuel the Imperium. Imperial cargo ships often transported these resources across the galaxy; slovenly and low-quality personnel, or fresh recruits just out of the Academy, often crewed these vessels, owing to their rather menial task. The T-44 landspeeder saw use by members of the Imperial Military for transport. Despite Imperial propaganda painting the picture of a government interested in uplifting life for all who fell under the Imperial flag, the Imperial system, its taxation program, and general expansion were built around uplifting life in the Core Reaches, extracting the wealth of the outer regions and funneling it inward.

title: Imperium
text:
As once noted by Dorian Quill, the entire galaxy ran on Tibanna gas as a vital fuel source. As such, the Imperial annexation of Aether Spire and Mistral overall was an advantage to the Imperium. After the Battle of Mossfell, the lockdown of the Anoat sector—where Tibanna gas was found in large quantities, such as on Mistral—proved to be a danger to the young Concordat, which suddenly was cut off from a major source of fuel in its earliest days. According to Quill's fears, the Imperium would effectively keep itself in control of the galaxy by maintaining control over the galactic fuel supply, such as through its continued rule over Mistral. Vela Sess and Elira Solen further suspected the Imperium would attempt to take over vital resources—whether they be food, fuel, or building materials—in order to keep itself in control of the galaxy.

### Communications and media

#### Overview

> " Citizen reporting has been a key tool in maintaining peace and order across the Imperium. " ― Alton Kastle

title: Imperium
text:
### Communications and media

#### Overview

> " Citizen reporting has been a key tool in maintaining peace and order across the Imperium. " ― Alton Kastle

Acquiring much of the galactic communications systems from the former Vantor Republic, the Imperium nationalized the HoloNet News and its galaxy-spanning broadcasts and hyperspace-powered communication systems. The new Imperial Holovision was overseen by the Ministry of Information, who in tandem with the Imperial Press Corps, ensured reporting stayed in line with "acceptable" news coverage and government policy. While the Imperial holoNet was the only state-sanctioned news agency, local news outlets that supported the Imperium were allowed to remain. Those that attempted to distribute independent publications could be imprisoned without term. It was also law that the Imperial HoloNet be broadcast at all times in every drinking establishment.

title: Imperium
text:
As expected, the galactic HoloNet remained one of the most-viewed news stations in the galaxy, forming public opinion and reporting on pro-Imperial issues and events. When military objectives trumped civilian information, the Imperium shut down the local HoloNet in varying sectors, and prioritized HoloNet transmissions to the military, giving Mal and his armed forces near-instantaneous communication across the entire galaxy. The Imperium even turned leisure activities, such as sports broadcasts, into extensions of its will: the popular grav-ball sport was turned into little more than a recruitment tool for the Imperium during its rule. Following the Battle of Mossfell, the Concordat abolished the Imperium's restrictions and censorship on HoloNet and encouraged the creation of several HoloNet channels including the Queen of the Core Network to win over the galactic public after it assumed control by 5 AVE.

#### Controlling history

title: Imperium
text:
#### Controlling history

> " The Imperium's been erasing the Aetheri from history, step by step. First they said the Aetheri tried to murder the last chancellor—Mal, before he was Emperor—in some sort of coup at the war's end. It's what I grew up hearing. " " I heard that version from the older officers. It never made any sense because— " " Because you were taught there weren't many Aetheri to begin with, right? That they were relics, mostly forgotten? That's the trouble when they keep changing the story. Nah, there were thousands of them, and real influential in the Republic. Believe me, you hear a lot about the legend of the Aetheri and Synth Flux when you join the Free Coalition. " " How do you know it's not all propaganda on your—on the insurgent side? " " I don't. That's the nasty thing about the Emperor changing history. Leaves you doubting, doesn't it? " ― Nath Tensent and Yrica Quell

title: Imperium
text: In order to secure the "unlimited power" he so desperately longed for, Mal's imperium needed to take control of knowledge through the spread of information and manipulation of how history was taught. For example, in regards to the Aetheri Order and its systematic eradication, Mal had openly branded the Aetheri Order as traitors since the declaration of his regime, and subsequent propaganda spread via the Imperial-controlled HoloNet maintained that image. In a rally held during the first days of the Imperial Era, Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon claimed that the Aetheri had been behind the "Dissidents plots" that had so recently rocked the galaxy, but he promised Mal had seen through their lies to deliver the galaxy into a new age of freedom. Imperial propaganda painted the Aetheri as traitors who had subverted democracy, disrupted peace, and caused the Replica Wars with their strange abilities in an effort to usurp control of the galaxy for themselves. The aim of the Imperium was to purge the Aetheri from the memories and thoughts of its citizens beyond just wiping out its remaining members.

title: Imperium
text: As noted by Lyra Arsa , the Aetheri seemed to vanish from galactic memory and enter myth over the course of a few weeks, with very little grief towards the people who had once protected the Republic. The historian Madelin Sun believed that the Imperium's successful suppression of the Aetheri was an example of its rule by fear.
