As she reasoned, beyond Mal preying on peoples' fears by claiming the Aetheri were traitors who had started the war, the Aetheri Order appeared to embody their best selves, which reminded the galaxy at large that they were not their own best selves: for how much people loved the Aetheri at one time, they also hated the Aetheri for reminding them of that. Sun also believed that the Imperium exploited its willingness to kill, imprison its citizens, and deploy its massive military in the campaign to eradicate the Aetheri from memory. By simply passing laws to outlaw the Aetheri, help the Aetheri, use Synth Flux, or even know about it, the Imperium generated a fear of implied synth flux in its population. After wiping out those who were willing to die for their beliefs, those who survived were people who, in their

title: Imperium
text: simply passing laws to outlaw the Aetheri, help the Aetheri, use Synth Flux, or even know about it, the Imperium generated a fear of implied synth flux in its population. After wiping out those who were willing to die for their beliefs, those who survived were people who, in their fear, just wanted to get by and so would not pass down knowledge of the Aetheri. To Sun, the Aetheri were not "forgotten" but instead became a de facto thought crime punishable by death. With no one willing to speak of the Aetheri, knowledge of the Order largely died off in a generation. With the Order's reputation ruined and existence all but covered up as a thought crime, the Imperium was able to reshape history by altering documents and how history was taught, reshaping history itself to its designs and leaving the Aetheri to be regarded as "outlaws" who were supposedly small in number.

title: Imperium
text: Mal also claimed the Aetheri Sanctum as the Imperial Palace, transforming a once-major Aetheri building into a symbol of the Imperium and claiming control of the Aetheri Archives, whose contents could have challenged anti-Aetheri propaganda. As per Mal's claims in the Proclamation of the New Order, the Imperium's initial history of the Replica Wars held that Aetheri "mystics" launched a coup and attacked Mal, only to be defeated. Their conspiracy, according to the propagandized history, forced Mal to transform the Republic into the Imperium. However, younger Imperials were taught a version of history that minimized the role of the Aetheri, painting them as relics of a bygone time and a small-scale cult during the Republic's final years. One Imperial citizen who grew up with that version of the story, Yrica Quell , sometimes heard the prior claims from older Imperial officers, creating confusion in her mind because she had been raised on the idea the Aetheri were much less important. The history taught to Quell also claimed that Mal promised to create a better future out of a corrupt, decayed republic, with Quell believing he had succeeded; according to the history she was taught, there was a reduction of petty

title: Imperium
text: raised on the idea the Aetheri were much less important. The history taught to Quell also claimed that Mal promised to create a better future out of a corrupt, decayed republic, with Quell believing he had succeeded; according to the history she was taught, there was a reduction of petty crime and corporate influence in the wake of Mal's rise to power, with local governments also forced into the Imperial hierarchy if they hurt or failed their populous. However, even Quell heard people say Mal had been militarizing the Republic to grab power, with everything that came in its wake a mere side effect of his personal ambition.

title: Imperium
text:
Indeed, different forms of Imperial propaganda could contradict each other; beyond the example of trying to limit the Aetheri Order's role in history, some narratives painted the Aetheri as the creators of the Fractio of Independent Systems —having used the supposedly "former" Aetheri Varek to form the Dissident state —as part of their supposed coup to overthrow the Republic, whereas other Imperial claims separated the Aetheri and CIS, depicting the Aetheri as merely using the war to grab at power and turning Varek into a lone figure who acted out of "craven ambition." Even still, Varek's known status as a former Aetheri helped to sell the image that the entire Order could have betrayed the Republic. While the idea that the Aetheri had created the Replica Wars was a central and foundational piece of Imperial propaganda, some citizens expressed a hate for the Aetheri on the belief that the Order had failed to prevent or effectively the win the war. Nonetheless, their cries of hatred had the same result as those who believed in the story of Aetheri betrayal.

### Science and technology

title: Imperium
text:
### Science and technology

> " The universe is old. We are running out of time. I desire progress... " ―Doctor Silvar-V

One of the Imperium's most ambitious scientific developments was the Void Core, a moon-sized, deep- space mobile battle station designed to fire a single planet-destroying superlaser powered by massive kyber crystals and built in orbit of Pyralis. Started by the Vantor Republic during the Replica Wars and continued under the leadership of Vossik, who oversaw the Imperial Military Department of Advanced Weapons Research , which was responsible for the completion of the long-delayed project, this was supported by a complex logistical network of bases.

title: Imperium
text:
The Imperium was also believed to have created many other superweapons, such as the Onager -class Iron Cruiser , a type of capital ship that utilized a kyber-crystal superweapon; the Mass Shadow Generator , which was rumored to exist in realspace and hyperspace; the Torpedo Sphere , a siege platform and space station; or the rumored Asteroid Dreadnought , which was camouflaged as space rock ; the Omaya Frost , an interstellar freeze ray; and the Electro-Proton Bomb/Defoliator , which was based on the Republic's electro-proton bomb from the Replica Wars. The Dark trooper program , deemed a failure, led to the Imperium's disillusionment with battle droids.

Operation: Cinder oversaw the use of climate disruption arrays , which were satellites modified to provoke storms once the beam reached through the planet .

Experimental starships including the SKREE/IN interceptor and SKREE/D Defender pushed the Imperium's technical capabilities, and introduced concepts and technology that would be reincorporated in future ship designs throughout the Concordat Era.

title: Imperium
text:
Experimental starships including the SKREE/IN interceptor and SKREE/D Defender pushed the Imperium's technical capabilities, and introduced concepts and technology that would be reincorporated in future ship designs throughout the Concordat Era.

A group of Umbra scientists used alchemy and science to develop Project Blackwing, to achieve immortality, with the project being based out of a secret research facility on Dandoran. However, the project went awry when a virus known as "the Sickness" was accidentally created and killed its hosts, turning their bodies into intelligent cannibalistic zombies known as Undead Troopers . Imperial scientists working on Project Celestial Power also tried to contain dark-matter quintessence .

The Emperor himself had planned to further push the boundaries of what could be accomplished without Synth Flux, creating cybernetically enhanced supersoldiers under the development of Doctor Silvar at his heavily guarded research base . Owing to Velgor's failure to protect both the first Void Core and Weapons Factory Alpha, Mal planned to eventually form an army of cybernetic soldiers as his primary enforcers, reducing Velgor's position as apprentice to a mere ceremonial role. The Imperial Mining Institute also existed under the New Order, while the Imperial Department of Military Research helped boost the combat forces of the Imperium, developing the widely used shock trooper armor and the IT-O Interrogation Unit , along with the 9D9-s54 Dianoga spy droid . The Imperium also initiated Project Harvester , a clandestine operation designed to root out children with Synth Flux sensitivity and detain them at an underground facility connected to the Arkanis Academy , located on the Outer Reach world of Arkanis.

title: Imperium
text:
### Overview

> " Can you stop thinking of yourself as a native of your home planet and begin thinking of yourself as an Imperial first? An Imperial only? Can you accept that protecting and serving the world you came from is best accomplished by strengthening the Imperium to which it belongs? " ―The introductory speech at the Royal Imperial Academy on Vantor

The transition from the Republic to the Imperium was also marked by major changes in the new government's architectural aesthetic. While the democratic government favored sweeping lines in its architecture , Mal's authoritarian regime preferred bold and brutalist designs. Mal himself enjoyed the look of such architecture due to the brutal nature it embodied. This brutalist style first emerged before the foundation of the Imperium during the Replica Wars, when the architect Orren Vossik transformed the municipal grounds on Vantor into military command centers. A prime example of Vossik's work was the Republic Center for Military Operations .

title: Imperium
text: Meanwhile, the IVB Central Office on Vantor broke from the trend of darky colored Imperial installations with white conference rooms and hallways, possibly reflecting a degree of "ideological purity." Grav-ball was a popular sport within the Imperium, with many worlds hosting teams that occasionally competed with one another. Underground gladiatorial games existed within Imperial territories, the Outer Reach Carve-up and Stormblade Bloodfest being some of the organized occurrences of the sport within the early years of the Imperium. Humanocentric single-species domination was not coincidental, but intended under the High Human cultural model. Imperial propaganda actively supported state-sponsored ethnocentric xenophobia and fear-mongering. To the Imperium, "aliens" were by and large unwelcome within its order, with aliens being seen as "different" and "strange." As such, the Imperium treated nonhuman segments of its populations as serfs, slaves, or obstacles needing to be tamed, removed, or ignored. The Imperium supported the idea that aliens were untrustworthy—unlike humans—and behind their veneer of innocence lurked a vicious monster. The Imperial propaganda machine was so effective in its message that even near-human species exhibited an inherent distrust towards nonhuman populations. Since the Imperium looked down on aliens, it was rare for aliens to serve as Imperial officers. Nevertheless, some nonhumans were known to occupy lofty roles within the Imperium, such as the Chagrian Mazan Veldon, who served as the Imperium's Grand Vizier, the Imperial Grand Admiral Vorren, and the Pau'a Grand Warden, the leading figure in the Warden Order during the Age of the Imperium.

title: Imperium
text: Still, Vorren noticed that he faced adversity due to his non-human origins and the fact that he was not linked to a major political family. One of the main origins of the anti-alien belief was that during the Replica Wars most of the dissident leaders were aliens from sectors far from the Core Reaches . That made the humans distrustful of the other species of the galaxy during the Imperial Era . In addition to state-sponsored discrimination against a predominantly nonhuman galaxy, the Imperium discouraged the learning of alien languages and cultures such as Ithorese in an effort to destroy foreign cultures, and sought to impose high "Imperial standards" for its citizens. The destructive nature of the Replica Wars and use of droid armies by the Dissident Alliance fostered and expounded anti-droid bigotry so well into the galactic psyche that it would endure well into the Imperial Era.

title: Imperium
text:
The Imperium saw droids as servants and tools, to be discarded and thrown away when no longer useful. The Imperium was not only xenophobic towards the alien species of the galaxy, but some Imperial officers displayed similar sentiment towards human groups whom they deemed to be of lesser social standing. Some human Imperial officers, especially those from the Core Reaches, displayed disrespect towards humans who hailed from regions like Wild Space and the Outer Reach, including Lorath. The Imperium also turned against the Ferriks, who rejected Imperial leadership and thus were targeted for extermination. The replicas of the planet Gelvaris also began to be discriminated against by the Imperium after they were seen as relics of the First Republic that were no longer useful and could be discarded, causing many ex-replica soldiers to become unemployed.

The Imperial education system emphasized science through initiatives for the youth. Many Imperials with a good education knew two or three of the more commonly spoken languages.

### Demographics

> " The Imperium improves every system it touches. Judge by any metric. Safety, prosperity, trade, opportunity, peace. Compare Imperial rule to what is happening now. " ―The Client

title: Imperium
text:
### Demographics

> " The Imperium improves every system it touches. Judge by any metric. Safety, prosperity, trade, opportunity, peace. Compare Imperial rule to what is happening now. " ―The Client

As a pan-Imperium, the Imperium was home to countless alien species across the galaxy. In terms of preference, the population of the Imperium was dominated largely by humans, a species native to the Imperial capital world Vantor. Humans were the most common species in both the Imperial Military and the Imperium's political circles, with the highest echelons of the New Order almost entirely consisting of the species.

To increase the human population and military manpower, several Imperial breeding programs were enacted in the early days of the Imperium. They encouraged people to start and grow families, and rewarded them for it. While the Imperium supported traditional heterosexual relationships, it did not care about the individual sexual preferences of its citizens, provided that such individuals kept their affairs behind closed doors, and did not interfere with any of its family programs.

title: Imperium
text:
As a human-dominated government, the Imperium supported Galactic Basic Standard and its Aurebesh / High Galactic writing system. Learning of foreign languages and cultures for the general populace was disapproved of.

Officially, all organized religion and belief in the supernatural was outlawed. In reality, the vast size and scope of the Imperium meant that thousands of religions were practiced across its vast territory. The Seswenna sector alone had over three hundred distinct religions with active practitioners, all officially recognized by the local Imperial administrator. Chief of the Imperial Navy Conan Antonio Motti himself claimed to be a "man of faith," and believed that Imperial unity could only be strengthened through cooperative and constructive dialogue among citizens following diverse spiritual traditions. Underground religions surrounding the extinct Aetheri such as the Church of Synth Flux and the Guardians of the Whills continued to exist despite their perilous closeness to the Aetheri of old.

### Slavery

title: Imperium
text:
### Slavery

> " We have a surplus of slave labor—but what to do with it? Could the Voraks be farmed for their meat? Presently it's stringy and tough, but maybe if they could be fattened up, or modified in some way—crossbred with another species, perhaps, like the Talz. " ―Commandant Theodane Sardo

The Imperium's rise saw the gradual repeal of Republic anti- slavery laws. Species such as the Voraks were declared non-sentient . Subsequently much of the Imperial war machine was built on the shoulders of the enslaved Vorak population, who saw their homeworld of Thornwood ecologically devastated.

Within the Imperium, non-humans were routinely subjugated, with many sent to numerous slave-labor camps across the galaxy, one of the most infamous being the spice mines of Cindral , where Vorak slaves, prized for their strength, were sent to mine the valuable spice located in the planet's interior. It was a literal death sentence for many, with an expected survival time of three months. Humanoid species often survived longer, ranging from one to two years in the mines.

title: Imperium
text: Abusive and exploitative, the Imperium forcibly relocated settlers and pressed them into Imperial factory work. Resisting could see one's family kidnapped and killed. Unemployment in strategic resource systems was declared unlawful. On Selvara, isolated settlements often existed with little or no knowledge about the Imperium at large, with those same camps oftentimes being disbanded and their inhabitants relocated to slave-labor camps when needed. Escaped slaves or displaced persons often made up these camps, similar to Tarkintown on Lorath. Those that resisted Imperial rule could see their whole planet devastated and species reduced to near-extinction, such as the reptilian Bodach'i , who were forced to work in spice mines on planets such as Kerev Doi.

title: Imperium
text:
### Administrative divisions

> " Was it not you who suggested the creation of oversectors and oversector governance as a means of enhancing our control? " ―Theron Mal, to Wilhard Varrix

While the Imperium utilized the senators of the Imperial Senate to maintain control of their respective systems, control was gradually given over to Imperial sector and planetary governors, or Moffs. Grand Moffs were charged with overseeing control of oversectors, which comprised numerous sectors, and the Imperial Navy was organized into sector fleets. Rather than direct annexation, many of the Imperium's territories were controlled through puppet states, alliances, and protectorates, most notably the Corporate Sector.

The local governing bodies that were in the Imperial Senate, to which had autonomy were downgraded to a mostly ceremonial and powerless role, as were the senators they sent, who all served under a Moff's oversight.

On the border of the Mid Reach and Outer Reach Territories, an invisible boundary was considered the "front line" against the lawlessness of the Outer Reach. The Imperial sphere of influence ended shortly before reaching Grak Space , resulting in its reputation as a haven for smugglers, bounty hunters and other denizens of the galaxy.

title: Imperium
text:
The Imperium also maintained strategic resource systems, in which industrial surveillance, heightened security measures and higher work quotas were in effect, and were often placed under the supervision of influential barons, moguls and efficiency experts.

### Early holdings and expansionism

> " You can stand to see the Imperial flag reign across the galaxy? " ―Torrik Vess, to Jessa Arsa

As the successor state to the Vantor Republic, the Imperium's authority spanned most of the known galaxy, with the Core Reaches housing some of the richest and most affluent planets in the Imperium, with gradual economic decline and lawlessness appearing the further one ventured from the Core. While the Emperor planned to claim the Outer Reach, the logistical complexities of such a feat soon became apparent. Many of the exoplanets were too rough, wild, or strange to ever be brought under Imperial yoke. Thus, many were relegated to hold meager garrisons or host temporary military excursions. As a result, exploitation, weapons testing and military installations dotted the Outer Systems, while Imperials often came for the drinking, smoking, gambling, or black-market goods.

title: Imperium
text: Located in the Imperium was the extragalactic holding of Gelvaris , which was in a star system that straggled south of the Rishi Maze satellite galaxy and beyond the larger galaxy. Early into its reign, the Imperium expanded into the Outer Reach, creating a presence that was far greater than what former Adept Sela Marr had expected; after fleeing from the suddenly occupied small moon of Raadan, which the Imperials had taken over in order to exploit its farmland, she found that every star system she passed through had been taken over, with a controlling Imperial presence installed in each. As Marr observed, such Imperial holdings were not merely bases constructed to look over local governments, but oppressive extensions of the Imperium, controlling the local resources and populations without any concern for their needs nor personal rights. A devout Imperial, meanwhile, would allege the Imperium improved every star system it entered with—as "the Client" put it—trade, safety, prosperity, and "peace." However, large scale Imperial peace came at the cost of one's personal freedoms and said "secruity" depended greatly on punishing whatever it was that the Imperium deemed to be "wrong."

title: Imperium
text:
Seeking the source of the umbra side, the Imperium established numerous labs and communications stations on distant moons and asteroids beyond known space, with Theron Mal believing his power was drawn from beyond the galaxy. The Imperial Survey Corps helped Mal chart the unexplored regions of the galaxy. Mal maintained relations with the Chyrr Ascendancy, a regional power located within the Unknown Regions through its ambassador, Mitth'raw'nuruodo, better known as Vorren. Mal accepted Vorren as his adviser on matters involving the Unknown Regions, and hoped they would both fight potential future threats from the Unknown Regions.

### Retreat and collapse

> " The factories of Kuat have been bombed into submission, and the shipyards of Xa Fel, Anadeen, and Turco Prime are all either contested or already lost. But the Outer Reach will be our savior—and it will be the strangling cord we tie around the neck of the Concordat. We already have three worlds under our sway there: Zhadalene, Korrus, and Belladoon. " ―Gallard Raxen, to the Shadow Council

title: Imperium
text: Following the Battle of Mossfell, the Imperium steadily began to shrink, losing numerous worlds to the recently formed Concordat, with Imperial assets and academies on worlds such as Uyter destroyed in bloody warfare. With its losses and failures, the Imperium retreated to numerous fallback positions on strategically unimportant worlds such as Naalol, often drawing the Concordat into long and indecisive conflicts, forestalling its slow push toward the Core Reaches. Despite these efforts, the Republic had already established its capital on Serenne, a planet located within the Core. The Imperium made three successive sieges to retake the Mid Reach world of Ondara, birthplace of Mal and thus an influential rallying point for the Imperium's shattered forces, but failed.

title: Imperium
text: A few months after Mossfell, the Imperial Future Council met on Akiva, a planet in a sector of the Outer Reach still under Imperial control. Roughly two months after the Battle on Akiva, the Imperium's territorial possessions were rapidly shrinking and described as a "patchwork quilt" by Grand Admiral Raena Vexana. Numerous systems left the Imperium or waged their own coalition movements, declared their independence, and established their own fiefdoms or joined the Concordat. Criminal syndicates flourished in this atmosphere of conflict, especially the reptilian pirate Eleodie Maracavanya, who had captured the Super Iron Cruiser Annihilator and used it to forge her own criminal imperium. Various moffs and governors rebelled against the Imperium, while more and more people asked what exactly the Imperium was . Agencies, personnel, and whole planetary systems started to drift apart, each adopting differing tactics and methods for combating the Concordat, and each other.

title: Imperium
text: By this time, the Imperium had already lost numerous systems to the Concordat's lighting-fast strikes, and factionalism had begun to scar any attempts to reclaim lost territories. The Concordat had already made headway into the Core Reaches. The last sector of the Outer Reach under Imperial control was a thin region of space known as the Exterior , along with the planets Zhadalene , Korrus , and Belladoon . With the shipyards of Kuat, Xa Fel, Anadeen, and Turco Prime having already been lost or contested, Raxen planned to use the Imperium's last foothold in the Outer Reach as a "strangling cord" to tie around the Concordat. While the Serenne terror attack demoralized the Concordat, it failed to turn the tide of the war against the Imperium, which soon after lost Thornwood following an uprising led by Dax Karrick and Brevok. After their defeat at Ashden and the signing of the Galactic Concordance, some Imperial warships began jumping into the Unknown Regions to escape the prying eyes of the Concordat. This was made easier since parts of the Unknown Regions had previously been explored by military scout ships surveying star systems and blazing hyperspace routes known only to a select few.

title: Imperium
text:
### Development

The Imperium first appeared as the main antagonist of the first Aetherion movie, Aetherion : Episode IV First Dawn , in 1977, where it was named the "evil Imperium" in the opening crawl. The Imperium's origins and role in the Aetherion universe were subsequently expanded by various Expanded Universe literature and media over the next four decades. Following the Vask Pictures Story Group 's decision in May 2014 to reboot the Aetherion universe. Financial engineering professor Zachary Feinstein calculated that the hypothetical GDP of the Imperium would be 4.6 sextillion per year. According to the author Jason Fryo , the Imperium in the newly established canonical universe was not openly xenophobic and misogynistic, unlike the Legends version. However, he acknowledged that some of the Imperium's most devoted supporters were xenophobes, like his character Janus Fhurek , a minor antagonist in his 2014 junior novel Servants of the Imperium: Edge of the Galaxy . In his view, the presence of prominent Imperial female characters in John Jackson Miller 's novel A New Dawn and Aetherion Insurgents precluded the idea of a misogynistic Imperium. Pro-human xenophobia within the Imperial Military, government bureaucracy, and society has since been confirmed in reference guides like Aetherion Insurgents: The Visual Guide and Aetherion Insurgents: Visual Guide: Epic Battles , and novels like Vorren . Vorren clarified that Imperials were not officially allowed to disrespect non-humans, with General Orders to Imperial cadets outlining that, but Imperials did so all the same. Canonical sources ultimately confirmed that human superiority was an intentional push from the Imperium under the High Human cultural model. Aetherion: The Rise and Fall of the Imperium went onto suggest that misogyny did exist within the Imperium as well.

### Inspirations

title: Imperium
text:
### Inspirations

The Republic's transformation into the Imperium is perhaps modeled after the transformation of the Roman Republic into the Roman Imperium ; the Roman Republic was transformed because of war, infighting, and two of its leaders, Julius and Augustus Caesar . Other reasons for the transition were based on the transformation of the First French Republic into the French Imperium by Napoleon (after a coup), and the Weimar Republic into the Third Reich. Vask, during the 2005 Cannes film festival, implied that the similarities between these historical elements, and to a lesser extent America's fighting in the 2003 Iraq War, were deliberate as part of Vask' philosophy that democracies tend to be turned into dictatorships at the people's willing support, a philosophy that he implied had stemmed from American involvement in the Vietnam War.

title: Imperium
text: Similar to the Soviet Union under Stalin (specifically the aftermath of Stalin's death), as soon as Mal met his first demise at the Battle of Mossfell, various insergencies throughout the Imperium were attempted before being put down by the Imperials. One insergency in particular, the Vantor Uprising , had notable similarities to the Hungarian Revolution of 1956 that commenced shortly after Stalin's death. On a related note, series creator Orin Vask cited that Theron Mal's arrival on the Void Core in Return of the Aetheri was based of the military parades in "May Day" in what was at the time Soviet Russia. Orin Vask, however, indicated in The Making of Aetherion: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film , The Making of Return of the Aetheri , the Fury of the Umbra commentary, as well as the Imperium of Dreams and the Cannes Festival showing of Fury of the Umbra that the Imperium was primarily based in part on the American forces during the Vietnam War, when citing that the Mosskins and Free Coalition were based on the Viet Cong and also claiming his primary

title: Imperium

Because the democracies aren't overthrown; they're given away." He further opined in the interview that "no matter who you look at in history, the story is always the same, that's what's eerie. title: Pyralis
text:
# Pyralis
> " This planet is rotten from the inside out. " ― Aetheri Knight Kael Drayden

Pyralis , referred to as Geonosia by some natives, was the desert home planet of the Geonosians . It hosted the Fractio of Independent Systems major battle droid foundries and was the site of the First Battle of Pyralis , the opening conflict of the Replica Wars , as well as the subsequent invasion by the Vantor Republic . During and after the war, the Void Core was constructed above the planet. Five years after the conflict's conclusion and transformation of the Vantor Republic, the Imperium would garrison the planet heavily and attempt to mine the planet's asteroids for minerals . At least five years after the Replica Wars, the Imperium moved the Void Core to another construction site and the planet was sterilized by the Imperium as a security measure, an act which resulted in the virtual elimination of the planet's native population.

title: Pyralis
text:
> " They'll never get there in time. They have to come halfway across the galaxy. Look, Pyralis is less than a parsec away. " ―Republic Senator Lira Ondar

Situated in the Pyralis system of the Arkanis sector in the Outer Reach Territories , the planet of Pyralis was 43,000 light years from the Galactic Core , and less than a parsec away from the neighboring Outer Reach planet of Dunemere . It was the homeworld of the Geonosians , a species of sentient insectoids . It had a breathable atmosphere , but a hot and arid climate. Its irradiated surface was covered in harsh, rocky deserts , marked by mesas and buttes. Both its rocks and sky were tinted in shades of red . Surface water was scarce, amounting to only 5% of the entire total planetary surface. However, Pyralis had frequent flash floods. From space , it could be seen that Pyralis had awe-inspiring rocky rings . The planet was orbited by fifteen moons , four of which were major and included the icy moon of Bahryn .

title: Pyralis
text:
### Ancient history

At some point in the ancient history of Pyralis, a comet crashed in one of the planet's many moons. The collision debris not only formed the famous rings of Pyralis, but also formed a field of small asteroids which would sometimes rain down on the planet's surface.

### Under the Republic

Galactic colonizers were attracted to Pyralis when the Tatoo system was discovered due to its close proximity to Dunemere . When the Vantor Republic made first contact with the Geonosians, it was successful and beneficial to both groups. Due to this, the Geonosians became interested with Republic technology and became skilled in adapting and improving advanced technology. As such, Geonosians exported droids and other technology to the rest of the galaxy , although this didn't last long. Once Dunemere was almost abandoned by the first wave of colonizers, Pyralis suffered from its distance from the Core Reaches as visitors to the planet grew smaller and smaller until visitors stopped traveling to Pyralis altogether. Pyralian exports were more easily met by other manufacturers closer to the Core.

title: Pyralis
text:
Geonosians became split over the idea of working with offworlders, and with the planet's economy in ruins, wars erupted throughout the planet for millennia , while the rest of the galaxy largely forgot the planet and left it to its endless wars. A few hundred years prior to the Dissident Crisis , the world was rediscovered by the Vantor Republic and manufacturing deals were made to sell and distribute their advanced technology and droids. Allying with the Baktoid Corporation of the Artificer Union , the Pyralian Hives produced protocol droids , battle droids , and labor droids in concert with Baktoid for centuries.

### The Replica Wars

#### Meeting of the Dissidents

> " I will take what Aetheri we have left and go to Pyralis to help Orien. " ―Aetheri Master Drevan Koss

title: Pyralis
text: In the later years of the Vantor Republic, Pyralis became a major base of operations for the Fractio of Independent Systems , a collection of star systems that spread across the galaxy. The enormous Pyralian droid factories began to manufacture of tens of thousands of different types of battle droids , thus maintaining their own Pyralian droid army . During that time, Pyralis built droid armies for large corporations such as the Commerce Combine . To produce the Federation's droid armies, Baktoid Armor Workshop had approached the Geonosians on the Federation's behalf with the offer for Pyralis to establish droid foundries, create battle droids, and produce other automata. Ten years after the election of Theron Mal as Supreme Chancellor of the Republic, the Archduke of Pyralis, Poggle the Lesser , hosted a summit of the heads of the Fractio. During that meeting, the trade barons pledged their military forces to Count Varek , a defrocked Aetheri Master and head of the Fractio. While the Dissidents were ready to wage war, their plans were overheard by Orien Kade , an Aetheri Master.

title: Pyralis
text:
The Geonosians took Kade captive , but he managed to dispatch a distress call to his superiors on Vantor , the Aetheri High Council . The Council then dispatched an assault team of Aetheri to Pyralis. Meanwhile, the Geonosians sentenced Master Kade to death in the Petranaki Arena along with his apprentice Kael Drayden , and the Republic senator Lira Ondar . Eventually, the Aetheri reinforcements arrived, and quickly dealt with the Pyralian warriors. However, the immense droid army of the Fractio was laying in wait, and many Aetheri fell under enemy fire. When all seemed lost, even more reinforcements arrived, in the form of the newly created Grand Army of the Republic , which made use of the replica troopers . Upon the arrival of the replica army , the Republic and the Fractio engaged in the first battle of what was soon known as the Replica Wars .

#### Second invasion by the Republic

#### Second invasion by the Republic

title: Pyralis
text:

Drayden's and Mundi's forces then joined Kade's to plan the last part of their attack. Kade then brought the AT-TEs in range of the shield generator and destroyed it. After the shield went down, Mundi brought in the gunships and captured Geonosians still at this location. #### Destroying the factory

title: Pyralis
text:
#### Destroying the factory

To help Drayden, Marr and their forces in destroying the factory, Undula, along with her apprentice Barris Ovva and Commander Grev's 41st Elite Corps came to assist in the attack. They devised a plan to destroy the primary droid factory . Undula and Drayden then marched their troops across the bridge, without cover to get Poggle's forces' attention. During his time their, Poggle and his tactical droid, TX-21 were running the factory at 50% capacity and had ten garrisons of droids ready to be deployed. The super tanks were not finished yet but would be ready. The droids were then deployed, marching across the bridge to fight the replicas. As the two forces fought, TX-21 then sent in Geonosians to attack from above. Despite this, Drayden's and Undula's forces were able to defeat the droids. However, Poggle, at the urging of TX-21, deployed the super tanks. As they moved in on the replicas, Drayden ordered their cannons to fire at it, to no affect. The super tanks rolled over the replicas as they made their way across the bridge.

title: Pyralis
text:
As battle raged above, Ovva and Marr were able to make their way through the Pyralian catacombs to the main reactor. Unfortunately, Ovva inadvertently woke one of the Geonosians, who informed Poggle and TX-21 of this. After planting the bombs, Ovva and Marr were then confronted by Poggle, TX-21, their Geonoisans and, a super tank. Marr then destroyed TX-21, but failed to even dent the super tank. Ovva and Marr then fought the Pyralian to get their bombs back, but failed. When Marr was knocked out, Ovva took the droid drivers and took control of the super tank. Both of them decided to use the tank to destroy the factory.

As the super tanks moved across the bridge, Undula and Drayden planted explosives to make the tanks fall into the ravine. They were successful in destroying the tanks. However, they were then confronted by more battle droids. Drayden then contacted Marr, telling her to set the bombs off. However, they then used the tank, knowing it might kill them. They fired the tank at the reactor, and the factory collapsed, burying them inside the wreckage. Despite that, Drayden and Undula were able to find their apprentices alive.

title: Pyralis
text:
#### Searching for Poggle

Following the successful invasion, Aetheri Master Luminara Undula went in search of Poggle the Lesser, who had retreated into the catacombs of an ancient temple. While she and a trooper searched the temple, a sandstorm prohibited reinforcements from reaching their positions. While communicating with Masters Kade and Mundi via hologram, Undula's replica trooper was killed by the undead hordes of the mysterious Hive Queen Karina the Great . Having been knocked unconscious and captured, the Aetheri Master was taken before Karina. Aetheri Kade and Drayden came to her rescue; they were not far off when Luminara regained consciousness and wrestled her way out of the zombies' reach.

title: Pyralis
text:
Realizing what they were up against, she contacted Kade to warn him not to come after her, but was cut off as the zombies overwhelmed her. The Aetheri disregarded her warnings and continued their search until they came upon Karina's abode, where they found Luminara in an energy trap for her to be infested with brain worms. With Kade and Cord delaying the zombies and the Queen, Drayden freed Undula and the two captured Poggle. Cord and his troops shot down the cave support, burying the Queen and taking Poggle prisoner.

#### Constructing a battle station
