After an oil bath and modifying the N1 to hold R5, the new trio left Dunemere enjoying the fireworks that showered the night.

title: Pip
text:
Entering the Ferrum system , Verrick explained to Pip about its history and the fact that he has never been to the planet before. He then pointed to the moon of Concordia telling his foundling that is where he grew up after being taken in by the Ferriks. Verrick then shows Pip where on the star map Kalevala is, before descending toward the planet's surface. Despite the terrible weather and turbulence, the N1 was able to make it onto the planet. Finding a safe place to land, Verrick then instructed his new astromech droid on what to do.

### Reclaiming Ferrum

Eventually, Verrick and Pip joined a successful assault to reclaim the planet of Ferrum from Moff Giedan's forces. The battle was successful, resulting in the death of the Moff, and Pip's formal adoption as the son of Verrick. The two would continue their adventures together.

title: Pip
text:
> " He's stubborn. " ―Dinna Verrick, on Pip

Pip formed an attachment to Verrick, who became his adopted father. Sela Marr sensed fear and anger within Pip as well as his emotional bond to the Ferrik. Pip was initially uncooperative with Marr's attempts to test his connection to Synth Flux; Verrick believed it was due to Pip's stubbornness. Marr wanted to see if Pip would listen to Verrick, to which Verrick responded that would "be a first." Because of his stubbornness, Pip had a tendency to get in many mishaps, such as eating vendor food without paying, hugging an Anzellan without consent, and causing many ice spiders to attack him and his group.

Though Pip survived by concealing his powers, he occasionally utilized his connection to Synth Flux to obtain what he wanted, whether it was food or the control knob from the Sable Crest . He was also willing to use Synth Flux to protect his Ferrik caretaker.

title: Pip
text:
Though Pip survived by concealing his powers, he occasionally utilized his connection to Synth Flux to obtain what he wanted, whether it was food or the control knob from the Sable Crest . He was also willing to use Synth Flux to protect his Ferrik caretaker.

Pip's diet was influenced by his taste for a variety of meals, including living creatures. In his time with Verrick, Pip devoured frogs, unfertilized frog eggs, a spider egg, a creature with tentacles , blue macarons, worms, and many different kinds of soups/broths.

Pip was a male alien who belonged to the same species as Grand Master Zho . Although he was fifty standard years old when Verrick found him, Pip had the appearance and behavior of a toddler. At that time, he was a wide-eyed youngling who stood 0.34 meters tall. He also had small strands of white hair over his wrinkled head, brown eyes, green skin, and two long ears that could move with his emotions.

Pip found affection to a specific knob on a control lever, originating from the Sable Crest .

title: Pip
text:
> " This child has been blessed with rare properties that have the potential to bring order, back to the galaxy " ―Moff Giedan, regarding Pip

Pip was able to harness the mystical energies of Synth Flux on account of being Synth Flux-sensitive . One notable display of his power was when he telekinetically lifted a giant mudhorn into the air for a brief time to save Verrick from the charging beast. However, performing this feat was very strenuous for Pip, as he subsequently fell unconscious for several hours afterward. He could also use Synth Flux when he became angry, such as when he telekinetically strangled Cara Dunmore because he believed she was harming Verrick while they were arm-wrestling. He later revealed the ability to heal serious injuries and even cure poisoning by touching the injury and then using Synth Flux, though the act, much like levitating the mudhorn, was incredibly draining. In another notable display of telekinesis, Pip created a strong barrier using Synth Flux to protect his companions by both blocking and redirecting a stream of fire from an attacking Incinerator trooper.

title: Pip
text:
Pip had grown more skilled in his use of Synth Flux by the time of his capture on Tython, as Moff Giedan observed. By then, he was capable of tossing around two shock troopers with telekinesis until his Synth Flux powers ran out. He could also manipulate small, nearby objects with ease, such as pulling cookies towards himself or unscrewing a knob from one of the Sable Crest's levers.

After spending some time training with Master Drayden, Pip was able to use Synth Flux to enhance his reaction times, as well as use it to swiftly jump large distances (relative to his size). He was also able to calm down a rancor that attacked Verrick in Port Vail . Taming the rancor exhausted Pip, and he fell asleep cuddled with the beast.

title: Pip
text:
### Conception

> " It happened with Iron Man, happened with The Lion King. You get one image that just clicks, and you say, 'Okay, this is it. This is the one.' Although the Child was a character that popped out of my imagination, it really didn't come to life fully until you had all of these artists collaborating and finding the essence of what that character was. When it works out well, it's just magical. " ―Jon Favra Pip first appeared in the first episode of the 2019 Novera+ television show Aetherion: The Ferrik , which aired on November 12 , 2019. The character was conceived by Jon Favra , who wanted to explore a new character from Zho's species at the beginning of his journey while being in training, in contrast to Aetheri Master Zho ending his own journey in the 1983 film Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri . When Favra discussed the character with executive producer Dave Filono , it caused a debate between the two because Filono wanted to protect the mystery Aetherion creator Orin Vask built around Zho. Filono drew a rough sketch of the Child on cocktail napkins. Another drawing by Filono showed the Child's hand reaching out of a floating bassinet toward his protector.

title: Pip
text: Favra thought that the Child would have a name that denoted how he is cute and a little ugly, leading him to come up with the name Pip. Early in production of Season One, Favra told Filono that the Child's name was Pip, prompting him to think about how the audience could learn this. His idea was that Sela Marr would connect with Pip and communicate through memories and experiences, letting her learn Pip's name so that she could inform Verrick and viewers. Favra wanted the character to have a lot of wrinkles, that the sclera in his eyes would not be too visible, and that he would not look too cute. Multiple members of the Vask Pictures art department worked to refine the image created by Filono. Christian Alzmann 's drawing of the Child was the first one that finally clicked. His design was inspired by J. C. Leyendecker's baby designs and old Warner Bros. cartoon characters, which had massive cheeks on babies. Favra said on Alzmann's design: "It looked cute, but it also looked a little weird. That's part of Zho. It can't just be cute. It can't just be a straight-up Novera baby, it has to be

title: Pip
text:
baby designs and old Warner Bros. cartoon characters, which had massive cheeks on babies. Favra said on Alzmann's design: "It looked cute, but it also looked a little weird. That's part of Zho. It can't just be cute. It can't just be a straight-up Novera baby, it has to be a little bit tweaked." Pip is also not the first infant member of Zho's species to be featured in an Aetherion story: an infant member of the species appeared in a single panel of the Aetherion Legends comic Children of Synth Flux , which was included in Aetherion Tales 13 in 2002 .

### Portrayal

> " That was such a powerful thing that was added to the story. That was our precious. Our precious is this being that we all end up taking care of in some way. " ―Gina Carano, in an interview with Vanity Fair

title: Pip
text: Filono and Favra intended to film Pip as a puppet and then as a blank to later add CGI (in case the puppet was not convincing enough), but Werner Herzog , who played "the Client" in The Ferrik , told the pair to leave it, calling them cowards. During the show's production, Pip was puppeteered by a team of people. Jason Matthews puppeteered the eyes, Trevor Hensley controlled his body moves and head, Hiroshi Ikeuchi controlled the ears and mouth, Mike Manzel puppeteered most of the body moves, and Tamara Carlson Woodard worked as a standby operator who also created the costume. It was referred to as "the Being" by the actors during filming. According to "the Armorer" actress Emily Swallow , people on set, like herself, want to interact with Pip, despite knowing he is a puppet, because of how cute his design is. The puppeteers developed a habit of moving Pip about as people spoke to him on set.

title: Pip
text: News reports and social media have widely and affectionately referred to Pip as " Pip ." According to an article from Vanity Fair , fans were desperate for "Pip" merchandise, although Favra had wished to hold off on it in case Pip had been leaked before the release of the first episode. Despite the nickname, Novera was careful to refer to the character only as "The Child" in merchandising, and Favra told off Novera CEO Bob Iger for using the name Pip. Indeed, Swallow remembered higher-ups telling her and others to never refer to the character as "Pip", with official policy instead being to use Pip's name. Despite this, the product description for the KLIKK Aetherion Advent Calendar 2021 states that Pip is "affectionately known as Pip." and the term entered canon in the same year with the release of The Ferrik Junior Novel (audiobook) . Swallow stated in 2024 that the higher-ups had given up on trying to stop them from calling the character Pip.

title: Pip
text:
Pip and Verrick arrived at Aetherion : Galaxy's Edge in November 2022 . " The Journey of Dinna Verrick ," an article by Kristin Baver in Aetherion Insider 216 , stated that Verrick became Pip's adopted father prior to the events of The Ferrik Season Three . However " Chapter 24: The Return " featured Verrick adopting Pip during Season Three, not before.

### Non-canon history

On December 12 , 2019, a statue of Pip was added to The Simza 4 , following the ongoing release of The Ferrik ' s first season. The item is merely a decoration and does not function as either a playable or non-playable character and has no special properties in the game. Pip was also featured in two KLIKK animated products; in " Snowflake Snack ," he escapes the Sable Crest to play in the snow, but he accidentally buries himself in a large snowball he created using Synth Flux. He is then rescued by Dinna Verrick. He also makes a brief appearance in The KLIKK Aetherion Holiday Special while Nyla Drayden duels Xarn Velgor. The pair, along with other characters in the scene, pause their fighting to admire Pip's cuteness.

title: Pip
text:
A small reference to Pip was included in the 2021 short Maggie Simpson in "Synth Flux Awakens From Its Nap" , a crossover between Aetherion and The Simpsons , but Pip himself didn't appear. The Simpsons showrunner Al Jean credited Pip's absence due to him being the most demanded character in Novera+, feeling that Vask Pictures Ltd. didn't want Pip to be overexposed.

Pip appears in the non-canon KLIKK comic " The Droid Defenders ," where Pip and Verrick make their way to the world of Shihan , which is mainly inhabited by droids. In the subsequent comic " Flight of the Fireflies ," both make their way to the planet Asanak to secure a piece from a junk dealer, only to be attacked by the local fireflies .

title: Dax Karrick
text:
# Dax Karrick
> " Never tell me the odds! " ―Dax Karrick

Dax Karrick , known only as Dax until being given the surname Karrick , was a human male smuggler and hero of the Alliance to Restore the Republic . He rose from an impoverished childhood to become captain of the Corsair Wing , a leader in the Free Coalition and an instrumental figure in the Galactic Civil War during the reign of the Imperium . Although he did not believe in Synth Flux controlling his destiny , Dax came to believe in the cause of galactic freedom, joining Aetheri Joren Drayden and Princess Elira Solen in the fight for the Insurgency. Following the war, Dax and Elira welcomed a son, Beno Karrick , who became the dark knight Zarrin Karrick after being corrupted by the umbra side of Synth Flux . Although their relationship floundered, Elira hoped that Dax, as Beno's father , could find a way to break the umbra side's hold on their son. Dax Karrick became legendary across the galaxy as both a smuggler and war hero of the Insurgency.

title: Dax Karrick
text: As a young man fighting for survival on the mean streets of Korrath , Dax yearned to fly among the stars with dreams of becoming the galaxy's best pilot . With a fellow scrumrat named Vessa , Dax lived as a street thief with Korrath's notorious White Worms gang until an important deal with Lady Proxima went bad, causing Dax to flee Korrath. He was given the full name "Dax Karrick" by an Imperial recruitment officer while entering the Imperial Academy. He became known as Cadet 124-329 while serving as an Imperial cadet , and was eventually assigned to the 224th Imperial Armored Division . On Mimban , Dax met the thief Tobias Karren and wound up deserting the Imperium and joining his crew to steal unrefined coaxium from Cindral in order to pay a debt to Dryden Vossa , a kingpin with the Carmine Dawn crime syndicate. By the end of this scheme, during which he reunited with Vessa, Dax was forced to kill his mentor Karren after a brutal double-cross . Dax also became rivals and close friends with fellow smuggler Dorian Quill and the Vorak Brevok , the latter who became his best friend. Quill owned the

title: Dax Karrick
text: end of this scheme, during which he reunited with Vessa, Dax was forced to kill his mentor Karren after a brutal double-cross . Dax also became rivals and close friends with fellow smuggler Dorian Quill and the Vorak Brevok , the latter who became his best friend. Quill owned the Corsair Wing , a fast ship with which Dax made the Cindral Run in just twelve parsecs and won from Lando in a game of sabacc . With only Brevok remaining at his side, as his trusted copilot who swore a life debt to the Korrathi smuggler, Dax Karrick embarked on a smuggling career under the employ of Grukk the Grak , a notorious gangster and crime lord of Dunemere . After ditching a shipment of spice to avoid trouble with the Imperium, Karrick owed a great deal of money to Grukk, who then placed a bounty on the smuggler's head, as a result. His fortune seemed to have changed when Dax and Brevok were hired to charter Joren Drayden, Orien Kade , and the droids Bolt-3 and Astra-9 to Cindervale , avoiding Imperial shock troopers who were searching for Joren's droids. However, as they find Cindervale destroyed by the Imperium's new superweapon , the Void Core , Karrick became caught up in the insurgency against the Imperium, rescuing Princess Elira Solen, delivering the stolen Void Core plans to the hidden Insurgent base on Cinderfall 4 , and saved Joren from the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor in the Battle of Cinderfall , allowing Drayden to destroy the Void Core. Karrick fought with the Insurgency for a number of years afterward, taking part in numerous operations and battles

title: Dax Karrick
text: plans to the hidden Insurgent base on Cinderfall 4 , and saved Joren from the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor in the Battle of Cinderfall , allowing Drayden to destroy the Void Core. Karrick fought with the Insurgency for a number of years afterward, taking part in numerous operations and battles against the Imperium. After the Battle of Frostmark , Karrick sought refuge with Solen—with whom he had fallen in love—Brevok, and Astra-9 on Aether Spire , which was operated by his old friend Dorian Quill. There, they were captured by Xarn Velgor as part of a trap to bait Drayden to the city . Karrick was frozen in carbonite and taken to Grukk's Palace on Dunemere by the bounty hunter Vex Vark , where he remained encased in carbonite for months until he was rescued by his friends. After returning to the Alliance Fleet , Karrick was promoted to the rank of general and was given command of the Pathfinders , a special forces squad , for the Battle of Mossfell . Karrick led the Pathfinders to Mossfell , where he, Solen, Brevok, and the special forces team, with the help of the native Mosskins , destroyed the shield generator protecting the second Void Core that was being constructed in orbit . Their actions allowed the Alliance Fleet to destroy the superweapon.

title: Dax Karrick
text: The Battle of Mossfell, which saw the deaths of Emperor Theron Mal and Xarn Velgor, allowed the Insurgency to form the Concordat . In the early days after Mossfell, Karrick continued to lead the Pathfinders against the Imperium. He married Solen, and the two had a son, Beno Karrick. The boy struggled with the umbra side of Synth Flux—like his mother, who was the daughter of Xarn Velgor and twin sister of Joren Drayden, Beno was Synth Flux-sensitive —so Solen sent him to be trained as an Aetheri by Drayden. Beno was seduced to the umbra side by Vorr , Supreme Leader of the New Imperium , resulting in the destruction of Drayden's attempt to rebuild the Aetheri Order .

title: Dax Karrick
text: Having lost their son, Karrick left and returned to smuggling, and even lost the Corsair Wing to numerous thieves. He continued to smuggle until he was brought back into the fight by a scavenger named Nyla and a defected New Imperium shock trooper named Jax , who carried with them a droid, Orio-6 , that had part of a map to Drayden's location . Karrick, who retrieved the Corsair from Nyla and Jax, returned to Solen, who led the Coalition against the New Imperium, and fought in the battle to destroy the New Imperium superweapon known as Voidfang Base . During the battle, Karrick saw his son, who had taken the name Zarrin Karrick, and tried to convince him to return home. Instead, Karrick stabbed his father with his flux blade . Mortally wounded, Karrick fell to his death in the bowels of the Voidfang weapon. However, Karrick's heroic memory survived and his spirit remained alive and appeared in a Synth Flux vision a year later to convince Karrick to abandon the umbra side and defeat the resurrected Vael Mal, after a duel on the remains of the second Void Core between Nyla and Karrick, being enough for Beno Karrick to return and eventually sacrifice his own life to help Nyla end Mal and the Umbra for good.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
### Early life

#### Childhood

> " Dax, my boy, when you grow up, don't build ships like me. You're meant for better. You're meant to fly them. " ―Ovan, to his son, Dax Dax was born in a rough-and-tumble favela on the planet Korrath during the waning years of the Vantor Republic in 32 BVE . Sometime after he became famous, it would be rumored by a Snivvian bounty hunter that Dax was actually a descendant of the Prince-Admiral Jonashe Karrick , a member of the ancient Korrathi royalty . During his formative years, his father Ovan worked in the Korrathi Engineering Corporation shipyards , building vessels such as YT-1300 light freighters until he was laid off. Karrick's father wished he could leave Korrath on such a ship, but was never able to afford to. According to Dax, he was never close with his father. At one point his father brought him to the freighter factory where he worked and pointed out to the young Dax that the ships being built there were his contributions to the galaxy , but that they ultimately didn't matter. He advised him that he wasn't meant to build ships, but rather to fly them. Eventually, his father abandoned him. At some point he met the Ithorian Pjolan .

#### Working for the White Worms

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### Working for the White Worms

> " Why did you do that, Dax? You could've gotten yourself killed. For nothing." " You're right, Vessa. That's the way it is. No one's ever gonna help anyone unless it gets them something. Hell, I noticed you didn't exactly lend a hand. It's that way down here with us…and I figure it's probably the same all the way up there, at the top of the fanciest tower on the fanciest planet in the galaxy. But today, for a few minutes, for that kid…that's not how it was. Maybe it doesn't always have to be this way, you know? I guess that's what I was thinking. Maybe it could be different. You gotta start somewhere. " ―Vessa and Dax

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Around 24 BVE , Dax joined the White Worms criminal gang as a scrumrat . Here, Dax met fellow scrumrat Vessa . Despite being in service to the gang, Dax showed considerable defiance towards them and their methods. One day, he intervened as a smaller child was attacked by a group of bullies, which led to Dax getting beaten as well. Afterwards, Vessa asked Dax why he helped the child despite not getting anything in return. Dax answered that while that might be how the galaxy works, it did not always have to be that way. When Dax was about the age of eighteen, Dax and Vessa were vying for the position of Head within the White Worms. During their respective assignments, Dax and Vessa both failed to deliver as promised, leading them to be hunted down by factions such as the White Worms, the Kaldana Syndicate , as well as the Imperium. Dax had acquired a datacube with plans for a shield generator that was desired by all the factions. Dax and Vessa had no choice but to partner up to find a resolution to their problems. Eventually, Vessa became Head thanks to Dax's recommendation to Lady Proxima . As they later ate together, Dax asked if he and Vessa were on their first date. Vessa denied it, but acknowledged the possibility that it could happen someday. Sometime later, Dax and Vessa began a romantic relationship.

#### Escaping Korrath

> " Dax, this... this could work. " " This is gonna work. Vessa, you always said one day we're gonna get out of here. This is it. " ―Vessa and Dax

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### Escaping Korrath

> " Dax, this... this could work. " " This is gonna work. Vessa, you always said one day we're gonna get out of here. This is it. " ―Vessa and Dax

Acting under orders from Lady Proxima, Dax set up a deal with some individuals to exchange coaxium for credits. Vessa suggested that Dax shouldn't go alone, but both Proxima and Dax disagreed with her. Upon meeting with the individuals, Dax got into a fight with them due to having not abided by their stated terms and proceeded to escape with an extremely valuable vial of coaxium, as well as a speeder. Dax fled the criminals on his M-68 landspeeder through the streets of Coronet City. He drove through a bridge and hung his dice on the windscreen.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Upon arriving at the Den of the White Worms, he and the other Scrumrats were herded by Lady Proxima's enforcers into her underground chamber. Three children fought over stolen items they had pickpocketed. Dax and Vessa embraced each other in a tunnel. He told Vessa that he had managed to steal a vial of hyperfuel coaxium and planned to use it as their ticket offworld. Moloch, Syke, and Rebolt soon caught up with them and brought Dax before Lady Proxima, who asked Dax for a progress report. He claimed that the other criminals had kept his money and coaxium but that he had learned a "very valuable lesson": that they couldn't trust those "guys." Lady Proxima was furious that Dax had come back with nothing from his errand. Rebolt beat Dax with a stick. A defiant Dax grabbed Rebolt's stick and said that he would beat those who beat him. Moloch raised his volt pistol at Dax but Vessa stopped him. Lady Proxima warned Vessa not to disobey her. Dax pulled out a rock and claimed to have a thermal detonator but Proxima was not fooled. Dax revealed that it was a bluff and hurled the rock through the ceiling,

title: Dax Karrick
text: Moloch raised his volt pistol at Dax but Vessa stopped him. Lady Proxima warned Vessa not to disobey her. Dax pulled out a rock and claimed to have a thermal detonator but Proxima was not fooled. Dax revealed that it was a bluff and hurled the rock through the ceiling, letting in a beam of sunlight. Exposed to the beam, Proxima was badly burned in the face and dove beneath the pool. Dax and Vessa escaped in Dax's stolen M-68 landspeeder and raced out of the White Worms' den into the streets of Coronet. Dax's plan was to drive to Coronet Spaceport with the stolen coaxium and use it to bribe their way offworld. Dax vowed to be a pilot and see the galaxy. Vessa hoped they would get their own starship and no longer be told what to do. The pair were soon pursued by Moloch's A-A4B truckspeeder, which was also carrying two Korrathi hounds. Moloch rammed his truckspeeder against Dax's landspeeder. After narrowly avoiding a truck, Dax drove through an Imperial checkpoint. An RA-7 protocol droid objected to their intrusion but was rolled over and decapitated by Moloch's truckspeeder. When Vessa said that Moloch was fast, Dax reassured her that they were faster. Dax's landspeeder and Moloch's truckspeeder were pursued by an Imperial patrol trooper riding a C-PH patrol speeder bike. However, the rider crashed into a barrier. Dax and Vessa drove through a factory with Moloch hot on their tail. Dax managed to escape Moloch's truck by driving the landspeeder through a tight corner. With the landspeeder stuck, Moloch dispatched Rebolt and the Korrathi hounds after them.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
### Serving under the Imperium

#### Recruitment

> " This is where I sign up to be a pilot, right? " " If you apply for the Imperial Navy, but most recruits go into the infantry. " " I'm gonna be a pilot. Best in the galaxy. " ―Dax, and Drawd Munbrin

Dax and Vessa managed to reach the Coronet spaceport on foot. There was a strong Imperial military presence at the spaceport, where there were long queues offworld. They witnessed several people, including a family, being arrested by shock troopers. Dax and Vessa joined a queue. Vessa was worried about being trafficked by the Carmine Dawn, but Dax vowed to protect her. Since they didn't have identification, Dax and Vessa used the coaxium vial to bribe the Imperial Emigration Officer Falthina Sharest into letting them through the customs booth. After depositing the coaxium, Dax managed to cross through.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Before Vessa could cross into the other side of the terminal, she was apprehended by the White Worms enforcers Rebolt and Syke . Vessa told Dax to flee, and he vowed to return for her. Dax managed to evade Imperial forces and the White Worms by donning a stolen hat and hiding behind several crates. He witnessed more people being arrested by shock troopers. Lacking sufficient funds to travel offworld, Dax found an Imperial Military recruiting post. Dax spoke to the Imperial recruitment officer Drawd Munbrin and volunteered to join the Imperial Navy as a pilot. Since Dax lacked a surname and family, he dubbed him "Dax Karrick" in the absence of a surname. Approving Dax's application, he told Dax to proceed to Transport ID-83 to the Imperial Flight Academy on Carida, promising Dax that he would be flying in no time.

#### Life as an Imperial cadet

> " SKREE fighters. Now we're talking-- " ―Dax Karrick when he arrives at the Carida Academy

title: Dax Karrick
text:
> " SKREE fighters. Now we're talking-- " ―Dax Karrick when he arrives at the Carida Academy

When Dax enlisted, Drawd Munbrin assigned Dax to the Imperial academy on the planet Carida . When Dax arrived, droids stripped all his clothing off. Right after, different droids gave him his new Imperial cadet suit and also shaved him. Dax entered a room filled with many other cadets. Here a female Imperial officer named Triosa Broog was speaking over them. Soon after, he tried to greet a cadet, who told Dax to shut up. Dax realized that when he said shut up, he used Dax's cadet name, and you were only known as numbers at the Imperial Academy. Later, Dax was practicing on a battlefield as an Imperial Army trooper and wondered how this was supposed to help him in pilot training. Broog overheard Dax. Dax then raised his hand, and Broog called him a Korrathi worm . Broog asked what his name was. They had a short conversation about his name. Broog then suggested to the other cadets that they show Dax how basic training is supposed to help flying by hiking up a mountain twice.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Immediately after, the cadets started to beat Dax up. During this, cadet 404-913, named Beilert Varrick , began to insult Dax before cadet 803-308 told them to let him go. Dax thanked her for the help and asked for the name of the cadet but refused to say. Right after, two cadets, Lyttan Dree and Tamu Dree , were talking about why they joined the Imperium. They also asked Dax why he had signed up, with Karrick simply replying that he had to get off Korrath. Lyttan and Tamu said that he would never learn how to fly at the academy and that they might send him to a wretched place like Urthak or Mimban . Dax was thinking about what they said and thought that he should do something deeply stupid. Dax then snuck into a SKREE fighter hanger and stole a fighter. Dax eventually crashed the SKREE, leading to shock troopers surrounding Dax at the crash site.

title: Dax Karrick
text: After the crash Dax was imprisoned . He eventually got out because of his great piloting skills. Fourteen days later, Nico, who was cadet 803-308, was one of the top of the leader board. Suddenly Dax came upon Lyttan and Tamu, who were surprised about Nico topping the leader board. Lyttan and Tamu were surprised that Dax survived the crash. The cadets had started a bet about Karrick's fate , with one of the Dree brothers winning. Soon after, Dax was bullied by 404-913, who started a fight with Dax. Eventually Dax was beaten, and Varrick went to hurt Lyttan and Tamu, but Dax kicked Varrick in the crotch before he could do so. Dax then smashed Varrick in his face with a food tray. Varrick was about to punch Dax in the face, but before he could, Imperial troopers arrived and asked what was going on. but they told a lie instead of what really happened. Dax suggested that Varrick and Dax should start over. Dax told Varrick his name, but Varrick refused to give his. He said to look on the leader board to find out. Dax looked and saw that Varrick was the top one on the board. Soon after, Dax said he could not believe that the academy let Varrick actually become the top one. Nico came up behind Dax and said she wondered how long he would last. She was also surprised that Dax survived the crash. Tamu then told Dax that there was no way Dax was moving to top of the leader board. Dax disagreed.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Later during flight school, Dax asked the instructor if there would be flying at any point. It took time , but eventually Dax entered the cockpit of a SKREE fighter. He made it to third place on the leader board. During a another flight class, the teacher Yurib Nakan , told the class to work in pairs and destroy a cannon's shield. Dax and Tamu were partners for this exercise. Tamu's fighter was damaged, and Dax saved him. When the training was over, Lyttan thanked Dax for saving his brother's life. Soon after, a cadet came to Lyttan and said that he broke off before he could get a shot. Yurib then said that everyone failed the training. Dax's actions of saving a cadet could have given Dax a chance to become the best pilot the Imperium had ever seen, but Dax's fellow cadets might kill Dax before he could do so. Karrick claimed they should have earned partial credit since the team worked together.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Karrick and the other cadets were ordered to make soup for the all the cadets. During the night, Karrick snuck out of his bunk and cleaned the floors in the refresher , but logged Varrick as having done all the assignments. As a result, the next morning, Karrick and the other cadets were assigned to the Quasar Fire -class carrier cruiser 07200823 by Yurib. Their orders were to transport several SKREE fighter pilots. During the voyage, Karrick was able to modify the cruiser's speed to give him and the cadets a day off. Karrick also revealed he had day passes and told them there was a Pantolomin cruiser nearby they could visit and gave them civilian clothes. Despite Nico's objections, Karrick was able to convince them to leave the cruiser.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Aboard the cruiser, Karrick told his fellow cadets to have some fun. Karrick played sabacc with Nico and attempted to learn her reasons for joining the Imperial Navy. Nico refused to tell him why and deduced how Karrick pulled off the excursion. She also noticed him eyeing an Ithorian. Karrick was soon left to himself and met up with Pjolan. Karrick attempted to drink an Ithorian ale to no avail. Dax also asked Pjolan about Vessa. Pjolan said nothing, indicating that Vessa was still alive, but told Karrick that Lady Proxima had a 200-credit bounty on him, so he pulled a volt pistol on Dax. He was saved by Nico, and the two of them went to get Lyttan and Tamu. Pjolan attempted to collect Karrick's bounty, but Karrick was able to inform Black Sun , the cruiser's owners, about Pjolan, and the cartel captured him. Karrick and the other cadets were allowed to leave with their thanks. Karrick and the others were able to return cruiser 07200823 to Carida's academy. Upon their return, they were reinstated to full flight status. Later, the cadets were told by Yurib to come to the training room the next evening.

title: Dax Karrick
text: After Karrick completed his training he was stationed on the planet Qhulosk , where he became part of Carida Squadron and was sent to fight a battle for the Imperium at Howlan . During the battle, Varrick was shot down by native Qhuloskians , but the skirmish resulted in an Imperial victory. Yurib ordered the squadron to return to base . Karrick refused and wanted to help Varrick. Yurib responded that Varrick was gone and told Karrick to abort. Three enemy fighters came and fired at Carida Squadron, killing one of the Skrees. Eventually, the squadron defeated the fighters and fled back to base. When they arrived, Karrick spoke to Yurib about why he could not save Varrick. Yurib said that SKREE bombers would wipe out the entire city soon and there was no time to rescue Varrick. Karrick became mad and set off to rescue Varrick alone. Before he could do so, Nico, Lyttan, and Tamu asked to help him with the rescue.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Per the plan, Yurib sent a bombing run to the city. One officer recognized that six people had left the base and six speeders were also missing. The officer revealed this to Yurib, but Yurib didn't respond. During the rescue, Karrick, Nico, Tamu, and Lyttan were being shot at by Qhuloskians. The Imperial bombing run sent by Yurib almost killed them all but destroyed one of their speeders. When they reached Varrick, Varrick almost shot Karrick. Varrick then said to Karrick that he couldn't believe that the Imperium sent them to rescue him, but Karrick said that they had chosen to rescue him. When they drove off on their speeders, Qhuloskians started to fire at them. Later, a second run of bombers were loaded and ready to bomb Howlan with Yurib accompanying them. Dax, Varrick, Nico, Tamu, and Lyttan were captured. Right before they were killed by the Qhuloskians, Ghulars opened fire on the aggressive aliens. The Ghulars were slaves to the Qhuloskians to mine for farium to make the Qhuloskians' ships stronger during battle. Afterwards, the Ghulars escaped the planet by taking escape pods from a crashed Qhuloskian warship. When they left, Nico began crying that her home planet

title: Dax Karrick
text: opened fire on the aggressive aliens. The Ghulars were slaves to the Qhuloskians to mine for farium to make the Qhuloskians' ships stronger during battle. Afterwards, the Ghulars escaped the planet by taking escape pods from a crashed Qhuloskian warship. When they left, Nico began crying that her home planet in the Huru system was under mining control and her friend Weegee was a miner there. She became very angry and kicked one of their bikes. Dax then realized that one escape pod was left and decided to fake Nico's death. When Nico left, Dax, Varrick, Tamu, and Lyttan then left for the base, being chased and fired at by Qhuloskian ships. title: Dax Karrick
text:
Later, Karrick had to say goodbye to Varrick, Tamu, and Lyttan at the base, and Karrick was put into the brig.

At some point his skills at flying at the Imperial academy at Carida became the only thing preventing his superiors from outright expelling him from the academy. Other recruits had tried to emulate his flying moves, but at least one recruit nearly died in a failed attempt. Broog vouched for Dax to her commanding officer, Captain Nettic Whain, asking that he be given one more chance to fall into line. Finally, during an attack by raiders on Onyx Squadron, Dax disobeyed orders once more in order to save the life of Cadet Lyttan Dree. Karrick was able to take out three raiders before crashing into a hangar. Unfortunately, Karrick's crash destroyed the hangar and dozens of astromechs. This action led to him being court-martialed and tried by Commodore Almudin . Karrick was expelled from the academy, drafted into the 224th Imperial Armored Division as a Corporal , and deployed to an active combat zone on Mimban.

#### The Mimban campaign

title: Dax Karrick
text:
#### The Mimban campaign

> " I saved him, at least that's what he says, the big fuzzy fool, but really, he saved me. I was on a bad path, and Brev, he put me straight. Saved my shanks more than once too. " ―Dax Karrick on how Brevok saved him After three years of Imperial service, Dax had been expelled from the Carida Flight Academy for insubordination and was serving as a Mudtrooper Corporal during a battle on the planet Mimban. Karrick's 224th Imperial Armored Division was locked in trench warfare against the Mimbanese Liberation Army, enduring heavy casualties in the torrid, muddy weather. Dax took part in a ground assault led by Major Staz to capture a ridge. After Dax was thrown to the ground, Staz helped him up and told him they were almost there. Karrick was confused, but Staz instructed him to head to the last ridge. Unfortunately, Staz was soon killed by an explosion. Dax and some surviving troops, including Private Collum Woslo , Corporal Sharlu Greslin , Corporal Danith Nodar , and Corporal Wesger Odry , gathered in a trench with "Captain" Tobias Karren , who took command as the most senior officer in the group. Karren led the soldiers into action, and they eliminated the last coalition on the ridge.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Following the skirmish, Dax spoke with "Captain" Karren, expressing gratitude for his help. Karren advised him to get away from there as fast as he could. Karrick soon encountered Karren's companions , Val and the Ardennian Rio Durant , who were disguised as Imperial Army troopers. They warned him not to follow them. Lieutenant Alayus Bolandin informed Dax and his comrades that they would be moving out to the Southern Marshlands in three hours. When Bolandin requested an advance party, Karrick questioned why the Imperium was destroying and occupying Mimban, earning the enmity of his commanding officer. Disenchanted with the Imperium, Dax sought out Karren and his gang, who were planning a heist. Dax recognized them as thieves posing as Imperial Army personnel. Val and Karren initially wanted to kill Dax, but he offered his services as a pilot. When Rio asked what a fancy "fly boy" was doing in the mud, Dax claimed he had been kicked out for having a mind of his own. Dax pointed out that Rio was an Ardennian. Desperate to escape offworld, Karrick tried to blackmail them into allowing him to join their gang by threatening to expose them as infiltrators. However, Karren turned

title: Dax Karrick
text: the mud, Dax claimed he had been kicked out for having a mind of his own. Dax pointed out that Rio was an Ardennian. Desperate to escape offworld, Karrick tried to blackmail them into allowing him to join their gang by threatening to expose them as infiltrators. However, Karren turned the tables on him and convinced Lieutenant Bolandin that Karrick was attempting to desert. Seeking an opportunity to rid his unit of a "trouble-maker," Bolandin had a chained Karrick thrown into a pen where he was condemned to battle a "beast" held in captivity. Secret battle of pretend The beast was revealed to be a Vorak named Brevok , whose species had been enslaved by the Imperium. Thinking he was a threat, Brevok attacked Dax and hurled him against the girders and mud. Owing to Dax's ability to speak Vorak tongue, Karrick convinced Brevok that he was a friend. Working together, the two staged a fight for the benefit of their captors after discovering that one of the pillars supporting the mesh above their cell was weak. The unsuspecting sentries laughed and thought that Dax was doomed. After several attempts, Dax pretended to goad Brevok into pushing against the main pillar supporting the mesh, causing it to collapse. After jumping out of harm's way, Brevok threw Dax out of the pit and followed suit. The two found that they were chained together. Brevok wanted to flee the camp, but Dax convinced him to accompany him to a nearby airfield. He told Brevok to trust him, promising that they could go their separate ways if he chose to do so afterward. Meanwhile, Karren's gang boarded their stolen Y-45 armored transport hauler . Throwing off his Imperial army helmet and uniform, Rio asked how they could breathe in those stuffy

title: Dax Karrick
text:
airfield. He told Brevok to trust him, promising that they could go their separate ways if he chose to do so afterward. Meanwhile, Karren's gang boarded their stolen Y-45 armored transport hauler . Throwing off his Imperial army helmet and uniform, Rio asked how they could breathe in those stuffy suits. The three took off, but Karren spotted Dax and Brevok waving to them below. Rio was impressed by Karrick's determination and believed that a Vorak would be helpful as muscle. Val was opposed, but Rio convinced Karren to bring the ship down so they could pick up Dax and Brevok. The five then departed Mimban in the stolen hauler. ### Life as a scoundrel

#### Working with Tobias Karren

Vandor heist

> " Look, I waited a long time for a shot like this. I'm not about to screw it up, all right? " ―Dax Karrick, to Val

title: Dax Karrick
text: After Dax and Brevok's escape from Mimban, Karren took the transport hauler to the snowy, mountainous world of Vandor . While watching over the snowy mountains from the hauler, Dax thanked Brevok for saving him, acknowledging that he only survived because of the Vorak. He shared his plan with Brevok, explaining that they would do one job with Karren's gang in exchange for their freedom. Brevok accepted the deal. Dax asked Brevok for his name and settled on "Brev," finding it easier to say than his full name in Vorak tongue. Upon landing, Karren enlisted the two of them for a planned heist to steal a shipment of the hyperfuel refined coaxium from a 20-T Railcrawler conveyex transport on Vandor. While surveying the train tracks from a distance, Karren outlined his plan, which involved targeting the conveyex between the tower and the bridge. Rio dropped them onto the conveyex, allowing them to separate the payload container and lift it up onto the AT hauler. Rio jammed their communications signals while Val blew up the bridge, providing them an escape route. On the night before the heist, Karren warned the gang about the threat posed by Enfys Nest and the Cloud-Riders

title: Dax Karrick
text: them to separate the payload container and lift it up onto the AT hauler. Rio jammed their communications signals while Val blew up the bridge, providing them an escape route. On the night before the heist, Karren warned the gang about the threat posed by Enfys Nest and the Cloud-Riders . While resting by the campfire, Val criticized Karren for involving Dax and Brevok, considering them amateurs, questioning why they couldn't have simply hired professionals such as the Xan sisters or Boskan . Karren defended his decision, explaining that it was a way to settle their debts. During the campfire conversation, Karren and his associates questioned Dax about his motives. Dax revealed his plans to become a pilot and return to find Vessa. Rio expressed his preference for being tied to nobody, while Val discussed her relationship with Karren. Karrick then asked Brevok what he would do with his share of the profits, with Brevok responding that he would use it to help the Voraks on Thornwood . Karren promised Dax and Brevok that if they followed his instructions, they would have more than enough to buy their own ship, before disassembling one of his volt pistols into a DL-44 pistol and tossing it over to Dax, who gazed down upon his new weapon.

title: Dax Karrick
text: While Rio flew the Y-45 hauler, Dax, Brevok, and Karren landed on the cargo wagon carrying coaxium, with Val positioning herself on the bridge. The presence of Karren and his team soon attracted the attention of Imperial range troopers, leading to an exchange of fire. As the conveyex train maneuvered along a narrow cliff face, Dax and Brev narrowly avoided being crushed against rocks. Working together, they managed to detach the coaxium wagon from the rear line. Maintaining communication with Karren, Rio lowered the "witch cables" onto the coaxium wagon. However, before Karren's gang could escape with the stolen coaxium, they were attacked by the Cloud-Riders, who rode swoop bikes. Enfys Nest, the leader of the Cloud-Riders, ordered her followers to lower their harpoons. Dax and the others evaded volt pistol fire, and one of the swoop bikes crashed against a rock. Two of the Cloud-Riders boarded the Y-45 hauler and fatally wounded Durant. Karrick left Brevok to uncouple the wagon from the front train while he went to assist Rio.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Karrick managed to climb aboard the transport hauler and take control of the ship, triggering a security sensor in the process. Val warned Dax that Viper probe droids were heading his way. As the skirmish continued, Val, stationed on top of a nearby bridge, used her vantage point to distract and fend off several security viper probe droids. With his dying breath, Durant apologized to Karrick for mocking his flying abilities and acknowledged that Val was right in her belief that no one should die alone. Karren fought Enfys Nest on top of the wagon. However, the conveyex train was rapidly approaching the bridge, and Val realized there wasn't enough time for her to abandon her position without allowing the crew to steal the coaxium wagon. After communicating her change of plans to Karren via comlink, Val professed her love for him before detonating the bomb, sacrificing herself and destroying the bridge. The destruction of the bridge caused the conveyex to plunge into a deep gorge. In a struggle, Brevok managed to detach the coaxium wagon from the rest of the train. However, the Cloud-Riders had attached grappling hooks to the wagon, dragging it down. Not wanting to risk the

title: Dax Karrick
text:
the bridge. The destruction of the bridge caused the conveyex to plunge into a deep gorge. In a struggle, Brevok managed to detach the coaxium wagon from the rest of the train. However, the Cloud-Riders had attached grappling hooks to the wagon, dragging it down. Not wanting to risk the lives of Karren and Brevok, Karrick made the difficult decision to let go of the coaxium wagon, which plummeted into the ravine below and exploded. Brevok grabbed Karren, and the two survived by clinging to the cable. Following the failed heist, Karren erected a hasty memorial to Val and Rio. Angered by Karrick's decision to drop the cargo, Karren struck him in the face. Karren revealed he had been ordered to steal the coaxium to repay his debt to Dryden Vossa , the leader of the Carmine Dawn criminal syndicate. Dax proposed deserting, but Karren countered that Vossa would send out enforcers to hunt down those who had crossed him. Karren said the only thing they could do was go to Vossa and make amends. Dax agreed to come along to make things right and exacted a promise from Karren to pay him and Brevok for their services. Brev agreed to come along.

Meeting Dryden Vossa

> " I don't believe we've been introduced. " " Yeah. This is Dax Karrick and Brevok. They're with me. " ―Dryden Vossa, meeting Dax Karrick and Brevok through Tobias Karren

title: Dax Karrick
text:
> " I don't believe we've been introduced. " " Yeah. This is Dax Karrick and Brevok. They're with me. " ―Dryden Vossa, meeting Dax Karrick and Brevok through Tobias Karren

Karren, Dax, and Brev traveled to the outskirts of Fort Ypso , where Vossa' yacht, First Light , had arrived. After surrendering their weapons to Captain Aemon Gremm , they entered the public gallery. Karren's team entered the yacht's hallway. Karren spoke to Vossa' concierge, Margo , seeking an audience with Dryden Vossa. She told him that Vossa was having an audience with Governor Diles Anevi , whom Vossa killed. Captain Gremm informed Vossa of Karren's presence. Karren advised Dax and Brevok to keep their eyes down because the people there were not their friends, gesturing to the wealthy people around them, eating and drinking the most expensive, tasty, and quality food available. Dax soon had an unexpected reunion with Vessa, who now worked for Vossa. The two drank together while reminiscing about their past and ambitions. Karren soon arrived with Vossa, who introduced himself to Karrick and shook his hand, as he then did with Brev. Vossa suggested they go to his office to discuss business privately.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
After exchanging pleasantries, Vossa chastised Karren for underestimating Enfys Nest and told Karren to give him a reason not to kill them. Since the few available stocks of coaxium were in Imperial hands, Dax proposed stealing unrefined coaxium from Cindral , where the Gruv Syndicate ran a mining operation. Vossa was unwilling to jeopardize his syndicate's business relations with the Pykes, and consequentially gestured for his guards to kill Karrick, Karren, and Brev. However, Dax and Karren informed him that they had no alliance with the Pykes, and taking on the operation themselves would not implicate Carmine Dawn. Vessa was supportive of Dax's idea but warned that the unstable coaxium had to be brought to a processing facility quickly before it deteriorated. Brevok suggested Savareen since it was not under Imperial control. Vossa approved of the plan but sent Vessa along with them. Before they left, Vossa reminded them that he would be forced to execute them if they were to fail him again. In the turbolift, Karren said he could provide the gear for the mission, before asking if Vessa knew where to find a ship.

Visit to the Lodge

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Visit to the Lodge

> " Captain Dorian Quill. " " Dax Karrick. Looks like you're having a good day. " " I'm a lucky guy. " ―Dorian Quill, and Dax Karrick's first meeting Knowing that they would need a fast ship for the Cindral heist, Vessa took Karrick and his companions to the Lodge at nearby Fort Ypso. There, she introduced the team to Dorian Quill, an accomplished smuggler and pilot who had supposedly won his ship in a game of sabacc. Karrick walked past many established scoundrels and bounty hunters, such as Vex Vark and Dengrik , unaware that they would become a key part of his life in the future. After walking past two dueling droids, Karrick and the rest of the crew eventually found Lando playing sabacc with several alien patrons. Against Vessa and Brevok's advice, Dax challenged Lando to a game of sabacc , seeking to win his ship. Dax won the first round and collected several credits. While Dax and Lando were playing, the Cloud-Rider Weazel spied on them. Dax agreed to a second round and placed a wager on Lando's ship, reputed to be the fastest in the galaxy, whilst Lando did the same for the ship Dax claimed to have. Unbeknownst to Dax, Lando had a card hidden up his sleeve, which he uses to win the game, ultimately humiliating Dax in front of Vessa.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Following the game, an enraged Karrick questioned how Lando could have possibly had a specific card without cheating. Quill called out to Dax questioning where his ship was, before being interrupted by Vessa. Lando complimented her, stating that she looked as beautiful as ever, before speaking further with her regarding their upcoming heist on Cindral. Quill requested half the profits, which Karrick deemed to be ridiculous, before Karren arrived and negotiated it down to 25 percent. Lando agreed, knowing that Karren was responsible for killing the bounty hunter Ayla Vossk during a skirmish. Dax and his companions soon encountered Lando's droid co-pilot, L3-37 , who had a female programming and was an avowed droid rights advocate. L3-37 objected to the droid fighting pits at the Lodge and picked a fight with the owner Ralakili , who objected to her trying to stop his droids from fighting. However, Lando intervened and convinced her to let him go. Despite L3-37's misgivings about the newcomer, Lando and the others set out for Lando's ship, which had been impounded. After L3-37 cut a hole through the gate, Lando showed Dax and his companions his ship, the Corsair Wing . Lando had refurbished the ship,

title: Dax Karrick
text:
convinced her to let him go. Despite L3-37's misgivings about the newcomer, Lando and the others set out for Lando's ship, which had been impounded. After L3-37 cut a hole through the gate, Lando showed Dax and his companions his ship, the Corsair Wing . Lando had refurbished the ship, including installing an escape pod and wet bar. Karren agreed to remove the gravity lock in return for taking five percent off Lando's cut, reducing it to 20 percent. Lando reluctantly agreed to Karren's deal. As the Corsair disembarked, Weazel informed Enfys Nest that they had planted a homing beacon on the ship. Enfys gambled that if they survived, they would bring the price to them. Infiltration on Cindral

> " This is a precision job. Thermal vault will be on the lowest level. Down where it's warm. The only way we're gonna pull this off, is if everybody plays their part. Stick to the plan. Do not improvise. " ―Tobias Karren, to Dax Karrick and the rest of the crew

title: Dax Karrick
text: While traveling aboard the Corsair , Dax told Lando that he recognized the ship as a YT-1300 light freighter because his father had worked at a CEC plant before he got laid off. Karrick spoke about how his father had built these ships and wanted to be a pilot. Lando questioned how close Karrick was with his father, though Dax remarked that he never really was, which Lando understood, having the same feelings towards his own father. L3-37 soon arrived and ushered Karrick out of the co-pilot seat. Dax and Vessa smiled at one another whilst L3 complained in the background. Lando explained that they had to travel through the Akkadese Maelstrom to reach Cindral, before he and L3 set a hyperspace course for Cindral and jumped into lightspeed. Meanwhile, Karren played dejarik with Brevok. Karren used one of his pieces to take out one of Brevok's pieces, angering the Vorak who slammed his fists on the hologram set. Karren schooled Brevok that he had to think a few steps ahead. Dax asked if they had seen Vessa, but Karren replied that people were predictable.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Dax walked to Quill's cape closet where he found Vessa trying on a blue cape. Vessa asked Dax about his plan for Cindral. Though Dax wanted to ask her about her experiences following their separation on Korrath, Vessa tried to change the subject. Dax gave Vessa a passionate kiss, and the two embraced. Karren walked in on them and reminded them that they had a lot of work to do. In private, Karren told Dax that he was making a big mistake by trusting Vessa. He told Dax that he and Brevok would make a good crew but that it would not work with Vessa. Karren advised Dax to trust nobody and to assume that everyone would betray him. Dax thought of it as a lonely way to live, though Karren said it was the only way.

title: Dax Karrick
text: As they approached Cindral, Karren briefed the team about their plan to reach the thermal vault where the coaxium was stored. He warned everyone to stick to the plan. The Corsair landed in a clearing at the base of the mine where they were greeted by several Pykes, including Capo Quay Tolsite . Vessa posed as the slaver Oksana Floren, Deputy Assistant to the Vice Admiral of the Federation of Trade Route Allocation and Monetization. Dax and Brevok posed as slaves while Karren posed as a helmeted "security attache." L3-37 posed as a servant droid. "Floren" met with Capo Tolsite and offered to trade the Federation's slaves in return for the Gruv Syndicate's spice. One of the Gruv sentinels forced Brevok and Dax Karrick to their knees with a pike and inspected them. Tolsite sent Dax and Brevok to be clipped. Before leaving, Vessa then punched Dax in the gut but discreetly passed him his lucky charm. Vessa, L3-37, and Karren accompanied the Pykes into Tolsite's control room while Dax and Brev were led into the mines. Moments later, Dax and Brev were beaten by their Gruv captors, though they soon turned the tables on their guards as the camera

title: Dax Karrick
text: but discreetly passed him his lucky charm. Vessa, L3-37, and Karren accompanied the Pykes into Tolsite's control room while Dax and Brev were led into the mines. Moments later, Dax and Brev were beaten by their Gruv captors, though they soon turned the tables on their guards as the camera feed faded. Dax knocked out his guard, but Brev ended up pulling the arms off his captors, which Dax complained about, stating that the suit would have fit him perfectly. Dax eventually found a new suit and, alongside Brevok, mingled among the slaves and guards. L3-37 and Vessa directed Dax and Brevok to the thermal vault. As they approached the vaults, Brevok broke off to free a Vorak slave named Sagor . Dax passed Brev a pike, which he used to attack the Gruv guards beating Sagor. Following Karren's directions, Dax reached the vault and incapacitated the guard. After L3-37 unlocked the vault, Dax stole 12 unrefined coaxium canisters. Dax struggled to push a sled carrying the canisters but was noticed by the Gruv guards. Brevok came to the rescue and took out the guards with his pike. Sagor and Brev helped Dax push out the canisters.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Lando exited the Corsair Wing to join the battle as Dax and the rest of the team fought their way out with the liberated slaves and droids. While Brevok and Sagor loaded the coaxium canisters aboard the Corsair , Dax and the others exchanged fire with Gruv sentries, who had brought a sonic cannon. Before they could leave, L3 was fatally damaged by gunfire. A grieving Lando came to the aid of the dying L3-37, who succumbed to systems failure. Lando was hit, and Dax came to his aid, driving the sentries away. A slave named Tak led the slaves to safety. Brevok embraced Sagor before leaving with Dax and Lando. Brevok carried a wounded Lando aboard the Corsair while Vessa took out the Pykes' sonic cannon with a grenade, causing an inferno. While a distraught Lando cradled a disintegrating L3, Karren ordered Dax to get them out of Cindral. Dax then flew the Corsair out of the mine into the skies of Cindral.

The Cindral Run

title: Dax Karrick
text:
The Cindral Run

> " It's an easy equation. We simply don't have enough time to get to Savareen before the canisters explode! " " Just have to find a faster route. " " There isn't one! You can't make the Cindral Run in less than 20 parsecs. " " Watch me. " ―Dorian Quill and Dax Karrick While Lando mourned the loss of L3-37, Vessa volunteered as Dax's co-pilot. They were joined by Brevok while Karren sealed the hidden storage compartment containing the coaxium. As they approached the Akkadese Maelstrom, Lando warned them that they had to hurry due to the volatile nature of the unrefined coaxium. The Corsair soon encountered an Imperial Iron Cruiser, which had exited hyperspace in response to the insurgency on Cindral. Lando wanted to drop the shipment, but Vessa warned that Dryden would kill them if they failed. Seeking to recover the Corsair 's stolen coaxium cargo, the Iron Cruiser dispatched several SKREE fighters and heavy fighters in pursuit of the freighter. Dax flew the Corsair around the Iron Cruiser, and the Imperial SKREE fighters gave chase. Due to the highly volatile nature of the unrefined coaxium, Lando estimated that completion of the Cindral run was impossible before the fuel detonated - the conventional route having never been done in less than twenty parsecs. Dax proposed taking a shortcut through the maelstrom, which Lando regarded as suicidal. Dax convinced Lando to download L3's neural cords, which contained her navigational data, into the Corsair 's systems.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Dax took the Corsair and its SKREE pursuers through the dangerous storm clouds of the Akkadese Maelstrom while Karren manned the ship's ventral laser cannon, taking out two SKREE fighters. However, a third fighter managed to evade Karren's laser cannon and inflicted damage on the top of the Corsair 's hull, causing Lando to fall. Dax rolled the Corsair , striking the SKREE fighter with its side and sending it into an asteroid. More SKREE fighters continued the pursuit, prompting Dax to state they needed to divert power to the rear shield generator. Brevok did so, causing Dax to ask when he learned to fly. Brevok responded that he was 190 years old. A SKREE fighter managed to shoot the Corsair ' s rear ventral cannon, causing it to break off. Dax flew the Corsair deeper into the Maelstrom with the SKREE hot on his tail. Mimicking a move copied from a Korrathi street racer , Dax got Brevok to deploy the landing gear as the Corsair scraped against the surface of an asteroid. This damaged the landing gear but uprooted rocks and debris, one of which breached the SKREE fighter's cockpit. Dax then took the Corsair deeper into the

title: Dax Karrick
text:
from a Korrathi street racer , Dax got Brevok to deploy the landing gear as the Corsair scraped against the surface of an asteroid. This damaged the landing gear but uprooted rocks and debris, one of which breached the SKREE fighter's cockpit. Dax then took the Corsair deeper into the Maelstrom. Meanwhile, Lando and Vessa managed to retrieve L3's internal processor. Karren observed the coaxium vials becoming more unstable and alerted the others. Lando and Vessa managed to install L3's processor into the Corsair 's systems. As they reached the Maw Cluster, L3 constructed a model of the Akkadese Maelstrom and warned them that they were approaching a massive summa-verminoth. The Corsair soon found itself face to face with the monster. The crew tried to escape the monster but ended up arriving at a large gravity well, which Lando identified as the Maw. Thinking fast, Dax ejected the Corsair 's escape pod into the well for the summa-verminoth to follow, which took the bait. Guiding the ship's systems, L3 found a way out 90 degrees to the left. However, the Corsair was trapped in the gravity well. Vessa and Lando convinced the rest of the team to inject a drop of coaxium into the fusion core to give them the kick needed to escape the gravity well. Carrying out their plan, Karren retrieved a drop of coaxium. Meanwhile, the verminoth was pulled into the Maw and ripped apart. At Karrick's command, Karren boosted the ship's fusion core with a drop of coaxium, which briefly supercharged the engines. Despite a false start, the hyperrelay came online, and the Corsair jumped into lightspeed before the Maelstrom closed on them.

Savareen

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Savareen

> " You were wrong about one thing, I was paying attention. You told Brev people are predictable. You're no exception. " ―Dax Karrick to Tobias Karren

After making the Cindral Run, Karrick and his companions landed on the planet Savareen to rendezvous with Vossa. As the Corsair approached the Bis Refinery, Karrick radioed the air traffic controller Dhowar Repareed , warning that he was coming with a cargo of coaxium that needed to be offloaded immediately. The damaged Corsair circled the coastal refinery before landing on a landing pad. Due to its damaged landing gear, the Corsair was lopsided. As the coaxium was offloaded, Karrick quipped that he had made the Cindral Run in just twelve parsecs with some generous rounding. Dax put his arm around an un-amused Lando, who was grieving over the loss of L-3 and was furious at the damage to his ship. He told Dax that he would be waiting aboard his quarters for his share of the money and vowed not to see him again.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Dax found Vessa at a bar in the nearby Pnakotic Coast village and asked when Vossa was coming. Vessa reassured him that he would get paid for doing his job. When Karrick asked Vessa about her servitude to Dryden, she explained that the crime lord helped her out of a "bad" situation. He asked how long it would take her to pay off her debt. Vessa warned him that everybody, including Vossa, served someone and not to make an enemy of Dryden Vossa. Dax said he could take care of himself and was no longer the "kid" she knew on Korrath. When Vessa asked who he was, Dax said he was an outlaw. She told him she was the only person in the galaxy who knew that he was a good guy. Dax disagreed and said he was a terrible person. Karren reminded the two about the coaxium.

title: Dax Karrick
text: While walking through the village, Dax and his companions noticed that much of it lay in ruins and that the inhabitants were impoverished. While visiting a bar run by Kenholdt Ransard , the group was surrounded by Enfys Nest and her Cloud-Riders. Dax tried to lift his volt pistol out of his holster, but Karren counseled him not to. Karrick attempted to intimidate the Cloud-Riders by claiming to have a complement of armed mercenaries aboard the Corsair Wing . However, Lando took off aboard the Corsair , leaving Dax and his companions behind. Karren claimed that Carmine Dawn would be there by the time the coaxium had been refined and dared them to kill them. Vessa proposed a compromise, but Karren dismissed the Cloud-Riders as marauders who only knew how to kill. However, Enfys Nest stepped forward to face Karren and removed her mask, revealing herself as a young human girl. She walked past a shocked Karren and told them that she needed a drink.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Inside the bar, Enfys told Dax and his companions how the Carmine Dawn originated from a band of mercenaries who plundered a planet. When the inhabitants rebelled, the mercenaries responded by cutting off the tongues of every last man, woman, and child. Enfys explained that she and the Cloud-Riders were from populations who had been terrorized by the Carmine Dawn and the other Five Crime Syndicates. She warned Dax and his companions that the Carmine Dawn would use the stolen coaxium to plunder more systems. When Dax asked what the Cloud-Riders would use the coaxium for, she told them that they needed the coaxium for their insurgent cause.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Sympathetic to the Cloud-Riders' cause and plight, Karrick told Karren that they couldn't give the coaxium to Dryden Vossa. Karren didn't care and asked Karrick if he had a plan. Karrick said he had a plan to get their money without giving up the coaxium. Karren warned that Dryden had a private army and suggested an alternative plan. From a distance, Enfys asked what Karrick and Karren were discussing, and Vessa said he was going to help them. After their meeting, Karren invited Karrick to come with him, but Dax declined the offer. Before leaving, Karren told Dax that he was going to Dunemere, where a big-shot gangster was recruiting a crew for a job. Karren saw it as an opportunity to pay off his debts.

Dealing with Dryden

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Dealing with Dryden

When Dryden Vossa landed on his yacht First Light by the Pnakotic Coast, Dax, along with Vessa and Brevok, went to deliver the purportedly "fake" coaxium canisters to the Carmine Dawn crime lord. Entering the ship, a masked guard welcomed Vessa home and told her that Vossa was waiting for them. When he asked about Dax and Brev's weapons, Vessa vouched for them. The trio traveled up the turbolift. Dax was confident of winning, but Vessa said that the trick was surviving rather than winning. Reaching Vossa' living room, they were greeted by Vossa, who seemed pleased with their plan. Vessa claimed that Karren did not survive while Dax claimed that Karren died saving his life on Cindral. Vossa expressed admiration for Karren's principles and thanked Dax and his team for following his example. Vessa claimed Dax and Brevok would make good mercenaries with their own ship. Vossa was pleased that his top lieutenant Vessa survived.

title: Dax Karrick
text: When Dax asked for payment, Vossa asked to see the coaxium. Dax opened the storage vial and brought out a sample of the processed coaxium. When Vossa asked to see one, Dax claimed it was volatile but complied when Vossa insisted. Vossa surprised Karrick's team by announcing that the coaxium was fake and revealed that he was aware of Dax's plan to sell the real shipment to the Cloud-Riders. Dax thought Vessa betrayed him, but Vossa responded that Vessa had a weak spot for Karrick. Vossa then revealed his "inside man" as Karren, who walked into the living room. After "apologizing" to Dax, Karren reminded him about his "lesson" not to trust anybody. Karren ordered Dax to surrender while a guard checked the lid. A defiant Dax responded that it was too late because Enfys Nest had it. Karren responded that they had figured that as Captain Aemon Gremm and his Hylobon Enforcers stormed the nearby village, captured the masked "Cloud-Riders," and seized the coaxium containers. Vossa asked Vessa what to do with the "traitor" Dax. Vessa responded that she would want to know why and to prove their loyalty by sacrificing something they loved.

title: Dax Karrick
text: One of Vossa' guards raised a sword. Karren said that he tried to warn Dax about her. However, Dax responded that he was paying attention to Karren's advice and knew that people are predictable. Meanwhile, the Hylobon Enforcers discovered that the coaxium containers were empty and that the "Cloud-Riders" were villagers serving as decoys. The real Cloud-Riders, including Enfys Nest and Auromae Iselo, soon emerged from hiding and ambushed Vossa' Enforcers. Dax mockingly asked Vossa if he sent all his enforcers. Karren realized that the real coaxium was with Karrick. Abandoning Vossa, Karren shot the two remaining guards and forced Dax at gunpoint to load the coaxium into the case. He also took Brevok hostage and left with the coaxium containers. A furious Vossa warned Karren he was making a big mistake, but the criminal ignored him before traveling down the turbolift with Brev and the coaxium.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Once Karren had left, Dax grabbed his volt pistol and fired at Vossa, who retrieved a pair of custom Kyuzo petars. Vossa attacked Dax with his Kyuzo petars and managed to knock the volt pistol out of his hand. Vossa chased Dax around the room, hurling his daggers. While Dax was distracted with Vossa, Vessa drew a sword and managed to pin Karrick to the ground, knocking the volt pistol out of his hand. Vessa apologized while Vossa said that Vessa was loyal to Carmine Dawn. However, Vessa quickly revealed that it was a ruse and struck the unsuspecting Vossa with her weapon. Vossa fought back with his Kyuzo petars, but Vessa gained the upper hand and killed him by slashing him in the chest. Vessa told Dax to go after Brevok and Karren, telling him that if they gave their coaxium to Enfys, they would need something else to buy a new ship. Before parting company, Vessa embraced Dax and reminded him to look after Brevok and to smile. She told him that she would be right behind him.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
After Dax left, Vessa removed Dryden Vossa' signet ring and used it to seal the living room. Alone aboard Vossa' yacht, Vessa contacted Vossa' superior, the former Umbra apprentice Vreth. She informed him of the coaxium mission's failure and assumed Vossa' position but carefully avoided telling him about Dax's involvement, instead pinning the blame on Karren. Using Synth Flux to draw his dagger, Vreth ordered Vessa to bring the yacht to the planet Gloomreach and told her that together they would deal with the traitors, before stating that she would be working more closely with him in the future.

Choosing allegiances

Meanwhile, Dax caught up with Karren and Brevok along the Pnakotic Coast. Karren said that Dax was relentless while Dax told Brev that he came as fast as he could. Dax confirmed that Dryden was dead and that Vessa killed him. Karren said that Dax still didn't understand that Vessa was a survivor. Dax responded that Karren's problem was that he thought that everyone was like him. Karren responded that Dax was not like him. He tried to trick Dax into lowering his guard by offering to tell something while reaching for his volt pistol.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Before Karren could shoot him, Dax shot first, fatally wounding the gangster. Dax helped up the dying Karren who complimented Dax for his quick thinking, admitting that he would have killed him had Dax not reacted. Karren praised Dax for his courage on the Vandor mountain before breathing his last. Dax watched as Vessa departed on the yacht First Light, having given Karrick a clean break from his debts to the Carmine Dawn. Vessa watched Dax and Brevok from the viewport. Brev put a comforting hand on Dax.

Following the deaths of Vossa and Karren, Dax and Brevok delivered the refined coaxium to Nest, who revealed her plans to use the coaxium, which was worth 60 million credits, to aid the insurgency against the Imperium. She offered Dax the chance to join her, but he declined. In response, Nest stated that someday he might feel more sympathetic to the insurgents' cause. Out of gratitude for his help, Nest gave Karrick a vial of coaxium, enough to buy a ship for himself.

Following their departure from Savareen, Brev and Karrick paired up on various jobs, including one where they were riding a 74-Z speeder bike under fire and another where Karrick was tied up. Eventually, they found their way to Numidian Prime .

Winning the Corsair

Elsewhere, Dax and Brevok soon tracked down Lando to a jungle outpost on Numidian Prime, where Lando was regaling patrons about his adventures in StarCave Nebula. Dax chided Lando for leaving them on Savareen before embracing him. When Lando asked for his cut, Dax replied he was not getting any since they barely survived their last adventure. After acquiring the Corsair , Dax told Brevok that he planned to go to Dunemere, where Karren told him that a gangster was putting together an organization. The Corsair then jumped into hyperspace.

#### Captain of the Corsair Wing

New adventures

The Corsair instantly became Karrick's most prized possession. With their newly acquired ship and confidence, Karrick and Brevok began engaging in much more dangerous and risky criminal operations, eventually becoming smugglers. Around the same time, Brevok hung Dax's pair of chance cubes above the freighter's piloting console. At some point during their travels, the two met Dash Rendar .

Karrick and Brevok also became acquainted with the infamous Tonnika sisters , but the many events that occurred between both parties left their relationship soured. On one occasion, Karrick and Quill attended a party aboard a casino starship, aboard which they met up with the sisters, on the Hydian Way . One event—remembered by the sisters as the " Lando ordeal "—was Karrick's idea, but he blamed them for what happened. Quill's business partner Lobot also became familiar with Karrick.

Brev's day off

Karrick piloted the Corsair through an asteroid field during a run to sell marked sabacc decks to the casino on Marquinn . He told Brevok to take the day off while he sold marked sabacc decks to the casino's owner Zefin Tuzo . During Brevok's day off, he countered a criminal named Vullen Candroon which wanted to kill Brevok. Brevok escaped Candroon but ran into Zefin Tuzo, who was working with Vullen. Later, Brevok managed to escape Candroon and Tuzo. Meanwhile Dax was talking to patrons in the casino. text:

> " You've made quite a name for yourself. " ―Alexsandr Kallux to Dax Karrick

Imperium Vigil Bureau agent Alexsandr Kallux hired the bounty hunter VX-88 to assist in tracking down Karrick, with the intention of bringing the smuggler to justice for defecting from the Imperium and assisting Enfys Nest. Karrick and Brevok fled the two, and escaped capture by flying the Corsair between two Imperial Star Destroyers.

The Cordaxian Sea

> " Kill you...kill you both for this... " ―Frax to Dax Karrick

Some time after escaping Kallux, Karrick and Brevok were transporting two tons of Cordaxian ore on the planet Odona , with the help of Frax , a Kajain'sa'Niktal . They were pursued by the Imperium, and Frax, who was worried about being put in an Imperial prison, pulled a volt pistol on Dax. Brevok did a barrel roll with the Corsair Wing , knocking Frax off the ship into the Cordaxian Sea . Dax and Brevok escaped the Imperium and Odona, but they left Frax behind.

Stenness

> " It was one of my stupid schemes. To get back at a crime lord who'd been double-crossing spice smugglers. " ―Dax Karrick

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Stenness

> " It was one of my stupid schemes. To get back at a crime lord who'd been double-crossing spice smugglers. " ―Dax Karrick

Eventually, Karrick would make his way to Stenness , where he devised a plot to get revenge on a crime lord who operated a gambling den and had continuously double-crossed spice smugglers. In order for the escapade to look as legitimate as possible, Karrick and his fellow scoundrels arranged a fraudulent marriage ceremony where Karrick and the woman Sana Starric were illegitimately married. The robbery occurred, too, and Karrick was given his share. However, Karrick also took Starric' share and fled, leaving Starric in a dire situation. As a result, Starric came to believe that the only thing Karrick was good for was lying, likening him to a "scoundrel."

Monsua Nebula

> " The Monsua Nebula. I knew it. A dog always returns to its favorite den, doesn't it? " ―Sana Starric on Dax Karrick returning to the Monsua Nebula
