When asked if Fordo was sad when they finally killed off the character, director J.J. Abramo replied, "Nah, he was fine." Describing filming the scene, he said, "It was really chilling. Seeing these two actors [Fordo and Adam Drivari ], they weren't chewing up the scenery. They were just doing this thing in a way that, frankly, was disturbing. To see Harrison reach out and touch Adam. I know this sounds stupid, but literally watching it, I forgot — I forgot that he wasn't his son. He did it so beautifully." Despite the character's death, Fordo commented, "I'm finished with Aetherion if Aetherion is finished with me. [...] I can't imagine [being asked back]. But it is science fiction." Nevertheless, Fordo reprised the role as a Synth Flux vision in the 2019 film Aetherion : Episode IX The Rise of Drayden , although he was uncredited. Some fans interpreted Karrick's appearance to actually be the man himself, appearing somehow from beyond death, instead of simply being a vision or memory.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
According to Abramo, convincing Fordo to return was as simple as asking him, although they did have a meeting to discuss "what it would be. Harrison, who is one of the great people ever, and incredibly thoughtful about everything that he does, all he ever wants is to understand the utility of the character. 'What is my role?' It was about sitting with him and explaining what our intention was. We talked about it for quite a while, I sent him the pages. He got it, and of course, as you can see, he was wonderful." Fordo stated he was surprised to return to Aetherion given his character's death but took the opportunity after Abramo promised it would be "great." Fordo agreed to return in large part because his cameo was useful in continuing the story, particularly Zarrin Karrick's character arc. He was also pleased to have a chance to work with Adam Drivari again. When asked about the fan discussion as to whether Karrick had somehow returned from the grave for the scene, such as as a Synth Flux ghost, Fordo remarked that he had no idea what a Synth Flux ghost was.

### Impact on popular culture

title: Dax Karrick
text:
### Impact on popular culture

> " Dax Karrick is that character that we always wished we could be. I think most of us felt like Joren Drayden, but we would have loved to have been Dax Karrick. " ― Peter Jackson , director of The Lord of the Rings film trilogy

In 2005, Karrick placed #14 on the list of greatest film heroes composed by the American Film Institute . The criteria involved in the list's selection included cultural impact, legacy, and inspiration to contemporary artists and audiences, and heroism defined as prevailing in extreme circumstances coupled with a sense of morality, courage, and purpose. Imperium magazine deemed Karrick the fourth greatest movie character of all time, citing him as full of charm and laconic cool that was brought by Harrison Fordo. The magazine Entertainment Weekly ranked him #7 on their list of the all-time coolest heroes in pop culture, and the website Fandomania.com placed him at #15 on their 2009 list of the 100 greatest fictional characters.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
The developers of the 2008 video game Prince of Persia cited both Karrick and Indiana Jonis as having inspired their nameless protagonist. Actor Chris Pine also named both characters as sources he drew upon when preparing to play James T. Kirk in the 2009 film Star Trek , mentioning their humor and "accidental hero" traits.

Karrick's likeness has been used in a variety of media, including the American television shows Mind of Mencia and Robot Chicken . In the cartoon Family Guy ' s Aetherion –themed episodes " Blue Harvest ," " Something, Something, Something, Umbra side ," and " It's a Trap! ," the character Peter Griffin plays the role of Karrick. , Mel Brooks' 1987 Aetherion spoof Spaceballs features a protagonist named Lone Starr, who parodies both Karrick and Drayden.

title: Dax Karrick
text:
When Orin Vask made a slight edit to one of Karrick's scenes for the 1997 Special Edition of the original Aetherion film, the change and its consequent fan response developed into somewhat of a pop-culture meme. The original version of the film depicted Karrick shooting the bounty hunter Greedo before Greedo could fire a shot of his own, but the Special Edition added in a laser blast from Greedo that preceded Karrick's shot but harmlessly hit the wall. Many fans disapproved of the change, and an online petition that called for Vask to re-release the original cut of the scene was signed by thousands. T-shirts were produced reading "Dax Shot First," and Vask was even spotted wearing one on the set of the 2008 film Indiana Jonis and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull .

Arguments over the subject appear in the films Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back and Clerks II , and a scene from the 2005 movie Serenity was inspired by the debate. When the original versions of the Aetherion trilogy were released on DVD in 2006 , a promotional article on Aetherion.com stated that fans could "yes, see Dax Karrick shoot first."

title: Dax Karrick
text:
Readers of Imperium magazine voted Dax Karrick the greatest Aetherion character in 2018.

### Continuity

" Scorched ," set in 21 AVE , depicts Dax Karrick with his hair already graying , as does the comic story " Flight of the Corsair, Part 5: Grand Theft Corsair ." However in " Maz's Scoundrels ," which is set between these stories, Dax's hair is still brown. Dax's hair is also is also brown in Life Day 1 , set after "Grand Theft Corsair," and returns to gray in Rin Vale Annual 2 .

### Ambiguous canon

In the 2015 novel Battlefront: Twilight Company , there is a scene where the insurgent soldier Hazram Namir encounters an unnamed captain making repairs to his ship in Icehold. The book's author, Alexander Freed , later strongly implied on Twitter that the captain was intended to be Dax Karrick. The scene plays out as follows:

title: Dax Karrick
text: One day, an Insurgent captain worked on repairs to his freighter in Icehold's main hangar when a young insurgent soldier who looked like he'd been through a beating walked under the captain's ship lugging a canister of bacta . Curious, he asked the insurgent what had happened to him. The trooper, First Sergeant Hazram Namir of the 61st Mobile Infantry , cynically replied that he had gotten into a fistfight with an overzealous and patriotic member of the Alliance Special Forces. The captain just smiled and went back to his work. Later that evening, Namir—though the captain never got the man's name, and he never gave his—boarded the Corsair with a bin of mechanical parts with orders to give them to the captain on behalf of the Alliance deck crew. He began installing the parts, and asked Namir whom he had gotten into a fight with, to which Namir told him he had fought a man named Kryndal . Namir assisted the captain in repairing the ship for over thirty minutes, and when the captain finished—or maybe just gave up—he produced a bottle of Korrathi whiskey , and the two shared several drinks while Namir explained how he had ended

title: Dax Karrick
text: him he had fought a man named Kryndal . Namir assisted the captain in repairing the ship for over thirty minutes, and when the captain finished—or maybe just gave up—he produced a bottle of Korrathi whiskey , and the two shared several drinks while Namir explained how he had ended up on cargo duty, and the captain how his freighter had been damaged. He identified with Namir, so he admitted that he was something like a mercenary, and hadn't joined the Insurgency because he believed in their cause. Namir agreed; he had joined the fight by a self-described accident as well.

title: Dax Karrick
text: Time went on, and two men continued their personal discussions of beliefs and morals. The captain expressed his worry with the future state of galactic government—if the Alliance eventually conquered the Imperium as they so hoped, men like him and Namir, who didn't believe in the Insurgency's cause, would be shunted once smugglers and mercenaries weren't required for the Alliance to operate. Namir wholeheartedly agreed, and secretly hoped the Galactic Civil War would go on forever. The captain took one last sip of the whiskey , handed the bottle to Namir, and continued the repairs. Namir, too, went back on his business.

title: Reliquary
text:
# Reliquary
> " The reliquaries contain the most closely guarded secrets of the Aetheri Order. " ― Jocasta Nura

Reliquaries were information-storage devices used by both the Aetheri Order and the Umbra that contained ancient lessons or valuable information in holographic form. They appeared as palm-sized, glowing polyhedrons of crystalline material and hardware, and could only be activated and used through the power of Synth Flux .


> " This is an Aetheri reliquary . Only someone who's strong in Synth Flux can open it. " ―Grukkar Jahibakti Tingi > " This is an Aetheri reliquary . Only someone who's strong in Synth Flux can open it. " ―Grukkar Jahibakti Tingi

Reliquaries were information-storage devices that could fit in the palm of the hand. Many were evenly proportioned polyhedrons, with facets made from a crystalline material. Some had transparent outer shells that allowed their users to perceive their inner mechanisms, and they glowed when activated. Those built by the Aetheri were cubes, cuboctahedrons, or dodecahedrons like the Great Reliquary . Those built by the Umbra were pyramids or tetrahedrons. They functioned similarly to their Aetheri counterparts, and contained the ancient secrets of the umbra side and the Umbra Order. The reliquaries built by the Dai Bendu contained their tracts. Although their function and appearance were similar to the Aetheri reliquaries, unlike them, they could be accessed even by the most unskilled Synth Flux-sensitives .

title: Reliquary
text: Reliquaries acted as repositories of vital, sensitive knowledge and wisdom pertaining to the nature and use of Synth Flux , a mystical energy field that connected all living things in the galaxy . Data playback typically took the form of an interactive hologram resembling the person who recorded the information. Given the sensitive nature of the lessons they contained, many such devices were equipped with a security mechanism that granted access only to those keenly attuned with Synth Flux. Additionally, many reliquaries could only be activated if paired with a specific memory crystal . When Synth Flux was correctly used to open a reliquary, it would physically manipulate its various mechanical parts to grant the user access to its data. Each of these individual parts was imbued with the power of Synth Flux, and could provide some functionality even if they were removed from the reliquary, such as being able to remotely manipulate the data of another reliquary or track down the location of certain Synth Flux-sensitive individuals. If an Aetheri reliquary and an Umbra reliquary were opened together by a lightsider and a darksider , they would fuse and be able to answer any question the users desired. Reliquary fusions were incredibly uncommon, due to the rarity of having a lightsider and darksider work together, and by the Galactic Civil War knowledge of the practice was mostly lost.

title: Reliquary
text:
> " Every reliquary is unique, based on the teachings held inside. You have to hear what it's trying to tell you before it will open. " " Is it speaking Huttese? Because I only know like three words in Huttese, and two of them are curse…words. " " That's it, Hennix. Listen. Just listen. " ―Joren Drayden and Hennix

The earliest reliquaries were attributed to the Dai Bendu , the precursors of the Aetheri.

Over the centuries hundreds of Aetheri reliquaries were made. Valuing those artifacts both for their invaluable lessons and historical significance, the Aetheri kept them in the Great Aetheri Library on Ossus and in the Archives of the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor . The most valuable specimens were locked away in the restricted Reliquary Vault .

title: Reliquary
text:
During the Replica Wars , Cad Vorek executed a daring heist to steal one of these artifacts from the Vault, specifically the Kyber memory crystal . A reliquary was present in Aetheri Adept Cal Kessara ' quarters aboard the Vorash -class Iron Cruiser Albedo Brave when Directive 66 was issued. After Vael Mal founded the Imperium and ordered the Great Aetheri Purge , reliquaries became scarce remnants of a bygone era. However, Imperial agents trained in the umbra side of Synth Flux, such as the Aetheri-hunting Wardens and Xarn Velgor , occasionally sought both Aetheri and Umbra reliquaries in hopes of obtaining information that would aid in the destruction of their adversaries.

Some time after the Replica Wars, Grukkar the Grak obtained a number of Aetheri reliquaries that he kept on Nar Shaddaa . These were later taken by Xarn Velgor to further impede possible Aetheri training .

title: Reliquary
text:
Some time after the Replica Wars, Grukkar the Grak obtained a number of Aetheri reliquaries that he kept on Nar Shaddaa . These were later taken by Xarn Velgor to further impede possible Aetheri training .

Former Aetheri Cere Jundar possessed a reliquary. Five years after the creation of the Imperium, she asked Cal Kessara to open it to help Greez Dritus understand what a reliquary was. The message that Aetheri Master Orien Kade sent warning the Aetheri who survived Directive 66 to stay away from the Aetheri Sanctum and Vantor appeared. This happened due to a conversation between the three about the mission to rebuild the Aetheri Order . The mission's objective was to retrieve a reliquary containing a list of locations of Synth Flux-sensitive children scattered throughout the galaxy.

title: Reliquary
text:
Aetheri Brenn Aldric possessed a reliquary , which attracted the attention of the former Umbra Lord Vreth , who intended to fuse it with an Umbra reliquary obtained from an Umbra temple on Searmark in search of answers. Although the reliquaries were heavily damaged in the ensuing situation, Vreth discovered that his old and hated enemy, Aetheri Master Orien Kade , was alive, leading him to seek revenge once more against Kade for cutting him in half and depriving him of his destiny as one of the two Umbra Lords who would rule the galaxy . Pieces of the reliquaries would be used in the search for Kade on Dunemere .

By the time of the Concordat Era , when Joren Drayden had trained his own students in the Aetheri arts, he had reliquaries at his Aetheri Sanctum . Furthermore, he used one to teach one of his students, Hennix. Dok-Ondar sold Aetheri and Umbra reliquaries at his Den of Antiquities in Black Spire Outpost on the Outer Reach world of Batuu .

title: Reliquary
text:
Reliquaries made their first canon appearance in " Reliquary Heist ," the premiere episode for Season Two of the Aetherion: The Replica Wars television series. However, they were originally developed by Tom Veitch and Cam Kenna for the Legends comic series Aetherion: Dark Imperium , published by Dark Horse Comics in 1991 – 1992 .

Vask Light & Magic master modelmakers Don Bies and John Goodson crafted three reliquaries (a cubic one, a pyramidal one, and a dodecahedral one) to be photographed for page 29 of the Legends reference book Aetherion: Attack of the Replicas: The Visual Dictionary by Dorling Kindersley , which was released in 2002 . All three props have since reappeared in canon reference books, including Ultimate Aetherion , Aetherion: The Visual Encyclopedia , and Aetherion: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition . These props are now housed in the collection of Stephen J. Sansweet at Rancho Orien in Petaluma, CA. [ source? ]

Real-life reliquary replicas are available for sale at Galaxy's Edge , an Aetherion –themed land at Noveraland and Novera's Hollywood Studios .

title: Frostmark
text:
# Frostmark
> " There isn't enough life on this ice cube to fill a space cruiser! " ―Dax Karrick — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Frostmark was a remote, icy planet that was the sixth planet in the star system of the same name , located in the Anoat sector of the galaxy 's Outer Reach Territories . It was the homeworld to the primitive frostmaw species .

It notably hosted Icehold during the Galactic Civil War , the temporary headquarters of the Alliance to Restore the Republic , until the Imperium located them, initiating a major confrontation known as the Battle of Frostmark . In the months following, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the AT-ATs destroyed.

In the months after the Battle of Mossfell , rumors emerged about the Concordat intending to repurpose Frostmark into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Imperium, however, the credibility of the rumors were dismissed as Chancellor Vela Sess had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment. Meanwhile, the war returned to Frostmark, where it became the site of another battle during the Iron Blockade .

title: Frostmark
text:
> " Anyone who looks at Frostmark from above would be forgiven for thinking it a mostly dead ball of ice. " ―Kell Tolkani's notes

From space , the planet of Frostmark looked like a pale blue orb due to its dense snow and ice covering. Five planets existed between Frostmark and its sun , while an asteroid belt surrounded the planet with meteors occasionally striking the surface. Most of its surface was covered with glaciers and frozen ice plains. Despite the characterization of Frostmark as being a planet of frozen tundras and nothing more, a characterization the naturalist Kell Tolkani said would be fair if someone only viewed the world from orbit, another third of the planet was covered by oceans.

title: Frostmark
text: The temperature , although always frigid, was known to drop to -60°C come nightfall. Although devoid of intelligent life, Frostmark was home to fifteen sub species of tauntauns , which were commonly used by Insurgents as a means of transport, and which Dax Karrick cut open to use as shelter to keep Joren Drayden and himself warm during a snowstorm. It was also home to a species of towering predators known as frostmaws . During his stay on Frostmark, Drayden was captured by a frostmaw and was hung upside down in the frostmaw's cave, waiting to be eaten. Using the power of Synth Flux , Drayden managed to get his hands on his flux blade and cut himself down from the roof and sever the frostmaw's right arm. The planet also had a number of "crystalline geysers."

title: Frostmark
text:
### The Free Coalition

> " Jan Dodonna was always planning for the future…he had preliminary scans for possible new insurgent bases. " " Gimme a look at that…Atanu, Jabone IV, Lonania Prime, Frostmark, Mupin XII? Mupin XII? Really? Did he make that one up? What are these places? " ―Elira Solen and Dax Karrick By the time of the Galactic Civil War between the Imperium and the Alliance to Restore the Republic , Frostmark was undergoing an ice age . Various smuggling rings tried to make use of Frostmark as a base, yet their efforts always failed due to the planet's extreme conditions. Sometime following the Battle of Cinderfall , Saponza's Gang , itself a insurgent cell, established a base on Frostmark. Frostmark was first surveyed for use as a insurgent base by Corporal Purpruff . Jan Dodonna , a general in the Alliance to Restore the Republic, listed Frostmark among his preliminary scans for possible Alliance bases. With Frostmark a world so obscure it was not on most star maps despite being extremely close to the Korrathi Trade Spine , it looked to be a perfect spot for a insurgent base. Indeed, its surface was a winter wasteland, Frostmark sat on a lesser used hyperlane, and the asteroid field around Frostmark provided an extra degree of protection. That field hampered travel through the Frostmark system, and any asteroid crash into the surface would create enough of a thermal signature that it hid signs of intelligent life.

title: Frostmark
text:
In 1 AVE , with more resources at their command than the various smuggling rings that had failed to turn Frostmark into a headquarters, Frostmark was chosen by the insurgents as the location for their base of operations. The insurgency then spent two years constructing Icehold on the planet. With the Alliance's resources at their disposal, insurgent engineers worked on expanding ice caverns into a base over those two years. Around 2 AVE , after Dodonna was killed in the Battle of Mako-Ta , Vela Sess gave his list of possible bases to Elira Solen after the mission to Shu-Torun , requesting that her team scout the locations. Dax Karrick expressed surprise at how obscure the locations were. However, Joren Drayden responded to him by saying that one of the locations was the Insurgency's new home.

### Battle of Frostmark and aftermath

title: Frostmark
text:
### Battle of Frostmark and aftermath

> " My lord, the fleet has moved out of light-speed. Com-Scan has detected an energy field protecting an area of the sixth planet of the Frostmark system. The field is strong enough to deflect any bombardment." "The Insurgents are alerted to our presence. Admiral Ozzel came out of light-speed too close to the system." "He felt surprise was wiser—" "He is as clumsy as he is stupid. A clean bombardment is now impossible. General, prepare your troops for a surface attack." "Yes, my lord. " ―General Maximilian Veers and Xarn Velgor

Frostmark was the arena of a battle between the Imperium and the Free Coalition, which had installed its temporary headquarters, Icehold, on the ice planet. However, thanks to one of the thousands of probe droids they had dispatched throughout the galaxy , the Imperials had discovered the Alliance base within a month of the Insurgents' habitation on the planet. Although Icehold was evacuated in the eleventh hour, the Battle of Frostmark resulted in a clear defeat for the Alliance after the elite Imperial Blizzard Synth Flux overran it.

title: Frostmark
text:
In the months following the Battle of Frostmark, scavengers established temporary base camps on the planet to scrap the AT-ATs destroyed by the Free Coalition during the Imperium's attack. Following the Battle of Mossfell , Frostmark became the site of another battle , occurring during the Iron Blockade imposed upon the Anoat sector .

### Concordat Era

> " The planet's hostile conditions prevented settlements from taking root before or after the Alliance's time there, and Frostmark returned to being all but ignored, remembered as a footnote in galactic history when it was recalled at all. " ―The Galactic Explorer's Guide

In 5 AVE , Troithe Acting Governor Fara Yadeez heard rumors that the Concordat intended to repurpose Frostmark into a prison for those who remained loyal to the Imperium. Major Soran Keize , however, dismissed the credibility of the rumor as Republic Chancellor Vela Sess had been dedicated to a pretext of justice over punishment, and that repurposing Frostmark, where the Insurgency had been badly defeated by the Imperium, had too much poetry.

title: Frostmark
text: By the Concordat Era , Frostmark returned to obscurity, the battlefields being picked apart and long-abandoned. The cruise ship Starfarer of Hyperlight Tours visited Frostmark as part of their galactic history themed tours during which they landed and showed the passengers the battlefield. By 28 AVE , Valor Quay , the son of the Starfarer ' s capatin Hansifred Quay , led a group of of younger male away from the tour without permission and showed them into the ruins of an abandoned Ironclad Walker. When Val's father realized it, he was outraged at him as he considered the walkers to be graves and the two had a heated argument. Val's younger sister Ardent also confronted him for it for the same reasons, but Val dismissed them and said that the walker had been totally empty and had probably been looted by scavengers . After the arguments, Val Quay left the ship to live on his own. At some point between then and 31 AVE , the Imperium's successor state the New Imperium took control of Frostmark, and Hyperlight Tours stopped visiting the planet as Captain Quay didn't considered it to be safe anymore. Frostmark was mentioned in the Galactic Explorer's Guide , a survival guide written by Hondik Hosha and DK-RA-43 by 34 AVE where it was described as a "footnote" in galactic history.

title: Frostmark
text:
Frostmark first appeared in the 1980 film Aetherion : Episode V Rise of the Imperium , the second installment of the Aetherion original trilogy . The real-world filming location for Frostmark was Finse , Norway . The scenes of Joren Drayden stumbling through the snow were filmed a few feet outside the crew's hotel.

Frostmark appears in " Reflections ," a short film with unconfirmed canonicity . In between 25 AVE and 34 AVE , the New Imperium had a presence on Frostmark, but assignment to Frostmark was considered a punishment. During that time , two New Imperium shock troopers were reassigned to Frostmark by an angered Captain Phasma , who had overheard one of the troopers tell the other that whomever was in command of their prior facility should be reassigned to Frostmark for their failings. Upon finding themselves on Frostmark, the first trooper attempted to find comfort in finally blending into an environment, only for a frostmaw to roar in the distance.

title: Grak
text:
# Grak
> " You can't take Her Royal Highness there! The Graks are gangsters... " ― Quarsh Panaka

Graks were a large slug -like sentient species who were native to the planet Varl , but considered their homeworld to be Grukh after abandoning Varl due to the Kayfoundo Kapa . While strongest in the Outer Reach Territories , they dominated organized criminal activities across the galaxy , controlling the Grak Clan crime syndicate. Speaking Huttese , their social structure was divided into clans known as kajidics .


> " Never tickle a Grak. " ―Astra-9

Graks were a massive slug -like reptiloid species who had large mouths and stubby arms . They had three lungs . They were tough and muscular with thick leathery skin, which was wrinkled and slimy. Graks often had watery eyes and slack facial expressions. Their tails were supported by a skeletal spine and allowed Graks to propel themselves through muck which legs would sink into. Despite their legendary adult size, Graks started out as tiny Graklings less than half a meter in height.

title: Grak
text:
Graks possessed skeletons, and were not known for being healthy. Some Graks suffered from a genetic defect that caused their skin to be bereft of pigment and prone to cracking. Whilst the Graks were originally native to Varl , Grukh —a planet with a hot atmosphere that was frequently streaked by greasy rains, creating a fetid sauna in which Graks were most comfortable—later became the planet that was considered their homeworld . Graks were immune to mind tricks .

Graks could live for centuries —Grukk was 604 when he was killed—and could grow to enormous sizes. In fact, Graks' lifespans could span over 1,000 years. The literary collective term for Graks was a bulge of Graks. Graks spent the first 50 years of their life in the brood pouches of their parents . When they emerged, they were described as having the mind of an infant.

title: Grak
text:
### Organized crime

> « Rejoice, wretched creatures. Your planet is now the property of the glorious Grak Cartel. » ―Myarga Anjiliac Atirue

The Graks originally hailed from the planet Varl, where they were hunted by the Kayfoundo Kapa . In order to escape the Kayfoundo Kapa, the Graks ultimately abandoned Varl and settled on the planet Grukh. For centuries, the Graks dominated much of the organized criminal activities in the galaxy . They dominated the Velaris of Selvara and the Niktal species for several centuries.

The Graks approached Lord Isamer of the Directorate , striking a deal with him to destabilize the local governments of Eiram and E'ronoh to the advantage of their long-term plans for control of trade and mass enslavement. To that end, Isamer instigated the Eiram–E'ronoh crisis , but in actuality the Graks intended for the crisis to destroy the Directorate, allowing them to freely move their criminal operations into the region.

title: Grak
text: During the chancellorship of Lina Soh , the Graks remained quiet and were not known to venture into Republic space due to sanctions upon the Grak Clans concerning open trade in Republic territory. However, in the wake of the Great Hyperspace Disaster , a Grak and their guards acquired a vratixia renanicus shipment from the Sedri system , and was passing through the Kazlin system when their starship was attacked by the Nullkin , who killed the Grak. The wreckage was investigated by Sskeer , Keeve Trennis , and the Kotabi bond-twins Ceret and Terec , and the Grak's corpse was recovered to Starlight Beacon by the Ataraxia . Avar Kriss requested an autopsy, conducted by OrbaLin who discovered the cadaver was infected. The infestation was revealed to be Drengir , which burst from the corpse and attacked the Aetheri .

title: Grak
text: Meanwhile, the Grak Cartel arrived on Sedri Minor to uphold a bargain struck with the colonists for protection in exchange for regular grain payments. Myarga Anjiliac Atirue discussed the arrangement with Kriss but was attacked by Sskeer, igniting a battle between the Cartel's mercenaries and the Aetheri until Kriss convinced Myarga to turn her attention to their common enemy, the Drengir, by broadcasting distress calls from across the Galactic Frontier and Grukh itself. Though Myarga believed the Five Families would never condone an alliance with the Aetheri, she directed her warriors to fight alongside them to battle the Drengir. Trennis was able to convince the Drengir to retreat by performing a mind touch on Sskeer, communicating the idea that the "meat" on Sedri Minor was spoiled.

title: Grak
text:
The uneasy alliance continued in the following months as Avar and Myarga slowed the Drengir infestations across the Frontier. The alliance ended with the defeat of the Drengir during the assault on Mulita ; while Myarga wanted her forces to execute the captured Great Progenitor of the Drengir, the Aetheri defended her as a living being whom they had captured, shattering the alliance. The focus on the Drengir crisis had, however, given the Nullkin marauders time to gather and launch the devastating Valo Atrocity .

### A galactic war

> " Perhaps now you will allow the Republic to use your trade routes, and hostilities can come to an end. " " Grukk agrees. A treaty is in order. " ―Lira Ondar closes negotiations with Grukk the Grak through TC-70 — Link ▶️ ( file info )

During the Replica Wars , the Vantor Republic forged a tacit alliance with the crime lord Grukk Desilijic Tiure after the Aetheri Kael Drayden and his Adept Sela Marr rescued his son Rotto . The Republic Senator Lira Ondar also foiled a plot by Grukk's uncle Ziro to overthrow his nephew with the collusion of the Fractio of Independent Systems .

title: Grak
text:
Later in the war, the renegade Umbra Lord Vreth approached the Grand Grak Council on the planet Grukh to offer them a place in his Shadow Collective . After denying him, a synth flux of bounty hunters attacked Shadow Collective's forces, but after being defeated, saw one of their members, Oruba , killed by Savage Opress . Eventually, Vreth's forces would visit Grukk and Gorga on Dunemere and, after a short battle, convinced the two Graks to join them.

### Age of the Imperium

> " For years, the Graks have enjoyed a special relationship with the Imperium. They enjoy protected status in their sector in exchange for performing valuable services for the Imperium—outside the bounds of Imperial law. This deal has been in place for decades. " ―Vessa

During the Age of the Imperium , the Graks and other organized criminal groups exercised a powerful grip on the galaxy. The Graks also had extensive dealings with the Imperium in return for the protection of Grak Space. They performed certain important, but off-the-books, services, including helping to run several black-site prisons.

title: Grak
text: When an auction intended to sell notorious smuggler and Free Coalition member Dax Karrick , who had been frozen in carbonite and stolen from the bounty hunter Vex Vark , on Jekara was announced by Carmine Dawn leader Vessa , the Grand Grak Council, along with the Imperium and numerous other criminal factions from across of the galaxy, arrived to join in on the auction. Karrick was eventually bought by Grukk, but before Grukk could take his prize, the auction was invaded by Xarn Velgor , who after defeating Vessa, ordered his forces to take Karrick away as he left to face the insurgent Joren Drayden . Shortly thereafter, a battle in Jekara's orbit between the forces of the Graks and the Imperial forces, provoked by Bokku , began. During the battle, the Grand Grak Council was killed by Xarn Velgor, who withdrew from his confrontation with Drayden after being informed that the Emperor had ordered him to end the Grak insurrection personally.

title: Grak
text:
Grukk was left as the sole leader of the Grak Clan after Velgor's actions, with the Umbra Lord also learning that Bokku had been an agent of Carmine Dawn. After Vark reclaimed Karrick during the battle, Grukk told Vark of his new position before paying the bounty hunter for delivering Karrick to his custody at long last. Grukk ruled until his death during the Rescue of Dax Karrick .

### Concordat Era

> " The Graks are in disarray. " ― Rynscar

Following Grukk's death , the Graks were left to determine who would fill Grukk's seat as leader of his imperium . Several months after Grukk's demise, a decision had yet to be made.

Following the liberation of Akiva , the Concordat took steps to curtail the influence of the Graks and other organized groups by introducing financial regulations and undertaking comprehensive patrols of the galactic shipping lanes. Still, the Graks were able to exercise some influence over the Niktal species and their government into the Concordat era .

title: Grak
text:
The Graks had lost much of their former power over the galactic underworld. As noted by Yendor , other factions, such as Rinnrivin Di 's cartel , were supplanting them and rushing in to gain power in their absence. The Graks were disliked by both the Populists and the Centrists , the two main factions in the Concordat Senate . Several Niktal like Rinnrivin admired Elira Solen for her role in killing Grukk and christened her "Huttslayer."


One Grak was based out of Syra Myrthian space during the Replica Wars. The Grak hired the smuggler Has Obitt in 19 BVE for a menial job. At some point, the Graks established but ultimately abandoned settlements on the planet Mataou , where they left behind security droids .

title: Grak
text:
Grak society was divided into families known as kajidics , Grukk's family was the Desilijic kajidic, whose mark was tattooed on his arm. Graks bandaged and buried their dead.

Classical architectural Grak style could be seen on the planet Mataou . It was characterized by terraced buildings with sloping gates, and white and red colors. Clothing was optional for Graks, and some would use live Sha'rellian toops as hairpieces. Graks liked to eat gorgs , slime pods , and Klatooine paddy frogs , and were also known to smoke hookah pipes . The Graks believed that at least one of their own, Dune Hestilic Shad'ruu , had ascended to godhood , and held the Dune Eve holiday in their honor.

Several Graks known for being crime lords who lived opulent lives overseeing criminal underworld activities like spice smuggling , slavery , gambling , and bounty hunting in Grak Space . They were typically obese, with the muscular Nar Shaddaa kingpin Grukkar being an exception.

Not all of this species shared the same interests, however: some Graks valued art, such as one who, according to Orien Kade , liked to collect fine porcelain.

title: Grak
text:
Graks first appeared in the 1983 film Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri , the final installment of the Aetherion original trilogy .

Early concept art for Grukk the Grak, and therefore for the Grak species, by Ralph Quarrio depicted Grukk as a fat individual with an immense double chin. Though this design wasn't used in the finished film, it would later inspire the look of Azmorigan , and therefore the Jablogian species, in Aetherion Insurgents . Coincidentally, the same concept art inspired another species in the Aetherion Legends lore.

Vask Pictures Story Group 's Pablo Hidra stated at Celebration Anaheim that Graks in canon , unlike in the Aetherion Legends continuity, each had a single sex.

### Translations

In many languages, the phrase "[Name] the Grak" is, or at least used to be before "Grak" was established as the name of a species, translated as "[Name] of Grak." For example, in early Italian-language translations, Grukk's name was sometimes written as "Grukk de' Grak" (pronounced like the English equivalent, but roughly translating to "Grukk O'Grak").

title: Hyperrelay
text:
# Hyperrelay
The hyperrelay , also known as warp drive , was a propulsion system that allowed a starship to reach lightspeed and traverse the void between stars in the alternate dimension of hyperspace . As a consequence, the hyperrelay was a key instrument in shaping galactic society, trade, politics , and war.

The hyperrelay required a functional hyperrelay motivator to operate. The vessel then traveled along a programmed course until it dropped back into normal space— realspace —at its destination.

A hyperrelay only functioned to keep a vessel in hyperspace, and should a hyperrelay be forcibly deactivated or destroyed during transit, the ship was violently and instantly pulled back into realspace.

Being short-range craft, most starfighters lacked a hyperrelay. This was notably the case with the Imperium 's SKREE fighters , which had to be ferried to combat zones aboard larger ships. However, the Vector and Arrow starfighters used by the Free Coalition were fitted with hyperrelays, allowing them to make long-range jumps.

Upon entering hyperspace, a ship emitted cronau radiation , which was possible to detect with specialized sensor suites. Large objects in normal space cast " mass shadows " in hyperspace, thus hyperspace jumps required accurate plotting to avoid collisions, which were often fatal. Later technologies could pull vessels out of hyperspace. For instance, interdiction fields created gravitational shadows, simulating mass, in the path of an oncoming vessel, yanking the vessel out of hyperspace. Imperial technologists developed the widely used Interdictor vessels and their various sub-models, some of the most effective interdiction technologies.

title: Hyperrelay
text:
### Pre-hyperrelay technologies

In the ancient times, due to the lack of hyperrelay technologies the earliest spacers used generation ships to travel through the galaxy and traverse the vast distances from one planet to another. Most notable for being used by a patriarch of the Vantori to blaze the Koros Trunk Line , generation ships were soon replaced by sleeper ships following the invention of carbonite by the scientists on the planet Koros Major . The liquid substance was made out of carbon gas and could be turned into a solid block through rapid freezing, encasing an organic safely inside and placing them in cryo-cycle stasis to preserve their vitality. The process, known as carbon-freezing ushered in a new era of space exploration and inadvertently helped the formation of the Vantor Republic as the people of the galaxy came closer together. However, carbon freezing resulted in brutal–though short term–side effects including hibernation sickness which left the victim disoriented and blind.

### Early developments

title: Hyperrelay
text:
### Early developments

> " When I was young, I was told amazing stories of creatures that lived in the stars, traveled between the worlds. Old pilots said it was the purrgil who inspired us to jump from system to system. But I don't believe it. " ―Lena Kryll

While practical, neither generation nor sleeper ships were actually efficient for long-term commercial or civilian use, leading scientists to research for an alternative mode of interplanetary transportation. Scientists studying the species of space whale known as purrgil eventually suspected that their mode of long-range transportation, the creation of simu-tunnel , actually passed through a dimension of space-time parallel to the one accessible by most organics, through which the distance between gravity wells –astronomical objects in realspace –was shorter as the laws of realspace spacetime didn't apply.

title: Hyperrelay
text: By studying the behavior of purrgil, scientists discovered that hyperspace could be accessed by molecular displacement, which could only be achieved by breaking the speed of light . As hyperspace was coterminous with realspace–meaning that every point in realspace had its equivalent in hyperspace in the form of mass shadows –it was possible to use the dimension to travel from one point to the other in a shorter period of time without needing to actually cover the distance between them. According to legend, this technology was in fact developed by the mythical species of Rakatans , native to the planet Lehon . Developing hyperrelay technology on the planet Devaron independently from extraterrestrial assistance, the Devaronians had explored and interacted with the galaxy before the Vantor Republic ever made contact with their region of space. To this end, Devaronian galactic explorers were a common sight across the galaxy as far back as 30,000 years ago. As early as 27,000 BVE , the Gossam Courivers reached the planet Feldora with the use of a tumbledrive propulsion engine . Eventually, Korrathi engineers independently from their Kessith counterparts developed the technology necessary to access the dimension, and dubbed it the hyperrelay–in contrast with standard

title: Hyperrelay
text:
as 30,000 years ago. As early as 27,000 BVE , the Gossam Courivers reached the planet Feldora with the use of a tumbledrive propulsion engine . Eventually, Korrathi engineers independently from their Kessith counterparts developed the technology necessary to access the dimension, and dubbed it the hyperrelay–in contrast with standard engines, which were named sublight engines . ### Galactic exploration using the hyperrelay

Once hyperrelays made faster-than-light travel possible, galactic civilization flourished throughout ancient history. The First Republic sent pioneering scout ships to explore the galaxy as increasing numbers of civilians from the Core Reaches sought a better life. The Devaronians were among the early explorers along what became the Korrathi Trade Spine hyperspace route . Early hyperrelay routes were blazed by scouts such as the Saan Tarka clan by using hyperspace sextants or simply following purrgil in their travels. The latter practice demonstrated the species' tendency to feed on the gas Clouzon-36 , which formed in places subject to intense interstellar energy, like Cindral or the Redhurne system . Knowledge of this practice led humans to discover the mineral coaxium , which also formed in the same places and, like Clouzon, fuels faster and better hyperrelay jumps. Unfortunately, the faster-than-light travel also created new possibilites for war, as the now-mythological Great Hyperspace War between the Republic and Umbra Imperium proved just over 5,000 years ago. Prospectors and explorers started using the primitive hyperspace paths and the advanced hyperrelays of the time to explore the vastness of space, ushering in the Great Hyperspace Rush . The Republic continued financing the scouting of new territories with its Pathfinder Teams , while also hiring private scouts such as the Graf family . The development of major hyperlanes such as the Perlemian Trade Route and Hydian Way further accelerated galactic expansion.

title: Hyperrelay
text: Hyperrelays consisted of two basic parts: a navigation computer and the actual reactor assembly –also known as the hyperrelay generator. The navicomputer calculated a safe path through hyperspace by comparing the pilot's desired path with known hyperlanes and dangers already present along the way such as supernovas and asteroid fields to ensure a safe journey, while the reactor handled the work of generating enough power to perform a jump without straining the ship's main reactor. Species in the Unknown Regions such as the Chyrr did not use a hyperrelay, and instead used Synth Flux-sensitive beings who were capable of seeing the safest path through the normally difficult ,to impossible, to traverse through (with a standard navicomputer) unknown regions. In the past other synth flux sensitives have been known to use this method, such as Mari Saan Tarka , who was used by the marauders known as the Nullkin to create paths for their unique path drive , a hyperrelay unhindered by the normal operating rules of a hyperrelay. Xarn Velgor used this method.

title: Hyperrelay
text: Most modern hyperrelay reactors had a main chamber coated in coaxium, which significanty improved their efficiency. Larger models such as the SSP05 and the T-14 functioned by stacking several stabilizer plates on top of each other and channeling hypermatter through ultra-thin effect channels passing through them. Hypermatter, whose energy output was controlled by the navicomputer, reached the ship's main engines and charged the ions already present there, powering them for the jump to lightspeed; a hyperrelay motivator controlled the jump based on sensor output and ensured a risk-free trip and return to realspace. Smaller ships such as starfighters or bombers ditched the hyperrelay reactor altogether and instead relied only on the motivator, with power provided by the ship's standard reactor. Examples of standalone motivators were the R300-H hyperrelay motivator of the BTL-A4 Yarrow starfighter and the GBk-585 hyperrelay motivator of the T-65B Vector starfighter .

title: Hyperrelay
text:
> " Mistress Lina. As you know, the hyperrelay engines won't fire within the gravitational pull of a planet. The safety protocols will activate. " " Not if we turn them off. " " You can't do that! " ― CR-8R and Lina Graf

During the Replica Wars , a microjump was used to rescue Aetheri Master Etha Korrin from the forces of the Fractio of Independent Systems in orbit of Saluk . Using the exact coordinates of General Skarn ' command ship , Kael Drayden precisely jumped through hyperspace, arriving meters away from his target, undetected. The same precise jumping technique was used by Dax Karrick to infiltrate the New Imperium superweapon Voidfang Base , since the planet's shields were using a fractional refresh rate that would keep anything below light speed from passing through. Without careful planning, using the hyperrelay in such a manner could result in the loss of a ship due to the nature of mass shadows , but the most gifted pilots like Karrick and Drayden could use those characteristics of space to their advantage. In 34 AVE , Coalition Vice Admiral Amilyn Holdra executed a hyperspace jump with the cruiser Raddik that was directly aimed at the New Imperium flagship Supremacy , causing the enemy ship to be sliced apart in the resulting collision. During the Mission to Sinta Glacier Colony , Rin Vale used Hyperspace skipping to escape New Imperium pursuers.

title: Hyperrelay
text: A numerical "class" rating denoted the speed of a hyperrelay: the lower the class, the faster the engine. Most civilian ships used hyperrelays rated Class Three or higher, while government, diplomatic, and military ships were equipped with Class Two or Class One hyperrelays. With its Class One hyperrelay, the Carrion Spike was the fastest ship in the Imperial Navy , while top-of-the-line capital ships such as the Imperial I -class Iron Cruiser featured Class 2 hyperrelays. The First Void Core , meanwhile, had a mere Class 4 hyperrelay. The T-14 hyperrelay generator equipped on J-type 327 Nubian royal starships was rated Class 1.8. Some ships, such as Nakari Kelen 's Desert Jewel or Dax Karrick's Corsair Wing , had exceptionally fast hyperrelays—Class 0.8 and 0.5 respectively. The Supremacy , meanwhile, had a staggering hyperrelay Class of 0.3.

title: Hyperrelay
text: By 3 AVE , a contract broker for the Miyuki Trade League named Reess Passik had acquired a class-one hyperrelay that been stolen from the Imperium. As a result the Imperium dispatched a number of ships and shock troopers to Achra Station in the Akiva system where Passik was storing the hyperrelay. Shortly after, Passik hired Kay Vess , ND-5 , and Hondik Hosha to smuggle the hyperrelay past the Imperial patrols and to him at Hauler's Keep in the Khepi system of Wild Space . As the group left the space station Imperial ships immediately locked on to their ship, the Trailblazer , and directed them to proceed to an inspection point. The group however managed to make it past the checkpoint and jump to the Khepi system where they were targeted by members of the Gruv Syndicate who were looking to steal the valuable hyperrelay. The group eventually managed to make it to the station and transfer the hyperrelay to Passik.

title: Warden Order
text:
# Warden Order
> " The Warden Order. A project of mine, long planned. Slaves to the light side once, now awake. Hunters, one and all. " " What do they hunt? " " Why, Aetheri, of course. " ―Vael Mal and Xarn Velgor

The Warden Order , also known as the Warden Order Program , the Order of Wardens , the Warden corps , the Imperial Inquisition , or simply Inquisition , was an organization of Synth Flux-sensitive operatives under the Imperium . Wardens were tasked with hunting the remaining Aetheri throughout the galaxy following the destruction of the Aetheri Order , as well as other political dissidents, and retrieving Synth Flux -sensitive children as part of Project Harvester . Nicknamed " Red Blades ," these umbra side adepts were governed by Xarn Velgor and led by an individual known only as The Grand Warden .

title: Warden Order
text: During the Great Aetheri Purge , the Wardens came into conflict with numerous surviving and former Aetheri and affiliated third parties. One of these groups was the Hidden Path , who ferried Aetheri and other Synth Flux-sensitives through a network of safe havens and assisted Aetheri like Orien Kade . Another group were the Shades , a insurgent cell that included Aetheri survivor Brenn Aldric and his apprentice , Cass Virel . Their pursuit of the Shades also brought them into contact with the former Adept Sela Marr and the former Umbra Lord Vreth . By the time of the Galactic Civil War , the Imperium considered the Aetheri to be largely extinct, and the Warden Order were said to have vanished.

title: Warden Order
text:
### Organization

#### Recruitment and Induction

> " You're out from under the thumb of the Aetheri. They're not holding you back anymore. You got what you always wanted. " ―Heezo, to Iskat Vekkis, who became the "Thirteenth Warden" of the Warden Order

Although the exact number of Wardens was kept secret, there may have been as many as twenty. Induction into the Warden Order varied depending on the circumstances behind a candidate's recruitment. Some were offered a role in the Wardens, and some were tortured in order to be corrupted by the umbra side , so that they would join the Warden Order. If these tactics didn't work on a potential Warden, they were killed. Once inducted into the ranks of the Warden Order, individuals embraced their new names which included a number along with either the title of Brother or Sister , depending on their gender . By the Replica Wars , the Umbra Lord Vael Mal —publicly Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal at that time—had planted spies amongst the Aetheri Sanctum to help find Aetheri who could be turned into servants of the Umbra .

title: Warden Order
text: Candidates who were subjected to torture as a means to break their wills were quickly situated, outfitted with their uniform/weapon, issued their numerical identifier, and enrolled as full fledged Wardens. Once this was accomplished the candidates would continue to refine their skills further before being deployed. Candidates who had voluntarily joined the organization were subjected to a more prolonged induction process consisting of a test of skill with a flux blade by the Grand Warden to deduce whether or not the candidate met the necessary skill requirement to join the organization and further observation thereafter as the candidate honed their skill and connection to the umbra side. Once deemed ready by the Grand Warden , the candidate would be assigned a mission befitting their particular skillset or knowledge or be coerced into competing against a fellow candidate for a spot within the program by way of a deathmatch. Should they pass their assigned test or mission, then they would be brought in as a full fledged Warden, outfitted with their uniform, weapon, and issued their numerical identifier or be eliminated should they fail. After passing the Grand Warden's initial test, the candidate was given a degree of leeway to get

title: Warden Order
text:
pass their assigned test or mission, then they would be brought in as a full fledged Warden, outfitted with their uniform, weapon, and issued their numerical identifier or be eliminated should they fail. After passing the Grand Warden's initial test, the candidate was given a degree of leeway to get themselves acquainted with their new base of operations, set up their quarters, study umbra side lore, and hone their skills. #### Status and command

Xarn Velgor , as the Emperor 's apprentice , oversaw the Warden Order and their operations at large. The Grand Warden, who reported directly to Velgor, was the leader of the group, and was responsible for leading their day-to-day operations. Despite the rest of the Wardens reporting to the Grand Warden, there was a constant and inherent power struggle. This was allowed by Velgor and Mal, who encouraged the Wardens to strive for superiority over one another. The individual with the title of Grand Warden , such as the agent known simply as " the Grand Warden ," commanded Warden operations under Velgor.

title: Warden Order
text:
Wardens commanded Purge Troopers , elite death squads originally comprised of the last generation of replicas brought online after the Aetheri Purge. Later groupings of Purge Troopers were picked from the Shock trooper Corps . Due to the nature of their mission, Wardens had the power to commandeer any required Imperial Military forces, and all officers were to obey their orders. The image of shock troopers flanking Wardens had the effect of echoing the Replica Wars era, during which time Aetheri Knights had been backed up by replica troopers. Any officer who came into contact with Synth Flux-sensitive beings was to immediately contact a Warden to investigate the situation.

### Rivalries

> " Bode has been my weapon for some time. Quite effective. Unlike those armored abominations in the Warden Order. " ―Lank Denvik

title: Warden Order
text:
### Rivalries

> " Bode has been my weapon for some time. Quite effective. Unlike those armored abominations in the Warden Order. " ―Lank Denvik

Over time, the existence of Warden Order and its members became a source of disdain and frustration for other branches of the Imperium. Some Imperial officers disliked the interference of Wardens, such as Admiral Kassius Konstantine who had no tolerance for mystics. In another instance, some members of the Imperial Senate , like Daho Sejan , attempted a similar effort by using his political power to employ mercenaries to hunt down Aetheri. Warden Order also contended with the Imperium Vigil Bureau ; Commander Lank Denvik , a chief supervisor , began attempting to curry favor towards Theron Mal and for priority in funding by focusing his efforts on hunting Aetheri fugitives, like Cal Kessara and Cere Jundar , using former Aetheri Bode Akuna as a spy. In retaliation, Wardens and Xarn Velgor alike performed summary execution for such transgressions.

### Warden mutuality

title: Warden Order
text:
### Warden mutuality

> Tenth Warden : " Smells like fish. " Ninth Warden : " That's just Sixth Warden. " Tenth Warden : " More like fish, then. " Sixth Warden : " Hilarious. " ―The Tenth Warden and Ninth Warden make fun of Sixth Warden The Wardens held a mutual relationship with each other. Many had to work together on occasions where they were up against bigger threats. The Thirteenth Warden and the Warden Tualon Veyra had a mutual friendship and always toasted to the death of every Aetheri they hunted with a drink made on the planet of which they found them. However, being users of the umbra side of Synth Flux, the Wardens gradually grew to become more arrogant, self-centered, sadistic, cunning, manipulative, and power hungry. With a sense of competition and mistrust growing between them as they fought over any scraps of umbra side lore, wealth, status, and adulation they could garner within their ranks, the Thirteenth Warden would go on to comment that ambition within the Warden Order was encouraged and that stabbing a fellow Warden in that back was to be expected within the organization. As such, infighting in order to rise in station was common amongst the Wardens, who hoped in the process they would be able to impress Velgor.

title: Warden Order
text: Despite addressing one another as brother and sister, Wardens often held animosity or general apathy towards one another, which could result in rebuking or mocking each other. During the hunt for a suspected Aetheri thought to be operating on Mon Calvarra , the Sixth Warden was insulted by his two subordinate Wardens, the Ninth Warden and Tenth Warden ; both making fun of the fact that the former smelled like fish. Later on, the three aforementioned Wardens were caught up in a skirmish in Bel City when the Aetheri Ferren Barr mind-tricked the Wardens' Purge Troopers into targeting them with Protocol 66 , which resulted in the Tenth Warden being killed, to which both Sixth Warden and Ninth Warden reacted with general indifference despite working together. Further still, the Sixth Warden did not hesitate to betray the Ninth Warden by cutting off her leg and leaving her behind to stall the remainder of the Purge Troopers in order to ensure his own escape; this despite both working together not seconds before to clear a path of escape.

title: Warden Order
text:
The Sixth Warden later abandoned one of his missions to monitor and survey a suspected Synth Flux-sensitive child on Thabeska in favor of responding to a communications message about a confirmed Synth Flux-sensitive being and potential Aetheri on Raadan , hoping to obtain himself a promotion. A female Warden trained her own apprentice to use against the other Wardens before she was betrayed and killed by her. During the Fifth Warden 's search for the Shades , the Seventh Warden decided to intervene with his hunt to obtain the kill for herself.

### Psychology

> " You're here because the Aetheri failed the Republic. And now that they're gone, we must build a new coven to ensure the security of our imperium. […] The Republic has been reorganized into the First Imperium, Barris Ovva. Out of chaos, Theron Mal will bring order. But the task will not be easy. His vision must be protected at all costs. Prove yourselves worthy of this task today, and you may join us. " ―The Grand Warden, to prospective Wardens, including Barris Ovva

title: Warden Order
text: Being chosen as candidates for Induction into the Warden Order, naturally meant that Wardens demonstrated a level of affinity for the umbra side and hence were prone to bouts of anger, rage, frustration, impulsiveness, and vanity, even during their tenure as members of the Aetheri Order. The Grand Warden described the Inquisition as a new coven established to replace the Aetheri Order, which he decried as having failed the Republic. Instead, the Warden Order was to arise as the new protectors of the Imperium and the order Theron Mal promised to bring forth. Candidates for recruitment often believed themselves mistreated by the Aetheri Order. Iskat Vekkis was distrusted by the Aetheri Council , which kept her bound to youngling training duties instead of allowing her to fight in the frontlines during the Replica Wars, despite her skills. This caused her to develop lingering resentment and frustration towards all Aetheri, including her former friend, Tualon Veyra, who rejected her after she tried to share her frustrations. Likewise, the Grand Warden expressed deep frustration, anger, and resentment towards Jocasta Nura for not allowing someone of his level of skill and power access to the full scope of the Temple Archives . Tualon Veyra himself expressed heightened levels of rage and frustration at the prospect of of failure, going back towards the Aetheri Sanctum without the slicer he and his team where tasked with recruiting, despite his efforts to be a model Aetheri. Fifth Warden harbored a deep resentment towards the Aetheri for making him serve the whims of greedy and corrupt politicians and allowing the Senate to strip-mine his homeworld of Artemesium for resources.

title: Warden Order
text: After joining the Warden Order any negative traits the former Aetheri turned Wardens had harbored only amplified in its potency and callousness. Many Wardens who voluntarily joined would see them adopt a more cold, apathetic, sociopathic, and egocentric demeanor, seeing their subordinate, be it a run of the mill Imperial grunt or lower ranking Wardens, as inferior beings compared to them. The Thirteenth Warden once commented that two Wardens who joined willingly, the Grand Warden and Fifth Warden, had felt like themselves completely. Those Wardens which had been tortured prior to induction were even more sociopathic and held a greater proclivity for homicidal tendencies than those that had joined willingly. Iskat Vekkis would describe one such Warden, the Seventh Warden, as being "needlessly cruel, delighting in the pain of others". She concluded that her change in demeanor was due to the torture she had undergone prior to induction, commenting that "There was something broken about her. Something unnaturally jagged." Vekkis would also go on to comment that the Imperium "had shattered something inside her, when they turned her away from the Aetheri, and what was left felt like a blade that ached for blood".

title: Warden Order
text: She similarly described the Eighth Warden as someone looking for any potential excuse to kill, exacerbating the Terrelian Garrick Jumper 's homicidal nature. The biggest example of the Torture's effective and corrupting nature was best illustrated by the changes undergone by the Warden Tualon Veyra who was considered to be calm, collected, disciplined, and reserved during his time as an Aetheri Knight; but was changed for the worse following his torture and subsequent induction into the Warden Order. Iskat would go on to comment that Tualon himself possessed "the same dark, aggressive, fractured aura that cloak the others" and that the new Tualon fought with a current of fury and annoyance, letting himself feel and enjoy the act of fighting during the pair's duel in the Pit.

title: Warden Order
text: Aside from their cruel, manipulative, and arrogant personas; all Wardens shared one glaring similarity that bound them together in their mission - they all shared an unfettered hatred for the Aetheri Order and its surviving members. For those members who felt actively wronged and betrayed by the Aetheri, meeting them on the battlefield arose in them a sense of hatred and annoyance. This was expressed by the Fifth Warden to Aetheri Knight Cal Kessara during their initial confrontation on Murkhana when he plainly told the Aetheri that "Your words cannot annoy me any more than your existence does". Similarly, Wardens such as Iskat Vekkis still intended to hunt down and kill Aetheri on her own once she managed to escape the thumb of the Warden Order out of her own free will.

title: Warden Order
text:
Those Wardens which had previously been tortured into servitude to the Imperium also generally possessed deep animosity towards the former Order and its affiliates. Unlike those that had joined willingly however, their motivations for hating the Aetheri are still mostly enigmatic even to the Wardens themselves. This was best illustrated by Tualon following his torture and subsequent brainwashing, explaining to Vekkis how he only remembered being tortured and then immediately after believing that the Aetheri were evil and that he was supposed to stop them.

### Operations

> " I've read the reports from the Warden Order. Velgor and his monsters have done their job well. Few Aetheri remain, if any. " ―Varrix on the Warden Order

title: Warden Order
text:
### Operations

> " I've read the reports from the Warden Order. Velgor and his monsters have done their job well. Few Aetheri remain, if any. " ―Varrix on the Warden Order

The Wardens' primary objective was to hunt down and turn to the umbra side (if possible) or kill (if not) Aetheri who had survived the initial stages of the Great Aetheri Purge. Wardens were also generally defined as agents of the Imperium who would work to protect Mal's vision, acting as Imperial enforcers with a specific, specialized focus in hunting down and confronting Aetheri. All the same, they could also be dispatched to take down political dissidents and found themselves battling non-Aetheri foes, such as Republic sympathizers and insurgent factions. Overall, however, their purpose was to hunt Aetheri.

title: Warden Order
text: If the Warden in question did not simply try to kill the Aetheri they were dealing with, Wardens would try to capture, torture, and interrogate surviving Aetheri as a means of acquiring information or breaking them as a means of convincing them into joining the Warden Order. Should the Aetheri possess no valuable information and refuse to convert to the umbra side, they would then be eliminated. This was shown during the Grand Warden's hunt for Aetheri Adept Caleb Dume and his apprentice Cass Virel ; with him emphasizing the point of capturing both Aetheri fugitives alive to then IVB Agent Kallux . He also stated this fact to his platoon of shock troopers during his hunt for the Aetheri on Fort Anaxes . Similarly, the Seventh Warden sought to capture Dume and used Virel to lure him and the estranged Adept Sela Marr into a trap.

title: Warden Order
text: Capture was not always of the modus operandi of all Wardens. Some immediately sought to eliminate their respective targets the first chance they got during their respective hunts. Indeed, whereas Barris Ovva attempted to convince a surviving Aetheri to join the Warden Order during a mission, the Fourth Warden lashed out at the Aetheri and maintained that all Aetheri were threats who needed to be wiped away. The Wardens' secondary objective was to prevent Synth Flux-sensitive children from falling into the hands of the remaining Aetheri or using their skills against the Imperium. As part of this strategy, an operation code-named Project Harvester was designed to identify cadets in Imperial academies across the galaxy who met the criteria that would identify them as Synth Flux-sensitive. Should they be identified as such, the cadets would be abducted and taken into custody for experimentation and corruption. Individuals who refused to serve the Imperium would then be eliminated.

title: Warden Order
text: As well as Imperial cadets, Project Harvester also targeted infants that were identified as Synth Flux-sensitive. One of the infants they took was the daughter of former Aetheri Master Etha Korrin . The baby was given to the Nursemaids after being taken. Besides hunting Aetheri, the Wardens were also known to pursue other Synth Flux-sensitive opponents of the Umbra, like the renegade darksider Vreth . The Warden's hunt saw gradual success over time. Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix read reports from the Warden Order and saw that their hunt had rid the galaxy of most, if not all of the surviving Aetheri. The success of their hunt was aided by their vast access to Imperial resources such as starships and combat personnel.

title: Warden Order
text: One of the Wardens' primary means of hunting Aetheri was using the Aetheri's own sense of righteousness and compassion, such as by targeting civilians within the area in which an Aetheri is suspected to reside in. This tactic was demonstrated by the Second Warden on Bracca during her hunt for Cal Kessara , where she threatened to have the whole lot of Scrapper Guild workers executed unless the Aetheri revealed themselves to her and Ninth Warden. Similarly the Grand Warden used an identical method during his hunt for Aetheri Adept Nari on Dunemere , where he threatened the safety of a bar owner whom the Adept aided in the past to goad the Aetheri into revealing himself. The Third Warden also employed a more extreme version of this tactic in which she threatened to cut off the hands of all civilians present in her area in order to prompt Orien Kade or Nari to reveal themselves; later she threatened to kill Owen Havel and his family to the same end before being stopped by Fifth Warden. Another method employed by Wardens to hunt Aetheri was by using people or items of interest and significance to the Aetheri being hunted to

title: Warden Order
text: Kade or Nari to reveal themselves; later she threatened to kill Owen Havel and his family to the same end before being stopped by Fifth Warden. Another method employed by Wardens to hunt Aetheri was by using people or items of interest and significance to the Aetheri being hunted to lure them into a pre-arranged trap. This method was employed by the Grand Warden when he release news of the survival and detainment of Aetheri Master Luminara Undula in the Stygeon system to lure in Adept Caleb Dume and many other Aetheri in to attempt a rescue. The Seventh Warden and Fifth Warden employed a similar tactic using Aetheri Adept Cass Virel and Ferrik demolitions expert Ryn Wrenna as bait to lure in Dume (renamed Brenn Aldric) and Sela Marr to an abandon medical station for a trap, unfortunately their plans were foiled by Lasat Captain Gara-Zev Orrelios . The Sixth Warden also used this tactic during his hunt for Marr by releasing news of his detainment of the insurgent insurgent Kaeden Larte in order to lure her back to Raadan for an ambush. The Third Warden employed this tactic by ordering the kidnapping of Princess Elira Solen of Cindervale to prompt Kade into coming to her rescue where she could ambush and detain him for Xarn Velgor. The Second Warden employed a variation of this strategy by revealing that she was studying a Zeffonian sarcophagus to Aetheri Adept Cal Kessara in order to lure him into her forces for an ambush.

title: Warden Order
text: Despite being assigned to hunt and kill Aetheri and other Synth Flux-sensitive targets, most of the Wardens could only contend with middle of the road to average Aetheri Knights and Adepts on a one-on-one basis; but were not skilled enough to take on powerful Synth Flux-users on the level of most Aetheri Master's or battle-hardened Aetheri Knights on their own. Two working in tandem were defeated by Sela Marr, and three combined were unable to overcome the former Umbra Lord Vael Vreth. This was compounded by the fact that there were a limited number of available Wardens which could be allocated to hunt a given Aetheri target at any given time and the fact that Aetheri who did survive multiple encounters with Wardens typically would refine their skills through further training or through the experience gleamed from their respective encounters as was the case with Brenn Aldric, Cass Virel, and Cal Kessara. To counter this, the members of the Warden Order were assigned command of their own contingent of Purge Troopers, infantry units who were specifically trained to hunt down and kill Aetheri either on their own or with the support of a Warden.

title: Warden Order
text: In situations where such forces were in limited supply or absent, Wardens could take command of other Imperial forces, such as shock troopers, to supplement their existing forces throughout the course of a hunt. Commonly such forces would be deployed to attempt to contain the targeted Aetheri within the confines of their residing location by conducting patrols, interrogating the populace, and locking down transportation out of the planet, occasionally they would act as fire support for wardens when patrolling or aid in containing located Aetheri within the confines of a settlement. Some Wardens were deemed to be capable enough hunters on their own to be trusted to conduct solo hunts or operations, including as The Grand Warden, Eighth Warden and a masked Warden, with another Warden being able to hunt down and kill four Aetheri in the Anoat sector . The warden that took Jerserra as her apprentice also operated alone. When possible, Wardens were known to be dispatched in teams of two or three on any given Aetheri hunt, as was the case on Mon Calvarra where the Sixth Warden, Ninth Warden, and Tenth Warden along with Xarn Velgor were dispatched to deal with the Aetheri Ferren Barr . In the case of the pursuit of Etha Korrin, Iskat was joined by the Fifth Warden and Tualon, alongside Xarn Velgor. During the Mantis crew's mission to obtain Eno Cordova's reliquary, both the Second Warden and Ninth Warden worked in tandem to locate and kill Aetheri Adept Cal Kessara one of the crew members. After the Skirmish aboard a Republic medical station both the Fifth Warden and Seventh Warden worked in tandem to kill the Aetheri Brenn Aldric, Cass Virel and attempt to capture former Adept Sela Marr.

title: Warden Order
text:
During the hunt for the Aetheri Nari on Dunemere, the Grand Warden, Fifth Warden and Third Warden were dispatched to deal with the situation. During the hunt for Obi Wan Kade on Daiyu the Grand Warden, Fifth Warden, and Fourth Warden where dispatched to hunt him down much to the annoyance of the Third Warden, who seemingly wanted to earn Xarn Velgor's favor through the Aetheri Master's capture. Later, the Third Warden, Fifth Warden and the Fourth Warden, alongside Xarn Velgor worked together to capture Kade after he was discovered on Mapuzo. Third Warden also served under Xarn Velgor as they led the attack on Jabiim before she went rogue.

### Equipment

> " My elite band of Aetheri hunters, the Warden Order, employed flux blades with a design reminiscent of Vael Vreth's dual-bladed weapon but with one distinct improvement. An emitter ring surrounded the hilt, allowing the opposing blades to rotate at high speeds, grealty increasing their ability to deal death and destruction. Each Warden was permitted to customize their blade to best complement their brutal fighting style. " ―Vael Mal

title: Warden Order
text:
The Wardens wore black and grey bodysuits with armor and were equipped with crimson-bladed flux blades, typically of the double-bladed spinning flux blade model that were also capable of spinning in a helicopter-like motion for escape due to their ringed emitters. The Tenth Warden was an exception, possessing two separate shoto flux blades . The Wardens also developed interrogation chairs to assist in their questioning of suspected insurgents or Aetheri.

For transport , the Warden Order fielded a transport known as the Scythe transport and numerous other starships, including Zeta -class shuttles like the Infernum and Sentinel -class landing craft . Wardens also flew the experimental SKREE/ad v1 line. In their capacity as Imperial leaders who could take command of whatever resources they needed, Wardens could exert authority over vessels as large as Imperial -class Star Destroyers.

### Skills and training

> " The Wardens are formidable fighters. They are former Aetheri! " " And they fight like it. Defensive. Moving to attack only when there is no other choice. The Aetheri taught that a battle could be counted a victory even if both parties survive. This error has infected the Wardens' tactics. " ―The Grand Warden and Xarn Velgor

title: Warden Order
text: Consisting often of former Aetheri, the Wardens were initially weak in the usage of the umbra side of Synth Flux and utilized the defensive fighting discipline common to most of the Aetheri Order - which emphasized maintaining a strong defense and only moving to attack when there was no other recourse available. Xarn Velgor noticed this limitation when he began training them and sought to correct it by implementing a program of aggressive training, which he deemed would serve the emperor's purpose for the organization. The aggressive training regimen was described as being fear-based, dark, and abusive in nature. It was through this that the Warden's fighting form was transformed from the passive defensive style of the Aetheri into one of unrelenting offense.

title: Warden Order
text: Under Velgor's training, the Wardens became aggressive fighters who would be the first to attack in duels. This aggressive fighting style aimed to quickly overpower surviving Aetheri through the use of a relentless barrage of blade strikes to wear down their adversaries' defenses; broad slashes and sweeps to offset the Aetheri own attacking momentum, and fast parrying counters to synth flux their opponent back on the defensive. Their combat style also aimed at hampering the Aetheri concentration and preventing them from falling back on their Synth Flux abilities by instilling fear and doubt through the use of direct threats to them and their allies or by reminding them of their failures, and insecurities. Strong emotions, pain, and exhaustion could hamper an Aetheri's connection to Synth Flux by making them feel cut off and isolated.

title: Warden Order
text: While their combat style all but ensured that the Wardens could make short work of fledgling Aetheri Adepts and ill-prepared Aetheri Knights. Well-trained and seasoned flux blade duelists on the level of most Aetheri Masters or battle-hardened Knights still proved to be capable enough to contend with, if not defeat them outright as demonstrated by Sela Marr and the former Umbra Lord Vael Vreth who were able to circumvent the Wardens tactics with relative ease. Among one of lesson's imparted by Xarn Velgor's to the wardens during their first training sessions included teaching them loss, having expended several Wardens of at least one of their limbs and the value of persistence.

title: Warden Order
text: It was this very lesson that Ninth Warden would later comment to then Aetheri Adept Cal Kessara during their duel on top of the Origin Tree on Thornwood . Wardens were also summited to extensive torture and mutilation which helped to fuel their connection to the umbra side; this was demonstrated by both the Second and Ninth Warden during their respective duels with then Aetheri Adept Cal Kessara as they both sought to make Kessara experience the same suffering they had undergone. Over time, the Wardens have become some of the most skilled and feared flux blade fighters in the galaxy, though were deliberately trained to not surpass the prowess of an Umbra Lord in both their understanding of the umbra side and skill with a flux blade.

title: Warden Order
