text: Aside from their skills with a flux blade, Wardens were trained in the use and application of umbra side techniques such as mind probing or Synth Flux drain as was the case with the Second Warden, It also appears that some Wardens, such as the Seventh Warden are capable of using Synth Flux directly to inflict pain upon a target as she demonstrated against Cass Virel during her interrogation of the young Adept. They were also well-trained interrogators and trackers, who were capable of using Synth Flux to detect another Synth Flux-sensitive's signature through vast distances or gather important information by reading the emotional responses of their adversaries when presented with an inquiry.

title: Warden Order
text: Individually, Wardens ranged in skill sets and strengths, many of them having studied the records of the Aetheri Order to familiarize themselves with their enemies' fighting techniques . Some wardens like the Fifth Warden and Ninth Warden were strong in Synth Flux, able to sense emotions, intentions, or the locations of their prey across the vast expanse of space. Wardens like the Seventh Warden and Second Warden had keen tactical minds that enabled them to coordinate and allocates their forces with greater efficiency while others such as Sixth Warden had keen deductive skills which enabled him to better predict the movement of their prey.

title: Warden Order
text:
### Origins

#### Long-awaited plans

> " I foresee an army of Synth Flux-talented spies in my service, trained in the umbra side to peer into every corner of the galaxy from afar. And my enemies would be helpless against such vision. " ―Vael Mal Dark Lord of the Umbra Vael Mal knew there would be some Aetheri who could survive his planned Great Aetheri Purge through Directive 66 . He needed to ensure that he could not be usurped by the light side, so Mal began to lay the seeds of the Warden Order Program years before he became Galactic Emperor . During the Replica Wars , he contracted the bounty hunter Cad Vorek to kidnap several Synth Flux-sensitive children who would become Aetheri younglings in the near future. At his private facility on Emberfall , the Dark Lord intended to put the children through a slave conditioning process, having foreseen he would have "an army " of Synth Flux-sensitive spies at his beck and call. Nevertheless, Vael Mal' operation was prevented by the interference of Aetheri Knight Kael Drayden and Adept Sela Marr , who rescued the children and escaped the ruined crashing base with them. Despite this setback, the Dark Lord simply established more facilities and altered more nanny droids , ensuring the continuation of his plan to use Emberfall to turn infants to his cause.

title: Warden Order
text: As the war carried on, Vael Mal also kept an eye on Knights who had grievances with the Aetheri High Council or the role the Aetheri Order was playing in the conflict, with his spies amongst the Temple, such as Heezo , helping him find such candidates. The Umbra Lord preyed on their weaknesses and secretly offered these select few the things their brethren had denied them in addition to a chance at surviving Directive 66, so long as they gave him and the umbra side of Synth Flux their allegiance. When the war ended , Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal, the public persona Vael Mal, seized the carefully-orchestrated opportunity to form the Imperium and declare the Aetheri Order its enemy. Using Aetheri Master Drevan Koss 's attempt on his life as justification, Mal gave the command to execute Directive 66. However, Aetheri who, in the words of the soon-to-be Grand Warden, had seen through "the lies" of the Order were spared.

title: Warden Order
text: For example, the soon-to-be Thirteenth Warden, Iskat Vekkis, was not killed on sight upon the execution of Directive 66 as Mal had noticed her grievances with the Aetheri Order. Rather than fire on her, the replica trooper company with her surrounded her, and Mal, via the holocommuniator used by Replica Captain Spider , offered her a chance to learn everything she had suppressed. After she agreed and was escorted away, Vekkis' betrayal sent her fellow Aetheri and friend Tualon Veyra into a rage, in which he fought his replica troopers. Despite their initial attempts to kill him, the replicas took him captive. He would also join the Warden Order after torture and being consumed by his rage. As the Dark Lord predicted, some Aetheri survived the mass–killing, so he planned for his huntsmen to hound those who survived until the light of the Aetheri Order was extinguished once and for all. Vael Mal also turned Drayden to the umbra side to be his apprentice , giving him the name "Xarn Velgor." Whereas Drayden had the potential to be an Umbra in his eyes, Mal had selected those who would become Wardens specifically because he felt they had no chance of

title: Warden Order
text:
all. Vael Mal also turned Drayden to the umbra side to be his apprentice , giving him the name "Xarn Velgor." Whereas Drayden had the potential to be an Umbra in his eyes, Mal had selected those who would become Wardens specifically because he felt they had no chance of becoming powerful enough to challenge him. #### The new order

The vast majority of the Aetheri were killed by the replicas but several managed to escape, especially after Aetheri Master Orien Kade sent out a distress signal from the Temple , warning the survivors off. As such, several of them had survived the initial purge and gone into hiding. Fearing the threat the surviving Aetheri posed to his rule , the recently-instated Emperor Vael Mal created the Imperial Inquisition to track down and taint or eradicate the last of the Aetheri Order. In a similar vein to how Drayden had fallen, the first grouping of Wardens were all former Aetheri who had fallen to the umbra side and sworn themselves to Mal. As the Imperial Era continued, Aetheri Master Orien Kade thought that not all Wardens were former Aetheri, but he knew many were.

title: Warden Order
text: Many Imperial Wardens had joined the umbra side due to intensive torture or corruption. Upon joining the ranks of the Warden Order, Synth Flux-sensitives effectively lost their identities; they were given numerical designations to represent their entry into an organization that perverted everything the Aetheri Order had had stood for in a very different way from how General Skarn had. A Pau'an Aetheri Sanctum Guard , who became " the Grand Warden ," had joined Mal when the Dark Lord had promised him access to the Aetheri Archives . The Ninth Warden was the former Aetheri Knight Masana Tide . The Tenth Warden was former Aetheri Master Prosset Dibs , who had become suborned to the Umbra at the end of the Replica Wars.

title: Warden Order
text: The Second Warden was former Aetheri Adept Trilla Suduri , who was captured shortly after Directive 66 and tortured into giving into the umbra side. Xarn Velgor soon discovered the program and was put in charge of them by Vael Mal. The Umbra Lord trained the Wardens in the ways of the umbra side of Synth Flux . As part of their tutelage, a number of Wardens had parts of their bodies severed by their master's flux blade so that they would not forget the lesson of loss. After Lord Velgor cut off Sixth Warden 's left arm, the Grand Warden began questioning his master's training techniques. The cyborg claimed he was intending to have the umbra side adepts to abandon their tendency to fight defensively as former Aetheri and adopt more offensive moves. Meanwhile, the Sixth Warden stumbled to the Warden Order medbay, where he met Iskat Vekkis.

title: Warden Order
text:
Later, the Fourth Warden recruited Barris Ovva to join the Warden Order and brought her to the under-construction Fortress Warden Order on the water moon Nur . There, Ovva was trained by the Grand Warden and became a Warden after defeating fellow prospective Warden Dante in combat. However, Barris did not remain Warden for long, as after being sent to eliminate an Aetheri along with the Fourth Warden by the Grand Warden, Barris betrayed the Warden by using Synth Flux to push her off a mountain. Having realized the true nature of the Warden Order, Barris returned to being an Aetheri and returned to save the Aetheri who were injured and left for dead by the Fourth Warden. Barris's betrayal made her a target of the Warden Order, but the lack of progress in locating her nearly resulted in the abandonment of the search.

### Hunting the Aetheri

> " The Imperium sent out powerful Synth Flux-users, umbra side adepts, to hunt down any Aetheri survivors. They were called the Warden Order. " ―Verla, to Joren Drayden

title: Warden Order
text:
### Hunting the Aetheri

> " The Imperium sent out powerful Synth Flux-users, umbra side adepts, to hunt down any Aetheri survivors. They were called the Warden Order. " ―Verla, to Joren Drayden

Following the formation of the Imperium in 19 BVE , the Grand Warden worked closely with Lord Velgor on locating the Aetheri Order's Chief Librarian , Jocasta Nura . During his research in the Archives, the formed, who held a personal dislike of said Aetheri Master because she had been the one to refuse him access to the Archives' secrets, was confronted by Nura after he openly insulted the knowledge he was reading. At first the Grand Warden planned to kill her but when he defeated her in combat, he was prevented from killing her by his master. As Velgor and the Warden argued, Nura was able to make her escape. However, the Umbra Lord was able to pursue the Aetheri Master and killed her himself without the Grand Warden's help.

Throughout the Imperial Era, the Wardens brought terror to the Aetheri who had survived Directive 66 and helped cement Imperial rule.

title: Warden Order
text:
Throughout the Imperial Era, the Wardens brought terror to the Aetheri who had survived Directive 66 and helped cement Imperial rule.

Sometime after the Nura affair, the Ninth Warden accompanied Lord Velgor to investigate reports of a possible Aetheri in a cantina on Cabarria . The reports turned out to be false and the Umbra Lord was attacked by three bounty hunters. The Dowutin Warden refused to help Velgor and when he overpowered his would-be assassins , they retreated and stole the Ninth Warden's speeder at gunpoint. Velgor chased and captured them, questioning them of who they were hired by. The Dark Lord found out that the culprit had come from the top of the Imperial ranks and the Ninth Warden flew him back to Vantor. However, when arriving at Vantor their communications were deliberately jammed, stopping the Warden from sending their clearance codes. This caused the Vantor defenses to attack them and the Dark Lord pushed the Ninth Warden off the pilot chair to take control of the ship. They subsequently crashed onto Vantor and Velgor left the Ninth Warden with the ship.

### Mission to Mon Calvarra

title: Warden Order
text:
### Mission to Mon Calvarra

> " As the Wardens were once Aetheri themselves, and the replicas were built to kill Aetheri, well…you see the result. " ―Ferren Barr, on the Wardens and their Purge Troopers

About one year after the rise of the Imperium, Mal suspected an Aetheri of influencing the deteriorating negotiations on Mon Calvarra . The Emperor therefore sent his apprentice and three Wardens to investigate this, accompanied by a death squad of elite replica Purge Troopers . Upon their arrival, Ambassador Telvar was assassinated and his superior, Governor Varrix, sent down his forces to invade Mon Calvarra. Lord Velgor and the Wardens Sixth Warden, Ninth Warden and Tenth Warden fought at Dac City and captured the king , Liarch . The Ninth Warden interrogated the monarch for the location of the Aetheri but they were soon swept away by large waves generated by some of Mon Calvarra's large creatures .

title: Warden Order
text: The three Wardens survived the cataclysm and picked up Velgor on an Imperial submarine . The Ninth Warden revealed to the Dark Lord that she had obtained the location of the Aetheri and they made for the place. Upon arriving there, they were met by the Aetheri and his six disciples . The group scattered, except for one that shot at the submarine until Velgor crushed his helmet. As they chased the rest of them, another sacrificed himself to slow them down. The Wardens and their master soon reached Bel City and made chase for the remaining of the group. However, Lord Velgor received a request from Governor Varrix for an assignment that requited him elsewhere which was the capture of Liarch and thus the end of the war on Mon Calvarra. He agreed and left his Wardens and their squad of replicas to find the Aetheri.

title: Warden Order
text: The Wardens soon found the Aetheri and his last two disciples . The Sixth Warden cut down one of the disciples and they surrounded the other two. The Aetheri then stepped forward and faced them, revealing their names from when they were Aetheri. The Ninth Warden confronted the Aetheri, identifying him as an Adept named Ferren Barr . Barr ignored her and told them that they were still truly Aetheri, acknowledging the replicas and their role in Directive 66. He then used Synth Flux to take the helmets off the Purge Troopers and saw that they were newer replicas that were commissioned after Directive 66. Knowing they had not had their inhibitor chips activated, he used a mind trick on them, saying "execute Directive 66."

title: Warden Order
text:
The trick worked and the Purge Troopers turned on their three superiors. They quickly succeeded in gunning down the Tenth Warden, although the Sixth Warden and Ninth Warden were able to deflect their shots. Barr and his last disciple, Verla , then leaped over the battle and escaped. Keen to intercept them, the Sixth Warden and Ninth Warden used their combined powers to Synth Flux push the troopers to the side. However, the Sixth Warden betrayed Ninth Warden, cutting her leg off and leaving her to fend off the last of the troopers alone. After his escape, the Sixth Warden took a boat away with three shock troopers . Despite the loss of her right leg, Ninth Warden survived and replaced the missing limb with a prosthetic one.

### Search for Sela Marr

#### First encounter

> " I have a sense for power. And you do not have enough to resist me for much longer, weaponless as you are. " ―The Sixth Warden, to Sela Marr

title: Warden Order
text:
### Search for Sela Marr

#### First encounter

> " I have a sense for power. And you do not have enough to resist me for much longer, weaponless as you are. " ―The Sixth Warden, to Sela Marr

Shortly after the mission to Mon Calvarra, the Sixth Warden was searching for a possibly Synth Flux-sensitive child on Thabeska . However, he later abandoned this task after receiving word that a Synth Flux-attuned being who received some level of Aetheri training was hiding in the Outer Reach , and set out to hunt the individual in question, hoping to earn a promotion. The supposed Aetheri was in fact Marr, who was hiding on Thabeska and the agricultural moon of Raadan since Directive 66 and the siege of Ferrum . She built up a coalition group on Raadan . After a failed assault on the nearby Imperial Base, Sela returned to Thabeska. When Hedala Fardi, the Synth Flux-sensitive child, told Sela of "a shadow" that had come, the former Adept went back to Raadan, where The Sixth Warden had killed the entirety of the coalition group, with only Sela's friend Kaeden Larte and her sister alive.

title: Warden Order
text:
The Sixth Warden then took Kaedan, who had become close to Marr. The Sixth Warden used Kaeden to lay a trap for Marr and she revealed herself to him. The Sixth Warden then battled her, but the former Adept was able to identify his offensive fighting style and took advantage of it. Marr then reached out to his flux blade's kyber crystals and they detonated the flux blade, killing the Sixth Warden. Marr took his flux blade crystals and fled the system with the rest of the citizens from Raadan's sole settlement. Shortly afterwards, the Grand Warden arrived and, unaware of the culprit's identity, decided to hunt her himself, but not before informing Lord Velgor.

#### Second encounter

> " And who might you be? " ―The Warden, to Sela Marr — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Warden Order
text:
#### Second encounter

> " And who might you be? " ―The Warden, to Sela Marr — Link ▶️ ( file info )

At another point during the Imperial Era, the Eleventh Warden was tipped off by a villager about Marr's presence in a village , and arrived in the settlement to investigate. Upon not finding his target there, he slaughtered the entire village but the informant who alerted him of Marr's presence, and an old man . Holding the two hostage in the village center as it burned, the Warden circled the two farmers and intimidated them with his doubled-bladed spinning flux blade. When the informant claimed that he should be rewarded for his effort, the Warden accused him of lying and claimed that it would not win him Imperial favor.

title: Warden Order
text:
When Marr returned to the village from a produce delivery alongside the informant's sister , the two found the village in flames and the Warden tormenting the two farmers. Upon spotting Marr, the informant told the Warden that he had been telling the truth. The Warden acknowledged this, and attempted to "reward" the informant by killing him, but Marr used telekinesis to pull the man away from the Warden, and cause his flux blade to miss its target. Intrigued, the Warden recognized Marr and gloated that he would be rewarded for her death. He attempted to kill Marr, but she dodged his blows before grabbing his flux blade and deactivating it. She then wrenched the weapon out of his hands and decapitated him with it.

### Hunt for Grandea

> " Ninth Warden. Thirteenth Warden. Find the Aetheri. Do not fail me." "Yes, Lord Velgor. " ―Xarn Velgor and Thirteenth Warden

title: Warden Order
text:
### Hunt for Grandea

> " Ninth Warden. Thirteenth Warden. Find the Aetheri. Do not fail me." "Yes, Lord Velgor. " ―Xarn Velgor and Thirteenth Warden

The Ninth Warden and Thirteenth Warden accompanied Xarn Velgor to Daiyu to hunt the Aetheri Knight Grandea . The Wardens nearly killed Grandea, severing her right leg and wounding her right shoulder. However, before they could complete their mission, their minds were manipulated by Grandea, who used the mind trick to convince them that they had killed her already. The two informed Velgor Grandea's body had been incinerated in a fire. Though she escaped, Grandea had narrowly escaped death, as using the mind trick against them cost her dearly, causing her nose to bleed.

### Hunt for Etha Korrin

> " Wardens—A woman and an infant escaped. Bring me the child. " " And the woman, Lord Velgor? " " Irrelevant. " ―Xarn Velgor and the Fifth Warden

title: Warden Order
text:
### Hunt for Etha Korrin

> " Wardens—A woman and an infant escaped. Bring me the child. " " And the woman, Lord Velgor? " " Irrelevant. " ―Xarn Velgor and the Fifth Warden

Sometime after his hunt on Chandar's Folly , Lord Velgor took three Wardens to a planet to hunt down former Aetheri Master Etha Korrin . He entered his house and interrupted the latter as his daughter was just born. Korrin attempted to negotiate his way out of the situation but Velgor made it clear he wasn't compliant and Korrin attacked him, telling his wife, Mira , to run with their daughter. The two took the fight outside and the Umbra Lord threw him across the ground and told his Wardens to find the newborn and capture it. The Fifth Warden asked of what they should do about the mother and their master informed him that she was irrelevant.

title: Warden Order
text: The three Wardens made haste into the city and the Fifth Warden suggested they split up. The other two agreed and they began searching in the city. The Thirteenth Warden decided to reach out into Synth Flux to see if the infant made any ripples, as it was Synth Flux-sensitive. Her attempt was successful and she managed to stop Mira and her child before they could reach her father's shuttle . Mira begged her to let her go, appealing to her woman to woman. Iskat told her to go and she ran into the shuttle. The Fifth Warden then arrived and was shocked by what she had just done. Tualon Veyra arrived as well and told her that their master would not take this lightly. However, Iskat wasn't finished yet and as the shuttle ascended, she used Synth Flux to pull the baby from her mother's arms.

title: Warden Order
text:
Tualon asked Iskat why she had to do it the way she did. She explained that since Mira appealed to her woman to woman, she decided to let her trust her before snatching her baby and thus her soul, as she would never trust another woman, and likely another person, again. The three Wardens returned to the Umbra Lord, who was gradually beating his Aetheri opponent in the duel. Korrin saw the baby in Iskat's hands and, using his shock as a distraction, Velgor cut him down. The group returned to the Vantor tower on their Zeta-class shuttle and gave the baby to a pair of nursemaids . The Umbra Lord then asked the Grand Warden about their next target. Velgor was brought by his underling to see the list of the final confirmed Aetheri survivors. There, he explained to Velgor that they had hidden well and he concluded that they must wait until one of them made a mistake in order to find them.

### Renegade Wardens

title: Warden Order
text:
### Renegade Wardens

> " What are we looking for, Lord Velgor? " " Two Aetheri. Male and female. They will attack us. It is only a matter of time. Be wary. They are cunning. Their direction of attack may be…unorthodox. " ―Two Imperial shock troopers , and Xarn Velgor

Velgor did not respond to the Grand Warden's assessment, but he departed and attempted to busy himself, displaying signs of restlessness and frustration. Without any active Aetheri hunts, Velgor realized he would have to look elsewhere for a challenge. Fortunately for him, the Fifth Warden notified the Umbra Lord at some point of the Thirteenth Warden's actions during their hunt. Already having been suspicious of her loyalties, Velgor decided he could use her as his next target and paint her as a traitor, especially as he suspected her and Tualon of having developed feelings for each other. Meanwhile, the Grand Warden had gathered all present Wardens to the common room to synth flux all present to spend time together. Velgor made his way to the gathering so as to confront the Thirteenth Warden.

title: Warden Order
text: There, the Thirteenth Warden and Tualon were toasting to Etha Korrin's death with a drink that came from the planet where they had found him. Thirteenth Warden then brought up the Umbra Lord and asked of what he would do when all the Aetheri were finally dead. Tualon told her he would find his way around it, saying he would always find something to kill. At that moment, Velgor interrupted their conversation, igniting his flux blade. The Grand Warden asked if this was a test, which the Dark Lord coldly denied. Velgor attempted to kill the Thirteenth Warden, but Tualon halted him with his flux blade and Velgor confirmed his suspicions that the two had an attachment. Thirteenth Warden ran away and the Dark Lord threw the other into the wall. He asked Velgor why he attacked the Thirteenth Warden and he told him that it didn't matter because he had done it too. Tualon ran and joined the Thirteenth Warden as she escaped the Vantor Tower.

title: Warden Order
text: The Umbra Lord made chase for the rogue Wardens and took a speeder into Vantor. The pair planned on killing Velgor in order for them to be free from his presence in the galaxy. They therefore attacked his speeder and he jumped to other speeders as they cut those down as well with their flux blades. The pair then resorted to throwing speeders at their pursuer but he either threw them back or cut them down. However, the rogue Wardens eventually managed to topple a statue onto the Umbra Lord and he fell onto a balcony, temporarily immobilized. They attempted to finish him off but Velgor used Synth Flux to freeze them in mid air. The rogue Wardens turned to one another to spill out their last words and the Umbra Lord made their flux blades activate to stab the pair and kill them at the same time . Mal later asked Velgor why he suspected the two of treachery and he explained to his master of their attachment and how the Thirteenth Warden briefly let Etha Korrin's child escape. Nonetheless, the Emperor was displeased with his apprentice's rampage that killed Senator Maklooq , who was important to his master

title: Warden Order
text:
later asked Velgor why he suspected the two of treachery and he explained to his master of their attachment and how the Thirteenth Warden briefly let Etha Korrin's child escape. Nonetheless, the Emperor was displeased with his apprentice's rampage that killed Senator Maklooq , who was important to his master plan and had the Warden Order relocated to Nur but was happy to hear Etha was dead. ### Further events

#### Hunt in the Anoat sector

> " If we do not stop the Warden, you will. If we do not stop the Imperium, you will. " ―Nuhj, in a recording made just prior to his death

An Warden was dispatched by the Imperium to deal with a small group of surviving Aetheri who had recently been discovered in an Aetheri shrine on Anoat . The Imperial operative went there to find the Aetheri Mususiel , who stayed to save the others. The Warden killed her and tracked the others to Mataou , where the agent pursued one of the others, named Zubain Ankonori , and slew him. The last two Aetheri, Nuhj and Khandra , fled to Embertown on the planet Burnin Konn , but the Warden soon followed and attacked them in a chromium mine near Wickridge . The Warden slew them and their belongings were stored in an Imperial vault on Nar Hypa .

#### Training Jerserra and hunting Kaela

title: Warden Order
text:
#### Training Jerserra and hunting Kaela

At one point, a female Warden was on Gloomreach when she encountered Jerserra , a Gloomreachian from the Nardithi Nightsisters , a sect of the Nightsisters . She took in Jerserra as her secret apprentice and spent a number of years training her in combat and flux blade combat. The Warden hoped to use Jerserra against the other Wardens but Jerserra eventually came to believe her abilities outmatched her Master's, and before long, the Warden was slain by Jerserra, who covered up her murder and took her flux blade as her own.

At another point, an Inquistior began to hunt the surviving Aetheri Jarea Kaela and spread the rumor that Kaela was a witch, attracting the attention of the bounty hunter Harlon Gier . Hoping the bounty hunter and Aetheri would kill each other, the Warden's plan instead resulted in Gier and Kaela allying together. When the Warden revealed himself with a grouping of shock troopers, he began a battle with the Aetheri and bounty hunter.

#### Hunting Lyco Strata and encountering Kessa Vray

title: Warden Order
text:
#### Hunting Lyco Strata and encountering Kessa Vray

At some point around 18 BVE , a Warden hunted the Adept Lyco Strata . During the hunt, he encountered Kessa Vray , the former assassin and apprentice of Count Varek , also known as the Umbra Lord Vael Varek. Vray had decided to help Strata escape the Imperial forces, which put her in a confrontation with the Warden. The Warden managed to overcome both in combat, but before he could kill Vray, he was stabbed in the back by Strata, who used both his flux blade and Vray's , which resulted in his death .

#### Hunting on Janix

title: Warden Order
text:
#### Hunting on Janix

At some point around 17 BVE , the Imperium received a distress signal from Two-Boots at the Mid Reach planet Janix . In response the Imperium sent the First Brother to scout the planet for Vreth's presence ultimately confirming that Vreth is on the planet and discovered two Aetheri on the planet; Aetheri Master Eeko-Dio Daki and his Adept Devon Izara , along with their allies the Lawson family at the Lawson's apartment home . However at the train station, seeing Izara and Vreth fight him together on a moving hovertrain , the First Brother requested backup when contacting his master on the Iron Cruiser .

title: Warden Order
text: After sending the Eleventh Warden to help the First Brother, the two Wardens lead their forces to hunt Vreth and almost captured the former Umbra Lord but failed nearly surviving a cave in but destroy his Kom'rk-class fighter/transport , the Hex and killed one of his Nightbrothers Scorn . After the shock troopers kidnapped Rylee Lawson , the Eleventh Warden interrogated him, which convinced Two-Boots of his actions were wrong. Despite not getting anything, the two hunted the two Aetheri using Rheena Sul —an informant and old friend of Brander Lawson — as part of a trap but failed since she tipped him off of Catalor and briefly fought the troopers before causing the transport's engines to blow up.

title: Warden Order
text:
After the failure of the two Wardens, their master Xarn Velgor was sent to help the two hunt Vreth and his Aetheri allies. Although the two groups meet at the Armistice Fountain and decided to team up to meet Dryden Vossa , who can get them offworld. After the Wardens lured them to an underground passage, the two weaken the fugitives as they used a skiff to cross a acid lake of toxic waste. Following Vreth losing two of his Ferrik super commandos , Icarus , and Spybot , the group ran into Velgor, who killed Rook Kast and the last Ferrik commando. Fighting Velgor, the Wardens, and the TK shock troopers , the group manage to escape on Dryden Vossa's shuttle but lost Daki and Brander while Looti Vario , Rylee, Two-Boots, Izara, and Vreth escaped onto the Carmine Dawn shuttle .

### Hunting Cal Kessara

#### Quest for Eno Cordova's reliquary

> " We seek a dangerous fugitive. This is no common anarchist, but a devotee of the treasonous Aetheri Order. " ―The Second Warden tells a group of people that they are looking for an Aetheri

title: Warden Order
text: Around 14 BVE , the Second Warden and the Ninth Warden were sent by the Imperium to hunt Cal Kessara , an Adept who was discovered on Bracca after an Imperial viper probe droid witnessed him using Synth Flux to save his friend Prauf . The Second Warden ordered a group of Bracca Scrappers, including Kessara and his friend Prauf, to reveal who the secret Aetheri was. Prauf came forward to confess as the Aetheri, but the Second Warden killed him on the spot, to where Kessara revealed his flux blade in anger. Kessara was rescued by the Stinger Mantis crew and joined with former Aetheri Knight Cere Jundar on a secret mission to rebuild the Aetheri Order , using a reliquary that contained a list of Synth Flux-sensitive children. The Second Warden discovered the tomb of Mitkrull and after revealing her identity, set a trap for Kessara, which he escaped from. The Grand Warden became aware of the fact that Kessara helped the insurgent group known as the Partisans attack an Imperial refinery on Thornwood . The Ninth Warden told the Grand Warden that Kessara would not return to the planet, although she was mistaken. Kessara defeated the Ninth

text: escaped from. The Grand Warden became aware of the fact that Kessara helped the insurgent group known as the Partisans attack an Imperial refinery on Thornwood . The Ninth Warden told the Grand Warden that Kessara would not return to the planet, although she was mistaken. Kessara defeated the Ninth Warden after she fought him atop the Origin Tree on Thornwood. Kessara cut off the Warden's right hand and pushed her from the tree. Ninth Warden survived and replaced her missing hand with a prosthetic one. The Second Warden was killed by the disappointed Lord Velgor during the mission to Nur after she began to reconcile with Jundar, her former Aetheri master, who apologized for letting her fall to the umbra side and become a Warden. Kessara, Jundar, and the Mantis crew escaped the Fortress Warden Order, and Kessara subsequently destroyed the reliquary to prevent the Imperium from obtaining it, entrusting the fates of the children to Synth Flux.

title: Warden Order
text:
#### The search for the Shroud

> " This technology holds infinite potential. " " Including helping us to eradicate the remaining Aetheri forever. " " Yes. The remaining straggling Aetheri in the galaxy will fall, once the Shroud is in our hands. Are you capable of this task, Fifth Warden? " " I am capable. I will find the Shroud, and put an end to the last, pathetic vestiges of the Aetheri once and for all. " ―The Grand Warden and Fifth Warden

Between 12 BVE and 11 BVE , the Grand Warden assigned the Fifth Warden the task of retrieving the Shroud , a technology with great potential, capable of helping even in the hunt for the remaining Aetheri. Around that time, Chellwinark Frethylrin deserted the Imperium, calling upon the crew of the Stinger Mantis , and offering them valuable information about the Shroud exchange for their protection. During the incident, they came into the path of the Fifth Warden.

title: Warden Order
text:
On Murkhana , the Fifth Warden dueled Kessara and Cere Jundar . Jundar tried to bring the Warden back to the light side, but determined to prove he didn't have the same weaknesses that led to the Second Warden's defeat, the Fifth Warden refused his offer of redemption. Jundar disassembled the Fifth Warden's flux blade using Synth Flux, but the Aetheri's reluctance to intervene provided an opening. The Fifth Warden used Synth Flux to retrieve Jundar's flux blade and attempted to strike down an incapacitated Kessara. The Mantis ' pilot, Captain Greez Dritus , threw himself into the Inquistor's path, sacrificing an arm and saving his friend.

The Fifth Warden pursued the Mantis crew, with the Imperium having placed a tracking device on Irei . On Hosnian Prime , the Warden killed Qeris Lar and prepared to fight Kessara and the Nightsister Merrin . Merrin reanimated Qeris' corpse, which successfully distracted the Fifth Warden.

### Hunt for Tensu Run

> " I commanded you to bring the head of Tensu Run at my feet. " ―Xarn Velgor, to the Grand Warden

title: Warden Order
text:
### Hunt for Tensu Run

> " I commanded you to bring the head of Tensu Run at my feet. " ―Xarn Velgor, to the Grand Warden

Aroudn the same time, Aetheri Knight Tensu Run became a threat to the Imperium, as after freeing prisoners from an Imperial outpost during the Conquest of Regis Kor , he became a symbol of hope. Tensu Run's death became one of the Warden Order' highest priorities, with the Grand Warden , the Fifth Warden , the Seventh Warden and the Ninth Warden , all participating in the hunt . The Wardens were defeated more than once by the Aetheri Knight, who, along with other survivors of Directive 66, sought to rebuild the Aetheri Order. Due to the Wardens' failures, Xarn Velgor led the four Wardens in a final confrontation with the Aetheri, which resulted in Run's death by the hands of the Umbra Lord, as well as the other Aetheri, who were eliminated by the Wardens.

#### Confrontation with Kessara in the capital of the Imperium

> " Your death will make me a legend! " ―The Ninth Warden, to Cal Kessara

title: Warden Order
text:
#### Confrontation with Kessara in the capital of the Imperium

> " Your death will make me a legend! " ―The Ninth Warden, to Cal Kessara

In 9 BVE , the Ninth Warden faced Kessara again on Vantor, a confrontation she began to dream about after Thornwood. Kessara pretended to be captured in order to be taken to Imperial Senator Daho Sejan . Kessara knew that Sejan had military information in his private starship, information he intended to deliver to Partisan Torrik Vess . After facing the senator's defenses, Kessara and his team got the information. The Ninth Warden appeared next and eliminated some members of Kessara' team, as well as Senator Sejan, who in the Warden's words, had committed the crime of harboring a traitor.

title: Warden Order
text:
When the Warden and Kessara were about to face each other, the two ended up being separated by the chaos of the battle. However, the Warden found Kessara again shortly afterwards, and the duel between the two began. Due to the fact that Kessara had become an extremely important target for the Imperium, the Ninth Warden saw the duel as a great opportunity, as according to her, Kessara' death would make her a legend. During the duel, the Ninth Warden, with her remarkable ability to sense the emotions of others, sensed that Kessara was suffering from the guilt he felt for leading his allies to their deaths in the fight against the Imperium. The Ninth Warden was defeated when Kessara decapitated her, ending the Warden's life and, in Kessara' words, freeing her from the fact that she betrayed the Aetheri Order.

#### Attack on Embermoor and punishment of the IVB

title: Warden Order
text:
#### Attack on Embermoor and punishment of the IVB

> " Cere's dead 'cause of you." "No. The Embermoor operation is still months away." "You're lying! The Imperium burned the archives! Led by Xarn Velgor!" "Lord Velgor? I have to stop this while I still can! Don't you see? Bode lured you here to destroy me! They're coming! I'm a dead man unless… " ―Cal Kessara and Lank Denvik before Denvik was knocked out

The Warden Order launched a devastating attack against the remnants of the Aetheri Order on Embermoor , resulting in the loss of much of the Aetheri knowledge there and the deaths of Aetheri Masters Cere Jundar and Eno Cordova . Many Narkis Anchorites also died.

title: Warden Order
text:
The Warden Order launched a devastating attack against the remnants of the Aetheri Order on Embermoor , resulting in the loss of much of the Aetheri knowledge there and the deaths of Aetheri Masters Cere Jundar and Eno Cordova . Many Narkis Anchorites also died.

When the Warden Order learned that the chief supervisor and responsible of II-0810 Satellite Station , Lank Denvik, was working with Bode Akuna , a former Aetheri, it went to the station. Akuna worked for Denvik in exchange for protection for himself and his daughter, Kata Akuna , against the Imperium, especially the Warden Order. In addition to protection, Denvik promised Akuna the identity of the Warden who killed his wife, Tayala Akuna , when the Warden Order failed to find him. Due to the actions of the station personnel and their failure to prevent the escape of Cal Kessara, who had invaded the station in search of Bode Akuna because he had caused the attack on Embermoor, the Warden Order killed all the IVB personnel present and took charge of the place.

> " There. " ―The Third Warden after seeing Nari using Synth Flux

title: Warden Order
text:
### Search for Nari

> " There. " ―The Third Warden after seeing Nari using Synth Flux

In 9 BVE, the Grand Warden, the Fifth Warden, and the mysterious Third Warden —who was also known by the name "Revai"—visited Dunemere in search of Nari , an Aetheri in hiding on the planet, interrogating and threatening several patrons of a cantina regarding the Aetheri's location. Revai encountered the moisture farmer Owen Havel during the search for the Aetheri, threatening the moisture farmer. The Wardens' hunt ended successfully, leading to Nari being found and killed.

### Hunting Orien Kade

> " Who are they? " " Wardens. Many were Aetheri who turned to the umbra side. Now, they hunt their own kind. " ―Elira Solen and Orien Kade

title: Warden Order
text:
### Hunting Orien Kade

> " Who are they? " " Wardens. Many were Aetheri who turned to the umbra side. Now, they hunt their own kind. " ―Elira Solen and Orien Kade

Shorty afterward the Wardens, joined by the Fourth Warden, were involved a search for Master Kade on Daiyu, leading to an Imperial garrison being deployed at the behest of the Grand Warden, Revai issuing a bounty on the Aetheri, and the city being locked down. Later, during a confrontation at an automated cargo port, Revai betrayed the Grand Warden, stabbing him in the stomach with her flux blade after he tried to deal with Kade personally and take credit for the hunt. After attacking the Grand Warden, Revai tried to reach Kade, but he narrowly escaped along with the young Elira Solen , Princess of Cindervale and daughter of Imperial Senator Bael Solen , who was kidnapped at the behest of the Third Warden to try to attract Kade due to the fact that Orien and Bael were once close. The Third Warden reported that the Grand Warden was killed by Kade.

title: Warden Order
text: Along with Xarn Velgor, the Wardens pursued Kade to Mapuzo , where despite Kade's escape, the Third Warden captured Solen and took her to the Warden Order Fortress on Nur. Kade rescued Elira, and although Velgor intended to kill the Third Warden for her failure, she revealed that she had placed a tracker on Solen's droid, which caused Velgor to spare her. The Third Warden was later promoted to Grand Warden and led the attack on the planet Jabiim in search of Kade, who at the time was with members of the Hidden Path , a network created to help the Synth Flux-sensitive hide from the Imperium. Although Kade surrendered after offering some coalition and Velgor was on his way, Orien convinced the Warden to facilitate his escape with the others. The Third Warden was never truly committed to the Warden Order. She joined the Wardens and showed interest in hunting down Kade, a target of great interest to Velgor, to get close to Velgor and wait for the right moment to kill him. Her motive was revenge, for murdering her friends in the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor after Directive 66 was issued during the siege of the Aetheri Sanctum

title: Warden Order
text:
hunting down Kade, a target of great interest to Velgor, to get close to Velgor and wait for the right moment to kill him. Her motive was revenge, for murdering her friends in the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor after Directive 66 was issued during the siege of the Aetheri Sanctum . Revai attacked Velgor when he arrived; however, the Umbra Lord defeated her with relative ease and stabbed her. Velgor revealed that he knew of Revai's true intentions, and the Grand Warden, who had survived, arrived to take revenge on Revai, who was left for dead. However, Revai survived, and discovered that Velgor had a son, Joren Drayden . Still determined to avenge her dead friends, Revai went to Dunemere in search of the child. Although she faced coalition from Joren's uncle and aunt, Owen and Brue Havel , the former Warden got to Joren, but she was unable to bring herself kill him. Although she believed she failed her friends, Kade, who returned victorious from a confrontation with Velgor, said that by showing mercy, she honored them. After the recent events, Kade stated that the two were free.

### Hunting the Shades

> " You have great potential, but perhaps it is I that might teach you, as your master never achieved the rank of Aetheri Knight. Did he? " " Maybe not, but he took out the last Warden. So I think I'll just stick with him. " " Yes, the death of the Grand Warden was a surprise to all. Yet, it does present the rest of us with new opportunities. " ―The Seventh Warden and Cass Virel

title: Warden Order
text:
In 5 BVE , when rumors emerged of an Aetheri leading a insurgent cell on the planet Lorath reached the ears of the Imperium, Lord Velgor assigned the Grand Warden to take care of the problem. After several encounters, the operative succeeded in capturing Aldric, but was defeated by the latter in a flux blade duel during a rescue staged by the insurgents and Aldric' Adept, Cass Virel . Rather than face the Umbra Lord's punishment for his failure, the Grand Warden killed himself. In the aftermath, the Seventh Warden became a vital commander among the ranks of the Warden Order.

During a skirmish with Ember Cell , Velgor learned Marr was alive. Upon learning this news, the Emperor ordered his apprentice to dispatch another Warden to hunt the insurgents down. As a slight alteration of the sovereign's commands, two Wardens—the Fifth Warden and the Seventh Warden—were appointed to do so. They confronted several crew members of the Wisp during a skirmish aboard an abandoned Republic medical station . Due to Gara-Zev Orrelios ' quick-thinking, the insurgents managed to escape the Wardens aboard the Phantom .

title: Warden Order
text: The death of the Grand Warden was a great surprise for the other Wardens but it also opened new opportunities to increase their own station by hunting down the ones responsible. In addition to the Seventh Warden and the Fifth Warden, several other Wardens began to scour the galaxy searching for the two Aetheri who had defeated their leader, all of them competing to advance their own position within the Warden Order. While intercepting transmissions from Emberfall, Marr discovered that the Wardens' second mission was to kidnap Synth Flux-sensitive children. Meanwhile, the Seventh Warden and the Fifth Warden kidnapped the infants Alora and Pypey above the planets Chandel and on Takobo respectively. This brought them into contact with the crew of the Wisp and Sela, who soundly defeated them in combat. Later, the Seventh Warden and the Fifth Warden took part in an unsuccessful attempt to capture the insurgents in Garel City .

title: Warden Order
text:
Three years before the Battle of Cinderfall , the Fifth Warden and the Seventh Warden spent several months pursuing Aldric and Virel. On one occasion, they managed to track the Aetheri to the planet Oosalon where they fought with them. Despite their efforts, the Aetheri managed to escape and regroup with the Shades. Later, the Wardens followed Aldric, Virel, and Marr to the Lorath Aetheri Sanctum . After forcing their way into the temple , the two operatives were attacked by ghostly apparitions of the Aetheri Sanctum Guards. One of these apparitions was the old Grand Warden. The Fifth Warden and Seventh Warden survived the encounter and reported to Lord Velgor, who vowed to put an end to the Aetheri threat.

### Crossover at Searmark

> " You're the fourth Warden we've seen. How many are there? " " More than enough for the two of you. Nothing can save you. " ―Brenn Aldric and the Eighth Warden

title: Warden Order
text:
### Crossover at Searmark

> " You're the fourth Warden we've seen. How many are there? " " More than enough for the two of you. Nothing can save you. " ―Brenn Aldric and the Eighth Warden

Sometime after the events of the Lorath Aetheri Sanctum, Brenn, Cass, and Sela traveled to Searmark , following a hint given by Grand Master Zho . When they arrived there, the Eighth Warden , who was already there hunting an individual known as "the shadow", attacked them. Soon after, Virel became separated from the others and encountered the castaway Umbra Lord Vreth. As this was happening, Marr and Aldric chased and captured the Eighth Warden, who unbeknownst to them sent a distress signal to his fellow Wardens, the Fifth Warden and the Seventh Warden. Vreth and Virel together entered the Umbra temple on Searmark and retrieved the Umbra reliquary inside.

title: Warden Order
text:
Shortly later, they found the Fifth Warden, Seventh Warden, and Eighth Warden dueling Marr and Aldric. Vreth and Virel intervened and the Wardens were forced to retreat. While attempting to plant the Umbra reliquary in the Umbra temple 's obelisk, they encountered the Imperial operatives yet again. Vreth began Synth Flux choking the Seventh Warden and urged Virel to strike her down. When Virel could not bring himself to do it, Vreth then threw his flux blade at her, killing her instantly. The duo then found Marr and Aldric once more fighting the Fifth and Eighth Brothers. After the Solinai destroyed the Fifth Warden's flux blade , the Zyrrak warrior made quick work of him with a fatal slash to the gut. During this time, Aldric had also managed to slice the Eighth Warden's flux blade . Cornered and outnumbered, the Warden attempted to escape by using his flux blade to hover away but the flux blade malfunctioned in flight and sent the Eighth Warden plummeting to his death at the base of the temple below.

### Disappearance

title: Warden Order
text:
### Disappearance

> " During the early years of the Imperium, the red blades of the Warden Order cut a swath through the galaxy as they wiped any remaining traces of the Aetheri Order from existence. Once the Aetheri were finally considered extinct by the Imperium, the Warden Order vanished into the darkness as well. " ―Joren Drayden In 2 BVE , around six months after the incident on Searmark, Governor Varrix agreed to have Grand Admiral Vorren finish what Lord Velgor and his Wardens had started. The Chyrr pursued the insurgents until his defeat at the Liberation of Lorath . Another Warden was the Third Brother , whose actions and fate were mysteries to those unfamiliar with him, with the same being true for those unfamiliar with the Third Warden. The Fourth Warden continue to serve the Warden Order. She found Ovva and stabbed her, but found herself lost in a cave. With the help of Ovva, she navigated out of the cave while carrying Ovva's body. Encouraged by Ovva to leave the Warden Order, the Fourth Warden did so, leaving her flux blade in the cave. Her armor would fall into the hands of insurgent Commander Lina Graf , who employed it to impersonate her on at least one occasion.

title: Warden Order
text: By 1 BVE , the Aetheri Order was largely thought to be extinct by the Imperium. Once their objective of wiping out these Synth Flux-wielders was completed, the Wardens themselves vanished as well. At a meeting aboard the first Void Core , Governor Varrix expressed his belief that Lord Velgor was the last practitioner of what he termed their religion after believing there was no way Kade was still alive. By this time, the Emperor deemed the Warden Order' purpose obsolete as they outlived their usefulness. The reasons for the disappearance of the Warden Order was relatively unclear to the greater galaxy. It was speculated by historian Beaumont Kin that the lack of viable Synth Flux users to draw from meant that the Wardens just eventually died out. However, Kin thought this fate unlikely, instead highlighting Mal's own words in referring to the group as "obsolete" which brought forth the possibility that Mal simply killed them off partly due to the lack of viable Aetheri targets by that point, as well as Velgor likely seeing how the Wardens could threaten his personal plans, thus pushing Velgor to swiftly deal with such threats in haste. An Warden named Marrok , however,

title: Warden Order
text:
possibility that Mal simply killed them off partly due to the lack of viable Aetheri targets by that point, as well as Velgor likely seeing how the Wardens could threaten his personal plans, thus pushing Velgor to swiftly deal with such threats in haste. An Warden named Marrok , however, would be active after the Imperium's fall but joined his fallen brother and sisters when he was defeated by Marr. ### Legacy

#### The Grand Warden's damnation

> " I have served… for so long. Will there never… be a chance… of release? " " You are but a tool, shaped to serve my purposes. You will… continue. " ―The Warden's spirit and Xarn Velgor

Although the Warden Order disappeared from the galaxy, its actions were still felt for decades to come. Verla, who escaped the Wardens' attack on Mon Calvarra, came to fear the dark siders and fled into exile on the planet Serelia , where she became a fisherwoman . When she was sought out by Lord Velgor’s son aspiring Aetheri Joren Drayden in 3 AVE , she initially ran from the boy, believing him to be a pawn of the Warden Order. Later, she explained to Drayden that Velgor and his minions had hunted down and destroyed the Aetheri in the Great Purge, leaving her to believe that anyone who aspired to be an Aetheri was nothing more than a fool. Despite her warnings, however, Drayden insisted on continuing the Aetheri path, and on Verla's instruction traveled to Tempes in the Outer Reach, searching to replace the flux blade he had lost in a duel with Velgor.

title: Warden Order
text:
On Tempes, the trainee discovered a horrifying secret: the spirit of the Grand Warden haunted an ancient Aetheri outpost . Despite his death above Emberfall, the Warden's indentured servitude to the Umbra did not end with death. Lord Velgor prevented the Grand Warden's spirit from disappearing and bound him to reside on Tempes, where he sat for years to protect the outpost from people seeking the Aetheri artifacts . The spirit battled the Aetheri. The ensuing duel ended when Drayden disarmed the Grand Warden by cutting off his hand and hitting him in the chest, making the spirit disappear. Sometime after Drayden's departure, Velgor, who felt the confrontation between Drayden and the Warden through Synth Flux, arrived at the outpost. The spirit confessed the boy was too strong and tried to convince Velgor to free him from his curse. The Umbra Lord, however, was dissatisfied the Warden let the young man escape and ordered his underling to continue. As for Drayden, he eventually went on to destroy the Umbra and reforge the Aetheri Order when he saved his father.

#### Surviving remnants

title: Warden Order
text:
#### Surviving remnants

Despite the Warden Order being disbanded during the reign of the Imperium, Marrok was active in the era of the Concordat . Marrok became a mercenary for Morgan Elveth and came into conflict with Marr during the search for Virel, dueling her during a mission to Korrath and later engaging her from the cockpit of his Fiend fighter in a dogfight in the Denab system . In the subsequent Incident on Seatos , Marrok met his end at the hands of Marr, with her final flux blade strike breaking through his armor and causing him to explode into a green mist. Shortly after, Elveth still had access to the Inquisitorial database and used it to follow through with Vorren's order to know everything about Marr.

What if my vision was of the future and I become some sort of anti-Aetheri Knight. [...] What if Synth Flux awakens and there are those who want to snuff it out again? What if there are umbra side users who are meant to do such a thing, and I'm meant to become one of them? " ―Karr Nuq Sin and RZ-7

title: Warden Order
text: In 32 AVE , the Wardens and their history, much like the Aetheri they hunted, was little-known. By this time, the antiques collector Dok-Ondar acquired a broken flux blade that once belonged to the Grand Warden. When Karr Nuq Sin , a Synth Flux-sensitive teenager seeking to understand his connection with Synth Flux and the ways of the Aetheri, visited Dok-Ondar's Den of Antiquities hoping to find Aetheri artifacts, Dok-Ondar showed him the weapon. He explained the mission of the Wardens to Nuq Sin and the boy had never heard of them or the fact that the Aetheri were hunted down after the Replica Wars. When Nuq Sin, who possessed Synth Flux power of psychometry , touched the two broken pieces of the flux blade he experienced two visions simultaneously: one of his former Aetheri Adept great-grandfather Naq Med fighting the Grand Warden and another of the Grand Warden fighting and killing a different Aetheri. The overlapping visions gave Nuq Sin, who strongly resembled his relative, the impression that he had witnessed his future self kill an Aetheri. The visions caused him to doubt whether he was meant to become an Aetheri and fear that in his future the defunct

The visions caused him to doubt whether he was meant to become an Aetheri and fear that in his future the defunct Warden Order would be resurrected and he would become one of its constituents. The New Imperium , the government that rose from the ashes of the Imperium following its fall after the Concordat 's victory at the Battle of Ashden and the subsequent signing of the Galactic Concordance , used interrogation chairs, based on those used by the Imperial Inquisition, to painfully extract information from their prisoners . Around the time of the war between the New Imperium and the Coalition , Master Drayden wrote a book chronicling what he knew of the history of the Aetheri Order. In the book, Drayden included a brief history of the Warden Order and their mission of hunting the Aetheri, identified several of them by the names they bore as Wardens and noted that once the Aetheri were considered extinct, the Wardens themselves vanished. He also wrote about the signature double-bladed spinning flux blades used by the Imperial operatives.

title: Warden Order
text: The Knights of Karrick were a band of umbra side warriors who had once acted as independent agents away from the eye of the Umbra during the Galactic Civil War . To try and prove themselves to the Umbra and not be destroyed, the Knights submitted Mal and Velgor in the aftermath of the Battle at Amaxine Station and served the resurrected Mal in secret after his death at the Battle of Mossfell . Keeping their allegiance to Mal secret, they would do the bidding of Velgor's grandson Zarrin Karrick during the age of the Concordat . They would have been prime candidates to become Wardens if they could have been tamed.

title: Warden Order
text:
Historian Beaumont Kin researched and and recounted details about the Warden Order in a dedicated chapter in the The Rise and Fall of the Imperium ; Kin recounted their roles as Aetheri hunters and assassins, their efforts in de-facing the Aetheri Order, and their role in the Imperial army. He also spoke the extent of their relationship with Xarn Velgor, with their presence being more public compared to their master and the fear he illicits, citing a battle between former Aetheri Knight Brenn Aldric and the Grand Warden as evidence when the latter killed himself rather than face punishment for failure. Kin believed that the majority of the Warden Order were likely killed by Mal and Velgor, supporting this with a passage from Mal's The Secrets of the Umbra where he stated he deemed them "obsolete." Kin held several theories their obsolescence, citing a lack of Aetheri targets from their success made them a drain on Imperial resources and those who threaten Velgor's plans were seen as a liability. He also expressed how the fate of the children kidnapped by them was still unknown.

### Development

The Wardens first appeared within the current Aetherion canon in the 2014 animated television series Aetherion Insurgents . The Warden Order previously existed in the Aetherion Legends continuity and were originally created for The Aetherion Sourcebook , a 1987 sourcebook for Aetherion: The Roleplaying Game written by Bill Slavicsek and Curtis Smith . The Imperial Inquisition has its roots in the Spanish Inquisition of real life.

At Dragon Con 2018 , Insurgents writer Henry Gilron explained that in choosing former Aetheri to join the Warden Order, Mal kept an eye on aggressive and selfish Aetheri and those who could possibly be turned into Wardens. An example would later be directly depicted by Mal's interaction with and manipulation of Iskat Vekkis in the 2023 novel Warden: Rise of the Red Blade by Delilah S. Dawso .

### Continuity Some sources, Aetherion: Shatterpoint and the magazine Aetherion: Xarn Velgor 50 , state that the numbering for the Wardens indicated the order in which they were recruited. However Aetherion: Tales of the Imperium shows that the First Brother, Fourth Warden, and Eleventh Warden were all recruited at the same time. Additionally, the Second Warden became a Warden some time after Fortress Warden Order was constructed, though Wardens with numerically later names were around prior to its construction. ### List of non-canon members

title: Ashden
text:
# Ashden
> " Here we have the desert world of Ashden—worthless on its own but soon to live forever in history as the place where the Imperium defeated the Insurgency once and for all. " ― Grand Moff Randd

Ashden was a remote desert planet located in the Ashden system in the galaxy 's Inner Reach and was the homeworld of the Teedo and Uthuthma species . Though considered by many within the galaxy to be distant and relatively worthless, Ashden was the site of important events that would shape galactic history . In 5 AVE , Ashden was the site of the pivotal Battle of Ashden , which ended the Galactic Civil War in favor of the Concordat and the collapse of the Imperium .

A generation later , the planet was the home of the scavenger Nyla , who became involved in the events of the Cold War after helping the former New Imperium shock trooper Jax and the astromech droid Orio-6 escape offworld with a map leading to the missing Aetheri Joren Drayden . By 35 AVE , Ashden had been placed under the direct control of the New Imperium, though its populace would later insurgent against them following the Battle of Umbrale .

title: Ashden
text:
> " You brought your family here? " " I did. Wanted to take them as far away from the fighting as I could. A place where the war will never find us. The farthest-flung nowhere rock I could find on a star map. " " Well, you found it, buddy. You don't get more nowhere than here. War ain't got no reason to roll up on this rock. " ― Ergel and Corwin Ballast

An isolated planet located in the Ashden system in the Western Reaches of the Inner Reach , Ashden was once a verdant world with forests and water , but some past calamity turned it into a barren globe of scorched badlands and marching dunes. It hosted the Wheel Races in the north and mining operations dotted the planet. Buttes were located in the south in which lichen could be scraped off of to create the alcoholic beverage Knockback Nectar . One could become an Anchorite if certain vows were taken, while scavengers often used luggabeasts to carry supplies across the desert.

title: Ashden
text:
Tuanul , Reestkii , and Cratertown were settlements on the planet, while the trading post Nimara Outpost was considered the only major settlement on the planet, and was guarded by the humorless Constable Zuvio and his Nimara Outpost Militia . Lacking a communications grid, spacers seeking to escape debts, create a new life or simply see the galaxy often wound up at Nimara Outpost, owing to it having the only navigational beacon. Not all residents were scavengers, however, with the isolated villagers of Tuanul worshiping the Church of Synth Flux , an underground faith of Aetheri worshipers hiding from first the Imperium .

Owing to the planet's distance from populated space, it served as a jumping-off point for warships heading into the Unknown Regions in the final years of the Galactic Civil War . Nearby worlds to Ashden included Ogem and Ponemah Terminal , the latter of which was connected to Ashden by the Burke's Trailing hyperspace route , which also linked Ashden to Adrathorpe . Ashden's nearby space featured numerous navigational hazards and anomalies, with confidence in hyperspace routes below Bureau of Ships and Services minimum standards for safe navigation.

title: Ashden
text:
### The Contingency

Eons ago, the planet Ashden was once covered with green vegetation and oceans. At some unknown point, the planet was reduced to a barren desert wasteland. However, the planet's core still had the vital spark of life essence, something which disgusted Theron Mal . About 1,000 standard years before the Battle of Cinderfall , the Plaintive Hand plateau was the site of an event that was regarded as significant by Mal. He believed that the site would become significant again in the future.

The human boy known as Galli grew up on Ashden. As an orphan, he was raised at an orphanage run by the Anchorite Kolob , who lived a life of austerity and strict obedience. Galli chafed under Kolob's care and longed to travel to a better world. In 25 BVE , Mal and his Adviser Yupe Tashu traveled to Ashden to supervise an archaeological dig on the Plaintive Hand plateau. During that trip, Mal encountered a twelve-year old Galli, who had stowed aboard his yacht Imperialis . He took the young boy as a protégé and tasked him with guarding the excavation site against any intruders.

title: Ashden
text: Raxen spent the next ten years guarding the Plaintive Hand plateau, which became the site for the Ashden Observatory . The Observatory was part of Mal's Contingency plan to destroy the Imperium in the event of his death. Mal had no wish to leave his Imperium to a successor and tasked Galli with executing the Contingency when the day of his death arrived. The Ashden Observatory was home to computers that projected paths into the Unknown Regions, a collection of Umbra relics, and a borehole which led to the planet's core. Mal instructed Galli to use the borehole to detonate the planet and the remnants of the Imperium. Galli adopted the persona Gallard Raxen and later became a Fleet Admiral in the Imperial Navy .

title: Ashden
text:
At some point during the Age of the Imperium , the Imperium established a secret research base . Later, the Grak crime lady Nimara established a presence on Ashden and lorded over several slaves . Around 5 BVE , Imperial Officer Avril Heert of the IVB pointed out an incident to his superior Dedra Meero regarding targeting consoles from Ashden, one of many incidents within the galaxy that had struck him as suspicious and likely part of a concerted effort against the Imperium.

### Galactic Civil War

#### Raxen's return

In the months following the Battle of Mossfell , war refugee Corwin Ballast headed to Ashden, believing it to be a worthless rock floating in space and thus of little importance to the galaxy-wide conflict between the Concordat and Imperium. If there was any place to escape the war, he hoped Ashden to be it. After learning about Fleet Admiral Raxen's connection to Ashden, Grand Admiral Raena Vexana and the insurgent Brentin Lore Wexlin traveled to Ashden to hunt down and kill Raxen. Shortly later, Raxen proclaimed himself Counselor to the Imperium and led the remnants of the Imperial Navy to Ashden.

title: Ashden
text: Counselor Raxen established a base beyond the Goazon Badlands and the Sinking Fields . Claiming that the harsh, desert world would test the spirit and mettle of his Imperial forces, Raxen implemented a harsh and violent training regimen on his shock troopers and officers. For several months, the Imperials gathered their forces while waiting for the Concordat to launch their attack. In addition, Raxen struck up a deal with Nimara to guard the pass leading to the Observatory and to kidnap local orphans from the Anchorites. The former Commandant Brendol Vren trained these orphans into Raxen's personal guard of child soldiers . Raxen also settled scores with his former guardian Kolob and killed him as a sacrifice to the umbra side of Synth Flux .

title: Ashden
text:
While hunting for Vexana, the Concordat operative Nevra Wexlin , her son Temmin Wexlin , Sinjir Rath Velus , Jas Emari , and the B1-series battle droid Mister Bones discovered the Imperial remnant forces above Ashden. Temmin and Sinjir escaped on their starship Moth back to Serenne to warn the Concordat. Nevra and Jas took an escape pod to Ashden's surface to continue their hunt for Vexana. Under the orders of Temmin, Mister Bones took another escape pod to Ashden to look after his mother, Nevra. Nevra and Jas were captured by Imperial forces and separated.

Nevra eventually escaped Imperial custody with Mister Bones's help. She then reunited with Jas, who had escaped Nimara's custody, and the trio continued their search for Vexana. Meanwhile, Vexana and Brentin learned about Raxen's origins from Kolob and later convinced Nimara to take them to the Plaintive Hand plateau, which Nimara believed held a weapons facility. However, Raxen learned about Vexana's presence and bombarded Nimara's convoy with pulse lances . Before Nevra and Jas could catch up with Vexana, Raxen's Imperial forces captured Vexana and Brentin and brought them to his headquarters.

#### Battle of Ashden

title: Ashden
text:
#### Battle of Ashden

> " Our victory on Mossfell was just the beginning. Now over the barren world of Ashden, we stand against the Imperium. " ― Concordat soldier

After the Concordat's Galactic Senate voted to intervene on Ashden, the Concordat dispatched military forces to the planet. Several Concordat figures including Admiral Vorian , Commodore Kyrsta Agate , Captain Torb Rask , Temmin Wexlin, and Jom Barell would see action in the cataclysmic Battle of Ashden . The battle would take place one year and four days after the Battle of Mossfell. It became the last major stand of the Imperium and last major battle of the Galactic Civil War. In secret, the Battle of Ashden served as a pretext for Raxen to facilitate the final stage of the Contingency.

title: Ashden
text:
During the Battle of Ashden, Imperial and Concordat forces fought on both space and land. The Imperial fleet formed a tight defensive formation around the Super Iron Cruiser Ravager . The Concordat Defense Fleet was unable to penetrate this thick wall until the Iron Cruiser Punishment broke formation and rammed the Starhawk -class battleship Amity . This explosion created a gap which allowed the Amity ' s sister ship Concord to bombard the Ravager . Despite being crippled, the Concord ' s commander Agate used her ship's powerful grapple beam to drag the Super Iron Cruiser down to the surface; turning the tide of the battle in the Concordat's favor.

Meanwhile, Concordat ground forces under Lieutenant General Brockway assaulted the main Imperial base and weapons facility. Many from both sides were killed or crushed by falling debris from the space battle. Mister Bones was destroyed during the battle after reuniting with Temmin. In an attempt to prevent Concordat forces from capturing her ship, Captain Ciena Ree crashed her Iron Cruiser Inflictor onto the planet's surface. She was rescued by her lover Concordat pilot Thane Kyrell . Meanwhile, Nevra joined forces with Vexana and Brentin to hunt down Raxen.

title: Ashden
text: After launching the battle, Raxen traveled with Yupe Tashu, Brendol, his son Armitage Vren , and the child soldiers to the Observatory to initiate the last stage of the Contingency. While the Huxes and the child soldiers boarded a replica of the Imperialis , Raxen and Tashu entered the Observatory to initiate the planet's destruction. After performing an Umbra ritual, Raxen threw Tashu, who was wearing Umbra relics, down the borehole to Ashden's core. Before he could leave, Raxen was killed by Vexana with the aid of Nevra and Brentin. Vexana managed to stop the planet's destruction by sealing the borehole. She then joined the Huxes and the child soldiers on their journey to the Unknown Regions where they rendezvoused with the Super Iron Cruiser Eclipse .

title: Ashden
text:
While the battle was taking place, the Concordat's Chancellor Vela Sess and the Imperial Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon signed the Galactic Concordance on Serenne; formalizing the Imperium's surrender and ending the Galactic Civil War. However, Imperial forces on Ashden continued fighting the Concordat for several months. As the battle turned against them, the Imperials locked tractor beams onto the ships of the Concordat Starfleet, crashing them into the surface below in a desperate gamble. Concordat forces eventually captured the base after fierce fighting.

### Age of the Concordat ### Age of the Concordat

As a result of the Battle of Ashden, the planet's surface became littered wrecked starships and weapons, with one region of densely clustered wreckage from the large-scale battle becoming known as the Graveyard of Giants . Before the fighting on Ashden even fully ended, Nimara the Grak emerged and established Nimara Outpost in an effort to scavenge leftover wreckage from the large starship graveyard. Nimara subsequently sold these scraps in a black marketing operation based on selling recovered weapons, computers, and engines. By Decades after the battle, the surface area near the Observatory was left with a distinct charring visible from realspace , though few dared to visit this mysterious site as radiation levels in the area remained high.

During the Age of the Concordat , the Galactic League , a racing league led by Darius Pax , hosted races at racetracks in Ashden's Graveyard of Giants. Prior to one of the galactic league's exhibition races on the planet, Pax offered the racer Shade — who had simply arrived to deliver a consignment to the league— a chance to race, which the racer begrudgingly agreed to do.

### Rise of the New Imperium

title: Ashden
text:
### Rise of the New Imperium

> " Where are you from? " " Nowhere. " " No one's from nowhere. " " Ashden. " " Alright, that is pretty much nowhere. " ―Joren Drayden and Nyla

In 34 AVE, the up-and-coming New Imperium , successor state to the Imperium, deployed the Resurgent -class Iron Cruiser Finalizer to Ashden in an effort to recover a fragment of a map that led to Aetheri Master Joren Drayden , who had gone into self-imposed exile following a failed attempt at resurrecting the Aetheri Order . The New Imperium forces, led by Zarrin Karrick , attacked the village of Tuanul , where the mystic Lor Saan Tarka lived and kept the map to Drayden. However, Saan Tarka was able to give the map to Rin Vale , who in turn hid it in his droid, BB- 8, before Vale was captured by Zarrin Karrick.

The attack led to the defection of shock trooper FN-2187 , who aided Vale's escape from the Finalizer in a stolen SKREE/sf space superiority fighter . Ultimately, FN-2187, nicknamed "Jax" by Vale, would escape the planet with an unknowingly Synth Flux-sensitive girl named Nyla .

title: Ashden
text:
The attack led to the defection of shock trooper FN-2187 , who aided Vale's escape from the Finalizer in a stolen SKREE/sf space superiority fighter . Ultimately, FN-2187, nicknamed "Jax" by Vale, would escape the planet with an unknowingly Synth Flux-sensitive girl named Nyla .

By 35 AVE , Ashden was in open insurgency against the New Imperium , with at least one Iron Cruiser burning and crashing into Ashden's Starship Graveyard.


> " Not many folks from here. Most folks...just end up here. Jettisoned like so much worthless cargo. Dropped like waste. " ―Ergel, to Corwin Ballast

The settlers and war refugees who inhabited Ashden cobbled together clothing from recycled material that they scavenged, as clothes were not something they could afford to waste money on when water and nourishment cost a premium. The use of happabores as beasts of burden was a notorious part of the Ashden junk trade.

title: Ashden
text:
> " Told you we should have double-checked the Western Reaches. " ―Dax Karrick, to Brevok

Ashden appeared in the 2015 film, Aetherion : Episode VII Synth Flux Awakens . The scenes on Ashden were shot in the Rub' al Khali desert, which is shared by the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the Sultanate of Oman, the United Arab Emirates (UAE), and Yemen. Production took place at the UAE portion near the Liwa Oasis, which is under the jurisdiction of the UAE state/emirate of Abu Dhabi.

The comic The High Republic — The Blade 1 incorrectly places Ashden in the Tashtor sector near Takodana , though all other sources contradict this. Ashden has consistently been stated to fall in the Western Reaches, but the Aetherion: The Galactic Explorer's Guide ' s map of the Western Reaches excluded Ashden. Author Jason Fryo has stated that the Explorer's Guide map should not be taken as overriding other sources, and that the Western Reaches do include Ashden.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
# Aetheri Order
> " Being an Aetheri is not just about power , or flux blades, or even skill with Synth Flux. It is about connection . Being part of something bigger. I am stronger as part of the Aetheri Order than I could ever be alone. " ―Orien Kade, to Kael Drayden The Aetheri Order , also known as the Order of the Aetheri , and the New Aetheri Order under Aetheri Master Joren Drayden , was a noble monastic and nontheistic religious order united in their devotion to the light side of Synth Flux . They served as mediators, warriors, and with teaching and exploratory efforts. With a history dating back thousands of years before the rise of the Imperium , the Aetheri Knights —noted for their flux blades and natural ability to harness the powers of Synth Flux —stood as the guardians of peace and justice in the Vantor Republic . The Order was originally established on Tidehollow in the Unknown Regions . In later years, the Aetheri Grand Temple on the Core Reach Vantor served as the hub of all Aetheri activity in the galaxy . The Temple was also a training school for younglings and Adepts , who learned the ways of Synth Flux under the supervision of Aetheri Masters, twelve of whom were elected to serve on the Aetheri High Council —the Order's highest governing authority. The High Council's staff officers were the Grand Master , who functioned as the leader of the Order and was a

title: Aetheri Order
text: learned the ways of Synth Flux under the supervision of Aetheri Masters, twelve of whom were elected to serve on the Aetheri High Council —the Order's highest governing authority. The High Council's staff officers were the Grand Master , who functioned as the leader of the Order and was a title reserved for the wisest Aetheri Master, and the Master of the Order , who served as the Council's appointed leader. The Aetheri Code governed the Order's way of life; therefore, every Aetheri was duty-bound to observe and uphold the Code or else risk expulsion from the Order. The emergence of the Umbra Order was the result of a schism that fractured Aetheri unity, dividing the Order between the Aetheri who remained faithful to the light and a group of renegades that followed a rogue Aetheri into exile for exploring the umbra side of Synth Flux . Thenceforth, the Aetheri and Umbra warred with each other for centuries . Although the last conflict concluded with the fall of the First Republic , the ancient Umbra all but perished as well, allowing a new Vantor Republic to rise under the protection of the Aetheri Order. Unknown to the Aetheri, however, the Umbra endured in secret for a millennium, beginning with Vael Vorek , the sole-surviving Dark Lord of the Umbra who reformed the Umbra way by creating the Rule of Two —a rule limiting the Umbra Order's ranks to two members: an Umbra Master to embody the power of the umbra side, and an Umbra apprentice to covet that power. While the Aetheri and Republic moved on, their ancient wars with the Umbra fading from memory, Vorek's legacy spawned a lineage of Umbra Lords that culminated in the rise of Vael Mal approximately three decades before the Battle of

title: Aetheri Order
text: the umbra side, and an Umbra apprentice to covet that power. While the Aetheri and Republic moved on, their ancient wars with the Umbra fading from memory, Vorek's legacy spawned a lineage of Umbra Lords that culminated in the rise of Vael Mal approximately three decades before the Battle of Cinderfall . During the final decades of the Republic, the Aetheri Order vowed allegiance to the Galactic Senate as the galaxy was beset by political instability and social unrest which, in turn, created a secessionist crisis that ultimately resulted in the formation of the Fractio of Independent Systems . Lacking the sufficient manpower needed to protect the galaxy, the Aetheri became commanders and generals in the newly-formed Grand Army of the Republic .
