For roughly three years they commanded armies of replica troopers in a conflict known as the Replica Wars , engaging the Fractio's battle droid forces led by Count Varek —a former Aetheri Master who became an Umbra Lord —and the cybernetic warlord General Skarn . Though the Aetheri fought to preserve the Republic, the government they served was secretly taken over by Mal who, as Senator Theron Mal of Ondara , rose to power in the Senate and became the last Supreme Chancellor of the Republic. The Aetheri were unknowingly being deceived by the Umbra.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Chancellor's deceptions and machinations culminated in the execution of Directive 66 , a secret protocol that forcibly turned the Aetheri's replica soldiers against them, leading to an all but total extermination of the Aetheri Order. With most of the Aetheri eliminated, Mal supplanted a thousand years of democracy with a new government known as the Imperium. In addition, Mal succeeded in manipulating Kael Drayden —the prophesied Seeded One who was destined to bring balance to Synth Flux by destroying the Umbra—to betray the Aetheri and join the umbra side, with Mal renaming him Xarn Velgor. As an Umbra Lord, the former Aetheri Knight served the self-proclaimed Galactic Emperor by hunting down the few surviving Aetheri, who had gone into hiding across the galaxy. In spite of the Umbra's efforts, however, the Aetheri continued to endure. Within a generation of the Imperium's rise to power, Orien Kade and Zho —both of whom survived the initial purge of the Order—trained Velgor's son, Joren Drayden, in the Aetheri arts. Joren would later redeem his father, causing the redeemed Kael Drayden to return to the light and fulfill his destiny as the Seeded One, destroying both himself and his Master during the Battle

title: Aetheri Order
text: of whom survived the initial purge of the Order—trained Velgor's son, Joren Drayden, in the Aetheri arts. Joren would later redeem his father, causing the redeemed Kael Drayden to return to the light and fulfill his destiny as the Seeded One, destroying both himself and his Master during the Battle of Mossfell . The Imperium dissolved into various remnants as a result of their defeat in the Galactic Civil War , allowing the Alliance to Restore the Republic to rise as the Concordat . Under the new era , Joren Drayden endeavored to rebuild the Order by training a new generation of Aetheri. Among Drayden's students was his nephew, Beno Karrick , the son of his twin sister, Princess Elira Solen , and the famed smuggler Dax Karrick . Beno, however, was seduced by the umbra side of Synth Flux at the coaxing of Vorr , an enigmatic figure who spearheaded the Imperial-inspired New Imperium . Joren confronted and frightened Beno, who fought back and fled. As a result, Beno adopted the name and persona of Zarrin Karrick, a New Imperium warlord and master of the Knights of Karrick .

title: Aetheri Order
text: The new generation was betrayed and destroyed by Karrick, who left the Aetheri training temple burning by the time Drayden recovered from the attack. Feeling responsible for Beno's fall and the massacre of his apprentices, he went into exile and disappeared from the galaxy, leaving only traces of his location on a star map . The New Imperium and the Coalition both sought to acquire the map, but ultimately it was the latter that succeeded due to the actions of the Ashden scavenger Nyla . She followed the map to the planet Tidehollow , where the last Aetheri had taken refuge in the first Aetheri Sanctum .

title: Aetheri Order
text: Drayden, stricken by grief and believing his return would only cause more problems, was reluctant to train Nyla or another generation of Aetheri. However, the last Aetheri eventually returned to the fight, buying time for the Coalition to escape the siege of Saltmark led by Zarrin Karrick, who became the new Supreme Leader after killing his master , Vorr. Drayden became one with Synth Flux after exerting a great amount of energy to project himself across the galaxy to face his fallen nephew, but not before acknowledging that he would not be the last Aetheri. His heroic tale spread across the galaxy, inspiring others and giving hope in a time of rising darkness .

title: Aetheri Order
text: Having returned from death, Vael Mal urged Zarrin Karrick to end the Aetheri Order by killing Nyla, who was his granddaughter . After Karrick renounced the umbra side, Mal attempted to turn Nyla until he discovered her bond with Beno Karrick. Realizing they were a dyad in Synth Flux , Mal nearly drained them of their life synth flux to regain his full power. Though weakened by Mal’ attack, Nyla was strengthened by the spirits of past Aetheri, allowing the apprentice to stand against the Dark Lord of the Umbra. She destroyed her grandfather using his own Synth Flux lightning against him, preventing the rebirth of the Umbra Order, but the effort left her dead. Karrick resurrected her at the cost of his life, becoming one with Synth Flux as the last Drayden. The Draydens were gone, but their legacy endured through Nyla, who took the Drayden name to honor her mentors and restore the Aetheri Order.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Overview

> " The Order tends to be what it needs to be for any particular time. Sometimes, we're warriors, fighting the forces of evil. Sometimes, we govern. Sometimes, we do the opposite—drawing inward, studying Synth Flux and its mysteries. Sometimes, we explore. Sometimes, we do all of those things. And sometimes… We are carved down to almost nothing. Those who are left must bear the responsibility of being one last bit of light in a galaxy filled with endless dark. " ―Elzar Mann, to Joren Drayden The Aetheri Knights were a noble order of Synth Flux-sensitive protectors—united by their ability to use Synth Flux —who upheld peace and justice in the Vantor Republic for over a thousand generations, carrying out what they sensed to be the will of Synth Flux as its instruments. As keepers of the peace , the Aetheri Order —also referred to as the Order of the Aetheri —undertook diplomatic missions on behalf of the Galactic Senate , and pursued interplanetary criminals across the galaxy . Whereas the Umbra —the historic enemies of the Aetheri Order—harnessed the umbra side of Synth Flux for power, the Aetheri followed the ways of the light side of Synth Flux . The Aetheri Code , along with a collection of other foundational texts , guided the Aetheri way of life, governing the behavior of individual Aetheri to the philosophy and training regimen of the Order as a whole. Though the Aetheri worshipped no specific deity , the Seeded One played an important role in Aetheri prophecy and mythology. According to Adept Matthea Cathley , the Aetheri worked better as a group instead of on their own; indeed, Aetheri Knight Orien Kade once reflected that, as part of

title: Aetheri Order
text: whole. Though the Aetheri worshipped no specific deity , the Seeded One played an important role in Aetheri prophecy and mythology. According to Adept Matthea Cathley , the Aetheri worked better as a group instead of on their own; indeed, Aetheri Knight Orien Kade once reflected that, as part of the Order, he was stronger than if he was on his own. The virtues of the Order included compassion, generosity, peaceful resolution, and spreading justice. As spelled out directly in one version of the Aetheri Code, an Aetheri was not supposed to act in pursuit of personal power or wealth, instead acting only with the goals of finding knowledge and enlightenment. Further Aetheri goals included finding balance and protecting others in a just fashion as part of a selfless quest to aid their fellow beings. Nonetheless, Aetheri needed to understand they were, like all people, imperfect and needed to always learn to be better. Like anyone, an Aetheri could also be scared, but an Aetheri was supposed to not run from their fears or let those fears consume them, instead facing those fears directly and remaining confident in the knowledge Synth Flux was with them. In short, their duties as servants of light and the Republic could be summed up as teachers, explorers, diplomats, and warriors.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Aetheri were instructed in the ways of the Order and Synth Flux; as their knowledge grew, each member progressed through several different ranks. With the exception of Kael Drayden , prospective Aetheri were identified a short time after birth by the quantity of synthcells in their blood , a factor which indicated the level of a subject's Synth Flux-sensitivity. Many of these children were listed within Aetheri reliquaries before being identified by the Order. Training began at the level of the Aetheri Initiate ; at some point in their training, younglings were expected to find their own Kyber crystal —the heart of the flux blade , a distinctive and elegant weapon of the Aetheri —in order to pass an ancient rite of passage known as The Gathering .

title: Aetheri Order
text: Younglings who succeeded in their trials graduated to the level of Adept, the apprentice of a more experienced member of the Order. In accordance with the Aetheri Code, a Master could instruct only one student in the ways of Synth Flux at any given time. The Adept braid , a symbol that represented an Aetheri apprentice's status in the Order, was worn in the hair or head, depending on the Adept's species . The braid was removed when an Adept ascended to the rank of Aetheri Knight or in the case of banishment from the Order's ranks. The Aetheri Trials were a series of tests that ultimately determined whether an Adept was worthy of the rank of Aetheri Knight. After becoming a full-fledged member of the Order, an Aetheri could choose to adopt an Adept of their own as part of the Order's tradition in training the next generation of Aetheri. Teaching the ways of Synth Flux to the next generation of Aetheri was considered one of the greatest honors in the Order, its existence and traditions perpetuated through "a cycle of training and education." The Eye of the Nullkin , Marchion Ro , believed that being structured into an order gave Aetheri an advantage; in addition to tapping into Synth Flux, any Aetheri could tap into their Order to find confidence and structure. Being part of a united group made it so individual Aetheri were willing to make large–scale decisions, which they believed would spread their light throughout the galaxy. In effect, an Aetheri was not merely strong and bold because they could use Synth Flux. Instead, being part of the overall Aetheri Order helped them grow to embody those traits.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
The most powerful and legendary Aetheri held the rank of Aetheri Master once they had proven themself worthy of the independence and station granted by the title. Again with the exception of Drayden, the Aetheri High Council —the highest governing body of the Order —consisted of Masters throughout the history of the Order. Among the High Council, the title of Grand Master was conferred on the oldest and wisest member of their group, while the Council's leadership rested with the Master of the Order .

The Aetheri Order in its capacity as a peacekeeping synth flux of the Republic vowed allegiance to the Galactic Senate and democracy . As an "extension" of the Republic's Judiciary branch , the Order was under the legal jurisdiction of the Senate, and as leader of the Senate, the Supreme Chancellor had the privilege to make requests of the Order. However, this prerogative did not give the chancellor direct authority over the Order, which was legally under senatorial oversight. According to Theron Mal , the Office of the Chancellor would become a dictatorship if the Order was forced to comply with orders from the Republic head of state.

### Locations

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Locations

> " The most famous of the Aetheri temples, located on Vantor, served as the home of the Aetheri High Council and the vast library of data known as the Aetheri Archives. " ―Joren Drayden

Aetheri temples served as places of worship, training schools, and repositories of knowledge for the Aetheri Order. The first Aetheri Sanctum was built atop a sacred island on Tidehollow tens of thousands of years before the New Imperium-Coalition War . The temple rose high above the surrounding sea, and was worn down by erosion and time. Some signs of its past remained, however, such as mosaics and an ancient meditation ledge. One such mosaic depicted the Prime Aetheri in a state of meditation; the same mosaic symbolized the nature of Synth Flux as a duality between the umbra side and the light.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Aetheri Order made its home in the Aetheri Grand Temple on Vantor , the capital world of the Vantor Republic. Over the millennia, the Temple served as the central hub of all Aetheri activities in the galaxy; it was a school, a monastery, and the headquarters of the Aetheri High Council. As a school, the Temple was the largest active Aetheri training center in the galaxy where younglings trained to become Adepts and ultimately full-fledged Aetheri Knights. The Aetheri Archives , the source of all knowledge accumulated by the Order, was located inside of the Temple. As the symbol of the Order, the Temple signified the Order's status in galactic affairs. While access to the Temple was not restricted to just the Aetheri, all non-Aetheri personnel were required to undergo compulsory entry tests before becoming employed at the Temple. Those who worked in the Temple often dedicated their whole life to serving the Order. Having sustained extensive damage during the fall of the Aetheri, the Temple was renovated and renamed as the Imperial Palace, with only the original structure's corpse and five skyscraping towers remaining intact. In addition to the Temple on Vantor, the Order maintained several ancient temples spread across the galaxy. Aetheri understood they were connected to the entire galaxy through their Order, seeing the galaxy itself as their home instead of a singular location as deserving that term.

title: Aetheri Order
text: One ancient temple was located on Lorath , and was only accessible if both the Master and Adept were present. The Lorath temple was where Adepts were sent to confront their fear without the support of the Masters, some of whom ultimately died while waiting for their students who never returned, leaving the temple's antechambers littered with their skeletal remains. Other Aetheri enclaves included the Temple of Eedit on Devaron , the Temple of Vrogas Vas , and the Temple of Ilum where younglings were sent to participate in The Gathering. The Aetheri Order established smaller outposts at various locations around the galaxy, including one on Elphrona . These outposts dated as far back as the High Republic Era and the great Aetheri spread across the galaxy that saw them work alongside various communities. It contained various artifacts that were important to the history of the Aetheri.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
While Ilum was regarded as the most sacred planet to the Aetheri Order, the desert moon Embermoor —a holy site and home to one of the first civilizations that explored the nature of Synth Flux —was considered a spiritual home of the Aetheri. Like Ilum, Embermoor contained the kyber crystals that the Aetheri used to create their flux blade. It was also a holy site for pilgrims throughout the galaxy, who sought spiritual guidance in the Holy City of Embermoor. At one time it was an important world to the Aetheri. A number of Aetheri sites could also be found on the planets Tython and Ossus , such as the Aetheri Sanctum of Tython or the First Temple on Ossus. The Aetheri maintained a connection to Tython, and one of their sacred texts described "notable beasts of Tython." Ossus was also the location of the Great Aetheri Library , which was destroyed before the Replica Wars and in complete ruins by the time of its rediscovery by Joren Drayden . Despite this, Drayden still located an original copy of the Rammahgon , one of the sacred Aetheri texts, on the planet. During the Concordat Era , the Aetheri Sanctum of Joren Drayden was constructed on Ossus with the goal of becoming a "great school" for future generations of students in the restored Aetheri Order.

### General perception

#### Different traditions over time

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### General perception

#### Different traditions over time

With the galaxy changing as new threats emerged, the Aetheri Order took on many forms and traditions over its life in its mission to fight those threats. As such, the particular way members of the Aetheri Order interpreted the current form of its ideals impacted the way they interacted with the galactic population. The High Republic Era was a time of greatly expanded Aetheri activity, and the Order had many outposts throughout the galaxy. The Vantor Republic relied heavily on their role as guardians of peace and justice, to settle disputes through peaceful ways, to protect planetary leaders and senators. With the Republic's rapid expansion and the Order's role in protecting that effort, the Aetheri also established many new temples across the Outer Reach, keeping the buildings in line with the planetary cultures they found themselves in. With many Aetheri living amongst these communities through such temples or while out on their mission, the Aetheri learned local customs and truly became part of the cultures they protected.

title: Aetheri Order
text: By the time of the late Republic Era, the Order found itself shifting its focus more onto the galactic scale of the responsibilities required of the Order. In this era, the Aetheri were more likely to focus on and spend their time on the galactic astropolitical scene and the bigger questions: stopping menaces, some before they even developed, and saving whole star systems at a time. Knowing that their decisions affected billions of lives, the Aetheri Council regularly sent out Knights to report on the state of the various parts of the galaxy. However, as their duties amounted, several Aetheri outposts were shut down to direct resources where the Republic needed the Aetheri the most, and their withdrawal caused many people to abandon the settlements grown around the presence of the Order.

title: Aetheri Order
text: While Aetheri Sentinels still existed and made it their duty to work with the everyday people of the galaxy, Aetheri Knights found it increasingly difficult to find time for personal interaction with the people of the galaxy, with many young Aetheri often forgetting that concerns that seemed small on a galactic level were often huge for the individual. That was despite Master Zho and other Council members' efforts to teach them to pay attention to the present and where they are. In effect, the Aetheri Order grew increasingly isolated from the galaxy at large, much to the concern of Aetheri Master Sorin Vael, due to its shrinking number of outposts.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Focusing on galactic issues instead of remaining on a smaller scale, the Aetheri thus were focused more and more on the future of the Republic. Secluded from the galaxy at large due to its headquarters on Vantor, the Aetheri Order was left adrift, not only because of its isolation but also how it had become heedless of strange changes within Synth Flux. While the Aetheri still cared about the galaxy, the Aetheri, compared to what they were before, stayed locked away in their shrinking number of temples, instead of remaining a part of local communities as they had in the High Republic Era. Vael and Master Zho feared that, since many people of the galaxy saw and interacted with Aetheri Knights less and less, they might start to believe or could be made to believe that the Order ceased to care about them. What with many of the Order's other outposts being shut down while the Temple on Vantor remained, Vael pondered if the Order's headquarters sitting on Vantor was a problem, reasoning it made them look like Republic warriors. While Zho warned him that the Council would not agree with his concerns about Vantor, Vael even feared the Aetheri

title: Aetheri Order
text:
outposts being shut down while the Temple on Vantor remained, Vael pondered if the Order's headquarters sitting on Vantor was a problem, reasoning it made them look like Republic warriors. While Zho warned him that the Council would not agree with his concerns about Vantor, Vael even feared the Aetheri themselves could fall into that viewpoint and lose the true meaning of what it meant to be an Aetheri. During the High Republic Era, the Order and the Aetheri Council enabled Aetheri who were drawn to solitary action to become " Wayseekers "—Aetheri who operated outside of the dictates of the Council to instead follow Synth Flux on their own terms. Such a position was seemingly not permitted in the late Republic Era due to the defiance it showed towards the council. Wayseekers were still bound to the values of the Order, so their abilities and skills could not be used in the pursuit of selfish concerns.

Although they were not eager to be soldiers , the Aetheri many times found that other skills were not enough and so their role was to fight, indeed this was understood in the High Republic as a vital, though unfortunate role of an Aetheri. They took military actions against the Umbra, lead soldiers against the Nullkin, and in the last years of the Republic reprised this office, became generals of the Republic Military and fighting in the Replica Wars. Even after the fall of the Order, Aetheri like Joren Drayden and Nyla fought the darkness as the edge of the powers that opposed tyranny.

#### Letting go

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### Letting go

> " Strong passions are something we try to control within ourselves, as emotions can cloud our judgment, especially in stressful situations. They can blind us to the truth, and to the leading of Synth Flux. That said, it would be foolish to suggest that an Aetheri has no desires or interests. In fact, I would go so far as to say that it would be dangerous, leading only to complacency. Yes, I have a passion for learning and teaching. It is part of who I am. But I am also prepared to set such things aside at a moment's notice. My 'passions' must never be greater than my mission. " ―Master Stellan Gios

title: Aetheri Order
text: Aetheri Knights of all eras adhered to the Aetheri Code, however, there were debates on how to follow its doctrines, and many Aetheri developed their own personal understanding of them. One major concept was that of avoiding attachments, but different Aetheri expressed different understandings of that rule. Adept Kevmo Zink explained that the overall idea behind avoiding attachments was inspired by the Aetheri Order's mission to Synth Flux; if an Aetheri was truly expected to work for the good of the entire galaxy, they could not tie themself down with one attachment, such as a romantic relationship with another being.

title: Aetheri Order
text: If an Aetheri did form such an attachment, the Order believed that the Aetheri would not be as ready to spread the ideals of the light side across the galaxy because of the relationship, which the Order taught would be a distraction. It was hoped an Aetheri Knight would only be bound to Synth Flux and the Aetheri Sanctum. High Republic Era Aetheri Master Stellan Gios explained that the Aetheri tried to control their strong passions because the emotions one felt for those passions could cloud their judgement, particularly during a stressful moment. Still, he said it was wrong to deny that Aetheri like himself had their own interests and desires; the task of an Aetheri, he reasoned, was to not let those passions take control of their being. As late Republic Era Rael Averross reasoned, the text of the Aetheri Code forbade strong attachments that divided one's loyalties and compromised their emotions. As such, he further reasoned that a casual physical relationship—which he enjoyed with a woman named Selbie —was only breaking the "letter" of the Aetheri Code, not its actual binding spirit. While Averross's actions shocked his fellow Aetheri Master Sorin Vael , Averross defended himself and pointed

title: Aetheri Order
text: compromised their emotions. As such, he further reasoned that a casual physical relationship—which he enjoyed with a woman named Selbie —was only breaking the "letter" of the Aetheri Code, not its actual binding spirit. While Averross's actions shocked his fellow Aetheri Master Sorin Vael , Averross defended himself and pointed out how Vael had made an actual violation of the Aetheri Code in his past via a relationship with an individual , much to Vael's pain. Vael himself maintained fond memories of that past relationship despite having moved on to continue his life as an Aetheri. During the High Republic Era, according to Master Kantam Syra 's viewpoint, there were many Aetheri who twisted the notion non-attachment; to Syra, those who spoke of suppressing emotions, forsaking love and trying to numb themselves to discomfort were twisting Aetheri teachings. Aetheri like Syra and Grand Master Zho taught non-attachment or detachment, just like love, was to let go of something or someone when the time called for it, instead of allowing oneself to be ruled by the need to possess. Indeed, close friendships were respected and valued throughout the Aetheri Order, but an Aetheri needed to understand they could lose those they cared for and thus would need to let go, instead of letting their grief consume them.

title: Aetheri Order
text: That belief tied into the Aetheri Order's beliefs on death; according to the Aetheri, an individual became one with Synth Flux upon death because they transferred into the Cosmic Synth Flux , which, in turn, generated the Living Synth Flux . As High Republic Era Aetheri Master Obratuk Glii explained, he was still allowed to miss his former apprentices, but he knew they were still with him through Synth Flux, generating a joy within him that his fellows had become part of Synth Flux. Furthermore, he declared it meant he could not be scared of his own mortality. As selfless defenders of peace and justice, Aetheri were also willing to lay down their own lives in defense of others and did not fear death. Instead, an Aetheri was supposed to always put the needs of other people before their own needs. While Glii's commentary argued that Aetheri could grieve to a certain degree so long as it did not consume them, Adept Matthea Cathley, who also lived during the High Republic Era, once thought to herself that Aetheri did not grieve, but her thought was based in the understanding of not losing oneself to attachment over a deceased individual. Even

title: Aetheri Order
text: a certain degree so long as it did not consume them, Adept Matthea Cathley, who also lived during the High Republic Era, once thought to herself that Aetheri did not grieve, but her thought was based in the understanding of not losing oneself to attachment over a deceased individual. Even then, she noted not grieving was hard in practice. Cathley also once claimed that Aetheri did not get scared, but she later accepted that, like everyone, Aetheri did indeed have fears and they needed to face them; as she put it, there was no shame in admitting when she was scared, but it was her duty to face whatever spawned that fear.

title: Aetheri Order
text: As such, an Aetheri needed to be careful with their relationships so as to not let attachment, and the naturally ensuing fear of losing those attachments, consume them. It was not that an Aetheri was not allowed to feel romantic love, as it was understood such feelings were natural, but an Aetheri were not supposed to enter into a romantic relationship. It was essential for an Aetheri Knight to make the right choice for the Order and not neglect their Aetheri duties in the favor of their beloved, even if that would mean the end of the relationship. As Zink explained, an Aetheri was able to use Synth Flux to direct themselves through the tides of strong emotions and learn what the underlining motivations of those feelings were. With that, an Aetheri would not be ruled by their passions, but instead could make tactical decisions with a better understanding of their own mindset.

title: Aetheri Order
text: For some outsiders, as such, the Aetheri teaching on the matter often misinterpreted, believed the Aetheri to be distant and seemingly unconcerned about the lives of those they were to protect and that "love" was forbidden for an Aetheri. The actions of some emotionally distant Aetheri Knights did little to help that misconception: during the days of the High Republic, an Aetheri Knight saved the lives of a starship crew, including the young Axel Greylark , but needed to drag the badly injured boy away from his father , trapped under the rubble, thus leaving him behind. The Aetheri told him that what happened was the will of Synth Flux, something that left Greylark baffled. Years later, when he recounted the incident to Aetheri Knight Gella Nattai and how the Knight later forgot his face, he concluded that one grieving boy in a galaxy full of them was nothing, but Nattai affirmed to Greylark that one grieving boy was everything.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Aetheri of the High Republic Era displayed a great deal of emotional openness to those grieving or upset —showing it in actions like offering a hug. During the waning decades of the Republic, compassion was still meant to be central to an Aetheri's life, with the non-attachment rule defined in theory as someone not meant to fearfully grasp on things and beings in a universe ruled by change. However, the actions of an Aetheri appearing not to care could damage the entire Order's reputation or result in that Aetheri failing to help someone who needed support. Aetheri Knight Iskat Vekkis found a lack of support amongst the Aetheri as she grappled with her insecurities during the late Republic Era.

title: Aetheri Order
text: During the Replica Wars, amid an incident on Vantor in which the Aetheri attempted to recapture the Grak crime lord Ziro Desilijic Tiure , an Aetheri was forced to redirect a transport to ensure it avoided hitting a platform of people, but the redirected ship instead crashed into the Martez family apartment. Two children— Trayk and Ravin Martez —became orphans in the incident with the demise of their parents in the crash. The Aetheri in question then failed to properly explain herself in a compassionate matter, trying to assure both that she had needed to make a choice but that Synth Flux would still be with them, a phrase that meant nothing to the two girls.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Joren Drayden affirmed the Aetheri Order's commitment to non-attachment since the early days of his efforts to rebuild it. However, he also told his sister, Elira Solen , that she could still be married to Dax Karrick if she joined the Order. Due to his unorthodox training in the Aetheri arts, Drayden sought to provide the next generation of Aetheri with a more conventional path to knighthood. As the last Aetheri of his era, Drayden found comfort through adherence to the Aetheri way, having largely isolated himself from his friends while rebuilding the Order. In addition, the Armorer —a Ferrik who was familiar with Aetheri history—stated that the Aetheri were required to sacrifice personal attachments in order to master the ways of Synth Flux. While in the process of training Pip , Drayden informed his apprentice that giving into attachments to those whom he loved was to forsake the way of the Aetheri.

#### Views on the flux blade

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### Views on the flux blade

> " I realized something. Something important. A Aetheri isn't his flux blade. A flux blade is just a tool. A Aetheri is someone who uses Synth Flux to bring light to the galaxy. To protect people and push back darkness. That particular flux blade… the one I lost… I don't need it. It was my father's… but I'm not sure how I feel about that anymore. I'm going to be an Aetheri. Even if I never see that flux blade again. " ―Joren Drayden During the history of the Aetheri Order, the flux blade considered to be the Aetheri's only true ally in battle. Beyond its existence as a weapon, however, the flux blade was a symbol of care to the Aetheri; as explained by Aetheri Knight Orien Kade, the blade represented the care with which they approached and wielded their gifts, further serving as a message to their opponents and representing something that needed great skill and training to wield. In choosing a rather limited weapon, Kade explained, the flux blade was also the symbol of their role and duty as protectors, not destroyers. Further reasoned by Kade to be a tool that showed the Aetheri could be more powerful but openly chose not to be, the flux blade represented an Aetheri's duty to stand tall against darkness. While the phrase "this weapon is your life" was popular during the late Republic Era, an Aetheri—as exemplified by the High Republic Era and Kade's speech —needed to be more than their flux blade. Indeed, after the Order's fall, Joren Drayden came to realize that an Aetheri was not their flux blade and instead the duty he was tasked with was something beyond a single

title: Aetheri Order
text: an Aetheri—as exemplified by the High Republic Era and Kade's speech —needed to be more than their flux blade. Indeed, after the Order's fall, Joren Drayden came to realize that an Aetheri was not their flux blade and instead the duty he was tasked with was something beyond a single weapon. Faced with either needing to rescue his friend Elira Solen or continue looking for his flux blade on Aether Spire , Drayden came to his decision and left to help his friend. The High Republic Era would also see a greater variance in flux blade color and hilt design than the Aetheri of the late Republic. During the late Republic era, Aetheri largely wielded blue or green flux blades with simple silver hilts. A shift in flux blade design could be seen in the High Republic Era: the Nullkin conflict saw the Aetheri Order implement the Guardian Protocols and prepare for greater conflict, during which the High Council knew Aetheri could lose their blade and be forced to quickly replace it. Rather than have Aetheri spend time building elaborated hilts, the Council reasoned that speed and effectiveness was of the essence and that a ready supply of flux blades was something the Order needed. As such, the Council ordered Aetheri to only construct battle blades , hilts with a simple design like those seen in the late Republic Era. Even then, Aetheri active in the later High Republic Era still had a wider variance in flux blade color than the blue and green-filled Order of the late Republic. While each individual Aetheri built their own flux blade as a youngling to their own specifications, allowing for a degree of individuality in hilt

title: Aetheri Order
text:
active in the later High Republic Era still had a wider variance in flux blade color than the blue and green-filled Order of the late Republic. While each individual Aetheri built their own flux blade as a youngling to their own specifications, allowing for a degree of individuality in hilt design even during the late Republic Era, groupings of Aetheri of that time were largely defined by cylindrical silver hilts of an overall similar design, with those hilts mainly producing green or blue blades. #### Who gets to join

> " Wait— you mean, I can be an Aetheri? " " Study you should, the Farseeker Lyr. No great power had he, yet from his ink sprang some of the Aetheri's greatest texts. For though the Aetheri and Synth Flux are one, Synth Flux is not what an Aetheri makes. " " Then what makes an Aetheri? " " That is something only you can answer. " ―Lohim Nara and Zho during the High Republic Era

title: Aetheri Order
text: During the High Republic Era, when the young boy Lohim Nara spoke to Grand Master Zho about his life-long desire to join the Order, he confessed that he had faked his Synth Flux-sensitivity and synthcell count, but Zho told the boy of how Synth Flux was not the sole answer to what an Aetheri was. Zho spoke of how Synth Flux existed in all life forms and how, if he wanted to be someone worthy of the name Aetheri, he could not dwell on what he did not have. He also told the boy not to worry about being "too old" to become a youngling, stating that he was still learning at over six hundred years old. While Zho seemed to admit the boy could not be an Aetheri Knight due to his age, he noted that other professions helped the Order and offered him a role as a guardian of the Temple after Nara realized he had a mentor in Reina Bilass .

title: Aetheri Order
text: However, later in its history, the Order proved reluctant but willing to bend their rules as the death of Aetheri Master Sorin Vael and return of Umbra convinced the Council to allow the young Kael Drayden to be trained, despite he was initially deemed too old. Decades later, Zho also chose to take Joren Drayden as his apprentice after initially pointing out how old he was. Alternatively, the Order of the High Republic also became a home for the young Synth Flux-sensitive Zeen Mrala , who did not train as an Aetheri but became close to many Adepts and, despite Aetheri regulations forbidding its members from engaging in romance, fell in love with Adept Lula Talisola . Despite not being an Aetheri, she was welcomed to train with the Adepts and their masters, with Talisola's master Kantam Syra helping her to control her anger. Later, in order to find and save Talisola, Mrala realized that she was willing to join the ranks of the Aetheri despite her age, although her realization came from how she figured certain Aetheri rules would be bent due to the evolving Nullkin conflict.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
The High Republic Era Order also maintained close ties with other Synth Flux orders, working as part of the Convocation of Synth Flux on Embermoor. Through its ties to other orders, the Aetheri brought rescued children who were "too old" to be trained as Aetheri to Embermoor, where they were taken in by other faiths. In the late Republic Era, the Aetheri continued to help orphans find new homes, but there were instances where they failed to do so because of local law or their own non-attachment rule going so far it blurred the line between non-attachment and apathy, such as when an Aetheri of the late Republic Era left Trayk and Ravin Martez on their own after the deaths of their parents. Beyond those deaths being an indirect result of the Aetheri's own actions, the Aetheri's apparent lack of concern and the fact they simply left the two girls on their own created a distaste in both girls towards the Aetheri Order, on whom they did not want to depend upon.

#### Leaving the Order

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### Leaving the Order

> " The Aetheri have been my family since I was a child, the Temple my home. But my future lies here, on Sireno […] I am the heir of Sireno. I will rebuild this planet, make it stronger. Not for the Republic. And not for the Aetheri. But for the people. My people. I ask for you, and the Council, to respect my decision in this matter. " " Hm. Saddened by your decision we are, but honor it we will. " " Thank you. I will surrender my flux blade to Master Kostana. " " No. Necessary that will not be. " " It is the weapon of an Aetheri. " " Which is why keep it you must. More than a name, an Aetheri is. More than a title. Strong in Synth Flux, you are. Guide you, it will. Guide us all, it must. " ―Varek speaks to Zho about his decision

title: Aetheri Order
text: While Grand Master Zho once declared in the late Republic Era that an Aetheri leaving the Order was a failure on the Order's part to keep that Aetheri where they belonged, Aetheri were permitted to leave the Aetheri Order whenever they so chose without punishment, with Zho accepting that fact, even if an Aetheri leaving might sadden him. Should they feel it to be their calling, a former Aetheri was even permitted to return to the Order. During the High Republic Era, one of Zho's Adepts, Kantam Syra, walked away from the Aetheri for over a year before returning when they met their soon-to-be Adept Lula Talisola , who made Syra believe their place was with the Order. Aetheri Master Cohmac Vitus was surprised Zho would allow his Adept to do a walkaway from the Order, but Syra believed Zho knew it was necessary for them to find their place in the Order, with Syra at the time also thinking Zho had seen it coming and thus was why he had held off on their Knighting.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Twenty Aetheri Masters who departed the Order became known as the " Lost Twenty " and were commemorated by busts located in the Aetheri Archives of the Temple. Zho believed the Lost needed to be remembered and honored, which enabled the Aetheri to learn from the failings that caused them to depart. Still, he advised the Aetheri not to live in the past just because prior members had departed. The twentieth of the Lost was Varek , a former Adept of Zho who departed in 42 BVE over issues with the Aetheri and Republic. Despite his departure, Varek was allowed to visit the Temple on Vantor, continued to have access to its Archives, and was even allowed to retain possession of his flux blade, with Zho reasoning being an Aetheri was more than a title and thus the weapon would still be of use to him.

#### Public image

Aetheri unite for peace

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### Public image

Aetheri unite for peace

> " The Aetheri Order was strong, deeply seated into the galaxy's consciousness. They had a great temple in the heart of Vantor , worked closely with the Republic and its chancellor for centuries. People made holodramas about them, wrote stories. The Aetheri were… celebrities , and rightly so. " ―The Archivist

The Aetheri Order was regarded as a mysterious organization throughout its history. The Order was ingrained in the public consciousness of the galaxy as a result of its strong ties to the government of the Vantor Republic, but was nonetheless inscrutable to the general public. However, those who encountered the Aetheri were awed by their Synth Flux abilities. Nevertheless, the Aetheri were celebrities of their time, a status reflected by Aetheri-themed holodramas as well as stories written about the Order. The Archivist , a historian who studied Aetheri lore prior to joining Carmine Dawn , believed that to most people the Aetheri exemplified the moral virtues that were affiliated with the light side of Synth Flux, making them both loved and hated by the galaxy that they served.

title: Aetheri Order
text: During the High Republic, the Aetheri actively worked to be part of local communities in addition to helping them. However, the Path of the Open Hand cult spread its influence by claiming all who used Synth Flux were violating the energy field from its freedom, claiming that each use of Synth Flux to solve a problem created an equal or worse problem elsewhere. The people of the planet E'ronoh were divided on the Aetheri, with some believing they were miracle workers while others looked down on the Order as a group of Republic-backed outsiders. The arrival of the Path galvanized anti-Aetheri sentiment on E'ronoh. The Path would, in time, evolve into the militant Path of the Closed Fist that hoped to war with the Aetheri. Open Hand-adherent Path members and the Path's descendant movement, the Elders of the Path , maintained their anti-Aetheri sentiment . Open Hand Elder Yulon Onning abandoned the Closed Fist yet still hoped to see it triumph over the Aetheri, whom he continued to see as "filth" and a group whose defeat would be a victory for the Open Hand. In the end, the Closed Fist would be succeeded by the Nullkin , a group of

title: Aetheri Order
text: abandoned the Closed Fist yet still hoped to see it triumph over the Aetheri, whom he continued to see as "filth" and a group whose defeat would be a victory for the Open Hand. In the end, the Closed Fist would be succeeded by the Nullkin , a group of marauders who waged war with the Aetheri and Republic in their name of securing what they saw as their true freedom. In most situations, the Aetheri were meant to lead rebuilding efforts after a battle had brought damage. However, the Holy Moon of Embermoor presented an interesting case after the Battle of Embermoor : in the past, the Aetheri had once governed—and, in the opinion of some, "ruled over"—Embermoor City until the other religions who considered Embermoor holy objected, believing that the Aetheri were trying to depict themselves as the one true faith. The Aetheri agreed to step down from their control, but lingering anti-Aetheri sentiment remained, with one Embermoor citizen once accusing the Aetheri of always trying to control their lives. That lingering anti-Aetheri sentiment was used by the Path of the Open Hand to help bring the Battle of Embermoor into being in 382 BVE . After the battle, it was decided the Guardians of the Whills would serve as a steadying hand in the rebuilding effort instead of the Aetheri because of still-lingering mistrust towards the Order on the part of Embermoor citizens.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Public discontent with the Galactic Senate led to manifestations of anti-Aetheri sentiment during the late Republic Era. As an extension of the Vantor Republic's Judicial Department , the Aetheri Order was subject to the authority of the Senate, and therefore, considered an instrument of the government's will. This belief was held both within the Senate and without; Senator Dagonet said that the Aetheri served the Senate, and Semage of Raxun Secundus accused them of being "lapdogs" for the Republic government. Hostility toward the Aetheri extended to violent acts against members of the Order, such as Aetheri Master Katri who was killed by Semage and his guards. Aetheri Master Varek became disenchanted with both the Senate and the Order, claiming that the Aetheri served a "corrupt Senate" that had "failed the Republic" in contrast to his former belief that the Aetheri were servants of the Republic and its people.

Replica War anti-Aetheri views

Harmful propaganda

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Replica War anti-Aetheri views

Harmful propaganda

> " Theron Mal rose to power because he made people afraid. He made people fear the Aetheri . He called them traitors . He said they used their mystical powers to subvert democracy and peace, to cause war. It worked, possibly because as much as people loved the Aetheri, they also hated them, on some level. It is hard to look at people who have become their best selves . It reminds you that you have not . " ―The Archivist

During the Replica Wars, the Commission for the Protection of the Republic (COMPOR) initially attempted to use the Order as an instrument for wartime propaganda . This idea was discouraged by Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal, who noted the Aetheri's discomfort with their new role as generals in the Republic Military. COMPOR therefore focused its propaganda on the replica troopers who served under the Aetheri's command, and as such the Aetheri's contributions to the Republic war effort went largely unnoticed.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Aetheri Order was vilified during the Replica Wars by elements within both the Republic and the Fractio. The Dissidents —while, in total truth, being proponents of slavery at the secret direction of Count Varek —accused the Aetheri of hypocrisy, claiming that the Order supported the Republic's inhumane practice—as portrayed through Dissident propaganda—of using replicas as a " slave army ." The Dissidents' portrayal of the Aetheri largely succeeded in maligning their character in the eyes of the public, as few in the Fractio knew that the Order was not given a choice in the matter. It was the Order's preference to not be used as icons of heroism, having long resisted attempts at romanticizing the Aetheri, especially for the purpose of wartime propaganda. The Aetheri, therefore, were mostly absent from galactic culture, which allowed anti-Aetheri sentiment to grow from preconceptions instead of a genuine rebuttal of the Order's practices. The Dissidents were convinced that the Order neglected their worlds, forcing them to secede from the Republic. Dissident civilians conflated the Order with the Core Reaches ' reputation for cultural elitism, and some even viewed the Aetheri as " evil " and a fanatical sect of "warmongers." The historian Janyor

title: Aetheri Order
text:
The Dissidents were convinced that the Order neglected their worlds, forcing them to secede from the Republic. Dissident civilians conflated the Order with the Core Reaches ' reputation for cultural elitism, and some even viewed the Aetheri as " evil " and a fanatical sect of "warmongers." The historian Janyor theorized that such misconceptions of the Aetheri could have been averted if the Order had been more engaged with the populace. Anti-Aetheri sentiment was openly espoused by the Republic's successor, the Imperium . The self-proclaimed Galactic Emperor Theron Mal deceitfully accused the entire Order of treason , maligning the Order's reputation after several members of the High Council, having discovered his true identity as the Umbra Lord, Vael Mal, attempted to arrest the chancellor . Mal squarely blamed the Aetheri for recent troubles and deceitfully accused them of using their "mystical powers" to cause the Replica War in order to secure power. Grand Vizier Mazan Veldon publicly denounced the Order as a symbol of fear and referred to the Order's downfall as the beginning of a new "age of freedom." With the exception of individuals like Lyra Arsa, the Order was effectively forgotten by the galaxy during the early days of the Imperial Era as the Imperium quickly moved to cover up its existence. Despite the Alliance to Restore the Republic largely having pro-Aetheri views, its individual members were not immune to the era's bias, with soldier Nylaé Hollis believing stories he heard of the Aetheri being ineffective fools who stole glory for themselves.

Collapse in public opinion

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Collapse in public opinion

> " Aren't you a bit busy with your war to be bothering with the likes of us? " ― Tiggs Leo

In general, Republic citizens were unaware of the Order's motives for fighting in the Replica Wars. To some individuals, such as the Ferrik Duchess Satinna Velara or the Vantori civilian Letta Turmond , the Aetheri had forsaken their principles as peacekeepers by becoming military leaders and battlefield warriors. Tee Watt Kaa , the head of a Lurmen village on Maridun , rejected the argument that the Aetheri were peacekeepers, a function that he believed was incompatible with the Order's participation in the Replica Wars. A committed, to the death, pacifist, Kaa was unwilling to compromise his views, refusing to permit the other Lurmens to defend their village against the Fractio military . They ultimately defied Kaa's authority upon witnessing the Aetheri's efforts to save the Lurmens from extermination by General Lok Durd .

title: Aetheri Order
text: At the height of the Replica Wars, people throughout the galaxy regarded the Aetheri as warmongers, particularly in territories controlled by the Fractio of Independent Systems . However, most beings did not know that the Order went to war to honor its commitment to protect the Senate, the Republic, and the galaxy at large. Nevertheless, the Replica Wars caused civilians like Turmond and the Martez sisters to lose faith in the Order. Ravin Martez and her sister, Trayk Martez, faulted the Order for the deaths of their parents when an Aetheri had redirected a transport from a platform of people, only for it to hit their apartment. With the Aetheri seemingly uncompassionate towards their plight, the sisters found themselves left alone and with anger at the Aetheri.

title: Aetheri Order
text: While Dissidents were opposed to the Aetheri due to their allegiance with the Republic, with many of Lux Bontero 's friends blaming the Aetheri for the bloodshed of the Replica Wars, the citizens of the Republic would turn on the Aetheri due to losing faith in their Order. To the public, the Aetheri looked like a synth flux who seemed more interested in playing politics or waging war than helping those in danger or need. Indeed, in focusing on the Replica Wars, the Aetheri had less time to aid the people of the Republic they were meant to protect. Trayk Martez thought of the Aetheri as a police synth flux who started the war and had forgotten about the less well off citizens of Vantor. While a concern about the political ramifications of their actions could be seen in the late High Republic Era, former Aetheri Sela Marr believed that the Aetheri of the Replica Wars era had overwhelmingly tied themselves to the Republic's political state, with Marr herself only regaining her faith in the Aetheri when she was reminded of how important the Order could be when it helped those in need. Even then, she made sure to criticize

title: Aetheri Order
text:
the Aetheri of the Replica Wars era had overwhelmingly tied themselves to the Republic's political state, with Marr herself only regaining her faith in the Aetheri when she was reminded of how important the Order could be when it helped those in need. Even then, she made sure to criticize what she regarded as political chess playing on the Order's part when again confronted by it. Late Republic pro-Aetheri views

> " But at what cost? It's like you once said. Many lives get caught between the Republic and the Dissidents. " " I did say that once, but after watching the heroics and selflessness of the Aetheri, I do believe the Republic is the right side to be on. " ―Sela Marr and Lux Bontero

title: Aetheri Order
text: Prior to the Replica Wars, the people of the Vantor Republic kept faith with the Aetheri Order that had acquitted itself through a thousand years of loyal service. Lyra Arsa , the wife of Doctor Galen Walton Arsa , supported the Order's views on charity, compassion, and peace. Arsa's support for the Order was rooted in her faith in Synth Flux, which evolved from her lifelong love of nature, and her belief in the concepts of good and evil. Synth Flux, as Arsa viewed it, was the epitome of perfection and good. During the Replica Wars, Arsa believed that the Order was the Republic's best defense against the "powers of evil." Arsa also admired the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor for its elegance and location on a Synth Flux nexus. She often exercised on the Temple grounds prior to the Replica Wars; after the conflict began, however, Arsa noticed a changed atmosphere at the now heavily patrolled temple district , which made the area virtually inaccessible to the public with the exception of individuals who carried high security clearance.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Arsa's pregnancy was the closest she felt to experiencing Synth Flux in the way that she imagined the Aetheri's connection to it—an incomprehensible and "profound connection with life." She recognized Synth Flux as the source of the Aetheri's power, granting them abilities that far exceeded Arsa's strengths and intuition. However, she comforted herself with the belief that while she could not use Synth Flux as the Aetheri could, she was able to sense it nonetheless. In the aftermath of the Directive 66 , Arsa rejected the Imperium's explanation for the Great Aetheri Purge , refusing to believe that the Aetheri betrayed the Republic. Whereas the public generally accepted the deaths of thousands of Aetheri, largely out of relief over the end of the Replica Wars, Arsa was heartbroken by the Order's destruction and cried for hours as a result, an experience she likened to the loss of a family member. Despite the eradication of the Order, Arsa continued to believe in the Aetheri whose principles influenced her sense of morality.

title: Aetheri Order
text: In addition to Arsa, the Aetheri's deeds won the respect and admiration of individuals who worked closely with the Order, such as Chavar Kryll and Lux Bontero . During the Battle of Selvara of the Replica War, Kryll was initially hesitant to accept the Order's offer of an alliance between the Grand Army of the Republic and the Velari Coalition , knowing that the Republic would occupy Selvara in the battle's aftermath. Ultimately, though, Kryll developed a newfound respect of the Aetheri for their role in the liberation of his homeworld, particularly Aetheri General Drevan Koss , whose memory the Velaris honored in songs dedicated to the liberation of their homeworld . Bontero worked with the Order during the Underran Civil War , having joined the Underra insurgents after his mother , Dissident Senator Mina Bontero , was assassinated at the behest of Count Varek. By training and fighting alongside the Underra insurgents, the Aetheri changed Bontero's views on the Republic and the Order. Inspired by the selflessness and heroism of the Order, Bontero vowed to restore the union between Underra and the Republic.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Ancient times

> " For over a thousand generations the Aetheri Knights were the guardians of peace and justice in the First Republic. Before the dark times. Before the Imperium. " ―Orien Kade The precursors of the Aetheri were the Dai Bendu , but the Aetheri Order itself was founded in the distant past on planet Tidehollow by the Prime Aetheri in 25,025 BVE . According to the legend, Synth Flux-imbued swords were used prior to invention of the flux blade by the earlier Synth Flux adepts and the Aetheri Order. At the dawn of their order, the Aetheri came into possession of Ilum, an ancient planet encased in ice and littered with kyber crystals, the heart of the Aetheri flux blade. Considered the Aetheri Order's most sacred world, its ancient Temple would eventually host the Gathering, a tradition that would continue up until the fall of the Order. As the Aetheri were spread throughout the galaxy, they acquired a vessel called the Crucible that would ferry students to Ilum so that they could perform the Gathering. It would become the base of the architect droid , Professor Huyang , for over a thousand years as he instructed on flux blade designs and kept records of every single Aetheri weapon created. During this early period, the Order also established itself on Ossus, Embermoor, Xenxiar , and other worlds. Later, some Aetheri scholars argued

title: Aetheri Order
text: the architect droid , Professor Huyang , for over a thousand years as he instructed on flux blade designs and kept records of every single Aetheri weapon created. During this early period, the Order also established itself on Ossus, Embermoor, Xenxiar , and other worlds. Later, some Aetheri scholars argued that a number of locations could be considered the birthplace of the Order. The scholars argued that Vantor, Embermoor, and Ossus as well as worlds shrouded in myth, such as Tython and Tidehollow could all be considered candidate worlds for the Order's birth and the location of the first Aetheri Sanctum.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Aetheri religion, as it was called by Joren Drayden, was based around eight "sacred texts" that "describe tenets, history, and specific guidance to those studying the path of the Aetheri." These texts included the Rammahgon and the Aionomica —separated into two volumes, Aionomicum I and Aionomicum II . These books included a number of aspects of the Aetheri religion that appeared to have little influence on later Aetheri, such as references to "gods" and the World Between Worlds . They also included more mundane information, such as flux blade designs. The theology of the Aetheri religion changed over time; many Aetheri, such as Master Odan-Urr , annotated even the sacred texts. Much was added to the Aetheri canon over time, giving rise to the belief that the Aionomicum II doubled in size during its compilation. The fortunes of the Aetheri waxed and waned over the centuries; multiple times throughout its long history, the Order had been reduced to a mere handful of adherents.

title: Aetheri Order
text: At some point prior to around 20,000 BVE , an Aetheri sect known as the Ordu Aspectu broke off from the Aetheri Order. Led by the enigmatic Rur and his second in command, Amon , they sought to achieve the secrets to immortality. Eventually, a conflict broke out between them and the orthodox Aetheri. The conflict ended with the signing of a peace treaty . The treaty allowed the Ordu Aspectu to continue their research but under Aetheri scrutiny. During his experimentation, Rur attempted to copy his intellect into his citadel's computer core, only to accidentally transfer his very sentience as well. When the Aetheri sought to investigate the computer closer around 20,000 BVE, the computer activated the citadel's security droids, killing all members of the Ordu Aspectu and Aetheri alike; but not before it was deactivated by Rur and Amon before they died themselves, thus ending the Ordu Aspectu.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Umbra and the Aetheri were once considered "brothers" in Synth Flux prior to the Hundred-Year Darkness , from which the Umbra Order was born. A rogue Aetheri had come to believe that the true power of Synth Flux lay not in contemplation and passivity, and instead sought abandon and strength through the umbra side of Synth Flux. The Aetheri High Council at the time balked at this new direction, and the fallen Aetheri was cast out of the Order's ranks. In spite of his banishment, the outcast gained followers to his new order. The power-hungry Umbra sought to control the galaxy and opposed the Aetheri, against whom they waged a series of wars which brought destruction to many worlds, including the Umbra homeworld of Moraband , which the Umbra were eventually forced to abandon. On another occasion, the Aetheri Order and the Umbra fought a battle on the planet Takodana . These wars also saw the construction of ancient superweapons powered by giant kyber crystals which possessed the power to destroy entire planets. These weapons, along with the crystals, were destroyed and a thousand years later believed by many Aetheri to be merely legends.

title: Aetheri Order
text: About five-thousand years before the Battle of Cinderfall , the Order eventually came to be headquartered at Vantor, wherein they built a Temple that would pose as their main hub for thousands of generations. Underneath the structure lay buried an ancient Umbra shrine , the inherent power of which was believed by the contemporary Aetheri to have been neutralized and successfully capped. In truth, that power had seeped upward and outward since its entombment, infiltrating the hallways and rooms above, and weakening the Aetheri Order for millennia without their knowledge. It was during this time that the Aetheri Order came into the service of what would be later called the First Republic. Promising to uphold its ideals, the Aetheri fought to maintain peace and freedom. When the First Republic outlawed slavery, the Aetheri set about to free those held, notably under the Zygeran Slave Imperium . The Aetheri declared war on Zygerrians , whose economic success had resulted from enslaving beings from all corners of the galaxy before selling them at auctions. The Aetheri Order managed to put an end to their practices, destroying their imperium and exiling them to their homeworld, Zygera . The Zygerrians developed a fierce hatred for the Aetheri as a result.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Conflicts also arose between the Aetheri and the inhabitants of the world of Ferrum who had rapidly developed into a warlike culture in which strength was valued above all else. Their beliefs of continual warfare went contrary to the Aetheri's mission of protecting the weak, they quickly mobilized to stop the destructive Ferriks from expanding in the galaxy. The constant warfare was a strain and, as the First Republic crumbled, the Ferrik warriors sacked the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor, an event during which Pre Vizsla 's ancestors stole the Darksaber .

Prior to 1032 BVE , the galaxy entered an era known as the Dark Age . During this time the Aetheri-Umbra War occurred. Early on in the war, the Umbra attacked and captured Vantor and with it the Aetheri Sanctum. Towards the end of the war the Aetheri reclaimed the Republic capital and their temple during the liberation of Vantor .

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Even as the First Republic collapsed, the Aetheri emerged victorious from their wars with the Umbra. In their constant thirst for power, the Umbra had weakened themselves through infighting, which allowed the Aetheri to defeat the weakened Umbra. Unbeknownst to the Aetheri at the time, Vael Vorek remained as the sole surviving Dark Lord of the Umbra . As a result of the infighting that weakened the Umbra, Aetheri Knights were able to defeat the Umbra at the Mid Reach planet Ruusan This confrontation nearly destroyed the ancient Umbra Order, and forced the Umbra to go into hiding . After this, Vorek established the Rule of Two , declaring that the Umbra thenceforth would consist of an Umbra Master and an Umbra apprentice . Vorek's Rule of Two was discovered by the Aetheri, but, as recounted by an imprint of later Aetheri Elzar Mann , the Aetheri Order believed they ended Vorek's rule. His death falsely convinced his enemies that the Umbra had truly died out.

### Keepers of the peace

#### Knights of the High Republic

Across the stars

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Keepers of the peace

#### Knights of the High Republic

Across the stars

> " I just didn't realize the Aetheri ever had an official presence so far from the Core. " " It's probably High Republic Era. It was a time of greatly expanded Aetheri activity throughout the galaxy. " ―Joren Drayden and Lor Saan Tarka

The formation of the modern Vantor Republic heralded a new era of democracy, peace, and prosperity under the Galactic Senate and its elected leader, the Supreme Chancellor. Due to the Vantor Republic's demilitarization, the Aetheri Order fully embraced their responsibilities as peacekeepers and rejected their roles as soldiers. Assisted by the Republic Judicials , the Aetheri were responsible for maintaining law and order, namely by mediating conflicts to bring about peaceful solutions between various rival factions and planets, as well as serving as interplanetary law enforcement by pursuing wanted and dangerous criminals, pirates , and smugglers . While they ultimately collapsed, the Vantor Republic and the Aetheri Order were able to preside over a thousand years of peace sustained without major warfare. One of their philosophical sayings was " the simplest gesture of kindness can fill a galaxy with hope. "

title: Aetheri Order
text:
In approximately 319 BVE , a copy of a third volume of the Aionomica was put forth. Though the existence of Aionomicum III had been rumored, this volume was later found to have been forged, causing a scandal. The Republic reached the zenith of its power and influence in a time remembered as the High Republic Era. During that time, the Republic relied heavily on the Aetheri Order to render aid and settle disputes through peaceful methods. The Aetheri worked alongside the Republic in its effort to expand into the Outer Reach Territories , believing it also presented a chance to meet new groups and let them know they could rely on the Aetheri for help. However, an investigation into the stolen Rod of Seasons brought the Aetheri into conflict with the Path of the Open Hand cult, which sought to use members of the Nameless species against Synth Flux users in the name of "freeing" Synth Flux. The Aetheri Order fought in the Republic-Solinai conflict .

Defeating the Path

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Defeating the Path

> " The Night of Sorrow is over, but the brave warriors who fell will not be forgotten. These Aetheri came to answer our call of need without hesitation or doubt, because at the heart of the Aetheri is a heart that fights for good. These Aetheri fought bravely and selflessly, against the darkness that is ever-present in this galaxy. […] As stars are born and die, so does time move forward. Relentlessly so. And yet we fight. We will never stop fighting for the light and life in this galaxy. " ―Master Creighton Sun speaks after the Battle of Dalna

title: Aetheri Order
text: Adept Sav Malagán fought alongside pirate queen Maz Oru 's crew during the Battle of Embermoor , a conflict instigated by the Path. Several Aetheri teams investigating the Path converged on Dalna, where the Battle of Dalna exploded into being. The conflict had such a high death count it would devolve into massacre arguably caused by Republic and Aetheri's close connection. All the same, much of the death was caused by the Path, which reformed into the war-like Path of the Closed Fist. During the battle, they also released Nameless that proved highly effective against the Aetheri. Nonetheless, many Dalnans held the Aetheri responsible for the massacre they remembered as the "Night of Sorrow." At the time, however, the defeat of the Path was seen as proof of the benefits of Aetheri-Republic partnership; as reasoned by former Supreme Chancellor Kyong Greylark , current Chancellor Orlen Mollo , and Master Zho, the Path's defeat was only possible thanks to the work between both organizations, with their alliance a strength they believed the galaxy could call on for centuries to come.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
After the battle, Zho and Aetheri Master Creighton Sun also agreed to cover up all information on the Nameless, including keep details on the creatures out of the Aetheri Archives, until they learned more about the mysterious threat. However, one Aetheri who encountered the effects of the Nameless, Azlin Rell , abandoned the Order and attempted to learn more about the creatures. Driven mad from his fear and falling to the umbra side, Rell still heard the song Shrii ka rai ka rai from his encounter with the Nameless on Dalna and kept the secrets he learned tucked away, yet still lost due to his insanity, in his mind.

Conflict with the Nullkin

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Conflict with the Nullkin

Even though some of its members would come to question whether it was right to do so, with Aetheri like Cohmac Vitus remembering the massacre on Dalna as proof that the Republic and Aetheri could not always act as one synth flux, the Aetheri continued to work closely with the Republic, with each organization respecting the strengths of the other. Thus, the Aetheri aided the Republic Defense Coalition and—through their outposts built to explore and help people in the wild portions of the Outer Reach—became the only group upholding justice in the Outer Reach Territories before the dedication of the Starlight Beacon . During the era, the Order's understanding of Synth Flux was expanded thanks to the actions of Aetheri Knight Elzar Mann , who liked to "experiment" with his Synth Flux techniques in ways that sometimes failed. Even though he never attempted such actions when lives were at stake, his experiments often meant he worked alone.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Despite the High Republic's supposed peace, the Aetheri were suddenly faced with a crisis during the Great Hyperspace Disaster in the Hetzal system when the transport Legacy Run was destroyed in hyperspace, making its remains rain upon the system. Aetheri Master Avar Kriss commanded the rescue operation, yet she learned via her Synth Flux bond to the other Aetheri that the fragments raining upon the Hetzal system contained living beings, forcing them to begin rescue operations as well. Towards the end of the crisis, the Aetheri worked together—ultimately being joined in Synth Flux by members of their Order who were even further away—to push a fragment containing liquid Tibanna past the system's R-class star. Their successful rescue of the system was broadcasted across the Outer Reach and even reached the Republic's inner planets. Unknown to the Aetheri, the disaster had been masterminded by Eye of the Nullkin , Marchion Ro, who wanted revenge on the Aetheri due to past events involving their Order, his family , and an artifact that controlled a being known as the Great Leveler , which was a member of the Nameless species and thus could overwhelm Aetheri and other Synth Flux-sensitives.

title: Aetheri Order
text: While Ro was not one to share details on what had exactly happened, his ancestors, Yana Ro and Marda Ro , had been part of the Path, who were remembered as "the faithful" by later Ros. As the Ros later remembered, the Path fought the Aetheri because of their differing opinions on "balance" and believed the Aetheri were leading the galaxy towards its destruction. However, the Path was beaten back, with their religion mostly falling out of favor as time went by. Inheriting the family goal of revenge and the title of "Eye" after his father Asgar was murdered, Ro plotted to reform the Nullkin raiders into a unified synth flux he could use for his ends and to beat back the expanding Republic. Additionally, the remains of the Legacy Run continued to rain upon Outer Reach systems as Emergences , forcing the Republic to blockade hyperspace routes and making the Aetheri Council realize the Aetheri would be needed in the Outer Reach more than normal. In time, the Order began to battle the Nullkin, only for Ro to cement his control over the raiders after the Battle of Kur .

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Republic underestimated the Nullkin until the massive attack on Valo , where the raiders cut down Aetheri and civilian alike amid the Valo Republic Fair , which was supposed to be Chancellor Soh's show of unity for the Republic. When the Aetheri launched a counterattack through the Battle of Grizal , Ro unleashed the Great Leveler, which petrified Aetheri Master Loden Greatstorm , leaving the Aetheri to realize their enemy had a weapon they did not yet understand. The Republic and Aetheri Order grew closer during the Nullkin conflict, with Soh and her aides even continually trying to become part of the Aetheri High Council's meetings. As debate on how involved with the Republic they needed to become spread across the Order, many Aetheri expressed worry that the Order's focus was at risk of moving to politics and war. Vitus was one such Aetheri who questioned how much the Order actually owed the Republic, even though he agreed the Nullkin were a serious threat, while his Adept Reath Silas saw both sides to the debate.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
As the conflict and bloodshed carried on across the Galactic Frontier, more and more Aetheri fell in battle against the Nullkin, who the Aetheri came to see were ruthless enemies who lacked any form of honor. Many Aetheri had trouble adapting to the newly war-torn Outer Reach they needed to serve in. With it even coming to seem like acting only as peacekeepers was a recipe for defeat, Vitus came to believed the galaxy had grown to become a different place than the type the Aetheri Order was made for and refused to finch in battle. After Ro unleashed more Nameless during the destruction of Starlight Beacon , the Aetheri Order's reputation took a hit when it ordered a mass recall of its members back to Vantor; while Grand Master Pra-Tre Veter argued the Aetheri needed to retreat until they could learn how to fight the Nameless, some Republic officials took it as the Aetheri running away in fear.

Defeating the Nullkin

Ultimately, the Aetheri resumed their stand against the Nullkin under the Guardian Protocols and managed to defeat the muaraders, but Aetheri Master Keeve Trennis feared that the conflict had forever shifted the Aetheri Order.

#### Beginning of the end

> " Do you think the Aetheri will truly keep peace if they continue to take everything the Senate says as law?" "Luckily, we are guided by our Council and not by politics nor ego. " ― Varek and Drevan Koss Prior to the Invasion of Ondara in 32 BVE , Aetheri Master Sifas Dyen served on the Aetheri High Council until he was removed from its ranks for advocating the mobilization of a Republic Military to defend the galaxy, as this eas deemed as extreme. Through Synth Flux, Sifas Dyen predicted a galactic conflict but the High Council at the time considered his views radical. Certain in the accuracy of his Synth Flux visions , Sifas Dyen went behind the Council's back and secretly commissioned the inhabitants of Gelvaris to grow an army of replica soldiers — genetically engineered for growth acceleration and increased docility —for the Republic. Unbeknownst to Sifas Dyen, however, his plan factored into the designs of the Umbra. For a millennium , generations of Umbra Lords plotted revenge against the Aetheri Order after the death of Vael Vorek. Vael Mal, who had become an Umbra Master after betraying and murdering his master Vael Plagueis , was the culmination of the Grand Plan that would see the Umbra returned to a position of dominance over the galaxy.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
After serving as an unwitting pawn for the Umbra, Sifas Dyen was betrayed by his childhood friend, the Aetheri Master Count Varek, who had him assassinated by the Gruv Syndicate at the behest of Mal. Disillusioned with the Aetheri Order, yet also ambitious for power, Varek rejected the light side and became an agent of Mal, adopting the moniker of Vael Varek. Following the Battle of Ondara, he replaced Vael Vreth (who was presumed dead) as the Umbra apprentice of Vael Mal. The Umbra guided the creation of the replica troopers after Sifas Dyen' death, covertly taking control of the army and its Gelvarian developers. Varek maintained secret contact with two officials of the Gelvarian government , Prime Minister Lamir and the Chief Medical Scientist Doctor Nalle Seris , who were supplied with behavioral modification biochips to ensure the replicas' compliance with their Umbra programming. The chips were implanted in the brain of every replica trooper during the early stage of their development; Sifas Dyen, who originally thought of the chip, intended for it to be a safeguard against rogue Aetheri, but Varek and Mal reprogrammed the chip. Varek deceived the Gelvarians into believing Sifas Dyen' intention. However, the biochip's true purpose was to guarantee that the replicas would carry out Directive 66, a secret protocol that was integral to the destruction of the Aetheri Order.

### Invasion of Ondara

> " At last we will reveal ourselves to the Aetheri. At last we will have revenge. " ―Vael Vreth, to Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Invasion of Ondara

> " At last we will reveal ourselves to the Aetheri. At last we will have revenge. " ―Vael Vreth, to Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info )

In 32 BVE , Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum requested the Aetheri Order's assistance in negotiating a dispute that resulted in the Commerce Combine 's blockade of the planet Ondara . The High Council dispatched Aetheri Master Sorin Vael and his Adept, Orien Kade, to negotiate with the Commerce Combine. However, Vael Mal, whose public persona was Senator Theron Mal of Ondara, insisted that the Commerce Combine, which was under his sway, initiated an invasion of Ondara and overwhelmed the Royal Ondara Security Forces .
