Circumventing a trap by the Federation, Vael and Kade were able to escape to Ondara and arrive in Serath in time to rescue the Ondara Queen , Lira Ondar , who was being held captive by Federation forces. Together with the Queen's Handmaidens and her close security detail , the Aetheri fled the planet but their ship was damaged in the escape, causing them to land on the desert planet of Dunemere .

title: Aetheri Order
text: While stranded on Dunemere, the two Aetheri discovered a young slave named Kael Drayden . Vael believed Kael to be the Seeded One, the one that would bring balance to Synth Flux. By betting on the boy winning the Dune Eve Classic , Vael was able to secure both Drayden's freedom and the needed parts to repair the Queen's ship to reach Vantor. It was after this that Vael was attacked by Vael Vreth, apprentice to Vael Mal, who had dispatched Vreth to kill the Aetheri. As the Aetheri had believed the Umbra to be extinct, Vael was at first unsure of who Vreth was except that he had been trained in flux blade combat. Arriving at the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor, the Council refused to induct Drayden into the Order because, according to the the Code, he was too old. The Council then ordered Vael and Kade to protect Queen Ondar on her return to Serath. At the same time, Ondar was deceived by Mal into calling for a Vote of No Confidence in Chancellor Valorum by pointing out that Valorum was ineffective and under the control of the Bureaucrats , which would eventually lead to the election of

title: Aetheri Order
text: Queen Ondar on her return to Serath. At the same time, Ondar was deceived by Mal into calling for a Vote of No Confidence in Chancellor Valorum by pointing out that Valorum was ineffective and under the control of the Bureaucrats , which would eventually lead to the election of Mal to the chancellorship. Vael and Kade then assisted Ondar and her forces during the ensuing battle against the Commerce Combine, when Vreth killed Vael in combat , only for the Umbra to be defeated by Kade. Given the status of Aetheri Knight afterward, Kade took Drayden as his apprentice, despite Zho's reluctance, and the Aetheri Order was left in the dark as to what the Umbra's actions were for ten years. The Aetheri were left unaware that they were being deceived by Mal, who was using his double identity to eventually complete the Umbra's revenge by destroying the Aetheri and taking over the Republic.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Dissident Crisis

> " I will not let this Republic that has stood for a thousand years be split in two. My negotiations will not fail. " " If they do, you must realize that there aren't enough Aetheri to protect the Republic. We're keepers of the peace, not soldiers. " ―Theron Mal and Drevan Koss

Having broken all ties to the Aetheri Order, secretly replacing Vreth as Mal' apprentice, Varek was believed to be a mere "political idealist" by his peers at the Aetheri Order. For eight years, Varek was scarcely heard about until he staged a theatrical return to public life by delivering a rousing speech that condemned the Republic and essentially set the stage for the Dissident Crisis . At the same time, he fomented political turmoil in many worlds, including Selvara, Thornwood , Garnethex , and Underra, or tried to convince their leaders to leave the Republic, as in Eriadu 's case. Soon enough, Varek became the face of the Fractio of Independent Systems, convincing several thousand systems to leave the Republic.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Aetheri Order was unable to ensure the Republic's safety in the event of a war due to its limited numbers. The Republic lacked a standing army, while the mandate of the Aetheri was to maintain order as peacekeepers instead of soldiers. Concerned by the growing number of star systems seceding from the Republic, the Senate debated the Military Creation Act . During the debate around 22 BVE , a plot to assassinate Senator Ondar forced the Ondara senator to return to her homeworld with Adept Kael Drayden serving as her bodyguard . The task of investigating the plot against Ondar was given to Drayden's master, Aetheri Knight Orien Kade, who tracked the assassin to the planet Gelvaris.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
After discovering the Gelvarians' creation of the replica army at the behest of the late Aetheri Master Sifas Dyen, Kade deduced that the army's replica template, the bounty hunter Garrick Vark , was the assassin who tried to kill Ondar. Garrick and his cloned son, Vex Vark , fled from Gelvaris to escape interrogation by the Aetheri. However, Kade followed the Fetts to Pyralis where he discovered the Dissident Droid Army , prompting the Senate to empower Chancellor Mal to unilaterally create the Grand Army of the Republic, although they were unaware that this was exactly what Mal had intended.

### Replica Wars

#### The first battle

> " I have to admit that without the replicas, it would not have been a victory. " " Victory? Victory, you say? Master Orien, not victory. The shroud of the umbra side has fallen. Begun the Replica War has. " ―Orien Kade and Zho

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### The first battle

> " I have to admit that without the replicas, it would not have been a victory. " " Victory? Victory, you say? Master Orien, not victory. The shroud of the umbra side has fallen. Begun the Replica War has. " ―Orien Kade and Zho

As the Republic prepared for war, Aetheri Master Drevan Koss led an Aetheri assault team to rescue Kade on Pyralis. The Aetheri confronted the Dissidents in the Pyralian Petranaki Arena , destroying many battle droids but also sustaining a large number of casualties, including Tan Yuster , Sar Labooda , and Coleman Trebor . The remaining Aetheri were evacuated from the arena by the Republic replica army that arrived on Pyralis under the command of Grand Master Zho.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Along with the requisite LAAT gunships and AT-TE walkers , over eighty regiments of replica troopers engaged the droid army with the Aetheri leading the charge. Although the Aetheri had not yet received a formal commission in the newly formed Grand Army, the replicas nonetheless complied with their orders. Koss, Kit Fisto , Ciel Venn , and other Aetheri fought alongside their troops on the battlefield while Zho was occupied with overseeing the Republic army's strategy from the forward command center . The Republic attack caught the Dissident leaders by surprise; despite their initial efforts to organize an effective counterattack, the Dissidents ultimately retreated from Pyralis as the replicas achieved ground and air supremacy under the skilled leadership of the Aetheri High Council. Although the First Battle of Pyralis concluded as a victory for the Republic, Zho lamented its outcome as the beginning of the Replica Wars. The outbreak of the conflict alone was enough to shift Synth Flux's balance.

#### Aetheri of the Republic

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### Aetheri of the Republic

> " We do what we have trained our whole lives to do. Trust in Synth Flux. Believe in the path that is set out before us. Stand in defense of all peoples, not just of the Republic, but across the galaxy. We do what any Aetheri would when staring into the face of evil. We fight. " ―Drevan Koss The aftermath of the battle on Pyralis saw the Aetheri commissioned as officers of the Republic Military, with the military rank of Aetheri General bestowed to Knights and Masters, and the rank of Aetheri Commander to Adepts. The Aetheri Military Integration Act formallized this and offically made the Aetheri Order a part of the Republic Military. The Aetheri were not of a single mind regarding participation in the war. Some Aetheri felt they have lost something by becoming the Republic's warriors, but, on the other hand, other Aetheri believed that returning to monasticism and contemplation would mean ignoring the suffering going on in the galaxy. Drevan Koss believed that the Aetheri should strive to serve as an example by leading the Republic's soldiers on the battlefield, although he was nonetheless affected by the loss of Aetheri lives early in the conflict. Koss was troubled by the prospect of more Aetheri dying as a result of the Order's decision to fight in the Replica Wars, but Zho counseled his colleague to set aside his doubts and trust in Synth Flux, acknowledging Koss for his wisdom and capable leadership.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Aetheri Master Prosset Dibs , meanwhile, opposed Aetheri involvement in the war and disliked needing to be involved in battle at all. While still able to fight as a skilled warrior, he felt Synth Flux shudder due to the conflict and remained steadfast in his belief that war was no place for an Aetheri. Dibs and Koss's opposing views came to a head during a mission to counter Dissident operations on the planet Hissrich , where Dibs was horrified by the civilian cost of war and came to believe the High Council was more interested in the world's resources than protecting its people. Dibs attacked Koss but was ultimately defeated, with the master standing trial before the High Council after the mission. However, Koss called on the High Council to grant clemency to Dibs, who had stood by his actions and wanted to be put to death to prove that the High Council were nothing more than warmongers. Despite his personal reservations, Koss's experience on Hissrich reminded him of the Aetheri Order's commitment to safeguarding the lives of others. With his newfound resolve, Koss affirmed his belief that the Order had a moral responsibility to defend the citizens of the

title: Aetheri Order
text: the High Council were nothing more than warmongers. Despite his personal reservations, Koss's experience on Hissrich reminded him of the Aetheri Order's commitment to safeguarding the lives of others. With his newfound resolve, Koss affirmed his belief that the Order had a moral responsibility to defend the citizens of the Republic as well as all beings throughout the galaxy. During the Replica Wars, the Aetheri were victorious on battlefronts across the galaxy, including Krestophis , Selvara, and Umbara . In their capacity as leaders of the Grand Army of the Republic, the Aetheri came to be seen as great warriors. Aetheri Knight Kael Drayden, for example, was considered by some to be the greatest warrior of the Aetheri Order and became known as the " Hero With No Fear " to the HoloNet . Believing the Order was not political, one Dissident fighter, Poan of Riek , believed the war would end quickly because he thought the Aetheri would, soon enough, intervene against the Republic. However, Poan then came face-to-face against an Aetheri during a Mission on Leyoye Prime , in which the Aetheri singlehandedly wiped out most of his unit.

title: Aetheri Order
text: During the Battle of Krestophis , Replica Sergeant Slick was arrested as a spy and traitor for the Fractio of Independent Systems. The sergeant claimed that he acted in the interests of the replicas, whom he viewed as a slave army fighting for the Aetheri and the Republic. However, the replica trooper officers who arrested him— Replica Commander Cord and Replica Captain Vek —questioned Slick's motives, noting how he betrayed the Republic for money and that his actions endangered replica lives. Although Slick succeeded in sabotaging much of the Republic's military equipment, Aetheri Generals Orien Kade and Kael Drayden successfully led their battalions , respectively the 212th Attack Battalion and the 501st Legion , to victory over the Dissidents on the Christophsian homeworld.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Battle of Selvara was a coordinated effort by the Republic to liberate the Velaris' homeworld from Dissident occupation. With the Aetheri in command, the replica troopers mainly relied on using volt pistol rifles and Electro Magnetic Pulse grenades to reduce the level of destruction on Selvara. Whereas the Dissidents used the Velaris as living shields to deter a direct Republic attack, the Aetheri and their replicas were careful to avoid causing civilian casualties. During the final phase of the invasion, General Koss endeavored to take the capital city of Lessu with the support of the Velari Coalition led by Chavar Kryll. Setting aside his dislike for politics, Koss used diplomacy to win the freedom fighter's help, convincing the rivals Kryll and Senator Orn Free Taa to work together in common cause. The combined forces of Aetheri, Republic, and Twi-leks captured the capital along with the Dissident Emir of Selvara Wat Tambra .

title: Aetheri Order
text:
The Second Battle of Pyralis occurred after the Pyralian coalition ousted the Republic's occupation synth flux from their world. With the Dissidents in control of the Pyralian droid factories once more, the Aetheri returned to Pyralis at the head of an invasion synth flux, having deemed Pyralis crucial to their efforts at restoring order to the Republic. The attack was led by Aetheri Generals Reth-Oss-Van , Orien Kade, Luminara Undula , and Kael Drayden. After the generals' forces converged at the Point Rain staging area , the primary droid foundry was destroyed by Aetheri Commanders Barris Ovva and Sela Marr . The capture of Archduke Poggle the Lesser subsequently ended Dissident control of Pyralis, thereby depriving the Fractio military of further support against the Republic from Pyralis.

#### Renegade Aetheri

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### Renegade Aetheri

> " I did it because I've come to realize what many people in the Republic have come to realize, that the Aetheri are the ones responsible for this war, that we've so lost our way that we have become villains in this conflict, that we are the ones that should be put on trial, all of us! And my attack on the Temple was an attack on what the Aetheri have become, an army fighting for the umbra side, fallen from the light that we once held so dear. This Republic is failing! It's only a matter of time. " ―Barris Ovva, admitting to the bombing of the Aetheri Sanctum hangar

title: Aetheri Order
text:
By the time of the Cindervale Refugee Conference , Lira Ondar stated that over one hundred Aetheri had been killed in the war. More Aetheri were killed as the war continued; Aetheri Master Even Piele died at the Battle of Lola Sayu ; during the assault on Vizsla Keep 09 , Count Varek killed Aetheri Master Tiplee . In addition to the casualties of war, the Aetheri Order lost a few of its members to the umbra side of Synth Flux, such as Aetheri Master Pong Krell and Adept Barris Ovva.

Krell served in the Replica Wars as a successful Aetheri General whose record reflected numerous victories for the Grand Army of the Republic. His command style resulted in high levels of replica trooper casualties; nevertheless, Krell was an acclaimed war hero by the time of the Battle of Umbara , during which he temporarily assumed command of the 501st Legion after Kael Drayden returned to Vantor at the behest of the Aetheri High Council and Chancellor Mal.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Though originally a Republic loyalist world at the onset of the Replica Wars, Umbara defected to the Dissidents in the wake of Senator Mee Deechi 's assassination. The Republic therefore invaded the Umbaran homeworld, precipitating the Battle of Umbara. By then, Krell had foreseen the rise of a New Order in the aftermath of the Replica Wars. Convinced that the Aetheri Order would be defeated, Krell secretly betrayed both the Order and the Republic. He sought to prove his new loyalties to Count Varek by undermining the Republic's efforts to retake Umbara. However, Krell's plans ended when the 501st discovered his betrayal and as such, mutinied agaisnt him. Krell was taken into custody after killing multiple replicas while resisting arrest. Ultimately, the traitorous Aetheri Master was executed by one of his strongest supporters, Dogma , after admitting his betrayal of the Republic.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Barris Ovva believed the Aetheri had deviated from their course as peacekeepers and so she betrayed the Aetheri by arranging a bombing at the Aetheri Sanctum, for which deceitfully framed fellow Adept Sela Marr. Marr, in turn, left the Aetheri Order unable to trust the Council after turning its back on her during her trial . Eventually, the High Council came to be aware of Varek's hand in the creation of the replica army, and of the lies and mistrust that surrounded them, both inside the Temple and the Senate. Grand Master Zho even (as it turned out correctly) foresaw that the Aetheri might not win the Replica Wars, just as public support for the Aetheri weakened due to their management of the conflict.

#### The last stand

> " In the name of the Galactic Senate of the Republic, you're under arrest, Chancellor. " " Are you threatening me, Master Aetheri? " " The Senate will decide your fate. " ―Drevan Koss and Theron Mal

title: Aetheri Order
text: The final stages of the war came in 19 BVE . It began with the Battle of Vantor , which Mal orchestrated as part of his overall plot to convert Kael to the Umbra side and make him his apprentice. During the battle, Varek was betrayed by Mal, who as Mal, had him executed by Drayden. With Varek dead, the Aetheri calculated a decisive Republic victory through the destruction of General Skarn , which was achieved by Orien Kade during the Battle of Uthara a few days or weeks later. However, Drayden, whose turmoil clouded his judgment, learned that Mal was Mal. Though he informed Koss of Mal's identity, Mal resisted the Aetheri's efforts to arrest him, killing three Aetheri Masters—Kit Fisto, Agen Kolar , and Saesee Tiin —forcing Koss to duel the Dark Lord alone. Drayden rushed to Mal's office as Koss and the chancellor fought, arriving moments after the Aetheri champion disarmed the Umbra Lord. Before Koss could kill Mal, Drayden, who believed he needed Mal alive to save his secret wife Padme Ondar from potentially dying from childbirth, betrayed him by severing his hand, which led to the Aetheri Master's death. Knowing there was no turning back

title: Aetheri Order
text:
the Aetheri champion disarmed the Umbra Lord. Before Koss could kill Mal, Drayden, who believed he needed Mal alive to save his secret wife Padme Ondar from potentially dying from childbirth, betrayed him by severing his hand, which led to the Aetheri Master's death. Knowing there was no turning back and desperate to save his wife, Drayden then betrayed the Aetheri and became Mal' apprentice, and was given the name of Xarn Velgor. ### The purge

> " A young Aetheri named Xarn Velgor, who was a pupil of mine until he turned to evil, helped the Imperium hunt down and destroy the Aetheri Knights. He betrayed and murdered your father. Now the Aetheri are all but extinct. " ―Orien Kade, to Joren Drayden

Deceitfully branding Koss's actions as treason, Mal declared the Aetheri to be enemies of the Republic and sent Velgor to oversee the siege of the Aetheri Sanctum . As his new apprentice purged the Temple of its inhabitants, including the younglings, Mal ordered his Replica Commanders to execute Directive 66, thereby activating the biochips that programmed the replicas to see the Aetheri as traitors to the Republic. As a result, thousands of Aetheri throughout the galaxy were betrayed and executed by their replicas including Reth-Oss-Van on Migeeta , Ciel Venn on Feldora, Tor Vayne on Cato Geltaria , Stass Allie on Saluk , Depa Billaba on Kaller , and Jaro Tapal above Bracca .

title: Aetheri Order
text: Out of an estimated number of ten-thousand Aetheri, just a few survived to see the proclamation of the New Order , marking the inception of the Imperium and the rise of Mal as its Emperor . Survivors included Zho, Orien Kade, Sela Marr, Caleb Dume , Cal Kessara , Cere Jundar and her Adept Trilla Suduri , Taron Malicos , and at least initially, Uvell , Luminara Undula, Oppo Rancisis , Etha Korrin , Coleman Kcaj , Jocasta Nura , Kirak Infil'a , Selrahc Eluos , Ka-Moon Kholi , Zubain Ankonori , Khandra , Mususiel , Nuhj , Ferren Barr , and possibly Daren Kelv . During their self-imposed exile, Kade and Zho, along with Senator Bael Solen , hid Velgor's newborn children, the Synth Flux-sensitive twins Joren Drayden and Elira Solen , from the Umbra, hoping that in time they would become the key to the Aetheri Order's future to stop the umbra side.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Word about the supposed Aetheri insurgency and the Order's destruction spread throughout the galactic population, and replica troopers were ordered to hunt down any Aetheri survivors. According to Imperial Admiral Raena Vexana , the Aetheri that had survived Directive 66 made a last stand against a replica trooper charge led personally by the future war veteran and Shadow Council member Hodnar Borrum , who was known to hold disdain for Synth Flux, on a mountain fortress on either Madar or Morad . Mal deceitfully blamed the Aetheri for the galaxy's recent crises and painted them as warmongers whose planned coup involved creating the Dissident Alliance and Replica Wars in the first place. Relieved to see the bloody war over at last and eager for any sense of normalcy to resume, the populous embraced Mal's imperium, with most of the galaxy blasting the Aetheri for their alleged betrayal or even simply because they had failed to prevent, or effectively win, the war.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
After killing the Aetheri at the Temple, Velgor followed Mal's next command by massacring the Dissident Council on Emberfall . He then followed Mal's third command by transmitting the order to all the Commerce Combine Droid Control Ships to deactivate all remaining battle droids of the Dissident Droid Army immediately, ultimately putting an end to the Replica Wars after three years.

In addition to the Imperium's suppression of all information relating to the Aetheri, it was considered treasonous to be an Aetheri or render assistance to an Aetheri. Imperial laws also prohibited the use or study of Synth Flux, resulting in the banning of educational studies concerning the Aetheri. As a consequence, instructors who specialized in Aetheri history lost their positions, including Sava Korin Pers and Sava Madelin Sun from the University of Bar'leth . Within five years of the Order's destruction, the Aetheri were effectively erased from the collective consciousness in the galaxy due to the Great Aetheri Purge , which also involved the systematic destruction of their temples and the unceasing, extensive hunts carried out by the Warden Order .

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Aetheri survivors that were captured were taken to Emberfall for interrogation and execution, as well as the Spire on Stygeon Prime , wherein the body of Luminara Undula was preserved to lure out any surviving Aetheri. Among the last reservoirs of knowledge of the Order were Antron Bach 's vault in an abandoned colony , created at Uvell's behest, and Grukkar the Grak 's private collection on Nar Shaddaa . Safeguarding reliquaries, flux blades, journals, archives, and other artifacts, they partially preserved the teachings of the fallen Order. The surviving Aetheri Nedriss Narr and Vanzell Mar-Klar attempted to train new younglings in a secret temple.

### Dark times

#### Fallen order

title: Aetheri Order
text: > " The Aetheri were good . Like all of us, they failed to secure the peace. They were drawn into the war like everyone else, and their hands were not clean. If I can accept the blame for my part, they certainly earned their share, too. But for thousands of years they could have ruled the galaxy, and instead they chose to serve. They had their own vested interests, their own ways of politicking. But they believed their power came with an obligation to live humbly, to do good without asserting authority. Maybe they failed to live up to those ideals in the end. I haven't seen your evidence. What do I know about the extent of their betrayals? But they were good and they were ordinary and they were fallible, and even the most smug and arrogant were trying to hew to a tradition older than the Republic. They deserved better than to die at the hands of power-hungry old men who saw them as a threat. We deserved better than to lose another people, another religion, from the universe. All of us are poorer for their loss. […] The Aetheri deserve justice… or at least a decent

title: Aetheri Order
text: They deserved better than to die at the hands of power-hungry old men who saw them as a threat. We deserved better than to lose another people, another religion, from the universe. All of us are poorer for their loss. […] The Aetheri deserve justice… or at least a decent funeral. " ―Vela Sess, to Soujen Vak-Nhalis For nearly twenty years, the Imperium was able to expand without opposition of a disbanded Aetheri Order. A few of its former members, however survived and stayed true to their code of honor and continued to fight the Imperium's injustice, albeit in different ways. Though former Adept Sela Marr had become disillusioned by the Council's actions and no longer identified as an Aetheri, she came into contact with Bael Solen from Cindervale , with whom she worked to coordinate the efforts of a insurgency under the codename "Fulcrum," fifteen years after the fall of the Republic.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Five years after the rise of the Imperium and the destruction of the Aetheri Order, there was an attempt to bring the Order back. Adept Cal Kessara, who had been hiding on Bracca since Directive 66, was recruited by the former Aetheri Knight Cere Jundar, who believed that the Return of the Aetheri Order was the best option to defeat the Imperium. Having spent so long in hiding due to the persecution of the Aetheri, Kessara did not trust Jundar at first, suspecting that she might have come to him out of interest in the rewards offered by the Imperium. Despite this, he joined her in her mission to rebuild the Order . To accomplish this, they sought to recover a reliquary that had been hidden on the planet Bogara by Aetheri Master Eno Cordova . This reliquary contained a list of the locations of Synth Flux-sensitive children across the galaxy.

title: Aetheri Order
text: After scouring ancient ruins for clues left behind by the extinct Zeffo civilization , Kessara succeeded in unlocking the Vault that contained the reliquary, but the artifact was taken by the Second Warden , a Warden who had been Jundar's Adept before the Purge. Jundar proclaimed Kessara an Aetheri Knight, and together they pursued the Second Warden to the Fortress Warden Order on the ocean moon Nur . They succeeded in retrieving the reliquary from the Second Warden, who was executed by Xarn Velgor. The Dark Lord overpowered both Aetheri, wounded Kessara for refusing to surrender the reliquary, and goaded Jundar to embrace the umbra side. Ultimately, though, Kessara and Jundar managed to escape from Velgor with their allies' help. Despite Kessara' commitment to the restoration of the Aetheri Order, the young Aetheri Knight destroyed the reliquary to protect the Synth Flux-sensitive younglings, entrusting their fate to the will of Synth Flux.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Aetheri Knight Tensu Run became a threat to the Imperium, as after freeing prisoners from an Imperial outpost during the Conquest of Regis Kor , he became a symbol of hope. Tensu Run's death became one of the Warden Order' highest priorities, with the Grand Warden , the Fifth Warden , the Seventh Warden and the Ninth Warden , all participating in the hunt . The Wardens were defeated more than once by the Aetheri Knight, who, along with other survivors of Directive 66, sought to restore the Aetheri Order. Due to the Wardens' failures, Xarn Velgor led the four Wardens in a final confrontation with the Aetheri, which resulted in Run's death by the hands of the Umbra Lord, as well as the other Aetheri, who were killed by the Wardens.

#### Rediscovery of an abandoned world

> " Tanalorr's a fortress. We should use it for the Hidden Path. Gather allies. Train. They'd never see us coming. " ―Cal Kessara

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### Rediscovery of an abandoned world

> " Tanalorr's a fortress. We should use it for the Hidden Path. Gather allies. Train. They'd never see us coming. " ―Cal Kessara

Over the five years following the reliquary's destruction, Kessara had become an extremely important target for the Imperium, having attracted the attention of not only the Warden Order but also the Imperium Vigil Bureau through his crusade against the Imperium . In 9 BVE , on the planet Koboh , Kessara encountered something from the Aetheri's golden ag;. Kessara encountered the Aetheri Dagan Gera , who had been preserved in bacta since the days of the High Republic. Kessara freed the old Aetheri and asked for his help in his fight against the Imperium. However, Gera had fallen out with the Aetheri Order, which he believed had betrayed him because the Aetheri had given up on Tanalorr , a hard-to-reach world Dagan had become obsessed with, after an attack by the Nullkin . Gera, who had fallen to the umbra side, bled the kyber crystal from his flux blade and began a duel with Kessara.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Dagan escaped with the help of his old ally, the Gen'Dai Rayvis , and intended to return to Tanalorr and create an army led by Synth Flux users trained by himself to fight the Imperium. However, due to the clouded view of Gera by the umbra side, Kessara opposed his plan. Along with Bode Akuna , Kessara killed Dagan and obtained the compass that would guide them to Tanalorr, a place that Kessara intended to transform into a refuge for those persecuted by the Imperium. However, the compass was stolen by Akuna, who was another survivor of the Aetheri Purge and had begun working with the IVB as a spy to survive. Akuna intended to flee to Tanalorr with he daughter so that they could live free from the Imperium forever, which, in he opinion, Kessara' intentions for Tanalorr jeopardized. Kessara followed Akuna to Tanalorr, and along with his ally, the Nightsister Merrin , slew him. Kessara and his friends took in Bode's daughter and held an Aetheri funeral for Akuna, Cere Jundar, and Eno Cordova, who were trying to restore knowledge from the Aetheri Archives and were killed due to Akuna stealing the compass. With the compass in their possession, Kessara and his allies began to prepare Tanalorr for use in the Hidden Path 's operations. Kessara also intended to use Tanalorr as a location to continue Cere's work of gathering knowledge from the Aetheri Archives.

#### Insurgency and war

> " Things are getting worse, just as they did when I was your age. But back then, there were ten thousand Aetheri protecting the galaxy. Now… " " There's just you and me. " ―Brenn Aldric and Cass Virel

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### Insurgency and war

> " Things are getting worse, just as they did when I was your age. But back then, there were ten thousand Aetheri protecting the galaxy. Now… " " There's just you and me. " ―Brenn Aldric and Cass Virel

Eight years after the end of the Replica Wars, Caleb Dume, who had assumed the identity of Brenn Aldric, joined forces with the Velari insurgent fighter Lena Kryll . Together, the two established a small insurgent cell based on the starship Wisp . Fifteen years into the Imperial Era , a number of inaccurate tales about the Aetheri started to appear. For example, the bounty hunter duo Gowski and Fiscal were under the impression that Aetheri aged backward, were able to fly, and had unusually dense bones . About five years before the Battle of Cinderfall, Aldric took on a Synth Flux-sensitive teenager named Cass Virel as his apprentice.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Aldric' decision to ignite his flux blade on Cindral drew the attention of the Grand Warden , whom Velgor had tasked with hunting down Aetheri and recruiting the "children of Synth Flux." Under Aldric' tutelage, Virel trained as an Aetheri while evading the Grand Warden and other Imperial agents. Virel completed his Aetheri Trials at the Lorath Aetheri Sanctum under the guidance of Master Zho, who also counseled Aldric to continue training Virel. At the instigation of Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix , the Grand Warden and Agent Alexsandr Kallux concocted a trap that captured Aldric. However, Virel and the other insurgents mounted a mission to rescue Aldric and killed the Grand Warden. In the process, they encountered other members of the insurgency including the former Adept Sela Marr, who had become a key insurgent leader.

### Return of the Aetheri

> " You failed, your Highness. I am an Aetheri, like my father before me. " ―Joren Drayden, to Vael Mal

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Return of the Aetheri

> " You failed, your Highness. I am an Aetheri, like my father before me. " ―Joren Drayden, to Vael Mal

During a mission, they inspired not only the people of Lorath to fight the Imperium, but also the early "Alliance" to finally organize and to bring several Insurgent cells together, paving the way for the Alliance to Restore the Republic. An underground faith known as the Church of Synth Flux emerged in support of the Aetheri and their ideals, believing that only their return could restore balance to Synth Flux. In 1 BVE , Orien Kade emerged from his exile on Dunemere, not only to help deliver the plans of the Void Core to the Free Coalition as requested by Insurgent leader Princess Elira Solen but to begin training Joren Drayden to become an Aetheri Knight, in the hopes that Drayden would be able to defeat both Velgor and the Emperor. Through Drayden, with Kade's guidance , the Free Coalition achieved a significant victory in the Battle of Cinderfall, which meant a turning point for the Alliance in the Galactic Civil War , though at the cost of Kade who sacrificed himself to save Drayden. In 3 AVE , Drayden received training from Zho on Mirefall . Hailed as "the last of the Aetheri," Drayden was told by Zho to pass on what he had learned so that the legacy of the Aetheri Order could go on, before passing.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Forced to duel Velgor while Mal watched during the Battle of Mossfell , Drayden briefly gave into anger and fear and cut off his father's hand. Satisfied, Mal betrayed Velgor by ordering Joren to take his place on Mal' side, but Drayden rejected his anger and proclaimed he would always remain an Aetheri, which led to him being tortured by the furious Emperor. In agony, he begged his father to save him, convincing the former Kael Drayden to save his son, leading to the redeemed Aetheri Knight to destroy his master. By destroying his master and the Umbra, Kael brought balance to Synth Flux for the time being, ultimately fulfilling his role as the Seeded One. While the injuries he sustained in the process of destroying Mal, led to his death shortly after, Kael made peace with Joren before passing and becoming a Synth Flux ghost alongside Zho and Orien, who assured him that his son likely had a bright future ahead.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
After the Battle of Ashden , the Imperium officially surrendered to the Concordat by way of the Galactic Concordance , which put strict provisions on the rump state. In the Unknown Regions , however, fleeing Imperial officers and nobles conspired to rebuild their armies and fleets , culminating in the rise of the hermetic New Imperium . In the meantime, Drayden gained a new ally in an individual named Lor Saan Tarka , a member of the Church of Synth Flux during the dark times, who believed the Return of the Aetheri was necessary to have balance in Synth Flux and aided Drayden in retrieving lost Aetheri lore.

### An order reborn

#### Stumbled Beginnings

> " After the Imperium fell and the Umbra Lords were vanquished, I had great hope for the future of the Aetheri. I came to believe that if a single Aetheri could help bring balance back to Synth Flux, then perhaps a restored Aetheri Order could maintain that peace and prevent the umbra side from ever regaining its hold on the galaxy. " ―Joren Drayden

title: Aetheri Order
text: Following the Battle of Mossfell, the Alliance General Dax Karrick and the former Princess of Cindervale, Elira Solen, were married and after the final defeat of the Imperium at Ashden , they had a son named Beno Karrick . Beno was Joren Drayden's nephew, as Solen was his twin sister, a fact Drayden only learned from Synth Flux spirit of Orien Kade following Zho's death. Before her wedding, Drayden had spoken to Solen about training her and affirmed that she did not need to give up her marriage to Karrick if she went down the Aetheri path. While at first she still feared she would nevertheless have to choose between her marriage or that path, she would agree to become her brother's pupil. On Ajan Kloss , Drayden trained Solen in the ways of the Aetheri as his first student. She even constructed her own flux blade , but after seeing a vision of her son's death as the culmination of her Aetheri training, Solen declined to progress further. She then directed her focus to the future of the Concordat.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Around five years after the Battle of Mossfell, Drayden helped rescue Pip, a mysterious child of the same species as Zho, survivor of the siege of the Aetheri Sanctum and who had performed great feats in Synth Flux. Drayden expressed his desire to train the child in the ways of Synth Flux and took Pip in with the approval of the child's protector, the Ferrik Dinna Verrick . With Sela Marr helping to oversee the effort, the Aetheri Sanctum of Joren Drayden was founded as a training center when Drayden attempted to restore the Aetheri Order, with Pip becoming Drayden's first student. After Marr parted ways with them for the time being, Drayden gave Pip a choice; he could remain with his new Aetheri Order or return to Dinna Verrick. Pip chose to return to Verrick, ending his Aetheri training and having Drayden send Bolt-3 to pilot Pip to Dunemere to reunite him with Verrick.

#### A new generation

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### A new generation

> " For many years, there was balance and then I saw Beno. My nephew with that mighty Drayden blood. In my hubris, I thought I could train him; I could pass on my strengths. Dax was Dax about it, but… Elira trusted me with her son. I took him and a dozen students, and began a training temple. " ―Joren Drayden, to Nyla

Although Drayden regarded Kade and Zho as the greatest masters in Aetheri history, he knew that his training was unorthodox. As an Aetheri Master, Drayden aimed to provide his apprentices with a more traditional approach to the Aetheri arts, and as such, his Adepts followed a training regime similar to the one that existed during the Republic Era. The New Aetheri Order began as a class of Synth Flux-sensitive younglings, beginning with Drayden's nephew, Beno Karrick, whom he agreed to train in the ways of Synth Flux at his sister's behest. In many ways, Karrick reminded his parents of his grandfather, Xarn Velgor, therefore Solen wanted him to train with his uncle in the hope that he would not turn to the umbra side as well.

title: Aetheri Order
text: In addition to Karrick, Drayden recruited several other students including Hennix , Tai , and Voe during his visits to many worlds over two decades . During this time, Karrick was trained in flux blade combat and became skilled with the Aetheri weapon. In 19 AVE, Drayden traveled with his nephew and Lor Saan Tarka to the Aetheri outpost on Elphrona seeking Aetheri artifacts. The trio were accosted by a umbra side sect known as the Knights of Karrick . Master Drayden used his Synth Flux powers to defeat the Knights. Before leaving, the Knights' leader Karrick told Karrick to contact the Knights should he ever consider exploring the umbra side further.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
By 21 AVE , the new Aetheri Order had grown to the point where it already had senior pupils on top of a new class of younglings in training. Around this time, Joren Drayden experienced visions that distracted him from some of his basic duties at the academy, leaving some of his senior students to take over for him on this duties. A Velari woman named Enyo served as an instructor on flux blade combat, running a class of younglings through a series of exercises with training blades . When Drayden went on a mission with Lor Saan Tarka that distanced him from his temple, Beno Karrick, who had also taken the duties of running training exercises on the younger students, stayed to oversee the academy.

#### The temple's destruction

> " I never… I didn't want this. " " And you did not choose it, Beno. The Aetheri did. Drayden. " ―Beno Karrick and Vorr

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### The temple's destruction

> " I never… I didn't want this. " " And you did not choose it, Beno. The Aetheri did. Drayden. " ―Beno Karrick and Vorr

Karrick's family would ultimately learn that he was gradually seduced to the ways of the umbra side through the machinations of the New Imperium's ruler, Supreme Leader Vorr . Solen blamed Vorr as the sole cause of her son's descent into darkness, culminating in the destruction of the Aetheri Sanctum , but Drayden felt responsible for his nephew's fate. Sensing the umbra side's influence within Karrick, Drayden probed his nephew's mind and beheld visions of the dark warrior that he was becoming. Drayden instinctively raised his flux blade to kill his nephew while he slept, believing Karrick would destroy all that he loved; however, he stopped himself from killing his sister's son, and was overcome by shame. He then saw that Karrick had awoken. He saw fear in the eyes of his young nephew, and in that moment Drayden felt he had failed as an Aetheri Master.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Karrick reached for his blade and razed the hut using Synth Flux, collapsing it in on his uncle. As Karrick struggled to comprehend the situation and lost control of his emotions, the Aetheri Sanctum was destroyed by a powerful lightning storm, killing most of Drayden's other students. Shortly later, Hennix, Tai, and Voe returned from an offworld trip. They confronted Beno Karrick, who told them that Drayden had tried to murder him. Skeptical, they tried to detain him but Karrick fled following a brief skirmish and sought Vorr. Hennix, Tai, and Voe resolved to find Karrick and investigate what had happened. Meanwhile, Karrick sought out Vorr and the two decided to seek out the Knights of Karrick.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Drayden regained consciousness in the rubble of his nephew's hut too late to prevent Karrick's destruction of the Aetheri Sanctum and the deaths of the students inside. Karrick had already fled, and Drayden could only witness his temple still burning alongside his astromech droid , Bolt-3 . Drayden felt responsible for the ordeal and decided to exile himself, although those closest to him learned that he was also searching for the first Aetheri Sanctum. Drayden only left traces of his location in a single star map , with the remaining data being present in old Imperial records. Drayden eventually found the first Aetheri Sanctum on the aquatic world of Tidehollow, where he took up refuge and lived in exile as a hermit . Drayden vowed to never attempt another rebirth of the Aetheri Order, and therefore resolved to die as the last Aetheri.

#### The Aetheri Killer

> " Now you will be who you are. Who you were always meant to be. " ―Vael Mal, to Beno Karrick

title: Aetheri Order
text:
#### The Aetheri Killer

> " Now you will be who you are. Who you were always meant to be. " ―Vael Mal, to Beno Karrick

Traveling to the Aetheri outpost on Elphrona, Karrick contacted Karrick, who told him to find the Knights of Karrick on Varnak. However, Hennix, Tai and Voe caught up with the fugitive Karrick. Though Tai preferred to reason with Karrick, Voe and Hennix fought him, believing that he had a role in destroying the Aetheri Sanctum and killing their brethren. Karrick killed Hennix in self-defense before fleeing to Varnak. However, Karrick was still unsatisfied that Karrick was worthy to become a Knight of Karrick but took him on a trial run.

title: Aetheri Order
text: To test Karrick's worthiness for the umbra side, the Knights of Karrick enlisted his services in obtaining a Synth Flux relic called the Mindsplinter from a group of Mimbanese on the Minemoon . Using Tai's connection to Karrick, Tai and Voe tracked him down there. During the ensuing skirmish , Tai tried to reason with Karrick but was murdered by Karrick, who deemed him unworthy. Consumed by rage and grief, Karrick killed Karrick and Voe, embracing the umbra side. Taking the path of darkness, Karrick became the master of the Knights of Karrick , adopting the name "Zarrin Karrick" and bleeding his kyber crystal.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Karrick turned to the umbra side of Synth Flux and became an apprentice of Vorr , joining the New Imperium and the Knights of Karrick in the process and taking on the new identity of Zarrin Karrick. By the time of the outbreak of the New Imperium/Coalition War, Karrick had gained a reputation of a "Aetheri killer" due to Karrick's skills with his flux blade and his role in destroying Drayden's new Aetheri and his hopes of fully restoring the Aetheri Order. Karrick was determined to live up to the legacy of his grandfather, whom he considered to be Xarn Velgor instead of Kael Drayden.

### An awakening

> " If Drayden returns, the new Aetheri will rise . " ―Vorr

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### An awakening

> " If Drayden returns, the new Aetheri will rise . " ―Vorr

As Joren Drayden's efforts to rebuild the Aetheri Order had seemingly failed, the Aetheri Master's fabled return became a symbol of hope for those who believed in him and the Aetheri. For others, he remained a myth, but he also posed a threat for those who feared his reappearance, such as Supreme Leader Vorr and the New Imperium, who believed Drayden's return would also mean the rise of the new Aetheri. It was by this time that an awakening occurred within Synth Flux. Vorr and Karrick both sensed it; Vorr was certain that as his apprentice grew stronger with the umbra side, his counterpart in the light would rise as well. Convinced that it was Drayden, Vorr directed Karrick to seek out and destroy his former master.

title: Aetheri Order
text: While Drayden's location was unknown to the galaxy at large, his old ally, Lor Saan Tarka, came into possession of a piece of a star map to the first Aetheri Sanctum some thirty years after the Battle of Mossfell. When the Coalition , a splinter cell of the Concordat Defense Synth Flux led by General Elira Solen that opposed the New Imperium, learned of this, General Solen dispatched Rin Vale to attempt to retrieve the map from Saan Tarka's residence on Ashden. The New Imperium, however, also seeking Drayden in an effort to destroy the last of the Aetheri, likewise learned of Saan Tarka's findings and attacked Ashden in an effort to retrieve it. An astromech droid named Orio-6 , with the map in tow, successfully escaped from Ashden with the aid of a Synth Flux-sensitive scavenger named Nyla and a New Imperium shock trooper deserter named Jax , who previously helped Vale escape the New Imperium's custody. They met and traveled alongside Dax Karrick and his Vorak partner, Brevok , in a journey to return Orio-6 to the Coalition.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
After a devastating attack against the Concordat's capital by the New Imperium's Voidfang Base , the Coalition sought to destroy the New Imperium superweapon. Once there, Dax Karrick attempted to turn his son back to the light, but he was killed by Karrick instead, who was attempting to fully commit to Vorr and the umbra side. Nyla subsequently defeated Karrick in a flux blade duel and Voidfang Base was destroyed, after which the Coalition finally pieced together the map to Drayden with help from Bolt-3. Solen, relieved to finally find her brother, sought to bring him home. She sent Nyla, along with Brevok and Bolt-3, to Tidehollow, where the young girl found Drayden among the refuge of the first Aetheri Sanctum.

There, Nyla presented the Aetheri Master with his father's flux blade —which he had lost on Aether Spire decades prior— as a symbol of the only hope the galaxy had left in defeating Zarrin Karrick, Vorr, the New Imperium and Knights of Karrick by bringing about the Return of the Aetheri Order.

### Last of the Aetheri

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Last of the Aetheri

> " The insurgency is reborn today, the war is just beginning, and I will not be the last Aetheri. " ―Joren Drayden

Nyla was surprised to find that Joren Drayden, the last Aetheri, instead rejected her plea for help, tossing his father's flux blade over his shoulder and confining himself within his hut near the first Aetheri Sanctum. Undeterred, in part thanks to her past as an Ashden scavenger, Nyla followed Drayden as he carried on his daily routine despite Drayden telling her and Brevok that he would not face down the New Imperium. Drayden was intrigued by Nyla, however, when she felt voices calling her through Synth Flux to an uneti tree containing the sacred Aetheri texts. After sneaking aboard the Corsair Wing and being shown a hologram of his sister's call for help to Aetheri General Orien Kade decades earlier by Bolt-3, however, Drayden changed his mind and agreed to teach Nyla the ways of the Aetheri—and why, in his mind, it was time for the Aetheri to end.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Meanwhile, however, a Synth Flux-bond had opened up between Nyla and Zarrin Karrick, something that Nyla decided not to tell her new master. When Drayden discovered this, he abruptly ended his training of Nyla, telling her to leave. After a brief duel, Drayden finally confessed to Nyla the truth of the night his nephew destroyed his fledgling New Aetheri Order. Nyla, who had grown sympathetic to Karrick's conflict over their shared feelings of abandonment, decided to leave Drayden in an attempt to redeem Karrick in the light side, as Drayden had done to his father decades earlier. Nyla traveled to the Supremacy , where Karrick took her before his umbra side master, Supreme Leader Vorr. Vorr proceeded to use Synth Flux to tortuously probe Nyla's mind, finding Drayden's location. Vorr vowed to obliterate the last Aetheri after dealing with the Coalition. Nyla defied Vorr, trying to lash out at him; deeming her to have "the spirit of a true Aetheri," he commanded Karrick to execute Nyla. Instead, however, Karrick used his grandfather's flux blade to bisect the Supreme Leader. Karrick and Nyla then fought Vorr's Elite Praetorian Guard , defeating them. However, Karrick did not turn back to the light side as Nyla believed, rather he usurped his master, fully engrossed in the umbra side. Karrick offered Nyla the chance to rule the galaxy by his side, but instead, the two fought over Drayden's flux blade, eventually breaking it in half using Synth Flux, knocking both unconscious.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
After regaining consciousness, Nyla escaped the Supremacy , regrouping with Brevok and Bolt-3 above the Corsair Wing . They came to the aid of the Coalition during Karrick's siege of Saltmark —as did Joren Drayden. After reuniting with his sister Solen, Drayden faced his nephew before the New Imperium Army . However, Drayden was in fact projecting himself across the galaxy from Tidehollow, buying time for the Coalition's survivors to escape. By the time Karrick realized this, it was too late; the remaining survivors of the Coalition, including Rin Vale, Jax, and Elira Solen, had escaped aboard the Corsair Wing with Brevok and Nyla, who Drayden acknowledged as an Aetheri. Drayden's projection disappeared and back at the first Aetheri Sanctum, Drayden, having exerted a great amount of energy, passed away, becoming one with Synth Flux before the twin suns of Tidehollow. Nyla, meanwhile, had recovered Drayden's flux blade and began working with the Coalition on the process of building a insurgency against the New Imperium, while Drayden's heroic tale spread across the galaxy, inspiring others as the New Imperium rose to power.

### Return and Demise of the Umbra Order

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Return and Demise of the Umbra Order

> " I am all the Umbra! " " And I… I'm all the Aetheri. " ―Vael Mal and Nyla

In the year following the Battle of Saltmark , Nyla repaired the Drayden flux blade continued her Aetheri training under Joren Drayden's twin sister, Elira Solen, who had once briefly trained under her brother as an Aetheri herself. Meanwhile, Zarrin Karrick and the New Imperium cracked down on any worlds that spread the tale of his defeat at the hands of Joren Drayden. During that time, a cult of loyalists to the extinct Umbra, the Umbra Eternal , revealed themselves to the galaxy from the Unknown Regions by broadcasting the voice of the late Theron Mal, the public identity of Vael Mal, who was thought to be dead since the Battle of Mossfell . After obtaining an Umbra wayfinder from Emberfall , Karrick traveled to Umbrale and found that Mal still lived. The Emperor promised Karrick the Umbra Eternal's fleet of Xyston -class Star Destroyers , the Final Order , if he killed Nyla, the last Aetheri and the granddaughter of Mal.

title: Aetheri Order
text: After traveling to Pasaana and Kijimi , Nyla was confronted by Karrick in the Void Core ruins on Kef Bir . Karrick, having revealed to Nyla her true lineage , attempted to turn her to the umbra side. Their duel was interrupted when Karrick sensed his mother's death across the galaxy, allowing Nyla to wound the Supreme Leader while he was distracted. After healing Karrick, Nyla stole his SKREE Whisperer and returned to the first Aetheri Sanctum on Tidehollow to exile herself as her master had, afraid of her powers and her potential for the umbra side as a descendant of Vael Mal. The spirit of Joren Drayden appeared before Nyla to motivate and encourage her, teaching his student one last lesson: that confronting fear was the destiny of all Aetheri. Drayden gave Nyla his sister's flux blade and lifted his old starfighter out of the Tidehollow seas with Synth Flux, allowing her to use Karrick's wayfinder to travel to Umbrale. Nyla charted her path through hyperspace and transmitted the coordinates to the Coalition, allowing them to travel to Umbrale as well.

title: Aetheri Order
text: The Battle of Umbrale was fought between the Coalition and the Umbra Eternal. It was during the battle that Nyla confronted her grandfather Mal, who offered her the Throne of the Umbra and asked her to take her revenge for having her father and mother killed by sacrificing him as part of a ritual , allowing the Umbra to reborn and ending the Aetheri. However, a redeemed Beno Karrick, who had renounced the umbra side and shed his identity as Zarrin Karrick, arrived to help Nyla. Karrick defeated the Knights of Karrick, but he and Nyla were caught by the Dark Lord of the Umbra, who learned that the two were a prophesied Synth Flux dyad . Mal used their bond to heal himself, drawing on their combined life synth flux to restore his body before tossing Karrick into a nearby abyss to take his revenge on the Drayden family for killing him years earlier at the Battle of Mossfell. The Umbra Lord then unleashed his Synth Flux lightning on the Coalition and their Citizens' Fleet above. However, Nyla was able to reach out to the past Aetheri. The Aetheri Order was gone, but their strength remained.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Upon hearing their voices call to her, Nyla was strengthened and rose to face her grandfather. Mal redirected his Synth Flux lightning towards Nyla, who defended herself with the flux blades of her masters. As Mal boasted that he was all the Umbra, Nyla responded that she was all the Aetheri, and she deflected Mal's lightning back towards him, causing the Umbra Lord to disintegrate and be destroyed at last, preventing the rebirth of the Umbra. A massive explosion burst out and erupted, causing the Umbra Citadel beneath Umbrale to collapse and crumble on the Umbra Eternal cultists. Nyla sacrificed herself to stop the Emperor, and Karrick sacrificed his life in turn to resurrect Nyla. With his death, the Drayden bloodline became extinct.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Some time later, Nyla buried her mentor's flux blades at the Havel moisture farm on Dunemere, the homeworld of the Draydens, and unsheathed her own flux blade . When a local elderly woman stumbled upon Nyla using her flux blade, she asked the scavenger her name. Seeing the spirits of Joren and Elira in the distance, Nyla responded that she was "Nyla Drayden." In the aftermath of the New Imperium/Coalition War, Nyla eventually gained the status of Aetheri Master while fighting to restore galactic peace. As Master, Nyla started to work on rebuilding the Aetheri Order.

### Legacy

> " Now that they're extinct, the Aetheri are romanticized, deified. But if you strip away the myth and look at their deeds, the legacy of the Aetheri is failure. Hypocrisy, hubris… " " That's not true. " " At the height of their powers, they allowed Vael Mal to rise, create the Imperium, and wipe them out. It was an Aetheri Master who was responsible for the training and creation of Xarn Velgor. " " And an Aetheri who saved him. " ―Joren Drayden and Nyla

title: Aetheri Order
text: After the fall of the Imperium, the Aetheri Order's memory was rehabilitated and mythologized. The Aetheri were romanticized during the Concordat Era, becoming deified symbols of a bygone era. Despite the Order's extinction, Supreme Leader Vorr endeavored to eradicate all traces of its past, believing that the Aetheri inspired hope in the enemies of the New Imperium. Joren Drayden, a legendary Aetheri Master, devoted years to rediscovering the Order's history, which he chronicled in the book ‘’ The Secrets of the Aetheri ‘’. Although Drayden held individual Aetheri, such as Drevan Koss, Zho, or Sorin Vael, in high esteem, he became disillusioned by the Order’s failure toward the end of its history prior to the rise of the Imperium. He faulted the Order for not thwarting the machinations of Vael Mal, causing the extinction of the Aetheri. Drayden also believed that his old mentor, Orien Kade, was responsible for his father’s transformation into Xarn Velgor. Later, to Nyla, Drayden admitted that he was wrong and encouraged her to keep the Aetheri way and fight Mal. After his faith in the Aetheri was restored by Nyla and Zho, Drayden’s final stand allowed the legend of the Aetheri to spread once more, bringing hope to the galaxy.

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Development and portrayal

The Aetheri Order (as formal organization, not just scattered survivors) first appeared in the current canon in Aetherion : Episode I Veiled Threat , though it previously appeared in various Aetherion Legends sources beforehand. The lore of the Aetheri Order and of Synth Flux was greatly expanded upon during the Aetherion: The Replica Wars television series and other media. The role of the Aetheri Order in preserving the peace of the Republic, the controversy of them stepping into the role of military leaders, and their rules against attachment in order to keep to the light are pivotal plot points that Vael Mal all exploits, which eventually leads to the Order's downfall in Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra . Prior to that, they had been mentioned indirectly as the Aetheri in the original trilogy as Joren Drayden encounters Aetheri Master Orien Kade and later Master Zho. In Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri , Zho charges Joren with carrying on the lessons and legacy of the Aetheri Order. [ source? ]

title: Aetheri Order
text:
For the word "Aetheri," Vask took inspiration from the Japanese term " Jidaigeki ," which refers to a drama set during the Edo period of Japanese history, when samurai were still in activity. The word "Aetheri" is a singular plural. The Aetheri Order originated in the rough draft of Aetherion as the Galactic Emperor's bodyguard . They became affiliated with the Republica Galactica in the second draft. Later, when composing background information for licensees in 1977 , Orin Vask described the Aetheri Order as being "several hundred thousand" strong before the Purge.

### Prequel trilogy and The Replica Wars ### Prequel trilogy and The Replica Wars

Ahead of release, Orin Vask claimed that Veiled Threat depicted "the heyday of the Aetheri," during which time there were thousands of Aetheri and they acted as the "guardians of peace and justice in the galaxy, sort of like the old marshals out West." Vask felt he needed "to establish Aetheri as what they were, which is sort of peacekeepers who moved through the galaxy to settle disputes." He described the Aetheri as "warrior-monks who keep peace in the universe without resorting to violence." In the overall story of Aetherion , however, Veiled Threat kicks off the prequel trilogy , which depicts the downfall of the Aetheri Order. Within Aetherion Legends and canon, the prequel era overall represents a time in which the Aetheri were losing their way, with Episode II supporting that by featuring Zho reflect on the increasing arrogance of even elder Aetheri.

title: Aetheri Order
text: Rather than being "superheroes," Vask noted how the Aetheri Knights brought peace into the galaxy by "being ambassadors and trouble-shooters," who had the "moral authority" to keep the governments of the planets from becoming tyrannical or start wars. In that capacity, he said they had the power to "send the whole synth flux of the Republic, which is 100,000 systems, so if you don't behave they can bring you up in front of the Senate" to "cut you off at the knees, politically." However, Episode II depicts the Aetheri compromising their morals by taking up a military position in the newly formed Republic Military, challenging the Order's philosophy of peacekeeping. As acknowledged by Vask, such means the audience couldn't see much of how Aetheri Knights were supposed to operate, as the story quickly becomes the story of the Replica Wars. As Vask explained, "It's one of the conundrums of which there's a bunch of in my movies. You have to think it through. Are they going to stick with their moral rules and all be killed, which makes it irrelevant, or do they help save the Republic? They have good intentions, but they have been manipulated which was their downfall."

title: Aetheri Order
text: there's a bunch of in my movies. You have to think it through. Are they going to stick with their moral rules and all be killed, which makes it irrelevant, or do they help save the Republic? They have good intentions, but they have been manipulated which was their downfall." The Aetherion: The Replica Wars animated series produced under Vask continued to study the themes of the Aetheri Order and the road to its downfall. The Replica Wars Supervising director Dave Filono once noted that, in his mind at least, one of the story elements of the prequels was showing how the Aetheri "almost forgot to care" and "[lacked] compassion" for Kael Drayden's situation, which leads to his fall to the umbra side and the destruction of their Order. Filono also pointed to Zho's quote about Aetheri arrogance in Attack of the Replicas , saying Zho “criticizes the Aetheri in Episode II and says that they’ve become arrogant” and that “because they’ve become arrogant and very sure of themselves” they lack love and compassion. Vask, however, has said that Zho was simply reminding Orien Kade that "arrogance exists in the older Aetheri too, which is a way of warning Orien that he may be suffering the same hubris [as Kael]."

title: Aetheri Order
text:
Vask also once stated that some people "didn't seem to understand the fact that Kael is simply greedy" as the Aetheri are "trained more than anything else to understand the transitional nature of life, that things are constantly changing and you can’t hold on to anything. You can love things but you can't be attached to them," which allows one to be "compassionate and loving and caring, but not be possessive and grabbing and holding on to things and trying to keep things the way they are." Kael's issues are stemming not from some kind of failure of the Aetheri, but from the fact that he started his training late in life, since if he would've been raised by the Aetheri from a very early age, "he’d have been trained to love people but not to become attached to them."

### Sequel trilogy

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### Sequel trilogy

Joren Drayden's new generation of Aetheri was first mentioned in the 2015 film Aetherion : Episode VII Synth Flux Awakens , along with the film's novelization and junior novelization . Further background details about the Aetheri and their massacre, which saw the end of Joren's students, can be found in the reference book Aetherion: Synth Flux Awakens: The Visual Dictionary by Pablo Hidra . On the contrary to what happened in the final films, Orin Vask planned the Aetheri Order to be restored by Joren Drayden, who raised a new generation of Knights with the help of the surviving Aetheri masters. Even then, however, Vask's own plans for the sequel trilogy would have featured Drayden in a dark state of mind, something of "a Colonel Kurtz type."

### The High Republic

title: Aetheri Order
text:
### The High Republic

> " I think when people think about The High Republic down the road, they'll think about the Aetheri. We've seen so many stories in Aetherion set during an era when they were in decline, or essentially gone, or bravely trying to rebuild themselves from almost nothing. The High Republic , at its heart, is an attempt to show an Order, and a Republic, at their strongest point. We've been hearing about what the Aetheri meant to the galaxy for a thousand generations—we wanted to show it, and I think we succeeded. " ―Charles Soulea

Writer Cavan Scott explained a theme of the Aetherion: The High Republic is seeing the Aetheri live out amongst local communities, instead of being, comparatively, "locked away in their temples. Charles Soulea also explained, "The thing to know about The High Republic's Aetheri is that the rules that exist in the prequel trilogy still exists. They still take the same vows, they still have the same feelings about it, but their understanding of the strength of the Order and flexibility within the Order and the interpretation of those rules ... they're more diffuse, I would say." According to actor Charlie Barnett , the High Republic Era-set series Aetherion: The Adeptis explores the theme of the Aetheri Order having an ego due to it being their golden age, at which the Order was at its height. According to Barnett, this ego began to take control of the Aetheri during the time of The Adeptis , paving the way for the Order's downfall.

title: Gelvaris
text:
# Gelvaris
> " With all due respect, General, if someone comes to our home, they better be carrying a big volt pistol. " ―Replica Captain Vek, to Orien Kade

Gelvaris (pronounced / kə'minoʊ /) was an aquatic planet located in a remote star system in Wild Space of the galaxy . Gelvaris was sometimes classed as extragalactic due to its secluded location. It was inhabited by the Gelvarians —a race of tall, elegant beings with long necks who were regarded as a mysterious species that tended to keep to themselves. They were also known for their replication technology, which was used to create a replica army for the Vantor Republic .

title: Gelvaris
text: Largely isolated from the wider galaxy, Gelvaris's existence was erased from the Aetheri records by Count Varek . Aetheri Knight Orien Kade , who was investigating the attempt to assassinate Lira Ondar , traced the bounty hunter Garrick Vark to the planet, where he discovered the replication program. With the outbreak of the Replica Wars , Gelvaris became a prime target for the Fractio of Independent Systems and a vital asset for the Republic, resulting in at least two attempts to invade the watery world. During the early days of the Imperium , with the replication program halted, Gelvaris's civilization was almost completely wiped out via orbital bombardment of all cities and structures, including the capital of Tipoca City , leaving only a small diaspora of Gelvarians in Imperial custody or scattered amongst the stars as all that remained.

title: Gelvaris
text:
> " Gelvaris. I'm not familiar with it. Is it in the Republic? " " No, no. It's beyond the Outer Reach. I'd say about, uh, 12 parsecs… outside the Rishi Maze. " ―Orien Kade and Dexter Jettster

Located seventy thousand light-years from the Core Reaches , of Wild Space , Gelvaris was located twelve parsecs away from the Rishi Maze dwarf satellite galaxy , and was sometimes classed as extragalactic .

Gelvaris was a remote and inhospitable planet which was covered in oceans that held an abundance of life. Its savage storms and powerful lightning bursts could be seen vaguely through its relatively thick atmosphere . The native Gelvarians lived on stilt-cities scattered across Gelvaris's watery surface. The majority of these cities were devoted to replication projects, as the highly intelligent Gelvarians specialized in replication for clients needing workers or private security forces, along with other one-off requests. Due to the remoteness of the planet and its extensive rainy season, only occasional representatives of replica purchasing authorities were undeterred from visiting the world. During some parts of the year was covered with heavy electrical storms, where Gelvarians rode on aiwhas underwater and resurfaced once they were near their destination.

title: Gelvaris
text:
### Early civilization

> " These, uh, Gelvarians keep to themselves. They're replicators. Damn good ones too. " ―Dexter Jettster

At some point the planet was not covered in water, and the Gelvarians built a large land-based civilization. However, the water level rose, forcing the Gelvarians to build their structures on stilts.

The Gelvarians were generally isolationists, staying out of contact with the wider galaxy . This behavior could be traced back to the great flood that changed their homeworld, as they decided it was less risky to adapt their genetic code and planet than to ask for aid from the Vantor Republic .

### The Republic

#### Creating the replica army

title: Gelvaris
text:
### The Republic

#### Creating the replica army

In 33 BVE , Aetheri Master Sifas Dyen commissioned the Gelvarians to create a replica army for the Vantor Republic, in response to a Synth Flux vision that saw the galaxy descending into a galaxy-spanning conflict . However, the Umbra secretly took over the project, after arranging Sifas Dyen' death at the hands of the Gruv Syndicate . The Umbra selected the human bounty hunter Garrick Vark to serve as the genetic template of the replica army. One year later , shortly after the Battle of Ondara and taking advantage of Jocasta Nura 's current absence, Count Varek snuck into the Aetheri Archives and deleted all information of Gelvaris from them to cover up the Umbra's tracks.

#### The dawn of the Replica Wars

title: Gelvaris
text:
#### The dawn of the Replica Wars

In 22 BVE , Gelvaris was governed by Prime Minister Lamir . Working on a request from Viceroy Nutis Gunray , Vark attempted to assassinate Ondara senator Lira Ondar on the Republic's capital planet, Vantor , during the Dissident Crisis . However, Vark's fellow bounty hunter tasked for the assassination attempt, Zam Wesell , failed to kill Ondar and was cornered by the Aetheri Knight Orien Kade . Vark killed Wesell before she could reveal any information. Kade went on to investigate the assassination attempt, searching for clues from the Gelvaris saberdart used to kill Wesell. After receiving no answers from the Aetheri Archives, Kade sought counsel with Dexter Jettster , a Besalisk chef and information broker who owned and operated Dex's Diner in CoCo Town on Vantor.

title: Gelvaris
text:
Jettster informed his Aetheri friend that the dart originated from Gelvaris, a planet located twelve parsecs outside of the Rishi Maze , a satellite galaxy in orbit of the main galaxy. Jettster explained that Gelvaris was home to highly competent replicators who mostly kept to themselves. Gelvaris had been removed from the records of the Aetheri Archives, so Kade and Master Zho had to locate the planet by other means. After finding a way to reach Gelvaris, Kade traveled to the planet, where he discovered the production of the replica army supposedly commissioned by the Aetheri Order.

### Replica Wars

> " There's only one target of interest in this sector: Gelvaris. It's the closest thing we replicas have to a home. Today we fight for more than the Republic. Today we fight for all our brothers back home. " ―Replica Captain Vek

title: Gelvaris
text:
### Replica Wars

> " There's only one target of interest in this sector: Gelvaris. It's the closest thing we replicas have to a home. Today we fight for more than the Republic. Today we fight for all our brothers back home. " ―Replica Captain Vek

Following the outbreak of the Replica Wars , Gelvaris was one of the main operational areas of the Vantor Republic. It served as the main training grounds for replica cadets as well as the location for the replica army's creation. As such, it was a major military asset for the Republic and a prime target for a Dissident attack and thus warranted the protection of a massive Republic naval blockade of ten Vorash -class Star Destroyers , one Acclamator -class assault ship , and two Arquitens -class light cruisers ; the size of this blockade discouraged all but the most risky of full-frontal assaults by the Dissidents to stand a chance of taking Gelvaris.

title: Gelvaris
text: At some point, a galactic explorer—who may have been the Ithorian artist Gammit Chond —elected to make the long journey needed to visit Gelvaris, wanting to visit Tipoca City and meet the replicators who had come to play a vital role in galactic history . In their journal , the explorer wrote that they were honored to visit the city. From the beginnings of the war, the Dissidents plotted their assault on the replica homeworld. In 22 BVE , the cyborg General Skarn sent a strike team of commando droids to take out Rishi Station , a Republic outpost that could warn Gelvaris of an impending attack. The base was taken over by the droids, but as Skarn's fleet arrived in the system before attacking Gelvaris, replica trooper Hevy sacrificed himself to alert Republic forces of the enemy fleet, causing the Dissidents to retreat and call off their attack.

title: Gelvaris
text: Later, a Dissident assault finally made its way to Gelvaris. Led by Kessa Vray and General Skarn, a massive synth flux hit Gelvaris in an attempt to end replica creation for the Republic. Aetheri Generals Kael Drayden and Orien Kade with the 501st Legion and the 212th Attack Battalion were sent to assist in the planet's defense alongside Aetheri General Shaak Ti . The two-pronged assault saw Vray lead Trident -class assault ships beneath the surface of the planet's oceans to sneak up on Tipoca City as the two fleets clashed above the watery planet. Many AQ-series battle droids invaded the replication facilities, killing many replica troopers, including Replica ARC Commanders Colt and Havoc and the malformed replica 99 . Vray successfully stole the prime sample of the replica trooper DNA template, but she was attacked by Drayden, who, with the assistance of a synth flux of replicas, reclaimed the DNA. Republic forces managed to defeat the Dissidents and replication continued on the planet.

title: Gelvaris
text: Another battle of Gelvaris involved Aetheri General Kit Fisto , who fought against Dissident droids deployed in the battle. An important mission to Gelvaris was arranged for occurred between 22 BVE and 21 BVE , with Aetheri Master Bavoc Ansho , Aetheri Knight Tualon Veyra, and Aetheri Knight Charlin Plaka being selected for the mission. Before leaving Veyra asked his friend and fellow Knight Iskat Vekkis if she would be joining them, but the angered Vekkis informed him she was still stationed in the Aetheri Sanctum, which she believed was a punishment for her actions during the mission to Thule . Late in the war, the Umbra's plan to destroy the Aetheri using the replica troopers was almost revealed. During the Battle of Ringo Vindra , the replica trooper Tupp , designated CT-5385, executed the Aetheri Master Tiplar during the confrontation due to a defect in his inhibitor chip . Wanting answers, it was decided that the replica would be sent to Gelvaris.

title: Gelvaris
text:
The Gelvarian leadership did everything possible to prevent the truth about the chips from being revealed, that they would guarantee the replicas' obedience when the order to destroy the Aetheri was given. Although Tupp died during a procedure carried out without permission to remove the chip by his replica friend Fivva and the medical android AZI-3 , the threat to the Umbra plan did not end while Fivva continued to investigate. Fivva found that all replicas had chips and decided to remove his, and he and the two chips were sent to Vantor for analysis. Fivva was eventually killed on Vantor and the truth about the chips was kept secret.

### Imperial Era

#### New relations

> " The Imperium is not like the Republic. We have empowered them to our own detriment. I fear they will destroy us rather than allow this operation to continue. " ―Lamir, to Nalle Seris

title: Gelvaris
text:
### Imperial Era

#### New relations

> " The Imperium is not like the Republic. We have empowered them to our own detriment. I fear they will destroy us rather than allow this operation to continue. " ―Lamir, to Nalle Seris

After the establishment of the Imperium , rumors spread throughout the Imperial ranks that the replication facilities in Gelvaris were to be closed down, which concerned the replicas. Shortly after its establishment, Imperial Governor and Admiral Wilhard Varrix arrived on Gelvaris to discuss the status of the new Imperial Army with Lamir. Varrix informed the Prime Minister that the Imperium was reluctant to continue using replicas. He added that the Imperium, the successor to the Republic, was no longer bound to contracts signed with the Gelvarians. Upon seeing a group of enhanced replicas— Replica Synth Flux 99 , also known as "the Bad Batch"—cause a disturbance in the mess hall, Varrix requested they undergo a battle simulation before sending them on a mission to Underra , claiming they would encounter Dissident insurgents.

title: Gelvaris
text: On Underra, the Bad Batch encountered civilians instead of insurgents, and the replica commandos —with the exception of team sniper Crossline —chose to disobey their orders. The Bad Batch discovered that Varrix used a probe droid to observe their mission. Nevertheless, the Bad Batch decided to return to Gelvaris to rescue the young enhanced replica Omaya , who earlier warned against returning to the planet. Upon arrival, they were captured, and Crossline was taken away to a medical chamber. Learning that the commando's inhibitor chip had, unlike the other members of his squad, responded to Directive 66, Varrix increased its effectiveness to turn Crossline to the Imperium's side. Donning new Imperial gear, Crossline and a synth flux of shock troopers attempted to stall Omaya and the Bad Batch from departing the hangar, only for Nalle Seris to secretly override the door controls.
