Karrick felt liberated by Vorr's death because it granted him the power and independence he had long coveted. He had no intention of ever serving another master and was, therefore, fiercely protective of his new rank. Like Velgor before him, Karrick believed it was his destiny to rule over the weaker beings of the galaxy. He dreamed of conquering the galaxy with Nyla at his side.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: If Karrick had chosen his own title, it would have been "Master of the Umbra side" or "Commander of the Knights of Karrick" rather than "Supreme Leader;" however, he considered the title right and just for himself as the head of the New Imperium. Embracing an authoritarian style of leadership, he believed that all people and their worlds must bend to his will. He was determined to show the New Imperium's true power to the galaxy and expected it to be met with gratitude. Karrick enjoyed the simplicity of fascism. Wielding absolute power reminded him of his grandfather, Karrick, like Velgor, was a leader who expected total obedience from his followers and punished those who failed him. Relic hunter Mika Grey once taunted Agent Raith with such knowledge, remarking that Karrick would surely punish the New Imperium Raider if he returned without any artifacts to show for himself.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick had little tolerance for those who defied him to his face, especially after he became the Supreme Leader. Defiance against the New Imperium, which he considered the greatest regime in the galaxy, perplexed him. Karrick did not understand why a person would reject a life of security under his rule, risking one's life just to show their contempt for the New Imperium. However, he was interested in understanding the views of those who opposed him, though he considered them "radicals" for doing so. Regardless of their reasons, he still intended to punish an entire world and its population if they resisted his authority. Ultimately, Karrick believed that coalition was futile, and that it was his right to lead the galaxy as the Supreme Leader of the New Imperium.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick was also distrustful of others; having isolated himself from his family and friends, the only people in Karrick's life were subordinates and a master that he hated. Gaining the title of Supreme Leader only made Karrick more suspicious of the individuals around him, particularly Vren, but also Pryde and Vael Mal. After the duel with Nyla on Kef Bir, Karrick questioned his beliefs and regretted the choices he made. His parents' love for him and Nyla's compassion brought him back to the light, destroying the persona of Zarrin Karrick. Although he still carried feelings of guilt and self-doubt within him, he later recognized them as remnants of Vorr's conditioning that led Karrick to become Zarrin Karrick. Having reconciled with his father in spirit, Karrick hoped that one day he would come to forgive himself.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Karrick's personality and his former persona as Karrick were different in several ways, as observed by both himself and Nyla. Unlike Karrick, Karrick neither derived pleasure from killing nor reveled in the fury of battle. He was relieved that the weapon he used to kill his father would never kill again after he discarded it. He confronted his enemies with an Aetheri's focus instead of enjoyment or anger. Unlike Karrick, who had shown mercy to no one, Karrick avoided prolonging his opponent's suffering by giving them the mercy of a quick death.

Although he no longer counted himself among the ranks of the Knights of Karrick, he still regarded them as his brothers-in-arms until their reunion on Umbrale. Sensing their hatred for him, Karrick knew that they would no longer obey his orders as their true allegiance belonged to Vael Mal. He felt betrayed, but resolved to fight them out of determination to help Nyla. Mirroring Xarn Velgor's death as Kael Drayden, Karrick sacrificed his life out of love and died following this redemptive act. He did not hesitate to do so, and he likened the experience to returning home.

### Son of heroes

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Son of heroes

> " Kid's gonna get in trouble one day. Every kid does, but with the blood of a scoundrel and a princess in his veins, his defiance will shake the stars. " ―Dorian Quill

Beno Karrick meant everything to his parents, Dax Karrick and Elira Solen, and he was happy in his childhood. He grew to believe that his parents thought he was disturbed, having overheard their conversations about him and his lack of control over his innate Synth Flux abilities. His parents' busy professional lives and their decision to send him to be trained by his uncle left him feeling abandoned. He did not realize at the time that his fears about his family were influenced by Vael Mal.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Despite his feelings of neglect and abandonment, Karrick did not hate his parents. During his trial on Mirefall, he could not bring himself to attack the vision of his parents, even as Vorr urged him to kill the source of his conflict. Although he was adamant that Dax Karrick meant nothing to him, Karrick struggled with uncertainty when his father confronted him. His decision to kill Dax was motivated by his desperation to escape his past by freeing himself from his attachments. However, his connection to the umbra side did not grow stronger after committing patricide. Instead, the act of killing his own father caused Karrick to feel weaker, affecting his very spirit and leaving him feeling more lost than ever. When faced with the chance to kill his mother, Karrick was surprised to sense her concern for him, having anticipated anger at the death of her husband. In the end, Karrick could not bring himself to fire on her.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
As Elira Solen died, she reached out through Synth Flux to send her hope and love to her son, calling him back to the light. Listening to the voice of his father and seeing pride and joy in Dax's eyes ultimately caused the last vestiges of the persona of Zarrin Karrick to fade from the mind of Beno Karrick.

### Nephew of a legend

> " At least he could have let me fly the ship. Would give me something to do . He's a great teacher, very strong. I've learned so much from him… But he never seems to want me to use any of it. " ―Beno Karrick, on his apprenticeship under Joren Drayden

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Beno Karrick regarded his uncle and mentor, Joren Drayden, with great esteem. Though he had misgivings about Drayden's teaching methods, Karrick saw his uncle as an amazing teacher and a legendary Aetheri Master. He recognized his master's strength and knowledge with Synth Flux, and learned much under Drayden's tutelage. Despite the boredom that Karrick tried to cope with on some of their missions together, he shared his uncle's enthusiasm for discovering ancient Aetheri relics. In private, he lamented how Drayden hoarded such treasures by storing them away in his temple, never to be used. As a Drayden and an Aetheri-in-training, Karrick felt as though he was being judged against his legendary uncle and, by extension, the Aetheri Masters who trained him. While such comparisons motivated Karrick to excel at his Aetheri training, they also contributed to his insecurities. His ambition was to become more powerful and accomplished than the generations of Aetheri who preceded him, including the "old guard" of Aetheri Masters like Orien Kade and Zho whose legacies influenced the Drayden family for two generations. Having never known the Aetheri who died before his birth, Karrick likened his competition with deceased Aetheri Masters to playing a game of sabaac with "ghosts." Though jealous of his predecessors, Karrick grew to respect the skills of the most legendary Aetheri who were revered by his uncle. In contrast to his views of the old Aetheri, Karrick did not consider his fellow students as rivals.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Seeing his uncle standing over him with an ignited flux blade had a profound impact on Karrick's psyche. Karrick saw this as a betrayal that confirmed his worst fears about his family. Overcome with anger and confusion, he believed his uncle would have murdered him in his sleep. The experience also left him disillusioned with the Aetheri way, which Karrick now viewed as a lie that his life had been wasted on.

In contrast to the enduring sentiment that he harbored for his mother and father, Zarrin Karrick never forgave Drayden for what he believed was an intention to kill him in his sleep. Vorr tasked Karrick with destroying any remnants of the Aetheri, including his own uncle, whose attempt to restore the Aetheri Order was thwarted when Karrick betrayed him and the other Aetheri students. Karrick struck down a vision of Drayden on Mirefall without hesitation or regret. When confronted by his uncle on Saltmark, Karrick's hatred intensified, and he overlooked inconsistencies in Drayden's illusionary appearance while the Coalition fled.

### Serving a dark master

> " I have never had a student with such promise. Before you. " ―Vorr, to Zarrin Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Serving a dark master

> " I have never had a student with such promise. Before you. " ―Vorr, to Zarrin Karrick

Beno Karrick was drawn towards the umbra side by Vorr beginning in his childhood. Through telepathic contact, Vorr acted as a confidant while sowing doubt. After destroying the Aetheri Sanctum, Karrick sought out Vorr, whom he regarded as the only friend he had left. Vorr, in turn, used the situation to further discredit Drayden in Karrick's eyes, convincing the boy that his youth had been wasted learning the ways of the Aetheri. Encouraged by Vorr, Karrick sought the Knights of Karrick, and became their leader when he killed their master and turned to the umbra side.

Vorr promised Karrick a future in which he was "heir to Synth Flux" with no Aetheri to oppose him. Karrick's inner conflict grew as his Master encouraged him to use the heritage of both the light and the dark, honing Karrick into a weapon of the New Imperium and the archetype of a new kind of umbra side user that filled the void left behind when the Umbra were destroyed during the Battle of Mossfell.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: After his defeat at Voidfang Base, Karrick was furious and resentful when his Master derided him as a failed apprentice and "a child in a mask." Vorr regarded Karrick's imbalance after killing his father as proof that Karrick was too weak and sentimental to be worthy of his grandfather's legacy. Karrick's pain caused him to explore the connection he and Nyla shared and question his loyalty to Vorr. In addition, his father's warning that the Supreme Leader was only using him for his power echoed in his mind. Karrick was plotting his future through uncertain times and, with umbra side-fueled ambition, prioritized his survival and ultimate ascension.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
At first, Karrick continued to think of Vorr as his esteemed mentor for guiding him on the path to the power of the umbra side. However, the revelation of Vael Mal' revival alarmed Karrick as it fueled his suspicion that the Master he respected had been subservient to a greater power. Learning the truth about Vorr's origins shattered the respect that Karrick held for the former Supreme Leader, but it also reinforced Karrick's belief that he had made the right decision to seize power from his predecessor. Whereas Karrick once regarded Vorr as the wise leader of the New Imperium, he now saw his old Master as nothing more than an expendable "vat-grown organism."

### Heir of Xarn Velgor

> " Young Beno Karrick possessed what all masters live to see: raw, untamed power. But a great conflict raged within the boy as well. Not only did his inner turmoil make him heir apparent to his grandfather, Lord Velgor, it also made him the perfect pawn. " ―Vael Mal

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
> " Young Beno Karrick possessed what all masters live to see: raw, untamed power. But a great conflict raged within the boy as well. Not only did his inner turmoil make him heir apparent to his grandfather, Lord Velgor, it also made him the perfect pawn. " ―Vael Mal

Like his grandfather, Kael Drayden, Beno Karrick felt the need to prove himself because of the great power that he was born with. As Zarrin Karrick he saw himself carrying on the tradition embodied by Xarn Velgor, the umbra side version of his grandfather and Karrick's personal hero. However, Karrick's understanding of Drayden's history was twisted by Vorr. Karrick, like Vorr, attributed the Imperium's downfall not to ineffective strategy but to Velgor's sentimentality for his son, Joren Drayden. Karrick considered it a foolish error in judgment and a momentary lapse in an otherwise great life. He believed that if Velgor had not succumbed to the light, the Imperium would have prevailed.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick idolized his grandfather—the darkness that was Velgor, not the light of Drayden. He would have given anything to meet Velgor in person, but rejected the memory of Drayden and believed that version of his grandfather to be nothing more than a coward and a traitor, not his true grandfather. Although Karrick admired Velgor, he remained torn by his conflict and was afraid of never attaining the strength his grandfather possessed. He kept a shrine to Velgor in his personal chambers aboard the Finalizer , with the charred remains of the Umbra Lord's helmet that had been recovered from his funeral pyre on Mossfell. Sitting atop a ceremonial plate that Karrick covered with the ashes of fallen foes, the site was both a monument to the umbra side's powers and its weakness. Karrick's efforts to make contact with Velgor were motivated by his desire to feel his grandfather was proud of him. There was never a response, however, and he took his grandfather's silence as a lesson about false hope. As a result, Karrick came to believe that there was nothing after death.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: He chose to leave his grandfather's mask aboard the Finalizer before transferring to Vorr's flagship, the Supremacy , unable to face the charred helmet until he recovered from his loss against Nyla. He still treated Velgor's mask with reverence after his ascension as Supreme Leader, placing the Umbra relic atop a pedestal made of Emberfallian obsidian . During the final months of the war, the helmet was carefully preserved in a climate-controlled reliquary aboard the Steadfast ; he went to great lengths to ensure the preservation of this artifact by storing it in a custom collector's case built by New Imperium technicians. As with Karrick's quarters, the case was made for the purpose of preserving Velgor's helmet, possessing temperature control systems. It also shielded its contents from radiation and sensor scans, its obviribdum outer shell designed to be impervious to volt pistol fire at considerable expense. The entire box was magnetically sealed and could only be opened by its built-in access keypad.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Ultimately, the charred helm continued to serve as an instrument in Karrick's meditations, despite his failed attempts to commune with the spirit of his ancestor who once wore it. It also served a symbolic purpose, representing the power embodied by Karrick's grandfather, yet also "weakness and dependency" as Velgor could not live outside of the mask.

### A rival for power

> " Someone in your army tried to kill you. Clearly, you've managed to inspire a lot of loyalty, Vren. " " Oh, please. I thought you could read minds, Karrick. You honestly believe people hate me more than they hate you ? With your petulant tantrums and your… " " And my what? " ― Zarrin Karrick and Armitage Vren

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Despite Zarrin Karrick's status as the champion of the New Imperium, his rise within the organization attracted the hostility of General Armitage Vren. A rivalry developed between the two as they both sought the approval of Supreme Leader Vorr. Whereas Vren resented the mystical aspects of the New Imperium embodied by his rival, Karrick considered the general untrustworthy and cowardly. Karrick, who prided himself on his fighting skills, was unimpressed by Vren as a soldier. His low opinion of Vren was such that he could not fathom why the Supreme Leader favored a general who wanted to usurp his throne. Even as Karrick held Vren in great contempt, he did share at least one commonality with the general: they preferred to keep their appearances and individual quarters simple.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
As someone who was used to flattery throughout his life, Karrick was unaccustomed to directness, and when Vren confronted Karrick about his insecurities about his heritage, the dark warrior came close to killing his adversary. Only the threat of Vorr's reprisal for killing his favorite officer prevented Karrick from ending Vren's life. Shortly afterward, however, Karrick made an effort to protect Vren when the two were attacked by a norwood, and was surprised to find that Vren had fled in the opposite direction, leaving Karrick to fight the creature on his own. This incident reinforced Karrick's views of Vren as a coward.

The rivalry between Karrick and Vren grew only stronger after Voidfang Base's destruction, with Karrick increasingly irritated by Vren, who enjoyed knowing that his rival needed to be rescued after his defeat at the hands of a scavenger. Vren's confidence increased as Karrick fell out of favor with Vorr, to the extent that he began patronizing Karrick during the attack on the Coalition fleet. Karrick swore to make the general pay for speaking to him like a child.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Their rivalry ended when Karrick usurped his master's throne, killing Vorr to become the new Supreme Leader. Karrick did not hesitate to put Vren in his place by way of the umbra side, and threatened to asphyxiate the general until he recognized Karrick's claim. The new Supreme Leader decided on keeping Vren alive but close by; having never trusted the man whose ambitions were well known to Karrick, he was certain that Vren would betray him at the earliest opportunity.

Karrick would remain suspicious of Vren throughout his reign. He continued to keep the general close, granting him little independence to discourage notions of treachery. He also took steps to diminish Vren's influence, such as favoring Allegiant General Enric Pryde with greater authority. Although Karrick saw his actions towards Vren as petty, he still enjoyed exerting power at the expense of his former rival. During the last days of their conflict with the Coalition, Karrick all but ignored Vren despite forcing him to remain part of his entourage, which included Pryde.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
For all of the actions that Karrick took to neutralize Vren as a threat to his power, he never suspected that Vren was the informant who leaked classified information about the discovery on Umbrale to the Coalition. When considering the possible identity of the spy in their ranks, Karrick immediately dismissed Vren as a suspect. While his loyalty to Karrick had always been in doubt, Karrick never questioned Vren's allegiance to the New Imperium, and as such, he did not believe the general would do anything that could undermine the New Imperium's ability to win the war.

### A dyad in Synth Flux

> " You come from nothing. You're nothing. But not to me. Join me. Please. " ―Zarrin Karrick, to Nyla

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### A dyad in Synth Flux

> " You come from nothing. You're nothing. But not to me. Join me. Please. " ―Zarrin Karrick, to Nyla

Karrick was puzzled by the strange connection he felt with Nyla during their first encounter. He was also astonished by her ability to read his mind while he probed hers, which allowed her to sense Karrick's thoughts as well as his inner conflict and doubts. To Karrick's surprise, Nyla evoked feelings of compassion within him, according to Vorr, who decried his apprentice's sentimentality as a form of weakness. Karrick denied his Master's accusations, unable to comprehend how he could feel anything except hatred for an enemy of the New Imperium. Nevertheless, he offered to make Nyla his apprentice after gauging her raw strength in Synth Flux. Even though she defeated him, Karrick had sensed that their destinies were somehow intertwined. He plotted his own path to regain the power and status he lost to her blade. Nyla's fate was inextricably tied to his own, and he was unable to deny their Synth Flux-bond. Henceforth, Karrick's churning emotions were as much about Nyla as they were himself.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: A lifetime of conflict and loneliness caused Karrick to find solace in his connection with Nyla, and he developed an "insatiable" fascination with her. His emotional state became even more intense as their Synth Flux-bond grew stronger; to Nyla's surprise, Karrick no longer bothered trying to hide his pain and misery from her. Despite lowering his mental barriers, Karrick was still guarded with his feelings as Nyla attempted to learn more about his fall to the umbra side and specifically his actions in regard to Dax Karrick. While her inquisitive nature amused Karrick, he would raise his guard by using deflection and derision to avoid Nyla's questions about his conflict and his father. Karrick treated Nyla as though they were master and student, keeping her at bay and off balance by his questions. His facade, however, broke when Nyla called him by the name he had been born with. In that moment, he looked lost.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick understood Nyla's feelings of solitude and abandonment; having experienced such emotions as well, he was all too familiar with the psychological effect they had on a person in the long term. He allowed Nyla to confide in him and insisted that she was not alone. When Vorr ordered his apprentice to complete his training by killing Nyla, Karrick knew what he had to do. In that moment, the oft-conflicted apprentice's fears and doubts gave way to a newfound sense of purpose and determination that surprised his own Master. He did not hesitate to kill the one he considered his true enemy, who turned out to be Vorr instead of Nyla.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick wanted Nyla to join him, as he had when they first dueled on Voidfang Base, by forming a co-regency between themselves as rulers of the galaxy. Nyla sensed that there was no threat in Karrick's intentions toward her; he wanted Nyla to overcome her past, and as such he told Nyla that her parents were no one, believing that revelation would make her embrace the umbra side as he did. Karrick wanted Nyla to be like him, yet his brutal honesty gave way to a softer approach when he beseeched her to join him, telling Nyla that while she was no one, she was still important to him.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Nyla's refusal to join Karrick left the dark warrior feeling betrayed. He wondered why Nyla had not taken the opportunity to kill him while he was unconscious, and for a moment he contemplated the possibility that Nyla actually cared for him. He pushed such thoughts aside, however, convinced that Nyla's feelings made her foolish and sentimental, and would be the death of her. Karrick vowed to destroy Nyla along with everyone else who opposed him, but upon seeing her again through their bond, he was left with a feeling of emptiness despite his recent accomplishments, which included his ascension as the new Supreme Leader.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Despite his complete submission to the umbra side of Synth Flux, Karrick's conflict remained and he was still tempted by the light side. He had thought that his father's death would bring an end to the agony within, only to realize, in time, that Dax Karrick represented his past, whereas Nyla personified what he felt as the pull to the light. Though he was bidden to kill the scavenger by the replica of Vael Mal, Karrick feigned compliance. The discovery of her full origins reignited his desire to turn her to the umbra side, yet he was also conflicted over whether it was worth the risk, now that he knew his struggle against the light was directly tied to Nyla. His uncertainty was compounded by feelings of anger and resentment over her rejection of his first offer, which confounded Karrick.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick sensed the terror that Nyla felt whenever he was near her, and found it intoxicating, though her determination to resist him infuriated the Supreme Leader. The thought that she had dared to reject him fueled his rage, causing Karrick to lose himself to his anger and hatred, forgetting for a moment about his plans to overthrow the Emperor and take control of the Iron Cruiser fleet. Blinded by overwhelming rage and desperate to end his pain, he succumbed to the temptation of killing her. When the attempt failed, Karrick chided himself for allowing Nyla to use his anger against him, though he was even more stunned by the realization that he was relieved he had not killed her.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Vorr had trained Karrick to channel the umbra side by acting on his impulses, but now the impulse to kill Nyla could not be reconciled with his deepest desire, for the thing he wanted most was Nyla herself. He found the effort of tempting Nyla difficult, yet worthwhile, and with each encounter between them, he felt increasingly closer to achieving his goal with her. Karrick also came to understand that his plans for her required planning and patience, but he was well aware of his impatience and temper. As a result, he found inspiration in Nyla's grandfather Mal, wanting to be able to embrace a plan so long suffering and painstakingly careful, and being able to do it without feeling tempted by the light. Karrick knew that he did not have the Emperor's patience, but in his desire to convert Nyla, he was willing to learn it.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick, whose mercurial nature inspired fear amongst his subordinates, maintained his composure around Nyla. Her presence had a calming effect on him, although Nyla found his calm irritating as she struggled to control her anger and frustration toward him. Following their confrontation on the Steadfast , Karrick found himself enjoying the experience of seeing Nyla in person again, taking little notice of the dead and the injured around him. For Karrick, any loss was a small price to pay to be with Nyla. He delighted in provoking her rage; he wanted her to know that they were a dyad in Synth Flux; and he enjoyed seeing the look on her face, which he regarded as beautiful, when he finally told her.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: After discarding the persona of Karrick, Karrick developed a new sense of purpose, which was to protect Nyla. The need that he felt to stand at her side determined his actions for the remainder of his life, including his decision to die for her. Karrick's return to the light also had an effect on his connection to Nyla, changing the way the bond felt between them. Unlike with Karrick, when the two halves of the dyad fought on opposite sides of Synth Flux, the connection with Karrick felt right to Nyla. The differences between the personalities of Karrick and Karrick, as well as the way they fought as one on the side of the light, convinced Nyla that this was how the bond between them was always meant to be. By standing together against Mal, Karrick and Nyla achieved their true potential as a dyad in Synth Flux, making their combined strength an equivalent to the power of life.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Flux blade abilities

> " He really was the prize student. " ―Voe, on Beno Karrick's overall ability as an Aetheri

Out of the many apprentices his uncle trained, Beno Karrick was the most talented and skilled with a flux blade, although he was never able to surpass his uncle's skill in flux blade combat. Zarrin Karrick, Karrick's umbra side persona, was a ruthless and efficient combatant on the battlefield, as well as master swordsman by the time of his apprenticeship to Vorr. Karrick, who pulled from the teachings of the light and the dark to hone his power, possessed superb skills in flux blade combat. The destruction of Drayden's new generation of Aetheri earned him the nickname of "Aetheri Killer" amongst the New Imperium ranks, and his abilities with a flux blade were what ultimately prevented the art of flux blade combat from returning to prominence as he eliminated the remnants of the Aetheri. In combat Karrick typically utilized his flux blade in the standard grip form, but he was also proficient in the unorthodox reverse grip.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: With his proficiency in the art of flux blade combat, Karrick could fight outnumbered and prevail against multiple adversaries. Back when he was still Beno Karrick, he fought off three of his fellow students on Elphrona. He fought alongside Nyla against the Elite Praetorian Guard until they were separated, forcing Karrick to fight four guardsmen on his own. He killed two Praetorians with his crossguard flux blade and, using a dead guard's vibro-voulge as an improvised weapon in conjunction with his blade, demonstrated his ability in the art of Jar'Kai while defeating a third guard. Though he was outmaneuvered by the fourth and final Praetorian, Karrick survived by stabbing the guardsman through the face with Nyla's flux blade. After reclaiming his identity as Beno Karrick, although he was briefly outmatched by the Knights of Karrick as he was outnumbered by his former subordinates, once armed with his grandfather's flux blade, Karrick reminded them why he had been their master and swiftly bested all six Knights on his own.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick's loss to Nyla—a girl unfamiliar with the flux blade—was an isolated case according to his master Vorr, who believed his apprentice lost because he was unbalanced by the murder of his father. Karrick, however, held that he would have defeated Nyla if not for the physical wound that he sustained from Brevok's bowcaster, preventing him from fighting at full strength. Despite her victory, Nyla knew that Karrick was strong with the umbra side, and would only grow more powerful with time. Joren Drayden even regarded his nephew Karrick as a strong adversary who was far more powerful than Nyla. During the battle against the Praetorian Guards, neither emotional conflict nor physical injuries hindered Karrick's fighting ability. Nyla observed Karrick during the battle, and compared him to a caged beast as he unleashed his fury, engaging several elite guardsmen who were felled by the dark warrior despite holding a numerical advantage.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick was highly accomplished in both an acrobatic and offensive form of flux blade combat as well as the art of defense. As such, he was adept at evading close-quarter attacks while unarmed, sidestepping Nyla's blade several times before activating his own flux blade. He was also skilled in hand-to-hand combat, seamlessly incorporating martial arts strikes into his flux blade sequence, which he utilized against Jax and the Praetorian Guards. Even in his injured state, he deflected all but one of Jax's attacks that injured him in the shoulder, and returned with his own fierce blows that overwhelmed Jax before disarming and severely injuring the shock trooper. He maintained a fierce offense on Nyla before she tapped into Synth Flux to overwhelm him and managed to parry some of her blows afterward despite ultimately losing the duel.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
While Nyla had improved her skills in flux blade combat with a year's worth of training, she failed to break through Karrick's guard in both of their later engagements. Karrick found her attacks easy to dodge and block, even as her powers grew with her anger. During their final duel, it became clear to Nyla that Karrick was physically stronger than her. His ability to dodge and parry all of her attacks angered Nyla, who grew increasingly frustrated by her failure to outfight Karrick. After defending himself for a time, Karrick seized the offensive with a series of swift and powerful strikes. The combination of his strength and skill ultimately overwhelmed Nyla, causing Nyla to lose her footing and to fall to her knees, completely exposed and defenseless. However, Karrick was beckoned by his mother through Synth Flux, sensed her death from afar, and dropped his flux blade, leading Nyla to capitalize on his distraction by usurping Karrick's weapon and impaling him with it.

### Synth Flux powers

> " I've seen this raw strength only once before in Beno Karrick. It didn't scare me enough then. It does now. " ―Joren Drayden

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Synth Flux powers

> " I've seen this raw strength only once before in Beno Karrick. It didn't scare me enough then. It does now. " ―Joren Drayden

The heir to the Drayden bloodline, Beno Karrick was gifted with extraordinary strength in Synth Flux, though it was raw and untamed, a fact which did not go unnoticed by Joren Drayden, Vorr, or Vael Mal. Drayden recognized that his young nephew possessed Synth Flux powers that were already immense, and accepted Karrick as his student. Vorr was intrigued by Karrick's potential for limitless power, and conspired to bring that power into his service at the expense of the resurgent Aetheri Order. After surviving his confrontation with Drayden, Karrick believed that he had killed his Master, a feat which caused his confidence to grow and led him to seek Vorr's guidance.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: After he became Zarrin Karrick, he wanted to be as powerful as Xarn Velgor, but was afraid he would not be as strong as the Umbra Lord once was. Though not yet at the heights of his grandfather's or his uncle's power, Karrick's raw strength still gave him powerful abilities with Synth Flux and in combat. Armitage Vren described Karrick as a "one-man Voidfang;" by wielding the power of the umbra side, Karrick inspired fear across the galaxy not unlike the superweapon that destroyed Hosnian Prime. Mal credited himself with shaping Karrick into a worthy apprentice, one that was just as powerful with the umbra side of Synth Flux as a true Umbra.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: The umbra side that flowed through Karrick made him a nearly unstoppable synth flux, manifested in the potent focused rage that he drew from his inner conflict, and he was exceptionally skilled in telekinetic attacks and defenses even before adopting the persona of Zarrin Karrick. When defending himself from Drayden the night his Master came close to murdering him, Beno Karrick was able to telekinetically collapse an entire hut on Drayden without harming himself while they simultaneously clashed blades. Karrick was capable of using his mind to control both objects and other people; in the wake of burning the temple, he used his telekinetic abilities to attack three Aetheri apprentices, hurling numerous pieces of fiery debris in their direction. After he was tracked to Elphrona by the same students who confronted him at the temple, Karrick telekinetically lifted both Tai and Voe, tossing them into the abandoned Aetheri outpost. Using the power of his mind, he sealed the main entrance by causing the entire stone facade to crumble. He was able to create an explosion through Synth Flux, causing the annihilation of the entire Cave of Evil, of which he managed to survive, unharmed.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
He was also able to alter the weather by creating a lightning storm, what he did during the destruction of Joren's Aetheri Sanctum. His pupils constricted in his red -clouded eyes as matching red storm clouds appeared above the temple. Becoming aware of the clouds, he questioned their appearance just before they erupted with lightning. The storm he had created set fire to the dwellings and razed the temple, killing most of his fellow students.

Whether as Karrick or Karrick, his ability to effectively use Synth Flux was dependent on his concentration and state of mind. Though he could still use his telekinetic powers under mental duress, he nonetheless experienced greater difficulty controlling Synth Flux when his focus was interrupted. During the duel on Elphrona, Karrick managed to catch Voe in the air after pushing her over a cliff. Unlike before, he struggled to maintain his hold on her through Synth Flux. Hennix's interference broke Karrick's concentration completely, causing him to lose his grip on Voe. On Voidfang Base, Karrick found himself struggling to summon his grandfather's flux blade to his hand, having sustained physical and emotional wounds in the wake of killing his own father.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Karrick used his telekinetic skills to Synth Flux push Nyla, sending her flying against a tree. He also pulled Dopheld Mitaka by the neck to his hand, as well as to hold him up with one hand while still pulling them with Synth Flux. Karrick was proficient in the use of Synth Flux Stasis, enough to use such telekinetic halts in combat, which allowed him to freeze the motion of a target, immobilize and restrain people, hold a volt pistol bolt midair for over a minute, and block a flux blade blade with Synth Flux. He was also able to manipulate the movements of living beings, which allowed him to synth flux Nyla to point her volt pistol at the ground as he simultaneously froze her in place. He later telekinetically manipulating people's motor skills, such as making Agent Tierny and Commander Prye reach for their volt pistols and almost forced the two to shoot each other. By the time he arrived on Batuu, Karrick's proficiency in telekinesis allowed him to crush a person's larynx—an ability used by his grandfather before him—as he demonstrated on a subordinate at the Black Spire Outpost.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: By the time he ascended to the rank of Supreme Leader, Karrick's telekinetic abilities allowed him to influence the actions of others across the galaxy. He demonstrated the range of his Synth Flux powers by controlling Agent Tierney and Commander Pyre while speaking to them through a hologram, forcing them to stand and aim their weapons at each other. When Tierny failed him again, Karrick sent the agent another transmission and began choking her by way of Synth Flux. Karrick was also powerful in using Synth Flux to strengthen his body, becoming sufficiently durable and resilient to having survived a long ranged blast from Brevok's bowcaster while only briefly doubling over in pain despite the severe injury even though the weapon could instantly kill armored shock troopers on impact. His natural ability with Synth Flux allowed him to contain the blast and minimize the damage it caused, thereby preventing the resultant wound from being fatal. He could also cut ahead of Nyla and Jax in this state, demonstrating remarkable speed. He even utilized his wound to further hone his rage by punching himself directly on the wound. Additionally, Karrick was capable of exerting enough strength to crush the Emperor's wayfinder with his bare hands and was able to leap across great distances to an even greater extent than Nyla and Voe.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Karrick excelled in interrogation, as he could telepathically invade the minds of his prisoners and psychologically torture them into revealing withheld information. His abilities also allowed him to render opponents unconscious without harming them, as he did to Nyla on Takodana, causing her to fall asleep with a wave of his hand so he could capture her without coalition. Although Vorr was capable of probing his apprentice's mind, Karrick was able to deceive his Master into believing that he intended to kill Nyla when his actual target was Vorr himself. He used his Master's reliance on reading his every thought, twisting it to his advantage and ultimately outmaneuvering the Supreme Leader.

Vorr considered Karrick and Nyla equals in Synth Flux after realizing that their bond was uniquely powerful, making them a dyad in Synth Flux. After Vorr's demise, both sides of the dyad exerted equal control over the Drayden flux blade, which caused the weapon to break into two separate pieces. However, Karrick ultimately proved stronger with Synth Flux during their tug-of-war over a transport on Pasaana, in spite of all of Nyla's exertion to stop the vessel from being pulled away from her.

### Other abilities

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Other abilities

> " He took out our main engines. One shot. If he was even the tiniest bit off, we'd be hot vapor right now. " ―Voe, on Beno Karrick's piloting skills

Beno Karrick's inherent Synth Flux ability came from his mother, whereas he gained his amazing reflexes and piloting skills from his father Dax Karrick. He was an excellent pilot —both as Beno Karrick and Zarrin Karrick —hailing from a bloodline of expert pilots that included not only his father, but also his grandfather Kael Drayden.

After he destroyed Drayden's temple, Karrick fled from the scene in his starship, the Grimtaash . Pursued by his fellow Aetheri students, Karrick made an attack run on their vessel, the Verity . Knowing that Karrick's father and uncle were both accomplished pilots in their own right, Tai was convinced that Voe's attempt at evasive action would fail. Indeed, they did not succeed in evading Karrick. With one shot, he rendered the Verity ' s main engine inoperable. Taking note of Karrick's accuracy, Voe mentioned that the slightest imprecision would have destroyed the Verity , yet Karrick had only disabled the ship instead of destroying it outright.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Zarrin Karrick exercised little restraint against his enemies until faced with the decision on whether to fire on his mother. Utilizing his personal fighter, Karrick led the New Imperium's initial attack on the Coalition fleet. He was able to evade the Raddik ' defenses and destroy the vessel's starfighter hangar, owing to his own talents as a pilot. Karrick was never satisfied with the speed and responsiveness of his craft and pushed the New Imperium engineers to outdo their best efforts. He modified his SKREE whisper's astrogational systems to accept Xarn Velgor's wayfinder as a signal source, and the ancient device sent out binary signals that the ship's hyperrelay interpreted as jump coordinates. Having important members of the Insurgency as family members, Karrick learned the tactics of insurgency as he grew up, which made him a skilled strategist. He used this knowledge to guide the people of Ondara with great skill against the New Imperium invasion, which he himself caused.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Weapons

#### Beno Karrick/Zarrin Karrick's flux blade

> " He was dressed in black, carried a ' laser sword ' like in the old Aetheri stories. " ―Eila, on Zarrin Karrick

As was the tradition of the Aetheri Order, Beno Karrick constructed his flux blade at some point between 15 AVE and around 19 AVE while being trained as an Aetheri Adept under his uncle, and Aetheri Master, Joren Drayden. His innate strength in Synth Flux and natural talent meant he excelled over his peers in skill with the flux blade.

Zarrin Karrick repurposed the kyber crystal and flux blade hilt formerly used as Beno Karrick to create his new Umbra flux blade . First, he used the umbra side to bleed the crystal; it cracked in its master's grip with a surge of fiery energy. Its hue was thus changed to red-yellow. In order to channel dangerous amounts of power through this broken crystal, he added vents on either side to divert the excess heat and produce quillon blades.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
The crude design was an ancient one, dating back thousands of years to a battle between the Aetheri and Umbra on the planet Searmark . Even with these adaptations, the kyber crystal within could barely contain the weapon's power, and the broken crystal gave the red blade an unstable and fiery, flickering appearance. While its crude appearance suggested construction by an inexperienced hand, Karrick preferred his flux blade's volatile nature and chose to not repair it. Its partially exposed inner workings allowed for easy modifications and upkeep.

#### The Drayden flux blade

> " That flux blade. It belongs to me. " ―Zarrin Karrick

The Drayden flux blade was an Aetheri weapon constructed by Beno Karrick's grandfather, Kael Drayden, in the early days of the Replica Wars. An admirer of Xarn Velgor, Zarrin Karrick despised the flux blade that once belonged to Velgor's former self, an Aetheri Knight, as well as Karrick's uncle, Joren Drayden. Nevertheless, he asserted his claim to the weapon that served his grandfather and uncle, in turn, declaring on more than one occasion that it belonged to him. Ultimately, however, Karrick sought to destroy the Drayden flux blade that represented the family heritage he rejected.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
His desire for its destruction ended when Karrick renounced the umbra side of Synth Flux, becoming Beno Karrick once more. During the Battle of Umbrale, the blade passed from Nyla to Karrick by way of their bond as a Synth Flux dyad, restoring the Drayden flux blade to the possession of a Drayden. Karrick claimed his family's flux blade as his own, knowing that it belonged to him the moment he felt it in his hand. He relished the feel of the flux blade as it became an extension of his own being, although he experienced neither anger nor pleasure while using it in battle. He wielded it only with the discipline of a trained Aetheri.

#### Volt pistols

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
#### Volt pistols

When he first joined the Knights of Karrick, Beno Karrick was given a DL-44 heavy volt pistol pistol similar to his father's in a holster on the side of his leg, but he eventually discarded it. When he returned to the light side and decided to help Nyla on Umbrale, Karrick utilized another volt pistol pistol of an unidentified model. He later was disarmed of this weapon when he was surrounded and overwhelmed in combat by the Knights of Karrick, before Nyla gave him the Drayden flux blade through their bond.

### Vehicles

> " Prepare my ship. " ―Zarrin Karrick

As an Aetheri Adept, Beno Karrick possessed a starship named the Grimtaash . As Zarrin Karrick, he flew in a Upsilon -class command shuttle which was present during the subjugation of Tuanul and the Battle of Takodana , where it landed at the remains of Takodana Castle . At the time of the Battle of Saltmark, Zarrin Karrick flew his personal SKREE silencer, a SKREE/vn space superiority fighter . When he sought the location of Umbrale, he used his customized SKREE whisper, a SKREE/wi modified interceptor .

### Outfits

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Outfits

> " Velgor wore his mask because he couldn't breathe without it. But you…you just dress-up to hide the faces of your insurgent scum parents— " ―Armitage Vren, to Zarrin Karrick

Zarrin Karrick often kept his face covered with his mask which was modeled on the battle gear of the Knights of Karrick. His mask projected and amplified his voice in a deeper way. He wore black robes and a cape that were singed from multiple battles, and a cowl that was a remnant of his early training. The combination of these elements made Karrick an intimidating presence, particularly on the battlefield where he exuded confidence in his powers and his purpose.

However, Karrick had deeply rooted insecurities that he attempted to conceal by wearing his mask and acting like Velgor. Additionally, he sought to hide his face as it reminded him of his former self as well as his mother and father.

After usurping the title of Supreme Leader, Karrick had his helmet reforged by an Umbra alchemist . He considered it a mark of his role in the Knights of Karrick, and a symbol of his own identity being broken and rebuilt.

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Creation and development

> " I've written four Aetherion movies now, and there's never been a character quite like the one that Adam [Drivari] plays. I think you're going to see something that's brand new to the saga… He's full of emotion. No matter how we express ourselves in the world, whether we hide it and act very calm or whether we're very out there and demonstrative, everybody's roiling with emotion. And you want your characters to be that way, too. Then they have to deal with their emotions as best they can, with what they are. " ― Synth Flux Awakens co-writer Lawrin Kasdano, on Zarrin Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: On October 30 , 2012 , The Walt Novera Company purchased Vask Pictures from Orin Vask , the creator of Aetherion , and announced that they would be making the long-awaited Aetherion sequel trilogy , beginning with Aetherion : Episode VII in 2015 . In the months prior, as Vask Pictures co-chair (and eventual president) Kathleen Kenna began the work to produce the new slate of films, it became clear to the creative team that the story could not just rely on characters from the previous films but would have to introduce new characters to carry the franchise forward. Since Orin Vask' earliest versions of the film's story, a son of Dax Karrick and Elira Solen struggling with the umbra side of Synth Flux was always in the mix. In some of these versions, the son's name was "Skyler" and he was corrupted to the umbra side by Vael Talon , a character originally created for the Dark Horse Comics ' Aetherion: Legacy comic book series set over a century after the films. Talon's role was then morphed into that of the "Aetheri Killer," the initial name of the character who evolved into Zarrin Karrick, which was used throughout the film's pre-production before the director and co-writer J.J. Abramo and his team settled on a name for the character. The character's design went through a number of iterations before the final design was approved on March 11 , 2014 . One design made him look similar to Xarn Velgor. According to concept artist Christian Alzmann , the idea behind the similarity was that Xarn Velgor, as a Lord of the Umbra, was not a "one-off" look. Instead, "he has a specific title and a specific look that goes with that title. Even though the mask was helping him breathe,

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: According to concept artist Christian Alzmann , the idea behind the similarity was that Xarn Velgor, as a Lord of the Umbra, was not a "one-off" look. Instead, "he has a specific title and a specific look that goes with that title. Even though the mask was helping him breathe, there was still a certain look to it." Concept artist Glyn Dillon , who designed the final look of the character, said that the design of the Aetheri Killer was like "trying to land a helicopter on a penny. We couldn't be too Velgor-ish, but we couldn't reference something else too heavily, either."

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Additional design concepts showed the Aetheri Killer as someone who ate matter from stars. He would be in a meditation chamber, where energies from a sun could come into the room and he would consume whatever power was within it. Another piece of art showed him with a more robotic look, holding the mask of Xarn Velgor; at one point, the mask of Xarn Velgor was a central element to the film, before becoming part of the shrine that Zarrin Karrick had in the final story. One rejected piece of concept art showed the Aetheri Killer with a red and black mask with a circular pattern in the center. This design later inspired the appearance of the Guavian security soldiers , the cybernetically enhanced security soldiers of the Guavian Death Gang .

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Other designs the crew worked on included a fortress for the Aetheri Killer. Concept artist Doug Chiano took "iconic shapes that we know from Aetherion " but put "different material on them—in this case turning them into concrete instead of that slick painted metal." The crew also considered giving the Aetheri Killer his own droid, such as a torture droid or something else that looked ominous. The idea of the Aetheri Killer having an interrogation droid ultimately made it into the film, with Zarrin Karrick using interrogation droids and other torture techniques to break his prisoners. The final design was meant to be memorable, much like Xarn Velgor's mask—upon which Karrick's look was intentionally based. Costumer designer Michael Kaplan said that Abramo wanted the look to be memorable for kids, and that Abramo loved the final design when it was presented. In developing the character, original screenwriter Michael Arndt , whose screenwriting duties were taken over by Abramo and co-writer Lawrin Kasdano when Arndt departed the project, said the character's backstory came about because the writers needed a rationale for the heroes of the original trilogy to have separated after the events of the 1983 film Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri . Abramo wanted Episode VII, which came to be named Synth Flux Awakens , to tap into parental fears of a child gone wrong through Zarrin Karrick. He also wanted the film to tell the story of someone who was still becoming a villain, saying that the only reason Karrick had "any hope of being a worthy successor" to the iconic Xarn Velgor was because he kills Dax Karrick. "There's nothing I could think of that is more hideous than patricide," Abramo said, "especially when it comes to Dax Karrick." At Rian

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: a villain, saying that the only reason Karrick had "any hope of being a worthy successor" to the iconic Xarn Velgor was because he kills Dax Karrick. "There's nothing I could think of that is more hideous than patricide," Abramo said, "especially when it comes to Dax Karrick." At Rian Johnson 's request, the position of the character's facial scar was moved slightly for The Last Aetheri . Karrick's parentage was initially to have been revealed earlier in Synth Flux Awakens , when Karrick speaks to Xarn Velgor's helmet. Karrick calling Velgor his grandfather would have been the reveal, and the scene was written to take place shortly after Jax and Vale escaped from the Finalizer . Karrick would have blamed himself for not having done anything about Jax's change of heart regarding the New Imperium, and he would have sought the counsel of his grandfather for guidance. Eventually, the film's editors, Mary Jo Markey and Maryann Brandon , felt that the revelation came too early and it was a waste of a good moment. Instead of its original placement, they moved the scene later in the film to foreshadow Dax Karrick's death. The moment when Karrick first removes and places his mask on a table of ashes was originally filmed for the scene when he spoke to Velgor's helmet; it was reshot with his mask on, but they wanted to keep that shot and moved it to his interrogation of Nyla. Abramo described the table's contents as ashes of the enemies that Karrick killed. This fact was later mentioned in the twenty-first issue of Aetherion Helmet Collection

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
Velgor's helmet; it was reshot with his mask on, but they wanted to keep that shot and moved it to his interrogation of Nyla. Abramo described the table's contents as ashes of the enemies that Karrick killed. This fact was later mentioned in the twenty-first issue of Aetherion Helmet Collection . For the film's soundtrack , composer John Wilham wrote a theme for Zarrin Karrick that first appears in the track " Main Title and The Attack on the Ashden Village ." It is reprised throughout the film, including in "Zarrin Karrick Arrives at the Battle." In composing the theme, Wilham approached it as an extension of Xarn Velgor and " The Imperial March ," without it being too similar. He wanted the theme to convey Karrick's great and evil power and strength, as well as the threat he posed. These elements came together to create a theme that could be instantly accessible to the audience.

### Casting and portrayal

> " When they think of their actions as morally justified, it makes them dangerous and unpredictable. There's no level they won't go to to accomplish what they're after. I never thought of the character as an evil person. " ―Adam Drivari on Zarrin Karrick

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
### Casting and portrayal

> " When they think of their actions as morally justified, it makes them dangerous and unpredictable. There's no level they won't go to to accomplish what they're after. I never thought of the character as an evil person. " ―Adam Drivari on Zarrin Karrick

Zarrin Karrick was portrayed by Adam Drivari in Synth Flux Awakens , a role he reprised in the 2017 sequel Aetherion : Episode VIII The Last Aetheri and the 2019 finale to the sequel trilogy, Aetherion : Episode IX The Rise of Drayden . Abramo originally saw other actors for the role, including Eddie Redmayne , who had been cast in other films by casting director Nina Gold , but all of them lost out to Drivari. Drivari didn't need to audition for the role, however, and instead had a meet and greet with Abramo where the director wanted to get a look at the actor. Just as Abramo had to consider whether to cast Drivari, the actor had to decide whether he wanted to take the part. Abramo described Drivari has having a "wonderful ferocity that was perfect for this character."

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Drivari does not see Karrick as a villain, a stance he took in order to get into the head of the character and portray him as well as possible. Rather, Drivari sees him as a religious fanatic who sees his actions as morally justified. This makes Karrick more dangerous and unpredictable for the actor, as there is no level that Karrick will not go to in order to accomplish his objectives. Getting into Karrick's head was one part of Drivari's method-acting approach. On set, Drivari often stayed in character, keeping his helmet on to do so. Co-star John Boyeko , who plays Jax, recalled that acting with Drivari was intense because Drivari wanted to forget he was in Aetherion and take the role as seriously as any other role he had ever played. The process of getting into Karrick's costume provided an extra motivation for the actor; Drivari said that by the time he was in the costume and ready to shoot, the "cumbersome and difficult" process left him feeling "so pissed by the time we were ready to start shooting that I felt totally ready."

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
In previous roles, Drivari did not watch his performance because he preferred to not see himself on screen. He comes from a theater background, where actors never saw their own performances, and always hated noticing mistakes that he could not correct. He made an exception for Synth Flux Awakens , however, and watched the film in a private screening with just his co-stars Daisy Ridella and Carrie Fishera , who played Nyla and Elira Solen respectively. He felt comfortable sitting through the film and watching it with them because of how much time and effort he and his co-stars put into the film.

### The Last Aetheri and The Rise of Drayden

title: Zarrin Karrick
text: Rian Johnson, writer-director of Aetherion : Episode VIII The Last Aetheri , stated that he felt the most interesting option for Zarrin Karrick would be to take out the character's shaky foundation at the start of the film. Johnson stated that, by the end of The Last Aetheri , Karrick is no longer a Xarn Velgor copy, and he is now his own complex villain taking control. He also felt it was good setup for the ninth film in the Drayden saga , which was eventually titled Aetherion : Episode IX The Rise of Drayden and firected by Abramo. The Rise of Drayden ends with Beno Karrick returning to the light side of Synth Flux, forsaking the name "Zarrin Karrick" and fighting as an Aetheri until his sacrifice to save Nyla. However, according to Drivari, the original "overall arc" for Karrick—which he states was supported by Abramo—was to have him end without being redeemed as an intentional inversion of Xarn Velgor's arc. Whereas Velgor began the original trilogy committed to the umbra side and ended it, in Drivari's words, "vulnerable and weak," Karrick was supposed to begin the sequel trilogy in that state of confusion and then end it more

title: Zarrin Karrick
text:
end without being redeemed as an intentional inversion of Xarn Velgor's arc. Whereas Velgor began the original trilogy committed to the umbra side and ended it, in Drivari's words, "vulnerable and weak," Karrick was supposed to begin the sequel trilogy in that state of confusion and then end it more committed to the umbra side than ever. However, Drivari stated that this plan changed while shooting. Nonetheless, he claimed he kept his mind focused on that plan regardless of what was filmed. In 2024 , Drivari stated that, as Karrick is dead, he has no intentions of returning to the Aetherion universe. Furthermore, he admitted that he made the filming process "way more exhausting for" himself than it needed to be because, while he was working on Aetherion , he "hadn't quite figured out the momentum of a set that was that big." Meanwhile, Daisy Ridella —who portrayed Nyla in the sequel trilogy and is set to return in a forthcoming film —did not confirm nor deny if Karrick would ever return to Aetherion because she did not have any information to that affect. When asked if Drivari or her other sequel co-stars could return, she simply said she not know "what or who is who" in the upcoming film. Later, she repeated that she had no idea if Karrick was set to make some kind of posthumous appearance.

> " What a gift that character is. Everything he does is driven by self-hatred and self-love in equal measure. A rich stew. " ―Charles Soulea, on Zarrin Karrick

### Further appearances
