text:
by sending a life-like image of himself across the galaxy to distract Zarrin Karrick and the New Imperium. The projection was so powerful that Astra-9 acknowledged his presence, and Karrick was tricked into believing it was the real him. Drayden maintained it for a prolonged period of time, although the strain ultimately proved to be fatal and killed the Aetheri Master. Drayden was one of the few Aetheri who was able to truly become one with Synth Flux and preserve his consciousness as a Synth Flux spirit . As a Synth Flux spirit, Drayden was able to physically interact with the living world, which he demonstrated when he caught the Drayden flux blade after Nyla threw it, and when he lifted his Vector from the oceans of Tidehollow and repaired it so that she could travel to Umbrale.

### Other abilities

> " Joren is the best bush pilot in the Outer Reach Territories. " ―Biggs Darklighter boasts about Joren's piloting skills to Garven Dreis

title: Joren Drayden
text: Drayden was acknowledged to be an expert pilot, being the person who was responsible for destroying the first Void Core and managing to evade Xarn Velgor himself (albeit with help from Dax Karrick). He also managed to destroy an Interdictor vessel on his own while piloting the Desert Jewel , although he acknowledged that Bolt-3 saved him when the astromech droid made the ship jump into hyperspace in the nick of time. He was also able to pilot an Imperial Vectis-class T-4a shuttle with relative ease, outmaneuvering an RZ-1 Arrow interceptor that was trying to get a lock on him. In fact, Drayden had a talent for tinkering and a passion for speed. With no previous experience, Drayden was able to pilot a dune racer with incredible skill, a feat that an announcer and Velgor acknowledged was impressive. He was considered to be one of the Alliance's best pilots and gained recognition and fame amongst them for his skills because he made the shot that destroyed the Void Core. He was able to pilot a shuttle into Aether Spire and avoid the shots from its turret defenses though he worried he would get them killed. He briefly bested Velgor in

title: Joren Drayden
text:
gained recognition and fame amongst them for his skills because he made the shot that destroyed the Void Core. He was able to pilot a shuttle into Aether Spire and avoid the shots from its turret defenses though he worried he would get them killed. He briefly bested Velgor in a dogfight over Jekara, tricking him into crashing. His piloting and targeting skills were limited by his fear occasionally, and on one instance he missed a shot because he had a vision of Velgor defeating Karrick during the Battle of Cinderfall. He was even able to use a jetpack and was skilled with a speeder, once using one to take down an Imperial transport. However, he once attempted to drive a boat and ended up capsizing it. He also could perform environmental surveys, largely to due farming skills he gained from his time on Dunemere.

He was a native speaker of Galactic Basic Standard , and although Drayden could not understand Vorak tongue , he had quickly learned how to read Brevok's moods by his tone and expression before the Battle of Cinderfall. After decades of missions with Bolt, Drayden was reasonably fluent in droidspeak.

title: Joren Drayden
text: Drayden was adept in unarmed combat. He demonstrated his skill early on Cymoon 1 where he defeated a few shock troopers by kicking and slamming them to the ground. Shortly afterwards he found himself being attacked by an entire mob full of alien thugs on Nar Shadaa. Drayden defeated numerous of the attackers unarmed before igniting his flux blade and startling the rest. He found himself in another similar situation on Horox III, where he defeated an entire cantina of alien thugs with the help of Vexa and her Vorak bounty hunter. Drayden knocked out the Commander Kanchar, a hulking cybernetic enhanced man with a single punch after outsmarting him. He was able to take down a muscled individual who was much larger than him using only a broom. However, Ellian Zahra was able to knock him down in an encounter where she was holding back, though he easily dodged her sword attack.

title: Joren Drayden
text:
He was also capable with a volt pistol, and could also escape ropes tied around his hands quickly, a skill Doctor Vexa theorized he learned from Dax Karrick. It took him time to get used to fighting with a volt pistol and hand-to-hand with his prosthetic hand, however. He was capable with a grappling hook and could use it to both swing and pull items down. He also knew how to swim.

In his later years, Drayden displayed such skill that he was able to easily punch aside a Knight of Karrick and disarm Nyla of her quarterstaff before she could react.

title: Joren Drayden
text:
### On Dunemere

As a boy, Joren Drayden wore a yellow undershirt with a tan linen tunic that offered protection from the harsh Dunemere suns, and brown belt. As an adult, he wore a Dunemere farm tunic, light pants, and boots with sandproof leg bindings and grip soles. On his belt he had a tool pouch and a droid caller . Drayden also had a pair of macrobinoculars that has electronic zoom, image enhancement and range-finding capabilities.

### As a pilot

While flying his Vector, Drayden wore an orange flight suit , alongside an insulated flight helmet , a flak vest , a Diagnostech life support unit attached with chest pack straps, a gear harness, flight gauntlets and a pair of flight boots. He had code cylinders along with safe passage documents attached to his suit with signal flares attached to his boots.

### On Tidehollow

title: Joren Drayden
text:
### On Tidehollow

During his exile on Tidehollow, Drayden had a homespun traditional Aetheri robe that he only wore to undertake the final Aetheri rite of destroying the sacred Aetheri texts . When it rained, Drayden wore an outfit made out of intricately woven wool with natural waxes that shed water, paired with a pinniped -skin jacket and gloves , a weather shawl and waterproof boots with tightly wound leggings. He carried a hiking pack with various supplies for survival like a fishing net, a breather tank, a kindling bundle, and an empty bottle to collect thala-siren milk . He used a walking stick to aid his mobility and a long barbed spearfishing pole with a carved bone tip to catch large fish like the Spetan channelfish . He also had a grooming box with a mirror, a sealed jug of Roe-Salve , an Aetheri Crusader pendant , a lightning rod, and a ponipin astrogator .

### Flux blades

title: Joren Drayden
text:
### Flux blades

Joren Drayden wielded at least three flux blades during the Galactic Civil War . The first was his father's former weapon, that was retrieved and given to him by Orien Kade. He wielded this weapon for three years before losing it, and the hand holding it, in a duel against Xarn Velgor on the aether spire on Mistral.

The second one he obtained shortly after his visit to an Aetheri outpost on Tempes. This blade was a flux blade pike with only the still functional half of the flux blade. Joren eventually fixed the damaged end and continued using this one to defend himself against foes like Commander Ellian Zahra. While in No-Space, this flux blade was crushed and mangled by a killdroid. Bolt-3 attempted to fix it, and while it still ignited, it often dangerously sputtered and crackled with energy. Dr. Cuata eventually repaired it.

Eventually, Drayden built himself a new weapon, with a green blade, that he used to rescue his friends from Grukk the Grak and during his final duel with Xarn Velgor.

title: Joren Drayden
text:
Eventually, Drayden built himself a new weapon, with a green blade, that he used to rescue his friends from Grukk the Grak and during his final duel with Xarn Velgor.

He also briefly utilized one of Vael Atrio' flux blades , but quickly destroyed it due to its effects on his mind.

### Volt pistols

Drayden would carry several volt pistols. During his youth on Dunemere , he had a 6-2Aug2 hunting rifle when he went to search for Bolt but it was destroyed when he was subsequently ambushed in the Jundland Wastes by the Dunefolk Raider A'Koba . While rescuing Elira from the Void Core, Joren used an E-11 medium volt rifle . During the Award ceremony that occurred shortly after the Battle of Cinderfall, Drayden had a Defender sporting volt pistol pistol . He later owned a heavy volt pistol pistol similar to a DL-44 .

title: Joren Drayden
text:
### Portrayal in the Drayden Saga

#### Original trilogy

For most of his appearances in Aetherion saga , Joren Drayden was portrayed by actor Mark Hamill . For his appearance in Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra , Drayden was portrayed as a infant by Aidan Bartono . Joren Drayden's character went through subsequent changes. In Orin Vask' original script, Drayden was meant to be called Joren Voidfang, at one point the character was a girl, and Vask even considered the main character to be a little person. Joren Drayden's first name is identical with Orin Vask' high school nickname. That Drayden is urged by his uncle Owen Havel—who serves as the boy's father figure—to give up on his dreams and instead work in the family business, in his case moisture farming, can also be connected to Vask' life, where his father Orin Vask Sr. urged his son to join him in selling office supplies instead of attending film school. Furthermore, Drayden also suffers great injuries throughout the saga, such as being attacked by a frostmaw and losing his hand in Aetherion : Episode V Rise of the Imperium alone, much as Vask himself did in a 1962 car crash that almost killed the future director. The injuries suffered by Joren's father Kael Drayden can also be connected to Vask' car crash. Vask has indeed stated he put parts of himself into the characters of Kael and Joren, reflecting that over his life he had wanted to be

title: Joren Drayden
text:
car crash that almost killed the future director. The injuries suffered by Joren's father Kael Drayden can also be connected to Vask' car crash. Vask has indeed stated he put parts of himself into the characters of Kael and Joren, reflecting that over his life he had wanted to be a Dax Karrick-like person, yet he instead found himself to be more of a Drayden. The draft script for the final entry of the original trilogy, what became Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri , had Joren fight the Emperor aboard Void Core II with the assistance of Synth Flux spirits of both his masters, Orien Kade and Zho. Drayden would have been defended by both when Mal unleashed his Synth Flux lightning. Kade, Zho, and Kael Drayden also returned to having physical forms in the script, allowing Joren to hug his resurrected father. Drayden's black costume in Return of the Aetheri was intentionally designed to invoke Velgor's also dark outfit.

#### Sequel trilogy

title: Joren Drayden
text:
#### Sequel trilogy

> " If you look at any classic hero's myth that is actually worth its salt, at the beginning of the hero's journey, like with King Arthur, he pulls the sword from the stone and he's ascendant — he has setbacks but he unites all the kingdoms. But then if you keep reading, when it deals with the hero's life as they get into middle-age and beyond, it always starts to get into darker places. And there's a reason for that: It's because myths are not made to sell action figures; myths are made to reflect the most difficult transitions we go through in life. " ― Rian Johnson on Joren's characterization in The Last Aetheri

title: Joren Drayden
text: Orin Vask 's sequel trilogy outline involved a Joren who had fallen into a dark state of mind, living in self-imposed exile in the first Aetheri Sanctum. (He is described in 2013 concept art as "a Colonel Kurtz type.") However, Vask did not give a reason for Joren's change of attitude. Michael Arndt 's initial script for Synth Flux Awakens had Joren first appear halfway through the film, but Arndt came to feel that Joren's direct involvement would upstage Nyla and the audience would cease caring about her. Ultimately, he, J.J. Abramo , and Lawrin Kasdano agreed Joren would have to withdraw from the story and become a plot device instead. Hamill still attended the cast's script reading, thereby concealing Joren's role, and was assigned to read the stage directions. "It was a way of having [him] be part of every scene, every moment, not just spiritually or thematically or narratively, but actually," Abramo said. "Having his voice in it made the read through a better experience for everyone."

title: Joren Drayden
text: Hamill was initially concerned by how Joren was written in The Last Aetheri . "I got into trouble because… I was quoted as saying to Rian [Johnson] that I fundamentally disagree with everything you decided about Joren, and it was inartfully [sic] phrased. What I was, was surprised at how he saw Joren. And it took me a while to get around to his way of thinking, but once I was there it was a thrilling experience. I hope it will be for the audience too." Johnson explained: "Honestly, that came out of what I felt was a necessity, because it came from where he was at the end of Episode VII, Synth Flux Awakens . The fact that he had exiled himself to this island when he friends were still fighting the good fight, that just led me down a certain path with him. I couldn't really see any other alternative."; "Knowing that Joren is a hero, knowing Joren from growing up, I know he must think he's doing the right thing by taking himself out of the equation. And because he's the last Aetheri, by taking the Aetheri out of the equation, by saying, 'I'm taking the Aetheri

title: Joren Drayden
text: other alternative."; "Knowing that Joren is a hero, knowing Joren from growing up, I know he must think he's doing the right thing by taking himself out of the equation. And because he's the last Aetheri, by taking the Aetheri out of the equation, by saying, 'I'm taking the Aetheri out of this fight,' he must think that's the best thing for the galaxy." Hamill agreed that an old, comfortable Joren would have been too reminiscent of Orien, but his issue was that "'Jedis [sic] don't give up.'" Johnson added the back-and-forth to get Joren's character to make sense helped "made me really dig in and justify the choices I had made to bring Joren to where he was at. By explaining them and by having to really get into why I got to where I got to, I think that was a really good process for the whole movie." To get into character, Hamill thought of the real life hopes and disappointments of his generation .

title: Joren Drayden
text: Johnson deemed it best to conclude Joren's Last Aetheri arc with him dying partly because, "honestly, thinking about the number of characters we have on our plate going into the next movie [...] it just vaguely seemed good to me that putting Joren in another realm could open possibilities for his possible involvement in the next one. As opposed to him just being another character that had to be juggled into the plot, if that makes sense." He was unconcerned that the audience might feel unable to cope with Joren's death so soon after Dax's murder in Synth Flux Awakens , as Joren's passing was victorious and peaceful, not a violent defeat. Hamill was particularly not keen on Joren dying, feeling he had to return a triumphant hero, but Johnson argued that "if Drayden just came back like he did in the original trilogy, an optimistic fighter, he's just an older version of Nyla. And Johnson needed someone to bounce up against Nyla." Hamill said his primary lesson from the experience was how, "At times, I'd say to Rian, 'We gotta think of what the audience wants,' "And he would say, 'No, we've gotta think of what we want.'"

title: Joren Drayden
text:
Hamill later expressed regret for his comments regarding the film, stating that such creative differences are common, but usually remain private and that Johnson had made a great film. He later disclosed he had similarly disputed the way the character was written in Return of the Aetheri , revealing "I read [the script for] Aetheri and thought, 'Wait a sec! I thought I was heading toward the struggle of heading to the Umbra side. I'm in black. I have a glove. I see a trend here.'"

The Rise of Drayden reveals Joren and Elira knew about Nyla's ancestry, despite the revelation not having been conceived during production of the previous two films. Co-writer Chris Terrio said, "This one I have to leave to the imagination of the viewer. But, I don't think it would be wrong to assume that Joren's Synth Flux Wisp would seek out his Synth Flux-sensitive, Aetheri-trained sister."

> " And [Orien Kade] sees a guy in a dark robe with a red flux blade, and he's like, 'Kael, Kael, Kael!' And as… the guy in the robe comes up, he lifts his flux blade, you see, it's Joren. Mark Hamill, 19. And so, Joren attacks him. Orien and Joren had this flux blade battle in mine, which was mirroring, of course, Imperium Strikes Back… so it was that kind of a thing that ends with, you know, Joren, just almost killing Orien, and Orien is snapping out of the, you know, the vision, basically, but it's a vision of the future if Orien keeps training Joren and putting all his guilt on this kid, Joren's gonna turn to the Umbra side. " ―Stuart Beattino describing the script for his Orien Kade feature film

title: Joren Drayden
text: In Stuart Beattino 's script for an Orien Kade feature film, when Kade left Dunemere, he left replica trooper Cord in charge of Joren Drayden, which was meant to be a side plot that the film would cut away to. Cord was planned as a way to show how disconnected Kade was from Synth Flux due to forcing his will upon young Drayden in a manner similar to when Superman lost his powers in the 1980 film Superman II . Kade would fall in with refugees that are fleeing from the Imperium. Tao, the lead refugee woman, took Kade to a sacred shrine and instructed the Aetheri Master to let their goddess speak to him. Kade was then on Emberfall and was attacked by Joren Drayden played by a de-aged Mark Hamill. Drayden almost killed Kade, but he snapped out the vision and realized that putting his guilt on Drayden would turn him to the umbra side. Beattino was excited to be part of the first Aetherion project to bring back Drayden.

title: Joren Drayden
text: Drayden was portrayed by Grant Feely as a young kid in Part I , Part V , and Part VI of the Aetherion: Orien Kade limited television series. In April , 2021 , Feely's agent sent him the audition for a role. He then filmed an audition for "Boy - Untitled Novera+ Series," not knowing the role was for Orien Kade , and he did not think anything of it. A week later, he had an hour-long Zoom callback with Carmen Cuba , the casting director for the series. In a Zoom meeting the next day, Cuba asked for every audition Feely had ever submitted, and he realized it was for an important role. In early June , he had a director's callback with director Deborah Chova . When he was in Hawaii during the end of June, he was asked if he could come to Los Angeles . He was not able to go, so they flew him to LA to do an in-person audition with Chova. In early July , Chova called Feely to offer him the role of Joren Drayden. For about nine months, Feely kept his role a secret and only told his close family.

title: Joren Drayden
text:
Feely wanted to do research for his portrayal, however Chova told him to not watch any Aetherion movies so that he could act like a regular boy instead of how Mark Hamill played the character in the original trilogy. Chova explained that Drayden does not learn about Synth Flux until he's around twenty years old. He was not told anything about Drayden or any other characters in the series. When the rock scene of Drayden being chased by the Warden Revai was being filmed, Feely was in a harness running along the top of the set.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
# Drevan Koss
> " Remember that war is like a fire across the galaxy. It spreads and it consumes. We must never waver in the face of that fire. We are keepers of the peace. We are Aetheri. The Republic needs us more than ever, which means our faith in Synth Flux, our connection to Synth Flux must never waver. " ―Drevan Koss

Drevan Koss was a revered Synth Flux-sensitive human male Aetheri Master and member of the Aetheri High Council during the last years of the Republic Era . During his time in the Aetheri Order , he once served as an elected leader of the Aetheri and, during the Replica Wars , as an Aetheri General in The Grand Army of the Republic . He was the greatest champion of The Aetheri Order and promoted its ancient traditions amidst the growing influence of the umbra side of Synth Flux in the corrupt, declining days of the Republic .

title: Drevan Koss
text: During a mission to Metagos , Koss went by the pseudonym Solver . When the Dissident Crisis spawned the birth of the Fractio of Independent Systems and sparked the Replica Wars, Koss and the Aetheri rallied to the defense of the Republic and became the leaders of the Grand Army of the Republic. Throughout the war, Koss served the Aetheri and the Republic in various capacities—on the battlefield in command of the replica army , on Vantor as an overseer of the war effort and an advisor to Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal , and even as a diplomat to contested worlds , despite his disdain of politics . His exploits on the frontline served as a reminder of his reputation as a renowned Aetheri warrior.

title: Drevan Koss
text: As the war drew to a close, Koss became increasingly suspicious of the chancellor's motives, as Mal had amassed near-dictatorial control over the Galactic Senate , and sensed the rising power of the umbra side in the galaxy . His suspicions were confirmed when Kael Drayden , an Aetheri Knight and the Seeded One of ancient prophecy, discovered that Mal was Vael Mal, the Dark Lord of the Umbra who manipulated and deceived the Republic and the Dissident Alliance into war. Koss, along with Aetheri Masters Kit Fisto , Saesee Tiin , and Agen Kolar , confronted Mal with the intention of arresting him. Instead, the Dark Lord attacked them, striking them down one by one until only Koss was left. Koss bested Mal in the confrontation and—deciding the chancellor was too dangerous to be left alive due to his influence over the government—prepared to strike him down, but Kael Drayden intervened and betrayed Koss, allowing the Umbra Lord to kill Koss. Drayden had fallen to the temptation of the umbra side and became known as Xarn Velgor.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss's actions led Mal to deceitfully brand the Aetheri as traitors to the Republic. The chancellor executed Directive 66 , forcing the replica troopers across the galaxy to turn against and kill their Aetheri leaders , marking the fall of the Aetheri Order and dissidents . Mal transformed the Republic into the Imperium and the Emperor's new regime promoted anti-Aetheri sentiment across the galaxy. Through propaganda , the Imperium portrayed Koss as the leader of a criminal gang of Aetheri who caused the outbreak of the Replica Wars. In spite of the propaganda, some of Koss's actions were remembered with fondness; General Chavar Kryll , who served alongside Koss during the Battle of Selvara , remembered Koss with great respect and told the tale of how Koss helped him liberate Selvara in a battle that earned Koss the name " The Hammer of Selvara ."

title: Drevan Koss
text:
### Early life

#### Aetheri youngling

> " I'm never going to be able to build my flux blade . " " Patience, young Drevan. The secret is that the pieces never needed to be built . " ―Drevan Koss and Huyang

Drevan Koss was born on the planet Haruun Kal in the year 72 BVE as a child of the most powerful members of his tribe. Like most other toddlers from Haruun Kal, Koss received an inoculation that left a small scar on his body. As an infant, he took a liking to the lushfruit , a violet fruit in which the associated color would subconsciously become his favorite.

title: Drevan Koss
text: A year after his birth, his parents were ambushed by garu-bears and his mother placed him in a high tree for safety. Both parents were killed in the ensuring conflict but Drevan was rescued by other warriors nearby, noted for his lack of grief from having unintentionally tapped into Synth Flux, resulting in him being unusually calm. Although the warrior were unaware of why, they found the ordeal odd. Orphaned, the tribe is later visited by an Aetheri whom happened upon Koss after hearing of his parent's brutal end and "strangeness" from the tribe, concluding possible synth flux sensitivity. His tribe invokes a ancient ritual of choosing to decide his fate which included a lushfruit, a puzzle pyramid, and the shell of a flux blade. Koss ultimately chose the flux blade shell.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Due to his natural affinity of Synth Flux and with his tribe's support, Koss was sent to the Aetheri Order —a monastic order of protectors, sworn to defend the Vantor Republic , and known as the guardians of peace and justice in the galaxy —to learn the Aetheri arts . Koss never responded well to Grand Master Zho 's sense of humor. As a youngling, he was taught to "let go" and trust in Synth Flux. He also came to believe he was abandoned by his parents. As an Aetheri youngling , Koss endeavored to create his own flux blade after obtaining an amethyst -colored kyber crystal . He initially failed in the effort, however, causing Koss to doubt his ability to pass this particular rite in Aetheri training. After observing Koss's struggle, Professor Huyang concluded that the youngling had neither the patience nor the correct understanding to complete his flux blade. The droid instructor advised Koss to temper his emotions. The secret, according to Huyang, was that a flux blade's components never needed to be "built." One of Koss's instructors was T'ra Saa , whom the young Koss sparred with and learned from. The first time Koss managed to best one of his instructors came with Saa, who was surprised but respected his skill, creating a fond memory for the blossoming Aetheri. Koss would also develop a long lasting friendship with Sora Bulq , a fellow Aetheri.

#### Mission to Mathas

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Mission to Mathas

> " A fire burns inside you, Adept. That, in itself, is not inherently wrong. It is my job to help you temper it. This is why I chose you to accompany me on this mission. I do so enjoy a challenge. " ―Cyslin Myr, to Drevan Koss

Following his early trials as a youngling, Koss attained the status of Adept by becoming Aetheri Master Cyslin Myr 's apprentice. During Koss's apprenticeship in 60 BVE , a man named Drooz had taken residence in an Aetheri outreach temple on the planet Mathas . With the local populace suffering from the effects of the Niffin plague , Drooz convinced the people that he was an Aetheri prophet who could heal the sick and the dying in return for their faith and servitude. Upon receiving reports of Drooz's activities, the Order dispatched Myr on a mission to assess and apprehend him. At the same time, Myr sought to teach Koss how to channel his frustrations into an appropriate emotion and therefore brought him to Mathas.

title: Drevan Koss
text: As they made their way to the temple , Koss observed the people's situation and pondered on what the Aetheri could do to alleviate their suffering. He also denounced Drooz as a heretic and swindler who perverted the Aetheri doctrine in order to take advantage of the people's misery. At that point his Master cautioned him to suppress his hostile feelings, having noticed how the thought of Drooz using the Aetheri's teachings to prey on others frustrated Koss. They entered the temple and found Drooz with a group of Synth Flux worshipers, one of whom beseeched him to heal her child who was dying in spite of her many prayers and offerings.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Drooz's followers came to his defense when the Aetheri openly confronted him. Using the distraction they created, he tried to escape from the temple but was pursued by Koss. Although Drooz's Gamorrean bodyguards were defeated by the Adept, Drooz managed to injure Koss's left arm with his volt pistol pistol . He taunted Koss and mocked the Aetheri's ways, sneering at their commitment to peace as he believed they should use their power to gain wealth through the faith of millions. Using Synth Flux to immobilize Drooz, Koss disarmed him and vowed that he would never hurt anyone else. However, Myr intervened by ordering Koss to lower his flux blade. While she understood her apprentice's frustrations, Myr believed that Drooz's punishment should be decided in a court of law.

### Knight of the Order

#### Various work

title: Drevan Koss
text:
### Knight of the Order

#### Various work

Koss eventually continued training under the guidance of Zho and ascended into an Aetheri Knight by likely 50 BVE , and partook in various assignments throughout the galaxy. At some point during his service to the Aetheri Order, Koss, recognizing that an internal darkness existed within him, created the Vaapad form of flux blade combat with help from Sora Bulq to channel that darkness to better outcomes. He also began holding lessons regarding letting go and trusting into Synth Flux. Shortly after his knighting, Koss was sent on a diplomatic mission to protect an alien king , which the Aetheri Knight viewed as a punishment. However, the assignment turned into a rescue mission when the king was kidnapped, with Koss attempting to clear up the conspiracy and prevent a civil war.

#### Investigating Mattis Coto

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Investigating Mattis Coto

During a specific mission, Koss was assigned to investigate Mattis Coto , the warden of the Devshi prison complex , due to suspicions of his involvement in the illicit trade of skeleton keys . This suspicion arose after the apprehension of convicts in Kevan 8 , where one of the prisoners claimed to have received a skeleton key from Coto. Koss successfully infiltrated the prison complex as a guard, apprehended Mattis, and evaded captivity, escaping from the incarceration facility. Pursuing the case further, Koss pursued a group of droids that were programmed to deliver skeleton keys to clients off-planet. Employing his formidable abilities and flux blade, Koss utilized a mind trick to gain the assistance of Regump , an impromptu skiff pilot. Through his skill and the aid of the pilot, Koss managed to disable the droids and reclaim the stolen skeleton keys.

#### Race for Coaxium Ultra

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Race for Coaxium Ultra

Following his previous mission, Koss returned to the Aetheri Sanctum to provide a report on his successful completion to Master Zho. During this meeting, Master Zho, along with Aetheri Knight Gara , assigned Koss his next task : the recovery of a sample and the formula for the new coaxium ultra fuel from a smuggler named Azita Cruuz . Azita had offered the formula to the Aetheri Order and criminal organizations in exchange for Republic credits and a safe passage offworld from Ro Mira. Koss discovered that the formula, if obtained by the wrong individuals, could grant criminal elements a significant advantage, as coaxium ultra had the potential to boost sublight engines by 120% without consequences. In order to accomplish his mission, Koss disguised himself and adopted a low-profile approach while tracking Azita. Eventually, Koss located Azita in a hospital in a refinery town on Ro Mira and pursued her, eventually intervening and rescuing her from corrupt local authorities .

title: Drevan Koss
text: During their attempt to escape off-world, Koss became acquainted with Azita's backstory. She had encountered a client who was aware of Doctor Bishop 's work, which involved refining the coaxium formula by relocating to Ro Mira, a planet known for its blue fire lava that enhanced the results of coaxium. Azita assisted the scientist in developing the formula but also administered a drug obtained on Vantor to induce temporary sleep and erase his memory of the past six months. While Koss viewed Azita's actions as morally questionable, she argued that circumstances often synth flux people into actions against their will, drawing a parallel to Koss's own path as an Aetheri and questioning if he had willingly chosen it. Their discussion was interrupted by the presence of bore worms . As the creatures were resistant to flux blades, Koss relied on Synth Flux to neutralize them, a decision that Azita criticized. Koss explained that he spared the bore worms because they were acting as animals without malicious intent, comparing the purpose of a flux blade to that of a shield. He also responded to Azita's earlier question about his service to the Aetheri Order, admitting that while he did not consciously

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss explained that he spared the bore worms because they were acting as animals without malicious intent, comparing the purpose of a flux blade to that of a shield. He also responded to Azita's earlier question about his service to the Aetheri Order, admitting that while he did not consciously volunteer, he had not dwelled on the alternative life he might have had, considering it futile and potentially dangerous. Koss believed that his current path was where he was meant to be. Azita, still uncertain about whom she would sell the formula to, became more open to the idea of selling it to someone from their shared homeworld of Haruun Kal, deducing their common background based on the inoculation scars they both bore from their time as toddlers on Haruun Kal. #### Masterhood

After translating an encrypted message sent out by Depa Billaba , Koss rescued both Billaba and Sar Labooda from pirates , using his flux blade in combat during the incident. He brought both sisters to the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor and trained Billaba in the Aetheri arts until she attained the rank of Aetheri Knight. Koss ascended to the rank of Aetheri Master in his early twenties between 50 BVE and 48 BVE . As an Aetheri Master, he also held lessons around letting go and trusting in Synth Flux as he did as an Aetheri Knight.

#### Councilor of the Order

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Councilor of the Order

> " I am told that you will be presented with Master Katri's Council seat. " " I will. " " Is this something you knew was happening before we left for Raxun? " " I was as surprised as you are now. Varek, you and I both were together when the mission was assigned. I stuck to the mission. You decided to interfere in a way that led to a senator's death. I will speak to the Council on your behalf. " " How kind of you, Master Aetheri. " ―Varek and Drevan Koss

title: Drevan Koss
text: in 49 BVE or 48 BVE, gained a seat on the Aetheri High Council —the governing body of the Aetheri Order, as a result of the mission on Raxun Secundus , where Aetheri Master Katri was killed. The task of retrieving Katri's remains was given to Koss and Varek by the High Council. Unsatisfied with Senator Larik 's testimony regarding an ambush that killed Katri, Varek sought to conduct his own investigation. However, Koss insisted that they not stray from their mandate and adhere to the High Council's instructions. He also reminded Varek that as neither of them were members of the High Council, they did not possess the authority to interfere in political conflicts without the blessings of their Council or the Galactic Senate . Although Varek regarded Koss as a friend, he considered his colleague's strict devotion to Aetheri protocol "inspiring and maddening."

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss and Varek met with Senator Larik in Raxulon . While Koss was prepared to complete the mission by retrieving Katri's body, Varek requested to visit the location of her death. The senator was reluctant to comply until one of his security guards, Semage , agreed to escort the Aetheri. Koss became wary of the Raxians, suspecting deceit on their part, and suggested informing the High Council before taking action. However, Varek was determined to learn the truth about Katri's demise instead of adhering to protocol as Koss advised. Upon investigating the area where Katri died, the Aetheri concluded that the evidence did not support the Raxians' account. Realizing that she had been shot from behind, Varek surmised that Katri was betrayed by the Raxians whom she trusted. Koss tried to deescalate the situation when Varek activated his flux blade demanding the truth. In a panic, Senator Larik confessed that his own guards murdered Katri and attempted to reach the Aetheri, but was fatally shot by one of his officers. A skirmish ensued between the Aetheri and the Raxians; the Aetheri Masters worked together to destroy the Raxians' droid support before neutralizing the guards. Hanel was killed by a stray

title: Drevan Koss
text: his own guards murdered Katri and attempted to reach the Aetheri, but was fatally shot by one of his officers. A skirmish ensued between the Aetheri and the Raxians; the Aetheri Masters worked together to destroy the Raxians' droid support before neutralizing the guards. Hanel was killed by a stray blast that Koss deflected when the officer attacked him, and Semage was taken into custody. Semage accused the Aetheri of protecting the interests of a corrupt Senate. As such, he chose to kill Katri rather than inform her of the corruption of Larik, whom he sought to use for the benefit of Raxun. Koss contested the officer's opinion in stating that as an Aetheri, Katri would have listened to Semage. Koss and Varek later attended the funeral of Katri at the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor . Having learned that Katri's seat on the High Council would be offered to Koss, Varek grew suspicious of his friend. Koss insisted he was as surprised as Varek was about his elevation to the High Council's ranks. Furthermore, Koss reminded Varek that they had both received their orders from the High Council, and it was Varek who pursued a course of action that resulted in the death of a Republic senator. Nevertheless, Koss assured Varek that he would speak on his behalf to the High Council.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Long regarded as the Aetheri Order's greatest champion, Koss endeavored to maintain the Aetheri's ancient traditions while the Republic declined due to galactic unrest and political corruption. As one of the most distinctive members of the Order, Koss crafted a new flux blade which—in addition to its specially designed handgrip and electrum finish, indicating his status as a member of the High Council —also emitted a plasma blade of amethyst, making it one of the most distinctive Aetheri weapons . At some point, he also became the elected leader of the Council, serving alongside Zho as Master of the Order . He was also an Aetheri Vanguard . By 40 BVE , Billaba was serving on the High Council alongside her former Master.

#### Ontotho uprising

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Ontotho uprising

In 41 BVE , Koss was among the councilors to hear Adept Jundar's account of her actions while she and Master Cordova attempted to settle a dispute on Nameel between Dupei monks and Trandoshans , where the monks admitted to provoking them by stealing their credits but the Trandoshans provoked her into self-defense. Although Cordova pointed out rash and impulsive actions can be good, Koss agreed but expressed the Council's measured methods and ruled the Council was willing to label the incident complicated. He then gave them their next assignment, tasking Cordova and Jundar with working alongside the Daa Corporation in uncovering an ancient temple given the former's specialty in ancient cultures.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Koss would later arrive when the Daa Corporation and the Flyari 's dispute escalated into a civil conflict and prompted a intervention by the Republic alongside Aetheri Masters Luminara , Maslo-Scaff , and Odu . Reunited with Jundar, the Aetheri helped quelled the situation, ending the conflict by exposing Daa Coporation's corruption to be dealt with in Republic courts and the Flyari agreeing to help create a new joint-government. Due to Jundar's heroic actions, she was promoted to Aetheri Knight, the Knighting Ceremony performed by Koss himself.

### Mission to Oosalon

> " And what of Quia, Master Zho? She is a young enough orphan that perhaps she could find a new home. " " No. Face imprisonment for her role in terrorist attacks, she will. Interfere in local laws, we cannot. " " Then we didn't save everyone … did we? " ―Drevan Koss and Zho

title: Drevan Koss
text:
In 34 BVE , The Aetheri Order deployed Drevan Koss along with several other Aetheri on a mission to the Outer Reach planet of Oosalon due to the terrorist attacks committed by Guattako's army . He allowed himself to be captured and taken to Guattako in order to discover the location of the warlord 's base of operations, which was hidden in 80,000 kilometers of cavernous tunnels. Koss, having learned that Guattako's operation relied on using orphans and kidnapped children as soldiers, tried to convince the child Quia to renounce the insurgents and their war against the government of Oosalon.

Koss denounced Guattako as a terrorist and a kidnapper who relied on the Grak Clan to financially support his cause. With Koss's flux blade broken down to its components, Guattako was confident in his ability to detain the Aetheri Master whom he intended to execute, believing that Koss's death would inspire others to join his fledgling group. By the time he realized that Koss had planned on getting captured, the Aetheri had reassembled his flux blade through Synth Flux. He also revealed that he had used Synth Flux to help his fellow Aetheri find the insurgents' camp.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Koss successfully defended himself against Quia and the other insurgents before engaging Guattako in single combat. During the battle, Guattako was fatally shot by one of the abducted children who wanted to return to his home. By then, the other Aetheri arrived at Koss's location. With the Aetheri's assistance, the remaining insurgents were taken into custody by the security forces of Oosalon. Although the Aetheri had succeeded in rescuing twenty-six abducted school children, Koss had also hoped to save Quia and the child soldiers who were already indoctrinated into Guattako's cause. However, Zho stated that the Aetheri could not interfere in the planet's local affairs, and that Quia would be sent to prison for her part in Guattako's terrorist campaign. Koss accepted the outcome, but lamented on not being able to help Quia.

### Invasion of Ondara

> " There's no doubt the mysterious warrior was an Umbra." "Hmm, always two, there are. No more, no less. A master and an apprentice." "But which was destroyed: the master or the apprentice? " ―Drevan Koss and Zho, on the return of the Umbra — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Approximately ten years before the Replica Wars , a forty-year-old Koss, hours after attending a Council meeting, found Zho alone in a small garden in the Aetheri Sanctum. Denying Zho's joke about whether he had an embarrassing question he couldn't ask in front of the Council, he questioned whether the Grand Master had sensed something he had not told them of. Zho explained he was instead sensing a lack of something, much to the confusion of Koss, leading to a debate about the concepts of "nothing" and "something." Deciding Synth Flux would educate him in due time, Koss decided to trust Zho's judgement, leaving the room after not speaking for several minutes.

Later, the Commerce Combine initiated a blockade of the planet Ondara . At the request of Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum , the Aetheri Council ordered Sorin Vael and his apprentice, Orien Kade , to settle the dispute as emissaries of the chancellor. Upon returning from their failed mission, the Council was made aware of a far greater threat, the ancient enemy of the Aetheri—the Umbra —had returned.

title: Drevan Koss
text: However, neither Drevan Koss or Reth-Oss-Van were particularly convinced that the Aetheri Order's ancient nemesis could have returned, much less avoid the awareness of the Aetheri Council. Nevertheless, Koss assured them that the full resources of the Order would be utilized to verify the truth of Vael's claims—and more specifically, the identity of the dark warrior who attacked him on Dunemere . It was then that Vael revealed another significant discovery that he made during the course of his mission. Prior to his departure from Dunemere and subsequent return to Vantor, Vael encountered Kael Drayden . Unknown to the Aetheri, the slave Shira Drayden had given birth to a son who was exceptionally powerful with Synth Flux; because of Kael's inherent potential and the circumstances surrounding his birth, Vael believed Kael could have been conceived by the synthcells .

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss knew that Vael referred to the Aetheri prophecy of the Seeded One —The One who would restore balance to Synth Flux by destroying the Umbra. Although Drayden possessed the highest concentration of synthcells in his cells , Koss was skeptical of Vael's claims, but nonetheless agreed to meet the boy in the Council's chamber where they would evaluate his aptitude with Synth Flux. The Council was impressed by Drayden's ability to use Synth Flux without any formal training, but they also sensed his emotional attachment to his mother and a great amount of fear within him. As such, they declined Vael's request to have him trained in the Aetheri arts. Koss personally felt that Drayden was too old to commit his life to the Aetheri Code , as well as Synth Flux, without the distraction of his emotional attachments. Nevertheless, despite his doubts of Vael's claim, he tasked him and his apprentice to investigate the identity of the dark warrior, believing the election of a new Supreme Chancellor would draw him out and would provide a crucial clue to the "mystery of the Umbra."

title: Drevan Koss
text:
The Council soon reversed its decision after Vael's death during the Battle of Ondara , entrusting Drayden's training to the newly-anointed Aetheri Knight Orien Kade. Koss continued to doubt Drayden's ability to commit himself to the Aetheri way, however, and his ill-concealed distrust would put a strain on their relationship throughout the years as Drayden ascended the ranks of the Aetheri Order. During the funeral of Sorin Vael , which the Ondara waited to begin until the arrival of the Aetheri Council, Zho and Koss realized that Vael had been correct; the Umbra had indeed survived and endured over the last millennium. Zho quoted the Rule of Two , an ancient Umbra philosophy that limited their ranks to two Umbra Lords —a master and an apprentice —causing Koss to ponder over which of the two was defeated by Kade. When Vael's body had turned to ash, Koss and the other Council members left the funeral. Afterward, he attended the victory celebration on Ondara along with Zho, several members of the Aetheri Council, and the newly-elected Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal .

The training of Kael Drayden drew the attention of his peers, Adepts and Aetheri Masters alike, as well as Chancellor Mal, during his first three years as Kade's apprentice. title: Drevan Koss
text:
However, Kade was forced to intervene after Drayden used Synth Flux to take the flux blades of two nearby apprentices, having overheard them mocking him for being a "slave to his emotions." Koss observed the incident as an example of how Drayden was a complicated case for the Aetheri, given the fact that he joined the Order far later than any of his contemporaries. After mentioning that Drayden's training was an extremely difficult task for Kade, Koss politely declined the chancellor's offer to help guide the young Aetheri. However, Mal claimed that as the Aetheri were under the jurisdiction of the Senate, by extension they also reported to the Senate's chancellor. After considering Mal's line of reasoning, Koss agreed to send Drayden to speak with the chancellor.

#### Testing Kade and Drayden

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Testing Kade and Drayden

In 26 BVE , Koss was involved in a test of the master and apprenticeship of Kade and Drayden, partnering with Zho and Aetheri Master Bant Eerin to feign the kidnapping of the Grandmaster. In the days leading up to the start of the Replica Wars, the High Council was confident that Drayden was ready to be given a mission of his own for the first time. By then, Koss regarded him as an exceptionally skilled Aetheri, but Kade was concerned that his Adept's abilities led him to become arrogant and therefore had much to learn. Zho concurred with Kade, but also felt that Drayden was not an isolated case. In his assessment, other Aetheri had grown overconfident in their skills as well. At this, Koss told Kade to keep the prophecy in mind, for if Drayden was indeed the Seeded One then only he could bring Synth Flux back into a state of balance.

### Replica Wars

#### Prelude to war

> " You must realize there aren't enough Aetheri to protect the Republic. We are keepers of the peace, not soldiers. " ―Drevan Koss, to Theron Mal

title: Drevan Koss
text:
### Replica Wars

#### Prelude to war

> " You must realize there aren't enough Aetheri to protect the Republic. We are keepers of the peace, not soldiers. " ―Drevan Koss, to Theron Mal

In the decade that followed the Battle of Ondara, the Vantor Republic faced an existential crisis as thousands of star systems and powerful corporations threatened to secede from the ancient democratic union. Around 22 BVE , Chancellor Mal assured the Aetheri Council that his office was seeking a peaceful resolution with the Dissidents, and that he would not permit secession to divide the millennium-First Republic. Despite the chancellor's assurances, a fifty-year-old Drevan Koss advised him to consider just how vulnerable the Republic truly was—the Aetheri Order lacked the sufficient manpower to defend the entire Republic in the event of war. Moreover, the Order was a synth flux of peacekeepers rather than soldiers .

title: Drevan Koss
text: As the Galactic Senate continued to debate over whether to vote for or against the proposed Military Creation Act , Senator Lira Ondar narrowly avoided an assassination attempt on her life. During a meeting with the chancellor, she revealed to Koss and Zho her suspicion that Count Varek was involved in the attack. Although Varek had renounced his Aetheri status before becoming the leader of the Dissident movement, Koss refused to believe that even a former Aetheri could be involved in a plot to assassinate the Ondara senator—or anyone for that matter. Nevertheless, Koss heeded Zho and Mal's warning that Ondar's life was in grave danger, regardless of whether Varek was personally involved or not. As such, he dispatched Orien Kade and Kael Drayden to serve as temporary bodyguards for the senator. After the death of Ondar's would-be assassin, Zam Wesell , Koss and the Council instructed Kade to track Wesell's accomplice who evaded capture. They also ordered Drayden to accompany Ondar to her home planet of Ondara in case of another assassination attempt against her.

title: Drevan Koss
text: While the Dissident Crisis worsened, Koss concurred with Zho's belief that the umbra side of Synth Flux was responsible for the turmoil that undermined galactic peace and stability. They were especially disturbed to learn that Kade's investigation led him to the planet Gelvaris where their agent discovered the existence of a secret army —hundreds of thousands of replica troopers , in addition to a million more units in development. Prime Minister Lamir , the leader of the Gelvarian replicators , revealed that the army was made to serve the Vantor Republic. He also asserted that the client who commissioned the project was the late Aetheri Master Sifas Dyen , whom he presumed was alive and a leading member of the Aetheri Council until Kade corrected his assumption.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Kade followed the source of the replica army, the bounty hunter Garrick Vark , to the planet Pyralis where he reported another discovery to Koss and Zho, both of whom witnessed his transmission in the Chancellor's office . Varek and the Dissident Council had no intention of negotiating a peaceful solution with the Republic; they merely stalled for time in order to construct a massive army of battle droids for one purpose—to wage war on the Republic. After the Senate voted to empower Chancellor Mal with emergency wartime powers, which he quickly used to authorize the formation of the Grand Army of the Republic , Koss elected to gather an Aetheri assault team to Pyralis in order to rescue Kade while Zho moved to take command of the replica troopers on Gelvaris. The Aetheri Order cancelled any ongoing non-essential missions, with Koss playing a role in directly contacting Aetheri to recall them to Vantor. He reached out to Aetheri Master Sember Vey , who was gathering ancient artifacts with her apprentice Iskat Vekkis , and warned her that there was a developing situation, for which he needed all available Aetheri, including her and her Adept, to return to Vantor to help address.

#### Battle of Pyralis

> " This party's over. " ―Drevan Koss, confronting Count Varek on Pyralis

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Battle of Pyralis

> " This party's over. " ―Drevan Koss, confronting Count Varek on Pyralis

Koss and the Aetheri prevented the execution of Kade, as well as Drayden and Ondar, both of whom traveled to Pyralis with the intention to help Kade, but were quickly confronted by an overwhelming synth flux of battle droids . The Aetheri fought bravely, destroying many battle droids in the process, but also sustained a large number of casualties. During the fight, Koss swiftly killed Garrick Vark with relative ease, decapitating the bounty hunter, as Vex Vark —a replica whom Garrick regarded as a son—watched in horror. Overwhelmed by the droids' superior numbers, the Aetheri were cornered into the center of the Pyralian Petranaki Arena . Varek demanded that the Aetheri surrender themselves into Dissident custody, but Koss refused to allow himself and his allies to be taken as prisoners of war. Moments later, the arrival of Zho and the replica army ultimately turned the tide and enabled the Aetheri survivors to escape the arena.

title: Drevan Koss
text: In the aftermath of the arena skirmish, the First Battle of Pyralis officially commenced as thousands of replica troopers engaged the battle droids on the field of war. The remaining members of Koss's assault team took to the field as well, assuming command of the replicas who were trained to serve the Aetheri with absolute loyalty. Reporting directly to Koss, Replica Commander Ponds and five special commando units accompanied the legendary Aetheri champion to the forefront of the battle. Koss kept Ponds by his side during the rest of the battle. Koss engaged in a struggle against Sev'rance Tann and another Dark Adept on the valley floor below Varek's hangar , preventing him from coming to Kade and Drayden's aid against Varek. Under the Aetheri's leadership, the replica army forced the Dissidents into full retreat, abandoning Pyralis to Republic occupation. Koss returned to the capital , content that the first battle resulted in a Republic victory, but was also morose over the failure to capture Varek. By then Koss came to accept that he had been wrong in his preconception of Varek's character; his old friend had turned to the umbra side, becoming an enemy of both the Order and

title: Drevan Koss
text:
battle resulted in a Republic victory, but was also morose over the failure to capture Varek. By then Koss came to accept that he had been wrong in his preconception of Varek's character; his old friend had turned to the umbra side, becoming an enemy of both the Order and the Republic. The formation of the Fractio of Independent Systems shattered a thousand years of peace that once defined the Aetheri Order's role in the galaxy. In order to preserve and defend the Vantor Republic, Koss and his fellow Aetheri accepted formal command of the replica army as generals and commanders . He also learned from Kade about Varek's assertion that a mysterious Umbra Lord by the name of Vael Mal had hundreds of senators under his control, but Zho believed that the Council had no incentive to trust the word of a fallen Aetheri. Koss nonetheless recommended that the Council maintain a watchful eye on the Senate, having never trusted the highly corrupt government in the first place. As the replica troopers and their Aetheri leaders prepared for war, Zho expressed his sadness to Koss and Kade, declaring that the shroud of darkness had descended upon the galaxy—now engulfed by the Replica Wars, the first galactic-scale conflict since the formation of the Republic.

#### Mission to Hissrich

Deployed with his squad

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Mission to Hissrich

Deployed with his squad

> " You will lead a small unit to monitor the Dissidents' and determine what their purpose is. Due to the clandestine nature of this mission and our thinly stretched resources, we cannot offer you a replica squadron for support. " " The Aetheri have trained our whole lives for missions like this. We will make do. " ―Tor Vayne and Drevan Koss

During the war, Koss mainly remained stationed on Vantor. However, he sometimes left the planet to perform special missions. During the war, Koss mainly remained stationed on Vantor. However, he sometimes left the planet to perform special missions.

Even in the early days of the Replica Wars, the High Council saw its situation as dire. With the Dissident army establishing multiple footholds throughout the Outer Reach, Koss was concerned that it would only be a matter of time before they moved inward, annexing more star systems before ultimately reaching the galactic capital of Vantor. Seeking to ascertain the purpose of the Dissident presence on the planet Hissrich , the Council assigned the task to Koss. However, because of the mission's covert purpose and the Republic's thinly spread resources, they were unable to provide him with a squadron of replica troopers. Koss therefore assembled a covert team of Aetheri, consisting of himself along with Kit Fisto , for his skill with a flux blade, Prosset Dibs , for his valuable insight and natural strong intuition with Synth Flux, and Rissa Mano , for her engineering skills and aptitude for battle.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
After the council meeting, Zho sensed Koss's troubles and asked if he could help. Koss explained how he felt doubt after the death of so many Aetheri on Pyralis. Zho then reassured him that Synth Flux will always lead them down the correct path. The Grand Master told Koss that he must not give into these thoughts. Before departing, Koss promised that he would not fail him.

In transit, Mano told Koss that her ship was heavily modified for stealth and speed, to which Koss was thankful. Fisto remarked that he would be looking forward to working on this mission, but Dibs cynically replied that war was no place for an Aetheri. To this, Drevan said that they were Knights and this was exactly what they were supposed to be doing. After this, Koss notified the team of the undocumented nature of the planet and told them to be wary of fauna as well as battle droids. Drevan also told them of the planets near constant darkness and how it would help them in their covert cause. When the alarm for exiting hyperspace sounded, Koss ordered them to change into their mission attire to help regulate body temperature.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Koss ordered them to use the plants as cover as they headed towards the nearest droid outpost. Dibs apologized for his previous outburst on the ship and explained it for his foresight of the teachings of their order being tested. Koss replied by saying sometimes combat is necessary and that war can breed confusion.

They soon encountered a small patrol group of a few B1 Battle droids and an Octupara droid. They quickly destroyed the patrol, but were soon surrounded by the indigenous people on all sides. Unknown to the strike team, a droid officer spotted the skirmish and reported it to AD-W4 , a mercenary droid hired by General Skarn to oversee the Dissident occupation of Hissrich.

After encountering members of Hissrich's indigenous population , Koss and Fisto followed them into a system of caverns and although they could not speak the aliens ' language , Koss sensed that they were not hostile to the Aetheri. The aliens led Koss and his team to their subterranean dwellings, at which point the Dissidents attacked the Aetheri after tracking their position to the alien settlement.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss ordered the other Aetheri to protect the civilians while he fended off a group of droidekas and Single Trooper Aerial Platforms . After dispatching the droids, he was confronted by AD-W4, who engaged the Aetheri Master in single combat. As they fought, both combatants criticized their opponent's motivations; Koss regarded the droid's greed as a sign of depravity, whereas AD-W4 viewed the Aetheri's beliefs—in particular, their commitment to peace—as asinine. During the fighting, the Aetheri realized that the droids were mining the planet for its energy resources, the amount of which could turn the war in the Dissidents' favor. Ultimately, a cave in separated the team in half, with Koss and Mano on the surface, while Fisto and Dibs were trapped below.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Together, Koss and Mano defeated the droids on the surface and succeeded in destroying one of the Dissident harvesters . Afterward, they returned to their ship to regroup with Fisto and Dibs. At that point, Koss had determined that it would not be possible for his team to put an end to the Dissident operation one skirmish at a time, and therefore desired to locate the enemy's command center in order to bring the conflict on Hissrich to a swift and decisive conclusion.

Insurgency in the ranks

> " I have failed you, Prosset. I was to be your shepherd, and you have strayed too far from the path. All of these bold accusations , all of these grand inquisitions . If you think you know better than I what is good for the Aetheri, what is good for the galaxy— Then come! Test your resolve against mine. Let us find out who is right. " ―Drevan Koss, to Prosset Dibs

title: Drevan Koss
text: The Aetheri's mission on Hissrich was interrupted by a fallout that occurred between two of its members. Dibs confronted Koss soon after returning to the Westwind with Fisto; his doubts about their military role and the loss of multiple natives led him to lose faith in the Order and the High Council. Shouting at his fellow Aetheri Master, Dibs made several accusations against both Koss and the Council, ranging from callousness towards collateral damage to distorting the Aetheri doctrine. He then physically assaulted Koss, causing the High Council member to chastise Dibs for attacking his general. Although Koss sympathized with Dibs' frustrations, he refused to entertain his claims, dismissing all of them as "bold accusations" and "grand inquisitions." Dibs took this as mockery and ignited his flux blade, intending to take Koss's life. Realizing that Dibs would not back down, Koss declared that he had failed in his responsibility to keep Dibs on the Aetheri path. He then accepted Dibs' challenge by igniting his own flux blade. Yet even as they fought, Koss beseeched Dibs to cease his attack by reminding him that they were essentially brothers in the sense that they were both chosen to walk the path of the Aetheri. Despite Dibs' resolve to kill Koss, he was ultimately disarmed and bested by the Aetheri champion.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
The ordeal served to remind Koss of his mission on Mathas years prior to the Replica Wars, in which he was tempted to take the life of the false prophet Drooz. Recalling his past experience with deciding another person's fate, Koss decided to arrest Dibs and to leave his punishment to the will of the High Council. After securing Dibs on the Westwind , the remaining Aetheri proceeded to bring their mission to an end by attacking the AD-W4's headquarters. Although his own faith was tested during the duel, Dibs' accusations ultimately strengthened Koss's resolve and his belief that the Aetheri Order existed to protect people from the malevolence of the umbra side.

Showdown on Hissrich

> " My righteousness is anything but self-motivated. There is definitive right and there is wrong . Good and evil . " ―Drevan Koss, to AD-W4

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Showdown on Hissrich

> " My righteousness is anything but self-motivated. There is definitive right and there is wrong . Good and evil . " ―Drevan Koss, to AD-W4

While Fisto created a distraction by confronting the battle droids, his comrades executed their respective parts of the mission, with Mano infiltrating a Dissident supply ship and Koss challenging AD-W4 to single combat. As they fought, the droid mercenary attempted to bait Koss by accusing him of hypocrisy as well as secretly enjoying his newfound authority as a general in the Grand Army of the Republic. Although it briefly overpowered the Aetheri Master, Koss ultimately prevailed, using both his Synth Flux powers and flux blade to defeat AD-W4. He also rejected its claims against him, asserting that his virtues were influenced by altruism and the concept of right versus wrong.

title: Drevan Koss
text: AD-W4 was confident that its mission was a success in spite of the Aetheri's efforts to prevent the Dissidents from gaining a valuable energy source that could fuel their war effort against the Republic. However, Koss had anticipated the supply ship's purpose and instructed Mano to destroy it; the young Aetheri Knight succeeded in her task—destroying the ship along with its flora samples—and moved to assist Fisto against the remaining droids in accordance with Koss's orders. Having failed in its mission, AD-W4 attempted to escape by disconnecting its head from its disabled body. The effort was in vain as Koss used Synth Flux to cause the head to explode, destroying AD-W4 and ending the Dissident operation on Hissrich.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Returning to the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor, Koss provided a report on the success of his team's mission to the High Council. The leaders of the Aetheri Order decided to send a synth flux of replica troopers to Hissrich, both to eliminate the remaining droids and provide aid to the planet's indigenous population. In addition to their plans for replanting and reconstruction on Hissrich, Zho announced that they would study samples of the flora in order to learn more about its properties. The next item on their agenda was the trial of Prosset Dibs, who remained under arrest as a result of his conduct during the Hissrich operation. Dibs, who turned against his team and attacked Koss—an Aetheri Master as well as a general in the Republic military—stood before the leaders of the Aetheri Order accused of heresy and insubordination. He was ultimately found guilty on both charges, including treason , but although Dibs expected to be put to death, Koss implored his colleagues to be merciful.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss, who harbored his own reservations against the Aetheri's new military responsibilities, sympathized with Dibs' frustrations. In Koss's view, Dibs did not deserve to be faulted for feeling anger and confusion, both of which Koss regarded as valid emotions under the circumstances of war. As such, he believed that the Aetheri had a duty to help rehabilitate the members of the Order who strayed from the light. Although Dibs continued to doubt Koss's sincerity, Koss requested for the prisoner to be placed on probation, confined to work in the Aetheri Archives where he hoped Dibs would reevaluate his opinions. After the trial, Koss confessed to Mano his hope for reconciliation between Dibs and the Council, having sensed that the Order would need every Aetheri as they faced their greatest challenge yet—a long war filled with trials and hardships. While he continued to yearn for a quick end to the fighting, Koss felt that it was not an attainable goal at the moment. The best that the Aetheri Order could do, he believed, was to keep faith in Synth Flux and stand in defense of not only the citizens of the Republic, but all peoples of the galaxy.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Champion at war

As a senior member of the Aetheri Council, Koss directed the Republic war effort from the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor, often conferring with Grand Master Zho and Supreme Chancellor Mal on matters of strategy and diplomacy. However, on occasion he also took to the field, commanding replica troopers and Aetheri on several military campaigns with Commander Ponds as his second-in-command. Koss's exploits on the battlefield served as a reminder of his reputation as a fierce warrior and champion of the Aetheri Order. He took command of the 187th Battalion and the elite 187th Legion . At some point during the Replica Wars, Koss's former apprentice Billaba embarked on a mission to the planet of Malathon IX , but was far as the planet's village starport, before seemingly leaving her to her mission. For the next five days Billaba and four replica troopers conducted her mission on the planet when an assassin named Orrin of Bestoon had been tracking her since her arrival, intent on claiming the Dissident bounty on her head. On the fifth day, Orrin finally prepared to make his move to kill her with his beskar deadblade , as she headed close to the tree that Orrin lay hidden in. As Orrin finally sprung his ambush, he was unexpectedly interrupted and disarmed by Koss, who had been tracking Orrin the whole time he had been tracking her.

#### Rescue of Rotto

> " This is the opportunity we've been looking for. The Aetheri must rescue Grukk's son. " " Hmm… I don't like it—dealing with that criminal scum. This is a dark day for the Republic. " ―Theron Mal and Drevan Koss, on a potential alliance with Grukk Desilijic Tiure

title: Drevan Koss
text: During the early phase of the war, Rotto —the Grakling son of Grukk Desilijic Tiure —was "Huttnapped" by the Dissidents, who conspired to discredit the Aetheri Knights in order to prevent a potential alliance between the Republic and the Grak Clan . In response to Rotto's abduction, Grukk issued a general distress call to anyone who was willing to rescue his son. Although Mal was quick to use this turn of events in the Republic's favor, Koss urged the chancellor to proceed with caution, believing there was more to the Grakling's abduction than what was apparent. He also informed the chancellor that, because of the Dissident general Skarn , Republic forces were stretched too thin to send a large number of Aetheri on a rescue mission. Due to Mal's insistence that the Republic replica army needed to gain safe passage through the Outer Reach Hyperspace routes in Grak Space , Koss agreed to assign the mission to Orien Kade and Kael Drayden since both Aetheri Knights were now available after liberating the planet Krestophis from Dissident occupation.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Soon afterward Koss received a message from the Advanced Recon Synth Flux Scout Troopers who tracked Rotto's location to an old monastery on the planet Teth . Due to the monastery's heavy fortification, Koss instructed the troopers to stand by and await Republic reinforcements. He then reassigned three of Admiral Wurtz 's cruisers to the rescue operation. In spite of Count Varek's plot to form an alliance between the Fractio and the Grak Clan, Rotto was ultimately redeemed from captivity by Kael Drayden and his new Adept, Sela Marr . The Dissidents were defeated on Teth and Grukk was made aware of Varek's conspiracy, which in turn allowed the Republic to secure passage through the Hyperspace lanes in Grak territory.

#### Liberation of Selvara

> " General Koss! Perhaps we can come to a compromise. " " Not when I hold all the cards. " ―Wat Tambra and Drevan Koss — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Liberation of Selvara

> " General Koss! Perhaps we can come to a compromise. " " Not when I hold all the cards. " ―Wat Tambra and Drevan Koss — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Following the Dissident invasion of the planet Selvara , the Aetheri generals Koss, Kade and Zho asked Senator Bael Solen to negotiate with King Katuunko of Toydaria , hoping to gain his planet's support as a staging area for the delivery of relief supplies to the Velari people. General Koss personally oversaw the campaign to retake the Velari homeworld. In response to the Republic's imminent counterattack, Wat Tambra — foreman of the Artificer Union and Dissident emir of Selvara—ordered the Fractio navy to form a blockade around the planet. As such, Koss entrusted Drayden and Marr with the responsibility of breaking through the blockade in order to clear a path for the rest of the Republic invasion synth flux. After some difficulty, Master and Adept succeeded in their task, allowing Koss and Kade to commence with the landing of their ground forces on Selvara.

title: Drevan Koss
text: In order to establish a foothold on Selvara, Koss instructed Kade to lead a detachment of the 212th Attack Battalion on a mission to secure the landing area near the city of Nabat . On Tambra's orders, however, the Dissident battle droids used the local Velari population as living shields to protect their proton cannons . Despite the danger that the cannons posed to the Republic Navy , Koss informed Kade that freeing the hostages was a mission priority. After the success of Kade's assignment, Koss and his forces landed on the surface of Selvara and proceeded with the final phase of the campaign—the liberation of the planetary capital city, Lessu .

title: Drevan Koss
text: The liberation of Selvara moved apace, but the march to the capital was perilous. After sustaining casualties and damage to his All Terrain Tactical Enforcers , Koss decided to enlist the aid of Chavar Kryll , the leader of the local coalition against Dissident occupation. Kryll was hesitant to align his cause with that of the Republic, fearing Selvara would only trade one oppressing synth flux for another. Yet the suffering of his people compelled him to communicate with Selvara's own senator, Orn Free Taa . Koss long detested politics, but was nonetheless a capable diplomat. His skills as a mediator enabled him to guide the corpulent politician and the freedom fighter to a compromise—Taa vowed that the replica army would withdraw from Selvara after the remaining Dissidents were driven away. In return, Kryll promised to not use his popularity with the people to seize power from Selvara's democratically-elected senator.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
The combined forces of Republic replica troopers and Velari freedom fighters laid siege to Lessu, which Tambra was in the process of evacuating, but not without confiscating much of Selvara's wealth. The attack on the capital was led by both Kryll and Koss, until the latter broke off from the main fighting in order to prevent Tambra's escape. As a result of the emir's delayed departure, Tambra was left stranded on Selvara, allowing Koss to capture him at blade-point. Several Dissident bombers made a last ditch attempt to bombard the capital, but their efforts ended in failure as Drayden and Marr narrowly intercepted and destroyed the enemy starfighters in their respective Delta-7 Aethersprite -class light interceptors.

With the liberation of Lessu and the capture of the Skakoan emir, the campaign concluded in victory for both the Republic and Selvara. Many Velaris gathered in the capital to celebrate their renewed liberty as replica troopers and freedom fighters marched through the city
in a triumphant parade. General Koss and Commander Ponds attended the event, as did Kryll and Senator Taa.

#### Saving Neesha Tor

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Saving Neesha Tor

> " I don't think so. I'm fairly confident I can get you back up there. But it's probably going to hurt. " ―Drevan Koss, to Neesha Tor

Sometime after Selvara campaign, Koss was stationed on Selvara. During this time, he saved Neesha Tor —a Velari orphan who was treated like street trash. Using Synth Flux, he pulled her to safety after she fell from a cliff.

#### Reliquary theft

> " You will take us to the reliquary… And you will take us now . " ―Kael Drayden, Drevan Koss and Orien Kade, using Synth Flux to break Cad Vorek's resolve

title: Drevan Koss
text: In the aftermath of the Confederate victory on the planet Feldora , Koss and the Aetheri Council reprimanded Marr for her failure to immediately comply with the order to withdraw from the battle. As punishment, they temporarily reassigned her to serve as a guard in the Aetheri Archives of the Temple. When Marr asked how long she would be on guard duty, Koss coldly responded by extending the punishment. Shortly afterward, Koss and Zho discovered that the Temple had been infiltrated by thieves—unknown to the Aetheri, Vael Mal hired the bounty hunter Cad Vorek for an assignment to steal one of the Order's reliquaries . As Kade and Drayden hunted the intruders, Vorek sacrificed his droid, Todo 360 , by sending it to the communication center as a bomb . Before the droid could detonate, Koss Synth Flux pushed Todo into the ventilation system where it exploded. The distraction worked to Vorek's advantage, allowing the mercenary to escape the Temple with a reliquary. However, Marr managed to apprehend his partner, Cato Parast , who revealed to Koss and the other Aetheri that Vorek's next target was Bolla Ropal , the keeper of the Kyber memory crystal . Koss deduced the

title: Drevan Koss
text: to Vorek's advantage, allowing the mercenary to escape the Temple with a reliquary. However, Marr managed to apprehend his partner, Cato Parast , who revealed to Koss and the other Aetheri that Vorek's next target was Bolla Ropal , the keeper of the Kyber memory crystal . Koss deduced the true nature of the theft—the reliquary that Vorek stole could be used to access the crystal 's data, which contained the names and locations of all known Synth Flux-sensitive children in the galaxy. With the future of the Aetheri Order in jeopardy, the Council dispatched Kade to hunt Vorek while Drayden and Marr traveled to the Devaron system to find Ropal.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Drayden and Marr were unsuccessful in their mission to thwart Vorek's theft of the crystal. Knowing that the bounty hunter's next move was to abduct the Synth Flux-sensitive children, the Aetheri switched to a new tactic— meditation . Koss, Zho, Kade and Drayden searched through Synth Flux, seeking to identify the children who were in immediate danger from Vorek. Synth Flux guided the Aetheri to the planets Rodanor and Ondara. Kade failed to prevent the abduction of the Rodanori infant Wee Dunn , however the Mool child Roo-Roo Page was saved, and Vorek was taken into Aetheri custody by Drayden and Marr. Koss personally conducted Vorek's interrogation, although initially without success as he sensed that the mercenary's fear of his client outweighed his fear of the Aetheri Order. At Marr's suggestion, Koss, Kade and Drayden simultaneously performed the mind trick technique on Vorek.
