Despite the possibility of permanently damaging Vorek's mind in the process, the Aetheri felt that he had given them no other recourse except to synth flux his compliance for the sake of the Order's future. The experience proved too painful for Vorek, who finally relented to the Aetheri's demands.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Vorek brought Koss, Kade, and Replica Commander CC-2224 to Black Stall Station where the reliquary was kept. The Aetheri inadvertently trigger the station's defense turrets , however, allowing Vorek to leave the space station in an escape pod while Koss and Kade defended themselves. Both Aetheri Masters ultimately survived the trap and escaped with the reliquary just prior to the station's destruction. Simultaneously, Drayden and Marr tracked the missing infants to the planet Emberfall and were able to rescue them all before they could be used in the schemes of the Dark Lord of the Umbra .

#### Battle of Malastare

> " I have a bad feeling about this. " ―Drevan Koss

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Battle of Malastare

> " I have a bad feeling about this. " ―Drevan Koss

When the Dissidents invaded the planet Malastare , homeworld of the Dug species , Koss again took to the field commanding Republic forces with the assistance of Commander Ponds and General Drayden. Preventing the Dissident conquest of Malastare was not their only objective; the Republic sought to gain access to Malastarian fuel . Doge Nakha Urus , leader of Malastare, agreed to sign a treaty of trade between the Republic and Malastare, provided that the Dissidents were first driven off of Malastarian soil by Koss's forces. However, the Republic soon found itself heavily outnumbered upon confronting the Dissident invasion synth flux on the open field of battle.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Despite this, the Republic had a backup plan—the electro-proton bomb , developed by the Republic scientist Doctor Sionver Boll , was designed to neutralize a specific target: the Dissident battle droids. The doctor assured Koss and Chancellor Mal—who communicated with Republic forces via hologram —that the bomb posed no threat to organic-based units, such as replica troopers and the Malastarian Dugs. The plan met with the Chancellor's approval, but did little to assuage Koss's concerns. Although the Aetheri Master proposed to seek an alternative solution, the bomb's use was authorized by Mal and Urus. Upon detonation, the immediate blast incinerated the droids that were closest to the explosion. The subsequent discharge of EMP radiation caused the remaining the droids to shut down, along with every form of machinery within proximity of the overall blast.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Though the experimental bomb succeeded in neutralizing the entire Dissident invasion synth flux in one fell swoop, the surface began to collapse as a result of the explosion, creating a massive sinkhole that began at ground zero and expanded in every direction. A rescue operation soon commenced in order to search for the Republic troops who fell into the sinkhole. After losing communication with the rescue party, Koss and Ponds led a team to ascertain the fate of the survivors. Their investigation ultimately led them to discovering the Zyll Beast —an ancient creature native to Malastare, its species was long believed to be extinct by the Dug population. The beast, awoken by the bomb, chased after Koss and his troops, namely Ponds, Trapper , and Hawkeye , until Drayden created a distraction by flying maneuvers around it in his Aetheri starfighter.

title: Drevan Koss
text: After escaping from the sinkhole, Koss regrouped with Drayden and Urus in order to develop a strategy to neutralize the Zyll Beast. The Malastarian doge was adamant that the creature (which he regarded as a "dangerous bloodthirsty monster") should be destroyed—a plan which Mal supported in order to ensure the Dugs' cooperation with the Republic's needs for Malastare's fuel . Koss strongly objected on the ground of Aetheri morality, however. Due to the possibility that the beast could be the last of its species, the Aetheri Master was determined to preserve its life. His value for life ultimately conflicted with Urus' insistence on the creature's extermination. Urus went ahead with his plan upon discovering the harmful effects that Malastarian gas had on the Zyll Beast, prompting Koss to intercede in defense of the creature's life by threatening the doge with his flux blade.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
The situation was ultimately resolved when a group of Republic RX-200 Falchion -class assault tanks concentrated their fire on the Zyll Beast and, as a result, incapacitated the creature. The Dugs believed that the beast was finally dead when in fact the stun cannons merely rendered it unconscious—long enough for Republic forces to transport the Zyll Beast to Vantor for scientific research. Though the Dug Council formally ratified Malastare's treaty with the Republic, Koss made no effort to conceal his disapproval of Mal's decision to bring the dangerous beast to the galactic capital—a move that the Aetheri Master regarded as folly on the Chancellor's part.

#### Zyll Beast incident

> " With respect, Chancellor, I believe this creature could pose any number of dangers. Bringing it here to Vantor is a mistake. " ―Drevan Koss, to Theron Mal

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Zyll Beast incident

> " With respect, Chancellor, I believe this creature could pose any number of dangers. Bringing it here to Vantor is a mistake. " ―Drevan Koss, to Theron Mal

Koss returned to Vantor with the sedated Zyll Beast in tow. As the replica army transported the beast to the Republic Science and Technical Center , Koss again expressed his disapproval of Mal's decision to move a dangerous creature to the capital. By then, however, it was clear to him that the Chancellor would not listen to the Aetheri Master's counsel on this matter. Mal claimed that the research conducted on the Zyll Beast would be beneficial to the Republic war effort, although his reassurance did little to alleviate Koss's concerns about the safety of Vantor. At Kade's suggestion, the Aetheri turned to Senator Lira Ondar in the hopes that she would have more success in reasoning with the Chancellor.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Shortly after its arrival, however, the Zyll Beast escaped from its confinement and proceeded to rampage through the cityscape of the galactic capital. Koss and the other Aetheri mobilized Republic forces in order to prevent the beast from causing more damage and casualties on Vantor. Mal, who had ordered the beast's destruction, was caught in its path while attempting to evacuate the Senate Office Building . Koss and the Aetheri consequently focused their efforts on saving the Chancellor's life, which ultimately led to the death of the Zyll Beast when Mal ordered the Republic gunships to fire Malastarian gas bombs on it.

#### Senate conspiracy

> " We chose Senator Ondar because she and Korvex entered the Senate in the same year. They served on the same committees. They were… good friends. " ―Drevan Koss, to Kael Drayden

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Senate conspiracy

> " We chose Senator Ondar because she and Korvex entered the Senate in the same year. They served on the same committees. They were… good friends. " ―Drevan Koss, to Kael Drayden

During the Replica Wars, Senator Rush Korvex of the planet Scipio became a suspected traitor to the Republic. Due to the lack of proof, however, Koss and the Aetheri Council instructed Drayden to recruit Senator Ondar as a spy , believing that their former relationship would enable the Ondara politician to gain the alleged traitor's confidence. Ultimately, the Council was right to be suspicious of Korvex as Ondar discovered proof that her colleague had secretly dealt with the Dissidents on behalf of the InterGalactic Banking Clan while pretending to be a Republic loyalist.

#### Battle of Steelgrove

> " I've just received a distress signal from our forces on Steelgrove. Master Koss's defenses held, but at a great cost to his men. They need medical supplies immediately. " ―Reth-Oss-Van

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Battle of Steelgrove

> " I've just received a distress signal from our forces on Steelgrove. Master Koss's defenses held, but at a great cost to his men. They need medical supplies immediately. " ―Reth-Oss-Van

On and off since the early weeks of the Replica War, Koss personally oversaw the defense of Steelgrove against oppositional forces that sought to wrest control of the planet from the Republic. The Aetheri Master's forces prevented the fall of Steelgrove to enemy control, but also sustained a large number of casualties in the process. After the battle Koss sent a distress signal, which Reth-Oss-Van received shortly after the Republic's reconquest of Pyralis , informing the Aetheri of his victory while simultaneously requesting medical supplies for his injured soldiers.

#### Mission to Ridlay

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Mission to Ridlay

Koss along with Commander Ponds and Lightning Squadron, were sent to investigate a communication blackout on Ridlay . There, they found a village abandoned and only one person, Agon . He claimed that ghost were coming toward the. Koss and the squadron then joined the villagers in their shelter. According to the villagers, the ghosts come every fifty years during Ridlay's eclipse for a celebration. However, the ghosts had driven them from their home. Koss believed there was something else with the ghosts and asked Agon to lead him to the Ascension Well . Koss and the squadron realized that ghosts were conflicted due to the presence of the Dissident being led by Varek.

Koss fought Varek until he Synth Flux pushed him. Varek left their fight and ordered his battle droids to finish Koss and his forces off. Koss ordered Ponds and Lightning Squadron to retreat while he would finish off the droids. Koss then saved Agon from a ghost and was able to clear their minds of Varek's poison. Koss and Agon watched as the ghosts returned to normal and left as the eclipse ended

#### Assassination attempt

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Assassination attempt

> " Vex was on Pyralis when his father died. He watched as I killed him. " " That would complicate things. " " Indeed. " ―Drevan Koss and Kael Drayden > " Vex was on Pyralis when his father died. He watched as I killed him. " " That would complicate things. " " Indeed. " ―Drevan Koss and Kael Drayden

As the war progressed, Vex Vark conspired to assassinate Koss out of vengeance for the death of father, the replica template Garrick Vark. Aided by the bounty hunters Ayla Vossk , Boskan , and Castas , Vark infiltrated a squad of replica cadets during a tour of Koss's starship, the Vorash -class Iron Cruiser Endurance . Initially, Vark intended to kill Koss by placing an explosive device in the latter's quarters. However, the Aetheri Master was called away mere seconds before the bomb was triggered, resulting in the death of a replica trooper. As the Endurance crew searched the vessel for Koss's would-be assassin, the rogue replica amended his plan by sabotaging the Iron Cruiser 's reactor core, causing the starship to crash into the surface of the planet Vanqor . After escaping the doomed vessel, Koss and Drayden's search for survivors led them to an escape pod that contained the cadets with the exception of Vark, whom Vossk retrieved in Reaver One prior to the Aetheri's arrival.

title: Drevan Koss
text: In the aftermath of the destruction of the Endurance , Koss and Drayden traveled to the crash site hoping to find survivors—including Admiral Kilian and CT-411, both of whom opted to remain with the ship as it went down. During the search, Koss chastised Drayden for encouraging individuality in his droid, the astromech unit Bolt-3 . Before long, the Aetheri generals discovered several dead replicas along with signs that they had survived the crash only to be executed shortly after. On the bridge Drayden discerned a Ferrik helmet in the rubble. At that moment, Koss remembered both Garrick and Vex Vark, leading the Aetheri Master to realize that it was the latter who attempted to assassinate him. Although Koss was unable to prevent Drayden from triggering the bomb within the helmet, he succeeded in saving the younger Aetheri's life by pulling him away from the explosion through Synth Flux. The blast caused even more damage to bridge, however, leaving both men trapped and injured under a large pile of debris. Unable to escape on their own, Drayden instructed Bolt-3 to relay their situation to the Aetheri Sanctum. Koss, on the other hand, expressed little faith in the droid's ability to

title: Drevan Koss
text: blast caused even more damage to bridge, however, leaving both men trapped and injured under a large pile of debris. Unable to escape on their own, Drayden instructed Bolt-3 to relay their situation to the Aetheri Sanctum. Koss, on the other hand, expressed little faith in the droid's ability to succeed. As they lay trapped and waiting for the droid to return with help, Koss began to reflect on his actions at the Battle of Pyralis, particularly his victory over Garrick Vark and how Vex witnessed his father's death at Koss's hand. Ultimately, Drayden's droid returned with a rescue party—consisting of Tor Vayne , Sela Marr, and the replica troopers of Wolfpack —and managed to save both Aetheri just prior to the full collapse of the Endurance bridge. Before returning to Vantor, Koss praised Bolt-3 for saving his life, much to Drayden's surprise.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
After returning to the Republic capital, Koss and Drayden recuperated at the Aetheri Sanctum where they initially argued over their next course of action in light of Vark's attempt on their lives. Although Drayden insisted that the Aetheri should hunt the renegade replica and bring him to justice, Koss was content to let the matter go, preferring to not become entangled in a vendetta as Vark was against him. A transmission from Ayla Vossk, who revealed the hostages she took from the Endurance , changed the Aetheri Master's mind. Koss decided to confront Vark and his accomplices upon witnessing Vossk's execution of CT-411, but due to his injuries he allowed Vayne and Marr to go in his stead. Their mission was a success, resulting in Vark's arrest and the rescue of the remaining hostages. On Vantor, Koss confronted Vark in person, who regretted his actions on the Endurance , but refused to forgive the Aetheri for Garrick's death. The unrepentant replica was then sent to prison by Koss.

### New threats and an ongoing war

#### Farr's funeral and the brother of Vreth

title: Drevan Koss
text:
### New threats and an ongoing war

#### Farr's funeral and the brother of Vreth

Following Vark's arrest, Koss attended the funeral of the Rodanori senator Onaconda Farr , who was assassinated by his personal aide , Lolo Purs .

Later in the war, the Aetheri Council received a holorecording of the Devaron massacre . Koss and Kade observed the footage which revealed the Zyrrak warrior Savage Opress whom Kade mistook for Vael Vreth. Koss informed his colleague that the Zyrrak in the recording was not the Umbra Lord he fought on Ondara. He further explained that the Zyrrak and Vreth were Gloomreachians of Gloomreach , not Iridonia as they previously believed in Vreth's case.

#### Kidnapping of the Chancellor

> " Tell me about my target. " " His name is Moralo Eval. Works directly for Count Varek. Rumor is their plot will be hatched in three revolutions at the festival on Ondara. " ―Orien Kade and Drevan Koss

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Kidnapping of the Chancellor

> " Tell me about my target. " " His name is Moralo Eval. Works directly for Count Varek. Rumor is their plot will be hatched in three revolutions at the festival on Ondara. " ―Orien Kade and Drevan Koss

When rumors reached the Council that the bounty hunter Moralo Eval was planning to abduct Chancellor Mal despite his incarceration at the Republic Judiciary Central Detention Center , Koss, Zho, and Kade conceived a plan for Kade to infiltrate Eval's operation by impersonating the bounty hunter Rako Hardeen . Koss arranged for Drayden to arrest Kade, posing as Hardeen, and have sent to prison. He was then informed that fellow bounty hunter Cad Vorek was planning to free Eval. Following Eval, Vorek and Kade's escape from the detention center, Koss and Zho rescinded the bounty to ensure that they would continue on their way to Sireno where Count Varek awaited their arrival.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
While Kade continued to impersonate Hardeen, Koss accompanied the Supreme Chancellor to his homeworld of Ondara for the Festival of Light . The bounty hunters executed their plan during the ceremony, disabling the ray shield and kidnapping Mal. Through Kade's intervention, however, Koss and Drayden were able to apprehend Vorek and Eval before they could escape with their prisoner .

#### Attack on the Temple

> " It is the Council's opinion that Adept Sela Marr has committed sedition against the Republic, and thus she will be expelled from the Aetheri Order. " ―Drevan Koss, pronouncing the Council's decision to expel Sela Marr

title: Drevan Koss
text: Following the a terrorist explosion in a hangar of the Aetheri Sanctum, the Council recalled Drayden and his apprentice to Vantor. After briefing the two Aetheri on the situation, Koss and Zho assigned them to oversee the Aetheri Order's internal investigation. In addition, they suspected that the attack was caused by a rogue Aetheri. As neither Drayden or Marr were present at the time of the bombing, Koss and the Grand Master considered them above suspicion and therefore suited to the task. Koss also assigned the analysis droid Russo-ISC to the investigation, to work alongside Drayden and Marr. During the investigation, Drayden and Marr reported directly to Koss, who informed them that a swift conclusion to the case was imperative as rumors began to circulate within the Senate that the military police could become involved. With the arrest of Letta Turmond , Koss and Zho concluded that the radical Vantori was the main culprit in the bombing of the Temple hangar. While there was no indication at the time of an Aetheri's involvement, the incident served to fuel anti-Aetheri sentiment among the Republic citizenry—an outcome that concerned Koss.

title: Drevan Koss
text: In the aftermath of Turmond's arrest, Koss attended a funeral ceremony to honor the six Aetheri Knights who were killed in the hangar blast. Shortly thereafter, Drayden's Adept came under suspicion of being the true mastermind behind the bombing after Turmond was Synth Flux-choked to death in her presence. Admiral Wilhard Varrix contacted the Council and claimed that Marr had not only murdered Turmond, but also several replica troopers during her escape from the Republic Center for Military Operations . The Council endeavored to apprehend the fugitive Adept, although Koss was concerned by Zho's decision to send Drayden after his own apprentice, believing that his emotional connection to Marr would complicate the mission.

title: Drevan Koss
text: The hunt for Marr led to her capture and subsequent confinement in the Aetheri Sanctum. As the Council debated on what to do with her, Varrix contacted them on the Senate's behalf, imploring the Aetheri leadership to expel Marr and surrender her to military custody. Koss was troubled by the Council's options in the matter—to either stand by Marr, as Kade insisted; or remove her from the ranks of the Order as the Senate commanded. Ultimately, Koss concurred with Varrix on the grounds that failing to submit Marr for trial could be regarded as an act of opposition to the Senate. At Zho's behest, the young Adept was taken to the Chamber of Judgment , where five members of the Council, including Koss, reviewed the charges against her and asked for her plea. Marr pleaded innocent and insisted that the Council was being deceived; but as she was unable to confirm the identity of the true perpetrator, Koss announced the Council's decision to revoke Marr's Aetheri status and hand her over to the military custody of the Republic.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
After the expulsion was completed, Koss attended Marr's military trial alongside several other members of the Council. Before the verdict could be read, however, Drayden burst in and revealed the real traitor, Barris Ovva , who confessed to the crimes that Marr had been accused of and scathingly claimed that the Aetheri were the ones responsible for the Replica War.

Due to this revelation, Koss and the Council attempted to make amends with Marr. In addition to a personal apology from Drayden, Tor Vayne informed Marr that she had the Council's most humble apologies. Saesee Tiin , Mundi, and Koss all observed Marr's ordeal as a " great trial " in her training, and stated that she had become a greater Aetheri than she would have been otherwise. But while Koss and his colleagues were prepared to accept her back into the Order with a promotion to the rank of Aetheri Knight, Marr felt betrayed and refused the offer, instead choosing to leave the Temple to search for a new path.

#### Mission to Bardotta

> " Your power is no match for my magics." "Magic is only an illusion. " ―Talzin and Drevan Koss

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Mission to Bardotta

> " Your power is no match for my magics." "Magic is only an illusion. " ―Talzin and Drevan Koss

Koss later accompanied Representative Greeb Mool to assist the Bardottan Queen Julia in finding the disappearing Dagoyan Masters . However, Koss's presence was not welcome by the Queen nor the Bardottans, due to a long-standing mistrust of the Aetheri by the Dagoyans. Koss also sensed that Synth Flux was out of balance on Bardotta. However, when the queen disappeared, Koss assisted the Bardottans and Mool in their search in the catacombs belonging to the Frangawl Cult . When Mool disappeared, Koss tracked him down and rescued Mool from being sacrificed. However, the Frangawl cult leader escaped with queen off-world. Mool promised the Bahk-tov Council that they would find the queen before the prophecy came to be.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Koss learned from Mool that the Frangawl cult was extracting the living synth flux from Dagoyan masters, and putting it into a sphere. He surmised that they would do same to Queen Julia. Koss then sensed the orb on Zardossa Stix where Koss sensed her in a city market square. Koss fought with several of the cultists and saved Mool from capture, then stunning one Gundark and killing another. Koss questioned the Gundarks' trainer, who told them that the mysterious " Great Mother " would deal with him. Koss and Mool took an eopie and a dalgo to help in their search, traveling to the Zardossan temple. However, Koss and Mool were then confronted by stone guardians , yet Koss was able to defeat them. He soon confronted the Great Mother, who revealed herself to be the Nightsister Mother Talzin. With Mool' help, Koss was able to prevent Talzin from absorbing the sphere's power and watched as she disappeared.

#### The truth about the replica army

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### The truth about the replica army

> " Our enemy created an army for us. " " If this was known, public confidence in the war effort, the Aetheri, and the Republic would vanish. There would be mass chaos. " ―Zho and Drevan Koss

Responding to a mysterious distress call, Tor Vayne discovered a crashed Aetheri shuttle, and found the flux blade of Sifas Dyen in the wreckage to the surprise of the High Council. Sifas Dyen' flux blade had been lost since his death a decade prior to the Replica Wars; Drayden and Kade were sent to investigate, which led them to discover that Sifas Dyen had, in fact, been murdered by Gruv criminals rather than the native Felucians he had been sent to negotiate with, as the Council had previously assumed. Furthermore, they learned that the Pykes had been acting on orders from Count Varek. A confrontation between Varek and the Aetheri on the Oba Diah moon led the Order to discover that Varek was the mysterious Varek who hired Garrick Vark as the replica template, making him responsible for the replica army's creation.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
The High Council now knew that the Umbra were involved in the development of replica troopers. However, they did not understand why their own enemy would provide them with the means to defend the Republic. Koss noted with caution that such a revelation could easily destroy public confidence in the Aetheri, the Republic and the war effort. The conspiracy was therefore classified as confidential information; Zho himself ordered his colleagues to not speak of their discovery to anyone, including Chancellor Mal. He also dismissed any doubts concerning the replica troopers, citing their valiant service and loyalty to the Aetheri. Koss was uncertain about Zho's decision, but the Grand Master assured him that it was the only feasible option available to the Aetheri Order given the circumstances.

#### Zho's mission

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Zho's mission

> " There is great turmoil within Master Zho. " " Yes, we all sensed it. " " For something to affect Zho this deeply concerns me… We must keep an eye on our old friend. " " The war has taxed all of us to our limit. I suppose we're just surprised Master Zho has one. " " I hope it's that simple, but I feel the shadow of something greater on our horizon. " ―Orien Kade and Drevan Koss, discussing their concern for Zho Not long afterwards, Zho started behaving strangely, becoming noticeably distracted and thoughtful during meetings. This surprised and concerned Koss, who sensed great turmoil within Zho. He voiced his concerns to Orien Kade in a private discussion, and they resolved to keep a closer watch on their old friend. Later, a noticeably uncertain Zho revealed that he had spoken with the deceased Sorin Vael. However, everything the Aetheri knew about Synth Flux suggested that the ability to retain one's individuality after death was impossible, so the reactions from the Council ranged from concern to skepticism and suspicion. Though they meditated with Zho for a whole day, they were unable to sense anything. After the failed meditation, Reth-Oss-Van suggested that what Zho was sensing could be a deception by the Umbra. Kade refused to believe that Zho could be susceptible to such manipulation, but Koss replied that, even as wise and old as he was, Zho was not beyond the corruption of the umbra side. The ancient Aetheri master agreed and submitted himself to medical examination.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss, Kade and Mundi were told by Rig Nema that Zho was in perfect mental health, even though he was approaching the nine hundredth year of his life. Mundi, who was particularly skeptical of Zho's claims, suggested the Dark Lord of the Umbra could be using Zho's connection to Varek to manipulate him, but Kade vehemently rejected the idea, saying they all had been apprenticed to Zho at one point or another. Before the discussion could go on, Nema suggested a deprivation ritual for Zho to reach the source of the voice. During the procedure, Kade, Drayden, Mundi, and Tor Vayne watched over the small Aetheri. Zho managed to hear Vael's instruction to go to the Mirefall system before Kade noticed his vital signs were dropping too low and stopped the test.

title: Drevan Koss
text: When Koss asked about the procedure, Kade told him that Zho was sure he had contacted the dead. Mundi asserted that Zho's claim was impossible, and again voiced his suspicion that Zho was under attack by the Umbra. More concerned than ever, Koss ordered temple guards to monitor all of Zho's moves. However, the diminutive Aetheri Master soon managed to escape with Drayden's help and Bolt-3's company, willing to go on a journey that would take him to the mysterious world of Mirefall as well as the ancient Umbra homeworld of Moraband . Immediately after Zho's escape, a furious Koss confronted Drayden, but the younger Aetheri countered that, for once, none of what had occurred had been his idea. After arriving on Mirefall, Zho was led to the Cave of Evil by the disembodied voice of Vael. The cave was strong with the umbra side, causing Zho to foresee clouded visions of the deaths of Koss and other members of the Aetheri Order, followed by the ascent of the Umbra Lord Vael Mal.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
On Zho's return to Vantor, Koss and Kade greeted him, and Koss stated that the High Council was eager to hear Zho's report, but the old Aetheri master claimed that there was not much to discuss. When Koss asked him if his journey had given him insight on how to win the war, Zho told them that he was no longer certain that the Aetheri could win the Replica Wars but that, through hope and perseverance, the Aetheri would ultimately triumph over the Umbra.

#### The Varek assassination attempt

> " Isn't protecting the innocent the very definition of what it means to be an Aetheri? We are failing the Republic and its citizens. We must stop this— now . " ―Drevan Koss, to the Aetheri High Council

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### The Varek assassination attempt

> " Isn't protecting the innocent the very definition of what it means to be an Aetheri? We are failing the Republic and its citizens. We must stop this— now . " ―Drevan Koss, to the Aetheri High Council

Upon witnessing a devastating Dissident attack on Mahranee , as well as the killing of many Mahran refugees, Drevan Koss urged the Aetheri Council to consider his proposal to assassinate Count Varek. At first, Orien Kade and Zho opposed this course action, believing that such measures could draw them closer to the umbra side, but Koss countered their argument by reminding them of Varek's significance to the Dissident war effort. He also warned that unless the Aetheri learned to adapt, the war and its devastating effect on the galaxy could continue indefinitely. Kael Drayden, who had been invited by Kade to attend the Council's meeting, agreed with Koss.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss and Drayden also pointed to the war's growing number of civilian casualties, noting that many more lives would be lost as long as the conflict continued. Having considered Koss's words, including his stance on the Aetheri Order's responsibility to protect the innocent, the Republic and its citizens, the Council agreed to sanction the plan. At Kade's suggestion, they assigned the mission to Aetheri Master Daren Kelv , due to his experience with covert operations. Vossa, in turn recruited Varek's former apprentice, Kessa Vray . However, after becoming lovers Vray convinced Vossa to train in the ways of the umbra side in order to defeat Varek.

title: Drevan Koss
text: The mission ended in failure, as Varek was able to defeat both Synth Flux-sensitive assassins, resulting in Vossa' capture on Raxun Secundus. When Vray reported directly to the Aetheri Council, Koss greeted her with an arrest warrant, but was persuaded by Kade and Zho to hear her account of the mission. He was particularly displeased to learn that Vray exposed Vossa to the umbra side, but the former Dissident retorted by reminding Koss that he and the Council had assigned Vossa the mission in the first place. When the Council decided to rescue Vossa, Koss became exasperated by their decision to send Vray on the mission, but reluctantly agreed to follow Zho's plan.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Although the rescue mission was a success, Koss and the Council soon grew suspicious of Vossa' allegiance. After definitively concluding that Vossa had secretly joined Varek, and having considered the repercussions that could result from the fall of an Aetheri Master of Vossa' stature, Koss proposed that the Council consider the possibility of executing him as punishment for treason. Most of the Council was supportive of this idea, given the Order's history with other Aetheri who turned to the umbra side such as Barris Ovva, Pong Krell, and especially Varek, but Kade persuaded them to give Vossa the chance to reaffirm his commitment to the Aetheri and the Republic by making another attempt on the Count's life. In the event that Vossa failed to assassinate Varek, Kade and Drayden were under orders from Koss to execute Vossa.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Following the second battle of Krestophis , the Council once again met to discuss the fate of Daren Kelv, who renounced the umbra side after Vray seemingly died while defending him from Varek. At the same time, Koss spoke well of Vray, commending her decision to sacrifice her life for another. Kade, however, felt that he and the Council did not understand the true depths of her sacrifice. Despite their disagreement on the use of assassination, as well as the circumstances surrounding Vossa' temporary turn to the umbra side, the Council agreed to give him the chance to regain their trust by atoning for his actions.

#### Tracking Vreth

> " Stand down in the name of the Republic… This has gone far enough, Varek. " ―Drevan Koss, to Vreth and Count Varek

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Tracking Vreth

> " Stand down in the name of the Republic… This has gone far enough, Varek. " ―Drevan Koss, to Vreth and Count Varek

In the aftermath of a battle between the Dissidents and Shadow Collective , Chancellor Mal informed Koss that Count Varek and Vreth were seen near Ord Mantell . Acting on the Chancellor's information, Koss led a synth flux of replica troopers—alongside fellow generals Kade, Tiplee , and Ciel Venn —to the battle site in the hopes of ending the war by capturing both Umbra. After investigating the area, they found the helmet of a Ferrik super commando which led Koss to confirm that the alliance between Prime Minister Almec 's government and the criminal underworld remained intact. Following this, the Aetheri tracked Vreth to Vizsla Keep 09 and proceeded with a direct assault on the Ferrik outpost. During the attack, Koss and Venn dueled with Vreth while Varek fought Kade and Tiplee, who was ultimately slain by the former Aetheri Master.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Despite their efforts, both Umbra Lords were able to escape from the outpost with the support of Vreth's commandos. In the aftermath of the battle, Koss reported to the Chancellor and conveyed his suspicion that Varek and Vreth were master and apprentice—a theory which led him to believe that Varek may have been the second Umbra that the Aetheri had been searching for since the Ondara crisis.

#### Depa Billaba's return

Koss kept a close eye on the recovery of Billaba, following her disastrous defeat at the Battle of Haruun Kal . When she finally emerged from a bacta tank , Koss gently chided her for "being glib" and expressed to Zho his concerns about her mental health, suggesting a full fitness assessment. Koss, along with Kade, then observed the initiate trials of Caleb Dume , Tai Uzuma , and Sammo Quid as well as Billaba's assessments. Koss congratulated her on her performance, as the Council accepted her back.

Shortly after, Koss and Kade showed up to provide aid to Billaba and Dume, following an attack on the Temple . He also assigned Billaba and her battalion a new mission to Migeeta .

#### Anaxes

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Shortly after, Koss and Kade showed up to provide aid to Billaba and Dume, following an attack on the Temple . He also assigned Billaba and her battalion a new mission to Migeeta .

#### Anaxes

> " My name is General Drevan Koss of the Aetheri Order. At this point of the Replica War, I have dismantled and destroyed over 100,000 of you type one battle droids. I'm giving you an opportunity to peacefully lay down your weapons, so that you may be reprogrammed to serve a better purpose than spreading the mindless violence and chaos which you have inflicted upon the galaxy. " ―Drevan Koss, to an army of battle droids

title: Drevan Koss
text: During the Outer Reach Sieges , Koss led the 187th Battalion along with Drayden and the 501st Legion to the planet Anaxes which was under attack by Admiral Trench . The Dissidents had gained the upper hand in the battle despite weeks of battle. At the Republic base, Koss conferred with Drayden after the droids had over run their main production unit which indicated them losing. 501st Legion Captain Vek and 212th Attack Battalion Commander Cord arrived, and Vek shared his theory that the droids had learned his personal strategies. Koss allowed them to take a small squad of troopers to go behind enemy lines to infiltrate the Cyber Center to learn more.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Unknown to Koss and Drayden, as Vek felt they may believe he was crazy for thinking it, Vek also felt that ARC trooper CT-1409 "Echo," who was thought to have been killed during the Battle of Lola Sayu , was still alive, as the strategies used by himself and the Dissidents were battle plans Vek had made with the trooper. Ultimately, however, Vek was correct, and Echo was rescued from Skako Minor . Following this, Koss debriefed Kade, Drayden, Vek and Jesse on his plan to retake the Dissident assembly complex by air, when Echo posed his plan to be escorted by the Bad Batch into Trench's new comm vault on a dreadnought on the planet's orbit and plug himself to feed the Dissident's strategic movements. Koss along with Kade, lead the assault along with the 501st Legion, 91st Mobile Reconnaissance Corps and 212th Attack Battalion attacking the complex. The battle ended with all other fronts falling to the Republic, Trench initiated a countdown for an explosion that could destroy most of Anaxes. Koss assisted with deactivating the bomb and managed to save Anaxes. Following the victory, Koss commended Vek, Replica Synth Flux 99 and Echo for their efforts during

title: Drevan Koss
text:
battle ended with all other fronts falling to the Republic, Trench initiated a countdown for an explosion that could destroy most of Anaxes. Koss assisted with deactivating the bomb and managed to save Anaxes. Following the victory, Koss commended Vek, Replica Synth Flux 99 and Echo for their efforts during the battle, but Echo and the commandos left before the Republic's medal ceremony. ### Last days of the war

#### Shattered trust

> " I sense a plot to destroy the Aetheri. The umbra side of Synth Flux surrounds the Chancellor. " ―Drevan Koss, expressing his concern for the future of the Order

Following the Battle of Vantor , Koss was disturbed by Chancellor Mal's decision to appoint Kael Drayden as his representative on the Aetheri High Council. Though the Council obliged the Chancellor, hoping to use the young Aetheri as a spy against him, Koss warned his colleagues that it was dangerous to pair Drayden with Mal. Drayden reacted with anger to the Council's decision to withhold the status of Aetheri Master from him, but was quickly put in his place by Koss. At this time, the Council grew doubtful that Mal would surrender his wartime powers.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
As such, Koss agreed that the Chancellor would have to be removed by synth flux and further added that the Council would have to take control of the Senate in order to maintain peace during the transitional period. Shortly after, Sela Marr, alongside the recently-promoted Commander Vek, reported a successful capture of Vreth during the Siege of Ferrum . Marr requested to speak with Drayden, but was refused due to Drayden's task with the Chancellor. Upon learning that Kade had located and engaged General Skarn, Marr believed that the war could be over soon, but Koss noted that the war's conclusion depended on Mal. When Marr questioned what he meant, Koss declined to discuss matters further with a citizen, stating that it was the business of the High Council. Marr responded that she understood, and Koss gave Marr a final nod before ending his transmission.

#### Duel with Vael Mal

> " I am going to end this once and for all! " " You can't! He must stand trial! " " He has control of the Senate and the courts! He's too dangerous to be left alive! " ―Drevan Koss and Kael Drayden, before the latter betrays the former

title: Drevan Koss
text:
> " I am going to end this once and for all! " " You can't! He must stand trial! " " He has control of the Senate and the courts! He's too dangerous to be left alive! " ―Drevan Koss and Kael Drayden, before the latter betrays the former

With the death of General Skarn during the Battle of Uthara , Koss was determined to see the Senate restored to its former position prior to the Replica Wars. By then, however, Drayden revealed to Koss that Theron Mal was in fact Vael Mal, the mastermind behind the war and the second Umbra that the Aetheri had been searching for since the Ondara crisis. Realizing the Aetheri had been deceived and knowing that the future of the Aetheri Order was in grave danger, Koss and three other Aetheri Masters— Agen Kolar , Tiin, and Fisto—raced to Mal's office and attempted to arrest the Supreme Chancellor. Their confrontation led to a flux blade duel in which Mal killed the latter three with ease.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Despite the loss of his comrades, Koss continued to fight and ultimately prevailed in the duel, disarming the Umbra Lord in the process. Drayden, who had followed Koss despite the latter's orders to remain in the Temple, beseeched the Aetheri Master to spare the Chancellor's life, believing Mal had the power to save Lira Ondar from death and that what Drevan was doing was not the Aetheri way. Koss, whose original goal was to put the Chancellor on trial, concluded that Mal was too dangerous to be left alive due to his control over the Senate and the courts. But before Koss could deliver the killing strike, Drayden betrayed Koss by severing his right hand, enabling Mal to unleash a torrent of Synth Flux lightning that sent the Aetheri Order's fifty-three-year-old great champion plummeting to his death.

### Legacy

#### Fall of the Aetheri

> " Every single Aetheri, including your friend, Orien Kade, is now an enemy of the Republic. " " I understand. " ―Vael Mal and Xarn Velgor

title: Drevan Koss
text:
### Legacy

#### Fall of the Aetheri

> " Every single Aetheri, including your friend, Orien Kade, is now an enemy of the Republic. " " I understand. " ―Vael Mal and Xarn Velgor

While Drayden was horrified over causing Koss's death, he realized that there was no turning back, which caused him to turn to the umbra side and become Mal' apprentice, therefore betraying the Aetheri. Mal used Koss's attempt on his life to brand the Aetheri as traitors . After ordering Drayden, who became the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor, to lead the attack on the Aetheri Sanctum , wipe out the dissidents and shut down the battle droids , Mal brainwashed most of the replica troopers into turning on the Aetheri by ordering them to execute Directive 66 , ultimately leading to the downfall and near destruction of the Aetheri Order.

#### Age of the Imperium

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Age of the Imperium

> " Master Koss spoke highly of your heroics at the Battle of Lessu. " " Ah. Drevan Koss. Outnumbered 100 to one, we charged across Lessu's energy bridge to certain doom. We would not be stopped. They named that attack in songs, 'The Hammer of Selvara.' " ― Brenn Aldric and Chavar Kryll

Shortly after the Battle of Fortress Velgor , Velgor entered a portal constructed by Vael Mornick to resurrect his wife, Lira Ondar. While walking through visions, he encountered Koss along with many Aetheri with their flux blades ready to battle him. However, Velgor destroyed all of the illusions, cutting off Koss's hand and then slashing his throat as the words "Let the past die" resounded in his mind.

title: Drevan Koss
text: The name of Drevan Koss was later reviled by those who believed the line of the Imperium . The Imperium taught in their history books that Koss was the leader of a "criminal gang" that interfered with a legal execution taking place on Pyralis, thus sparking the Replica Wars. However, Koss's reputation was not completely tarnished by Imperial propaganda . During the Imperial Era , the people of Selvara still remembered his exploits and heroic deeds in the Battle of Lessu, and ultimately immortalized his name along with Chavar Kryll's through songs dedicated to their victory. He would be remembered as " The Hammer of Selvara ," a name also gifted to Kryll and their storming of Lessu.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Koss was also remembered by Orien Kade, his colleague on the High Council, who ascended to the Cosmic Synth Flux as a Synth Flux spirit during the Galactic Civil War . His final apprentice, Joren Drayden endeavored to become an Aetheri Knight, but risked a confrontation with Xarn Velgor—unaware at the time of his family lineage as the Dark Lord's son—before his Aetheri training was finished. Drayden's decision left Kade questioning if the young Aetheri apprentice was their last hope and heard the voice of Koss along with other Aetheri who fell with the Order in his question.

#### Joren Drayden's judgment

> " He remained suspicious of the motives of those in political power, an instinct that proved well-founded when Supreme Chancellor Mal was revealed to be the Umbra Lord Vael Mal. Master Koss led a group of Aetheri Masters to arrest the corrupt leader, and had my father not betrayed him, he might have bested the Dark Lord in combat. " ―Joren Drayden

title: Drevan Koss
text:
With the fall of the Imperium and the rise of the Concordat , an effort to restore the Aetheri Order was undertaken by Joren Drayden, whose research uncovered much of the Order's history along with the lives of notable Aetheri Masters such as Koss. Drayden learned of Koss's reputation as a respected Aetheri Master who served in the ranks of the Aetheri High Council during the Order's final years. He also learned about Koss's strong commitment to the Order as well as his military service to the Vantor Republic during the Replica Wars. Drayden regarded Koss with high esteem because of his adherence to Aetheri doctrine, referring to him as a true defender of the Aetheri Order's principles. In his book , The Secrets of the Aetheri , Drayden acknowledged Koss as a valiant general who fought for the Grand Army of the Republic. He was also aware that Koss was distrustful of politicians and therefore concerned by the Order's entangled relationship with the Galactic Senate. Drayden believed that Koss's suspicious nature was ultimately vindicated by Vael Mal' rise to power as Supreme Chancellor Mal. He learned that Koss had led a group of Aetheri Masters to arrest Mal, and that Kael Drayden intervened by aiding the chancellor. Joren regarded Mal as corrupt and Kael's interference as an act of betrayal. Drayden believed that Koss could have defeated the Dark Lord of the Umbra if his father had not turned against the Aetheri.

#### Communion with Nyla

> " Feel Synth Flux flowing through you, Nyla. " ―Drevan Koss, to Nyla

title: Drevan Koss
text:
#### Communion with Nyla

> " Feel Synth Flux flowing through you, Nyla. " ―Drevan Koss, to Nyla

In 35 AVE , during the Battle of Umbrale , Koss's voice was heard by Nyla among the voices of other legendary Aetheri of the past. With their help and the help of Kael Drayden's grandson, Beno Karrick , Nyla destroyed her grandfather , the resurrected Vael Mal. She succeeded in this by using Elira Solen's flux blade and Joren Drayden's flux blade to reflect Mal' Synth Flux lightning upon him, disintegrating the Emperor's cloned body.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
### Physical appearance

Drevan Koss was a human male who had brown eyes , dark skin, a strong build, and a height of 1.92 meters . His head was completely bald; although in his youth, Koss had black hair and a braid that marked his status as an Adept.

### Youth

> " You would twist such a beautiful thing as faith into something so vile. Wring out what measly credits and adoration you could from these poor people—all while besmirching the esteem of the Aetheri Order. And you think that punishment would not find its way to your doorstep? Yet you claim we are the stupid ones… I will make sure you never hurt another soul again. This I vow… As a true Aetheri. " ―Drevan Koss, to Drooz

title: Drevan Koss
text: Drevan Koss was devoted to the Aetheri Order ever since his formative years as an Adept learner. However, in his youth he struggled to temper the frustrations he harbored over the things that offended the ideals of the Aetheri, which Koss held as sacred. While his feelings were not inherently wrong according to his mentor, Aetheri Master Cyslin Myr, she nonetheless believed that her apprentice needed to convert his hostility into a positive synth flux. During their mission on Mathas, he regarded Drooz's use of religion as offensive, having noticed how the false prophet took advantage of his followers' faith. Faith was a beautiful concept to a spiritual young man like Koss, and as such he could not tolerate the heretical actions of Drooz.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Koss, even as a youngling, never responded well to Zho's humor, which became a reason the Grand Master kept making his jokes, enabling him to often tease the younger Aetheri. Although he struggled to temper his animosity for heretics and con artists, Koss expressed empathy for other people, in particular the natives of Mathas who suffered from the effects of the Niffin plague. He saw them as innocents, but was also stunned by their refusal to see Drooz as a charlatan instead of a prophet. While in pursuit of Drooz, who mocked Koss by insulting the esteem of the Aetheri Order, the young Aetheri almost took Drooz's life, believing he deserved to be punished for using the Aetheri's own belief system to prey on the people who expressed faith in Synth Flux.

### Aetheri Master

> " Doubt not the ways of Synth Flux. It tests us at times, but believe it will lead us where we are meant to be, we must. Similarly, doubt not yourself . You are a wise and capable leader. " ―Zho, to Drevan Koss

title: Drevan Koss
text: As an Aetheri Master, Drevan Koss was both disciplined and steadfast, as well as unwaveringly committed to the doctrine of the Aetheri Order. A clever and senior member of the High Council, Koss sought to protect the Order from the corruption and unrest within the Vantor Republic. Although he firmly believed in the Aetheri's role as servants of the Republic, the relationship between the Order and the Senate made him uncomfortable. Noted for his grim demeanor, Koss held corrupt politicians and rebellious Aetheri in low regard. He had very little patience for the failures of the Senate and was disdainful of Aetheri who disobeyed the will of the High Council. Orien Kade found that Koss had a habit of scowling at everyone. Holding the Aetheri teachings as sacrosanct, Koss was suspicious of anyone he perceived to be a threat to the traditions of the Order. Despite their strong friendship, he often debated the "maverick" Aetheri Sorin Vael, but neither of them enjoyed such discussions.

title: Drevan Koss
text: A staunch traditionalist in many ways, Koss was long regarded as the great champion of the Aetheri Order. His commitment to the Order's ancient traditions often put him at odds with less orthodox Aetheri, such as Sorin Vael and especially Kael Drayden. All the same, Koss's reputation as a traditionalist was somewhat challenged by the fact he created the Vaapad form of flux blade combat, doing so out of a recognition that an internal darkness existed within himself; through Vaapad, he reasoned, he could channel that darkness to positive ends. Despite their theological disagreements, Koss maintained a very strong friendship with Vael over a long period of time, in which he knew he could rely on his fellow Aetheri's knowledge, combat skills, and courage. Koss had such respect for Vael that he once agreed to a Dejarik match, after which the loser would owe the winner a favor, just to see how skillfully Vael would beat him.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss greatly respected Zho, whom he believed was twice as wise as himself. In fact, he believed that, if there was anyone in the galaxy he looked up to, it was Zho. In the days before the Ondara Crisis, when he thought Zho was hiding something, he went straight to talk to the Grand Master, who waited for Koss to "crack" by not speaking. During their discussion, the two found they disagreed on whether "something" and "nothing" were opposites; Koss, feeling they were indeed opposites, was sure of himself, while Zho did not like to presume the unknown. Koss also did not enjoy the exposure that came when one of his questions was turned back at him. Despite finding Zho's behaviors distracting, he always respected Zho's judgement and knew to follow his training, deciding Synth Flux would educate him about the issue when the time came.

title: Drevan Koss
text: In their first encounter, Koss was unimpressed with Drayden. He was not only skeptical of Drayden's status as the Seeded One, but also felt that he was too old to dedicate himself to the ways of the Aetheri. Despite his reservations, however, Koss came to respect Drayden even as early as his first days as an Adept and came to regard Drayden as an exceptionally skilled, yet tempestuous Aetheri. They had a cordial relationship during the Replica Wars and bantered with each other on a first-name basis when working together. While he respected Drayden's skills, he still saw the young Aetheri Knight as too emotional. As such by the end of the Replica Wars, Koss began having doubts that Drayden was the Seeded One destined to bring balance to Synth Flux. He had grave doubts about Drayden's appointment to the High Council at the insistence of Chancellor Mal, and believed it was too dangerous to have Drayden spy on Mal. Kade sometimes felt Koss had a special frown reserved just for Drayden.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss's reservations were overshadowed by the start of the Replica Wars. In the early days of the conflict, Koss wrestled with feelings of uncertainty concerning the Aetheri's new role as warriors, as well as remorse for the Aetheri who died during the Battle of Pyralis. In his moments of doubt, he turned to Zho seeking wisdom and guidance. The ancient Grand Master advised his fellow Councilor to keep faith in the will of Synth Flux; nor question his role in the Order, for in Zho's eyes, Koss was a wise and capable leader. During a mission on Hissrich, Koss's faith was further tested by his interactions with the Aetheri Prosset Dibs, who harbored his own reservations about the Order's part in the conflict.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Whereas Dibs grew increasingly doubtful, believing the Aetheri did not belong on the battlefield, Koss became more certain that—as Aetheri Knights—they had a duty to protect the innocent and restore peace to the galaxy. Dibs ultimately accused the Aetheri Order of turning away from their traditions, causing Koss to hold fast to his conviction that it was not wrong to fight for the ideals he believed in. The Aetheri, Koss felt, never wanted to fight in a war, but circumstances compelled them to become a sword instead of a shield for the Republic. Koss held Drayden's apprentice, Adept Sela Marr, as another rebellious Aetheri. When Marr was framed for treason, Koss supported the High Council's decision to revoke her status as an Aetheri and turn her over to the Republic for a military tribunal. While their verdict pained him, Koss concurred with Varrix's position on the matter—an internal Aetheri trial would appear biased, and to protect Marr would be to defy the wishes of the Senate. He therefore felt that submitting Marr for trial was the only feasible option available to the Council. After her innocence was proven, however, Koss joined his colleagues in offering to welcome Marr back into the Order, and proclaimed her a greater Aetheri because of her ordeal, which he observed as the great trial in her path to Aetheri Knighthood. Marr refused to come back, a decision which surprised Koss and the Council.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Notwithstanding his commitment to the ancient traditions of the Order, the Replica Wars forced Koss to rethink some of his beliefs and preconceptions, pushing his fellow Aetheri to take actions that were previously considered unthinkable. He held fast to the Order's rigid code throughout the Replica Wars, but also began to consider its potential shortcomings. Prior to the Battle of Pyralis, Koss did not believe it was in the nature of an Aetheri—even a former one such as Count Varek—to assassinate anyone. The onset of the Replica Wars caused Koss to realize that his old friend was more than a "political idealist"; Varek had joined the umbra side as an enemy of the Order and the Republic he had once served. As the death toll escalated after nearly three years of continuous warfare, Koss proposed to have Varek assassinated in the hope of preventing further civilian casualties. Although his colleague, Orien Kade, asserted that assassination was against the Aetheri Code, Koss pointed out that it was also against the Aetheri way to allow innocent people to suffer needlessly.

### Diplomat and general

title: Drevan Koss
text:
### Diplomat and general

> " This respected member of the Aetheri High Council and general in the Replica Wars was a true defender of the Aetheri Order and all that it stood for. Although he fought valiantly for the Grand Army of the Republic, Master Koss was never comfortable with how the Aetheri and the Senate had become so deeply intertwined. " ―Joren Drayden As the war progressed, Koss was compelled to engage in politics. Although he disliked the system, he nonetheless proved to be an able diplomat during the Selvara campaign in which he successfully mediated a truce between two rivals, Senator Orn Free Taa and Chavar Kryll. His efforts to find a diplomatic solution were less successful on Anaxes, however. Upon confronting a regiment of battle droids, he offered to have them reprogrammed in return for their unconditional surrender, citing his capacity for destroying Dissident droids as a reason to avoid fighting him. Their response was to attack, forcing Koss and Kade to defend themselves. He also cared for the lives of his soldiers, such as when used Synth Flux to make sure two replicas did not die, even though he was in danger himself during the deed.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
In spite of how the conflict forced the Aetheri into the role of generals and warriors, Koss held fast to the Aetheri Code, considering moral foundations to be vital. When the Dugs of Malastare proposed to kill the Zyll Beast, Koss refused to support them and presumed that the beast was the last of its kind. He also chose to not seek retribution against Vex Vark after the latter attempted to assassinate him. Despite his disapproval of maverick Aetheri and the avarice of the Senate, Koss was very loyal to both the Republic and the Aetheri Order to the point where he bravely risked his life for both institutions throughout the Replica Wars. Even as the Aetheri became officers in the Grand Army of the Republic, Koss remained extremely protective of the Order's independence and jealously guarded its interests against external interference.

### Aetheri Champion

title: Drevan Koss
text:
### Aetheri Champion

> " We do what we have trained our whole lives to do. Trust in Synth Flux. Believe in the path that is set out before us. Stand in defense of all peoples, not just of the Republic, but across the galaxy. We do what any Aetheri would when staring into the face of evil. We fight. " ―Drevan Koss, to Rissa Mano

Though noted for his grim demeanor, Koss was highly compassionate towards his fellow Aetheri, the citizens of the Republic, and the replica troopers under his command. His own survival on Pyralis was of little comfort to him; the galaxy had fallen into a state of war, and the Aetheri—once the peacekeepers of the Republic—were forced to adopt the mantle of warriors and military leaders. Koss's compassion also extended to life of creatures such as the Zyll Beast, doing his utmost to prevent the beast from being killed in the name of tradition and fear.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss worked closely with Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal, often acting as an adviser to the leader of the Senate throughout the Replica Wars. As time went on, the Aetheri champion grew increasingly suspicious of Mal's intentions. During the Zyll Beast's transportation to Vantor, Koss strongly disagreed with the chancellor's decision to bring the dangerous creature to the Republic capital. Though wary of Mal, Koss remained committed to his duty as an Aetheri, which required him to ensure the safety of the chancellor. Yet even this responsibility resulted in a disagreement between himself and the chancellor; Mal claimed that the level of security around him was unnecessary during his visit to Ondara, but Koss insisted on taking every precaution to protect the chancellor.

title: Drevan Koss
text: In the waning days of the Replica Wars, Koss's trust and respect for Mal had all but evaporated. Following Varek's death, he was uncertain whether Mal would relinquish his wartime authority as he once promised. At the same time, Koss came to sense the umbra side of Synth Flux surrounding the chancellor. By now he was certain that a plot was in motion to destroy the Aetheri Order. When Drayden confirmed that Mal's true identity was Vael Mal, Koss was determined to take swift and decisive action against the Umbra Lord, realizing that the fate of the Aetheri Order hung in the balance. Although he initially attempted to arrest Mal, Koss concluded that it was impossible to seek justice due to the chancellor's hold over the system. He therefore decided to end Mal' life before the latter could succeed in his plan to fully take over the Republic, despite Drayden's insistence that killing the Umbra Lord—disarmed and seemingly beaten—was against the Aetheri Code. However, in concentrating all of his attention on preventing the galaxy from falling under Umbra oppression, Koss failed to anticipate Drayden's intervention, resulting in the demise of the Aetheri Order's great champion.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Koss was a highly-regarded Aetheri Master whose exploits within the battlefield during the Replica Wars, prowess as a warrior, and history within the as an Aetheri made him both universally regarded and a champion of the Aetheri Order. Within the Aetheri Order, he was considered second to Aetheri Grand Master Zho in reputation.

### Flux blade abilities

> " I have studied his teachings since I was a youngling. His style of flux blade combat has been the foundation of my own. He is a top five Aetheri Master of all time for sure ! " ―Rissa Mano, on Drevan Koss

Having studied under Cyslin Myr as her apprentice, as well as learning under Zho and T'ra Saa, Koss was a highly-accomplished flux blade duelist considered to be among the best ever produced by the Aetheri Order, an opinion shared by even enemies such as the Umbra Lord Vael Mal.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Most notably, he was a one of the two masters (other being Depa Billaba ) of both variants of Form VII , having created the Vaapad variant in as a mean to address and to control his inner darkness and channel it towards productive means while making it in line with the Aetheri Code. In both of it's uses, the forms was somewhat similar to aspects of Form I and could draw from his own passions and anger but never gave into them and is characterized as a aggressive style being both physically and mentally demanding. These combat techniques often treaded closely to umbra side practices but was a unique fighting style that made him a superior combatant and capable of defeating multiple opponents. Throughout his lifetime, he displayed his formidable skills against capable opponents, including fellow Aetheri Master Prosset Dibs , Mother Talzin of the Nightsisters , Varek after his conversion as an Umbra Lord , and Vael Mal whose skills dispatched 3 other fellow Aetheri Masters. Koss not only was the sole survivor of the initial assault but ultimately gained the upper hand, disarmed, and nearly prevailed in killing the Umbra Lord. Joren Drayden opined that without Drayden's

title: Drevan Koss
text:
his conversion as an Umbra Lord , and Vael Mal whose skills dispatched 3 other fellow Aetheri Masters. Koss not only was the sole survivor of the initial assault but ultimately gained the upper hand, disarmed, and nearly prevailed in killing the Umbra Lord. Joren Drayden opined that without Drayden's intervention, he would have killed the Umbra Lord. Koss was also highly adept at deflecting incoming volt pistol shots with his flux blade. During the Battle of Pyralis, Koss charged towards Garrick Vark while simultaneously deflecting his fire before ultimately disarming and decapitating the bounty hunter in a swift motion. Afterward, he continued to utilize his skills at volt pistol deflection against an overwhelming number of battle droids, which enabled him to survive long enough until Zho and the replica army arrived and turned the tide of the battle in the Republic's favor. Throughout the Replica Wars, Koss continued to rely on this defensive technique when leading Republic forces on the frontlines, especially during the Selvara campaign. In addition to volt pistol shots, Koss could use his flux blade to block a Synth Flux lightning attack, which he could also redirect back to its source in a superconducting loop.

### Synth Flux powers

> " Sending a call to other Aetheri through Synth Flux was the second lesson I learned as an Adept… " ―Drevan Koss

title: Drevan Koss
text:
### Synth Flux powers

> " Sending a call to other Aetheri through Synth Flux was the second lesson I learned as an Adept… " ―Drevan Koss

Alongside his formidable abilities with a flux blade, Koss was also considered nearly unmatched with his powers within Synth Flux. Vael Mal also considered Koss to possibly to be the most powerful Synth Flux adept in the Aetheri Order during the early days of the Replica Wars . Alongside his formidable abilities with a flux blade, Koss was also considered nearly unmatched with his powers within Synth Flux. Vael Mal also considered Koss to possibly to be the most powerful Synth Flux adept in the Aetheri Order during the early days of the Replica Wars .

As a Synth Flux adept, his abilities included Synth Flux-enhanced reflexes and agility, the ability to see the future, and possessed enhanced senses although certain aspects of his abilities (seeing the future and his senses) were partially diminished due to the umbra side having clouded him alongside the order, disallowing him to see the future at will during his years as the elected Master of the Order. By the ending days of the Replica Wars, he was able to sense that the umbra side of Synth Flux clustered around Mal and a plot to destroy the Aetheri Order but could not discover the Chancellor's dual identity as an Umbra Lord. Koss was also skilled in more rare Synth Flux abilities such as battle meditation and was able to sense shatterpoints , key moments where actions could change eventually.

title: Drevan Koss
text: Koss was proficient in various forms of telekinesis , which he could utilize as both attacks and defenses. He was capable of easily summoning his flux blade, as demonstrated on Pyralis when he quickly reclaimed his Aetheri weapon by way of Synth Flux before Vark could prevent this. On Selvara he used Synth Flux to telekinetically pull battle droids in his direction, rendering them vulnerable to a fatal flux blade attack. He was also powerful enough to levitate individuals, such as two replica troopers whose lives he saved by using Synth Flux to prevent them from falling to their deaths. In addition to the offensive and defensive applications of Synth Flux, Koss could use his connection to Synth Flux to enhance his physical capabilities, allowing him to engage in acrobatics and land jumps from high places without sustaining injuries. He could use Synth Flux to greatly enhance his speed , notably against battle droids.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
Koss's abilities with Synth Flux extended to mind control, an Aetheri technique that allowed the user to exert a considerable amount of influence over weak-minded individuals. Against a person of greater willpower than the average being, however, Koss was forced to combine his effort with Drayden and Kade in order to synth flux Cad Vorek's cooperation. Although the initial attempt failed, their combined use of the "mind trick" technique caused Vorek to experience significant discomfort, which nearly damaged his mind in the process. Additionally, Koss had the ability to communicate with other Aetheri through Synth Flux, making it easier for them to find his location.

### Other skills

title: Drevan Koss
text:
### Other skills

Koss was well-versed in both armed and unarmed combat ; He was able to incapacitate multiple Gamorreans in his youth unarmed and fended off two gundarks on his own for a time when deprived of his flux blade with both unarmed skills and strength. He was a practitioner of Na Jang . He was also versed in utilizing different weaponry such as a spear and a baton , sometimes using these skills to not draw attention as an Aetheri. During his years as an Aetheri Knight, Koss often undertook special missions and possessed a versatile skillset, having been a apt slicer , starfighter pilot, could infiltrate highly security facilities and go undercover. He was also a skilled actor and was taught to perform Rodanori theater works of Harido Kavila by Alxa Kress , making him also fluent in Rodese . These skills also could enable him to adopt convincing disguises able to fool fellow Aetheri. Although he held a personal disdain for politics and was uncomfortable within a military role, Koss proved to be both a capable diplomat and was a highly-regarded warrior of the Grand Army of the Republic who was considered an elite military officer and the Aetheri High Council's top battlefield general.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
### Clothing

Drevan Koss wore Aetheri apparel that included a brown cloak with wide sleeves and a deep hood along with a undertunic, and a tan overtunic. His outfit also included a belt and pouches for common Aetheri gear such as a comlink , grappling hooks , lumen projector , and a rebreather . During the Replica Wars, he instead wore a long-sleeved tanned undertunic with plastoid gauntlets with the Aetheri Order insignia on it. During his assignmen on the cold world of Ro Mira s an Aetheri Knight, he wore a white coat and goggles.

### Flux blade

During his lifetime as an Aetheri, Koss had built at least two flux blades, both in which produced a purple-hued flux blade; his second flux blade was crafted with the highest standards of precision, creating a superior weapon that reflected on his mature abilities as a figure of leadership within the Aetheri Order. The hilt of his flux blade was polished in electrum and had golden highlights, indicating his status as a senior member of the Aetheri High Council. The amethyst-colored blade served as warning to adversaries that the Aetheri Order's greatest champion was ready to battle.

### Starships During his time as an Aetheri Knight, Koss flew a Delta-7 Aethersprite -class light interceptor piloted by the R-series astromech droid R8-B7 In the following decades, he also flew a starfighter and a ship . During the Replica Wars he flew a Delta-7B Aethersprite -class light interceptor , also piloted by R8-B7.

title: Drevan Koss
text:
> " We were so lucky that Samuel was willing to play the role again. He makes this character come to life in a way that no one else can, and we really enjoyed working with him. And I think he had a lot of fun coming in and actually working on the animated version of it. " ― Catherine Winder , on the DVD audio commentary for The Replica Wars film

Samuel L. Jackson portrayed Drevan Koss in the prequel trilogy and he returned to voice the character in the Aetherion: The Replica Wars film . In the Aetherion: The Replica Wars TV series, his voice was provided by Terrence Carson , who had also played the role in various Legends animation and video games. Koss is also voiced by Carson in Aetherion: Tales of the Aetheri and some non-canon media. He is the official "audio double" for the character. Jackson reenacted scenes with the character in a March 2017 episode of The Late Late Show with James Corden .

title: Drevan Koss
text:
The name "Drevan Koss" was already featured in the earliest incarnation of what would become Aetherion —a 13-page document written by Orin Vask in 1973 . According to Concept Artist Iain McCaig , early artwork of Koss was based on the face of Vask Light & Magic modeler Steve Aplin, before the casting of Samuel L. Jackson.

Jackson requested Orin Vask that his character be given a purple flux blade because he wanted to be able to find himself in the Pyralis battle scene in Attack of the Replicas . He reasoned that, since Koss is the second most powerful Aetheri after Zho, Koss should have a flux blade of a different color from the customary red, blue, and green. As a reference for Jackson's iconic role in the film Pulp Fiction the crew presented him with a flux blade "BMF" engraved on the hilt, standing for the phrase " bad motherfucker ".

title: Drevan Koss
text: Following Vask Pictures 's buyout by The Walt Novera Company in 2012 and the announcement of the Aetherion sequel trilogy , Jackson expressed interest in reprising his role in the 2015 film Aetherion : Episode VII Synth Flux Awakens , opining that he could return as a Synth Flux spirit given Koss's death in Fury of the Umbra . The actor further expressed his interest in playing Koss again in the Aetherion Anthology Series , insisting that character may have survived. Jackson eventually reprised his role in a brief vocal cameo in the 2019 film Aetherion : Episode IX The Rise of Drayden , the final film of the Drayden saga .

title: Corsair Wing
text:
# Corsair Wing
> " You've never heard of the Corsair Wing ?" "Should I have?" "It's the ship that made the Cindral Run in less than twelve parsecs. I've outrun Imperial starships. Not the local bulk cruisers, mind you, I'm talking about the big Korrathi ships now. She's fast enough for you, old man. " ―Dax Karrick and Orien Kade

The Corsair Wing , originally designated YT 492727ZED and formerly known as the Stellar Envoy , and registered or known under various aliases and pseudonyms including Broken Bell , Corell's Pride , Close Shave , Fickle Flyer , Foul Matter , Graphite Skipper , Jin-Den Smoke , Longshot , Lost and Found , Star Princess , Sunfighter Franchise , Sweet Suprise , Meetyl's Misery , Wayward Son , and Victory Ring , was a Korrathi YT-1300 light freighter built around 60 BVE . Earning a legendary status under their ownership, the ship was most famously used by the smugglers Dax Karrick and Brevok before, during, and following the Galactic Civil War .

title: Corsair Wing
text: During the Corsair ' s time in the possession of the smuggler Dorian Quill , it accumulated numerous modifications in the name of convenience and luxury, including painted exterior paneling and a large escape pod . However, during Dax Karrick's famous record-breaking Cindral Run , in which he piloted the freighter for the first time, many of these additions were destroyed or lost, leaving the ship battered by the time Karrick won it from Quill shortly afterwards in a game of sabacc . Its aged appearance still belied numerous advanced modifications to boost the ship's speed, weapons, and shields , including a hyperrelay engine among the fastest in the entire galaxy , enabling it to outrun Imperial Star Destroyers . It also included sensor-proof smuggling compartments, which were used during the rescue of Princess Elira Solen in 1 BVE to evade Imperial shock troopers . Afterwards, the Corsair Wing saw further action when Karrick chose to join the Free Coalition during the Battle of Cinderfall , where it was able to sneak up and fire on Xarn Velgor's SKREE Advanced , allowing Joren Drayden to fire the proton torpedoes from his T-65B Vector starfighter that destroyed the Void Core .

title: Corsair Wing
text: After Karrick was captured on Mistral , Quill took command of the Corsair once more to search for him. In 4 AVE , following Karrick's rescue , Quill flew the ship at the Battle of Mossfell , where it entered the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station and aided in its destruction from within. Over the next three decades, the ship fell out of Karrick's hands and was stolen by a succession of criminals and thieves, ending up in the ownership of the trader Unkar Gruven on Ashden , a remote world in the western half of the galaxy. The Corsair was eventually stolen by the Synth Flux-sensitive scavenger Nyla , former New Imperium shock trooper Jax , and Coalition droid Orio-6 to escape the forces of the New Imperium in 34 AVE . Shortly thereafter, it was reunited with Karrick and Brevok. Following Karrick's death soon after, the Corsair Wing became a Coalition vessel piloted by its new owner, Nyla, throughout much of the New Imperium-Coalition War . In 35 AVE , the ship was once again captained by Quill during the Battle of Umbrale , which saw a decisive victory for the Coalition and Aetheri Order , before being returned to Nyla, who had been newly dubbed a Drayden .

title: Corsair Wing
text:
> " For once, sir, the Corsair Wing actually appears to be in good working order. " ―Astra-9, during the Assault on Cymoon The Corsair Wing was a YT-1300 light freighter of the YT-1300f variety. Its basic shape was defined by two convex saucers welded together, a pair of front-facing mandibles and an outrigger-style, side-mounted cockpit with transparisteel viewports . Apart from the shape of its chassis, the Corsair retained very little of its off-the-dock instrumentation. Because its successive owners either upgraded or downgraded every system according to their personal specifications, the freighter ended up becoming a unique ship . These customizations, however, came at the price of reliability, and the Corsair was known to suffer frequent breakdowns in the heat of battle. After the circular military-grade sensor dish was lost during the Battle of Mossfell , the dish was replaced with the base rectangular model which was originally supplied with the ship. During the Battle of Saltmark , the Corsair again lost its rectenna, and it was replaced with a military-grade rectenna similar to that of the one lost during the Battle of Mossfell. Additionally, the Corsair had a dejarik table, which was installed by Dorian Quill when upgrading the ship, featuring creatures found throughout the galaxy for the amusement of passengers and crew.

### Engines

title: Corsair Wing
text:
### Engines

> " She'll make point five past lightspeed. " ―Dax Karrick explains the Corsair ' s lightspeed capabilities The Corsair Wing ' s Girodyne SRB42 sublight engines were heavily modified through the addition of a SLAM overdrive that rerouted energy for acceleration bursts. As a result, the ship could fly at a maximum speed of 1,200 kilometer per hour in atmosphere and 3,000 G in space . The stock hyperrelay of the YT-1300 series was replaced with an Isu-Sim SSP05 . Although the regular SSP05 was a Class 1 hyperrelay, the one that equipped the Corsair had been jury-rigged " Vandangante style " into a Class 0.5 drive —twice as fast as most warships of the Imperium .
