text: Fascinated by the power he tapped into in the Umbra cave on Emberfall, and associating the world with his rebirth and personal connection to the umbra side, Velgor requested that the world be given to him by his master in 14 BVE, believing that the planet held the key to seeing the deceased Lira Ondar once again. Gifted with the late Ondar's royal starship , the mask of the ancient Umbra heretic artisan Vael Mornick , and a team of top Imperial architects , Velgor departed Vantor for his new home. The Umbra Lord entered the planet's violent atmosphere unshielded, causing severe damage to his vessel and casting a streak of fire across the smokey sky. His entry was witnessed by the Emberfallian Father Kkkt , who warned his clanmate Zzzs that the fireball was an omen of events to come.

title: Emberfall
text:
Landing near the Umbra cave, Velgor meditated in its dark walls, leaving the Emperor's architects, Colonel Alva Brenne and Lieutenant Roggo , to draw up plans for a personal base Velgor could inhabit. Brenne scouted the planet's terrain, believing that, although Velgor was seemingly impossible to satisfy, she could manage to design a home suitable for the Dark Lord. Unbeknownst to the architects, the mask that Mal had gifted Velgor was possessed by Vael Mornick's spirit; it took control of Roggo, using his body to kill Brenne and create its own designs for the base. Velgor confronted the spirit, killing its host body and demanding that it gives him answers. The spirit introduced itself as Mornick and offered to help Velgor construct a fortress that would harness the energies of the umbra side locus below the cave to open a door into Synth Flux itself; through and beyond the limitations of time and space. Upon being attacked by Father Kkkt's scout party, Velgor abducted the Emberfallian Sssp to serve as Mornick's new body and let Rrrn flee. The two Umbra Lords subsequently took command of a vast Imperial construction synth flux on the Gahenn Plains and began their work on what would become Fortress Velgor .

Velgor would exercise control over the entire Emberfall system. Around this time, the Warden Order' headquarters were moved from Vantor to the moon Nur in the Emberfall system, keeping close to Velgor and his planet. A base but also a clandestine place of incarceration and torture for Aetheri, the Fortress Warden Order tower was built to complement the castle on Emberfall using black stone from the world in 14 BVE.

#### Portal to the past

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Portal to the past

> " I have been in contact with the other clanholds. We are not the only one affected—the entire planet screams at what the dark one is building on the Gahenn Plains. " ―Father Kkkt

The construction of Velgor's fortress was not a simple task. Over the course of eight attempts with at least five separate designs, Mornick struggled to find the perfect structure that could correctly channel the umbra side. The energy Velgor exerted while attempting to open a rift in the locus caused electromagnetic storms to rage across the planet, throwing the world's creatures into a frenzy and casting the Emberfallian people into disarray—the natives found that their "lifefires" barely burned. As an Imperial -class Iron Cruiser loomed overhead, the new Imperial garrison managed to defend the site against small uprisings by the Emberfallians and lava fleas. Father Kkkt, realizing the danger Velgor posed to his world, rallied the clanholds across Emberfall prepared to mount an attack on the Imperial intruders.

title: Emberfall
text: Upon the completion of Mornick's ninth design in 12 BVE , Velgor was finally able to reach through Synth Flux and open a pathway into time , but he was interrupted in his moment of triumph by Kkkt and his forces. With the Dark Lord distracted, Mornick entered the portal and claimed his original body, betraying Velgor. Kkkt's army had initial success in pushing back Captain Junus ' garrison, attacking the Imperials, whom they outnumbered by ten to one, with surprise tactics. Velgor, however, soon arrived on the front lines and rallied his magma troopers to double their efforts. Recognizing Velgor as the Imperial leader, Kkkt led the Emberfallians in a powerful usage of Synth Flux , drowning the enemy forces in a vast flood of lava. With his army wiped out, Velgor retreated into the fortress, summoning his own massive synth flux of energy to destroy the Emberfallian attackers.

title: Emberfall
text:
Returning to the inner sanctum, Velgor confronted Mornick, who mocked the cyborg Umbra for his failures in service to the umbra side. Using Mornick's hubris against him, Velgor crushed and killed the resurrected artist. With no one to stop him, he entered the portal, encountering visions of his past and future, including his beloved wife, Lira Ondar. Upon witnessing what her husband had become, however, the vision of Ondar ran from Velgor, choosing to plunge into an abyss. A beam of light containing a figure that he did not know was his son then overwhelmed Velgor. Frustrated with the dark visions, Velgor retreated and crushed the altar in the Umbra cave, destroying the portal and accepting that the truth he encountered was exactly what he needed. The Dark Lord later returned Mornick's mask to Mal; both master and apprentice frequented Emberfall, using it to focus their meditation on the power of the umbra side of Synth Flux.

#### Emberfallian revolts

> " This is an Imperial facility. " " And this is our world. A world with secrets that I have vowed to protect at all costs. " ―Rersey and Sssl

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Emberfallian revolts

> " This is an Imperial facility. " " And this is our world. A world with secrets that I have vowed to protect at all costs. " ―Rersey and Sssl

Black Sun departed Emberfall to a lower profile world after the Imperium had established a garrison there. The Artificer Union similarly abandoned their operations, and their remaining resources were taken over by the Mining Guild, but they struggled to profit on Emberfall due to the strict travel restrictions imposed by the Imperium. The Imperium replenished their garrison and maintained secret facilities on Emberfall where survivors of the Aetheri Purge were interrogated and executed , although the lava planet remained publicly notable only for its mining operations. Rumor had it that Xarn Velgor carried out these interrogations, torturing the Aetheri for any useful information before their execution. As the world remained under heavy Imperial guard, mining operations there eventually ceased.

title: Emberfall
text: In 11 BVE , the term " Emberfallian Special " was used by smuggler Dorian Quill and his first mate , L3-37 , to refer to a starfighter maneuver that involved great speed and surprise, and which ensured at least one side of a starship confrontation "end[ed] badly." L3-37 explained that the tactic was named such in reference to the eponymous lava world's fiery nature. Following Kkkt's failed attack and the completion of Fortress Velgor —according to a story told years later by the Emberfallian Lellis—Xarn Velgor sought candidates for a servant who would attend to his needs, searching for months until a human named Vainé came into his service around 12 BVE. During Velgor's search, an Imperial officer was sent from Imperial Command to Emberfall by Moff Seward , and was tasked with handling an outbreak of insanity amongst Imperial lava troopers assigned to Fortress Velgor. On Emberfall, the inspector found that the troopers had inhaled toxic fumes from the planet's depths that gave one illusions of fears and doubts, and he entered Velgor's castle to speak with Xarn Velgor himself with the intention of resolving the matter. However, Velgor, bathing in his bacta tank , instead forced the officer to inhale the fumes and confront his fears by holding him in place via Synth Flux, refusing to let the human go. Face with the illusions caused by the Emberfallian fumes, the inspector denied their existence and began to laugh, laughing for days until he took advice from the voices by his head and became Velgor's servant, named Vainé.

title: Emberfall
text: Eventually, years before the Battle of Mossfell of 4 AVE , the lava fumes leaking into Velgor's castle were blocked off. During the early days of Velgor's reign over the planet, Vainé witnessed the efforts of a second synth flux of Emberfallians to push the Umbra away from their homeworld. The group, led by Criakan , desired vengeance for their slaughtered kin and stormed the fortress in a surprise attack. Surrounding Vainé, Criakan and his forces intended to show no mercy to the Imperials, but were shown the same respect by Lord Velgor, who cut them all down before they could burn down the castle.

title: Emberfall
text:
Sometime later, during a visit from the Emperor's adviser Rersey , a third attack on Fortress Velgor was undertaken by Clan Rrrt 's Mother Sssl , an Emberfallian priestess who could synth flux her will upon others by subjecting them to a mind-altering plague . Sssl's forces soon overwhelmed the Imperials, infecting Velgor's soldiers and turning them against the Umbra. Although Sssl had only intended to scare off the invaders, her plans changed when the Dark Lord himself was seemingly infected. In reality, Velgor's mechanical body was immune to the plague, allowing him to feign subservience and draw the priestess out. Using a mind trick , Velgor forced Sssl to order her own forces to drag her into the lava—a scene that made Rersey lose his sanity. Vainé praised his master and noted that the Emberfallians would fear Velgor's name in the future.

### Galactic war on Emberfall (9 BVE–1 AVE)

#### Insurgents in peril

> " Yes the naval action at Emberfall was a short-term win. But the Imperium now knows the measure of the Alliance's naval strength. " ―Vela Sess, The Insurgent Files

title: Emberfall
text:
### Galactic war on Emberfall (9 BVE–1 AVE)

#### Insurgents in peril

> " Yes the naval action at Emberfall was a short-term win. But the Imperium now knows the measure of the Alliance's naval strength. " ―Vela Sess, The Insurgent Files

In 9 BVE , Xarn Velgor conferred from Fortress Velgor with the Third Warden via hologram regarding their hunt for Orien following a failed attempt to capture him. Kade later infiltrated Fortress Warden Order on the nearby moon Nur using intelligence from the Hidden Path insurgents, who further found that Velgor was not in the Emberfall system at the time, instead being aboard his vessel elsewhere. The hunt was ultimately a failure, and from his castle, Velgor was instructed by Vael Mal via hologram to abandon his obsession with Kade.

title: Emberfall
text: In 4 BVE , the Aetheri Brenn Aldric of the insurgent cell named the Shades was detained aboard the Imperial Iron Cruiser Sovereign , the flagship of Wilhard Varrix , Grand Moff and Governor of the Outer Reach. The vessel entered Emberfall's orbit after the Imperium's capture of the Aetheri on the Outer Reach planet Lorath , where the Shades were based. Escorted by a fleet of three other Star Destroyers and support vessels, the Sovereign bore witness to the Grand Warden 's interrogation of Aldric for information about the insurgency and the informant named " Fulcrum " —who was secretly the former Aetheri Sela Marr. Lena Kryll led her Shades crew on a rescue mission over Emberfall. Using a stolen Imperial Gozanti-class cruiser and SKREE fighter to infiltrate the Sovereign , the Shades freed their captive Aetheri from the Grand Warden. The latter's flux blade was bisected during flux blade combat against Aldric and his Adept, Cass Virel , and fell into the Sovereign ' s reactor , dooming the Iron Cruiser. The Warden himself chose to fall to his death rather than suffer for his failures.

title: Emberfall
text: With the aid of Ember Cell , a coalition group affiliated with "Fulcrum" in a growing network of insurgents formed by Senators Bael Solen and Vela Sess , the Shades successfully fled the Emberfall system and joined the larger Ember Cell. Grand Moff Varrix also evacuated from his flagship, which crashed into Emberfall's lava fields in a defeat that embarrassed Varrix and displeased Theron Mal. The skirmish over Emberfall marked one of the earliest insurgent victories in the Galactic Civil War against the Imperium and heightened rebellious activity in the Outer Reach, with unrest occuring on Lorath that Imperium Vigil Bureau Agent Alexsandr Kallux attributed to some Lorathites perceiving the Imperium as vulnerable following rumors of the Imperium's show of weakness at Emberfall. Vela Sess wrote in documents assembled in The Insurgent Files that the action at Emberfall was but a short-term success, considering that the insurgents had revealed the naval capacity of their sector fleet to the Imperium. Indeed, the Emperor sent Xarn Velgor to personally handle the insurgent group.

title: Emberfall
text: Having become a part of Bael Solen's insurgent network, Brenn Aldric and Cass Virel began working with their fellow insurgent Synth Flux-sensitive, Sela Marr. In 3 BVE, Marr reached out to Aldric with report of her investigation on the Umbra Lord who attacked them over the planet Lorath shortly prior—unbeknownst to them, he was Xarn Velgor and formerly the Aetheri Kael Drayden, who instructed Marr. She had been monitoring transmissions from Emberfall, and while information on the Umbra Lord remained elusive, she had gathered more intelligence on the Imperium's Wardens. The former Aetheri decoded two sets of coordinates from the Emberfall transmissions, and after she learned of an incident above the planet Chandel , she and the Shades investigated the world Takobo , where they uncovered the Wardens' plot to kidnap Synth Flux-sensitive infants. Marr recalled that it was similar to the kidnapping attempt that she and her master had foiled on Emberfall during the Replica Wars.

title: Emberfall
text:
In 1 BVE , based on intelligence about the Imperium's operations on Emberfall, a small insurgent synth flux was sent by Captain Kassian Andris to infiltrate an Imperial base located near Velgor's castle and steal a vital artifact. Upon infiltrating the base, the insurgents discovered the artifact was a proto-blade , a precursor to the flux blade, and escaped with information about the ancient weapon despite Velgor's intervention.

#### Legacy of Corvax

> " Whoa. Whoa, that looks like—that looks like Emberfall. Emberfall's a mining planet. Why are the Imperials taking us there? " ―ZO-E3, to her captain #### Legacy of Corvax

> " Whoa. Whoa, that looks like—that looks like Emberfall. Emberfall's a mining planet. Why are the Imperials taking us there? " ―ZO-E3, to her captain

In the same year, while Emberfall maintained its reputation as a mining world, a smuggler and ZO-E3 aboard the Windfall were forcefully taken to Emberfall, having been taken out of hyperspace in the Emberfall system by an Interdictor -class Iron Cruiser commanded by Admiral Gable Karius . Karius served Velgor as his second-in-command on Emberfall, and the smuggler and ZO-E3 were held in Velgor's castle. The Umbra Lord then interrogated the smuggler, realizing that they had a strong connection to Synth Flux and was a descendant of Lady Corvax. However, they then escaped below the castle to the underground Corvax Fortress, meeting the Emberfallian Priestess and activating Lady Corvax's droid army to attack the Imperials.

title: Emberfall
text:
Xarn Velgor briefly taught the Corvax descendant to harness the power of Synth Flux in order to retrieve the Bright Star artifact, wishing to revive Lira Ondar with it. The Umbra Lord was prevented from doing so by the descendant, who staged an escape from the fortress and destroyed the Bright Star and the Aeon Engine, allowing Emberfall to begin restoring its forested ecosystems. Near Fortress Velgor, the fertile soil grounds of a bog named Corvax Fen began developing.

#### Crushing aspirations

> " You seem unsettled. " " No…just pressed for time. " ―Lord Velgor and Director Vossik #### Crushing aspirations

> " You seem unsettled. " " No…just pressed for time. " ―Lord Velgor and Director Vossik

Later still in the year, the Imperium completed construction on the Void Core , an orbital battle station capable of destroying a planet. After a insurgent attack on a laboratory on the world Eadu threatened to expose the Void Core's capabilities to the galaxy at large, Velgor summoned the director of the project, Orren Vossik , to his fortress on Emberfall. Vossik, arriving while Velgor was sustained within a bacta tank, was escorted into Fortress Velgor's rotunda by Vainé to await the Dark Lord. Confronting the uneasy director, Velgor admonished Vossik for his mistakes, using Synth Flux to choke the aspirational officer when he further requested an audience with the Emperor. With his message relayed, Velgor watched Vossik's ship depart for the planet Halcyon . Despite Velgor's threats, Vossik failed in his endeavors and the Void Core was soon destroyed by the Free Coalition. Around the same time, the insurgents also destroyed the Imperium's Mirkanite Mining Facility on Emberfall.

title: Emberfall
text:
Later in the war, a crew of insurgents led by Commander Lina Graf was attacked by Imperial forces, and their ship, the Auric , was heavily damaged. They were forced to crash-land on Emberfall, a planet that Graf hoped would lead to her crew's salvation. Surrounded by lava, the insurgents abandoned their ship and began toward the only structure in sight; Velgor's fortress.

They did not make it far before being attacked by Emberfall's exploding beetles. After defeating the beetles and arguing over the best course of action, Graf and her crew were cornered by a squad of Imperial Lava Troopers. Escaping the troopers, the group entered the fortress but soon became separated in its dark halls. Alerted to their presence by his aide Vainé, Velgor confronted the insurgents, capturing Lieutenant Thom Hudd and destroying the bodyguard droid XM-G3 , although Graf and her remaining crew managed to escape Emberfall. The insurgents' successful escape from Velgor's castle was remembered by the native Emberfallians by the aftermath of the Imperium's collapse.

title: Emberfall
text: For the next several weeks , Vainé kept Hudd locked within the fortress and tortured him, all the while tormenting him with horrific tales from across the galaxy, including the story of Velgor's brutal murder of Sssl years prior. The abuse and starvation that Hudd suffered while chained to the Umbra servant's torture web was so severe that he lost enough body mass to slip from his shackles and escape his cell. Hudd managed to send a distress signal to the Alliance but was ultimately recaptured and sentenced to death. His execution was stalled by Graf, however, who had returned to Emberfall disguised as a Warden . Although Vainé saw through her ruse, Graf and Hudd were able to escape and flee the planet with the rest of their crew. Velgor, angered at his servant's ineptitude, rigged Vainé up to the torture web.

title: Emberfall
text:
The loss of the Void Core served to galvanize coalition across the galaxy, causing trouble for the weakened Imperium. In response to the outbreak of insurgency, Velgor was met at Fortress Velgor by Admiral Kendal Ozzel and General Maximilian Veers . Overlooking Emberfall's lava fields, the trio discussed the proper route to deal with the rising Alliance, although Velgor viewed Ozzel's suggestions as nothing more than excuses for incompetency. An interesting point from General Veers, however, persuaded Velgor to view the insurgents in a new light, prompting him to develop a different plan to cripple the Alliance.

### Crucible of fate and hate (3–4 AVE)

#### Into the fire

> " The last time you were broken …I found you…and I rebuilt you. This time… you must rebuild yourself. " ―Mal, to his battered apprentice

title: Emberfall
text:
### Crucible of fate and hate (3–4 AVE)

#### Into the fire

> " The last time you were broken …I found you…and I rebuilt you. This time… you must rebuild yourself. " ―Mal, to his battered apprentice

In 3 AVE , Velgor attempted to turn his son, Joren Drayden, to the umbra side during a duel over the planet Mistral . After Drayden fled , Velgor temporarily abandoned his duties to the Emperor, embarking on a personal quest that led to the discovery of a insurgent cell led by Sable , the former decoy of Lira Ondar. Velgor allowed the insurgents to live, a decision which convinced Mal that his apprentice was in need of a reminder of his place. The Emperor mutilated Velgor on Vantor, ripping his cybernetic limbs from his body and strangling him as he had done to men like Vossik in the past.

title: Emberfall
text: Not finished with his lesson, Mal took his student back to Emberfall. He had Velgor's personal guard of death troopers drag him to the spot where Kade had defeated him decades ago, leaving the apprentice to fend for himself. Warned by his master that there would be consequences should he use Synth Flux to save himself, a one-armed Velgor crawled along the lava banks and retrieved his fallen flux blade before slowly making his way to the ruins of the Artificer Union installation. Mal watched from Velgor's Vectis -class shuttle as the broken man pulled himself across the sand. Although Mazan Veldon , the Emperor's Grand Vizier , warned that the Dark Lord planned to kill his master, Mal was unconcerned and sent his Umbra assassin , Orrin of Bestoon , to turn Velgor's anger into pain.

title: Emberfall
text: Having reached the Artificer Union installation ruins, the very building where he had slaughtered the Dissident Council decades prior, Velgor repurposed surrounding Dissident droid parts as his own limbs and confronted Orrin, overpowering the assassin and demanding him to reveal Vael Mal' plans. As Velgor did so, the oracle Eye of Webbish Bog called out to the Umbra Lord, who, despite being deprived of his chest box and flux blade by Orrin, fought his way through hordes of lava nymphs, lava fleas, and even a roggwart to reach the Eye's lava cavern. As Velgor did so, he was tested by the Eye and reminded of his inner conflicts between his chosen Umbra and Aetheri destinies as well as between his personal desire of power and his need for his son. During Velgor's journey to the Eye's lair, Senior Administrative Aide Sly Moore and a group of death troopers spoke to Orrin, reminding the assassin to abide by the Emperor's directives.

title: Emberfall
text: At the end of Velgor's trek to the Eye, the latter gave the cyborg a wayfinder and allowed him to leave the cavern to rejoin Orrin. Once outside, Velgor made his way to the green Aetheri starfighter that he took to Emberfall at the end of the Replica Wars, repairing the ship until Orrin reappeared with the Droid Crush Pirates of Bestoon . Having been promised Velgor's cybernetic parts by Orrin, the army of droid pursued the Emperor's enforcer until they found that his parts were no more special than their own. In the midst of a quarrel with Orrin about their deal, the droids were interrupted by Velgor, who took down the machines for use in retrofitting his green starfighter and an escape pod , which he locked Orrin in after forcing the assassin to activate his wayfinder. In his determination to find the Emperor's secrets, Velgor bound the pod to his starfighter and set off to the wayfinder's coordinates, reaching the vicinity of the Unknown Regions world Umbrale via hyperspace.

title: Emberfall
text:
With Orrin in tow, Velgor confronted Mal on Umbrale, an ancient Umbra world which housed hundreds of Mal' secret experiments and weapons. The Emperor reminded his wayward apprentice that he left him weak and broken on Emberfall's burning shores, and asked Velgor what he learned from the experience. However, Velgor remained rebellious, stating his intention to make his "master" fear him. Despite Velgor's efforts, he was overwhelmed by Mal' power. Terribly pained, Velgor, despite having experienced a vision of his son telling him it was his destiny to destroy Mal, accepted his master's dominance over him before leaving Umbrale with him and Orrin.

#### Carmine Dawn intrusion

> " Ha! You lose, chump!" "Uh, boss, you sure that's such a good idea? " ―Karrick, shouting at Velgor, and a Knight of Karrick

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Carmine Dawn intrusion

> " Ha! You lose, chump!" "Uh, boss, you sure that's such a good idea? " ―Karrick, shouting at Velgor, and a Knight of Karrick

Later, between 3 AVE and 4 AVE, Lady Vessa 's criminal syndicate, Carmine Dawn , hired the Knights of Karrick , a group of umbra side warriors, to raid Fortress Velgor and acquire the Screaming Key artifact —Vael Mal had placed the key there, but did not know that it unlocked Mornick's fabled Fermata Vault , which held power that threatened even the Umbra. In her quest to destroy the Umbra, Vessa had obtained the full layout, access codes, and security details of the fortress and convinced the Knights' leader , Karrick , to go ahead with the raid despite initial reluctance from other Knights. The Knight Massif had complained that "the job was too hot" not just because Emberfall's surface was a hellscape, and fellow Knights Bazzra and Marinda also had their own concerns. Nevertheless, Vessa promised the Knights glory and the freedom to claim any objects to keep for themselves aside from the key.

title: Emberfall
text: The group landed their vessel , the Night Buzzard , on the Gahenn Plains and used speeder bikes to approach the fortress from the south. Karrick had concluded that the sensors of the Imperial garrison on the building's far side could not detect them given Emberfall's magnetic field, and as they used their speeder's signal jammers , they were able to approach undetected. The Knights approached an old entrance to the fortress that was covered by lava, but by using Synth Flux to clear a way through, they entered the Umbra cave below the installation. The helmet of Mornick still lay in the cave, which spooked Bazzra into shooting and destroying it. They then continued on their route towards the vault.

title: Emberfall
text: As they neared the vault, the Knights were spotted by Vainé, who warned them that it was too late for them to turn back and that Velgor would learn of their presence. The Knights turned their weapons on Vainé, but he was protected by a synth flux field. Meanwhile, a large group of lava troopers surrounded the Knights and a battle began. As the Knights fought their way to the vault, Karrick began to cut open the door to the vault with his flux blade . Inside the vault, Karrick used Synth Flux to listen for the Screaming Key, and located the small gray key. Realizing that the battle had also gone quiet, Karrick asked if they had defeated all the troopers, and while the Knights told him that they had all departed for unexplained reasons, Xarn Velgor emerged. Velgor quickly killed the Knight Fyodor with a Synth Flux choke before Karrick engaged him in flux blade combat. As Velgor and Karrick traded blows, Velgor learned that his opponents were the Knights of Karrick. The remaining Knights fled at Karrick's command, and Karrick soon jumped out of a window to join them, using controlled descent to survive the fall. Velgor

title: Emberfall
text: before Karrick engaged him in flux blade combat. As Velgor and Karrick traded blows, Velgor learned that his opponents were the Knights of Karrick. The remaining Knights fled at Karrick's command, and Karrick soon jumped out of a window to join them, using controlled descent to survive the fall. Velgor attempted to use Synth Flux to grab the key back out of Karrick's hand, but the other Knights fired their volt pistols at Velgor, forcing him to use his energy to deflect their shots. The Knights then fled on their speeders and left Emberfall with the key, which they delivered to Vessa's ally, The Archivist , at a location where The Archivist believed the Fermata Vault to be.

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Vrak and Schism

> " I have never been stronger . " ―Xarn Velgor, training to focus his abilities on Emberfall

The Eye of Webbish Bog called out to Velgor, who entered his lair and experienced visions that the being hoped would serve as a warning to the Umbra Lord of an impending culmination of interconnected galactic events. After receiving the visions, Velgor found that the Eye was being poisoned by a device left in his cave and subsequently ambushed by several Emberfallians. The natives were unhappy with the Umbra Lord's intrusion on their planet, but Velgor dispatched them at the cost of only a scar left on his helmet and eliminated the device that had been plaguing the Eye. The Umbra then returned to his castle, where he spoke with the Emperor via hologram about Lady Vessa's machinations against them.

title: Emberfall
text: After the Umbra overcame Vessa's attempt to defeat them, Joren Drayden communicated with a red kyber crystal on the planet Krestophis , in the process experiencing a vision in which he saw Fortress Velgor in the midst of a red lightning storm as well as his father, Xarn Velgor. Vessa's activation of the Fermata Vault during her war against the Umbra had destabilized Velgor's mastery of Synth Flux, and the Dark Lord, wielding the Zaly Shield alongside a staff , returned to the lava fields before his castle to train himself in focusing his powers. Meanwhile, the Vrak , a droid-possessing malady , intended to control Velgor as he was a cyborg who could use Synth Flux. It arrived on Emberfall as the corrupted insurgent protocol droid Astra-9 and as the MSE-6 droid Petyr on a Taylander shuttle . The initial attack on Fortress Velgor failed as the Vrak's attention was diverted by an attack elsewhere and the breakthrough of being able to control the consciousness of cyborg organics.

title: Emberfall
text: While training with his droid army, Velgor received a hologram transmission from Grand Vizier Veldon, who relayed the Emperor's order to reclaim his flagship, the Sovereign —it had been infiltrated by the Vrak. Velgor and his droids thus departed for the Sovereign aboard an Imperial transport . After successfully reclaiming the flagship, the Umbra Lord took his droids and his personal SKREE fighter and returned to Emberfall, where another droid repaired its fellow veterans while Velgor confronted the Eye of Webbish Bog, demanding power and control—while battling the Vrak, Veldon had ordered the Sovereign ' s destruction with Velgor onboard. The Eye reminded Velgor that power lied with his master, Vael Mal, citing the Tragedy of Vael Plagueis the Wise in which Mal murdered his own master. While Velgor prepared to depart for Vantor's Imperial Palace with his droids and a Vectis -class shuttle , one of his droids, ZEV-6-7 , succumbed to the Vrak and activated an octuptarra tri-droid in the secret Artificer Union droid factory.

title: Emberfall
text: The octuptarra attacked Velgor on the lava plains, and the Umbra Lord's crude Synth Flux power through his Zaly Shield and staff proved ineffective. In their attempt to trigger Velgor's hatred so that he could further draw on the dark power that hate channeled, the Dark Lord's droids Gee-Ninety and Arekso joined in the attack, but to no avail. Arekso urged the Umbra to think about what he hated most, and the cyborg realized that he hated himself; using his self-loathing, Velgor channeled his hate into fine Synth Flux power to destroy the Vrak's octuptarra, damaging Gee-Ninety, Arekso, and ZEV-6-7 in the process. Velgor also found that he hated his master, Vael Mal, even more than himself, and set off for Vantor with a compliment of Vrak spider-droids aboard his SKREE Advanced x1 , setting the stage for a confrontation with his master and the Vrak of Vantor .

title: Emberfall
text: Velgor's attack failed, as the Emperor turned Velgor's own troops, including his hand-picked squad of death troopers, against him. Velgor eliminated the squad and had their bodies sent to a medical lab on Emberfall. There the Umbra Lord mused that although the death troopers organic minds made them superior to droids, it also supplied them with a will that could be turned against him. Following the end of the droid crisis, Velgor sought to appropriate the Vrak's ability to control automatons and cyborgs for his own ends. The Dark Lord captured the members of M.A.R. Corps —a Free Coalition squad of cybernetically-enhanced commandos—and brought them to Emberfall for experimentation. Under the supervision of ZEV-6-7, the insurgents were equipped with droid brains that allowed Velgor to interface with and command them. The process was extremely invasive, however, causing severe mental anguish in the commandos that was shared by Velgor. During these experiments, Administrator Sly Moore met with Velgor in his fortress with the intent of persuading him to join her Schism Imperial , a splinter group of disaffected Imperial officers and bureaucrats who planned to overthrow the Emperor.

title: Emberfall
text:
Velgor and the Schism's crusade against the Emperor finally came to a head in a skirmish on Caranthanax B , where Velgor fully submitted to the will of the Emperor. The aftermath of the battle saw the Schism revealed as a ruse concocted by Mal, as well the recovery of energy capsules from the site by the former slaves Kitster Banai and Wald . Orrin of Bestoon later recovered the capsules on Dunemere and presented them to Velgor in his castle throne room on Emberfall.

### Ashes of Imperium (4–35 AVE)

#### Lingering darkness

> " It is not over. Not yet. Not while you can bring him back…your master will return to the fires of Emberfall and, this time, will be made whole… Velgor triumphant. Velgor supreme. Velgor… reborn ! " ―A voice speaks to Vainé

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Lingering darkness

> " It is not over. Not yet. Not while you can bring him back…your master will return to the fires of Emberfall and, this time, will be made whole… Velgor triumphant. Velgor supreme. Velgor… reborn ! " ―A voice speaks to Vainé

Toward the end of the Galactic Civil War, Velgor was saved by the selfless compassion of his son, Joren Drayden, and in turn sacrificed himself to destroy the Emperor aboard the second Void Core during the Battle of Mossfell in 4 AVE. Having re-embraced his identity as Kael Drayden as he succumbed to the injuries inflicted upon him by his late Umbra Master, Velgor died leaving his fortress without a host. After the battle, pilot Torb Rask scouted suspected Imperial planets and reported his findings to the leadership of the Concordat —the Insurgency's successor state—on the world Raydonia ; due to Emberfall's proximity to Raydonia, Admiral Gial Vorian sent a scout to there, along with the planets Dunemere, Dermos , Pyralis , and Akiva .

title: Emberfall
text: Following news of Xarn Velgor's death over Mossfell that the Free Coalition had broadcasted, Emberfallians gathered around the fortress' vicinity in celebration. Lightning storm clouds and lava on Emberfall stirred around Velgor's castle, howls sounded in the night, and cries echoed across the lava plains. The Emberfallian boy Giggek recognized that his kind were not truly free as long as they lived under the shadow of Velgor's castle, and so resolved to rid the land of Velgor's curse by bringing the castle to ruin. Along with Tuttel , Giggek acquired detonators from a store of equipment from the obsidian mines belonging to Tuttel's uncle, Lellis. However, the latter forbid the young boys from entering Velgor's castle for the reason that it was lethal and evil, telling the story of how Vainé came into servitude under Velgor and further speculating that the young Emberfallians were only pursuing glory.

title: Emberfall
text:
Nevertheless, Giggek led Tuttel into Velgor's castle by way of lava flea, venturing in to find a pit trapping Vainé, the servant of Velgor and the self-styled "one true Adeptis of the Beyond " who was detained by Velgor there some time ago. Rescuing The Adeptis in hopes of not bringing death upon anyone in the process of destroying Velgor's castle, Giggek was at once betrayed by Vainé, who dropped the boy down the pit in hopes of bringing death to those who sought to tarnish his master's legacy. However, after instructing his Emberfallian companion to flee, which Tuttel did with their lava flea, Giggek ignited his explosives through a remote detonator , and although the blast did not bring down Velgor's castle, Vainé was buried in black sand. However, the Umbra servant survived. A voice familiar to Vainé told him not to fear, and assured its servant that he could return Velgor to the fires of Emberfall and be made whole.

#### Wrath of Velgor's ghost

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Wrath of Velgor's ghost

> " And I'm sorry. You of all people must be— " " Scared out of my wits? Wishing I'd never even heard the word Emberfall? It's the dreams, Lina. They're getting to us all. " " You're right, Hudd. That's all they are… dreams. And dreams aren't real… Dreams can't hurt you. " ―Lina Graf and Thom Hudd, on Emberfall once more At some point, Vainé witnessed holonews reports on the Battle of Mossfell and the death of Velgor, but he refused to believe that his master had met his end. The Adeptis continued to maintain the Dark Lord's castle, anticipating his return at any time. Following the Imperium's defeat at the Battle of Ashden in 5 AVE , Vainé told the voice he believed to be his master that everyone in the galaxy believed that he was dead, which the supposed ghost of Velgor replied to by saying that the Umbra can never truly be killed since it was the will of the umbra side. Vainé then orchestrated a ritual in which Velgor's ghost reached out across the galaxy to imprint nightmares upon others' minds. One such nightmare reached Milo Graf , brother of Lina Graf, in which Milo had a nightmare about undead droids and himself being taken to Emberfall by CR-8R , controlled by Vainé.

title: Emberfall
text: After he discussed Velgor's castle with his sister and CR-8R, Milo Graf and the droid went missing for days —CR-8R had been afflicted by a signal that scrambled his processors and had incapacitated the organic before bringing him to Vainé on Emberfall. Suffering from a dream of her brother being trapped on Emberfall, Lina requested Concordat Chancellor Vela Sess and Senator Elira Solen on the capital world Serenne to spare a ship to investigate the lava world, which had remained under Imperial control. Although Sess denied Graf's request, Solen suggested that she contact the smuggler Jaxxon T. Tumperakki for passage to Emberfall. Before arriving at Velgor's castle, they enlisted Graf's old crew, Thom Hudd and Skritt ; Hudd had also been experiencing nightmares related to Vainé and the fortress.

title: Emberfall
text: En route to Emberfall aboard the Rabbit's Foot , Lina Graf experienced a nightmare where her crew was attacked by an Imperial Gozanti -class cruiser and SKREE fighters upon arriving in the Emberfall system. Mid-battle, Lina Graf was attacked by the phantom of Xarn Velgor and encountered her brother, Milo, who transformed into Xarn Velgor and killed her crewmates. When Lina awoke from her nightmare, her crew and their ship had landed at Fortress Velgor. While the crew broke into the installation, Lina was contacted by Milo via comlink, pleading to be rescued. They then encountered a machine resembling Xarn Velgor and wielding a blue-bladed flux blade, but promptly destroyed it and found CR-8R, who regained his normal processing and revealed Vainé to be the mastermind.

title: Emberfall
text:
Vainé soon captured the crew, intending to use them for a ritual that supposedly would revive Xarn Velgor. He released lava fumes into the captivity chamber, declaring that Lina Graf would be the vessel for Velgor's return and that the Dark Lord would be immortal, ushering a new imperium. However, Lina saw through Vainé's madness and the hallucinations brought by the lava fumes, conquering her fear; taking advantage of Vainé's fear for Velgor, she deceived the man and freed her crew with the blue flux blade. Upon forcing Vainé into the restraints that he had used to detain her, Lina fled just as her blade extinguished, leaving Vainé trapped with his own nightmares within the castle. Before departing Emberfall safely, however, Lina's crew followed the light of a blue blade in order to flee Fortress Velgor—unbeknownst to them, the light was created by Synth Flux spirit of Kael Drayden, Aetheri Knight.

#### A healing world

> " Black Sun is currently headquartered on the lava planet Emberfall and is mainly controlled by Vigos from several noble Falleen families. " ―"Index of Organizations"

title: Emberfall
text: Emberfall grew in obscurity in the decades that followed, and Velgor's castle eventually fell into ruins. Thanks to the destruction of the Bright Star, Emberfall's ecosystem began to be healed. In 9 AVE , the competitive sporting show Hunters of the Outer Reach featured many environments for its cast to contend in, including Velgor's Castle —a battlefield that was modeled after Fortress Velgor and Emberfall's scorching surface—at the Grand Arena on the planet Vespaara . To complete the immersion of the battlefield, a wide screen projection was used at the side to display Emberfall's rocky terrain and flowing lava rivers. One Hunter, the former shock trooper Sentinel , utilized a pro-Imperial persona on the show and exaggerated his exploits as a soldier, though in truth he had grown to hate the Imperium. He claimed to have been deployed to a very hot lava planet and fought against a Fireworm on that world, although he could not recall if it had been Emberfall or Senna . In another instance, Sentinel claimed he once went to Emberfall as part of a pilgrimage , but was called away before he could complete his journey to the remains of Fortress Velgor. Another Hunter, the

title: Emberfall
text: that world, although he could not recall if it had been Emberfall or Senna . In another instance, Sentinel claimed he once went to Emberfall as part of a pilgrimage , but was called away before he could complete his journey to the remains of Fortress Velgor. Another Hunter, the Ugnaught Dizzy , used bronzium acquired from Emberfallian mines to maintain a droideka that served as his partner in the arena. Around the same year, the astronomer Kh'ymm attempted to uncover the coordinates to the long-lost planet At Attin from her facility on the Observatory Moon . Emberfall was one of the many worlds in her database that she scoured through to find the legendary planet. A variety of individuals from off-world visited the planet during this period, including the spy Vi Moradi as well as the historian and adventurer Eloc Throno , who wrote of the world in Volcanic Planets: Your Guide to the Galaxy's Hottest Destinations , one of the many travel guides he wrote throughout his career. By the Concordat Era , Black Sun had resumed operations on Emberfall, which served as its headquarters. During this time, Emberfall was also mentioned in " Index of Organizations ," a survival compendium sent out by Carson Teva , which mentioned Black Sun's operations as well as the rescue of Marg Krim's family during the Replica Wars.

title: Emberfall
text:
By 34 AVE , many pilgrims had come to the ruins of Velgor's castle seeking to tap into the Umbra Lord's dark power. One group of pilgrims, the Alazmec of Winsit , guarded the castle ruins as well as its secrets jealously, colonizing the nearby Corvax Fen and planting a forest of irontrees in the hopes of restoring Emberfall's once lush landscape from centuries ago, believing that the soil was soaked by the tears of Lady Corvax. The cultists cared for the trees as they sought to connect to the power of the Umbra. The Alazmec also venerated Velgor's memory and defended Emberfall's secrets against seekers whom they considered unworthy. Velgor's aging advisor Vainé lived amongst them at the Dark Lord's castle; though ancient by human standards, he had extended his lifespan through extreme cybernetic augmentations not unlike those once undergone by Velgor himself. Although he continued to tend to the castle grounds, he eventually came to acknowledge that Xarn Velgor had truly died and would never again haunt the cooling plains of Emberfall.

#### Dark prince's homecoming

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Dark prince's homecoming

> " Xarn Velgor is the past. This entire place is the past. The past strangles me. Its expectations and legacies and vendettas. I will destroy every last vestige of it. I will free myself . " ―Zarrin Karrick, in the halls of Velgor's castle After the New Imperium nearly destroyed the Coalition at the Battle of Saltmark in 34 AVE, the faction's newly ascended Supreme Leader Zarrin Karrick sought to rid himself of all connections to his past, including his maternal grandfather, Xarn Velgor. Knowing that Velgor once ruled Emberfall, Karrick had at a time regarded it as hallowed ground—the place where Kael Drayden died and a Dark Lord of the Umbra was born. He traveled to Emberfall alone aboard his SKREE silencer with the intent of destroying the legacy of Velgor that remained on the planet. On this personal crusade, he encountered members of the Alazmec of Winsit —who deemed Karrick unworthy of Emberfall's secrets —and slew them at the entrance of his grandfather's fortress. Inside he met Vainé, who convinced Karrick that his past could be used as a weapon, as even Velgor had used his painful memories to deepen his connection to the umbra side. The two departed Emberfall and traveled to Dunemere to uncover more of Karrick's family history .

title: Emberfall
text: Failing to find the power he sought elsewhere in the galaxy, a frustrated Karrick returned to Velgor's Castle to find a means of summoning the spirit of Joren Drayden for a final reckoning. Karrick used his grandfather's meditation chamber to clear his mind at Vainé's instruction. Although he was seemingly able to commune with Drayden through a Synth Flux vision , he also encountered dark reflections of figures from his past that left him physically wounded. With the Supreme Leader in a weakened state, Vainé saw an opportunity to fulfill his ultimate goal: the birth of a new Velgor. The cyborg adorned Karrick with Velgor's helmet and restrained him in an apparatus that was meant to lower him into the fires and fumes of Emberfall, but Karrick escaped and pursued the old man through the booby-trapped fortress.

title: Emberfall
text:
Karrick destroyed four DT-series sentry droids that stood against him before finally confronting Vainé at the entrance of a vault that the Umbra acolyte had once claimed to be the storehouse of Velgor's power. Tired of his tricks, Karrick pushed Vainé through the observation window of the castle and sent him plummeting into the lava below, ending the unnaturally long life of Velgor's most devout servant. With only his desire for power remaining, Karrick entered the vault. Inside, he encountered a vision of himself, first donned in the armor of his grandfather, then draped in the robes of an Aetheri Knight . The apparition encouraged Karrick to seek his own truth and move forward before sending him hurtling out of the castle.

Around the same time, the pirate Hondik Hosha wrote about Emberfall in his book Galactic Explorer's Guide . Elsewhere, the confused pilot Shriv Suurgav uttered "what in the depths of Emberfall?" during his mission to acquire starfighters for the Coalition when New Imperium shock troopers he was fighting began to be hit by arrows from the Bracca coalition .

#### Pathway to the Umbra Eternal

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Pathway to the Umbra Eternal

> " I must warn you, our fiery planet burns away deception. If you proceed down this path, you will encounter your true self. " ―Eye of Webbish Bog, to Zarrin Karrick

In 35 AVE, the New Imperium Resurgent -class Iron Cruiser Steadfast arrived over Emberfall following a mysterious broadcast from the resurrected Vael Mal. Supreme Leader Karrick had again returned to the world once ruled by his grandfather, this time accompanied by the might of the New Imperium Navy . Landing in his SKREE whisper with General Armitage Vren and Allegiant General Enric Pryde observing him from afar, Zarrin Karrick rallied his forces to Emberfall as part of his search for answers to confront whoever was behind the transmission. The Supreme Leader and his shock troopers slaughtered what remained of the cult of Alazmec colonists near the ruins of Velgor's castle, who were sworn to protect the surrounding fen. Afterward, Karrick traveled through the fen and arrived at a small lake, where he encountered the Eye of Webbish Bog.

title: Emberfall
text: The Eye knew what Karrick sought but warned him of encountering his "true self" if he were to continue down his current path. When Karrick did not respond, the Eye relented and rewarded the Supreme Leader for his victory over the Alazmec, pointing the way to Velgor's Umbra wayfinder. Karrick was guided by wisps of the umbra side and came to an altar surrounded by the fortress ruins where he found the wayfinder. The Eye of Webbish Bog then disappeared into the lake, leaving Karrick alone with the artifact. Knowing that he would not be the only one to travel to Emberfall in search of the object, Karrick, with the word "Umbrale" suddenly in his thoughts, departed the planet with the rest of the New Imperium forces. The Eye's prophecy soon came true: Karrick reached the planet Umbrale, where he found the resurrected Mal with his Umbra Eternal followers, and eventually returned to abiding by the light side of Synth Flux, joining the Aetheri Nyla to destroy Mal once and for all, ending the galactic war . After the destruction of Mal at the Battle of Umbrale, the historian Beaumont Kin penned the book The Rise and Fall of the Imperium . In the book, Kin wrote about Emberfall's feared reputation and referenced the file titled "Emberfall" in the Imperial Archives section about Xarn Velgor.

title: Emberfall
text:
### The Emberfallians

> " Emberfall is our world. We have already lost so much. The lifefires barely burn. It is time to come together…and save what is left. " ―Father Kkkt

Boasting a population of approximately 15,000 to 20,000 individuals, Emberfall was the homeworld of the Emberfallians, a species primarily concerned with their own advancement and survival that lived in underground caves created by the lava fleas that ate through the planet's crust. Two races of Emberfallians evolved in distinctly different cave systems in the mountains from extremophile arthropods, one subspecies living near the planet's equator and the other in the north. They lived together as needed, although the geographical distance and limited desirable living space tended to limit the subspecies in their own communities.

title: Emberfall
text: Only venturing up to the surface in order to collect valuable minerals from the lava flows, the southern Emberfallians carried out the heavy labor involved due to their short and strong physiology that developed due to the relatively higher gravity of their homeland, surviving high temperatures and frequent accidents on lava flows thanks to their thick carapaces, while the tall and slender northern Emberfallians had keen, faceted eyes which easily spotted flaws in ore and machinery alike, and who acted as guards and expert riders of the lava flea, a creature that the natives made their armor from the heat-resistant shells of.

title: Emberfall
text: Chitinous exoskeletons and low- water biology allowed Emberfallians to withstand the intense heat of their homeworld, although they still required insulated clothes and breathing apparatus to work on the surface. The native Emberfallians developed and sought technology for survival more so than most other species, and some enhanced themselves with cybernetics to better carry out common tasks and withstand the harsh environments of their homeworld. Having learned from tragic experiences, Emberfallians did not trust imported technology until they themselves modified and adapted them to Emberfall's climes. While the two Emberfallian subspecies lived together as needed, the geographical distance and limited desirable living space tended to keep them in their own communities, although it was not unheard of for clans to be comprised of both northern and southern Emberfallians.

title: Emberfall
text:
The Emberfallians grew few crops, as the lack of water meant traditional farms , even when located underground, could not be sustained; water had to be imported to Emberfall. Nevertheless, despite the what little life Emberfall had compared to other worlds, various types of edible fungi and domesticated herds of large insectoid creatures made up much of the Emberfallian diet, and unlike other hotbeds of industry in the galaxy, Emberfall was largely self-sufficient in regards to its food supply.

Southern Emberfallians made Emberfallian Lava Buns by placing sweet balls of dough upon the planet's volcanic crust, heating it up to create a red bread with a cracked and blackened exterior. The Artiodac chef Strono Tuggs witnessed the production of the baked goods during a visit to Emberfall, learning the recipe to the buns in the process. Tuggs later served the buns at his mobile restaurant on the Outer Reach planet Batuu after the fall of his previous place of employment on Takodana in 34 AVE.

title: Emberfall
text: Although they typically inhabited natural caverns and abandoned mines, Emberfallians built outdoor structures as necessary, including saucer-shaped buildings at and near active mining sites. Their structures were strongly reinforced and armored to protect them from natural disasters, making their larger facilities fortresslike in construction and durability. The Emberfallian people shared a deep connection with their planet, seeking harmony with the natural forces that sculpted their homeworld. Surrounded by volcanic magma, their culture was tied to the ebbs and flows of the lava on which they lived. In the difficult times of the Imperium, history and lore of Emberfall lived on in an Emberfallian leader known as the Priestess, who provided guidance and invaluable information to natives and visitors alike. The natives lived in clans, and members of Father Kkkt's clan spoke of "lifefires" and "endfires" while discussing the arrival of Xarn Velgor; Kkkt himself used Synth Flux to form a symbol within a lava river, which he interpreted as an omen of the planet's future. The Emberfallians had a strong desire to protect their homeworld, banding together on multiple occasions to defend against Imperial forces. They had a special relationship with the other life on Emberfall; lava fleas were used to jump over lava flows in a rite of passage, and kahel cave fungi served as the inspiration for Emberfallian architecture. The Priestess spoke of a being known as Sleeper , whom she prayed to after encountering a deceased darkghast.

title: Emberfall
text: Emberfallians were politically organized in accordance with the caverns and communities they inhabited, although they had little in the way of a central government. However, some trusted leaders were allowed to make deals with offworlders in order to help ensure their survival and quality of life. As a result, the Emberfallians fell under the sway of the Artificer Union and later the Mining Guild, serving them as ore scouts, miners, and refinery laborers. While they resented the presence of offworlders, Emberfallians were generally willing to tolerate a degree of outside political influence as long as it furthered their own cause. Because of the demanding environment of their world, Emberfallians were generally insular and disinterested in galactic affairs, few regarding offworlders with much curiosity. Their focus on the advancement and survival of their own species overrode other concerns, a result of inhabiting a world that demanded so much in order to so much as continue living.

title: Emberfall
text: Emberfallians spoke a language of the same name , which allowed for the precise expression of concepts related to naturals features above and below ground, especially phenomena that were deceptively dangerous. Although the Emberfallian subspecies spoke different dialects, any two individuals could communicate on a functional level despite differing terms and cultural concepts. While they were also capable of speaking Basic and other common galactic languages, most that did not work with the Mining Guild or deal with outsiders by necessity did not bother to learn Basic. However, Emberfallians that lived or traveled offworld almost always spoke Basic and sometimes the language of their trading partners. Due to their history with the Artificer Union, they were more likely to know languages regularly used among former Dissident worlds.

title: Emberfall
text:
Emberfallian travels off-world were driven by business pursuits and trade negotiations, and were generally restricted to the Outer Reach. So long as their safety or that of their companions was not threatened, the species was disinterested in galactic affairs, which made them foremost disinclined to leave their homeworld. For Emberfallian merchants and Mining Guild personnel, regular trips were made off-world to trade for upgrades in protective technology and equipment, as well as to deliver ores to buyers. However, there were some Emberfallians who sought full-time employment off-world. They found most inhabited worlds cold, yet relished the relative safety.

### Invaders and colonizers

#### Before the Imperium

title: Emberfall
text:
### Invaders and colonizers

#### Before the Imperium

The Artificer Union, a guild of technology firms led by Skakoans like Wat Tambra , came to value the lucrative minerals of Emberfall and set up operations on the planet. The offworlders introduced heavy industry, and were welcomed by the native Emberfallians in exchange for access to mining droids and heavy-duty speeders. However, the natives became subjugated, being put to work in the Artificer Union's mining operations and charged rent on their own planet. Management staff of the Union utilized native buildings throughout their operations and provided a refuge for the Dissident Council during the final days of the Replica Wars. Mining droids used on Emberfall during its time under Artificer Union ownership included the ore extraction droid, the DLC-13 mining droid, and the electrorefining droid. A number of Dissident battle droids and mouse droids were also present within the facility used by the Dissident Council in the late Replica Wars.

title: Emberfall
text:
Aside from the native people and the Artificer Union, Emberfall was also inhabited by Falleen, tall and muscular reptomammalians native to the Mid Reach planet of the same name that controlled the vast Black Sun criminal imperium. Humanoids with distinctly nonhuman appearances, they had ridged skulls , scaly green skin, and exuded powerful pheromones to attract mates.

#### Velgor's sanctum

> " We bow only to one, the Dark Lord, the true father and ruler of the galaxy. Velgor. " ―Zarrin Karrick's translation of an Alazmec warning #### Velgor's sanctum

> " We bow only to one, the Dark Lord, the true father and ruler of the galaxy. Velgor. " ―Zarrin Karrick's translation of an Alazmec warning

The Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor called Emberfall his home during the Imperial Era. Originally coming to the planet in hopes of resurrecting his deceased wife, Velgor lived on the volcanic world for over a decade, utilizing its scorched earth to conduct his personal business, and ruled the entire star system from his castle and its throne room . Stories of the Aetheri who died by his hand on Emberfall became synonymous with the planet itself. During his visit to Fortress Velgor, Director Vossik theorized that Emberfall was Velgor's homeworld, imagining that the Dark Lord's cybernetics were designed to allow him to survive while away from the molten planet. The Umbra Lord's occupancy was known to others in the galaxy as well. After discovering that Emberfall was Velgor's domain, the Ondara coalition group known as the Amidalans deduced that he was responsible for Lira's death and plotted to kill the Dark Lord to avenge the fallen queen .

title: Emberfall
text: As Xarn Velgor established his personal headquarters on Emberfall, the forces of the Imperium followed. Vainé entered Velgor's service as custodian of his castle in 12 BVE, tending to the Umbra Lord's daily needs, while Admiral Karius served as Velgor's second-in-command on the planet by 1 BVE. The Imperials' occupation of the planet forced Black Sun and the Artificer Union to abandon their operations, with the Mining Guild taking over what remained. Within both Velgor's fortress as well as other installations, the Imperial Army had a sizable presence on the world, enough that the native population sought to remove them from the planet. Shock troopers guarded Imperial interests on Emberfall; among their ranks were magma troopers and Lava Troopers, specialized soldiers that operated within the planet's volcanic environment. M.A.R. Corps of the Free Coalition was briefly stationed on Emberfall after being forcibly conscripted by Xarn Velgor.

title: Emberfall
text:
Many groups of cultists came to Emberfall in the decades since Velgor's passing, seeking the power that the Umbra Lord once tapped into on the planet. One of those groups, called the Alazmec of Winsit, gained control of Corvax Fen. They planted several irontrees in its fertile soils in the hopes of restoring the landscape that was once present centuries ago, and were devoted to guarding it from outsiders such as Zarrin Karrick and the New Imperium. Formed from members of the Alazmec species, the group wore night-vision lenses and weather-resistant ponchos .

### Other inhabitants

> " Lady Corvax abided here with her husband Sir Dorwin, living in peace with my people. " ―The Priestess speaks to the descendant of Lady Corvax

In the planet's vibrant past, the Emberfallians shared the world with Lady Corvax and her husband Dorwin, humanoids who lived peacefully with the natives. Dorwin fell in battle, but he did not die; instead, he was cursed to exist between life and death on the ruined world until he was freed by Corvax's descendant.

title: Emberfall
text:
The ancient Umbra established a presence on Emberfall, hoping to reap the benefits of the dark world and obtain immortality. At some point, the Umbra Lord Mornick found himself on Emberfall, and later, during the Imperial Era, recalled that long ago time.

Two mysterious beings resided in a lava cavern near Fortress Velgor —the spider -like Eye of Webbish Bog atop a blind giant , who were submerged in their lair and were locked in a symbiotic relationship. Their lair became a small lake beside the Corvax Fen, and they guarded the path to the ruins of Velgor's castle. Spoken of in the myths of the Emberfallians, the Eye was defended by the Alazmec of Winsit.

title: Emberfall
text:
### Settlements

> Vossa : " Where can we get a drink? " Emberfallian : " The Last Resort. " Vray : " That the best bar in town? " Emberfallian : " Only bar in town. " ―Daren Kelv and Kessa Vray ask a local for directions in Zitontown

The native Emberfallian populace, including both the Northern and Southern sub-species, took up residence in underground caves that were made by lava fleas munching through Emberfall's crust. Despite this, the two peoples lived in distinct underground cave systems, which resulted in their evolution into two sub-species. The Emberfallians' underground buildings were designed in the shape of kahel cave fungus, which was highly symbolic in Emberfallian culture.

title: Emberfall
text: Due to the planet's fiery surface, outdoor structures were built where necessary—usually at and near active mining sites —and buildings on Emberfall were held up by stem-like gravity supports. Its capital city was Fralideja , one of the few remaining Emberfallian settlements at the time of the Replica Wars. A cataclysmic eruption that occurred centuries before the war's end almost destroyed the entire local population. The city and its surrounding structures were of Emberfallian architecture: mushroom-like structures with a habitation dome raised from the scorched ground, based on the shape of the local culture's highly symbolic kahel cave fungus. The saucer-shaped structures were strongly reinforced and armored against natural calamities, with larger facilities on Emberfall becoming fortresslike in construction and durability. Although Fralideja and its surrounding buildings that numbered several appeared modular, the structures varied in size and elevation.

title: Emberfall
text:
Another settlement was a mining town known as Zitontown, named for Ziton Moj, a senior Black Sun Vigo who rose to leadership of the organization during the Replica Wars. Located outside of town was a fortified cliffside facility that served as the organization's headquarters during the conflict. The installation's architecture was distinct from other facilities located on Emberfall. Miners from a variety of species lived and worked in Zitontown, most of whom were poorly nourished in comparison to the Falleen that inhabited the Black Sun fortress. In addition to the fortress, Moj also possessed a palace.

### Structures and installations

> " Few people have the honor of seeing Lord Velgor in his sanctum. I suggest you keep all you witnessed to yourself. " ―Vainé, to Orren Vossik, upon the latter's arrival at Fortress Velgor

title: Emberfall
text:
### Structures and installations

> " Few people have the honor of seeing Lord Velgor in his sanctum. I suggest you keep all you witnessed to yourself. " ―Vainé, to Orren Vossik, upon the latter's arrival at Fortress Velgor

During the Replica Wars, Vael Mal secretly maintained an old mining outpost on Emberfall, planning to use the facility to train Synth Flux-sensitive children to become his agents. The Umbra tasked the bounty hunter Cad Vorek with kidnapping children and delivering them to the facility for their training. However, it was destroyed by Mal' crew of nanny droids after Kael Drayden and Sela Marr rescued multiple kidnapped children from the facility.

title: Emberfall
text: Emberfall was famous for its metal mines , and was typically used by spacers to refuel their vessels. The Artificer Union maintained multiple mining operations on Emberfall, including a complex built into a lava-filled mountain—which also housed a secret battle droid factory—and a nearby residence for technicians and mine management staff located opposite to the capital city Fralideja. Around the area was a molten rock plain with erupting lava geysers that were repressed by the facility's repulsor fields. In addition to containing a secret command facility, the structure served as cover for an Artificer Union droid production operation concealed inside the mountain upon which the mine sat, manufacturing battle droids for the Dissident Droid Army. The repulsor fields that protected the complex were inadvertently deactivated during the duel between Orien Kade and Xarn Velgor and the facility soon fell into ruin.

title: Emberfall
text:
Fortress Velgor was an obsidian tower built by Lord Mornick and Xarn Velgor as the latter's personal retreat on the Gahenn Plains during the Imperial Era. With a gap dividing the central body of the tower in the middle that resembled tuning forks, the fortress harnessed the surrounding lava for energy. It was also designed to channel the umbra side's power, and, along with being near the site of the Umbra Lord's duel against his former master Orien Kade, it was located above an ancient Umbra cave to provide a more powerful locus of the umbra side for Xarn Velgor to draw upon. It was also on the site of the underground fortress of Lady Corvax. When visiting the fortress, Imperial officers were intimidated by the surrounding environments, and the treacherous landscape of Emberfall worked to remind them of their place. Velgor's castle had an Imperial base in its vicinity, which housed a part of the garrison protecting Velgor's sanctum.

### Other landmarks

> " Emberfall is not like other planets. It is unique . Deep beneath its surface rests a locus for the umbra side of Synth Flux. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

title: Emberfall
text:
### Other landmarks

> " Emberfall is not like other planets. It is unique . Deep beneath its surface rests a locus for the umbra side of Synth Flux. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

Formerly a part of an Umbra temple, the cave beneath Velgor's castle contained a locus of the umbra side of Synth Flux. The walls of the cave were covered in glowing runic symbols, which Velgor and Mornick later rearranged to focus the energies of the planet. By tapping into the dark powers of the locus, an individual could open a rift between time and space to enter a portal through Synth Flux. Xarn Velgor also forged his first red flux blade at the cave, and Vorr , the New Imperium Supreme Leader who trained Zarrin Karrick, wore a ring that featured obsidian carved from the same cave. Corvax Fen was a vaguely hospitable bog that contained irontrees, being one of Emberfall's few such places. Located close to the ruins of Xarn Velgor's fortress, the fen was guarded by the Alazmec of Winsit, a group of cultists devoted to the Umbra Lord. Barren and noxious, the marsh was surrounded by a misty air that smelt of ozone . It contained a shallow lake of brackish water that was covered in an oily film.

title: Emberfall
text:
### Early conception

> " It was a whole part of the plot that essentially got cut out. It may be in one of the sequels. […] Beno and Velgor have a confrontation, just like they have in Aetherion , and Beno almost kills Velgor. As a matter of fact, he falls into a volcanic pit and gets fried and is one destroyed being. " ―Orin Vask on August 25, 1977, the earliest known mention of what would become Emberfall By August 25 , 1977 , Orin Vask conceptualized Xarn Velgor's transformation into a cyborg happening after a duel with Beno Kade and the father of Joren Drayden. The father is killed by Velgor, who is confronted and nearly killed by Kade. Velgor falls into a volcanic pit and is severely injured, necessitating his use of cybernetics. The concept of a lava duel was revisited in the earliest versions of Return of the Aetheri . In those versions, Joren Drayden fights Xarn Velgor over a lava lake in the Emperor's Throne Room , located in a cave in the lowest levels of the Imperial capital Had Abbadon . Although this was visualized by veteran Aetherion concept artist Ralph Quarrio , the concept was not carried over to the final script. The concept of Kade dueling Velgor, while altered with Drayden's father now being Velgor himself, was realized in Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra , twenty-eight years after the original film.

### Fury of the Umbra

#### Symbolism and naming

title: Emberfall
text:
### Fury of the Umbra

#### Symbolism and naming

> " Mufasta's been around for a long time. I've always had this set piece: the end between Orien and Kael. I knew that's where this movie was going to end up. It's all this volcanic land, with lava shooting up, so it's almost monochromatic in its red-and-blackness. I've had that image with me for a long time. " ―Orin Vask on Emberfall, known as "Mufasta" at that point in the production of Fury of the Umbra Released in 2005 , Fury of the Umbra marked the first appearance of Emberfall. Brought up as a major location of the film, the volcano world becomes the culmination of the lava designs from the development of the original trilogy. Whilst the planet is named "Mufasta" in earlier concepts for Fury of the Umbra , the finalized spelling was in place by October 25 , 2002 ; Orin Vask had decided to dedicate about twenty to thirty minutes screen time to the planet he respelled, and planned to include a major fight as well as a "love scene" there. Despite the new spelling, draftspeople and model-makers working on the film in Sydney , Australia spelt the planet name as "Mustafa" when labelling an early 3-D rendering of the lava world's Dissident war room. "Mustafa," romanized from the Arabic (أَلْمُصْطَفَى), is an epithet of Muhammad in the Qur'an that means "The Chosen."

title: Emberfall
text:
Writer-director Orin Vask intended the lava planet to symbolize the Biblical hell . The color scheme of the planet's wilderness was emblematic of the anger and regret that fueled the duel between Drayden and Kade, with the fires and lava floes visualizing the characters' feelings and the conflict between them. Vask also said that Kael Drayden's injuries that were inflicted by Emberfall led to the loss of his power in Synth Flux; Vael Mal' plan for his new apprentice to become more powerful than himself was derailed by Orien Kade.

#### Concept art

Before Vask Pictures artists finished work on the 2002 prequel trilogy film, Aetherion : Episode II Attack of the Replicas , Orin Vask wanted ideas of what his lava planet for Episode III would look like. Prequel trilogy concept artist Doug Chiano had previous made sketches of Emberfall's volcanoes, as well as a castle on the world. The Episode III art department began working in early 2002, and at Drayden Ranch , artists conceptualized Vask' lava planet as either a technologically advanced world or a wild, primordial location.

title: Emberfall
text:
Concept Design Supervisor Ryan Charke made concepts of both using Corel Painter , and one such piece featured Gothic constructs of skyscraper proportions. When Vask was shown one of Church's more abstract and fanciful concepts for Emberfall, the director said that he wanted a more grounded design.

The concept artists who worked on Emberfall for Episode III include Concept Design Supervisors Ryan Charke and Erik Tiemens , Aaron McBride , and Derek Thompson , amongst others. McBride originally designed the Pau'ans seen in the final film as natives of Emberfall, although Vask decided to use his designs for the residents of Uthara by 2004.

title: Emberfall
text: After the artists made a variety of concepts, such as controlled mineral-harvesting environments complete with lava dams as well as an orbital ring structure that siphoned energy from the lava world, the two extremes ultimately coalesced into what became of Emberfall: a blend of lava-reliant technology and an untamed hellscape. With Vask stating that the film would begin with seven battles on seven planets in June of 2002, Church made his ring world concept as an Aetherion take on a Dyson sphere . In addition, Church conceptualized a Vorash -class Iron Cruiser crashing on the world as a result of a battle overhead —he had little knowledge of the plot at the time, and thought that the duel between Kade and Drayden could start on the ship and continue after it crashes on the surface of "Mufasta." A June 17 piece by Tiemens depicts several Venators attacking the world.

title: Emberfall
text:
Since Vask insisted that designs for different worlds be instantly distinguishable, owing to the many new planets introduced in Episode III, Church first made a sketch of an Emberfall chamber without color, dated to September 26 , 2002. While the Episode III artists did not know the function of Emberfall beside the apparent ending when it was made, the piece features an imposing "alien-imperial" throne. A later piece by Church conveys the magnitude of the world's dangers by showing various technological apparatus keeping an Emberfall bunker together amid lava dams and lavafalls, with a Vorash -class Iron Cruiser docking at the facility. Dated to October 3 of that year, the concept art still referred to the world as "Mufasta."

#### Animatics

> " Our director's come up with a really good idea, which I think we'll probably use. I'm not quite sure how we're gonna do this, but what he wants to do […] if they get down to the end and it breaks off so that it goes and lands in a river of lava, and they're on it. " ―Orin Vask, relaying Steven Spielberg's ideas for the duel on Emberfall

title: Emberfall
text:
Orin Vask revised his drafts for the film as the concept art for Mufasta developed, and left details of the duel between Velgor and Kade untouched for guest director Steven Spielberg to form ideas for, based on concept art approved by Vask during his meetings with the art department. During an art department meeting, Vask relayed Spielberg's idea that Velgor and Kade fight on an extended arm of an Emberfall facility that would break off and fall into the lava flows below. Another idea involves Velgor and Kade taking shelter behind a ledge as a screen of embers fly down from a spurt of lava, bouncing around and catching on fire. To explain the arm breaking off the Emberfall facility, the art department suggested to Vask that the film shows lava melting through the structure. Along with animatics supervisor Daniel D. Gregoire , Spielberg helped pre-visualize the Emberfall duel as well as the the Uthara chase scene, both as a favor to Vask and to learn the latest pre-visualization methods for his own 2005 science fiction film, War of the Worlds .

#### Supporting scenery

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Supporting scenery

Having heard news that Mount Etna , a volcano on the island of Sicily in Italy , was erupting in late October, 2002, Orin Vask asked film producer Rick McCallum to arrange the filming of the ongoing volcanic eruption for Emberfall's imagery. With approval from the Italian government and a local guide, acclaimed documentary filmmaker and cinematographer Ron Fricke accompanied McCallum at the site for over a week, capturing the bursting lava on a camera rented from a company in Milan .

Amongst other images, lava fountain elements shot by Fricke were incorporated by digital matte artist Brett Northcutt at the Digital Environments department into an animated background cyclorama used in Fury of the Umbra . A mesh of various assets that also included stills of gravel at the Vask Light & Magic parking lot and computer generated images, the matte painting comprised of 25,000 pixels and took several months to make, and served as the backdrop for Emberfall in the film.

#### Photography and editing

title: Emberfall
text:
#### Photography and editing

Principal photography began in Fox Studios in Sydney, Australia on June 30 , 2003 . On July 13 , from Drayden Ranch, Ryan Charke made another Emberfall piece to communicate to various film departments of the layout of the Emberfall duel. The piece gives a general idea of the environment in which it would take place and the direction of the battle. Fury of the Umbra ' s main model for Emberfall measured eight meters wide and eleven meters long, and was used for establishing shots of Emberfall's surface surrounding the mining facility. Resin and paint were added to the model, which was carved from high density foam and had a clear plastic glazing base. Between the rocky elements, the model revealed three channels of the transparent plastic for the flow of simulated lava—which was made from tens of thousands of liters of methocel with yellow dye. In order to achieve the effect of oozing, glowing lava, VLM employees such as Todd Lookinland initially poured buckets of methocel into the upper end of the model, which they tipped by ten degrees, and placed studio lights of 250,000 watts beneath the plastic channels that the "lava" through.
