During Ferrum's Civil War and his apprenticeship under Sorin Vael, Kade fell in love with the young Duchess Satinna Velara. The two lived on the run for over a year. Velara reciprocated his feelings as he saved her life from insurgents and bounty hunters. When Kade's mission ended, he chose to honor his obligations to the Aetheri Order in accordance to the Aetheri Code. However, he regretted leaving the Duchess alone to rebuild Ferrum.

title: Orien Kade
text: Years later during the Replica Wars, Kade and Velara still had feelings for each other, but found themselves on opposing sides. Velara had begun to advocate a course of neutrality for herself and 1,500 systems that wanted no part in the war. Meanwhile, Kade defended the use of military action to end the conflict with the Dissidents, including a military presence on Ferrum to protect it from the Grave Watch. As such, their inability to express their feelings led them to bicker relentlessly about their conflicting philosophies. Only when forced into action did their camaraderie return. When Velara was taken hostage by Senator Merrick, she confessed that she had always loved him. Kade, despite the situation, confessed that he too loved her and would have left the Aetheri Order if she asked it of him. Despite their confessions, Kade and Velara continued with their responsibilities as peacekeepers. When Vreth resurfaced on Ferrum, Kade attempted to rescue her from him, but the pair were captured. Kade was forced to watch Vreth choke Velara and ultimately kill her with the Darksaber. Kade mourned her, but refused to give in to his anger and desire to avenge her, only doing so out of peace and justice nearly twenty years later.

title: Orien Kade
text:
### Flux blade abilities

> " This weapon is your life. " ―Orien Kade, to Kael Drayden

Kade was a very capable flux blade duelist, one of the greatest swordsmen of his time. Throughout his training years, he had learnt several forms of flux blade combat, especially Form III . In contrast to the aggressive dueling styles of his master, Sorin Vael, and his apprentice Kael Drayden, Kade's combat style was mainly defensive, though he would use aggressive attacks when pressed. He faced some of the most dangerous people in the galaxy, such as the deadly Umbra Lord Vael Vreth and infamous Aetheri Hunter General Skarn, respectively, the latter of whom he fought on at least seven occasions. Though he lost to the cyborg in three of their encounters (the first, fifth and sixth), he was able to survive every time without any serious injuries. [ source? ]

title: Orien Kade
text: Kade was able to duel Skarn to a draw in their third and fourth encounters, and was able to overpower him in their second duel and ultimately killed him in the final round, albeit with a volt pistol rather than his flux blade. However, his final victory may have been helped by Skarn' fresh injuries, which would have hampered the cyborg's fighting abilities. Although Kade usually used only one flux blade, he also seemed to have been well-versed in the art of Jar'Kai , which was perhaps most prominently displayed during his duel with Vreth and Savage Opress, in which he wielded both his own flux blade and the blade of the slain Adi Gallia. His mastery of dual-blade combat allowed him to hold his own against both the Umbra brothers, and he even managed to break Opress's left knee and sever his left arm. The duel ultimately ended as a stalemate when an angered Vreth used his Synth Flux powers to briefly incapacitate Kade, giving the brothers time to escape.

title: Orien Kade
text: Kade also situationally, and somewhat less successfully, used Jar'Kai against General Skarn and Cad Vorek respectively. He was also capable of using his flux blade to ground Synth Flux lightning, as he demonstrated against Varek on Pyralis. Kade was also able to defeat his former apprentice Kael Drayden, then Xarn Velgor, in an epic duel on Emberfall. Making use of his staunch Form III defense throughout the fight, Kade was eventually able to exploit Velgor's aggressive nature, and dismembered the hate-filled Umbra Lord when he recklessly jumped towards him. While initially not as skilled due to having lost his connection with Synth Flux, Kade was able to get the edge once again over his former apprentice Xarn Velgor on another duel ten years later.

title: Orien Kade
text:
Decades later, he defeated his old nemesis Vreth within seconds despite the former Umbra Lord having demonstrated the ability to hold an advantage against three Wardens simultaneously, and duel his former master Vael Mal for a short time. A few years later, during his rematch with Velgor on the first Void Core, Kade proved formidable enough to hold his own against the Umbra Lord for a short time. However, Velgor's cautious but relentless assault ultimately overwhelmed Kade's defenses, and he was forced to begin retreating. Ultimately, he chose to become one with Synth Flux rather than continue the fight and in doing this, he taught both of his Drayden students one final lesson.

Though Kade focused largely on flux blade combat, he was also very skilled and powerful in use of Synth Flux. He was trained in the use of the mind trick , making use of it whenever he wanted to avoid physical confrontations. He was also able to use Synth Flux to tame, control, and lead a group of angry gutkurrs on Selvara. As befitted an Aetheri, Kade was adept at concealing his feelings in Synth Flux when he chose to. Kade was adept at Synth Flux healing , improving his physical capabilities, leaping around with Synth Flux , knowing the future , and could, with great effort, make himself and his use of Synth Flux go unnoticed by all. He also felt when Cindervale was destroyed and so many died.

title: Orien Kade
text: He was also capable of using telekinesis to push or levitate objects, or to crush them, as seen when he destroyed two commando droids to recover his flux blade after a difficult hand-to-hand fight with Darts D'Nar. He would also use Synth Flux to augment his natural leaping ability. His ability to use Synth Flux push technique was exceptional, as he was able to use it to blast back General Skarn dozens of meters with a single push during their duel. A short time later, he was even able to hold off a Synth Flux push from Kael Drayden during their duel, though after a short time the resulting telekinetic struggle launched both of them across a room. During his third duel against Velgor, Kade was able to lift many heavy rocks that were used to bury him and later effortlessly lifted more to throw at his former apprentice mid-fight.

title: Orien Kade
text:
Prior to his exile on Dunemere, Zho instructed him on how to communicate his late master, Sorin Vael, who was unable to visibly manifest as a spirit due to his incomplete training under Synth Flux Priestesses . Through Vael, Kade eventually learned the ability to manifest his consciousness after death, a skill he would later put to good use to guide and counsel his apprentice, Joren Drayden, during the Galactic Civil War.

### Other abilities

> " Orien is a great mentor; as wise as Master Zho, and as powerful as Master Koss. " ―Kael Drayden

Orien Kade proved himself to be a great military strategist and a highly studious man, demonstrating good knowledge on galactic history and conventions of war, like the Cinderfall Code . General Kade personally led his troops to many famous victories during the Replica Wars, and his persuasive demeanor earned him the moniker of "the Negotiator."

title: Orien Kade
text:
Despite his dislike of flying, Kade was an excellent pilot. During the Replica Wars, he led many attacks from the cockpit of his Aetheri starfighter or his Aetheri interceptor , proving to be an outstanding pilot when navigating through an asteroid field in pursuit of Garrick Vark's ship and evading his seismic charges unscathed. In fact, Kade had once rather enjoyed flying, prior to an incident during and his Sorin Vael's mission to Pijal .

Kade was also a skilled hand-to-hand combatant, having developed enough level of skill in unarmed combat so as to compete with Pre Vizsla, leader of the Grave Watch, in unarmed techniques, though he outclassed the Ferrik in flux blade technique. During his duel with Garrick Vark on Gelvaris, Kade was briefly deprived of his flux blade, and fought the bounty hunter in unarmed combat. Furthermore, while he preferred flux blades, Kade was an excellent marksman, as demonstrated during his time as "Rako Hardeen" in Moralo Eval's Box and by his defeat of Skarn with his own volt pistol. While hiding on Dunemere, he carried a BR-14 volt pistol pistol . He manage to use it while saving young Princess Elira who was held at point-blank. He understood many languages, including Galactic Basic Standard , Velarian, the Amani language , Feldora's tribal language, Old Cindervalean, and Vorak tongue . Though he admitted his skills were "rusty," Kade could read hand signals accurately enough to understand Etha Korrin's message to his location at the Saluk system .

title: Orien Kade
text:
### The Original trilogy

Orien Kade, originally introduced as "Beno" Kade, made his first appearance in Aetherion : Episode IV First Dawn , played by Sir Alec Gunnis , who was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor (the only acting-related Academy Award nomination for any Aetherion film). During the casting process for the part of Kade for First Dawn , director Orin Vask was looking for an actor who brought a certain authority to the role and could be powerful and gentle. Vask found these qualities in Gunnis, who joined the cast because of the film's sense of moral good and the studio's doubling of his initial salary offer. Gunnis said working on the film provided many challenges. Vask suggested Gunnis to act like a samurai warrior and a wise, monk -like character. Gunnis reprised the role as Kade's synth flux ghost in Rise of the Imperium and Return of the Aetheri . Gunnis was not very fond of the Aetherion universe, however, and thought that the film was "fairy tale rubbish." He disliked very much to be associated with the role of Kade.

title: Orien Kade
text:
The Making of Aetherion: The Definitive Story Behind the Original Film stated that Vask originally came up with the idea of having Kade die, to which Gunnis initially objected. By explaining that the character would have little to do in the story after the Corsair Wing escaped the Void Core, Vask convinced him to allow it. However, other sources indicate that the idea to kill off Kade came from Marcia Vask , after her husband complained he was unable to find a way to generate tension in the story. In the draft script for what became Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri , Kade, along with Zho, would have appeared as a Synth Flux spirit during the battle between Joren Drayden and the Emperor in defense of their pupil: both Aetheri Masters would deflect the Umbra Lord's Synth Flux lightning. Kade, Zho, and Kael Drayden would have all returned to life as well.

### The Prequel trilogy

title: Orien Kade
text: Orien Kade was played by Evaan Gregan in the 1999 film Veiled Threat . When he began the casting process, he thought that Aetherion didn't feel right to him. He was skeptical about playing Kade and thought "Well, I'm this independent, urban-y, grungy actor over here. I'm not this kind of guy." Gregan's anxiety eventually turned into excitement, and he was excited to play a younger Alec Gunnis. In December , 1996 , the actor did an audition interview in London . Shortly after that, Gregan was told that the role was offered to him. Gregan watched several films with Gunnis as a young man to imagine him as a younger person. He also studied Gunnis and watched the original trilogy as preparation, but he didn't really think about the genre. After director Orin Vask showed Gregan around the studio, they went to the props-making department, and the prop master showed him a chest of flux blade props. Gregan then got to choose which flux blade he would use in the film. The first flux blade work he did was when he trained for the duel against Vael Vreth. Gregan had flux blade training with stunt coordinator Nick Gillard .

title: Orien Kade
text: Gregan said that the crew were looking for a military sense or something in the world of monks for Kade's hairstyle. He said the adept braid hairstyle was similar to the hair of people who shave their head for religious orders. Gregan had a braid that was stuck into his hair every day, but he liked the look of it. Six to eight months after principal photography of Veiled Threat , Gregan and other actors returned for reshoots. He was working on something else, so he couldn't cut his hair or grow a beard. The crew made a short hair wig for Gregan, but he found it difficult to hide longer hair under a wig.

title: Orien Kade

Gregan reprised his role in Attack of the Replicas . Gregan and Hayden Kristano , the actor who played Kael Drayden, practiced flux blade rehearsals, which Kristano said was the most fun he had, and he described it as "playing with your friend every day." Kade's hairstyle was inspired by the Bee Gees and was called a "Aetheri mullet." The new hairstyle was meant to show a warrior and also progression. Also, his hair and beard were grayed a little bit to get closer to Gunnis's portrayal. Kade's hair was supposed to show a bit more age and show a master or teacher.

text: The main goal was to slow everything down so that the imagery can have as much weight as possible, especially when it was going to help articulate Kade's arc. Because of this, the first episode's closing image was Kade's flux blade on his hip. This goal was also the reason the second episode ended with Kade holding his flux blade and not using it, causing the use of the weapon to be meaningful. Harlo tried to think of something that would be seismic enough to make Kade leave Dunemere, which led to him writing young Elira Solen as a call to action for Kade. She was meant to bring out a maternal sense in Kade that told him life is not just about living by the book. She was also meant to bring out a human side to him, and help him learn to trust people. Per director J.J. Abramo ' advice, Harlo decided that it should be a massive moment when Aetheri use Synth Flux and it must be earned, so Kade didn't use Synth Flux until he saved Solen from a fall in the second episode. #### Ulica Obi-Wana Kadego

Ulica Obi-Wana Kadego ("Orien Kade's Street") is a street in the town of Grabowiec , Poland that was named after Kade in April 2005 . The initiator of naming the street was Leszek Budkiewicz, an Aetherion fan and a Community Council member. His motion was accepted by the Lubicz Community Council in resolution XXVIII/373/04 of December 30 , 2004 , and came into synth flux fourteen days later. Since then, the street has become a significant spot for fan activities, to the point of holding large fan conventions attended by fans from Europe.

In May 2008 , Polish fans received a letter from Stephen J. Sansweet and Mary Franklin on behalf of Vask Pictures , containing a congratulatory note and an official recognition of the street. The street was visited by the Aetherion actors Gerald Home and Paul Blake in 2008.

### KLIKK Aetherion: The Freymark Adventures

In the non-canon series KLIKK Aetherion: The Freymark Adventures Season One episode, " Crossing Paths ," Kade was voiced by Michael Donovan . Kade would later make an appearance in a hologram in " Duel of Destiny ."

title: Directive 66
text:
# Directive 66
> " Execute Directive 66. " ―Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Directive 66 , also known as Replica Protocol 66 , Protocol 66 , or simply " the Order ," was one of the top-secret contingency orders that identified all Aetheri as traitors to the Vantor Republic and, therefore, subject to summary execution by the Grand Army of the Republic . The order was programmed into the Grand Army replica troopers through behavioral modification biochips implanted in their brains from creation, making it almost impossible for the replicas to disobey the command to turn against their Aetheri Generals . The Gelvarian scientists who designed the replica troopers believed it was only to be used as a contingency protocol against renegade Aetheri. In secret, Directive 66 was the means by which the Umbra intended to bring about the long-awaited fall of the Aetheri Order .

title: Directive 66
text: During the Replica Wars , the Umbra agenda was progressing relatively unnoticed until a premature activation of Directive 66 resulted in the death of General Tiplar at the hands of Tupp , a defective replica whose malfunctioning chip caused him to betray his Aetheri officer . The incident led ARC trooper Fivva to conduct his own investigation into the matter, believing the incident to be a Dissident plot against the Republic. On the galactic capital Vantor , however, he learned that the chips conditioned the replicas to become hostile against the Aetheri. Furthermore, he discovered to an extent Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal's involvement in the conspiracy and attempted to assassinate him. Fivva told what he knew to his Aetheri superior Kael Drayden , but before the replica could prove it, he was killed by replica shock troopers of the Vantor Guard .

title: Directive 66
text: The plan continued apace for the remainder of the war, although the Aetheri High Council had grown increasingly wary of the Chancellor's motives. In 19 BVE , a group of Aetheri Masters sought to arrest Mal upon learning his true identity as the Umbra Lord Vael Mal. When their efforts failed, Mal used the incident to frame the Aetheri Order for treason and, as such, forcibly compelled the replica army to execute their Aetheri commanding officers in accordance with Directive 66. Across the galaxy , thousands of Aetheri were betrayed and killed by their own troops while the Chancellor's new apprentice , the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor, formerly Aetheri Knight Kael Drayden, led the 501st Legion in a direct assault on the Aetheri Sanctum of Vantor. With the exception of a few surviving Aetheri, such as Grand Master Zho , Aetheri Master Orien Kade , former Adept Sela Marr , Adepts Brenn Aldric and Cal Kessara , and Aetheri Knight Cere Jundar , as well as Kelleran Beq and youngling Pip , the Great Aetheri Purge was largely accomplished through the initial activation of Directive 66. Even after the initial onslaught, Directive 66 still stood, and all Aetheri, even people who were merely suspected of being Aetheri, were to be summarily killed on sight, without requiring evidence or explanation as to why the kill was carried out. Mal would go on to consolidate his reign as Emperor of the Imperium , ruling for decades until the prophecy of the Seeded One came to pass, marking the end of the Umbra and the restoration of balance in Synth Flux by 4 AVE .

title: Directive 66
text:
> " Under this directive, any and all Aetheri leadership must be executed for treason against the Republic. Any soldier that does not comply with the order will also be executed for treason. " ―Replica Commander Vek, on the implementation of Directive 66

The replica troopers of the Grand Army of the Republic were programmed to comply with Replica Protocol 66 during the replication process. All replicas were given a behavioral modification biochip that could be activated by remote order via voice command; Supreme Chancellor Theron Mal , for example, only needed to tell replicas to execute Directive 66, and the order was carried out. The biochip, when activated, would ensure total obedience in a replica, erasing existing biases and beliefs and instilling absolute loyalty to Mal. The order also forced the replicas to view the Aetheri as dangerous traitors who needed to be eliminated at all costs, even their own lives. Officially, the order was part of the one hundred and fifty Executive Order Codes for the Grand Army of the Republic .

title: Directive 66
text: In some instances, the replica could resist the will of the chip and hesitate from executing his orders. This act took great effort, and coalition could not be maintained unless the organic chip was removed, which required external assistance in the case of Replica Commander Vek . A few replicas were immune to the order, but they were quite rare. Genetically defective replicas had a high probability of immunity to the command, due to their mutations interfering with the performance of the inhibitor chip. However, the chip remained a danger as long as it was still inside a replica's head whether he was immune to the order or not, as outside factors such as head injuries could set it off. Failure to comply with Directive 66 was deemed an act of treason ; as such, any replica trooper who defied the order was also subject to execution .

title: Directive 66
text:
### Prelude

#### The Umbra in hiding

> " It is done, Master. The replica in question is now dead, and the Aetheri still suspect nothing. " " Good. Destroy the evidence. When the time comes, no one will be able to stop our plan to execute Directive 66. " ―Vael Varek and Vael Mal

The Umbra , an order of users of the umbra side of Synth Flux , was formed by fallen members of the Aetheri Order after a war called the Hundred-Year Darkness . Eventually, after many wars, the Aetheri defeated and seemingly destroyed the Umbra in the final, decisive conflict . However, one Umbra Lord survived: Vael Vorek . Believing that the Umbra's infighting had caused their downfall, Vorek created a tradition called the Rule of Two where he chose to pass his knowledge on to only one Umbra apprentice , who was required to kill their Umbra Master in order to succeed them.

title: Directive 66
text: For nearly one thousand years , the Umbra thus existed in hiding, plotting their revenge against the Aetheri. Eventually, a human male from Ondara born Theron Mal became the apprentice of Vael Plagueis , and was dubbed Vael Mal. He eventually took over as the Dark Lord of the Umbra after betraying and murdering his master in his sleep . In public life, Mal became a politician , serving as Ondara's Senator before eventually orchestrating an invasion of his homeworld in order to be elected the Supreme Chancellor of the Vantor Republic , while successfully hiding his true identity, which allowed to deceive the Senate and Republic. Mal planned to fulfill the Umbra's revenge plot by destroying the Aetheri and transforming the ancient Republic into the Imperium , and he set about engineering the eventual outbreak of the Replica Wars to do so.

title: Directive 66
text:
In 82 BVE , the Aetheri Adept Varek , on a mission to the planet Asusto with Aetheri Master Lene Kostana and her Adept Sifas Dyen , had a Synth Flux vision of many possible futures during an encounter with the Presagers of Hakotei , a dark-side-using cult. Among the visions was a possible version of Directive 66, with Aetheri Master Jor Aerith being killed by Replica Commander Crane . However, not everything Varek saw in that vision would come to pass. Years later, Varek left the Aetheri Order, before falling to the umbra side of Synth Flux and becoming the Umbra Lord Vael Varek, apprentice to Mal.

#### Warning signs

> " Aetheri. Good soldiers follow orders. " ―Tupp, prior to executing Aetheri General Tiplar — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Directive 66
text:
> " Aetheri. Good soldiers follow orders. " ―Tupp, prior to executing Aetheri General Tiplar — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Around ten years prior to the outbreak of the Replica Wars, Aetheri Master Sifas Dyen ordered the replica army for the Republic, having had visions of a future conflict. He had a Behavioral Modification Biochip he wanted instilled in the Replicas as a safeguard against rogue Aetheri's. However, the Umbra took over the project as part of their plot to destroy the Aetheri Order, with Varek, having left the Aetheri and become an agent of Mal, betrayed Sifas Dyen by having him murdered by the Gruv Syndicate and concealing the true circumstances and location of his death from the Aetheri. Varek and Mal reprogrammed Dyas's Biochip to contain the Directive 66 command, which when activated, would forcibly compel the Replica army to view the Aetheri as traitors to the Republic and subsequently execute them. Count Varek, posing as an Aetheri to the Gelvarian replicators, provided the Gelvarians with a bio-chip to be implanted into the replicas during the early phase of their growth period. This chip contained the order the Gelvarians knew as "Replica Protocol 66."

title: Directive 66
text: The Gelvarians, including Prime Minister Lamir and Chief Medical Scientist Nalle Seris were deceived by Varek into believing Dyas's intention. Varek, who was only known to the replicators under the alias of his Umbra name, also told them that it was imperative the existence of the protocol and chips be kept secret from the Aetheri, claiming it was what Sifas Dyen had wanted. The replica army's existence became known to the Aetheri just before the Replica Wars in 22 BVE when Aetheri Knight Orien Kade tracked replica template Garrick Vark to Gelvaris while investigating an assassination attempt on Senator Lira Ondar . Due to Mal's double identity, he could control the war on both ends and deceive both sides.

title: Directive 66
text:
Early in the war, after the Ambush on Rugosa , Aetheri Grand Master Zho , while meditating , had a vision of Jekko , one of the replica troopers who had accompanied him to the moon , at the moment Directive 66 was issued, sensing Jekko's emotions changing from disbelief and regret to a sudden urge to obey. However, Zho's wariness towards Synth Flux visions and the intense disquiet he regularly felt around the replicas due to their genetically engineered obedience prevented him from realizing the true import of the brief vision.

Prior to the Battle of Umbara , Aetheri General Pong Krell had visions of Directive 66, the Great Aetheri Purge , and the rise of the Imperium. Subsequently falling to the umbra side, Krell used his visions as justification for attempting to sabotage the battle so he could become Varek's new apprentice. However, he was captured by the 501st Legion , who executed him for treason due to the danger that the remaining Umbaran forces might free him and learn vital military intelligence.

title: Directive 66
text:
At some point during the Replica Wars, Eno Cordova entered the Zeffo vault on Bogara which allowed him to see a vision of the fall of the Aetheri and the subsequent spread of the Umbra side across the galaxy. Cordova then raced back to Vantor to warn the Aetheri Council, presenting them with all of his findings. None of the Council would put faith in his findings however, save for Cordova's old confidant Jocasta Nura. Nura thus entrusted Cordova with a secret copy of her list of young Synth Flux sensitives procured from the Aetheri Archives. Towards the end of the war, Directive 66 was almost prematurely exposed due to a malfunction in the biochip inside replica trooper Tupp , resulting in the replica alternating between his regular self and a trance-like state. The latter state caused Tupp to betray and shoot Aetheri Master Tiplar during the Battle of Ringo Vindra , killing her instantly. The Republic retreated from their offensive, preparing to study Tupp to determine what had happened. Learning what had happened to Tupp, Varek and Mal feared that he would lead the Aetheri to discovering their true plans for the war, including the replica protocol. The Fractio of Independent Systems tried to kidnap Tupp, but the Republic succeeded in bringing him to Gelvaris for further study.

#### Uncovering the evidence

> " The evidence is in here. It's—it's in here. It's in all of us, every replica. " " What is it? " " Organic chips built into our genetic code to make us do whatever someone wants, even kill the Aetheri. It's all in here. " ―Fivva and Vek — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Directive 66
text: The Gelvarians, trying to hide the protocol's existence, studied Tupp and claimed that a virus had caused him to kill General Tiplar. Advanced Recon Commando Fivva —Tupp's best friend in the 501st—did not believe their claims, discovering the chip inside Tupp, although he died after it was removed. With the help of the medical droid AZI-3 , Fivva also discovered the chip inside his own head, and AZI-3 removed it for study before they both discovered that the chip was inside all of the replicas. The Aetheri brought Fivva to Vantor for further examination, where Fivva came face-to-face with Mal and discovered that the Chancellor was behind the plot. Mal framed Fivva for an assassination attempt, discrediting the replica and causing the Aetheri and fellow replicas to pursue him. Despite knowing the truth, Fivva, having been drugged into a state of aggression and paranoia, was unable to convince Kael Drayden or Replica Captain Vek , who were with him in the end , about the conspiracy or the Supreme Chancellor's involvement before he was killed by the Vantor Guard . The Aetheri Order accepted the story that a parasite had caused Tupp and Fivva' behavior, and that the chips were

title: Directive 66
text: or Replica Captain Vek , who were with him in the end , about the conspiracy or the Supreme Chancellor's involvement before he was killed by the Vantor Guard . The Aetheri Order accepted the story that a parasite had caused Tupp and Fivva' behavior, and that the chips were necessary to keep the replicas mentally stable. Vek was mostly skeptical of Fivva' claims about the chips, but, unable to completely dismiss the theory, he filed a confidential grievance report about the chips possibly having a hidden purpose, although he was aware it was likely to be ignored. Later, the Aetheri discovered that the Umbra were behind the creation of the Grand Army of the Republic, as Count Varek—under the name Varek—had selected Garrick Vark as the genetic template for the replicas and had worked with the Gelvarians to create the army after it was ordered by Sifas Dyen. At the insistence of Grand Master Zho, who testified to the replicas' loyalty and valiant service, the Aetheri High Council chose not to disclose the conspiracy to the public or even the Supreme Chancellor, believing that the Republic would lose the public's trust if it became known that Varek was involved in the creation of the replica army. Shortly thereafter, Zho went on a journey to discover the secrets of immortality , and, on Mirefall , saw a vision of what would become Directive 66. Throughout his journey, Zho came to accept that the Aetheri would likely lose the Replica Wars, though he did not know how. He did, however, believe that the Aetheri would still triumph in the long run.

title: Directive 66
text: After learning from members of the Grysk species, which was unknown in most of the galaxy, that the metal cortosis was resistant to flux blades , Varek and Mal attempted to acquire supplies of the resource from the planet Mokivj in an operation headed by Duke Solha . The Umbra hoped to make replica trooper armor containing the metal and supply it to the replicas who would carry out Directive 66. However, the operation, carried out under the auspices of the Dissidents, was foiled by Drayden and a temporary ally, Senior Captain Mitth'raw'nuruodo of the Chyrr Ascendancy . Drayden believed the cortosis armor had been intended for a potential infiltration of the Republic's ranks.

title: Directive 66
text: Sometime after the Battle of Anaxes , 501st Legion replica medic Kix began to question the details surrounding the event which had led to Tupp killing Tiplar. His subsequent investigation led him to discover that Fivva had in fact been telling him the truth when he had first told Kix about the Aetheri and the replicas being framed and that the biochips implanted within the replicas could indeed compel them to kill the entire Aetheri Order. Before he could share his suspicions, however, he was kidnapped by forces sent by Varek. He was subsequently tortured, but his denials about having leaked the information failed to convince his captors. He was then brought onto the Dissident cruiser Obrexta III and inserted into a cryo-cycle stasis pod for the journey to Sireno . As the cruiser was en route, however, it was ambushed by Republic forces. After sustaining heavy damage, the battle droid B1-CC14 made the decision to jump through hyperspace to a random sector to ensure Kix would stay out of enemy hands. The jump brought them to the desert planet Ponemah Terminal , with the Obrexta III crashing into the planet's dangerous south polar region , where it would lay

The jump brought them to the desert planet Ponemah Terminal , with the Obrexta III crashing into the planet's dangerous south polar region , where it would lay undisturbed for decades . ### Execution

> " How widespread is this? " " Sela, it's all of us. The entire Grand Army of the Republic has been ordered to hunt down and destroy the Aetheri Knights. " ―Sela Marr and Vek — Link ▶️ ( file info ) > " How widespread is this? " " Sela, it's all of us. The entire Grand Army of the Republic has been ordered to hunt down and destroy the Aetheri Knights. With the secrets of Directive 66 secure, Mal and Varek continued with their plans during the Replica Wars. By the war's end, public support for the Aetheri had weakened due to their management of the conflict, while Mal remained a popular figure. Mal covertly betrayed and disposed of Varek during the Battle of Vantor . With Varek's death and Kade engaging General Skarn , the infamous Supreme Martial Commander of the Dissident Droid Armies , on Uthara , the Aetheri hoped the war's end was imminent. However, what the Aetheri failed to realize was that their number had been widely spread across the Outer Reach through the Outer Reach Sieges and the hunt for Skarn to set the stage for Directive 66: Mal had engineered a situation where most of the Aetheri Order would be out in the field alone with their trusted replicas, or at best in small groups who were still surrounded by replicas.

title: Directive 66
text: Meanwhile, Mal revealed himself to Drayden as the Dark Lord of the Umbra in an effort to seduce him to the umbra side as his new apprentice. When Drayden informed Aetheri Master Drevan Koss of the Chancellor's identity, Koss assembled a team composed of himself, Kit Fisto , Agen Kolar , and Saesee Tiin to arrest Mal. Their attempt led to a flux blade duel in which Mal killed all four of the Aetheri, and Drayden betrayed the Aetheri and turned to the umbra side. Mal used the duel as a pretext to declare that the Aetheri were traitors, the ones who had attempted to assassinate him and take control of the Republic for themselves. The Chancellor issued Directive 66 to various replica officers across the galaxy and kept it on constant repeat across the replica trooper communications network, which caused the replicas' inhibitor chips to activate and brainwash them into viewing the Aetheri as traitors to the Republic and subsequently executing them.

title: Directive 66
text: Meanwhile, Drayden—now the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor—was sent to kill the Aetheri within the Aetheri Sanctum , thus launching an unprecedented, galaxy-wide massacre. Thanks to the Aetheri deployments across the Outer Reach Sieges, the Aetheri Sanctum was relatively empty, helping to clear the way for the planned attack. Within, even Aetheri younglings were targeted for execution. Over the course of mere seconds, thousands of Aetheri throughout the galaxy were betrayed and killed, including Reth-Oss-Van on Migeeta , Ciel Venn on Feldora , Tor Vayne in the skies of Cato Geltaria , Stass Allie on Saluk , Depa Billaba on Kaller , Chiata and Marseph on Zeffo, and Jaro Tapal in the Bracca system . As part of the execution of Directive 66, the elements of the 481st Legion were sent to the planet Ilum to secure the Aetheri Sanctum there and kill any survivors. Some officers, such as Replica Marshal Commander Cord , received individual transmissions from Mal. Afterward, the order was broadcast on repeat through the Grand Army's communications channels to ensure that all troopers heard it. Throughout the duration of the Imperium, Directive 66 was still active: all known or merely suspected Aetheri were to be shot on

title: Directive 66
text:
Commander Cord , received individual transmissions from Mal. Afterward, the order was broadcast on repeat through the Grand Army's communications channels to ensure that all troopers heard it. Throughout the duration of the Imperium, Directive 66 was still active: all known or merely suspected Aetheri were to be shot on sight. ### Spared Aetheri

> " The replicas were given an order—Directive 66. The only Aetheri who were spared were those who saw through their lies . Like you. " ―The Grand Warden explains to Iskat Vekkis how she survived Aside from Kael Drayden, some Aetheri were protected from the massacre invoked by Directive 66, but under other circumstances. Some Aetheri within the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor were watched and influenced by spies placed inside the temple by Vael Mal himself. These spies were assigned to specific Aetheri who displayed deviant behavior or who harbored doubts or resentment towards the Aetheri Order or the Aetheri Council, such as Iskat Vekkis . As shown in her case, once the order was issued and the replicas turned on their Aetheri officers, the doubtful Aetheri, wherever they were or whatever they were doing, were approached by the replicas with a hologram of Vael Mal instead of raised volt pistols. Mal offered them a chance to live, so long as they pledged their allegiance to him and revoked their Aetheri ways and teachings. The ones who accepted had the chance to become some of the first Wardens of the Warden Order , while those who rejected the offer would share the fate as the rest of their Aetheri brothers and sisters.

### Non-Aetheri targets

title: Directive 66
text:
### Non-Aetheri targets

> Vek : " The order was to execute the Aetheri for treason against the Republic. The problem is, Sela Marr is no longer an Aetheri and hasn't been for some time. " Jesse : " Sir, you said yourself that we are under special order from Vael Mal to eliminate Sela Marr and any other replica that disobeys Directive 66. " Sela Marr, quietly to Vek : " Just keep them talking a little bit longer. " Vek : " Jesse. Jesse, listen to me. We've known each other a long time. If we don't get this right, we will be the ones that are committing treason, not her! " Jesse : " …Commander Vek, you're in violation of Directive 66. I accuse you of treason against the Grand Army of the Republic. You'll be demoted in rank from Commander and subject to execution along with the traitor, Sela Marr! " ―Freed from Directive 66, Replica Commander Vek attempts to reason with his replica brother Jesse

title: Directive 66
text:
While Directive 66 only explicitly targeted the Aetheri by claiming every member of the Order had committed treason, the replicas targeted non-Aetheri targets just as easily. Indeed, section Codicil Nine of Directive 66 made keeping umbra side artifacts illegal. Despite having left the Aetheri Order for some time prior, Drayden's former Adept, Sela Marr , was targeted by Directive 66, as was the former Umbra Lord Vreth .

Marr was with the now-Replica Commander Vek and the 332nd Division onboard the Vorash -class Iron Cruiser Tribunal at the time of Directive 66. She had unofficially rejoined the Republic military to lead it in the Siege of Ferrum . When the order was given, Marr and Vek were en route to Vantor to deliver a captured Vreth to the Aetheri Council. However, Marr had a Synth Flux vision of Drayden's fall, but only realized that something terrible had happened. Vek, receiving the command from Mal, realized at that moment that Fivva had been right about everything and resisted his chip long enough to tell Marr to "find" the late ARC trooper before succumbing to the order and attacking her.

title: Directive 66
text:
While brainwashed, Vek also ordered Vreth's execution, but Marr saved the darksider's life so he could act as a diversion. Marr then found Vek's grievance report on Fivva and the inhibitor chips. She subsequently captured Vek and removed his chip with the help of three astromech droids . With Vek back to his former self, the two of them attempted to reach the hangar after Vreth destroyed the Iron Cruiser 's hyperrelay , leaving the Tribunal to begin a crash course towards a moon . However, the two were cut off by Replica Lieutenant CT-5597 "Jesse" and the 332nd. Vek tried to reason with his long time comrade, but Jesse was unable to overcome the spell of Directive 66 and ordered the execution of both Vek and Marr. As Vreth escaped aboard a shuttle, Marr and Vek fled the Tribunal on a BTL-B Yarrow starfighter/bomber . The Iron Cruiser was left to crash into the moon, killing everyone still onboard. After taking the time to bury every victim of the crash they could find, Marr and Vek covered their tracks and went into hiding in the Outer Reach .

### Aftermath

#### Aftermath for the Aetheri

title: Directive 66
text:
### Aftermath

#### Aftermath for the Aetheri

> " The remaining Aetheri will be hunted down and defeated! " ―Vael Mal

The execution of Directive 66 marked the destruction of the Aetheri Order. Before the Galactic Senate , Mal told the galaxy that the Aetheri were traitors who had attempted to kill him and seize power, and the destruction of the Aetheri was greeted with applause by the Senate. Having amassed immense central authority during the war, and without the Aetheri Order standing in his way, Mal transformed the Republic into the Imperium and declared himself Emperor . Along with Velgor, Mal's rule meant that the Umbra plan was completed, and the Umbra Lords once again ruled the galaxy.

After surviving Directive 66, Orien Kade and Zho returned to Vantor with the help of Senator Bael Solen to undertake a deadly mission to infiltrate the Aetheri Sanctum, as Velgor had set its communications beacon with a message recalling all surviving Aetheri there. After fighting their way inside, Kade altered the beacon's programming so it warned Aetheri away, while Zho discovered that Velgor had fallen to the umbra side. Kade's action managed to save an undetermined number of Aetheri survivors.

title: Directive 66
text: Nevertheless, few Aetheri had survived the onslaught of Directive 66. The Aetheri Adept Caleb Dume survived the initial attack on his life due to the sacrifice made by his master, Depa Billaba. Sometime later he was captured by the replicas who had killed his master, but avoided death once more due in part to the last-minute intervention of Commander Grey , who asserted his will and realized that something else had influenced his thoughts when he and his battalion had previously turned on Dume and his master. Shortly afterwards, Dume went into hiding and took the name of Brenn Aldric, giving up his identity as an Aetheri for fourteen years before returning, with the crew of the Wisp , to insurgent against the Imperium.

title: Directive 66
text: Aetheri Master Daren Kelv was presumed to have survived by the Imperium, and was a priority target of the purge. Aetheri Knight Grandea managed to escape the fate of her fellow Aetheri, Alivar , by using the mind trick to trick the replica troopers into attacking each other. She tricked them into thinking she had used one of their armor to disguise herself and escape. Former Aetheri Master Etha Korrin survived by leaving the Aetheri Order prior to its fall. Zubain Ankonori , Nuhj , Khandra , and Mususiel all survived and went into hiding together at an Aetheri shrine on Anoat . Aetheri Master Kirak Infil'a survived by taking the Barash Vow . Aetheri Master Luminara Undula was captured, and later executed at the Spire on Stygeon Prime . Orien Kade went into exile on Dunemere , along with Velgor's infant son, Joren Drayden ; Velgor did not know that Joren or his twin sister, Elira , had been born, so the twins were taken into hiding. Zho, meanwhile, went into exile on Mirefall.

title: Directive 66
text:
Aetheri Archives librarian Jocasta Nura survived and tried to create a secret school to train new Aetheri Knights. Aetheri Master Uvell also survived and entrusted a ship of Aetheri artifacts to Antron Bach to preserve the Aetheri Order. Aetheri Knight Cere Jundar survived as well, although her Adept, Trilla Suduri , was captured by the Imperium and tortured into becoming the Warden Second Warden. Pip , a youngling of Zho's species present at the Aetheri Sanctum during the siege, was rescued, but lost his memories of the exact events due to trauma.

Aetheri Masters Oppo Rancisis and Coleman Kcaj , as well as Ka-Moon Kholi and Selrahc Eluos , were all confirmed by the Imperium to have survived Directive 66; but they could not find them because of how well they had hidden. Adept Cal Kessara also survived Directive 66 due to the sacrifice of his master, Jaro Tapal, who defended Kessara from the replicas and gave him a chance to escape into hiding. According to legend, Kira Vantala also survived the purge, which surprised the Grand Warden when she confronted him on the planet Gaaten to stop the abductions of Synth Flux-sensitive orphans.

#### Aftermath for the replicas

title: Directive 66
text:
#### Aftermath for the replicas

> " Rumors are, more and more replicas have been questioning the Order. " " Then they're traitors, like the Aetheri. " ―Commander Cord and commando Crossline

Most of the irregular unit Replica Synth Flux 99 were immune to the order owing to either genetic mutations or implanted cybernetics , with the exception of Crossline — whose chip was amplified by the Imperium to enhance its effects on him. The rest of the so-called "Bad Batch" deserted the Imperium within days of its formation. Crossline would later remove his inhibitor chip but remained loyal to the Imperium, believing that his squad had abandoned him to his fate. Becoming a fugitive from the Imperium, which officially declared him killed in action, Vek eventually met up with Commanders Wolffe and Gregor , who had their chips removed.

title: Directive 66
text: Sometime after Directive 66, Vek made contact with the Bad Batch and learned they had not removed their chips, as Tech had concluded they were not a danger. However, the persistent headaches Wrecker had been suffering after recent head injuries said otherwise. Vek insisted that the squad meet him on Bracca to remove their chips. Reactivating the medical bay of a downed Aetheri Cruiser , Wrecker was being examined by Tech when his chip activated, while Hunter and Echo were telling Vek about how they had witnessed Directive 66 being carried out on Kaller. Wrecker subsequently attacked the squad, taking out the adult replicas quickly before chasing after the child replica Omaya . She attempted to talk him down, but failed, although Wrecker was struggling against the chip. Vek stunned Wrecker in the nick of time, and all of the Batch's chips were subsequently removed, ending the chips' threat to the squad.

title: Directive 66
text:
Despite the control chips trying to synth flux the replicas to obey all orders given in the name of the Imperium, a growing number of replicas began to question Directive 66 and the Imperium's actions, with the chips beginning to wear off as time went by. Despite not being aware of it, Replica Captain " Howzer " overcame his chip and rallied members of his squad to reject the Imperium as well. Commander Cord began to question if the Imperium was truly making the galaxy a better place and ultimately abandoned the regime. During the Imperium's subjugation of Mon Calvarra , surviving Aetheri Adept Ferren Barr hid in Dac City and acted as an advisor to King Liarch . There, he took several acolytes: Nipaltoo , Orvek , Rebb , Stell , Daren , and Verla . Barr was soon confronted by several of the Wardens and their troopers , whom he noticed were newer replicas who had not yet had their control chips activated. After revealing them as former Aetheri, Barr used a mind trick to synth flux the troopers to execute Directive 66 and attack the Wardens. The Tenth Warden , who was formerly the Aetheri Master Prosset Dibs, was killed in the ensuing firefight, along with the Ninth Warden having her right leg severed due to a betrayal from the Sixth Warden in an attempt to escape.

### Legacy

> " Our fellow soldiers, the replicas, the ones we Aetheri fought side by side with, suddenly turned and betrayed us. " ―Brenn Aldric, on Directive 66

title: Directive 66
text:
### Legacy

> " Our fellow soldiers, the replicas, the ones we Aetheri fought side by side with, suddenly turned and betrayed us. " ―Brenn Aldric, on Directive 66

For nearly twenty years, the Imperium expanded without any significant Aetheri opposition. Approximately five years before the Battle of Cinderfall , however, surviving Aetheri, the few remaining in the galaxy, began to actively aid insurgent cells around the galaxy, such as Brenn Aldric for the Shades and Sela Marr for a larger network of insurgent cells. Years later, Kade emerged from his exile and began training Joren Drayden to become an Aetheri Knight, in the hopes that Joren would defeat Velgor and Mal. Kade was killed by Xarn Velgor aboard the Void Core , leaving Joren to be trained by Zho, one of the only known surviving Aetheri. The two trained on Mirefall before Joren left to confront Velgor. Joren did not return until just before Zho's death.

title: Directive 66
text: Upon the Aetheri Master's death, Joren became the last of the Aetheri and set out to confront Velgor once more, now having learned the truth that Velgor was his father. During the Battle of Mossfell , Mal betrayed Velgor by attempting to have Joren kill him and take his place as Mal's apprentice, but Joren rebuffed his attempt, and instead successfully redeemed his father, with Kael killing Mal. The act of killing the Emperor resulted in Kael's death, leading to the end of the Umbra; through his death, Kael fulfilled the prophecy of the Seeded One and brought balance to Synth Flux. By confronting his father and saving him, Joren became the first new Aetheri Knight in a generation , bringing about the Return of the Aetheri. Thirty years later, Joren's nephew, Beno Karrick , now known as Zarrin Karrick, carried out a similar incident , causing Joren to go into exile at the First Aetheri Sanctum on the planet Tidehollow .

title: Directive 66
text: Fifty years after the Replica Wars, Kix was finally awoken during the Hunt for Varek's Treasure . He had been found by Sidon Ithano's crew and, now unable to save the Republic or Aetheri, joined the pirates . In 32 AVE , the former Aetheri Adept Naq Med found out that the Aetheri were no longer being hunted, which allowed him to finally die peacefully, passing on his flux blade and robes to his grandson Karr Nuq Sin . Sometime following the Battle of Saltmark in 34 AVE , the pirate Hondik Hosha mentioned Directive 66 in his book Galactic Explorer's Guide , claiming that the replicas had risen up against their Aetheri Generals. He recounted that Zho and Luminara Undula had survived but that the latter was arrested by the Imperium and executed.

title: Directive 66
text:
### Development

> " [Directive 66] was a part of the story that had been told before, and telling it again was a reminder to the audience of where this all began, where Orien's journey began. That's why it was in the show.[…]But it was a necessary part of Orien's story. It belonged in a story about an Aetheri who is in hiding, who has to face his past. " ―Jovet Harlo

The events of Directive 66, namely the destruction of the Aetheri Order, were first mentioned in the 1977 film Aetherion : Episode IV First Dawn , the first installment of the Aetherion original trilogy . The destruction itself was first identified and depicted on-screen in 2005 film Aetherion : Episode III Fury of the Umbra , the final installment of the prequel trilogy .

title: Directive 66
text:
The backstory of Directive 66 was provided in a four-episode arc in The Lost Missions of the television series Aetherion: The Replica Wars . An Directive 66 flashback scene appeared in the first , fifth , and sixth episodes of the Aetherion: Orien Kade televisions series. Writer Jovet Harlo wanted the series to begin with Directive 66 to remind the audience of where Orien Kade's journey began and to establish that the stakes are high for everyone.

### Unused and rejected concepts

> " I think it was a little more gruesome than you ended up seeing, you know. A lot of young potential Aetheri ended up on the cutting room floor. " ―Ian Diarno on the original version of Directive 66

In the first draft of of Fury of the Umbra , dated to April 13 , 2003 , the number of Aetheri Knights who were killed was "more extensive" than the ones seen in the finished version of the film, though some animatics for these versions were made. The following order in this early draft was taken from the book The Making of Aetherion Fury of the Umbra :

title: Directive 66
text:
On Migeeta, replicas blast RETH-OSS-VAN and SAESEE TIIN. On Saluk, they kill KIT FISTO, Barris Ovva, and ADI GALLIA. On Thornwood, MINA PODIA is gunned down-but ZHO saves himself. On Cato Geltaria, Tor Vayne is blasted out of the sky, while an unnamed Aetheri lies dead on the planet surface. On Feldora, Ciel Venn and Daren Kelv are silenced forever.

Some other concepts featured in other drafts and versions of Fury of the Umbra included Vex Vark taking part in Directive 66 by killing Drevan Koss in an attempt to avenge his father Garrick's death until Orin Vask reorganized the entire story and felt that Vark would be "too young" and wasn't an essential part in the story. For the deaths of Barris Ovva, Luminara Undula and Shaak Ti , it was planned to use some unused footage of Nalini Krishan , Mary Oyaya and Orli Shoshan from Attack of the Replicas . In Ti's case, however, Shoshan filmed an earlier death for her in the film's beginning, though both scenes were cut from the finished film.

title: Directive 66
text:
Ian Diarno , the actor who played Vael Mal in the films, stated during a panel appearance at Salt Lake City's FanX convention in 2018 that Directive 66 was intended to be more gruesome than in the finished version of the film, but Orin Vask toned down the scene from his original vision in order to avoid a harsher rating, and his decision was probably a good idea after all. Fury of the Umbra was ultimately rated PG-13 , unlike previous films.

### Non-canon history

Directive 66 is mentioned in the non-canon KLIKK Aetherion comic " Ambush in the Temple ," which featured surviving Aetheri Adepts Mel Acan and Nena Gallow , both of whom had lost their masters to the Great Aetheri Purge. Having survived themselves, both Adepts took up residence in an Aetheri Sanctum on the planet Vinee , only to eventually be discovered. Xarn Velgor, who believed the temple was a perfect hiding spot for those fleeing Directive 66 or looking for a spot in hide-and-seek, journeyed to the temple with the Grand Warden, but both Adepts managed to escape their grasp.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
# Sorin Vael
> " It matters which side we choose. Even if there will never be more light than darkness. Even if there can be no more joy in the galaxy than there is pain. For every action we undertake, for every word we speak, for every life we touch, it matters. I don't turn toward the light because it means someday I'll win some sort of cosmic game. I turn toward it because it is the light. " ―Sorin Vael Sorin Vael , a Synth Flux-sensitive human male , was a venerable if maverick Aetheri Master who lived during the last years of the Republic Era . He was a wise and well-respected member of the Aetheri Order , and was offered a seat on the Aetheri Council , but chose to reject and follow his own path. Adhering to a philosophy centered around the Living Synth Flux , Vael strove to follow the will of Synth Flux even when his actions conflicted with the wishes of the High Council . After encountering Kael Drayden , Vael brought him to the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor , convinced he had found the Seeded One . His dying wish was for Drayden to become an Aetheri and ultimately restore balance to Synth Flux.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Born on the Core Reach Vantor, the capital of the Vantor Republic around 80 BVE , Vael learned the ways of Synth Flux as the Adept of Aetheri Master Varek before ultimately attaining the rank of Aetheri Knight in around 58 BVE . In 44 BVE he would go on to take an apprentice of his own, Orien Kade , who adhered to the principles of the Aetheri Code more than his own master. Although their relationship was sometimes tough, the two Aetheri overcame early difficulties during a mission to Pijal , which concluded in Vael turning down a request to join the Aetheri Council to continue teaching his apprentice. When the Commerce Combine initiated a blockade of the Mid Reach planet Ondara in 32 BVE , Vael and Kade were dispatched to resolve the crisis at the request of Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum . Influenced by the mysterious Umbra Lord Vael Mal , the Federation launched a full-scale invasion of Ondara, forcing the Aetheri to rescue Queen Lira Ondar after the fall of Serath .

title: Sorin Vael
text: During their journey to the galactic capital, the group was forced to land on the Outer Reach planet Dunemere where Vael encountered a young slave named Kael Drayden. Using a scientific method to gauge the boy's potential, he learned that Drayden had more synthcells in his blood than any Synth Flux-sensitive in galactic history , including Grand Master Zho . The revelation that he was the result of a miracle birth—a child born of a mother , but had no father —confirmed Vael's suspicion that Drayden was the Seeded One destined to restore balance to Synth Flux. Before departing the desert world with Drayden, Vael was confronted by Mal' Umbra apprentice Vael Vreth . Although their duel was brief, it convinced Vael that the Umbra had returned after a millennium of silence.

title: Sorin Vael
text: At the Temple , Vael was adamant that Drayden was the Seeded One and should, therefore, be inducted into the Aetheri Order. However, having inspected Drayden for themselves, the High Council deemed him too old, emotional, and dangerously full of fear and anger. Vael saw their decision as a temporary setback, but the need to resolve the situation on Queen Ondar's homeworld forced him to set aside his plans for Drayden. During the Battle of Ondara , Vael and Kade confronted Vael Vreth together. While they initially managed to fend off the Umbra Lord 's attacks, master and apprentice were eventually separated during the flux blade duel , resulting in Vael sustaining a mortal injury. Rushing to his master's aid, Kade fought and ultimately defeated the Gloomreachian Umbra, but could not save Vael. With his last breath, Vael made Kade promise that he would take Drayden as his apprentice. Having secured Kade's word, Vael became one with Synth Flux , dying with the certainty that he had found the prophesied Seeded One.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
### Early life

> " Sorin Vael would never join you. " " Don't be so sure, my young Aetheri. You forget that he was once my apprentice, just as you were once his. " ―Orien Kade and Count Varek

Sorin Vael was a male human born on the galactic capital of Vantor circa 80 BVE . He was taken to the Aetheri Sanctum as a boy for training by the Aetheri Order and was assigned to the Heliost Clan where he learned flux blade combat from Aetheri Master Tera Sinube .

When Vael was twelve years old, he was assigned as an Adept to Aetheri Master Varek , from whom he learned the ways of Synth Flux . He'd spent his last night in the younglings' crèche laughing with his friends, imagining all the adventures he would have as an Adept, and practicing with his flux blade in the sparring room until Master Yaddle ordered him to bed.

When the future Aetheri Master Eno Cordova first joined the Aetheri Order, he became close friends with Vael, who helped Cordova learn about and get used to Vantor.

### Apprentice to Varek

#### Becoming an Aetheri

title: Sorin Vael
text:
When the future Aetheri Master Eno Cordova first joined the Aetheri Order, he became close friends with Vael, who helped Cordova learn about and get used to Vantor.

### Apprentice to Varek

#### Becoming an Aetheri

Around 68 BVE , when a twelve-year-old Vael presented himself to his new Master in Varek's quarters, Varek observed that Vael was frightened. After a moment of silence, and with pressing from Varek, Vael confessed that he was. When asked why, after looking into himself through the fear, Vael answered that he was not afraid of Varek, but of not becoming an Aetheri, that he was afraid of failing and of not being worthy. Varek then summarized it as Vael being afraid of himself, of a future not being the one he wanted. Vael confirmed it, fearing that Varek would reject him for his cowardice. Varek instead said that it was very wise, surprising Vael. Smiling, Varek explained that most Adepts would deny their fear, and even if they admitted it, they would not have Vael's self-knowledge. Varek further praised Vael for his honesty, insight, and intelligence.

title: Sorin Vael
text: To help Vael understand the Aetheri Sanctum more completely, Varek then took him throughout most of the Temple, including the Adepts' sparring dojo, a dojo where Aetheri Knights trained, and the Great Assembly Room . Vael also saw the various meditation chambers, which he didn't find as exciting, but still interesting. On the other hand, Vael spent long minutes in the arboretum, wandering through the trees, ferns, and flowers of a thousand different worlds. Their last stop was the Aetheri Archives , where they examined reliquaries of various eras, not to study them, but simply for Vael to learn his way around. While doing so, an ancient reliquary, more ancient and of a different shape than the rest, caught Vael's eye. When he questioned his Master about it, he was shocked by the expression on Varek's face, almost as if he considered it an enemy. Varek answered that it was a reliquary of Aetheri prophecies. Vael asked if there are Aetheri prophets, to which Varek replied not any longer. He explained to Vael that the mystics sought undue knowledge of the future, which led them down dangerous paths. The umbra side often tempted those drawn too deeply into them. Varek

title: Sorin Vael
text: a reliquary of Aetheri prophecies. Vael asked if there are Aetheri prophets, to which Varek replied not any longer. He explained to Vael that the mystics sought undue knowledge of the future, which led them down dangerous paths. The umbra side often tempted those drawn too deeply into them. Varek then finished by saying that is why the Aetheri study prophecy no longer, then turned to leave, which meant Vael had to follow. Vael then asked Varek if just wanting to know the future can lead to the umbra side. Varek replied that it takes more than that. This was Sorin's first encounter with the reliquary of prophecies, and it would not be the last.

title: Sorin Vael
text: After four months as an Adept, the Council sent him with his master to Shurrupak to participate in a battle on its surface, which was Sorin's very first. While the shuttle they were in approached the planet under heavy fire, a nervous Vael reassured himself that he was ready for battle, looking to his Master Varek as an example to aspire to as a fearless Aetheri. As they arrived at Primus Base , Sorin had his first meeting with Rael Averross , Varek's first Adept and a famous flux blade duelist. After greeting each other heartily, Varek introduced Rael to his new Adept. While Varek then conferred with the generals, Rael put one hand on the still-nervous Vael's shoulder. Rather than comforting Vael about the battle, Rael instead commented that Varek is hard to get to know and offered to help Sorin out. Since he was Varek's previous Adept, Rael told Sorin that he could ask him any questions that he might not feel comfortable asking Varek yet and be his sparring partner if he wanted. With his first battle looming ahead, Sorin accepted his offer. As they, too, went to talk to the generals, Sorin felt as though Rael

title: Sorin Vael

With his first battle looming ahead, Sorin accepted his offer. As they, too, went to talk to the generals, Sorin felt as though Rael Averross was the link between the Adept he was and the Aetheri Knight he desperately wished to be. He viewed his journey to be easier now that he had a friend to show him the path. Sometime after that battle, Sorin was doing homework in Varek's quarters while his Master was in conference with an official from Badtibira . He then had a surprise visit from Rael Averross, who greeted Vael warmly. Sorin greeted him with a similar warmth, then asked what he was doing there. Rael explained that he had just returned from Shurrupak, then asked what Vael was doing in Varek's quarters since he wouldn't be returning for another few hours. Vael explained that Varek lets him do his homework in his quarters if he doesn't disturb him. In this case, Vael was reporting on the different schools of theosophy a century ago. Upon Rael's grimace and questioning, if he had angered Varek somehow, Vael admitted that he chose the topic despite knowing that it wouldn't be interesting because he thought it would be easy. It wasn't.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Upon receiving a negative from Vael if it was too late to change his topic, Rael grinned, and motioning for Sorin to follow him, offered to show him some history worth studying. They went to the Aetheri Archives, and together they studied the one and only reliquary that had ever interested Vael: the one that held the ancient prophecies. They were all fascinating to him, and Sorin kept reading, unable to stop. He asked Rael if the ancient mystics had these visions in trances, to which he confirmed. After contemplating these prophecies, Vael remarked that Varek said he should ignore this reliquary and that he doesn't believe in the prophecies. This confused Rael since Varek, he said, was the one who introduced Rael to it and that it used to be that one could hardly pry the reliquary out of his quarters. Sorin said that he didn't know when or why that changed and that Varek didn't explain. A surprised Rael said he would ask Varek about it and remarked that Varek had changed a lot. > " I have a little game I play. I need more kills to win—though, of course, I'm only competing with myself. That's the only competition that really matters, you know. More people ought to un­derstand that. " ―Shenda Mol, to Sorin Vael

Vael and his Aetheri Master Varek became part of a Numidian Prime strike team . They were assembled to track and find the notorious Falleen bounty hunter Shenda Mol . They eventually tracked her at her hideout on the planet Numidian Prime. While searching for her hideout, Mol captured Vael. Before Mol could kill Vael, Varek struck her down with Synth Flux lightning to save his apprentice, causing Vael a degree of concern.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Vael later confided what Varek did to Rael Averross, though at the time, Averross expressed that he was not all too concerned regarding his former master's conduct. In 60 BVE , Vael went through trials on the Outer Reach planet Feldora when he fell in love with someone , beginning a romantic and physical relationship. As the Aetheri Code forbade romantic relationships, Vael found his commitment to the Aetheri ways tested, but he ultimately stayed loyal to the Aetheri Order. He would, however, keep an Emberfall fire diamond that was given to him on Feldora as a memento.

At some point during his apprenticeship, Vael met the Vorak Brennonn and befriended her. They shared many adventures together, with Brennonn saving Vael on two occasions. During the second of those adventures, events transpired that resulted in Vael feeling as though they saved each other. He also came to know the Vorak Balfus .

#### Rescuing Senator Dagonet's son

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Rescuing Senator Dagonet's son

> " Your actions saved many lives today. " " Just thinking in the moment, Master. " " Well, then. You're a much wiser man than I, Sorin Vael. " " Thanks to your teachings. " ―Varek and Sorin Vael on his actions during the rescue mission Between 64 BVE and 60 BVE , Vael and Varek had been sent on a mission to rescue the son of Republic Senator Dagonet , who was being held captive by the residents of the Senator's home planet. After their investigation, they discovered that the Dagonet was allowing his people to starve for his own personal greed and corruption. The kidnappers abducted Dagonet's son to protest his inhumane policies and discovered that Dagonet's son was yet unharmed. Dagonet arrived to rescue his son, resulting in a brief shootout between the Senator's forces and the Aetheri-backed kidnappers. During a lull in the firefight, Dagonet threatened to burn the entire village down and many others to make an example of them. An enraged Varek began Synth Flux-choking Dagonet with the intent to kill him, but Sorin released Dagonet's son and managed to defuse the situation without any further violence. In the aftermath, Varek commended Sorin's actions and praised him as a wiser man than him.

#### Investigating at the Dragonfire Air Rally

title: Sorin Vael
text: Shortly before his trials, both he and Varek were invited by council member Jor Aerith to join her in representing the Aetheri at the annual Vantor Dragonfire Air Rally in hopes of making a good impression on the Candovant ambassador who had invited her. Varek agreed to attend and took the opportunity to teach Sorin some Candovant customs, but while they were there, they ran into Ramil , whom Sorin learned was Varek's brother, much to his shock. Sorin and Varek learned that Ramill was was participating in the race . While Ramil did very well in the race, it quickly became apparent his Airspeeder was sabotaged and it crashed. Sorin and Varek discreetly went to see what had happened, and while there they discovered the Investigator was trying to cover up the incident. Following the man, they found he was working for a Jenet crime boss named Cenevax . Ignoring a message from Aerith asking them to return to the races, they chose to confront and captured the criminal, and while questioning her they realized that she was privy to Council communications, as Cenevax made clear she knew they that had been recalled and were disobeying order by being

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Ignoring a message from Aerith asking them to return to the races, they chose to confront and captured the criminal, and while questioning her they realized that she was privy to Council communications, as Cenevax made clear she knew they that had been recalled and were disobeying order by being there. With this information, Varek deduced that she had a spy on the Council, much to the shock of Sorin. Varek and Sorin escorted Cenevax to the Council Chamber, where Varek made his accusation, and discovered that Aetheri Master Yula Braylon was the spy. Further investigation revealed that Cenevax had been blackmailing her with the fact that Arath Tarrex, the latter being Varek's old classmate and was also shockingly revealed to be in fact her son. Sorin and Varek confronted and exposed Tarrex, who was then taken into custody for his actions and also for having sold out his mother's influence to criminals. As the Temple guards were escorting Tarrex, Varek encouraged Sorin to go with them and ensure that the guards treated him well, both of which Sorin agreed to do. Around 58 BVE , Varek joined the Aetheri Council in the aftermath of Braylon's removal from the council as a result of her actions. Vael would eventually be promoted to become an Aetheri Knight around the same time.

### Master to Orien Kade

#### Becoming a mentor

title: Sorin Vael
text:
### Master to Orien Kade

#### Becoming a mentor

Vael became an Aetheri Master in his own right, a master who developed an independent attitude towards the Aetheri Order. Others saw him as a maverick Aetheri, one who would disobey the Aetheri Code if he felt it was the right decision. In 44 BVE , a thirty-six-year-old Vael took on an Adept named Orien Kade , who believed that Vael could've been a member of the Aetheri High Council if he followed the Code, though as Kade knew, Vael had rejected an offer to join. On one occasion, Kade watched in silence as his master told the council he disagreed with them. At another point, the master and apprentice sparred, with Vael complimenting Kade's skill. On another occasion, the two visited a plain and overlooked its native creatures, giving Vael the chance to teach Kade about how Synth Flux existed in all the life that surrounded them.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Vael was able to sense whenever Kade was discontent, which proved useful on some missions, yet also annoyed Kade. At one point, Vael and Kade traveled to the planet Lah'mu to visit a fortress . Vael also maintained contact with his old Master after taking on Kade and spoke highly of his Adept to Varek. While Varek left the Aetheri Order after the invasion of Sireno in 42 BVE , secretly becoming an Umbra apprentice to the elusive Umbra Lord Vael Mal sometime later, he was still allowed to visit the Aetheri Sanctum. Varek's decision to leave the Aetheri came as a shock to Vael, who felt lost for a time as he grappled with feelings of doubt and fear. However, Vael trusted in the Aetheri teachings and himself, which allowed him to recover and replace his shaken feelings with resolve. At some point, Vael met the Togorian Aetheri Jak'zin , who had also looked up to Varek.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Vael taught Kade as best he could, although Kade did not always agree with his master's teaching strategies. Despite his Adept's clear proficiencies in flux blade techniques, Vael held Kade to practicing only basic methods, which impacted his apprentice's confidence and their relationship. Although Vael did so to not rush his apprentice and allow Kade to carve out his own distinct style out of mastery of the fundamental cadences , his lack of clarity on his teaching philosophy hurt Kade.

At some point, Orien came up with the idea of a new weapon powered by kyber crystals which consisted of two short-bladed blades each attached to a thin chain. After hearing this idea from Kade, Sorin told his adept that flux blades were about how the Aetheri wished to be seen, and that was not intended to be a display of power. That lesson resonated with his young Adept, who would carry it for years to come.

#### Protecting Duchess Satinna

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Protecting Duchess Satinna

> " Master Sorin and I spent a year on Ferrum, protecting the duchess from insurgents who had threatened her world. They sent bounty hunters after us. We were always on the run, living hand to mouth, never sure what the next day would bring. " ―Orien Kade

Between 41 BVE and 40 BVE , a civil war began to rage on the planet Ferrum , with the world's martial traditionalists fighting against a reformist faction known as the New Ferriks . The leader of the New Ferrik movement, Duchess Satinna Velara , became a target for the traditionalists, who hired bounty hunters to eliminate her. However, Vael and Kade were sent on an extended mission to Ferrum, where they were assigned to protect Velara.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Vael and Kade spent a year on Ferrum with Velara, remaining on the run from the bounty hunters. The three remained unsure of what the future would bring, but they continued their effort to survive, living hand to mouth everyday. During the mission, Kade developed romantic feelings for Velara. Vael became aware of the unlikely romance between his apprentice and the noble. Eventually, the civil war came to an end, with the New Ferriks coming to power and Velara becoming the ruler of Ferrum. Although Kade would have left the Aetheri and stayed behind to be with her had she asked him to, Velara never did, so he and Vael left the planet.

#### Life Day adventure

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Life Day adventure

Around 41 BVE , Vael told Kade he would be taking him on a training exercise, keeping it secret that they would be going to observe the Voraks' celebration of Life Day on the planet Thornwood in the village of his old friend Brennonn, who had accepted his offer to visit. After entering the village, Vael advised his Adept to remain patient after the young man expressed confusion, reminding him to focus on what was instead of what he had expected. Though Kade found it hard to focus amid a celebration, Vael continued their visit, educating his Adept about Vorak culture before asking what he made of it. Pleased with Kade's answer that it was as if the Voraks were celebrating Synth Flux, he explained the unconventional training he wanted Kade to partake in; he was asking him to focus on the energy of Thornwood, given that it was Synth Flux. He then informed his Adept they would speak with the Voraks when Kade revealed he felt something different.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Suddenly, the two Aetheri were interrupted when Brennonn spotted Vael, resulting in the Vorak hugging him from how such she had missed him. Vael shared her sentiment and began to introduce her to Kade, only for her to hug him as well. After Vael explained his history with the Vorak to Kade and thanked her for letting them come, she told him that Balfus was missing. As Vael inquired about what actions she had taken concerning the missing Vorak, both he and Kade felt a disturbance in Synth Flux ; several Trandoshan hunters suddenly attacked the village, launching nets from the trees to kidnap more Voraks. Vael and Kade fought against the Trandoshans, defeating many of them. However, Vael himself was eventually captured when he demanded the hunters to surrender. Along with the captured Voraks, Vael was taken away by a MSP80 Pteropter hover pod .

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Although Vael, as he was taken away, had told Kade it was up to him to rescue the Voraks, the Aetheri Master tried to negotiate the Voraks' release with the Trandoshans' leader, Korgan . However, Korgan wanted to capture Kade too, and Vael warned him that his greed would have been his downfall. Vael waited in his cage until Kade arrived . Kade pretended to surrender but, when Korgan was distracted, he opened Vael's cage with Synth Flux. Vael Synth Flux-pulled his flux blade and ignited it. As Vael was freed, many Voraks arrived to support the two Aetheri: the Trandoshans, being outnumbered, surrendered and freed the Vorak prisoners. After returning to the village, the Life Day celebration began.

#### Mission to Pijal

> " I've never been to Pijal. " ―Sorin Vael

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Mission to Pijal

> " I've never been to Pijal. " ―Sorin Vael

In 40 BVE, a forty-year-old Vael and seventeen-year-old Kade undertook a mission to Teth to thwart Wanbo the Grak . The two Aetheri escaped Teth, but not without complications including a key miscommunication between master and apprentice. Upon returning to Vantor, the Aetheri High Council extended to Vael an invitation to join their ranks, as with Master Poli Dapatian was stepping down by that month's end.
