Vael was shocked to be asked due to his disagreements with the Council on various occasions, and while he was initially pleased to hear the offer, he thought of his Adept, who he would have to pass on to a new master if he were to accept. While it would solve the growing problems between them, Vael felt guilt at the thought of it and thus told the Council that he would meditate on their proposition.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Meanwhile, a political dispute erupted on the Inner Reach planet Pijal . A performance troupe known as the Opposition that began playing political pranks to protest a treaty signing that would end the absolute monarchy on Pijal, allow the world to join the Republic, and give more power to Czerka Corporation was thought to be making increasingly violent attacks nearing the treaty's signing. Vael's old friend Rael Averross requested Vael and his Adept's assistance to end the dispute and ensure the signing of the treaty. The Council sent Vael and his Adept to Pijal to help. However, as the mission began, Kade became aware of the offer presented to Vael regarding the Aetheri Council when the two met with Supreme Chancellor Kirames Kaj . Vael felt great shame at not being the first to tell his Adept learner. Before they left, Vael sought out Kade and the Adept's dojo. He attempted to apologize for not being the first to tell him the news and said that he had several reservations that he had to dwell on before committing to the position, but Kade made a sarcastic reply. Vael told his Adept that he would continue to discuss the matter when

title: Sorin Vael
text: attempted to apologize for not being the first to tell him the news and said that he had several reservations that he had to dwell on before committing to the position, but Kade made a sarcastic reply. Vael told his Adept that he would continue to discuss the matter when Kade was in a more rational mood, and when Kade quipped again, Vael sadly said that he supposed that Synth Flux always allowed things to turn out for the best. As they traveled to Pijal, the tension between them grew. Vael and Kade both were briefed on the situation, learning that Averross served Crown Princess Fanry , who was only fourteen years old, as an advisor and that he needed to protect her from the Opposition as she waited to take Pijal's throne. Vael and Averross became reacquainted quickly, although Vael was skeptical of several of Averross's choices during his service, as Averross also loosely interpreted the Aetheri Code. As he and Kade began to do more investigating on Pijal's moon , they encountered two jewel thieves, Pax Maripher and Rahara Wick . Although Maripher was very abrasive towards Vael, Wick was more cooperative. Onboard their ship, the Meryx , Vael recruited the two to help them find the terrorists that posed a threat to the treaty. Shortly after returning, Vael received a vision of the event, which turned into a bloody battle. He brought it to Averross's attention, but the older Aetheri did not share his level of concern.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
As their investigation continued, Vael eventually met with the Opposition's leader, Halin Azucca , and learned that her group was being framed. Although they had peacefully made demonstrations against the treaty, the violent terrorist acts that had alerted the Republic were not caused by Azucca's people. As Sorin learned of the complications surrounding the treaty due to the lack of Pijali representation and the heavy influence gained by the Czerka Corporation , he decided to oppose the treaty himself and refused to act as a Republic representative. However, eventually, the Aetheri discovered that Fanry was deceiving them and had been building a military group called the blackguards, framing the Opposition to restore the full monarchy. At the coronation, she rejected the treaty as well as the Republic's influence, proving herself to having been underestimated by the Aetheri. Ready to remove Czerka influence from the system by synth flux, she prepared to attack their ships. Vael attempted to convince her to stop and prevent the innocent casualties that were the Czerka slaves onboard the ships, but when she refused, Vael took matters into his own hands, and with the help of Kade as well as their two new friends Maripher and Wick, they succeeded in saving the slaves. After the mission, Vael decided to stick with training Kade and declined the offer to join the Aetheri Council.

#### Helping Master Zho

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Helping Master Zho

Around 40 BVE, Vael and Kade were operating near a planet that served as a base of the Flesh Mongers pirate group, flying a pair of Delta-7 Aethersprite -class light interceptors . The two received a message from the planet's surface from Aetheri Master Zho , who asked for assistance. Landing on the planet, Vael and Kade discovered that Zho had taken out the entire pirate gang to rescue a young Synth Flux-sensitive child , known as Lo , as the pirate had planned to sell him due to his Synth Flux abilities. Zho asked Vael and Kade to escort the infant to the Aetheri Sanctum , with Zho assuring Lo that he was in safe hands with Vael. Vael expressed that he was happy to help out as they had been so close. While the two conversed, Kade took particular interest in that Zho took out an entire room of pirates and was totally in awe. Vael then proceeded to ask Zho if everything was all right, to which the revered master replied that he could sense a calling disturbance in Synth Flux that he felt he must follow. Vael noted that he could not feel the presence himself, but offered to join him on his quest if he so wanted. As Zho climbed into his starship , he responded that he felt it was simply a calling for him alone and embarked on a mission to a planet in the Vagadarr system , where he became involved in a tribal war between the planet's native inhabitants.

### Truths of Synth Flux

#### Discovering the secrets of life after death

title: Sorin Vael
text:
### Truths of Synth Flux

#### Discovering the secrets of life after death

Sometime during his life, Vael began discovering the secrets to manifesting his consciousness after death . He traveled to a planet strong with Synth Flux, a world that legend said was the birthplace of life and the origin of synthcells . He learned from five Synth Flux Priestesses who had retained their consciousness after death. He learned that, when a living thing died, its life passed through the Living Synth Flux and into the Cosmic Synth Flux to become one with Synth Flux.

As the Living Synth Flux and Cosmic Synth Flux existed in tandem, it became possible for one to retain consciousness and physically manifest themselves after death. Vael was considered worthy of the knowledge of eternal life and secretly began his training to unlock its mysteries fully. He also learned from a Shaman of the Whills that achieving eternal consciousness required absolute selflessness.

#### Questioning his purpose

> " Being called a coward isn't what bothered me, Master Zho. It was being called a great warrior. " ―Sorin Vael

title: Sorin Vael
text: Vael began experiencing an inner turmoil over how the Aetheri should interact with Synth Flux. Although Zho sensed that internal debate in the man, Vael continued on with his Aetheri duties for sometime. In 37 BVE , when Vael and Kade were sent to the planet Bri'n to establish negotiations between the the Priestess Th'er of Wooda and the Metal Clan , Kade stayed within their Eta -class shuttle while Vael met with the Priestess's rivals. When the Metal Clan instead tried to kill Vael and the Priestess as a justification to begin cutting down the world's trees, he moved to defend Th'er and escape with her. Deflecting many volt pistol bolts with his flux blade, the Aetheri contacted Kade to start their shuttle and inform him about the failed negotiations. After being surrounded by the Metal Clan, Th'er proclaimed that Vael was a warrior who could take down all who opposed her, yet Vael instead used Synth Flux jump to escape with her aboard their shuttle, ordering Kade to take them to Vantor so as to protect the Priestess.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Th'er was nevertheless disgusted by Vantor—viewing it as a city of metal—and demanded Vael to act as a warrior, ordering him to cut down every member of the Metal Clan. Although Vael informed her that was not the path of the Aetheri Order, Th'er felt Vael was instead a coward who did not live up to the legends that proclaimed the Aetheri to be great soldiers. Greatly distressed at being called a warrior, he returned to the Aetheri Sanctum, where he did not report to the Aetheri High Council. Deciding to confront Vael over his internal turmoil, Zho located the Aetheri Master on one of the Temple's balconies under the pretense of asking for him to report to the Council. Aware that Kade had filed his own report, Vael quickly saw through Zho's claim, leading to a discussion about how the Aetheri should act between the two masters.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Even though Zho and him had different opinions, they both agreed that Vael should seek answers. Needing a world full of life to find a deep communion with Synth Flux, Vael—travelling off Vantor in his Delta-7 Aetheri Interceptor with his astromech droid —trusted Synth Flux to guide him to answers, resulting in him coming out of hyperspace above a charted but unnamed world . After leaving his ship and admiring the planet's beauty, Vael quickly felt the presence of the umbra side on the world and noticed how a spreading darkness was starting to corrupt the planet. Unsure whether Synth Flux wanted him to stop it or learn from it, Vael continued until he found a temple and sat its throne. Pondering whether he would find light in the dark monument, Vael entered a frightening Synth Flux vision .

title: Sorin Vael
text: In his vision, Vael—his skin and Aetheri robes covered in marks—was surrounded by red humanoid beings who grew out of dark tendrils. Although at least one of these beings tried to attack him as he fought, Vael quickly ignited his flux blade and cut the beings down, only for the red coloration to vanish from those he had killed. Vael saw he had murdered Aetheri, and the same darkness that he had seen on their bodies began to consume him; by choosing violence, the umbra side had gained power over him. As the darkness wrapped across his face, Vael awoke from his vision horrified, only to see the light side had entered into the monument. He realized Synth Flux had taught him he could find balance that could be achieved without conflict, as unchecked violence would make the Aetheri turn into what they sought to confront. In fact, he found that some of the planet's dark corruption had instead formed into flowers, existing in harmony with the light.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Leaving the planet—albeit with new questions about the nature of Synth Flux—and returning to Vantor, Vael found Th'er in one of the city world's parks, where offered to help her find off-world allies with whom to fight against the Metal Clan. Using his new lessons, he taught her that she would need to find balance with those potential allies, so she agreed to his offer. During the night, he again met with Zho on a temple balcony, leading to another discussion about Synth Flux. Speaking with the Grand Master, Vael defended finding balance in Synth Flux, believing the Aetheri could not be too rigid yet could also not give into the umbra side.

#### Aetheri operations

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Aetheri operations

In 34 BVE , Vael—alongside Aetheri Masters Drevan Koss , Tor Vayne , and Depa Billaba —was sent to the planet Oosalon by Supreme Chancellor Finis Valorum due to the actions of the warlord Guattako , who was backed by the Grak Clan and had kidnapped children to serve as soldiers. Being a planet that had around 80,000 kilometers worth of tunnels, the Aetheri would be unable to find the base of Guattako's army , so they made a plan that Koss would be purposely captured, allowing him to send a signal in Synth Flux to lead his fellow Aetheri to Guattako. Although Vael and his fellow Aetheri—joined by at least two soldiers—were unable to make it through the tunnels in time to help Koss, the Aetheri Master had nevertheless defeated Guattako's army, while the warlord himself had been shot by one of the children he had kidnapped. Thus, Guattako's revolution was thwarted, the children could be return to their homes, and the remaining members of the terrorist army were captured.

### War on Ondara

#### Failed negotiations

title: Sorin Vael
text:
### War on Ondara

#### Failed negotiations

> " Is it in their nature to make us wait this long? " " No. I sense an unusual amount of fear for something as trivial as this trade dispute. " ―Orien Kade and Sorin Vael — Link ▶️ ( file info ) Ten years prior to the outbreak of the Replica Wars , the Commerce Combine blockaded Ondara and planned to invade it in retaliation for the Vantor Republic 's taxation of trade routes in outlying star systems. Unknown to the Republic, the Vael Mal—secretly Ondara's Senator Mal—controlled the Federation and engineered the conflict so he could be elected Supreme Chancellor. Before the blockade, Vael felt that something was amiss and took Kade to the Aetheri Archives to read through Senate documents, as they often did whenever Vael felt something was wrong in the Senate. While reviewing bills concerning the recent tax reforms, Orien grew listless and Vael, sensing his apprentice's discomfort, asked him what he thought. Kade opined to Vael that people had too much time on their hands and he did not understand why people spent so much time talking about taxation. Sorin looked up from the file he was reading and admonished Kade, telling him that it was a matter of perspective and that the most important thing to the people who submitted the bills was control. Vael noted that there was a lot of control to lose between the planets and corporations involved in the tax dispute.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Orien questioned why they were personally purviewing the bills, and Vael replied that they were listening so they could act when they needed to. Orien teasingly asked if they would act with or without orders, which made Vael smile, though the Aetheri Master informed his apprentice that they were likely to be following orders. Kade quipped that, because they would be under the Council's alignment, they would be less likely to be involved in local labor disputes. Bothered by Kade's comment, Vael rebuked that they would also be less likely to kick-start romances with the local nobility. The reference to Duchess Satinna let Kade know better than to treat such things so trivially, and he changed the subject as they continued reading the taxation bills. Vael's precautions proved useful as Chancellor Finis Valorum dispatched Vael and Kade to Ondara, tasking them with resolving the situation through diplomatic means.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Upon arriving at the Commerce Combine command ship Saak'ak , Vael and Kade were escorted into a conference room, where they were told that Viceroy Nutis Gunray would greet them. As the Aetheri were waiting, the Federation leaders contacted Vael Mal, informing him that the Chancellor's ambassadors were Aetheri Knights . Mal ordered their execution, while Vael could sense the fear that the Neimoidians felt, letting Vael know this wasn't a common trade dispute. These suspicions were confirmed when the Federation flooded the conference room with poison gas to kill the Aetheri. But the two were able to hold their breath long enough for the Federation to open the doors and inadvertently give the Aetheri a chance to escape . They fought off the battle droids waiting outside the door and fled through the corridors, where they made their way into the ventilation system.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Moving through the ventilation shafts, the Aetheri made their way to the hangar , where they saw the Federation Army preparing to mount an invasion of the planet. After Kade quipped that Vael had predicted that the negotiations would be short, the Aetheri stowed away aboard separate ships , which made their way to the planet's surface and planned to warn the Ondara that the invasion was coming.

#### Rescuing the Queen

> " The situation here is not what it seems. There is something else behind all this, Your Highness. There is no logic in the Federation's move here. My feelings tell me they will destroy you. " ―Sorin Vael, to Queen Ondar — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Sorin Vael
text:
> " The situation here is not what it seems. There is something else behind all this, Your Highness. There is no logic in the Federation's move here. My feelings tell me they will destroy you. " ―Sorin Vael, to Queen Ondar — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Once on the surface, Vael ventured through a forest to rendezvous with Kade and encountered a Mool named Greeb Mool , who latched onto him in the chaos of the Federation invasion. This encounter nearly got them killed as they fell to the ground just in time to avoid being run over by a Federation troop carrier . Mool swore a life debt to Vael for saving him, as Vael tried to get rid of the Mool. He finally rendezvoused with Kade and planned to find shelter, which Mool offered to give them in the Mool city beneath the ocean . The Mool momentarily changed his mind, revealing that he had been exiled and would be punished for returning; however, Vael and Kade convinced him to take them there to avoid the approaching Federation forces.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Mool led the two Aetheri into the Mool city , where how they were immediately apprehended and brought before the Mool leaders . Vael attempted to persuade the Mool leader, Boss Nass , that the Federation posed a threat to them just as much as they threatened Ondara. But Mool prejudices against the Ondara were too strong for the Boss to care about what happened on the surface. The Aetheri Master used Synth Flux to telepathically persuade Nass to give them a bongo aquatic transport that the Aetheri could use to reach Serath , the capital of Ondara. Nass was also persuaded to allow Mool to travel with them, as Vael, claiming the life debt custom, believed the Mool could be a guide to make it through the planet core and to the capital.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
After traveling through the core and evading multiple large sea creatures, they arrived in Serath and rescued Queen Lira Ondar , who was taken into Federation custody. Together, along with a number of the queen's guards and handmaidens , they made their way to a hangar to take the queen 's starship off of Ondara. They were able to board the ship after fighting through many battle droids and took the vessel into orbit where they encountered the Federation blockade. They managed to escape, but the ship was damaged and needed to be set down for repairs. Vael suggested that they land on Dunemere , a desert planet where the Graks ruled and the Federation had no presence. Although the queen's lead guard, Panaka , objected because of the danger posed by the Graks , the decision was made to seek refuge on Dunemere.

#### Discovery of the Seeded One

> " Finding him was the will of Synth Flux. I have no doubt of that. " ―Sorin Vael to the Aetheri High Council — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Discovery of the Seeded One

> " Finding him was the will of Synth Flux. I have no doubt of that. " ―Sorin Vael to the Aetheri High Council — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Landing on Dunemere, the crew determined they needed a new hyperrelay generator to make it to their final destination: Vantor, the Republic's capital. Vael decided to venture out into the local settlement to find a store that would sell a generator. He brought Ondar—masquerading as a royal handmaiden—and Mool along with him. While they were in town, everyone on the Royal Starship was left waiting for Vael's return, leaving them to worry or read to pass the time. Vael, Ondar, and Mool arrived at a shop owned by a Toydarian junk dealer , Waddu , who had the parts they needed, but would not accept Republic credits for payment. Vael attempted to persuade him that credits would be acceptable telepathically, but the Toydarian was immune to Aetheri mind tricks. Vael left empty-handed, but not before meeting Kael Drayden , a young boy who was a slave of Waddu's.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Drayden followed Vael and the others, where he warned them that a sandstorm was coming and that they would need to find shelter. The boy knew the group would not make it back to their ship in time and brought them back to his home , where he introduced them to his mother , Shira , who was also one of Waddu's slaves. They all shared dinner, where Drayden deduced that Vael was an Aetheri, having seen his flux blade . Vael revealed that he and the others were on a critical mission for the Republic and stranded on Dunemere until they could repair their ship. Knowing that it could help them escape, Drayden volunteered to help by racing in the Dune Eve Classic dune race and give them the profits to repair their ship if he won. Vael accepted the offer, though Ondar was unconvinced that trusting their fate to someone they barely knew was the right course.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
The next day , Vael spoke to Waddu about entering Drayden in the race with a pod that Drayden had built in secret, and Vael convinced Waddu that it was the Aetheri's pod . The two agreed that Waddu would pay Drayden's entry fee and collect all of the winnings from a potential victory, except for whatever money Vael needed to repair his ship. If Drayden lost, Waddu would keep the queen's ship. Waddu agreed to the condition, and Drayden set out to begin getting his pod race-ready.

In watching Drayden work on his pod, Vael told Shira he could sense an Aetheri's potential in the boy. Vael wondered who Drayden's father was and was intrigued to hear Shira had conceived her son without a father. Later that night, Vael tested the boy's synthcell count and sent the sample to Kade on the queen's ship, who told his master that Drayden's synthcell count was over 20,000—higher than any known Aetheri. Through the supposed virgin birth and the synthcell count, Vael came to believe that Drayden was the Seeded One of Aetheri prophecy, a being who would bring balance to Synth Flux and stop the Umbra .

title: Sorin Vael
text: With the belief that Drayden was the Seeded One, Vael knew that he should bring Drayden to the Aetheri Sanctum on Vantor to be trained as an Aetheri. Vael approached Waddu with a new wager: if the boy were to win, Waddu would free Drayden and his mother. Waddu scoffed at the idea of freeing two slaves, but he did agree to release one if Drayden won. However, he left it up to chance and threw a small multi- colored cube ; if it landed on blue, Drayden would be the slave in question. Vael used Synth Flux to help it land on blue, and Waddu agreed to free Drayden if he won the race—but, according to Waddu, the Dug racer Sebulba was sure to win.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
The race began later that day, and Drayden emerged victoriously. Waddu, who lost everything betting on Sebulba, freed the boy as per their agreement. Vael took what profits he needed to repair the ship, gave the rest to Drayden and his mother, and told them that Drayden had been freed and could go with him to Vantor to become an Aetheri. Drayden was unsure about leaving his mother, but he always had dreamed of becoming an Aetheri and decided to go. After Drayden shared a tearful goodbye with his mother, Vael and the boy set off for the queen's ship to make their way to Vantor.

Just before arriving at the ship, Vael Vreth , an Umbra Lord and Vael Mal' apprentice attacked Vael. The two fought across the desert floor while Drayden rushed back to the ship to get help, and the ship made its way to Vael's location, where he was able to board it and flee Dunemere, leaving Vael Vreth behind. Once onboard, he introduced Drayden to Kade.

title: Sorin Vael
text: With its hyperrelay repaired, the ship finally arrived on Vantor, where Chancellor Valorum and Senator Mal greeted the crew. After arriving, Vael went before the Aetheri Council and told the Aetheri Masters that he believed Vael Vreth was an Umbra Lord. The Council was dubious of the claim, as the Order thought they destroyed the Umbra a millennium earlier, but they committed themselves to learn Vael Vreth's identity. Vael also revealed that he discovered Drayden on Dunemere and believed him to be the Seeded One, asking that the boy be trained as an Aetheri. At Vael's request, the Council agreed to test Drayden to determine if he was eligible for training. Kade was skeptical that Drayden would pass the test given his age, as Aetheri began their training at infancy, and worried that Vael would defy whatever decision the Council made. Despite his Adept's concerns, Vael was determined to see Drayden become an Aetheri Knight. After the meeting, he along with Yaddle met up with Varek who offered him advice. Unbeknownst to both of them, this would be the last time they see each other.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
The Council tested Drayden and agreed with Vael that he was mighty with Synth Flux, but declined to accept him for training. They believed that he was too old to begin training and dangerously full of fear and anger despite his power. Nonetheless, Vael insisted that Drayden receive training, saying he would take the boy as his Adept learner. Meanwhile, Kade could take his Aetheri Trials and become an Aetheri Knight, as the Aetheri Code forbade an Aetheri from having two Adepts. The Council delayed the discussion for another time and ordered that Vael and Kade return to Ondara as Queen Ondar was preparing to return to deal with the invasion without the Senate's help. Vael took Drayden with him and began giving him some initial lessons about Synth Flux.

#### The Duel of the Fates

> " Orien. Promise…Promise me you will train the boy. " " Yes, Master. " " He… is the Seeded One. He… will bring balance. Train him… " ―Vael's dying request to Kade — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Sorin Vael
text: Upon arrival on Ondara, the Aetheri traveled with Ondar to find the Mools hiding in a sacred area of the forests. There, the Ondara and Mools allied to fight the Federation. The queen's handmaiden Lira revealed herself to be the true Ondar, having masqueraded as a servant while one of her handmaidens, Sable , portrayed the queen as a safety precaution. Vael, for his part, had not been fooled by the Queen's disguise since their first meeting, but had gone along with the charade for reasons of his own, which she appreciated as it helped safeguard her life. Together with the Aetheri and the Mools, Ondar put together a plan of attack , where the Mools would fight the Federation army away from Serath as a diversion, allowing Ondar, her forces, and the Aetheri to infiltrate the city with little opposition. Vael made it clear, however, that while he would protect the queen, he could not fight a war for her.

title: Sorin Vael
text: As the Mool army led the bulk of the Federation forces away from the city, Vael snuck into Serath with the others and fought their way to the palace. Once in the hangar, they were again confronted by Vael Vreth, who the two Aetheri prepared to fight as the Ondara fought their way to the throne room to capture Viceroy Gunray. Vael and Kade fought Vreth in the hangar, with the Umbra Lord dominating the duel, though Vreth did give ground to lead the Aetheri out of the hangar and throughout a palace generator complex . Vreth separated the two Aetheri by knocking Kade down several levels and eventually trapping him behind shielding, leaving Vael to fight the Umbra Lord in single combat without his apprentice. As they made their way through the area, the two combatants were evenly matched. However, Vreth eventually countered Vael with a physical strike from his flux blade hilt and seized the opportunity since Vael was off-balance, fatally stabbing the Aetheri Master through the torso as Kade watched in horror from behind the shielding.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
When Kade finally reached Vreth, he and the Umbra Lord engaged in a furious battle, with Kade grieving for his master and friend. Vreth was able to disarm and knock Kade partly down a reactor shaft and kick his flux blade into it. Then Kade used Synth Flux to summon his master's flux blade, jump out of the pit, and slice the blade through Vreth's torso in one swift movement, cutting the Umbra Lord in half, sending him tumbling down the shaft, and avenging Vael. Nevertheless, it was too late to save Vael through medical intervention; no amount of bacta could heal the maverick Aetheri's mortal wound. The Adept ran to his dying master, cradling him in his arms, and Vael made his apprentice promise that he would train with Drayden as an Aetheri. With his dying breath, Vael once again said that Drayden was the Seeded One and would bring balance to Synth Flux.

### Post mortem and legacy

#### Effect on those he knew

Funeral and effect on the Aetheri

> " The Council has granted me permission to train you. You will be an Aetheri. I promise. " ―Orien Kade to Kael Drayden, at Sorin Vael's funeral

title: Sorin Vael
text: In the aftermath of the battle, in which the Ondara successfully captured the Viceroy and ended the Federation occupation, Kade was granted the Aetheri Knight rank and insisted on taking Drayden as his apprentice. Although Zho disagreed, the Council approved Kade's request, fulfilling Vael's dying wish: Drayden would undergo Aetheri training. Later, Vael was memorialized when he was given an Aetheri funeral on Ondara, where his body was cremated on a funeral pyre. Many delegates, including Queen Ondar, the Aetheri Council, and Chancellor Mal, attended the funeral; notably absent were his former master Varek and Aetheri Master Yaddle , who, suspicious of Varek's intended absence, followed Varek in his confrontation with Vael Mal in Vantor . At the funeral, Kade told Drayden that the Council would allow him to be trained and that Kade would be his master. Together, the two mourned the death of their fallen friend, as Kade vowed that Drayden would become an Aetheri. Amongst the Aetheri, Vael was remembered as a great member of their Order despite his past of disagreeing with the council.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Even though he had always wanted Vael available as guidance for when he eventually trained an Adept, and he had wanted time between his apprenticeship and eventual mentorship to decide what kind of Aetheri he should be without Vael by his side, Kade upheld his vow to his master dutifully over the years. At one point, when Drayden was considering leaving the Aetheri Order at the age of twelve , Kade was intent on following suit. However, he was still going to complete the boy's training even outside the Order. Drayden, however, chose to remain an Aetheri in the aftermath of a mission to the planet Carnelion IV . Even though Kade could become easily annoyed by Drayden—leaving him to question if he had ever annoyed Vael in similar ways, although he doubted he ever had—he nevertheless befriended and grew close to his Adept, with the Aetheri duo coming to act like brothers.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Although Drayden remained thankful of Kade's teachings, he, at times, pondered how his life as an Aetheri would have changed if Vael had survived; even though he knew the Aetheri Order disapproved of attachments, he thought these questions were alright because he believed nothing—not even interpersonal relationships—could ever be fully untethered. As Kade later recognized, Drayden developed a habit of growing very connected to and not wanting to lose anyone he was close with after leaving his mother. Desperate for new connections, he had found one with Vael, only for the Aetheri Master to be taken away from him shortly after they met.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Varek, still an Umbra in secret, eventually learned of Vael's death at the hands of Vreth. Later, on the planet Garnethex , Varek unexpectedly reunited with the Aetheri Knight Jak'zin, who noted he had met Vael before being interrupted by a representative of the SoroSuub Corporation . Later, Varek, appearing as if he could be compassionate ally, discussed Vael with the Aetheri Knight. Varek claimed he wondered if his former apprentice would still be alive if he had not left the order, reflecting that the company of Kade was not enough to save the late master. The Umbra used his speculations to trick Jak'zin into letting him in on the Aetheri's mission on Garnethex .

Effect on Ondara

> " His name was Sorin Vael, an Aetheri. He died defending Ondara during the battle for the planet against the Commerce Combine. The Aetheri memorialized him there, and we honor him as a hero. " ―Lira Ondar, to Bael Solen

title: Sorin Vael
text:
> " His name was Sorin Vael, an Aetheri. He died defending Ondara during the battle for the planet against the Commerce Combine. The Aetheri memorialized him there, and we honor him as a hero. " ―Lira Ondar, to Bael Solen

Ondar, meanwhile, came to believe that her relationship with Vael had been an odd one, given that he had seen through her disguise, yet she hoped she would have been able to consider him a friend and ally if he had survived. In the years following the Ondara Crisis, she remained saddened by his death, and she made sure to light a candle of incense for the fallen Aetheri during the yearly memorial for all who had died for Ondara. In fact, many others did the same; though few on Ondara had met the Aetheri Master, it was believed everyone on the world knew his name, with Ondara like Tonra —who had actually been present for many of the so-called "stories" about what had happened—hearing tales of what he did for their planet. For years after the invasion, the handmaiden Saché continued to incorrectly believe Vael had been fooled by the decoy act like most had been.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Nevertheless, events like Vael's time on Dunemere were not part of public record, so they were not spread amongst the Ondara. However, Tonra and Sable discussed such events during a mission to the desert world. Ultimately, the people of Ondara honored Vael as a hero who had given everything to save them. One of the ways they honored him was by building a shrine to his memory, a shrine which was known to gain some popularity over the next ten years and was visited by Kael Drayden shortly before his secret wedding to Lira Ondar. Several years after the invasion, when Ondar was asked if she would become Ondara's Galactic Senator after her term as queen ended, she looked to the Handmaiden Saché ; the Handmaiden remembered when Vael asked them to go to Vantor, given that Ondar had have to give a similar wordless signal to her allies.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Having met Aetheri, Ondar was unique amongst her colleagues in the Senate, but she nevertheless found the manners of the Aetheri Order unsettling. She considered that her reaction to their ways may have ended up different if Vael had survived. While speaking with Senator Bael Prestor Solen after he too had realized Ondar used decoys, albeit only after seeing Lira in a guard's uniform while Sable was acting as the Senator at a gala, she told him about Vael, feeling a great sadness wash over herself while she explained his fate. Solen responded that he was sorry for her loss, further stating that he realized Vael's death was an example of the dangerous life that followed her. Having been told Vael was the only other person who had managed to deduce she used decoys in the midst of the maneuver, Solen admitted he was happy to have found himself in what he deemed to be excellent company.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
For a mission to the planet Bromlarch , Ondar and several other senators partnered with Aetheri Master Depa Billaba, whom the former queen recognized due to her being present at Vael's funeral. While she found it odd to interact with an Aetheri Knight once more, Ondar also noticed Billaba carried herself very differently from how Vael had. While she understood all Aetheri in their Order would be different, she could not let go of the strange feeling it gave her, as if Billaba looked through her, while Vael had taken the time to look at her. Soon afterward, Ondar met the liaison Ninui ; given that it was the first time the liaison was meeting an Aetheri, Ondar noted how she had met Kade and Vael, explaining that the Aetheri were people like them, albeit people whose teachings could be confusing to non-Synth Flux-sensitives, and Ninui noted she wished to hear the complete story of how she met them.

#### Surviving as a spirit

> " Kael! Kael! NO! " ―Sorin Vael trying to hold Kael back through Synth Flux as he massacres the Tuskens

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Surviving as a spirit

> " Kael! Kael! NO! " ―Sorin Vael trying to hold Kael back through Synth Flux as he massacres the Tuskens

Though his training had been incomplete, Vael utilized what he learned from Synth Flux Priestesses to become one with Synth Flux and retain his identity after his death. However, he hadn't fully learned the mystery, so he could not physically manifest himself, only speak as a disembodied voice. Though his training had been incomplete, Vael utilized what he learned from Synth Flux Priestesses to become one with Synth Flux and retain his identity after his death. However, he hadn't fully learned the mystery, so he could not physically manifest himself, only speak as a disembodied voice.

One time that Vael communicated through Synth Flux was approximately ten years after the events on Ondara. Drayden had returned to Dunemere to find his mother, about whom he had been having recurring nightmares, and discovered she had been kidnapped by Dunefolk Raiders . He found her in a Dunefolk camp , but she died only moments later. In his anger, Drayden slaughtered all the Tuskens in the camp. Feeling the great pain and distress, Vael called out to Drayden through Synth Flux, which Zho could hear—but not comprehend—through his own meditations . In Vael's own words, he begged Kael to listen to his better nature and refuse to give in to his hatred. However, Vael's pleas were for naught, as Drayden didn't heed his words in his uncontrolled rage, telling himself that he was only imagining Vael's presence in that moment.

title: Sorin Vael
text: In the meantime, Varek, who had remained an Umbra and became the Head of State of the Fractio of Independent Systems , captured Kade on the planet Pyralis . While interrogating Kade, Varek—who was also secretly an Umbra Lord—expressed his belief that Vael would have joined his cause if he had been alive. Shortly after that, a conflict known as the Replica Wars began between the Vantor Republic and Varek's Fractio. Shortly after the conflict's beginning, Drayden prepared himself to partake in a secret wedding with Senator Ondar . As part of his preparation, he visited Vael's shrine on Ondara in partial repentance for having refused to heed Vael's words during his rage against the dunefolk, additionally having realized it meant there was a chance his old mentor could somehow see him and offer advice. Although he had told himself he had only imagined Vael's presence, he knew he was lying to himself. While at the shrine, Drayden attempted to reach out to Synth Flux in an attempt to connect with Vael in a similar manner to that previous instance. The attempt seemingly yielded nothing in his senses, which he theorized was Vael's way of telling him that things could

title: Sorin Vael
text: lying to himself. While at the shrine, Drayden attempted to reach out to Synth Flux in an attempt to connect with Vael in a similar manner to that previous instance. The attempt seemingly yielded nothing in his senses, which he theorized was Vael's way of telling him that things could always be made right. After feeling a sudden sense of calm despite the brewing Replica Wars, he then expressed his thanks despite not knowing if Sorin was responsible for his personal interpretations. During the Replica Wars, Drayden was promoted to the rank of Aetheri Knight and was assigned an Adept of his own, the Solinai Sela Marr , to whom he recited Vael's teachings on at least one occasion. Additionally, Vael's teachings were indirectly passed down to Marr during her apprenticeship, as she was learning from Drayden, who had learned from Kade, who had learned from Vael. Despite the fact that he was dead, the Fractio put out a citizen's alert on Vael and offered a 50,000 credit reward, charging him with conspiracy against the Commerce Combine.

title: Sorin Vael
text: The Aetheri made an effort to capture Varek during the war, feeling his arrest could help bring an end to the fighting. During one attempt to capture him in 21 BVE , Drayden and Kade boarded the count's Munificent -class star frigate , yet the Umbra Lord managed to escape through a secret hatch. Drayden pursued, making Varek shoot Synth Flux lightning at the Aetheri Knight; according to what Varek said in a recording he intended to send to Vael Mal, he knew such an attack would not defeat Drayden, believing that—because his Adept Vael had trained Kade, who had trained Drayden—his personal power had partly been passed down to his foe. He only intended to block the Aetheri's sight to enable his escape. Later in the same recording, Varek—recalling how he, Drayden, and Kade had been captured by the Hosha Gang of pirates —again mentioned Vael, feeling that Drayden was a fool who did not compare to the apprentices he had trained. Ultimately, Varek did not send the message to Mal.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Due to his incomplete training, Vael's spirit couldn't physically manifest himself, but he occurred in a vision on one known occasion; Kade, Drayden, and Marr, had been lured to the planet Mournis by three beings known as the Father , Son , and Daughter . These beings believed that Drayden was the Seeded One, as did Vael, whose vision first appeared to Kade to warn him that the beings sought Drayden and his potential as the Seeded One, to use it for their own means. When Kade questioned how Vael could appear, the figure told him that the planet acted as an amplifier and that it was a conduit through which Synth Flux flowed. The two spoke about Drayden and his power, with Kade having the opportunity to tell Vael that the late Aetheri Master's predictions about Drayden were true: he was stronger than any other Aetheri, yet still could not find balance. Vael warned that if Drayden were the Seeded One, then the boy would discover it on Mournis. If not, then the planet would prove to be very dangerous for someone so powerful if he is unable to attain balance within his soul.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Drayden himself later experienced Vael's vision. The figure of the late Aetheri informed him that he still believed the boy would bring balance to Synth Flux after facing his demons . After the three Aetheri escaped Mournis, where the Father professed his belief that Drayden was the Seeded One, Although it had truly been Vael who appeared before them, Kade came to believe, and told the Aetheri Council, that the appearance of his old mentor was simply an illusion, one manifested from their memories by the beings on Mournis; however, Drayden wasn't as confident, despite Aetheri teachings saying that it was impossible for a being to retain their identity after death. The report about Mournis did not change these Aetheri beliefs or teachings.

#### Guiding Zho

> " It is I, Sorin Vael. " " That cannot be. Dead, you are. " " No. I am part of the Living Synth Flux, Zho. " ―Vael communes to Zho during the Replica Wars

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Guiding Zho

> " It is I, Sorin Vael. " " That cannot be. Dead, you are. " " No. I am part of the Living Synth Flux, Zho. " ―Vael communes to Zho during the Replica Wars

The Replica Wars also saw the return of Vael's murderer, Vael Vreth. Believed to have been killed by Kade on Ondara, Vreth had survived, replacing his lower body with a cybernetic apparatus. Vreth sought revenge on Kade for maiming him, and the two fought on several occasions; prior to the first of these duels , Vreth recalled how he had killed Vael before being cut down himself, proving to Kade that his old foe had indeed returned. During the duel itself, he mocked Kade by recalling how he had murdered Vael, making the Aetheri Master briefly give into anger to strike against his mentor's murderer. Although Vreth was captured during the Siege of Ferrum , which occurred during the waning days of the Replica Wars, he escaped and survived the conflict.

title: Sorin Vael
text: It was not until the Replica Wars' waning days that Zho learned Vael had retained his consciousness after death. Knowing Zho was destined to be a significant player in bringing balance to Synth Flux, and that it was Zho's destiny to complete the training Vael himself did not, the late Aetheri Master spoke to Zho through Synth Flux. He guided him to Mirefall , the first leg on Zho's trials, to determine whether he was ready to learn the secrets. Vael told Zho about his training and how the Living Synth Flux fed into the Cosmic Synth Flux, allowing him to return after death. At first, Zho was only interested in the Replica Wars' truth, asking if he knew the identity of Vael Mal, but Vael could only guide Zho through his trials. The Living Synth Flux guided Zho in the form of a glowing swarm of fireflies . Later they directed Zho to the planet of Synth Flux Priestesses, where Zho could continue his trial.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Zho completed the trials and was deemed worthy of learning the secret of eternal consciousness, as Zho would one day train the person who would help Drayden bring balance to Synth Flux. Synth Flux Priestesses instructed that Vael would guide Zho's training. After the end of the Replica Wars and the fall of the Aetheri Order, Zho chose to go into exile on Mirefall, but not before telling Kade that Vael had returned from the netherworld of Synth Flux and could guide his former Adept in learning the secret. However, Orien was unable to make contact with Sorin until 9 BVE despite sometimes hearing him as a voice in his head. One time during meditation, he felt himself phase out of reality for a few moments. During this time, he felt Vael commune through Synth Flux with him, with his old Aetheri Master telling him to let go.

#### Guiding Orien Kade

> " Master Sorin." " Well, took you long enough. " " Beginning to think you'd never come. " " I was always here, Orien. You just were not ready to see. Come on. We've got a ways to go. " ―Orien Kade and Sorin reuniting

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Guiding Orien Kade

> " Master Sorin." " Well, took you long enough. " " Beginning to think you'd never come. " " I was always here, Orien. You just were not ready to see. Come on. We've got a ways to go. " ―Orien Kade and Sorin reuniting

The end of the Replica Wars also saw the fall of Kael Drayden, who was seduced to the umbra side of Synth Flux by Mal, becoming the Umbra Lord Xarn Velgor. The fall confirmed the Council's fears about Drayden's training, but he was still the Seeded One. During Orien Kade's self-imposed exile on Dunemere, where he watched over Kael's son, Joren Drayden, he frequently dwelled upon his failure to train Drayden. At one point, he traveled to Shira Drayden's grave and apologized for failing to complete Vael's promise. Kade also had possession of his master's flux blade during his exile.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Shortly following Kael's fall to the umbra side, Sorin started to push himself to emerge fully in the land of the living instead of remaining a voice. Sorin committed to the effort to ensure that Orien did not have to spend his following years on Dunemere alone. Overall, it took Sorin nearly a decade before his efforts finally met success. While it was sometime before Kade saw his former master again, he often spoke to Vael but began to fear his master would never appear. In reality, Vael was always with Kade, even if Kade was not emotionally ready to see him due to his guilt over Drayden's fall.

One morning in 16 BVE , when Drayden was three, Vael spoke to Kade after he awoke from a nightmare, warning him to get to the boy to protect him. Thus, Kade raced to the Havel Homestead , where Joren was being raised by his aunt and uncle, Brue and Owen Havel . Once there, Kade helped defend against a gang of bandits, yet Owen demanded he never return after the skirmish.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
In 9 BVE, Aetheri Master Eno Cordova recounted his friendship and introduction to Vael to Aetheri Knight Cal Kessara .

In 9 BVE, after Kade had another duel with Velgor and came to terms with Drayden's fall, Sorin appeared to Orien as the latter was riding towards Beggar's Canyon , telling his former Adept that it had taken him long enough. Orien showed amazement at his appearance, stating that he had begun to think that Sorin would never arrive. Sorin then clarified that he had always been there, and that Orien had not been ready to see him prior to that moment. Sorin then asked for Orien to continue following him, with Sorin disappearing from view as he proceeded further into the canyon, Orien following shortly. In the years after the Replica Wars, Kade and Zho completed their training to retain their consciousness after death. During his time on Dunemere, Kade continued to speak with Vael, telling him about the hardships of living in exile and Drayden's possible destiny of the Seeded One.

title: Sorin Vael
text: After Kael's fall to the umbra side, Vael continued his training to manifest himself, becoming clearer to Kade over the course of his visits to him. The two never discussed Vael's supposed mistakes whenever he traveled into the mortal universe; Kade did not blame his old master for Drayden's fall, while Vael thought his old Adept did. During an encounter with the Vorak bounty hunter Zazzik , Kade called upon his Master to give him strength to defeat the foe. Kade finally killed a resurgent Vreth in a duel on Dunemere in 2 BVE , using Vael's Ataru stance to defend himself against Vreth. In 1 BVE , Vael's voice was heard by Adept Cass Virel during his mission to a place that existed between time and space .

title: Sorin Vael
text: After Kade introduced Drayden to the life of an Aetheri, as the droids Bolt-3 and Astra-9 had arrived on Dunemere with secret plans that needed to be delivered to the Free Coalition , Drayden rushed off to the Havel Homestead, having realized the Imperium 's shock troopers would track the droids to his aunt and uncle. Vael was compelled to appear after hearing Kade call his name, taking on the exact same appearance that he had carried in life and appearing a few centimeters from his former Adept. Kade asked for his guidance, as he feared that the Imperium would capture Joren upon his return to the Havel Homestead. Already knowing the circumstances Kade was speaking of, Vael informed him that he had seen Joren's destiny go beyond the current event, listing off possible solutions that would occur, while the surrounding landscape became clearer to him. He spotted the corpses of Duskkins , feeling the memory of their deaths wash over him, but was slightly comforted when he noticed Bolt-3 and Astra-9; he believed it was the work of Synth Flux, bringing them back to where Kael's journey had begun.

title: Sorin Vael
text: The news that Joren would survive relieved Kade, yet Vael knew his former apprentice had no idea how the young man's journey would unfold. When Kade confided in him that he found it difficult to give up his exile, Vael understood it was a symptom of him adapting to the new life, informing him that he would quickly feel like an Aetheri Knight when the time came. He also congratulated his former student on remaining steadfast in his devotion to the light side. He also apologized to Kade, believing he had failed his Adept long ago when he made him train Kael. Kade disagreed, arguing that Kael was the main person at fault for his fall, but Vael resolved to wait to discuss this matter, knowing that the two of them would be together in Synth Flux soon; in the near future, Kade would sacrifice himself to save Joren and be struck down by Xarn Velgor, and Vael knew this was coming.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Vael and Kade then both felt Joren's horror at seeing his aunt and uncle, Brue and Owen Havel, dead outside their home. Even so, Kade sensed Joren's reaction at a greater remove, while Vael, due to him being of Synth Flux, could see their burned corpses in front of him, as clearly as he could see Kade. Thinking his former Adept needed guidance, he then told Kade that he had made the right choice in choosing not to tell Joren everything about Kael; he knew Joren could have gone down his father's path if Kade had revealed everything, or he could have thought Owen was right about Kade being insane, which would have resulted in him being killed with his aunt and uncle. After telling Kade to wait to reveal the truth until Joren was ready, Vael's appearance was very nearly corporeal, the clearest Kade had ever seen his master's spirit. Vael illuminated him in some of the ways he had managed it, all the while, considering that Kade did not have long to live. Sensing that Joren would soon return, he bade farewell, telling Kade that they would meet again soon. His former student did not understand the true

title: Sorin Vael
text: spirit. Vael illuminated him in some of the ways he had managed it, all the while, considering that Kade did not have long to live. Sensing that Joren would soon return, he bade farewell, telling Kade that they would meet again soon. His former student did not understand the true meaning of the statement, and Vael disappeared, returning to Synth Flux. On the DS-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station , Kade was indeed killed by Xarn Velgor to protect Joren. After his death, Kade found himself overwhelmed by visions of the past, present, and future; among the people he saw was Vael, including when he was slain by Vreth and when his voice told him to protect Joren in 16 BVE. While worried about not completing Joren's training as he lived through his past, relived the present, and saw glimpses of the future, Kade again heard that Joren had called out to him on the Void Core; hearing Vael's voice, louder than it had been for years, telling him to go with Joren, Kade ensured his spirit would remain with the Aetheri trainee. Thus, after his death, Kade first appeared as a disembodied voice, telling Joren to flee the Void Core with his friends, and then later to guide Joren through the Battle of Cinderfall , helping the young Synth Flux-sensitive to destroy the Void Core.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Zho, meanwhile, had hidden himself on Mirefall, staying away from the Imperium, but also growing lonely over the years. Fortunately, he knew how to call out to Vael for company. One of the few personal items Zho brought with him was Vael's cloak , which he made into his blanket. Around the time of Kade's death, Zho was preparing to move to the lowlands of Mirefall for the dry season, and he found himself questioning how long ago Vael had died when he counted his personal items for the journey. He also realized that, while people strong in Synth Flux could sometimes leave an imprint of themselves in what they owned, too many years had gone by for any trace of the Aetheri Master to remain in the cloak, if he had ever felt such a trace at all. As he always did, he gathered his cane, several seeds, a pot made by Kade, and Vael's cloak before making his way down to his lowland hut.

title: Sorin Vael
text: As he journeyed, he felt Kade and Velgor's duel in Synth Flux, taking his focus away as an old Imperial probe droid finally located him. After throwing Kade's pot into the droid to destroy it, he sensed Kade's death, distracting him as two other probes appeared. One fired and hit Zho's carrying bag, which he rushed to to protect Vael's cloak from burning. After taking out the droids, he saw that the cloak was only slightly singed and that his seeds were fine. Afterward, Vael, currently in the netherworld of Synth Flux , laughed at Zho, which the Aetheri Master sensed. Once Zho moved back into his lowland hut, he trimmed the cloak, which also meant it better compensated for his shrinking size. Several days after his move, Zho, missing the friends he had lost, called out to Vael to appear from the netherworld several times, only to be unable to sense him.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Vael was in fact preoccupied, so Kade instead appeared. During his visit, Kade quipped that Zho's encounter with the probe droids could not have been too dangerous, given that he had saved Vael's cloak, annoying Zho. Afterward, Kade asked him to train Joren, which Zho reluctantly agreed to.

#### The lives and times of Joren and Nyla

> " Every Aetheri who ever lived lives in you. We stand behind you, Nyla. Rise. " ―Sorin speaks to Nyla

In the aftermath of the Battle of Cinderfall, Velgor was shot down over the planet Vrogas Vas . During a confrontation with Free Coalition forces on the planet, Velgor found an ancient Aetheri Sanctum , where he heard disembodied voices of people from his past, including Vael. A few years later, Kade appeared as a physical spirit to tell Joren to train with Zho on Mirefall. He continued to manifest himself to help guide Joren through his training.

title: Sorin Vael
text: It was on Mirefall that Zho fulfilled the destiny first spoken of by Synth Flux Priestesses, training Joren to become an Aetheri Knight. When Drayden left his training early to save his friends, Kade questioned if the boy was the last hope of the Aetheri, hearing Vael, along with any Aetheri whose actions had led to current circumstances, in his voice. Vael himself later appeared as a vision to Joren in the Living Sea of Gazian , as the imprint of long-past Aetheri Master Elzar Mann imparted wisdom upon Drayden. After Drayden returned to Mirefall, Zho died shortly after and passed on into Synth Flux, where he retained his identity. Through the training Zho gave Joren, the boy confronted and redeemed his father from the umbra side, and Kael killed Vael Mal. Through this act and his own death, Kael helped defeat the Imperium, brought balance to Synth Flux, and was able to return as a spirit as well. By killing Mal and sacrificing himself, Vael's strongly-held belief from thirty-six years ago was finally proven right; Kael Drayden was the Seeded One.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
In the years following Kael's redemption and fulfillment of the prophecy, Joren embarked on a quest to rediscover the Aetheri Order's forgotten history in hopes to re-establish it. In his search for Aetheri knowledge, Joren learned about the life of Vael, his relationship with Orien Kade, his encounter with Synth Flux Priestesses, and the role he played in his father's training. While Vael was not related to the Draydens by blood, his close connection to the family was noted by Joren in his book The Secrets of the Aetheri , which chronicled the Aetheri Order's history.

In 35 AVE , during the Battle of Umbrale , Nyla heard Vael's voice among the voices of many Aetheri of the past who aided her with destroying the resurrected Vael Mal for good. "Every Aetheri who ever lived lives in you," he told her, adding that they stood behind her.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
### Ideals and spirituality

#### A unique Aetheri

> " Do not defy the Council, Master, not again. " " I shall do what I must, Orien. " ―Orien Kade and Sorin Vael — Link ▶️ ( file info ) Sorin Vael was a human male who stood 1.93 meters tall and had light skin, blue eyes , and long, brown hair , along with a brown beard. Though he had risen to the rank of Aetheri Master, Vael did not always agree with the structures and rules of the Aetheri Order. Vael was known to prefer following the spirit of the Aetheri Code than the letter and was willing to rebuff the Aetheri Council. Where all Aetheri knew you could love others as long as you were not possessive, Vael was less concerned with the dangers of strong connections in comparison to his peers. While he knew Synth Flux could often present more questions than answers, he nevertheless trusted in it and its guidance. As an Adept, his commitment to the Order was tested by his romantic relationship on Feldora, but he ended up returning to the Aetheri. While he did keep an Emberfall fire diamond he was gifted on Feldora for twenty years as a prized possession, specifically keeping it in a pouch on his belt to ensure it was with him every day, he would ultimately give up the stone to Pax Maripher and Rahara Wick, reflecting

title: Sorin Vael
text: he did keep an Emberfall fire diamond he was gifted on Feldora for twenty years as a prized possession, specifically keeping it in a pouch on his belt to ensure it was with him every day, he would ultimately give up the stone to Pax Maripher and Rahara Wick, reflecting to himself that it was the memories, not physical mementos, that mattered. While during the Replica Wars other Aetheri came to focus on meditation to try to understand the future, Vael lived in the moment. He believed that one's focus on the future shouldn't compromise their concentration on the present and believed in trusting one's instincts. Vael was more interested in obeying the will of Synth Flux than caring about climbing the ranks of Aetheri hierarchy, leading to his lack of care about joining the Council despite his own apprentice, Orien Kade, insisting he could secure a spot. Vael further believed that an Aetheri needed to interpret the Aetheri Code for themself, arguing that otherwise the Code would become a prison. Although he was unconcerned whenever someone claimed he was a coward, Vael came to have a distaste for how many people, even people on Vantor, saw the Aetheri as warriors and political servants. Although Zho simply thought that people who could not use Synth Flux would be confused by those who could, Vael was faced with a great turmoil due to his concerns as he understood that the Order's actions reflected who they really were.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Instead of focusing on what he had expected out of situations, Vael decided it was best to focus on what actually was happening. Vael took the time to truly look at and understand the people he worked with. In the case of Queen Lira Ondar, she reflected that he had, at times, looked too deeply into her; Vael realized that she had swapped places with one of her Handmaidens, making him one of the few people who was ever able to deduce the deception tactic. Keeping it a secret that he knew, he would address his questions to the fake queen, making those around them, like fellow Handmaiden Saché, think he had been fooled. Ultimately, Vael and Orien Kade taught Ondar that the Aetheri were sentient beings like herself, even if she did not understand their teachings.

title: Sorin Vael
text: While the Aetheri Council would likely have disagreed with his assessment, Vael believed that the Aetheri being based on Vantor was part of the problem with the Order's perception as warriors and political servants; their Vantor temple enabled them to become and be seen as a synth flux that served the Republic, even possibly making themselves believe it. Vael often entered into debates with Aetheri Master Drevan Koss, but neither of them enjoyed those disagreements. They were, in any case, strong friends despite their theological disagreements. Over the years, the two of them grew close, with Koss describing Vael as an "old friend" by the time of Vael's death in 32 BVE. When working together, the two Aetheri would rely on each other's courage, combat knowledge, and intelligence to become an effective team. On one occasion, the two played dejarik with the additional challenge that the loser would owe the winner a favor; Koss agreed to the challenge despite knowing Vael would best him, wanting to simply see how effectively Vael could defeat him in the game.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Ultimately, Vael could be described as being like a maverick when compared to his fellow Aetheri. Although it was a rare viewpoint, he was not the only "maverick" Aetheri during the late Republic Era, as Master Tu-Anh was also active in the Order. During the Replica Wars, Kade compared the two while overlooking Tu-Anh's body after her death. Still, such a defiant outlook towards the council was rare in Vael's time. Had Vael been alive during the High Republic Era, Kade once reasoned, he would likely have become a Wayseeker , an Aetheri who operated without direct council oversight to follow the will of Synth Flux as they felt it. Vael was also considered to be an Aetheri Vanguard .

#### Respect in prophecies and balance

> " We must all interpret the Code for ourselves or it ceases to be a living pact and becomes nothing but a prison cell. " ―Sorin Vael, on the Aetheri Code

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Respect in prophecies and balance

> " We must all interpret the Code for ourselves or it ceases to be a living pact and becomes nothing but a prison cell. " ―Sorin Vael, on the Aetheri Code

Although the other Aetheri of his era thought little of prophecies and argued that looking into the future could be dangerous and uncertain, Vael respected the prophecies made by the Aetheri mystics of old. Even though he had in his younger years, Vael did not view prophecies to be literal. Nevertheless, he did not take them to be meaningless, and he felt that learning what the ancient mystics believed helped tie the Aetheri Order to its history. Still, he did also know that trying to learn the future could be considered a form of control, which could lead to the umbra side. Ultimately, he told Orien Kade that explaining his view of the prophecies was "complex."

title: Sorin Vael
text: To Vael, the ultimate purpose of the Aetheri was to find balance. Although he once pondered whether Synth Flux wanted him to learn from the umbra side, he came to the conclusion that the umbra side's corrupting nature made it so it could never create balance. However, much like his argument about the Aetheri Code needing to be a living pact instead of a prison cell, he also believed that, if the Aetheri Order acted too rigidly in its beliefs, it too could not achieve balance. Thus, he believed that the Aetheri needed to make a compromise between both extremes; they could not bend to the umbra side, yet they also could not become too rigid. Vael used his understanding of balance to help the Priestess of Wooda, Th'er, telling her how she could find compromise with people who had faced similar struggles to her, which would allow her to enrich her people while also preserving their culture.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Similarly, Vael displayed a great respect towards Vorak culture. He saw that their connection to their homeworld was like a balance, further thinking that their Life Day celebrations were a celebration of Synth Flux. He also respected the wisdom held by members of the Vorak species, knowing that it could teach both him and his Adept, Kade, many things. His understanding of Vorak culture also helped in conventional problems; he knew it was odd for any Vorak to be away from their family on Life Day, helping him to realize something was behind the disappearance of Balfus. Even after his death and becoming part of Synth Flux, he continued to respect balance and see it as necessary.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Most other Aetheri did not seem to share the same concerns as Vael about how they should act. According to Vorr during his ongoing seduction of Beno Karrick to the umbra side, the Aetheri believed their rules made them stronger, and so continued to use a seemingly endless series of rules and codes. Much like how Vael had compared being too rigid to a tree branch that breaks off in the wind after refusing to accommodate it, Vorr told Karrick the rigid nature of the Aetheri Order helped to bring about its downfall at the end of the Replica Wars. Following his death, Vael knew of how Owen and Brue Havel took in Joren Drayden despite the risks of raising the boy; he considered them examples of pure heroism, becoming pained and horrified by their deaths.

#### Beyond the world of the living

title: Sorin Vael
text:
#### Beyond the world of the living

> " You're very nearly corporeal. I've never seen you appear like this. " " It is a matter of learning to both claim the physical world and detach one's self from it. A matter of finding center, of calming one's soul and giving one's self over completely to Synth Flux. Some Aetheri choose to transition between life and death in that way, though I could scarcely have imagined it when I was alive. Even after death, we continue to learn. " " I look forward to learning the art someday. Hopefully in the distant future. " ―Orien Kade and Sorin Vael

Even during his life, Vael understood that Synth Flux was larger than a single Aetheri's connection to it, even believing it was larger than the concepts of life and death. As part of the Living Synth Flux after his death, Vael was able to understand how every aspect of every environment played a part in the great song of the Whills ; he saw that nothing was barren, as Synth Flux existed within everything, even understanding how the desert of Dunemere was not truly barren, given everything that made it up.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Although his identity had survived death, he no longer had an "individual existence;" no longer existing as "Sorin Vael" and instead existing as part of Synth Flux, he was unconcerned with linear time, individuality, awareness, and consciousness, even existing beyond what he believed to be the "crude" language used by living humans. Although he thought being part of Synth Flux was a better state, he nevertheless fondly, but distantly, remembered the vitality of his mortal life. He could leave his unity with Synth Flux to commune with the living, yet such an action caused pain, making the definition of himself separate from Synth Flux. Despite providing a vantage point for the complex physical universe, the pain of entering back into individual existence was only endurable to Vael because he understood he could return to Synth Flux quickly and because he knew he may be needed. He also found that using his old Adept's name was worth separating from being one with Synth Flux.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Existing as a fracture of Synth Flux, he understood that his past existence was best summarized by his name, given that it was who he was during his temporal life. He guided Zho through Mirefall to learn the secret of eternal consciousness; but, Zho was interested in knowing if Vael, existing outside of normal time, could tell him Vael Mal's true identity. Although Vael hinted that he knew the truth, he explained he could only guide Zho towards greater knowledge, not provide him with the answers. Vael's training to retain his identity after death led him to new philosophies unknown to the Aetheri Order at the time. Vael learned that there were two sides to Synth Flux, a Living Synth Flux channeled by the energies of all living beings, and the Cosmic Synth Flux into which it fed. It was this symbiotic relationship that allowed Synth Flux to bind the galaxy together and speak to living beings through the synthcells.

title: Sorin Vael
text: After learning how to manifest himself into the physical universe instead of only existing as a voice, he could draw upon the memories of his life, using them to form into a shape that appeared like how his body had. He could feel everything, from his flesh to his robes, form around him; when he was summoned by Orien Kade after Joren Drayden ran to see what had become of his aunt and uncle, Vael found that removing his hood came naturally. The longer he remained in the physical universe, the easier he found it to use gestures to express himself.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Vael thought that the most beautiful type of mastery was learning to let go, such as how Aetheri like himself let go from the mortal universe. Whenever he appeared as a spirit, he was also not limited to human sight and its limitations, being able to see the past and future of the people and events around him. Appearing as a spirit required balance and devotion to Synth Flux, with Vael explaining he needed to both claim and detach himself from the mortal universe. It took nearly a decade of training to be able to enter such a state. The longer he remained in the mortal realm, the more corporeal he became. He was even able to smell the cremation of the Duskkins.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
Finding human lives incredibly brief and death an inevitable—but almost a neutral—event, Vael had come to believe that it was one's journey through Synth Flux that mattered. Believing that truths always eventually came out, he was able to know what living people would call the future, as he no longer existed in linear time. When he appeared on Dunemere to speak with Kade, he felt the deaths of nearby Duskkins, specifically feeling the memory of their helplessness and fear wash over his consciousness. Finding their deaths meaningless, Vael was comforted by the sight of Astra-9 and Bolt-3, knowing it proved time to be a circle; Synth Flux had ensured they were present once more on the desert world, making the beginning of a journey its end as well.

Vael understood that he could never have understood the process of appearing as a spirit when he was alive. Whenever Vael intended to return to Synth Flux, his awareness spread out, again allowing him to sense how every aspect of a planet fit together to form the system of life. Upon letting go, he again would release his name and form to become one with the energy field that was Synth Flux.

title: Sorin Vael
text:
### Apprentice of Varek

> " I once knew someone, a teacher, a mentor. Someone who I looked to as my guide in all things. He made a choice—he did something that I couldn't fathom. It created a feeling inside me. A doubt and fear that I never thought I could overcome. I was lost for a good while. Shaken to my core. But over time, that fear and doubt became something else—it became resolve. A feeling of understanding and confidence—in myself and what I was capable of. It would have been normal to resent him. To blame this other person's decisions for whatever errors I made. But that would also have been the easy path, a lazy and passive one. […] I trusted myself. I worked harder. I accepted that one man's mistakes would never carry the weight of my own. I studied the Aetheri teachings. I interpreted them as best I could. And I listened and learned. We are all flawed, Lizel. We all make errors of judgment. It's how we recover from them that defines us. " ―Sorin Vael talks to Lizel Liit about his thoughts on Varek after the man left the Aetheri Order

title: Sorin Vael
text: Varek was Vael's master and friend. Further described by Vael as a teacher and mentor figure who could guide him through any issue, Vael was nonetheless shocked by Varek's decision to leave the Aetheri Order, with Varek's choice also creating fear and doubt inside his former disciple. In that mindset, he found himself lost and made several mistakes. In time, however, those concerns Vael faced would give way to resolve he described as confidence and understanding. While he suspected resenting Varek would be a normal reaction, he also decided it was the easy, lazy, and passive path; instead, Vael turned inward and towards his studies, concluding in the end that everyone made mistakes, yet it was how one decided to respond to those errors that mattered the most. His experience after Varek's decision and his time healing gave him wisdom he imparted to Lizel Liit .

title: Sorin Vael
text:
In secret, Varek fell to the umbra side and became the Umbra Lord Vael Varek, yet Vael remained a crack in Varek's armor. On Pyralis, Varek claimed to Kade that he wished Vael were still alive so the late Aetheri Master could have helped him with the Fractio of Independent Systems. Kade rejected the idea that Vael would have joined Varek. Still, Varek told Kade that Vael knew about the corruption in the Galactic Senate and might have joined the Dissident cause—especially if he had learned that the Republic was under Vael Mal's control, although, in truth, the CIS was just as much under Umbra control as their rival state. Shortly into the war, Kade invoked Vael's memory in debate with Varek concerning a mission to the neutral planet Cato Geltaria , which created a minor but present shift in the Umbra Lord's demeanor. Trying to hide his reaction, Varek only responded by noting Vael had been an honorable figure, ultimately agreeing that the CIS would let Kade carry out the mission when Kade declared that he carried on Vael's teachings and, thus, could be trusted as well.

### Mentor to Orien Kade and empathetic nature

title: Sorin Vael
text:
### Mentor to Orien Kade and empathetic nature

#### Training the Aetheri Adept

> " You've been a good apprentice, Orien. And you're a much wiser man than I am. I foresee you will become a great Aetheri Knight. " ―Sorin Vael, to Orien Kade #### Training the Aetheri Adept

> " You've been a good apprentice, Orien. And you're a much wiser man than I am. I foresee you will become a great Aetheri Knight. " ―Sorin Vael, to Orien Kade

During his service to the Aetheri Order, Vael took on Orien Kade as his Adept learner. Although they were able to work well together, both had major differences in their view of the Aetheri; the by-the-book Kade was more willing to obey the orders of the Aetheri Council, being willing to fill out detailed reports of their missions, while Vael was willing to hold back on such duties, partly because he knew Kade would handle them, and disobey the Council. Kade and Vael's conflicting natures initially caused friction in their relationship, but both grew close over time. Though he still did not entirely agree with it, Kade came to understand it was normal for Vael to disagree with the Council, viewing his Master's actions as a viable alternative to their orders, as it avoided giving into absolutes. Even so, he always preferred to have advanced warning when they were to go on unapproved missions, at least because it allowed him to pack.

title: Sorin Vael
text: With an Aetheri Master who had a more "relaxed" attitude instead of a rigid reading of the Aetheri Code , Kade understood that his lessons were often unconventional, but he did not display annoyance with that, even if Vael's attempts at moving him away from a standard Aetheri viewpoint—asking Kade to embody the spirit of the Aetheri Code instead of a literal reading—instead resulted in Kade trying even harder to embody the traditional Aetheri spirit. Vael nevertheless defended his unconventional choices, believing that Aetheri could not learn new lessons if they only stuck with their specific teachings. Beyond thinking Kade was always well learned in his answers to questions, Vael also truly trusted his Adept; when he and many Voraks were captured on Life Day, he trusted in Kade to rescue them. He also felt sustained by Kade's strength.

title: Sorin Vael
text: Vael also tasked Kade with reading political bills with him whenever he got a feeling that something was wrong. While Kade was annoyed by how time consuming the process was, he respected that, and was further annoyed by how, his mentor's feelings on such matters were often correct.
