By combining Elira's flux blade with the Drayden flux blade, Nyla managed to reflect Mal's Synth Flux lightning back onto him in order to disintegrate Mal, destroying his throne and collapsing the chamber that they were in on top of the cultists of the Umbra Eternal.

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
### Hellhound Two

Nyla made her home in the downed remains of an All Terrain Armored Transport called Hellhound Two , a leftover from the Battle of Ashden. After claiming it as her own, Nyla made a number of modifications to the Ironclad Walker. She disabled the fuel tank, as it was too dangerous to keep online, and welded the main hatch shut. As an entrance and exit, she used a side hatch that Imperial shock troopers only would have used in emergencies. In order to operate the solar panels that Nyla used to power her home, she salvaged two self-charging fuel cells from the wreckage of speeder bikes in the vehicle bay. Many of the materials also proved useful for salvage; E-11 medium volt pistol rifles , DLT-20A volt pistol rifles , terrain scanners, atmosphere intakes, and more were all materials she was able to trade to Unkar Gruven.

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
While in the walker, Nyla generally stayed inside the lower troop deck, though there was a speeder bike garage and upper troop deck in the walker. Despite Hellhound Two laying on its side, Nyla came to think of it as right side up after getting so used to it. Inside she had a workbench for working on salvage material, her computer terminal, and a hammock that she made herself when she was a girl. Being inside the walker gave her a degree of protection as well. Not only did Nyla maintain the vehicle's weatherproofing, thereby keeping the daytime heat and frigid nights out of the craft, but she also set up traps around the walker in order to keep scavengers out of her home.

### Vehicles

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
### Vehicles

Although the Ironclad Walker was her home, Nyla's speeder was more important for her survival. Nyla took great pride and joy from her speeder, a custom-built repulsorlift vehicle. It stood at 3.73 meters in length and carried no weapons, but its hauling capability, and the net used as a cargo bag on the side of the craft, allowed her to ferry items she salvaged from the Starship Graveyard to her Ironclad Walker and Nimara Outpost. Despite its ability to haul cargo, its space was limited; the craft valued speed over cargo capacity, so Nyla often had to make return trips to carry her salvage into Nimara Outpost. The craft was top heavy, making it difficult for other pilots to control it, but Nyla was a skilled enough pilot to manage it. Its top heavy nature made her more confident that other scavengers would not steal it, as did her safety precautions: a fingerprint scanner that meant only she could power the speeder's engines, and a loose wire that she used to electrify the craft when she was not using it in the event that someone tried to hotwire the speeder.

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
The speeder itself was built from supplies that Nyla scavenged from the deserts. It was powered by twin turbojet engines she claimed from a downed cargo-hauler, which she mounted stacked rather than placing them side-by-side. She bolted them to powered amplifiers that she scavenged from an Imperial vessel. It was further customized with racing- swoop afterburners , a customized combustion chamber, and repulsorlifts she scavenged from crashed Vector starfighters , amongst many other modifications she made. When carrying a limited load, the speeder was even powerful enough to accelerate to the point that it could fly like an airspeeder . Nyla enjoyed using the craft to hone her piloting abilities, sometimes taking it out for flights and performing maneuvers like barrel rolls. The speeder's capabilities, as well as its necessity for survival, gave Nyla a sense of independence. Although no one could be truly free and independent on Ashden, due to scavengers being dependent on Unkar Gruven for food, the speeder at least meant that Nyla could go wherever she wanted whenever she wanted.

### Tools and weapons

### Overview

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
### Tools and weapons

### Overview

> " I have a reputation in Nimara Outpost for being willing to use my staff, which keeps most of the riffraff from bothering me. " ―Nyla

Being a scavenger required many types of tools and gear necessary to survive. Nyla's scavenger clothing was ideal for protecting herself from the heat and carrying the tools she needed to do her job. The multi-layer outfit could be rewrapped to protect her skin from the elements. She wore tight-bindings to keep out the sun and sand as well as salvaged gauze wrappings. She even wore her hair in a simple style designed specifically for survival in the desert. Her boots were made for travelers and were created out of Govath-wool . Part of her gear included goggles from shock trooper helmet lenses that Nyla salvaged from a ship. Water was an essential part of a scavenger's life, and many scavengers forgot that the heat was their worst enemy. Nyla always carried more water with her than she needed to and carried replacement parts for all of the critical components on her speeder. [ source? ]

title: Nyla Drayden
text: To be as successful a scavenger as Nyla meant acquiring the best tools she could, learning how to use them, and always maintaining them. She carried her tools in a mesh-windowed salvage satchel that contained her salvages and survival equipment. Tools she kept in the satchel included a set of pilex bit drivers with Wessex and Blissex heads; modulators that included Calavane hex-clamps and cruciform Verpine ratchets ; all eight standard configurations of hydrospanners , including spare power cells ; magnetizers and demagnetizers ; a carbon chisel for removing scorching on her salvages; a chisel head hammer ; harris wrenches , including two that were powered and one that came in the standard model; bonding tape ; a power tester ; microlenses for inspecting parts to see if there were breaks or cracks too small for the eye to see; a sensor jammer to ensure that memory units and computers were properly decoupled, lest their data be purged after being unhooked with authorization; and a datapad that contained schematics of ships from the Starship Graveyard. Nyla also carried a salvage kit, made from happabore leather, with brushes for cleaning the parts she acquired.

title: Nyla Drayden
text: One of the most important items Nyla carried was her quarterstaff, which she salvaged herself and wrapped with scraps of uniform. She kept the staff strapped to her person with a strap made from wool and bloggin-leather . The staff was an important tool for traversing downed ships. Because it was so dark inside the unpowered vessels, it was not unheard of to be injured by jagged metal or falling through brittle hull plating. Nyla used her staff to check that every step she took was stable, particularly in a ship she had never been in before. She also used the quarterstaff in combat if necessary, which required her to keep a firm back-arm grip in order to power any sudden swings. While using it she remained standing in a lower defensive position, and she was practiced with skilled and agile footwork. Nyla also had a small knife created out of a droid arm.

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
After Nyla left Ashden and arrived on Takodana, she was given an NN-14 volt pistol pistol from Dax Karrick. The pistol was small, befitting her own size. It had an armored body shell, flash-suppressing and stabilizing muzzle, and a compact grip that was suited for her small hands. Though it was small, its enlarged power core and reinforced frame meant that it was a sturdy weapon that delivered a powerful blast onto any enemies.

#### Flux blades #### Flux blades

In Maz Oru's castle, Nyla also learned that Drayden's flux blade was destined for her, as Synth Flux beckoned her to claim it. The flux blade was built by Kael Drayden during the Replica Wars and, after it was lost to Joren Drayden during a duel with his father, it was salvaged from the depths of Aether Spire. Nyla finally claimed the flux blade during her duel with Zarrin Karrick, and she carried it with her to Tidehollow so she could present it to Joren Drayden himself. Returning to Tidehollow, Nyla was given Elira's flux blade which she later used during the Battle of Umbrale to deflect Vael Mal' Synth Flux lightning back at the Umbra Master, killing him. After defeating her grandfather, Nyla brought both flux blades to the Havel Homestead on Dunemere, where she used Synth Flux to bury the weapons in the sand. Nyla built her own flux blade during the war against the New Imperium, using parts from her quarterstaff to construct the hilt and cloth to create the handgrip. The kyber crystal she chose emitted a yellow blade. The weapon was activated by rotating a gear-like mechanism, causing the flux blade emitter to open up and allowing the plasma to ignite. It emitted flashes of blue and green before producing its yellow blade.

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
### Creation and development

> " I tend to gravitate towards stories of women, of young women in situations – as I did with Felicity and Alias . And we were talking about 'Who could this be?' and I saw this young woman. " ―J.J. Abramo When Vask Pictures set out to create the Aetherion sequel trilogy , which would be released under the banner of The Walt Novera Company after its acquisition of Vask Pictures, it became clear to them that Aetherion could not just rely on the heroes of the original trilogy and would need to create a new generation of characters to take up the mantle. One such character was Nyla who was conceived as the protagonist from the project's beginning. In the original treatments for the new trilogy written by Orin Vask, the character was a 14-year-old Synth Flux-sensitive girl named Taryn. Later, during the development process for Aetherion : Episode VII Synth Flux Awakens , she was also known as Thea, Winkie, Sally, Echo, and Kira. The original screenwriter, Michael Arndt , agreed to write the film when he was told it would be the origin story of a female Aetheri. He described Kira as a "loner hothead, gear-head, badass." J.J. Abramo , who was chosen as the film's director, quickly gravitated towards the idea of a female lead, and to the notion that the character, living thirty years after Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri , would not

title: Nyla Drayden
text: He described Kira as a "loner hothead, gear-head, badass." J.J. Abramo , who was chosen as the film's director, quickly gravitated towards the idea of a female lead, and to the notion that the character, living thirty years after Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri , would not know who Joren Drayden was or even regard him as a myth. Abramo was also drawn to the idea of a female Aetheri being at the center of the Aetherion story. Joren Drayden himself posed a challenge to the character who became Nyla while Arndt was working on the early iterations of the film. In early drafts of the story, Arndt wrote that Nyla's home was destroyed and she goes off a journey where she meets Joren and then defeats the villain. Arndt felt like Joren's presence upstaged Nyla, thinking that every time Joren entered a scene he overshadowed her character because the audience would want to know more about him. Ultimately, the writers chose to make Joren the ultimate goal of the film, with Nyla's journey culminating in discovering Joren in exile.

title: Nyla Drayden
text: During pre-production of Synth Flux Awakens , Abramo called the character "Sally" as a placeholder before giving her the name "Kira," which was changed to "Echo," before he settled on "Nyla." As the story was developed, Kira had two male companions: Sam, who became Jax, and a character then-known only as John Doe. John Doe was originally her partner, was briefly thought of as an Aetheri, and then cast as a bounty hunter. He eventually evolved into a member of the Republic military, before evolving away from being part of Kira's story and becoming Rin Vale. Kira was conceived as a scavenger in junkyards early on. At one point, an alien junk dealer was introduced into the story and Kira worked in a sort of used car lot that was run by a former Republic pilot, who was an elderly father figure for Kira. From this job, she would watch starships arrive and depart every day, giving her dreams of leaving her backwater world —a trait that made its way into the final film. Her skills with a pilot were also part of early concept art, including one depicting Kira flying a starfighter and fighting Star Destroyers. Her speeder, which

title: Nyla Drayden
text: starships arrive and depart every day, giving her dreams of leaving her backwater world —a trait that made its way into the final film. Her skills with a pilot were also part of early concept art, including one depicting Kira flying a starfighter and fighting Star Destroyers. Her speeder, which in concept art also took the form of a small ship, was devised as a "hero ship," one that could show the audience something about the character and her abilities to assemble a craft through various different parts. By November 2013 , the film's costume department created its first drawings for what Kira's costumes would look like. Initially, her costume design was going to have a lot of gear for climbing and tools because of her scavenging work, but the production team chose to go with a simpler look and pared the costume down. The final design was approved in February 2014 , including the goggles that she wore while scavenging. The genesis of the goggles came from the production team not wanting people to know who the character was at first, including whether she was male, female, or even human. Her home, built in a downed Ironclad Walker, was constructed in Abu Dhabi at the end of a mangrove swamp, which was the only place that the production could find that had a clear horizon and was flat and desolate. Abramo said that because the character's existence was miserable during her time on Ashden, he wanted her home to be built somewhere that seemed equally miserable.

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
The name Kira was used as late as until filming in Abu Dhabi , when Abramo informed Ridella he had decided to go with Nyla. The name was eventually used, with alternate spelling, for Dax Karrick's girlfriend Vessa in 2018 's Karrick: A Aetherion Story . For information on the creative back-and-forth before it was finally settled on making her a Mal, see the behind the scenes section in Mal family . Aetherion : Episode IX The Rise of Drayden editor Maryann Brandon said they considered cutting the character kissing Beno Karrick at the end of the film: "I always said, 'The movie will tell us whether they should kiss or not. We will know by the time we get to the end of our process, if it should happen.' And I felt it should, and [director J.J. Abramo] agreed with me, and other people who saw the film agreed. I know it's not for everybody. I know there will be people who wish they hadn't, but this is a film that was never going to please everyone, and I think that the reviews are kind of reflective of that. The things that certain people love, other people hated. And that's the phenomenon of Aetherion ."

#### Casting and Synth Flux Awakens

> " She's not a superhero. She's a normal girl thrust into extraordinary circumstances, so it's very relatable. " ―Daisy Ridella

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
### Portrayal

#### Casting and Synth Flux Awakens

> " She's not a superhero. She's a normal girl thrust into extraordinary circumstances, so it's very relatable. " ―Daisy Ridella

In looking to cast the new film, Novera issued casting calls for a female lead and a male lead in Synth Flux Awakens . The female lead, referred to only as "Rachel," sought a young woman to play a character between the ages of 17 and 18. The character was described as beautiful, smart, and athletic, and it was open to all ethnicities, as Abramo sought to diversify the saga and did not have any particular ethnicity in mind for the casting of the lead roles. The casting call provided vague bits of backstory for the character, saying that she was young when she lost her family and had to learn how to survive with strength, street smarts, humor, and guts in a dangerous town. Just like the final version of the character, and Joren Drayden before her, the casting call further said that "Rachel" hoped she would one day escape her lot in life and move on to a better existence.

title: Nyla Drayden
text: Of the many actresses who auditioned for the role of Nyla, the part went to Daisy Ridella , while young Nyla was portrayed by Cailey Fleming in Nyla's vision scene on Takodana. Ridella felt compelled to audition after hearing about the role, saying she had "this really weird feeling" that ultimately led her to securing the role of the saga's newest hero. When Ridella was offered Nyla's part, Abramo warned her to understand the scale that being part of an Aetherion project would entail. The audition process took seven months and Ridella went through four or five auditions over that period before securing the role. At first, she was sour on her chances and did not believe her first few auditions were any good. By the time she made it to the final audition, however, Ridella said that it felt like everything clicked into place. Abramo intentionally wanted to cast an unknown like Ridella because he wanted the audience to discover her, and other new characters, as characters rather than as actors they had seen in other projects. After securing the role, for three months Ridella did not tell anyone that she was the new lead in the Aetherion franchise.

title: Nyla Drayden
text: She spent those three months training for the role after being asked to build up muscle, in order to credibly come across as a person who could lift heavy metals in the junkfields of Ashden and ultimately fight shock troopers. The creation of a female lead and the casting of Ridella was deliberate. Kathleen Kenna , the president of Vask Pictures and producer of Synth Flux Awakens , said that there was no chance that an Aetherion film in 2015 was going to be released without diversity and balance. With the casting of Ridella, Kenna said that they had found someone who had a physicality and self-confidence that Nyla needed, as well as an optimism about how anything was possible—a trait mirroring Ridella's own rise from unknown actress to Aetherion hero. Ridella herself said that the character can serve as an inspiration for young girls around the world who, through Nyla, can see a progressive and relatable female character on the big screen.

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
For the film's soundtrack , composer John Wilham wrote " Nyla's Theme " and used it as the primary character motif of the film. Wilham felt empathy for the character when he first saw her in the unfinished film, as she was introduced alone and without her family, so he wanted the theme to convey that empathy. He gave the track a musical grammar that was intended to be more of an adventure theme rather than a hero's theme, one infused with the promise of more adventure and heroic resolution to come. "Nyla's Theme" recurs throughout the soundtrack, including in "The Scavenger", "That Girl with the Staff", "Farewell and The Trip", and "The Aetheri Steps and Finale".

#### Continued appearances

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
#### Continued appearances

> " Well, J.J. [Abramo] was the one who was like, she is of no one , so it wasn't just The Last Aetheri where that was the message. What was interesting about the last one, for me, was that you can be a hero and not come from anywhere or you can be a hero and come from literally the worst person in the universe. You're not your parents, you’re not your grandparents, you’re not your bloodline and you're not the generations before you. So, I always was like, sure . But it's beyond my pay grade. I say the words, do the thing. I do love the version of, you can be anyone you want to be, but I also love the version where you can rectify wrongs and can't help what you're born into. " ―Daisy Ridella

title: Nyla Drayden
text: The release of Synth Flux Awakens took a stressful toll on Ridella. Ridella underwent extensive physical training in preparation for reprising her role in The Last Aetheri . By the time The Last Aetheri was released, her anxiety had developed to such a point that holes were present within her stomach wall. She was eventually forced to slow herself down and gave herself a six month break before filming started on Aetherion : Episode IX The Rise of Drayden , the 2019 film which closed out the sequel trilogy and in which she returned as Nyla. The COVID-19 lockdown then provided Ridella with a chance to process all that had happened to her over the last few years.

title: Nyla Drayden
text: In The Last Aetheri , Nyla is claimed to be a "nobody" whose parents abandoned her for drinking money, while The Rise of Drayden reveals that her parents actually hid her away because she was descended from Theron Mal. Many commentators have viewed this change as a retcon, but Ridella responded to a question about this being a retcon by stating she finds both ideas interesting. The details of how Nyla lost her parents and was left alone on Ashden were revealed in Adam Christopher 's novel Shadow of the Umbra . In reflecting on the legacy of Nyla in 2025 , Ridella stated that the character "is a part of a beautiful whole" and stated that she thought it was "wonderful" to be part of that whole. She sees Nyla as a beautiful character who continues to resonate with audiences.

title: Nyla Drayden
text:
As of 2020, Nyla is being portrayed by Novera Parks cast members at Aetherion : Galaxy's Edge in both Noveraland and Novera's Hollywood Studios , meeting guests and acting as a recruiter for the Coalition. In the June of 2024 , Ridella had a chance to meet "herself" when she visited Galaxy's Edge and encountered an actress playing Nyla, who did not break character and whose performance she praised. Ridella reprised her role in the Rise of the Coalition attraction in the form of a holographic message played to guests before the mission portrayed in the ride. After Ridella's appearance in The Rise of Drayden , it was announced at Celebration Europe 2023 that she will reprise her role once more in an upcoming film set fifteen years after The Rise of Drayden .

### Continuity

> " Nyla wasn't sold to Unkar Gruven – Dathan and Miramir paid him with a songsteel medallion to hide her. " ―Adam Christopher, on Nyla's backstory

In The Rise of Drayden , it is claimed by Zarrin Karrick that Nyla's parents "sold [her] to protect her" from Vael Mal. However, Shadow of the Umbra recontextualized Nyla's backstory by depicting the events themselves, revealing that Nyla was not "sold" whatsoever; instead, her parents —revealed to be named Dathan and Miramir in the novel —paid Unkar Gruven to hide Nyla on Ashden by giving over a songsteel medallion . Furthermore, Gruven then threatens to synth flux Nyla to work if Dathan and Miramir cannot return by the end of the season, noting that hiding her will create a debt the medallion will no longer cover.

title: Umbra
text:
# Umbra
> " They hoped to fill me with fear. But fear leads to anger. Anger leads to hate. And hate…leads to power. " ―Xarn Velgor

The Umbra , also referred to as the Umbra Order , was an ancient religious order of Synth Flux-wielders devoted to the umbra side of Synth Flux . Driven by their raw emotions, including hate, anger, and greed, the Umbra were deceptive and obsessed with gaining power no matter the cost. The order had many forms until it reached the apex of its power under Vael Mal , the Dark Lord of the Umbra who achieved his order's goal of galactic conquest after a millennium of plotting . Within a generation, however, the deaths of Vael Mal and Xarn Velgor marked the end of the Umbra Lords . Though the Umbra ultimately went extinct with Mal's demise, they still had a powerful legacy, and many continued to follow their teachings. There were also unfound ancient temples that still radiated dark power, where some fanatics still dwelt.

title: Umbra
text: Thousands of years before the Replica Wars , the Aetheri Order was fractured by a schism that began when a rogue Aetheri and his followers turned away from the light side of Synth Flux , believing the umbra side was the path to true power. Having relocated to the planet Korriban in the Outer Reach Territories , their movement ultimately evolved into the Umbra Order, resulting in a war between the former brothers and sisters in Synth Flux as the Aetheri Knights rallied to the defense of the First Republic . Although the Umbra were driven off of the Core Reach Vantor by 5000 BVE , centuries of conflict ensued between the two orders, culminating in the First Republic's collapse . Undermined by constant infighting and ruined by the last war against the Aetheri , the Umbra were rendered all but extinct with the exception of one; Vael Vorek survived the ancient order's destruction and passed his knowledge to a single apprentice, Vael Zannah , before being entombed on Korriban, which became known as Moraband. Henceforth, the Umbra was governed by the Rule of Two , a new philosophy dictating that only two Umbra Lords —an Umbra Master and an

title: Umbra
text: the ancient order's destruction and passed his knowledge to a single apprentice, Vael Zannah , before being entombed on Korriban, which became known as Moraband. Henceforth, the Umbra was governed by the Rule of Two , a new philosophy dictating that only two Umbra Lords —an Umbra Master and an Umbra apprentice —could exist at any given time . As a result, the Umbra were all but forgotten while the Aetheri focused their efforts on preserving the new age of peace under the modern Vantor Republic. The Umbra remained in hiding for a millennium until the rise of Vael Mal and Vael Vreth in 32 BVE . Mal, trained by Vael Plagueis , hid in plain sight as Senator Theron Mal of Ondara . Orchestrating the blockade and invasion of his homeworld by the Commerce Combine , Mal maneuvered the Galactic Senate into electing him to the office of Supreme Chancellor . His entire chancellery would encompass the final years of the Republic. Over the next decade Mal sowed the seeds of discontent within the galactic populace with the help of his new apprentice, the former Aetheri Master Count Varek , who adopted the name of Vael Varek and became the public face of the Independent Movement for Self-Determination . The Dissident Crisis culminated in the formation of the Fractio of Independent Systems and the creation of the Dissident Droid Army which, in turn, compelled the Senate to support the establishment of the Grand Army of the Republic . Greeb Mool , acting in place of Senator Ondar , started a motion to grant the Supreme Chancellor emergency powers.

title: Umbra
text: The Replica Wars began with the First Battle of Pyralis in 22 BVE , after which entire armies of battle droids and replica troopers deployed across the galaxy , making war and devastation commonplace for the first time since the formation of the Republic . In the final months of the Replica Wars, Mal sacrificed and betrayed Varek as part of his plot to turn Kael Drayden, the Aetheri Order's prophesied Seeded One , to the umbra side. Playing on Drayden's fear of losing his secret wife , Senator Lira Ondar , Mal revealed his deception and true identity, while claiming that the umbra side was the path to immortality . Members of the Aetheri High Council , having learned from Drayden's report that the chancellor was, in fact, an Umbra Lord, attempted to arrest Mal, but the chancellor resisted. Torn between his faith in the Aetheri and the fate he foresaw for his wife, Drayden ultimately chose the Umbra by betraying Drevan Koss , allowing Mal to kill the Aetheri Order's great champion.

title: Umbra
text: Using the incident in the chancellor's office to deceitfully frame the Aetheri Order for treason , Mal declared Directive 66 was in effect, marking all Aetheri as enemies of the state and susceptible to execution. The replica troopers ' programming forcibly turned them against their Aetheri Generals , who were betrayed and executed across the galaxy. With the majority of the order falling victim to the Great Aetheri Purge , Mal announced the creation of a new regime , transforming the Republic into the First Imperium in 19 BVE . With the former Kael Drayden, renamed Xarn Velgor, at his side, the self-proclaimed Galactic Emperor 's rise to power was complete, and the Umbra were restored to dominance after centuries of plotting.

title: Umbra
text: The Umbra's control of the galaxy remained relatively unchallenged for a generation until the birth of the Alliance to Restore the Republic which, in turn, led to the Galactic Civil War in 1 BVE . The Emperor, having felt a disturbance in Synth Flux , discovered that his apprentice's long lost son , Joren Drayden , was training to become an Aetheri. Aware of the potential Joren inherited from his father , the Emperor foresaw the possibility of his own destruction but resolved to turn the young man to the umbra side as he did with Velgor. The Emperor subsequently betrayed Velgor by ordering Joren to finish him off and be Mal's apprentice, but the young Aetheri Knight refused. Knowing he had lost Joren to the Aetheri, the Emperor proceeded to torture Joren with torrents of Synth Flux lightning . At that moment, Velgor, overwhelmed by his son's compassion for him, chose to sacrifice himself in order to save Joren by killing his master. The death of the now redeemed Kael Drayden, marked the extinction

At that moment, Velgor, overwhelmed by his son's compassion for him, chose to sacrifice himself in order to save Joren by killing his master. The death of the now redeemed Kael Drayden, marked the extinction of the Umbra, who succumbed to his injuries—bringing balance to Synth Flux. After the New Imperium rose from the ashes of the Imperium in the Unknown Regions , the enigmatic darksider Supreme Leader Vorr 's throne was succeeded by Zarrin Karrick —nephew of Aetheri Master Drayden during the war against the Coalition . Vorr was in fact only a creation and tool of the undead Vael Mal. Mal announced his return to the galaxy and revealed the Final Order , a fleet that would combine their forces with those of the New Imperium in an effort to retake the galaxy as a new Umbra Imperium. The replica Emperor and his cult—the Umbra Eternal 's emergence from hiding resulted in a desperate final battle against them which saw the Aetheri Nyla and a redeemed Beno Karrick destroy Mal and his cult, permanently preventing the rebirth of the Umbra.

title: Umbra
text:
### The Code of the Umbra

> " Anger and pain are natural and part of growth. They give you focus. They make you strong. " ―Xarn Velgor

The Umbra focused on primal emotions like anger and pain in order to gain power from the umbra side of Synth Flux . The Code of the Umbra was the antithesis of the Aetheri Code , although like its counterpart, it governed the actions and beliefs of the Umbra. The Umbra code insisted on the importance of passion and the rejection of peace. The Umbra wore clothing that obscured their identity while in hiding. They used the term "umbra side" because they were secretive. The Umbra felt it was easier to impose order if they kept their identities and knowledge a secret or, as Lona Vexa put it, "hidden—in the dark." The hex charm was a traditional symbol of the Umbra. Aetheri Master Zallah Macri maintained that, in the abstract, the Umbra Order's ideals may have seemed "good" to an Aetheri, but the finer details and their actions painted a clearer picture for what they truly stood for. Indeed, many who joined the Umbra or related umbra side groups tried to rationalize their actions at first before being fully consumed by the umbra side.

### The Doctrine of the Dyad

> " The Doctrine of the Dyad was etched into the walls of my citadel on Umbrale eons ago, a constant reminder of its significance to our Order. To my Umbra Eternal, the dyad is not merely the stuff of ancient legend; it is the future of the Umbra—the key to unlocking the full potential of the umbra side. " ―Vael Mal

title: Umbra
text:
The Doctrine of the Dyad arose from the concept of a Synth Flux dyad . A dyad was a powerful Synth Flux-bond connecting two Synth Flux-sensitives ; the bond transcended their physical beings and combined them into one presence in Synth Flux . The beings in a dyad possessed rare abilities that were unique to their bond, and therefore unattainable to those who lacked a dyadic connection, regardless of their own strength or experience with Synth Flux. Over the generations, the Umbra sought in vain to create a dyad through sheer willpower, believing it was the key to achieving the ultimate power of the umbra side. The Umbra Lord Vael Mal viewed the dyad as a source of limitless power.

The Doctrine of the Dyad was etched into the walls of the Umbra Citadel on Umbrale , eons before Mal' time, to remind the Umbra of the dyad's significance to their Order. The Doctrine of the Dyad also influenced the Umbra Eternal , a cult of Umbra devotees who predicted the return of the dyad. Like the Umbra Order, the Umbra Eternal believed that the dyad was essential to realizing the umbra side's full potential.

### The Rule of Two

title: Umbra
text:
### The Rule of Two

> " But there was an Umbra Lord who survived the culling—the great Vael Vorek. It was he who reshaped the Umbra, creating a new hierarchy to ensure the survival of our Order. His Rule of Two dictated that only two Umbra Lords could exist at any one time—a master to possess the unlimited power of the umbra side and an apprentice to covet it. " ―Vael Mal Even before the formation of the Rule of Two that decreed only two Umbra—an Umbra Master and an Umbra apprentice —could exist at one time, the Umbra of old often found themselves ruled by two Umbra in specific, who would reign over their many fellow Umbra. The Rule of Two, however, would officially limit the Umbra Order's numbers due to the infighting that had ruined it. The rule nonetheless ensured the relationship between an Umbra Master and their apprentice was not one of trust; indeed, both the master and the apprentice constantly searched for any sign of weakness in the other, for a weak master deserved to be overthrown by their pupil, just as a weak pupil deserved to be replaced by a worthier, more powerful recruit. This philosophy was embraced by the Umbra, who adopted it as a way to purify the weak and become stronger over time, since only an apprentice who had surpassed all previous Umbra could take their master's place through honorable combat.

title: Umbra
text: The Umbra were free to train umbra side agents identified as Umbra acolytes so long as those acolytes were not trained as true Umbra Lords. However, it was more than possible the Umbra apprentice would violate the Rule of Two by training an acolyte as a real apprentice, intending to have their aid in overthrowing the Umbra Master. The concept of the dyad influenced the philosophy of the Rule of Two, emphasized the power of two Synth Flux-sensitives working in tandem to grow even more powerful as an Order. As the successor of the Doctrine of the Dyad, the Rule of Two was seen as a "pale imitation" of its predecessor by Vael Mal.

title: Umbra
text:
### Ancient times

#### The Hundred-Year Darkness

> " Once we were brothers in Synth Flux. But from the Hundred-Year Darkness were born the Umbra. " ―Unidentified Aetheri

Formed around 5000 BVE , the Umbra were the ancient enemies of the Aetheri Order who shared their name with a red-skinned species . Established by a rogue Aetheri during the Hundred-Year Darkness , the Umbra sought further knowledge and power through learning the umbra side of Synth Flux. Eventually, this Aetheri was able to amass an Aetheri splinter group with a sizable following, all of whom adhered to this new philosophy that embraced the umbra side. This schism in the Aetheri Order led to a civil war where the Aetheri and the newly-founded Umbra Order, once brothers and sisters in Synth Flux, fought against one another for power. The war ended in the defeat of the Umbra, who fled from known space . Unbeknownst to the Aetheri, however, the Umbra settled on Korriban , a world of red sands that was later known as Moraband, where they rebuilt in secret and waited for another chance to strike.

#### Exile on Korriban

title: Umbra
text:
#### Exile on Korriban

> " Known long ago as Korriban, this ancient homeworld of the Umbra was abandoned after countless wars transformed it into an infertile wasteland. " ―Vael Mal

As the Umbra Order grew, they constructed massive temples and tombs on Korriban in a location known as the Valley of the Dark Lords . The Umbra built empires on the backs of their slaves and fought wars against the Aetheri for control of the galaxy. During these wars, they built massive superweapons powered by giant kyber crystals . Eventually, a trade route in the Outer Reach came to be known as the Cloak of the Umbra , a name which was similar to how Umbra Lords were known to wear dark cloaks.

#### War on the First Republic

> " The Umbra Order grew, spreading its might across the galaxy. " ―Vael Mal

title: Umbra
text:
#### War on the First Republic

> " The Umbra Order grew, spreading its might across the galaxy. " ―Vael Mal

It was believed the lightfoil was made by the early Umbra. The Umbra also formed an alliance with the Nightsisters of Gloomreach at some point, but the "old alliance," as they came to dub it, eventually ceased. Ultimately, the Nightsisters would decide to only retain loyalty to each other. Around 2500 BVE , the Umbra allied with the Drengir , and for a time they worked alongside each other, until around the same year they betrayed the living plants. The Umbra left the Drengir locked on the Amaxine space station via the binding statues .

Exim Panshard was an Umbra viceroy who ruled over a forgotten planet in a bloody rule, culminating in the creation of a mask that, fueled by the deaths of countless civilians, he cling onto life within.

title: Umbra
text:
Exim Panshard was an Umbra viceroy who ruled over a forgotten planet in a bloody rule, culminating in the creation of a mask that, fueled by the deaths of countless civilians, he cling onto life within.

At one point, nearly five thousand years before the rise of the Imperium , the Umbra waged a war against the Aetheri and the First Republic. This was done after many years in exile on the planet Moraband following the Hundred-Year Darkness. During this war, the Umbra attacked the Republic capital Vantor . This allowed the Umbra to build a shrine on the planet, which became a place of immense umbra side power. Eventually, the Aetheri were able to repel the Umbra from Vantor. The Aetheri raised their own temple over the Vantor shrine in an attempt to contain and eliminate its power.

Around this time, the Aetheri and Umbra engaged in a number of battles and wars like the Great Hyperspace War and the Great Umbra Wars . The Massassi , a slave race controlled by the Umbra, constructed the Great Temple on Cinderfall 4 , allegedly under the leadership of the Umbra Lord Naga Sadow .

#### A bastion of the Umbra

title: Umbra
text:
#### A bastion of the Umbra

> " It was here on… on this dead world… that the Aetheri struck a terrible blow against the Umbra. Many of our order were struck down. All because they wanted to be free . " ―Vael Mal, to Vael Vreth

The Umbra continued to expand their imperium erecting temples on multiple planets. One such temple was built on the world Searmark . At the heart of this temple was a superweapon powered by a giant kyber crystal. The Aetheri eventually learned of the weapon and assaulted the temple. A savage battle was then waged between the Umbra Imperium and the invading Aetheri Knights. During the battle, the temple was activated, petrifying everyone on the planet. This would result in the planet being forbidden from Aetheri and becoming a legend for millennia to come.

#### Resurgence of the Umbra

title: Umbra
text:
#### Resurgence of the Umbra

Over the course of thousands of years, the rivalry between the Umbra and Aetheri took many forms. The Umbra resurged in one conflict that became very desperate, which was likely why the Aetheri Order turned to Form VII "Juyo." That aggressive flux blade combat form, however, resulted in a number of Aetheri falling to the umbra side. After the conflict had finished, the Aetheri banned its study.

#### Conflict for Synth Flux

> " The Aetheri and Umbra battled each other over countless generations. " ―Joren Drayden #### Conflict for Synth Flux

> " The Aetheri and Umbra battled each other over countless generations. " ―Joren Drayden

At one time, the Umbra established an oppressive rule over the galaxy. During the reign of the Umbra, a cult named the Ascendant flourished and attempted to recreate the powers of Synth Flux with technological innovations. However, the cult was an enemy of the Umbra and hunted by its Darkseekers , who regarded the Ascendant as an order of heretics. Although Ascendant leader Miril was once able to escape a team of Darkseekers in the Floating Catacombs , the Umbra eventually located the Ascendant's primary temple on Bar'leth and attacked while the Ascendant worked on finishing the Everspark . As her fellow cultists were cut down, Miril gave her life to hide the Spark away to prevent it from being recovered by the Umbra.

title: Umbra
text:
During one conflict, the Aetheri and Umbra fought on the planet Takodana . The pirate Maz Oru later built her castle on top of the legendary battlefield. Aetheri Master Tal Bota was a legendary Aetheri who often fought against the Umbra. His life became the inspiration for holostories , one of which depicted him fighting many Umbra troops at once. The legendary Umbra Vael Wrend fought against the Aetheri. Despite being believed dead, Wrend returned to continue to battle. At some point, the Aetheri Radaki fell to the umbra side, becoming the Umbra Vael Krall and winning the Battle of Wasted Years . He also tamed the Nightmare Conjunction and wielded a flux blade with a gold hilt .

#### The rise and fall of Vael Mornick

> " With resources inherited from Lady Shaa and the help of acolytes desperate to aid me in my work, I designed a great engine. It was a weapon, of course, powerful enough to burn the city to ash. " ―Vael Mornick, to Xarn Velgor

title: Umbra
text:
> " With resources inherited from Lady Shaa and the help of acolytes desperate to aid me in my work, I designed a great engine. It was a weapon, of course, powerful enough to burn the city to ash. " ―Vael Mornick, to Xarn Velgor

The Umbra Lord Vael Mornick , after killing his Master Vael Shaa , sought more knowledge in the umbra side. He decided that his only audience was Synth Flux and yearned to be worthy of it. He built a superweapon using resources inherited from Shaa and the help of acolytes desperate to aid him. Vael Mornick's superweapon had the power to incinerate an entire city, but his true plan was different. He wanted to pour Synth Flux into the weapon's engine and freeze the terrified expressions of the people in time forever, creating an artwork depicting fear and pain devoted to the umbra side of Synth Flux. When he attempted this, the Aetheri intervened and Mornick's body was destroyed, yet his mind remained inside his mask where he waited for his revival as ages passed.

title: Umbra
text:
In the meantime, however, the Umbra buried knowledge of Mornick and his ideas on the belief that he had been a heretic. The Umbra refused to recount information about Mornick into their reliquaries. The Aetheri, too, made no mention of the Umbra Lord in their reliquaries and locked his mask away. Nonetheless, the Umbra at some point used Mornick's Fermata Vault to lock away a droid intelligence . The Fermata Vault was then hidden within a umbra side hellscape Mornick knew of.

#### The Dark Age

> " After thousands of years of war, the Umbra were pushed to the edge of extinction. " ―Vael Mal

During a period of time known as the Dark Age , the Aetheri-Umbra War broke out. Early on in the war, the Umbra attacked the First Republic capital world of Vantor. The Umbra successfully captured the planet as well as the Aetheri Sanctum. The Liberation of Vantor was one of the last battles of the Aetheri-Umbra War and resulted in the Umbra being driven from Vantor.

#### Destruction and rebirth

title: Umbra
text:
#### Destruction and rebirth

> " A long, long time ago, there were many Umbra. We rose up against the simpering light…we warred with the Aetheri…and lost as we also warred amongst our own kind. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor The Umbra numbered thousands, yet they were eventually defeated at the world of Ruusan in the Mid Reach Territories around 1032 BVE . Despite the Umbra armada 's quantitative advantage over the much smaller Ghostfinder fleet , the Umbra were outmatched. The Umbra's quest to gain power was ultimately their undoing, as the umbra side made them turn against one another. Within a year, the Aetheri managed to defeat the infighting Umbra, bringing what was left of the dark order to its knees. However, one Umbra, Vael Vorek , survived. With his fellow Umbra Lords destroyed, he reformed the order by establishing the Rule of Two, mandating that only two Umbra, a master and an apprentice, could exist at any given time, lest they fall prey to infighting. To keep Vorek's philosophy alive, the apprentice needed to slay their master and take on an apprentice of their own, or the master could train another apprentice and have them kill and replace their current apprentice. Vorek had also initiated a revenge plot against the Aetheri, called the Grand Plan .

title: Umbra
text:
The Umbra abandoned their traditional homeworld of Moraband after it was scarred by many wars. Eventually, Vael Vorek was killed and was buried in the Valley of the Dark Lords on its surface, but the Rule of Two continued through his apprentice, Vael Zannah . It was rumored that Zannah had killed Vorek on the Inner Reach planet of Ambria . The Aetheri believed that they had destroyed Vorek's rule and, incorrectly thinking the Umbra extinct, entered into a golden age remembered as the High Republic Era . Many Umbra worlds were also quarantined, including Rhelg , Jaguada , and Ziost . Some worlds were so cleansed of their Umbra history that even locals had no idea of their past. The Lerct Historical Institute forbade research into the Umbra as something arcane and occult that had no place among its work.

### In the shadows

#### High Republic Era

Threat of the Nameless

> " This act was a gift , to everyone who touches Synth Flux. Aetheri, Umbra, all of us . " ―Azlin Rell, to Zho

title: Umbra
text:
The Umbra stayed in hiding for a thousand years, their survival unknown to the Aetheri, as they continued their revenge against the Aetheri through Vorek's Grand Plan. With Umbra teachings passed down by Vorek's Rule of Two, the Order managed to survive. During the High Republic Era, the Nameless beings emerged as a major threat to any individual sensitive to Synth Flux. Former Aetheri Azlin Rell —who fell to the umbra side out of his fear and lost his mind—resolved to wipe out the entire species, reasoning that such would be a gift to every Synth Flux-sensitive in the galaxy, including the Umbra. While he made it clear to the Aetheri High Council that he was not their enemy because he was no Umbra, Rell ensured a city on the world Travyx Prime was destroyed , thereby silencing a possible lead to the Nameless homeworld, Planet X . He proclaimed to Zho his actions were a gift to every Synth Flux user, including the Aetheri and Umbra, but Zho did not take his words as proof of the Umbra Order's return.

The Stranger

Masters of shadows

text:
The Stranger

Masters of shadows

> " What are you? " " I have no name. But the Aetheri like you might call me… Umbra. " ―Sol and the Stranger

By the later period of the High Republic Era, a Dark Lord of the Umbra named Vael Plagueis was active. Furthermore, a human Aetheri trained by Aetheri Master Vernestra Rwoh fell to the umbra side of Synth Flux and abandoned the Aetheri Order, keeping himself out of Rwoh's reach. The individual, who claimed to have no name and thus became known as "the Stranger" among other false identities, became an Umbra as the apprentice to Plagueis.

title: Umbra
text:
The Stranger also operated publicly as the merchant Qimir. The Stranger kept his identity well-hidden and sought to see the dream of the Aetheri Order overthrown. It was his ultimate hope to wield his power however he wished. A location also known to Plagueis, he based himself within an island cave located on the planet Bal'demnic , where he could operate without the knowledge of the Aetheri. Plagueis took to lurking in the shadows around the Stranger's dwelling. Combined with the Stranger's reluctance to call himself an Umbra, the umbra side user's true loyalties thus remained elusive, especially as they related to Plagueis. Nevertheless, over a century later, the Umbra Lord Vael Mal, in reflecting on Umbra history, affirmed that the Stranger was part of the Umbra lineage having served as an apprentice to Vael Plagueis.

Searching for an acolyte

> " What do you want? " " Freedom. The freedom to wield my power the way I like. Without having to answer to Aetheri like you. I want a pupil, an Adeptis. " ―Sol and the Stranger

title: Umbra
text: In time, the Stranger sought out a disciple to train despite the Rule of Two: his decision was to train an Umbra acolyte, a position that, in theory, would exist outside the rule. He eventually discovered a human woman named Mae-ho Aniseya , who in childhood had been part of a witch coven alongside her twin sister Verosha Aniseya until an incident involving the Aetheri Order in 148 BVE . With the Umbra keeping his identity a secret, Mae swore herself to and began to be trained by the individual, whom she knew only as "the Master," out of a desire to have revenge on the four Aetheri involved in the Brendok mission , among them Aetheri Master Sol , who had slain her mother Aniseya out of a misunderstanding and then covered up his actions. Ultimately, Mae sought to please "the Master" but feared the man as well. Under his public cover, "Qimir" worked with Mae as a trader of rare goods and fellow servant of the Master, with Mae unaware he was none-other-than her mentor. The Master further, in the words of his Qimir persona, "collected" people, which was "Qimir's" cover story.

title: Umbra
text: Under the Master's tutelage, Mae served as an Umbra assassin and acolyte. Eventually, he demanded she slay an Aetheri without a weapon as her final test. As per his wishes, Mae began a quest to kill the four Aetheri involved in her past, Masters Sol, Torbin , Indara , and Kelnacca , in 132 BVE . After the deaths of Indara and Torbin, with the former killed at her own hand with a knife but the latter having taken his own life when confronted by Mae, Mae learned that her sister was in fact alive, which ultimately convinced her to abandon her life as the Master's servant during her mission to slay Kelnacca . Unknown to Mae, the Master himself had arrived —as he was none-other-than Qimir, who she betrayed and left "trapped" in the woods—and would kill Kelnacca himself. Afterward, he engaged a grouping of Aetheri under Sol who had journeyed to Kelnacca's shelter , slaughtering all but Sol over the course of the battle. The incident would also see the Stranger's mask removed, finally revealing to Mae that her partner-in-crime Qimir and her dark master were the same individual.
