> " I need you to help me find someone. " " Who? " " A pupil of mine before he turned to evil. " ―Vernestra Rwoh and Mae-ho Aniseya After Qimir's double identity was revealed and the Umbra was swarmed by a grouping of umbramoths , Mae knocked out her sister and swapped places with her, returning to the Aetheri transport with Sol. Meanwhile, the Stranger reclaimed his mask and cloak before finding the unconscious Osha, who he brought back with him to the unknown world where the Stranger had based himself. Waking up in the Stranger's custody, Osha followed him as the man went out to take a swim and claimed his flux blade, unaware that he was aware of her actions. Noticing how she thought killing an unarmed foe was not honorable, the Stranger managed to convince her into letting him live and divulged details of his past, attempting to tempt Osha into doubting the ideals of the Aetheri and instead embrace his own. All the while, Sol discovered that Mae had swapped places with her sister and subdued her, leaving the orbit of Khofar and promising to save Osha from Mae's master once they had a chance to truly talk.

title: Umbra
text: Just as Sol departed, an Aetheri investigation team under Master Vernestra Rwoh arrived on Khofar, where they discovered the aftermath of the battle with the Stranger. Unaware of who had committed the massacre, Adept Mog Adana suggested that Sol had fallen to the umbra side. With all parties converging on Brendok once Sol returned to the world where all his troubles had began, as Sol activated his tracking beacon for the Aetheri to follow him and Osha experienced a Synth Flux vision of his death on the planet, Sol and the Stranger began a final duel , after which Mae rejected the ways of anger and instead wanted to see Sol brought to justice for his crime: striking down her mother and lying about his actions. However, the revelation that her master had killed her mother broke Osha, who Synth Flux choked the Aetheri Master—thereby killing an Aetheri without a weapon—and bled his flux blade.

title: Umbra
text:
Osha accepted the station as the Stranger's acolyte, while Mae allowed her memory of her sister to be wiped so she could be handed over to the Aetheri. As the Aetheri party under Rwoh arrived too late to catch the Stranger, Rwoh blamed the murders of Kelnecca, Indara, and Torbin on Sol. Having sensed her former disciple's presence, however, she met with Mae and requested her aid in finding the Stranger. Meanwhile, Osha returned to the Stranger's island with him as his new acolyte, all while Plagueis continued to lurk on the planet.

#### Late Republic Era

> " For a thousand years we have kept to the shadows, not afraid of the Aetheri—but ourselves . The umbra side is powerful. It is too powerful. The weak will meekly stand in regimented order. The Umbra… One master. One apprentice. No more. For generations. Generations building to me . " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

title: Umbra
text: In 82 BVE , the Aetheri Adept Varek , after encountering the Presagers of Hakotei cult, heard the voice of the Umbra Lord Vael Skrye in a Synth Flux vision . Within the vision of a possible future, Skrye stated that the Umbra were reborn and that something called the Cauldron was opening, all alongside the sound of a planet being torn in two and an explosion. The visions greatly worried Varek, who also saw a glimpse of himself falling to the umbra side as the apprentice of another Umbra Lord, but Aetheri Master Lene Kostana tried to ease Varek's concern by assuring him what he saw were merely possibilities, not certain futures.

title: Umbra
text:
Eventually, the Umbra apprentice known as Vael Mal —the same Umbra glimpsed by Varek in his vision —betrayed his master Vael Plagueis, by killing him in his sleep , seizing the status of master for himself as he forwards a plot to destroy the Aetheri. Thus, generations after the fall of the Umbra, Mal moved to strike a fatal blow against the Aetheri Order and the Vantor Republic . Orchestrating his public persona's rise to the Republic's Chancellorship and the creation of an army that would purge the Aetheri, Vael Mal fulfilled the return of Umbra rule over the galaxy, giving rise to the New Order under himself as Emperor.

### Fall of the Vantor Republic

#### Veiled Threat

> " They have numbers on their side. And the faith of the Republic. " " For the moment. In time, and with careful planning, they will lose both. " ―Vael Vreth and Vael Mal

title: Umbra
text:
### Fall of the Vantor Republic

#### Veiled Threat

> " They have numbers on their side. And the faith of the Republic. " " For the moment. In time, and with careful planning, they will lose both. " ―Vael Vreth and Vael Mal

The Umbra remained a distant memory until the last years of the Vantor Republic when Vael Mal and his apprentice, Vael Vreth , revealed themselves to the Aetheri in 32 BVE . Although Vreth longed to avenge his ancient Umbra forebears, he admitted that the Aetheri Order was too powerful for the Umbra to challenge directly, mainly due to the Aetheri's superior numbers and the Vantor Republic's support for the Order. Mal assured his apprentice that they would undermine the Order's strength with time and careful planning.

title: Umbra
text: Mal hid in plain sight as the unassuming Senator Theron Mal of Ondara . His double identity allowed him to infiltrate and deceive the Galactic Senate , as well as the inner circle of the Monarch of Ondara , Queen Lira Ondar whom he served as a close advisor . Mal orchestrated the Invasion of Ondara by the Commerce Combine as part of his agenda to accrue more political power at the expense of his people and homeworld. This allowed the Dark Lord to make a play for the galaxy's highest office in his civilian persona and sow the seeds of the Umbra's revenge.

title: Umbra
text:
During the Battle of Ondara , Vreth killed Aetheri Master Sorin Vael , but was defeated and left for dead by Adept Orien Kade . Despite the loss of Vreth, Mal discovered a prospective apprentice in Kael Drayden , a child whom Synth Flux was exceptionally strong with. However, Drayden been discovered and recruited by the Aetheri Order. Nevertheless, Mal promised to monitor Drayden's career, intending to turn the Aetheri Order's prophesied Seeded One to the umbra side of Synth Flux. Additionally, Mal succeeded in his efforts as Mal to become elected as Supreme Chancellor of the Vantor Republic.

#### Dissident Crisis

> " I told you everything you needed to know on Pyralis all those years ago, Kade. You should have joined me. Sifas Dyen understood, he saw the future. That is why he helped me. " ―Vael Varek, to Orien Kade

title: Umbra
text: Following Vreth's apparent demise on Ondara, Vael Mal approached the fallen Aetheri Master Varek, who had taken on the title of Count of Sireno , and offered him the chance to destroy the Aetheri Order and reshape the Republic by becoming his new apprentice. Varek agreed and was given the name Vael Varek, desiring both power and the elimination of the corruption that plagued the Republic. After earning a bloody reputation as a Kaleesh warlord on his homeworld, Varek and his master, Vael Mal, saw Skarn ' potential as he led his people in a merciless war against their planetary neighbor, the Yam'rii from Huk . The Umbra, researching technology enhanced beings, gave Skarn an irresistible offer to improve himself. Driven by his desire to increase his combat skill, Skarn became a far more effective fighter through Umbra-sponsored cybernetic technological enhancements. Varek also trained the fallen Gloomreachian Aetheri Kessa Vray as his assassin and potential Umbra apprentice while still apprenticed to Mal.

title: Umbra
text: For nearly a decade after accepting Mal's offer, Varek helped his new master to implement much of the groundwork necessary to begin the Replica Wars . Aetheri Master Sifas Dyen secretly commissioned the creation of an army of replica troopers a year before the Invasion of Ondara , having foreseen a future conflict through Synth Flux. However, Mal needed him silenced to the Umbra could take control of the army, so he ordered Varek to kill him. Varek then betrayed his friend by having him murdered by the Gruv Syndicate , which allowed the Umbra to secretly take control of the army. Varek personally recruited the bounty hunter Garrick Vark to be the replica template of the Grand Army of the Republic , which the Umbra intended for the Aetheri to lead. An essential part of the Umbra's plan was the behavioral modification biochip ; every replica trooper was designed with a biochip in their brain . The chips were programmed by Mal to synth flux the Replicas to comply with Directive 66 when the time came to destroy the Aetheri.

title: Umbra
text:
Vael Varek, under his public identity as Varek, reentered the public eye in spectacular fashion, commandeering a Vantor Republic Holonet station in the Raxun system and delivering a rousing speech in which he thoroughly lambasted the corruption and shortcomings of the Republic. He then began to rally rebellious star systems to his cause and secretly allied himself with powerful commercial entities, resulting in the formation of the Fractio of Independent Systems .

War broke out as both the Fractio's droid armies and the newly-formed Grand Army of the Republic fought over the desert-landscape of Pyralis after the extent of Varek' secret alliance with the Commerce Combine , the Artificer Union , the InterGalactic Banking Clan , the Corporate Alliance , and the Commerce Guild was revealed in 22 BVE . Though the Republic was able to score a victory, Varek and the rest of the Dissident leadership were able to escape the planet.

title: Umbra
text:
In preparation for the upcoming galactic-scale conflict and its aftermath, Varek traveled to Vantor's industrial district, known as the Works , after the First Battle of Pyralis , where he met with Mal and delivered the "good news" of the war's beginning, as well as presented him with the plans for the DS-1 Void Core Mobile Battle Station .

#### Replica Wars

> " I have good news for you, my Lord. The war has begun. " " Excellent. Everything is going as planned. " ―Vael Varek and Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info ) #### Replica Wars

> " I have good news for you, my Lord. The war has begun. " " Excellent. Everything is going as planned. " ―Vael Varek and Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info )

In the aftermath of the battle at Pyralis , the Aetheri transitioned from peacekeepers to generals and commanders , ranks that they were formerly denied due to the Aetheri Code. During the war, Varek was briefly captured by the Hosha Gang . With most civilians in the galaxy unaware of what a "Umbra" was, pirate leader Hondik Hosha indeed believed Varek was simply a rogue Aetheri who had broken away from the Republic. Upon hearing Varek declare himself to be an Umbra Lord, Hosha remained unconcerned and focused on the great bounty he would gain by ransoming the Dissident leader to the Republic. However, Varek ultimately escaped when Hosha was distracted by Kade and Drayden, who were also captured to be ransomed. Varek decided against telling his master the details of the incident, believing it to be an embarrassment.

title: Umbra
text: On her tasks for the Umbra, Vray engaged Kael Drayden, Orien Kade, and Sela Marr in flux blade duels on numerous occasions. While loyal, she was ultimately betrayed by her Master on the orders of Vael Mal. Varek soon after traveled to Gloomreach to meet with the Nightsisters in hopes of finding a new apprentice. Varek and the Nightsisters eventually decided on a young Zyrrak named Savage Opress , brother of the long-presumed dead Vael Vreth. However, Kessa Vray sought revenge for Varek's treachery and used Opress as a means of attaining her goal. Torn between two demanding masters, Opress eventually turned on both Varek and Vray.

title: Umbra
text:
Returning to the Nightsisters, Opress found that his brother, Vreth, had not been killed as previously believed. Vreth had survived his injuries on Ondara because of his sheer reliance on the umbra side and was living in the junk heaps of Lotho Minor . However, Vreth's tragic events had driven him to insanity. He remembered only one word: "Kade." Guided by an Anacondan named Morley , Opress was able to return Vreth to the Nightsisters for treatment. Now fully healed by the Nightsisters' magic and given a pair of new robotic legs, Vreth began a hunt for the man who had nearly destroyed his life, Orien Kade.

His revenge scheme eventually ended with Vreth's control of Ferrum and the death of Satinna Velara . However, Vael Mal sensed his former apprentice's action and his stance as a potential rival, and traveled to Ferrum to put an end to it. He killed Opress and took Vreth captive, locking him away in an old mountaintop prison known as the Spire , in an elaborate Umbra gambit to settle a longstanding and deadly dispute with the Nightsisters.

title: Umbra
text:
Later during the war, Zho visited Moraband, the Umbra homeworld. The Aetheri Master encountered an illusory spectre of the ancient Umbra Vael Vorek, who was buried on the barren planet and battled Mal on a spiritual plane as the result of an ancient, arcane Umbra ritual . Through his experience, Zho gained a new enlightenment about Synth Flux that the Umbra did not foresee.

#### Fury of the Umbra

Seduction of the Seeded One

> " Good is a point of view, Kael. The Umbra and the Aetheri are similar in almost every way, including their quest for greater power. " " The Umbra rely on their passion for their strength. They think inwards, only about themselves. " " And the Aetheri don't? " " The Aetheri are selfless. They only care about others. " ―Vael Mal and Kael Drayden

title: Umbra
text:
After three years of the Replica Wars, Vael Mal' grand scheme was almost complete. Realizing the time had come to make Kael his apprentice, and Count Varek's purpose had been served, he sacrificed and betrayed Varek to a violent killing by Drayden, as part his plot to push the young Aetheri further to the Umbra side and him. As Mal, he told Kael an Umbra legend about Vael Plagueis the Wise. Plagueis, through the umbra side, had gained the ability to keep people from dying until his apprentice killed him in his sleep. This story entranced Kael, who was desperate to learn this power to save his wife, Lira Ondar.

Eventually, Mal revealed himself as Mal and converted Kael to the umbra side. Aetheri Master Drevan Koss tried to arrest the Dark Lord but was killed after Kael betrayed Drevan and the Aetheri. After this, Kael pledged himself to service under his new Umbra Master, Mal, and became Xarn Velgor.

The New Order

> " Once more the Umbra will rule the galaxy, and we shall have peace. " ―Vael Mal

title: Umbra
text:
With Koss's attack and a new Umbra apprentice at his side, Mal realized this was the perfect opportunity for him to destroy the Aetheri. He ordered Velgor to lead the 501st Legion 's attack on the Aetheri Sanctum , and then go to the Emberfall system to wipe out the Dissident Council . With Velgor at the temple, Mal unleashed Directive 66, which led to the Replicas' biochips activating and brainwashing them into murdering the Aetheri. Thousands of Aetheri across the galaxy were then betrayed and killed by their replica troopers. Prior to Velgor arriving on Emberfall to execute the Dissident Council, Mal deceived the council into believing that Velgor would protect them. After Velgor slaughtered the Dissidents, Velgor followed Mal's third order by shutting down the droid army, which ended the Replica Wars. In the political arena, he reorganized the Republic using the powers given to him as a result of the Replica Wars to transform the Vantor Republic into the Imperium to restore the Umbra Imperium, installing himself as Emperor . Once more, the Umbra ruled the galaxy, unbeknownst to all but the few surviving Aetheri.

### Rise of the Imperium

#### Reign of the Umbra

title: Umbra
text:
### Rise of the Imperium

#### Reign of the Umbra

> " And my apprentices? Vael Vreth was a loss, but Vael Varek…he was a proton torpedo. He served his purpose and was gone. I had a… superior candidate in mind. We did it, Velgor. The Aetheri destroyed! The Republic a shattered corpse for me to resurrect as a puppet! And you, Velgor—the boy transformed into the man you were destined to be… " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

Following the reorganization of the Republic and purging of the Aetheri Order, Vael Mal and Velgor ruled over the First Imperium for over twenty years until the Battle of Mossfell . The two Umbra Lords established a cadre of Umbra side wielders known as the Warden Order . The Wardens were tasked with hunting down Aetheri Purge survivors and preventing Synth Flux-sensitive children from becoming Aetheri. The leading Warden was a Pau'a Grand Warden , who was a former Aetheri Sentinel and Knight. The Wardens were trained by Velgor and wielded double-bladed spinning flux blades .

#### Mornick's return

title: Umbra
text:
#### Mornick's return

Sometime into the Imperial Era , Velgor embarked on a mission to Emberfall . With him, he took the Chief Imperial Architect Colonel Alva Brenne , her assistant Lieutenant Roggo , and the mask that once belonged to Mornick. Mal had assured Velgor that Mornick's mask would guide him during his studies there. Whilst on the planet, Velgor meditated in the Umbra cave there. That was when Mornick's mask possessed Roggo and Mornick used his body to design a structure. When Brenne discovered this, she was shot dead, alerting Velgor to the situation. Velgor killed Roggo and removed the mask from his body.

Velgor took it to the cave and reached into it using Synth Flux. Mornick revealed himself to Velgor and told him his story, before attempting to possess him too. Velgor resisted but came to let the mask take control of an Emberfallian , giving Mornick a body again. The two discussed the structure Mornick had designed and Mornick claimed it could tune the energies of the umbra side locus on Emberfall, opening the door to the umbra side that could resurrect Lira Ondar. Velgor subsequently agreed to let Mornick build Fortress Velgor .

title: Umbra
text:
In truth, Mornick hoped to use the energies to resurrect his own body. As the Battle of Fortress Velgor raged outside, Mornick successfully revived himself. In his duel with Velgor, Mornick insulted the current state of the Umbra as "Aetheri-obsessed weaklings," remarking that it saddened him and further claiming it disgusted the umbra side itself. Velgor, in the end, triumphed over the ancient Umbra and killed Mornick once more. All the same, his mask survived again and was returned to Mal by Velgor, who tried and failed to use the portal to resurrect Ondar. For its failure, he destroyed the gateway. Nevertheless, the incident had concluded with Velgor fully committing himself on the path of the umbra side.

#### Spark of Insurgency

title: Umbra
text:
#### Spark of Insurgency

Five years after the end of the Replica Wars, the Free Selvara Movement led by Chavar Kryll embarked on a large-scale operation to assassinate the Emperor and Velgor. Chavar wanted to kill the two Umbra Lords to bring about the demise of the Imperium. However, Mal had anticipated Chavar's move, and the two Umbra eluded Chavar's attempts to assassinate them. This operation dealt a major blow to the Free Selvara insurgents, who were forced deeper underground, and also led to the exposure of Colonel Belka Drayn as a traitor . Despite Mal' hopes, he failed to stamp out the sparks of the growing insurgency.

title: Umbra
text:
Among those opposed to Mal's rule was Luthen Rael , who maintained the cover of an innocent artifact collector and dealer while secretly building up a insurgent network . Among the artifacts in Rael's collection were an Umbra reliquary he kept in the back of his Galactic Antiquities and Objects of Interest store and several pieces of Umbra armor . After the outbreak of the Lorath insurgency about four years before the Battle of Cinderfall , Mal dispatched Velgor to hunt down the Shades , who were part of the growing insurgency. Velgor lured the Shades into a trap on Lorath in an attempt to track down the Ember Cell . Velgor led an attack on the Ember fleet which destroyed the insurgent flagship Ember Home but failed to destroy the insurgency. During the skirmish, Velgor discovered that his former apprentice Sela Marr was still alive. Under Mal' orders, he dispatched more Wardens to hunt down the Aetheri Purge survivor Brenn Aldric and his apprentice Cass Virel .

#### Struggle on Searmark

> " The power within will soon serve the Emperor. " ―Xarn Velgor

title: Umbra
text:
#### Struggle on Searmark

> " The power within will soon serve the Emperor. " ―Xarn Velgor

A year later, Velgor visited the Lorath Aetheri Sanctum where the Fifth Warden and the Seventh Warden had attempted to capture Virel, Aldric, and Marr. Velgor remarked that the Emperor would be pleased with their discovery. When the Fifth Warden remarked that the power of the Aetheri was growing, Velgor responded that it would be their undoing. The Umbra Lords later took an interest in the Umbra temple on Searmark, which was reputed to be home to a weapon capable of destroying all life. Velgor sent another Warden called the Eighth Warden to hunt down a "shadow" and to obtain an Umbra reliquary .

title: Umbra
text: Virel, Aldric, and Marr encountered the former Umbra apprentice Vreth—who was the "shadow" that Velgor sent the Eighth Warden to hunt—in the Searmark Umbra Temple. Vreth had become stranded on Searmark several years prior and had discovered a secret inside the Umbra temple that would allow them to destroy the Umbra. However, he lacked the strength to do so on his own. Vreth managed to befriend Cass and the two Synth Flux-wielders succeeded in obtaining the Umbra reliquary. Vreth later helped the Aetheri drive several Wardens away. Despite Aldric and Marr's distrust, Vreth managed to convince them to help him by teasing the opportunity of destroying the Umbra once and for all.

title: Umbra
text: Vreth convinced Cass to place the Umbra reliquary in the obelisk at the top of the temple complex. He then helped Aldric and Marr kill the Wardens before turning on both of them. Eventually, Vreth blinded Aldric. Despite this, the Aetheri Knight defeated Vreth in combat and pushed him off the edge of the temple. Meanwhile, Cass discovered that the Umbra reliquary was the key to reactivating the Umbra temple, which was a powerful superweapon capable of destroying life. Shortly later, Xarn Velgor arrived to claim the temple's power for the Umbra. Xarn Velgor fought with Sela while Aldric and Virel removed the reliquary; triggering the temple's implosion. Virel and Aldric escaped the temple, but Velgor and Marr were trapped inside when the Temple began to implode. Velgor and Marr survived and parted company.

title: Umbra
text: Later, Virel came under the influence of the Umbra Reliquary, which was inhabited by an entity called Presence . Under the reliquary's guidance, Cass learned more aggressive combat techniques including forcing an AT-DP walker driver to attack his comrades and walk his machine off a bridge. Virel's use of the Umbra Reliquary strained relations with his master Aldric, who confiscated it. Aldric later met a powerful Synth Flux-wielder called the Bendu , who formed a middle ground between the light and dark sides. He advised Aldric that an object could be used for both good and evil and that only the person had the power to change it. Aldric left the Umbra reliquary in the Bendu's care.

title: Umbra
text: Vreth, who was revealed to have survived the events on Searmark, later captured Aldric and Virel's insurgent friends and used them as hostages to synth flux the two Aetheri to bring him the Umbra reliquary and Brenn's Aetheri reliquary . Aldric and Virel recovered the Umbra reliquary from the Bendu, who warned them that Vreth planned to combine the power of the reliquaries to provide clarity of vision. After rendezvousing with Vreth, Virel and the former Umbra combined the two reliquaries. Virel wanted to find a way to destroy the Umbra while Vreth was looking for hope. The reliquaries projected a vision of twin suns , an old enemy of Vreth, and offered to show Virel the "key" to destroying the Umbra. However, Aldric convinced his apprentice to look away, and the two reliquaries separated. Vreth took the opportunity to escape into space.

title: Umbra
text:
Using the fragments of Virel's memories in his mind, Vreth tracked the insurgents down to their base on Atollon . Using the umbra side of Synth Flux, Vreth manifested in Virel's visions. Vreth managed to convince Virel to follow him to Gloomreach by offering to keep Chomper Base a secret. At the Nightsister lair , Vreth and Virel underwent a ritual to uncover the remaining fragments of the reliquaries in each others' minds. After drinking a magic potion, Vreth learned that Master Kade was still living on the planet with twin suns while Virel learned that Kade held the key to destroying the Umbra. The two were then attacked by the spirits of the Nightsisters, who demanded payment in flesh and blood for their services. Aldric and the Ferrik weapons expert Ryn Wrenna arrived to confront Vreth but were possessed by the spirits. Virel and Vreth managed to flee outside the lair. When Vreth offered Virel a place as his apprentice, the young Aetheri refused to abandon his friends. After exorcising Aldric and Wrenna, the three resolved to find the planet with twin suns and to reach Kade before Vreth could kill him.

### Galactic Civil War

title: Umbra
text:
### Galactic Civil War

> " We kept the skeleton of the Republic for nearly twenty years while the Void Core was constructed. Twenty years, my apprentice. All that planning is now a layer of dust orbiting around Cinderfall. Now, we no longer have the Senate to hold order. We do not have the Void Core to synth flux it. Our greatest weapon is gone. Our production is in ashes. We are besieged. In all these years, we have never skirted closer to disaster. " ―Vael Mal, to Xarn Velgor

In the years leading up to the Battle of Cinderfall, the Imperium faced a growing insurgency that had grown into the Alliance to Restore the Republic . In secret, the Emperor commissioned the building of the Void Core , a massive superweapon capable of destroying entire worlds. After insurgent elements stole the Void Core plans , Velgor led a secret mission to Dunemere which ended with the capture of Princess Elira Solen , the adopted daughter of Bael Solen and one of the offspring of Kael Drayden. Shortly thereafter, the Emperor dissolved the Imperial Senate and ordered Cindervale 's destruction .

title: Umbra
text: Lord Velgor and Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix presided over Cindervale's destruction in the presence of Princess Elira. Before they could terminate Elira, she was rescued by a group of travelers including Kael's son Joren Drayden , the smugglers Dax Karrick and Brevok , the droids Astra-9 and Bolt-3 , and the Aetheri Master Kade. While the other insurgents escaped aboard the Corsair Wing , Kade sacrificed his life to delay Velgor. Elira and her rescuers retreated to the insurgent base on Cinderfall 4. The Void Core traveled to Cinderfall base in a bid to destroy the Free Coalition once and for all but this plan was ruined by a insurgent starfighter synth flux. During the Battle of Cinderfall, Velgor sensed that Synth Flux was strong in the insurgent pilot Drayden; who fired the missile that destroyed the Void Core, Velgor, however, survived the destruction.

title: Umbra
text:
Three years after the events on Cinderfall and following the Battle of Frostmark , the Emperor disclosed that Joren was one of the offspring of Kael Drayden, though this was something Velgor already knew. Velgor believed that Joren would be a powerful ally if he could be turned. The Emperor charged Velgor with winning Joren over and destroying him if he refused to turn to the umbra side. During that time Joren had traveled to Mirefall , where he had been trained by Zho, an Aetheri Master who was once the leader of the Aetheri Order. Velgor managed to capture Elira, Dax, Astra-9 and Brevok in Aether Spire on Mistral . Sensing the danger that his friends were in, Joren left his training and traveled to Aether Spire where Velgor was waiting for him. During their confrontation , Velgor severed Joren's right hand and revealed that he was Joren's father. Despite the pain, Joren refused to join Velgor, threw himself down a vane and escaped.

### Fall of the Umbra

title: Umbra
text:
### Fall of the Umbra

> " Now, fulfill your destiny and take your father's place at my side. " " Never. I'll never turn to the umbra side. You failed, Your Highness. I'm an Aetheri, like my father before me. " " So be it, Aetheri. " ―Vael Mal and Joren Drayden

In secret, the Emperor directed the building of a second Void Core above the forest moon of Mossfell . In an attempt to destroy the insurgency once and for all, the Emperor arranged for intelligence on the second Void Core to be leaked to Botran spies. Using this information, the Free Coalition made preparations to launch an attack on the second Void Core. Before the Battle of Mossfell, Velgor traveled to the second Void Core to warn Moff Tiaan Jerjerrod to accelerate construction. Shortly later, Mal traveled to the battle station to oversee the final construction stages.

title: Umbra
text: Joren confronted Zho and Synth Flux spirit of Kade about Velgor's claims on Mistral, and accepted that the Umbra Lord was in fact his father, Kael Drayden, after his mentors confirmed it. Joren accompanied the Insurgents to Mossfell with the intention to confront Velgor, believing that he could help the former Aetheri return to the light side. Likewise, the Emperor sought to turn Joren to the umbra side in order to replace Velgor as an apprentice. On the second Void Core, Joren confronted Mal who wanted to provoke Joren's anger by having the Imperial Navy engage the Insurgent fleet, thus putting his friends' lives at risk.

title: Umbra
text:
Joren and Velgor engaged in a flux blade duel while the Emperor observed from his throne, still encouraging the Aetheri apprentice to use the umbra side. Joren gave into his anger after Velgor learned of his sister's identity and threatened to turn her to the umbra side. After witnessing the power that Joren demonstrated when he defeated Velgor, Mal betrayed Velgor by ordering Joren to take his place at the Emperor's side. Joren, however, steadfastly refused in turn. Realizing Joren was a true Aetheri, and would not be swayed, Mal attempted to kill him through torturing him with Synth Flux lightning . However, Velgor, torn between his loyalty to his master, his old Aetheri connections, and his son, ultimately threw the Emperor down a reactor shaft, killing him and returning balance to Synth Flux. With his life-sustaining armor badly damaged from the Emperor's Synth Flux lightning, Xarn Velgor died, but his selfless act allowed him to rejoin Synth Flux as a Synth Flux spirit, and be "reborn" as his old self, Kael Drayden. Thus, the Umbra Order, along with their tyranny was no more, as foretold by the ancient prophecy that predicted their downfall.

### Interregnum

title: Umbra
text:
### Interregnum

#### Acolytes and new traditions

> " Through the ages, I've seen evil take many forms. The Umbra. The Imperium. Today, it is the New Imperium. " ―Maz Oru

While the Umbra Order was defeated at the Battle of Mossfell, it was merely one of many denominations of Synth Flux-worshiping religions that existed throughout galactic history. The Umbra's ancient legacy as enemies of the Aetheri and, at times, rulers of the galaxy, would continue to be felt in the decades that followed its extinction. The downfall of the Umbra at Mossfell left behind a vacuum that others sought to fill, such as the Knights of Karrick . Thus, while the ancient prophecy that foretold the destruction of the Umbra came to pass, it did not foretell the destruction of the darkness, for as long as there existed light, there would always be shadow.

title: Umbra
text:
Immediately following the deaths of Vael Mal and Xarn Velgor, many individuals and groups still adhered to their philosophy. Yupe Tashu , an advisor to the late Mal, was an admirer of the Umbra interrogation methods, as well as their teachings and cunning. He believed that the remaining Imperial Military had to retreat "beyond the veil of stars," to the Unknown Regions, to search for the source of the umbra side that Mal had come to feel reaching out to him. The Acolytes of the Beyond , who worshiped the Umbra, collected Umbra artifacts , such as what they believed to be Xarn Velgor's flux blade , to destroy them, believing this returned the relics to their deceased owners. The Acolytes eventually collapsed, but one of their members, Kiza , was corrupted by the mask of Viceroy Exim Panshard and the promises the dead Umbra gave her if she could bring him to Umbrale.

#### Rieve's charade

title: Umbra
text:
#### Rieve's charade

In 9 AVE , a Synth Flux-sensitive human named Rieve joined the competitive sporting show Hunters of the Outer Reach , where she would adopt the onstage persona of an Umbra Lord. In that act, she wielded a red flux blade and owned a suit of Umbra armor modified to her liking. While in private the two would grow close, on stage she had a great rivalry with J-3DI , a droid programmed to believe he was an Aetheri. Their rivalry was even made the subject of the first edition of Arena News , where the Arena refreshed fans on the concept of the Umbra. After challenging J-3DI to a battle on one occasion and quickly walking out of interview with Arena announcer Boz Vega , who claimed to fans Rieve was an Umbra Master, Rieve won the "epic battle" against J-3DI, which Arena News claimed brought glory to the Umbra. Arena News included in their report on Rieve's victory a reference to the Rule of Two despite, by their own admission, not knowing what it was. Rieve made an effort to learn more about the Umbra, but she admitted there was not much about the order in the records she reviewed. She did, however, know of Vreth and uncovered a reference to his brother Savage Oppress in Umbra-related records.

### Rebirth of Vael Mal

#### A sinister plot

> " At last the work of generations is complete. The great error is corrected. The day of victory is at hand. The day of revenge. The day of the Umbra. " ―Vael Mal — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Umbra
text: Although Vael Mal perished at Mossfell, the Umbra Lord was able to cheat death, using the umbra side of Synth Flux to escape from his falling original body into a cloned body far away from Mossfell, and returned. Mal settled on the hidden world of the Umbra in the Unknown Regions , Umbrale , along with a cult of followers, the Umbra Eternal. However, the cloned body was unable to withstand Mal's power and, as a result, it physically decayed, requiring it to remain connected to cybernetic components, such as an Ommin harness , in order to be sustained and move. On Umbrale, the Umbra Eternal oversaw the building of the largest fleet ever known to the galaxy, the Final Order , to establish a resurrected Umbra Imperium. Meanwhile, owing to a secret Contingency plan designed by Mal, former Imperial officers , nobles , and technologists were able to flee into the Unknown Regions, where they established the New Imperium .

title: Umbra
text: The Umbra Eternal created artificial replica humanoid aliens , Strand-Casts, and bioengineered abominations one of which, Vorr , came to be Supreme Leader of the New Imperium, though the New Imperium was unaware of Vorr's true origins nor of the existence of the Umbra Eternal and the fact that their former Emperor was apparently alive in some form. Vorr held a strong connection the umbra side of Synth Flux and became deeply knowledgeable of its lore and a master of its ways, but was not an Umbra himself. Nevertheless he still grew to have knowledge of Umbra teachings. Such a thing gave him the ability to be a useful pawn for Mal to use as a way to influence galactic events from the shadows of Umbrale, and build the armies of the New Imperium, with Vorr's knowledge saving the faction from ultimate destruction.

title: Umbra
text:
In 21 AVE , Drayden sensed a growing darkness in Synth Flux and launched a quest for Umbrale upon learning from the ghost of his father it was the planet at the center of his visions. At the same time, Kiza and the spirit of Panshard carried on in their own search for Umbrale, while the Umbra assassin Orrin sought out Nyla on the orders of the Umbra Eternal and Mal. After Kiza's death and the destruction of Panshard's mask , which destroyed the Umbra viceroy for good, Drayden believed the disturbance was at an end, but his friend Landonis Balthazar Quill elected to stay on the planet Pasaana for any signs of Orrin, who truly had died in the Forbidden Valley , any signs of his daughter Kadara Quill , who had been kidnapped by the New Imperium, and any signs of Nyla. While he nor Drayden had ever learned her name, they knew she had been hunted by Orrin for reasons unknown to them.

#### The rise of Zarrin Karrick

An heir to the Umbra

title: Umbra
text:
#### The rise of Zarrin Karrick

An heir to the Umbra

> " Once reborn as Zarrin Karrick, he was mine to control. From the shadows, I shaped him into a worthy apprentice—not a true Umbra but equally as powerful in the umbra side. " ―Vael Mal The birth of Beno Karrick presented Vael Mal with another opportunity to convert a member of the Drayden family to the umbra side of Synth Flux. As the grandson of Xarn Velgor, Karrick was born with raw and powerful connection to Synth Flux. As such, Mal planned to turn Karrick to the umbra side through Vorr, whom he used as a proxy for Karrick. In time, Vorr turned Karrick to the umbra side. Karrick's fall to the umbra side occurred after several events, including when he thought his uncle Joren Drayden tried to kill him, a mysterious storm that he summoned and destroyed the Aetheri training temple , and when " Karrick " killed his friend Tai . Karrick succumbed to darkness, killing Karrick, changing his name to Zarrin Karrick, and becoming the new master of the Knights of Karrick, an enclave of umbra side users. Although Vorr was not an Umbra, he was strong with Synth Flux. Vorr took Karrick as his apprentice and trained him in the ways of the umbra side, but Mal considered himself to be the true master of Karrick. Elsewhere, Drayden went into a self-imposed exile, his location unknown to the galaxy.

title: Umbra
text: Zarrin Karrick pledged to finish what his grandfather Xarn Velgor had begun, although Supreme Leader Vorr scorned the sentimentality of Velgor, which he believed had led to the Imperium's downfall. Ultimately, Karrick hoped to build an immunity to the light, and succeed where Velgor failed. Joren Drayden, Karrick's former master and the last Aetheri, once blamed the Aetheri Order for Vael Mal' rise to power. Unbeknownst to Karrick, his training in the umbra side was monitored by Mal. The Dark Lord regarded Karrick as a worthy apprentice and the heir to Velgor. Although he did not view Karrick as a true Umbra, Mal confirmed that Karrick was powerful with the umbra side nonetheless. Karrick was a warlord and champion of the New Imperium by the time of the New Imperium-Coalition War , a galactic conflict that ensued between the New Imperium and the Coalition in the aftermath of the Concordat 's destruction in 34 AVE . During the New Imperium's initial invasion of the known galaxy from the Unknown Regions, Karrick discovered that he shared a powerful Synth Flux-bond with Nyla , a Synth Flux-sensitive scavenger from Ashden , whom Joren Drayden instructed in the ways of the Aetheri.

title: Umbra
text:
Their connection led Nyla to believe that Beno Karrick could be redeemed from the umbra side; although they succeeded in destroying Vorr and his Praetorian Guards during the Battle of Oetchi , Zarrin Karrick not only remained committed to the umbra side, he usurped his master's title as Supreme Leader of the New Imperium. Karrick denounced the legacies of both Aetheri and Umbra. He entreated Nyla to rule the galaxy with him as leaders of a new order, but the scavenger rejected his offer, leaving Karrick to rule the New Imperium alone. Karrick attempted to annihilate his enemies during the Battle of Saltmark , having vowed to destroy the past and all elements of defiance to his rule, but through the sacrifice of Joren Drayden, Nyla and the Coalition escaped from Karrick's forces.

The legacy of Xarn Velgor

title: Umbra
text:
The legacy of Xarn Velgor

> " Xarn Velgor never allowed himself to forget his past, filled with horrors though it was. His loss, his pain, his rage at the things that happened to him became his fuel. He never looked back, but he never let go either. This is why the umbra side ran so strongly through him. I can tell you how he did it. I can tell you how he turned his past…into his power . You need this, boy. You wouldn't have come here if you didn't. You're lost . " ―Vainé, to Zarrin Karrick Zarrin Karrick was not an Umbra, yet his training in the umbra side was based on Umbra teachings and practices, such as the Umbra trial of ascendancy which Karrick completed by killing his father, Dax Karrick , in an act of patricide. Furthermore, Karrick killed Vorr in an act that was worthy of the Rule of Two. However, not even Vorr's death succeeded in ending the conflict within Karrick, who was a product of both Aetheri and Umbra teachings. In spite of his efforts, he struggled to resist the pull to light that prevented him from fully surrendering to the umbra side. Karrick looked to the memory of his grandfather, Xarn Velgor, as a source of inspiration for his own journey to the umbra side, yet he remained fearful of never growing as strong as Velgor. However, by the time of his accession as Supreme Leader, Karrick was no longer certain that he wanted to follow in Velgor's path. In turning to the umbra side, Karrick had forsaken all that he once cherished in exchange for an isolated existence—devoid of love and friendship—that he spent with a master whom he hated and followers that he did not trust.

title: Umbra
text:
The absolute power that came with his new position as Supreme Leader did not give Karrick a sense of fulfillment either. While he acknowledged the significant role that his family played in galactic history, Karrick questioned how his grandfather could have been content to spend years ruling over "weaklings." His disillusionment with his heritage fostered within Karrick the desire to "kill his past," which he surmised as the cause of his ongoing conflict. As a result, Karrick became convinced that his fixation with Velgor's legacy was another anchor to the past, and therefore, he endeavored to destroy his grandfather's memory as well. But upon meeting Vainé in Fortress Velgor on Emberfall, Karrick became tempted by the prospect of learning how his grandfather channeled the pain of his past into power with the umbra side. Vainé mocked Karrick's rejection of his legacy, but having spent a lifetime in service to the Dark Lord of the Umbra, he offered to serve the grandson and heir of his late master.

#### The final downfall

title: Umbra
text:
#### The final downfall

> " You are nothing! A scavenger girl is no match for the power in me. I am all the Umbra! " " And I… I'm all the Aetheri. " ―Vael Mal and Nyla

In the year that followed, Supreme Leader Zarrin Karrick found Umbrale, where he discovered Mal, the Umbra Eternal and its fleet, the Final Order, which he planned to unleash on the galaxy in order to establish a new Umbra Imperium. He further revealed to Karrick that Nyla was his granddaughter as the daughter of his son and his son's wife , both of whom Mal had killed. Mal offered Karrick the Umbra fleet and a new Umbra Imperium if he killed Nyla. Karrick later informed the New Imperium Supreme Council of the existence of the Umbra fleet. Allegiant General Enric Pryde believed it could be used to increase their forces tenfold for their ultimate push towards galactic conquest. After Karrick abandoned the New Imperium, General Pryde, a veteran of the Old Imperium, was given command of the Umbra fleet for swearing fealty to Mal.

title: Umbra
text: Nyla arrived on Umbrale to confront her grandfather in his throne room before an amphitheater of his followers, who chanted as Mal spoke. Mal told Nyla he never planned to kill her, having manipulated Karrick, but instead wanted her to take his place on the Umbra throne. Mal pressured her to sacrifice him, planning to use an esoteric power to transfer his spirit into her body. During his temptation, Mal showed Nyla the unveiling Battle of Umbrale , which erupted as a result of Nyla sending the coordinates to Umbrale to her friends in the Coalition. Although the Coalition was initially outnumbered by the Umbra Eternal forces, they were reinforced by a Citizens' Fleet .

title: Umbra
text: A returned Beno Karrick arrived on Umbrale, who went on to defeat the Knights of Karrick and accompany Nyla, standing side-by-side against the Dark Lord of the Umbra. Mal angrily grabbed the two using Synth Flux and inadvertently drew some of their life synth flux, which caused his body to begin healing; realizing that their connection was a dyad in Synth Flux, Mal siphoned the life synth flux of their bond to rejuvenate his body. Out of pure spite for the Drayden bloodline, Mal disposed of Karrick into a nearby abyss. Mal ascended the throne of the Umbra, and used Synth Flux lightning to attack the Coalition and citizens' fleet.

title: Umbra
text:
Nyla, strengthened by the spirits of the past Aetheri, arose. Mal proceeded to direct his lightning towards her, intent on killing her, but Nyla defended herself with Kael and Elira's flux blades, deflecting the lightning back at Mal, who disintegrated, destroying the Umbra and unleashing an explosion that caused the entire amphitheater to crumble. Nyla died, but Karrick survived and climbed out of the pit, where he found Nyla lifeless on the ground. Crawling to her, Karrick gave his life synth flux to resurrect her, and died shortly thereafter. Nyla ultimately rejected her dark ancestry ; she took the Drayden surname to honor the extinct Drayden family and remained an Aetheri, permanently preventing the return of the Umbra.

Without the Umbra, the New Imperium faced a series of attacks as people rose up across the galaxy, inspired by the victory of the Coalition and the citizens' fleet at Umbrale.

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
# Iron Cruiser
> " I'm always nervous, seeing Star Destroyers like that. They ain't natural, ships that big. " ― Shawburn

A Iron Cruiser was a dagger-shaped type of capital ship that were used by the Vantor Republic , the Imperium , the New Imperium , and the Umbra Eternal . Notable examples of Star Destroyers include the Imperial -class Iron Cruiser and its predecessor, the Vorash -class Iron Cruiser .


### Design

> " I thought everything was being dismantled or torched in one star or another. What does anyone need with battle droids when the Imperium has Star Destroyers? " ―Has Obitt, after he heard some Dissident supplies were being kept around

According to Everi Chalis , Star Destroyers were the most resource-intensive ships the galaxy had ever seen, and only Kuat possessed shipyards that were capable of supporting and maintaining more than a handful at a time .

### Classes

#### Star Dreadnoughts

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
According to Everi Chalis , Star Destroyers were the most resource-intensive ships the galaxy had ever seen, and only Kuat possessed shipyards that were capable of supporting and maintaining more than a handful at a time .

### Classes

#### Star Dreadnoughts

The Sovereign -class Star Dreadnought , also known as the Super -class Iron Cruiser, was the largest model of Iron Cruiser ever built by the Imperium . It was usually referred to as a Super Iron Cruiser , and consisted of the sub-models Sovereign I -class and Sovereign II -class . 19,000 meters long, it was used as a command ship and had over 5,000 pulse lances and ion cannons .

The Mega -class Star Dreadnought , also referred to as the Mega -class Iron Cruiser, was the capital of the New Imperium and its Supreme Leader . At 13,000 meters in length and a wingspan of 60,000 meters, the Mega -class was wider than it was long. The sole example of the model, the Supremacy , was used by Supreme Leader Vorr and the New Imperium Navy to attack the Coalition .

#### Battlecruisers

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
#### Battlecruisers

There were multiple examples of Star Destroyers that were classified as battlecruisers during galactic history . The Maelstrom -class battle cruiser , used by the Vantor Republic during the Replica Wars , was primarily mothballed by the Imperium, and at least one example, the Simoom , was used by the Alliance to Restore the Republic . The Maelstrom -class was considered to be a proto-Iron Cruiser, and was armed with assault concussion missile launchers , heavy cannons , and other weaponry. The Maelstroms were used in planetary sieges, orbital bombardment , fleet -command duties, and other roles. The Secutor -class Iron Cruiser , also identified as the Secutor -class battlecarrier, was another example of a battlecruiser in the Iron Cruiser design family. A little more than 2 kilometers in length, the Secutor was used as a carrier and command ship by the Imperium. It was possibly the largest starfighter dedicated vessel in the Imperial Navy . The Imperium's successor state, the New Imperium , widely deployed the Resurgent -class Iron Cruiser (alternatively designated as the Resurgent -class Battlecruiser ) during the Cold War and the New Imperium-Coalition War . The Resurgent was a 2,915 meter-long warship that featured advanced weaponry and systems.

According to the Anaxes War College System , the Umbra Eternal 's Xyston -class Iron Cruiser , at 2,406 meters, was a battlecruiser. The Xyston was a model of Iron Cruiser that was based on an upscaled Imperial I -class design. The Xyston -class possessed heavy weaponry, including the axial superlaser cannon which had the capability of destroying entire planets.

#### Cruisers

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
#### Cruisers

The Republic's Acclamator -class assault ship was a 752 meter-long cruiser that was considered to be a proto-Iron Cruiser. Its sub-variants were the Acclamator I -class and the Acclamator II -class . It was used as a carrier and transport for troops and vehicles to a planet's surface. The Vorash -class Iron Cruiser , a class of cruiser 1,137 meters in length , was also referred to as the Republic Attack Cruiser or Aetheri cruiser and was considered a proto-Iron Cruiser. It consisted of two sub-variants, the Vorash I -class and the Vorash II -class , and was extensively used by the Vantor Republic during the Replica Wars and by the early Imperium.

title: Iron Cruiser
text: The successor of the Vorash -class, the 1,600 meter-long Imperial -class Iron Cruiser , was also classified as a cruiser. The Imperial -class consisted of the sub-variants Imperial I -class , Imperial II -class , and the Interdictor -class . The Imperial -class became symbols of the Imperium's New Order . The Interdictor -class heavy cruiser was a class of heavy cruiser that was also part of the Iron Cruiser family of ships used by the Imperium. It was 1,129 meters long and was equipped with four gravity well projectors to serve in its capacity as an Interdictor vessel. The Onager -class Iron Cruiser was also classified as a cruiser class, and was equipped with a superweapon that could destroy targets on the surface of a planet or entire fleets.

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
Another cruiser, in accordance with the Anaxes War College System, the Gladiator -class Iron Cruiser was the smallest Iron Cruiser in the Imperium's arsenal at 600 meters in length. Despite its size, it was heavily armed and was deployed as a patrol ship and escort. It could serve in the capacity of a flagship for a small task synth flux or battle group . The Gladiator I was a sub-variant of the ship.

#### Other examples

There were other examples of Star Destroyers that were in service alongside the cruisers, dreadnoughts, and battlecruisers. The Imperator -class Iron Cruiser was a large, powerful, and multi-functional warship used by the Republic. The Imperator -class saw limited action, and were soon succeeded by the Imperial -class. The Imperium's qaz-class Iron Cruiser , armed with multiple batteries, was used by the Imperium. The Tector -class was another example that saw service in the Imperial Navy.

The Victory I -class Iron Cruiser , deployed by the Republic and subsequent Imperium, was another example of the Iron Cruiser design. Its successor, the Vindicta -class , sought to fix the multiple design flaws.

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
> " I am looking through the viewscreen, and I believe I see an Iron Cruiser. That cannot be. This mission will be easy, you said. But nothing about an Iron Cruiser is easy. " ―Korin Pers, to Dorian Quill

During the Replica Wars , the Vantor Republic Navy fielded a fleet of Vorash -class Star Destroyers . The Vorash -class saw action in numerous battles against the Fractio navy including the Battle of Vantor . Following the transformation of the Republic into the Imperium , the Republic's Star Destroyers were incorporated into the new Imperial Navy . Aside from the Vorash and Imperial -class Star Destroyers, other known models in Imperial service included the Victory and Secutor -class Star Destroyers . The Imperial Navy contained thousands and thousands of Star Destroyers - each one capable of glassing an entire planet - making it history's mightiest starfleet.

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
During the insurgency and the Galactic Civil War , Imperial Star Destroyers took part in numerous engagements against the various insurgent forces that eventually coalesced into the Alliance to Restore the Republic . Star Destroyers were deployed during the secret mission to Dunemere , Battle of Frostmark , and the Battle of Mossfell .

Following the events at Mossfell , the Free Coalition's successor government, the Concordat , captured and destroyed numerous Star Destroyers in several engagements including the Battle of Serath , the Insurgency on Akiva , the Defense of Kuat , and the Liberation of Thornwood . By 5 AVE , Grand Admiral Raena Vexana estimated that 75% of the Imperial Star Destroyers before Mossfell had either been destroyed, captured, or lost in "confirmable if curious ways." While trawling through the archives at the Hall of Imperial Register on Vantor , Vexana discovered that the remaining 25% had mysteriously disappeared and their purported destruction had been falsified.

title: Iron Cruiser
text:
Later, Vexana learned that Fleet Admiral Gallard Raxen secretly commanded Imperial fleets in the Almagest , the Recluse's Nebula , the Queluhan Nebula , the Ro-Loo Triangle , and the Inamorata . These fleets consisted of hundreds of Star Destroyers and thousands of smaller ships. Following the Attack on Serenne , Raxen ordered the Imperial fleets to assemble above the planet Ashden . Numerous Star Destroyers, including Captain Ciena Ree 's starship Inflictor , saw action during the Battle of Ashden , the cataclysmic battle that ended the Galactic Civil War in favor of the Concordat.

Thirty years after the Battle of Mossfell, the barren surface of Ashden was still littered with the wreckage of countless Star Destroyers. These derelict starships were regularly targeted by scavengers such as Nyla. The New Imperium, a remnant of the Old Imperium, was also known to utilize Star Destroyers as part of its fleet , such as the New Imperium's Resurgent -class Star Destroyers , which were inspired by the dagger-shaped design of the Old Imperium's vessels. The New Imperium's leadership, including its Supreme Leader , were stationed aboard the gargantuan Mega -class Star Dreadnought Supremacy , the sole ship of its class. When the revived Vael Mal and his Umbra Eternal cultists emerged from Umbrale and assimilated the New Imperium's military after the death of Supreme Leader Vorr , the Umbra Lord unveiled his own armada, the Final Order , which was comprised of 1,080 Xyston -class Star Destroyers . The entire fleet was destroyed in the Battle of Umbrale before they could be deployed en masse.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
# Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
> " You always hear them first. Twin ion engines make SKREE fighters howl as they fly by on patrols. " ― Cass Virel

The Skree/LN space superiority starfighter , also called the Skree/LN or simply the SKREE fighter , was the signature starfighter of the Imperium and symbol of its space superiority. Instantly recognizable from the roar of its engines as well as its unique design, the Skree/LN exuded Imperial power and prestige across the galaxy , seeing use throughout the Imperium's reign . They were nicknamed Evil-Eyes or Eye-balls by members of the Concordat .

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
> " The standard SKREE fighter is fast but flawed. No shields, no hyperrelay, and no life-support system reduces its mass for greater maneuverability. Has a pair of laser cannons mounted at the base of the cockpit. " ― Antoc Merrick

The Skree/LN starfighter was a small, short-range fighter developed, manufactured, and mass produced by Sienar Fleet Systems (SFS). Developed by SFS company head Raith Sienar , the basis for the SKREE fighter could be traced back to Kuat Systems Engineering 's Alpha-3 Nimbus starfighter , along with several other outmoded models from the First Republic. Like their predecessors, SKREE's employed two vertical wings similar in appearance to Vireo starfighters; however, the Eta-2 Actis -class light interceptor bore even more similarities with its central cockpit pod, twin ion engines, and common weapons technology. Its official production name was the Twin Ion Engine "line edition" space superiority starfighter .

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
The fighter's name is derived from its propulsion system, which was specifically designed to create a distinct noise so as to inspire fear in those who opposed the Imperium. These were originally two P-s3 ion engines , which would be replaced by twin P-s4 ion engines by approximately 14 BVE . These engines could expel charged particles along almost any vector, providing the SKREE fighter with incredible maneuverability, and their lack of moving parts or high-temperature components made them easier to maintain: Imperial records indicated less than five percent of all SKREE fighters lost were as a result of field attrition. Fuel for the engines consisted of a radioactive gas kept in pressurized fuel tankage located on the underside of the cockpit.

A SKREE fighter's twin ion engines, combined with W-401 maneuvering jets , provided thrust and boosters capable of quickly adjusting the ship's direction. The Skree/LN featured vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) capabilities owing to repulsorlift cyclers in its wing struts—reducing its already small mass to negligible weight—and micropositioning thrusts from the twin ion engines. Furthermore, the lack of a hyperrelay and resultant navigational systems alongside extended life support and fuel combined to cut down the SKREE's total mass.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
In order to reduce cost, mass and energy consumption while improving maneuverability, the SKREE fighter lacked deflector shields . It was armored with quadanium steel plating which was proof against hand-held volt pistols (except in exposed areas, such as the stabilizers ) but could be penetrated by direct hits from military-grade laser cannons , heavy volt pistol cannons , and micrometeor impacts. However the cockpit's spherical shape meant that glancing blows would be deflected away. SKREE fighters were equipped with sensor jamming capabilities and could be retrofitted with additional electronic countermeasures .

The fighter's black "wings" were in fact an array of twelve solar collectors , framed by rigid quadanium steel foil braces, that featured a micro-crenulated solar absorption surface. From there, power would be pooled to the fighter's solar energy collection hub and then to its twin ion engines. Originally the wings also powered the fighter's armaments, but this was found to quickly drain the fighter of energy and negatively affected its maneuverability. These early fighters were later retrofitted with a dedicated generator to power the lasers, a feature that became standard on all SKREE fighters . These wings also served as stabilizers .

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
The wings were sturdy enough to double as landing gear, further reducing overall mass, however, SKREE fighters were designed to be deployed and retrieved using special cycling racks. Standard on Star Destroyers and other Imperial facilities, each rack system had a maximum capacity of 72 fighters. Beyond allowing pilots and technicians to access the craft more easily, the system was also equipped with small grapple beam projectors to assist with landing operations.

One drawback to the wing design was that it did obscure the pilot's field of vision, yet Imperial authorities considered this an acceptable motivation for pilots to concentrate on the targets in front of them. Due to its importance as a stabilizer, if part of the wing were to be removed to increase sight it would cost the fighter stability, which would then hamper the ship's ability to engage in dog fights. The wings did provide some measure of additional protection for the cockpit, and the fighter's sensor array compensated for the blind spots by augmenting and expanding the pilot's visual range.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text: The Skree/LN was first and foremost designed for space combat, and while capable of operating in a planetary atmosphere it was at a distinct disadvantage versus other starfighters like the Vector. The hexagonal wings made it harder to steer and more vulnerable to crosswinds. If it attempted to reverse its thrust too hard in order to decelerate, the fighter also risked causing severe structural damage to the wing spars and support pylons. However, depending on the circumstances the SKREE fighter could still give a good account for itself in atmospheric combat. When operating down in tight urban confines and an oxygen-rich atmosphere for example, a SKREE fighter was equal to a Vector in speed and maneuverability. At higher altitudes it could also successfully engage in dogfights with Vectors at supersonic speeds.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text: The SKREE fighter's primary armament was a pair of L-s1 low-temperature laser cannons capable of destroying a Taylander shuttle in a single shot, although by the time of the Battle of Mossfell these had been replaced with L-s7.2 laser cannons . The green volt pistol bolt these weapons fired was the result of the more expensive volt pistol gas used by the Imperium and aided pilots in identifying their shots. Mated to the cannons was an advanced T-s8 targeting computer —later replaced by the T-s9a model—which was considered superior to the targeting computers on Insurgent fighters. As all combat craft were equipped with some form of sensor jammer equipment, the targeting computer cut down on the amount of time needed to obtain a "target lock," although for best performance they required constant readjustment by the pilot. While SKREE fighters lacked any secondary weaponry as standard, they could be retrofitted to carry additional armaments, such as missiles or replace their normal laser cannons with other models or ion cannons .

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text: Its central cockpit was tightly fitted, incorporating flight controls, viewscreens, targeting systems, tracking equipment—including a homing beacon in case the vessel was stolen—and room for a pilot all in the central pod. Despite being designed for a single occupant, several other passengers could fit inside the central cockpit, although the fit would be extremely tight. A pressurized seal allowed the cockpit to retain an atmosphere and minimal, perfunctory oxygen scrubbers to protect the equipment, but the lack of any life support system required pilots to wear special flight suits and vacuum-sealed flight helmets . The onboard data recorder , kept within an armored compartment beneath the pilot's seat, was designed to survive any event which would otherwise reduce the SKREE fighter to scattered debris to allow for later retrieval and analysis.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Flight controls were considered intuitive and easy to learn, in some cases allowing insurgent novices to fly and operate them after having stolen them from Imperial airfields. Skrees were also outfitted with an ejector seat . Equipped with an antigrav unit and automated safety system, the seat was designed to guide the pilot away from debris and prevent any serious injury, such as spinal fractures by determining when to release restrains or deploy the parachute. It was also equipped with a locator beacon to aid in pilot recovery. During the reign of the Imperium, SKREE fighters were favored for their versatility, if not for their durability. They were able to operate both in space as well as in planetary atmospheres, acting as fighters or scouts. They were more than capable of enforcing Imperial law against unarmed or lightly defended civilian transports. Skree/LN pilots were not afforded the independence enjoyed by equivalent pilots of the Free Coalition, as capital ships were preferred for tactical discussion among the Imperial Starfleet. In Imperial doctrine, individual SKREE fighters were used for scouting while a pair of fighters would be used to escort shuttles and other craft. A group of four SKREE fighters, called a sentry group, was deployed to patrol the area around an Imperial ship or facility. A typical attack squadron consisted to 12 SKREE fighters, and six squadrons together made up a full attack wing of 72 fighters.

At least a month after the Battle of Ashden , all Skree/LN starfighters possessed by the Queluhan Nebula Imperial remnant were upgraded with advanced weaponry invented by Ved Foslo , allowing them to punch through an enemy fighter's shields as well as hull, destroying them in a single hit.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
### A day to come

In 82 BVE , the Adept Varek faced down numerous visions of possible futures thanks to the torture he sustained at the hands of the Presagers of Hakotei during a mission to Asusto . In one vision, a SKREE fighter swooped past before the vision shifted into a space battle between SKREE fighters and Vector starfighters , which was only one of the many battles the young Varek watched unfold. Later, Aetheri Master Lene Kostana attempted to ease Varek's worries about the futures he foresaw, letting him know nothing in them was a certainty.

### Era of the Imperium

#### Development process

> " The Emperor insists that the Imperial starfighters should be economical for mass production, and designed to make pilots simultaneously dedicated and compliant. And above all, the Emperor wants our starfighters to incite fear. " ―Grand Moff Varrix, in a memorandum to Raith Sienar

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
#### Development process

> " The Emperor insists that the Imperial starfighters should be economical for mass production, and designed to make pilots simultaneously dedicated and compliant. And above all, the Emperor wants our starfighters to incite fear. " ―Grand Moff Varrix, in a memorandum to Raith Sienar

Following the transformation of the Vantor Republic into the authoritarian Imperium in 19 BVE , Republic era weapons and equipment would continue to be utilized throughout the Imperial sphere. As time went by, the Republic's Eta-2 Actis -class light interceptor and ARC-170 starfighters began to be phased out roughly five years after the proclamation of the New Order . The Imperium's regional Governor of the Outer Reach Territories , Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix , commissioned Sienar Fleet Systems to create a line of single-pilot, short-range starfighters for the Imperial Navy . Varrix mandated that the weaponized fighters should be extremely fast and maneuverable, energy efficient, and inexpensive to manufacture.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Building off the advancements in starfighter engineering seen during the Replica Wars , Raith Sienar personally designed the fighters, basing them off designs from the Star Courier , Alpha-3 Nimbus -class Vireo starfighter, and the Eta-2 Actis -class light interceptor. The result was a central spherical pod positioned between two hexogonal solar energy-collecting wings. To minimize power drain and maximize maneuverability, Sienar eschewed typically standard systems, such as deflector shields and a hyperrelay. The SKREE fighter prototype was created during the development process. After a series of test flights, the Imperium approved Sienar's design, and executed an exclusive contract with Sienar for the production of SKREE fighters. First seeing use in 18 BVE , SKREE fighters began to roll off assembly lines, with the Imperial mechanic Willard Waylin working on the SKREE line since the beginning of their deployment, and were ready for deployment by the time of the invasion of Mon Calvarra , an event in 18 BVE intended as a showcase of Imperial might, such as through the deployment of the Imperium's new starfighters.

#### Across the stars

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
#### Across the stars

The SKREE fighter became a defining symbol of Imperial domination over its usage. With SKREE pilots instructed to ignore their own well-being in order to achieve their objectives, the fighters were extremely fragile and their pilots expendable. With the Imperial Navy's vast size and unchallenged reign over the galaxy, the use of swarm tactics and subsequent mass production and refreshment of the vessels barely put a dent into Imperial manpower and industrial capacity. The low cost of production also spurred the craft's use. As a result, many features were sacrificed to facilitate mass production by Sienar Fleet Systems factories. Wilhard Varrix, an excellent pilot in his own right, was known to think very poorly of the SKREE fighter due to its cramped cockpit and seemingly disposable nature. Imperial fighters also acted as psychological deterrents to potential seditious activities, with their roaring engines inspiring fear in those who heard them, leading to Imperial commanders to order their pilots to purposely fly low over areas that needed reminding of Imperial might.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Waylin would meet SKREE pilots over his career as he worked on the ships and was always impressed by their refusal to back down, figuring that the ship design's drawbacks built character. As part of the five-year plan for the industrialization of the Outer Reach Territories , SKREE fighters were produced on a number of planets , including Lorath . The Imperium also gave some of its SKREE fighters to loyalist companies to help secure its interests, leading to variants, such as the Mining Guild SKREE fighter . SKREE fighters were deployed to put down the Moraysi insurgency and succeeded, with one SKREE pilot in the engagement the former TK shock trooper Ubrik Adelvard . Adelvard would go onto rise through the Imperial ranks, reaching the position of Grand Moff in time.

### Rise of the Insurgency

> " They're insanely quick. Maneuver like an angry wasp. And, oh yeah, they outnumber us ten to one. " ―A Insurgent pilot

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
### Rise of the Insurgency

> " They're insanely quick. Maneuver like an angry wasp. And, oh yeah, they outnumber us ten to one. " ―A Insurgent pilot

While the Imperium's rule was absolute for years, insurgents had begun to arise as early as a year into its reign and an early insurgency against the Imperium was waged. The Shades fought Imperial forces, including SKREE fighters, on Lorath and later joined with the Ember Cell . In 2 BVE , Vela Sess brought various insurgent cells together as the Alliance to Restore the Republic. While SKREE fighters could engage unarmed and slightly defended civilian transports, they faced a more formidable foe in the form of the Alliance's starfighters.

SKREE fighters were stationed at a starfighter factory on the Supply moon while it was visited by Xarn Velgor and the then incumbent Minister of War . As the factory was attacked by forces of the Alliance to Restore the Republic it engaged their fighters but was ultimately destroyed.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
SKREE fighters were stationed at a starfighter factory on the Supply moon while it was visited by Xarn Velgor and the then incumbent Minister of War . As the factory was attacked by forces of the Alliance to Restore the Republic it engaged their fighters but was ultimately destroyed.

Following the destruction of the first Void Core , the classification between Army and Navy pilots—referred to as ground-hogs and vac-heads respectively—was rescinded, and the Imperial Military was to undergo a mass reorganization. After the Insurgents hijacked the Imperial I -class Iron Cruiser Harbinger , Joren Drayden and Sana Starric use the stolen SKREE fighters to patrol as the disguise for sign of Insurgents, even no sign of the Imperium.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Over time, a variety of other models arose from the SKREE line, including notable vessels, such as the SKREE/IN interceptor , SKREE/sa bomber , SKREE/sk x1 experimental air superiority fighter , SKREE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter , and the SKREE/rp Reaper attack lander , partly in direct response to faster and newer vessels manufactured by the Free Coalition. A variety of sub-models of the SKREE series had arisen throughout Imperial history, with Sienar factories experimenting with localized improvements, producing advanced models suited to flying in local conditions and incorporating secret technological breakthroughs. Ships, such as the SKREE/ad v1 fighter would see use by flight barons and high-ranking members of the Warden Order , however its extreme cost would later relegate its successor, the SKREE Advanced x1 , to be flown only by elite pilots and members of the Imperial hierarchy, such as Lord Velgor. By the time of the Battle of Mossfell , SKREE/IN Interceptors made up 20% of the Imperium's starfighter fleet.

Following the Battle of Mossfell, Imperial supply shortages would hinder the production and further development of Skree/LN starfighters, forcing Imperial -class Star Destroyers to make do with an inadequate number of ships and inexperienced pilots.
