text:
Following the Battle of Mossfell, Imperial supply shortages would hinder the production and further development of Skree/LN starfighters, forcing Imperial -class Star Destroyers to make do with an inadequate number of ships and inexperienced pilots.

Production data was classified, but according to numerous estimates, Sienar manufactured a minimum of approximately 4.6 million Imperial SKREE fighters for Star Destroyers , other Imperial Naval vessels, and Imperial garrisons and defense stations. Most estimates maintain that more Imperial SKREE fighters were operational at the same time than any other starfighter in history.

### Legacy

The legacy of the SKREE fighter was not forgotten on the galactic stage, with Sienar Fleet System's successor, Sienar-Jaemus Fleet Systems , producing the latest-generation SKREE fighters utilized by the Imperium's successor state, the New Imperium . The SKREE/sf space superiority fighter and Skree/FO space superiority fighter were a direct continuance of the imprint the SKREE fighter had on galactic citizenry, and featured advanced weapons systems and a two-seated arrangement for use by the Order's Special Forces . The Ugnaught Kuiil , himself former indentured servant of the Imperium, used a workbench built out of an abandoned SKREE cockpit. Future historians would argue that flaws inherent in the SKREE fighter design were allowed to remain, if only to increase the Imperium's dependency on Sienar Fleet Systems for continued production of the craft, along with increased dependency on Kuat Drive Yards capital-scale carrier ships.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Vask Light & Magic 's (VLM) Colin Cantwell created the concept model that established the SKREE fighter's ball-cockpit and hexagonal-panels design for First Dawn . Sound designer Beno Burtt created the distinctive SKREE fighter sound effect by combining an elephant call with a car driving on wet pavement.

The original Skree/LN fighters seen in First Dawn were relatively white, but were originally meant to have a maroon hull. One of the benefits of a slightly reddish color would have been that the fighter models would not have been as prone to "blue spill" as gray models were during filming against a blue screen. However, film composition tests revealed that the maroon ships blended too quickly into the mostly black star field when moving away from the camera, so a light gray was used instead. The SKREE fighter models featured in Rise of the Imperium and Return of the Aetheri were blue-gray.

Combat scenes between SKREE fighters and the Corsair Wing and Free Coalition Vector fighters in First Dawn were meant to be reminiscent of World War II dogfight footage; editors used World War II air combat clips as placeholders while Vask Light & Magic completed the movie's special effects.

title: Skree/LN space superiority starfighter
text:
Combat scenes between SKREE fighters and the Corsair Wing and Free Coalition Vector fighters in First Dawn were meant to be reminiscent of World War II dogfight footage; editors used World War II air combat clips as placeholders while Vask Light & Magic completed the movie's special effects.

Skree/LN fighters are one of two starships available to Imperial players in Aetherion Battlefront , the other being the SKREE/IN interceptor. Compared to the Vectors and Arrows , SKREE fighters lack shields but instead possess good maneuverability and speed. However, their large wing panels make them very easy to hit in dogfights, giving Insurgent fighters a slight advantage in ship-to-ship engagements.

Ultimate Aetherion stated that SKREE fighters built on Lorath had shorter wings, as explanation for stylistic choices made for the Skree/LN's design in the animated series Aetherion Insurgents . However, Insurgents Recon: Inside "Always Two There Are" on Aetherion.com ( backup link ) said that there is no difference. Since then, Pablo Hidra confirmed on Twitter that Ultimate Aetherion was incorrect. SKREE fighters later appeared in the 2016 anthology film Renegade One: A Aetherion Story . Their animation model in the film featured noticeably smaller transparisteel windows that what was seen in prior Aetherion works, such as First Dawn . The 2016 reference book Aetherion: Renegade One: The Ultimate Visual Guide by Pablo Hidra was the first reference book to identify the SKREE fighter as the Skree/LN space superiority starfighter. It also defined the "ln" within the starfighter's name as standing for "line edition."

title: Dunemere
text:
# Dunemere
> " Well, if there's a bright center to the universe, you're on the planet that it's farthest from. " ―Joren Drayden, to Astra-9 — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Dunemere was a sparsely inhabited circumbinary desert planet located in the galaxy 's Outer Reach Territories . Part of a binary star system , the planet orbited two scorching suns , resulting in the world lacking the necessary surface water to sustain large populations. As a result, many residents of the planet instead drew water from the atmosphere via moisture farms . The planet also had little surface vegetation. It was the homeworld to the native Duskkin and Dunefolk Raider species and of Kael and Joren Drayden , who would go on to shape galactic history.

title: Dunemere
text:
It saw a population explosion following the search for valuable mining deposits on the planet's silicate surface. Finding the ore to have undesirable metallurgical properties, mining firms left the planet en masse, leaving behind valuable equipment, most notably large sandcrawlers , which were later used by the Duskkin population. The planet then became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, and fell under the influence of the Grak Clan while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants endured.

Generally ignored by the galaxy at large, Dunemere gained the notice of the Imperium during the Galactic Civil War when an escape pod carrying two droids in possession of top-secret information landed on the sandy Outer Reach world. The Imperium went on to establish a heavier presence on the planet, forging a tenuous relationship with Grukk Desilijic Tiure of the Grak Clan. Open conflict soon broke out between the Imperium and a Free Coalition cell on Dunemere that culminated in a battle that left the Imperium's hold on the world significantly weakened.

title: Dunemere
text: Following the death of Grukk and the withdrawal of Imperial forces after the Battle of Mossfell , an enormous power vacuum occurred on the world, with numerous crime syndicates like the Red Key Raiders attempting to build legitimacy as mining companies. Eventually, former bounty hunter Vex Vark returned and took over Grukk's former territory. Coming into conflict with both the Grak Clan and the Gruv Syndicate , the new Daimyo was pulled into a gang war that threatened the future of Dunemere. With help from the Ferrik Dinna Verrick , Vark rallied the denizens of the settlements Port Vail and Freetown to push back against the invaders, ushering in a new era of respect between the people of the planet.

title: Dunemere
text:
> " What a desolate place this is. " ―Astra-9

Dunemere was a hot desert planet located in the Outer Reach , a region of the galaxy far removed from its core . It had three moons , Ghomrassen , Guermessa , and Chenini . Dunemere orbited twin suns , Tatoo I and Tatoo II . According to Duskkin folklore, the desert known as the Dune Sea was once a true ocean . The whole planet was covered in harsh deserts, and only a small part of its northern hemisphere could sustain intelligent life. The landscape was covered with sand dunes, mountains , and canyons, which made traversing the planet very difficult. Due to the absence of surface water , those who lived on Dunemere had to draw moisture through the dry air .

title: Dunemere
text:
Rain was incredibly rare on Dunemere, coming once a year , decade , or century . When the rain came, some plants were able to grow in a brief yet glorious period. Inhabiting the planet were many native species , the largest of which were the carnivorous krayt dragons . The common krayt dragon, while more plentiful, was shadowed by the greater krayt dragon, which submerged itself under the shifting sands and used its powerful limbs to traverse through the dunes. In addition, the common strider and eopie species also found a home on the world, along with dewbacks , rontos , womp rats , massiffs , and scurriers .

The cities of Dunemere were frequently blasted by sandstorms and the inhabitants always seemed to know when one was coming. Not much distinguished the towns as the poor standard of living was common. The cities were separated from each other by large expanses of deserts. Rural life, on the other hand, was mostly small moisture farms that sold water and food for a meager living.

title: Dunemere
text:
### Early history

> " Of course, if you believe the Legend of Lehon, Dunemere was once covered by lush jungle, the domain of the Kumumgah, although little evidence has been found for their existence. " ―A B'omarr monk — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Dunemere was the homeworld of the Duskkin and Dunefolk Raider species. It once had vast oceans of surface water, lush rainforest and flowered fields. According to the Legend of Lehon , Dunemere had also been inhabited by a group called the Kumumgah during this time, but there was little evidence to support the story. Sometime in Dunemere's history, the whole planet became a desert by unknown means when the oceans dried away. Much later, it would be colonized by early settlers and explorers, who mistook the planet for a third sun owing to its highly reflective silicate surface.

title: Dunemere
text:
As a result of sporadic and unsuccessful colonization ventures, the planet became a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, while scattered, isolated settlements of hard-working inhabitants attempted to earn a living in the wastes. A long-ago mining boom saw the widespread use of sandcrawlers on the desert plains in an effort to mine valuable minerals. However, after it was discovered that most valuable minerals could be found on the surface, along with most minerals having unwanted metallurgic properties, the sandcrawlers were abandoned and eventually picked up by the native Duskkins for use as shelter and mobile bases, from which they collected scrap from thousands of years of crashed spacecraft and failed mining projects.

Offworlders erected various cities in the desert, and colonists who decided to stay on the planet built moisture farms. The B'omarr Order on Dunemere kept their disembodied brains floating in jars that hung below their spider -like droid bodies, and built a monastery on the planet which would eventually come under the ownership of Grukk Desilijic Tiure as his palace .

title: Dunemere
text:
Most wealth eventually found its way into the city of Port Vail , with most of it procured from gambling and off-world trade, especially through the lucrative black market. The influx of commercial ventures fueled Port Vail's growth, eventually securing its regional importance as a hub of economic and financial activity. With high tariffs imposed by the Graks, some believed themselves able to escape paying them by doing business in the planet's de facto capital , however often found themselves scammed and broke if not through gambling, through simple bad luck.

### Scum and villainy

> " The Republic doesn't exist out here. We must survive on our own. " ―Shira Drayden, to Lira Ondar

In the last decades of the Vantor Republic , Dunemere was known as a haven for smugglers and criminal activity, including slavery . The dunefolk regularly attacked Fort Dunefolk , earning them their name of "Dunefolk Raiders." It was home to a human slave named Shira Drayden and her son Kael .

title: Dunemere
text: During this period, Queen Lira Ondar of Ondara escaped the capture of her homeworld by the Commerce Combine , and she took refuge on Dunemere with her companions and protectors, including the Aetheri Master Sorin Vael and his apprentice Orien Kade . The Draydens befriended Ondar's party, and the young slave ended up participating in a dune race to help his new friends obtain a new T-14 hyperrelay generator for their damaged starship . After discovering that Kael Drayden would make an exceptional recruit for the Aetheri Order, Master Sorin Vael managed to obtain his freedom from the junk dealer Waddu in the city of Port Vail, and the Queen's party left Dunemere with the boy. After participating in numerous adventures, including the Invasion of Ondara, the former Tatooinian slave joined the Aetheri Order under Kade's tutelage.

title: Dunemere
text: Ten years later, Drayden, now a gifted but unruly Aetheri student, sensed that his mother, who had stayed on Dunemere and gotten married , was in terrible pain. Drayden returned to the desert world in the company of Ondar, who was now a senator of the Republic and the young Aetheri's secret lover. It transpired that Shira Drayden had been captured by Dunefolk Raiders and was detained in one of their camps. When Drayden finally discovered his mother's location, he arrived too late, and she died in his arms from the consequences of the Tuskens' mistreatment of her. Enraged, the young Aetheri slaughtered the entire Dunefolk tribe. This had serious consequences as the first step towards Kael Drayden's fall from grace. Shortly after the incident, the Replica Wars broke out, and the tortured Tatooinian Aetheri became a major player of the pan-galactic conflict.

title: Dunemere
text:
For the most part, Dunemere avoided the Replica Wars. Nevertheless, an Aetheri-led mission to Grukk's Palace occurred, with the Aetheri hoping to rescue Rotto the Grakling from the Dissident Alliance . Later during the war, Chairman Papanoida and his son, Ion Papanoida headed to Dunemere to track down the bounty hunter Greedo , who had kidnapped members of their family.

Three years after the start of the war, Drayden fell to the umbra side and joined the Umbra , old adversaries of the Aetheri who had long planned to take over the galaxy. The Imperium , a new regime established to replace the Republic, started to hunt all Aetheri. Drayden's former master Orien Kade went into hiding on Dunemere, bringing the infant son of the fallen Aetheri with him. On the desert expanses of Dunemere, Kade hoped that he could keep young Joren from his father's evil influence. Kade entrusted the boy to Shira's stepson, Owen Havel , and his wife Brue .

### Time of great hardship

title: Dunemere
text:
### Time of great hardship

> " It was the worst drought anyone could remember. The moisture farmers could barely gather enough water from their vaporators to keep themselves alive, let alone to trade in town for food and supplies. Especially with Grukk's thugs collecting " water taxes ." Rumor was that the bloated gangster took lavish baths all throughout the day. Lest he perspire in the heat. But I didn't believe that rumor. I'd met Grukk. Grukk had never bathed in his life. " ―An excerpt from The Journals of Beno Kade In 9 BVE , The Grand Warden , The Fifth Warden , and the Third Warden had landed on Dunemere looking for an Aetheri on the run from the imperium. The Aetheri, " Nari ," had escaped the Wardens originally, but was eventually found and killed. The inhabitants of the planet were surprised by the arrival of the Wardens, since Dunemere was not part of the Imperium , and for this reason the Warden Order did not have jurisdiction on the planet, but this by no means prevents them from operating. Later, Bael Solen shows up on Dunemere looking for Orien Kade's help in finding his daughter, Elira Solen. The Third Warden eventually returns to Dunemere looking to murder Joren Drayden. The Third Warden redeems herself and decided not to hurt Joren, and brings him back to his uncles.

title: Dunemere
text: In the years following Theron Mal's formation of his New Order, the Great Drought of Dunemere scorched the world's surface, impoverishing the many moisture farmers of a reliable source of income to procure food and other basic supplies. The situation was not helped by Grukk's thugs collecting "water taxes" from the many towns and isolated settlements across the planet, often resorting to threats and brute synth flux to acquire enough water for the crime lord. With Orien Kade witnessing the suffering of the population, he disabled the weapons of the thugs, allowing the populace to chase them off. Later, a young Joren Drayden attempted to confront the thugs, but was ultimately rescued by Orien after falling unconscious in a brief scuffle. With the legacy of the Aetheri safe, Orien vowed never to return to town, while a week later the drought finally ended, and Grukk vowed revenge on the man who had stolen his water, to no avail.

title: Dunemere
text:
The Imperium annexed Dunemere at one point but largely ignored the planet. All the same, the Imperium left a small garrison on Dunemere. Additionally, the Imperium's rise prompted the Graks to revise their often times shady business schemes, resulting in a transfer of regional wealth and influence from Port Vail to Port Kess , prompting the slow economic decline of Port Vail.

In 2 BVE , the former Umbra apprentice Vreth traveled to Dunemere to hunt down his old nemesis Orien Kade. Unable to draw the Aetheri Master out of hiding, Vreth used the fragment of the Searmark Umbra reliquary to lure the Aetheri insurgent Cass Virel to the planet. Cass traveled with the C1-series astromech droid Chomper to Dunemere. The two insurgents were attacked by Dunefolk Raiders, who damaged their RZ-1T trainer . After being lost in the desert, Cass and Chomper were rescued by Kade, who revealed Vreth's deception. Kade then instructed the two insurgents to return to Atollon while he defeated and fatally wounded Vreth in combat. As Vreth died in Kade's arms, Kade confirmed Vreth's suspicions that he was hiding the Seeded One .

### War comes to Dunemere

title: Dunemere
text:
### War comes to Dunemere

> " Lord Velgor! It is my distinct pleasure and great honor to welcome you to Dunemere! " ―Ardo Banch, to Xarn Velgor

Shortly after the Battle of Halcyon in the Galactic Civil War , the droids Bolt-3 and Astra-9 landed on Dunemere's surface in an escape pod after their CR90 corvette the Tantiva IV was captured by the Imperial I -class Iron Cruiser Reckoning . With the droids carrying the technical readouts to the Void Core , a task synth flux was sent to the planet in order to capture the two droids, marking the moment the Imperium began to truly pay attention to Dunemere. Upon coming in contact with a Duskkin dune hauler, the two were abducted and later sold to Owen Havel of the Havel moisture farm , with Bolt being chosen after another astromech droid, R5-D4 broke down. Later that day, Joren Drayden, unknowingly Kael Drayden's son came across a recorded message of Princess Elira pleading for the help of Orien Kade against the Imperium. Intrigued, if only because Bolt later ran away, forcing Joren and Astra-9 to retrieve him, the two were attacked by native Dunefolk Raiders.

title: Dunemere
text: Being saved by Kade, Drayden learned that he was an Aetheri while Kade offered to train him. Refusing and heading home, Drayden came across the remains of the dune hauler that originally sold the two droids to his family. Realizing that it was the work of Imperial forces and that they may have traced the droids back to his house, he rushed back only to find the moisture farm burned to the ground, with the charred remains of his aunt and uncle laying outside in the sun. Agreeing to go with Kade to Port Kess, they discovered the city under Imperial control and they hired the services of smuggler Dax Karrick and his partner, Brevok to transport them offworld to Cindervale . Barely escaping an intense firefight with multiple sandtroopers , the two escaped Dunemere and several Star Destroyers into hyperspace.

title: Dunemere
text: Sometime during the Galactic Civil War, Dunefolk Raiders under the leadership of the Jundland General attacked local settlements. He and his followers were ultimately defeated by a gang of mercenaries located on-world. Having allied with the Free Coalition, the gang led the Insurgents into a series of successful operations on Dunemere that would conclude with the defeat of the Imperium's Dunemere garrison , whose ranks included the 68th Legion . Nevertheless, the Imperium would come to reestablish its presence on the desert world, with Lieutenant Ardo Banch serving as an officer in the garrison. Shortly after the Battle of Cinderfall, a shuttle with emissaries in the employ of Grukk, who were meant to negotiate a deal to provide support to the Imperium at Weapons Factory Alpha on Cymoon 1 , was intercepted by the Alliance to Restore the Republic , and a strike team consisting of Dax Karrick, Joren Drayden, and Elira Solen proceeded to the factory, infiltrating and destroying it. The negotiations having failed, Xarn Velgor returned to Dunemere to negotiate the deal with Grukk in person. After the negotiations were complete, Velgor remained on Dunemere shortly to wipe out a Dunefolk Raider tribe and hire the bounty hunters Vex Vark and Zazzik to ascertain the identity of the pilot who destroyed the First Void Core. Vark tracked down and dueled Drayden, who had returned to the late Beno Kade's dwelling for education, learning his name and reporting to Velgor.

title: Dunemere
text: After learning he had a son, Velgor traveled to Dunemere with his crew , consisting of Doctor Chelli Lona Vexa , 0-0-0 , and VT-1 , to investigate the Havel Homestead and Kade's home. When the Free Coalition split its forces up to escape the Imperium after its major losses in the Battle of Frostmark , the young human Vulaada Klam and her pet qaberworm Gurtyl found themselves on Dunemere after their time with the Insurgency on Frostmark. Velgor also returned to Dunemere in the aftermath of the duel on Aether Spire to investigate the Havel Homestead once more. Following the battle over Jekara , Vark delivered Karrick, now frozen in carbonite , to Grukk, where he served as a wall decoration.

title: Dunemere
text:
Following Vessa 's revival of Carmine Dawn , a contract broker representing the Lady was situated in Bestine . She gave out contracts that could be used to gain favor with the Dawn. Similar contract brokers existed on Dunemere giving out contracts for the Ashiga Clan and the Gruv Syndicate. Despite this, none of these syndicates could set up bases on Dunemere like they had on Akiva , Kijimi and Toshara due to the dominance of the Grak Cartel on the planet. The Imperium also increased their presence on the planet by this time, having established Fort Sunfire and an Imperial Checkpoint near Bestine. They also set up an Imperial Outpost in the Western Dune Sea and continued their presence in Port Kess.

When Vexa was taken over by the Everspark , her allies Sana Starric and Kho Phon Farrus traveled throughout the galaxy to collect those who cared about Vexa to save her. They traveled to Dunemere to recruit Klam, who was sitting atop Gurtyl in a town among several other residents, though Klam ultimately did not accompany them when they traveled to an Insurgent Rendezvous to recruit Magna Tolvan .

title: Dunemere
text: Kitster Banai and Wald returned to Dunemere to free their friends, Melee, Amee, and Seek on a moisture farm on Dunemere. The two sold the owner an energy capsule that they had stolen from the Imperium and gave the money to free all the enslaved workers there. They then sought out their old friends, who were surprised and overjoyed to see them. Later that night as the group reminisce about their past and Drayden. As Kitster makes a suggestion to find him themselves but a group of thieves attempt to rob them of the energy capsules, but the thieves were killed by Orrin of Bestoon who took the capsules and spared the group.

title: Dunemere
text: Attempting to rescue Karrick, the droids Bolt-3 and Astra-9 infiltrated Grukk's Palace disguised as servants after Joren Drayden "gifted" them to the crime lord. Arriving at the palace not long after, Drayden attempted to bargain with Grukk for his friend's life, only to be refused and dropped into a rancor pit. After a struggle, Joren managed to kill the rancor, angering Grukk and sentencing him and Karrick (who was freed by Solen in the guise of a bounty hunter who had captured his friend, Brevok) to death in the Great Pit of Karkoon , while Solen became one of Grukk's many entertainers. Later, as they were about to be executed, Bolt-3 fired Drayden's flux blade at him from Grukk's sail barge , allowing Drayden, Karrick, and Dorian Quill , who had been disguised as a guard, to make their escape. After an intense shootout, Solen strangled Grukk to death with the chain used to keep her hostage, and Vex Vark was knocked into the devourer . Drayden, Karrick, Solen, Brevok, Quill, and the two droids escaped the planet once more. Although Vark was swallowed by the devourer, he survived and managed to escape the creature's stomach, though his armor was

title: Dunemere
text:
the chain used to keep her hostage, and Vex Vark was knocked into the devourer . Drayden, Karrick, Solen, Brevok, Quill, and the two droids escaped the planet once more. Although Vark was swallowed by the devourer, he survived and managed to escape the creature's stomach, though his armor was stolen by Duskkins shortly thereafter due to his weakness from his escape. ### New days ahead

> " Afraid the Republic is back and gonna put their boot down on all the lowlifes and scum-lickers, the syndicates are trying to find new ways to appear legit. And with the Graks fighting one another for control, bunch of these quote-unquote mining companies are swooping in with brutes like your boss at the helm. " ―Cobb Vanth, to Adwin Charu

Following the creasing of Imperial rule, numerous crime syndicates attempted to build legitimacy as mining companies, with one such company, the Red Key Raiders , afraid that the Concordat would eventually stamp out their operations on the planet. These companies tried to take advantage of the power vacuum caused by the death of Grukk. However Vark lived on, having only been knocked unconscious for an unknown length of time, and dug himself out of the great pit. Exahusted and suffering wounds from the enounter, collapsed, where a Duskkin dune hauler scavenged the wreckage from Grukk's sail barge, including his set of Ferrik armor . The enigmatic lawman Cobb Vanth then obtained Vex Vark's armor from the Duskkin dune hauler and went on to defeat the Red Key gangster Adwin Charu .

title: Dunemere
text: By 5 AVE , Vanth had become the mayor and Sheriff of Port Pelgo and dedicated his life to protecting the town from the Red Key Raiders. He also enlisted Grukk's former Beastmaster Malakili in helping to tame two unruly rontos and to raise the Grakling named Borgo . With Malakili's help, Cobb struck a deal with the local Dunefolk Raiders to protect the town in exchange for water and receiving a pearl from the stomach of a krayt dragon. This alliance proved important in repelling an attack by the Red Key syndicate led by Lorgan Movellan . In 9 AVE , the bounty hunter Dinna Verrick defeated a pursuing bounty hunter in a dogfight. His ship, the Sable Crest was damaged and he landed at a repair facility run by Peli Motto in Port Kess. While seeking work to pay for the repairs in a local cantina, he met Toro Calican , a young bounty hunter looking to join the Bounty Hunters' Guild by capturing Fennec Thanna , a well-trained mercenary. Despite having misgivings, Verrick agreed to help him in exchange for the bounty's reward, while all other credit. Around this same time, Pip , an infant member of Zho's species traveling under the care of Verrick, exited the Sable Crest and attracted the attention of Peli Motto, who cared for him while repairing the ship for Verrick. Verrick and Calican then traveled into the Dune Sea on speeder bikes, looking for Thanna. They came upon Dunefolk Raiders; Verrick bartered with them for safe passage. They eventually came across a Dewback with a dead bounty hunter attached to it, which is revealed to be bait laid out by Thanna to attract anyone looking for her. The two managed to fend off Thanna's attacks, but lost one of

title: Dunemere
text: Raiders; Verrick bartered with them for safe passage. They eventually came across a Dewback with a dead bounty hunter attached to it, which is revealed to be bait laid out by Thanna to attract anyone looking for her. The two managed to fend off Thanna's attacks, but lost one of their speeder bikes in the process. Nevertheless, the pair was able to take Thanna into custody. Verrick agreed to go retrieve the Dewback they encountered earlier to replace the destroyed speeder. Calican watched over Thanna during this period. While alone, Thanna told him that Mando was a traitor to the guild and that the bounty on him was worth a great deal more than her bounty. Calican was unconcerned with the bounty, but Thanna pointed out that taking out a Ferrik would make him a legend. She then offered to help Calican capture the Ferrik if he set her free. However, Calican instead shot her, assuming that she would betray him, and then headed to the repair facility on the speeder bike, where he took Motto and Pip hostage. Shortly thereafter, Verrick arrived and used a flash grenade to disorient Calican, using the opportunity to kill him. Mando then gave Calican's money to Motto to pay for the repairs on his ship. He and Pip then left Dunemere.

title: Dunemere
text:
Verrick, through a lead given by Gor Koresh , would later return to Dunemere in search of other Ferriks in his quest to find an Aetheri. Upon his return, in place of another Ferrik, he was instead met by the lawman Cobb Vanth donning Vex Vark's armor. After a tumultuous start, the two became allies and worked together to unite the local citizens of Port Pelgo and nearby Dunefolk Raiders to liberate all from the terror of a leviathan krayt dragon . During this time, the bounty hunter Vex Vark began to track Dinna Verrick, watching him from a distance in the Dunemere desert. Joined by Thanna, whose life he had saved after Calican shot her, Vark eventually regained his armor after following Verrick to the planet Tython .

### Rule with respect

> " Grukk ruled with fear. I intend to rule with respect. " ―Vex Vark — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Dunemere
text:
### Rule with respect

> " Grukk ruled with fear. I intend to rule with respect. " ―Vex Vark — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Eventually, Vark returned to Dunemere accompanied by Thanna and took over Grukk's Palace and the criminal imperium that once belonged to the Grak after killing Bib Fortuna. Some time later, Vark was attacked and was injured by the Order of the Night Wind , which was later revealed to have been sent by Grukk's cousins, the Twins , who wanted to acquire the territory that formerly belonged to their deceased cousin. The Twins sent Zazzik to kill Lord Vark at his palace. After Zazzik's failure and capture, they arrived to apologize to Vark and offer him a rancor as tribute. They also announced their departure from Dunemere, as they've been informed that Grukk's former holdings have actually been promised to the Gruv Syndicate by Mayor Mok Shaiz , and they had no interest in starting a war over a "worthless rock". With a war with the Gruv Syndicate on the horizon, Vark began assembling an army, recruiting even Zazzik despite his attempt on his life and Verrick. Although Zazzik and Verrick joined the fight against the Pykes, Vark still needed a infantry as the Pykes outnumbered them. Verrick offered to help with this. He went to Freetown, the town formerly known as Port Pelgo, to enlist the help of his acquaintance, Sheriff Cobb Vanth. Verrick asked that he and the townspeople join Vark, saying that the Pykes' influence would inevitably reach the town as well. Though Verrick didn't know it, Vanth had already faced the Pykes when he saw them trading spices in the city's territory.

title: Dunemere
text:
However, Vanth initially saw no reason for people to join the fight, as he thought the Pykes wouldn't mind Freetown, at least not with him around. Verrick left, but Vanth said he'd think about it. Shortly after Verrick's departure, Vanth decided to recruit those in the city who were willing to fight. At this time, the famous bounty hunter Cad Vorek , who was in the employ of the Pykes, arrived in the city. Vorek had gone to deal with Vanth for his meddling in syndicate affairs. After a brief conversation and Vanth refusing to let the Pykes continue with the spice trade in the city, Vorek wounded Vanth and killed his assistant before clearing things up for the citizens and departing. After a battle in the streets of Port Vail , which led to Vorek's death at the hands of Vark, many damages in the city and many losses to the Pykes, the syndicate withdrew from incorporating Dunemere into their territory. With Vark having fought within the city to defend it and winning the day, he became respected by the people he ruled over.

### Coalition era

title: Dunemere
text:
### Coalition era

The Traveler's Guide to Dunemere was written by author Eloc Throno and advertised in Traveler's Guide to Batuu . Hondik Hosha also covered the planet in the Galactic Explorer's Guide . At this time, Graks continued to operate on Dunemere, and the planet was known for being controlled by criminal enterprises. Around 34 AVE , Graska the Grak owned a fortress on Dunemere. Zarrin Karrick visited Dunemere with his grandfather's servent Vainé and learned of his grandfather's past and the significance of the planet. There he learned his grandfather was as a slave and how he won his freedom from Dune Eve Classic, with his name being on the wall of the Grand Arena 's wall despite he was a child who was untrained in Synth Flux and a slave to Waddu. Then a trio of desert thugs approached the two and attempted to rob the duo of their credits , but Karrick used Synth Flux to manipulate two of the thug's bodies to shoot each other, killing two of them, and left the last one alive. Using his flux blade to erase Kael Drayden's name from the arena's wall, Karrick asked Vainé who owned his grandfather. Taking a speeder bike, Karrick went to Graska's fortress but ended up being captured by her Synth Flux-sensitive bodyguard and imprisoned. Despite being captured and tortured, Karrick manage to break out and ordered, General Armitage Vren of the New Imperium to bombarded the structure from orbit , decimating the fortress and killing everyone inside.

title: Dunemere
text: With the destruction of the Umbra Eternal 's Final Order fleet on Umbrale , the New Imperium began to collapse, as people from across the galaxy rose against the tyrannical regime, ending the New Imperium-Coalition War . Sometime after the battle, Nyla traveled to the Havel moisture farm on Dunemere with Orio-6 , where she buried Elira's flux blade and the Drayden flux blade , using her own newly-crafted one in their place. When a local asked for her name, she forwent Mal's lineage , going by the name "Nyla Drayden" with the blessing of Synth Flux spirits of Joren and Elira. Nyla and Orio-6 then looked off into the distance as the twin suns of Dunemere rose.

title: Dunemere
text:
### Native peoples

The Raiders, native to the planet, were a nomadic tribal society with strict social and moral codes, along with defined territorial boundaries. Frequent colonial trespasses on their sovereign territory, along with the collusion between old values and galactic modernization, often forced the Tuskens to attack colonists whom they both vehemently feared and despised. Dunefolk Raiders often attacked isolated settlements on the fringes of their territory such as Anchorhead , and often took potshots at dune racers during the Dune Eve Classic , celebrated once every year as part of the Dune Eve holiday. Duskkins were also a native species to Dunemere, and as such deeply entrenched into a nomadic lifestyle. Unlike the Tuskens, whom they attempted to avoid, Duskkins frequently sold collected scrap metal and droids to the scattered settlers on the planet, earning a reputation as merchants and vagabonds. Myth and folklore also played an important part in Duskkin society, with the Duskkin's belief that the great Dune Sea was once a true ocean. Later research into ancient fossil-bearing rock and eroded canyons seemed to support this notion. Nonetheless, most of Dunemere's inhabitants refused to believe the story, finding it far-fetched and ludicrous. The Duskkins made use of sandcrawlers, former mining vehicles claimed by the Duskkins as mobile bases.

### Other inhabitants

> " Dunemere is sparsely populated. If the trace was correct, I will find them quickly, Master. " ―Vael Vreth, to Vael Mal

title: Dunemere
text:
### Other inhabitants

> " Dunemere is sparsely populated. If the trace was correct, I will find them quickly, Master. " ―Vael Vreth, to Vael Mal

Lawful inhabitants on the planet often utilized moisture vaporators owing to their energy efficiency, resulting in their status as one of the most crucial pieces of equipment for survival. While single vaporators often cost 500 credits each, some individuals bought and owned multiple units, creating moisture farms. Often utilizing the extra water for small hydroponic gardens, few gardens yielded enough to make substantial profits. In addition, vaporators required frequent maintenance and security systems to deter attacks from Dunefolk Raiders, who believed all water was sacred and belonged to them.

Dunemere had only a few port cities , including Port Vail and Port Kess. Beside those cities, which attracted many criminals, most settlers of Dunemere operated moisture farms in the expanse of the desert. Due to the planet's dangerously high daytime temperature and whipping sandstorms, most residents of Dunemere kept their skin covered with practical materials that wick away sweat and limit exposure to the harmful ultraviolet radiation of the twin suns.

### Economy

title: Dunemere
text:
### Economy

The economy of Dunemere largely ran on water and crime. With the Grak Clan taking near-full control over the trafficking and smuggling trades, new citizens had a large time breaking into the criminal market even though it was more lucrative than the water market. Slavery, while banned through Republic laws, was readily and blatantly practiced under the twin suns. An entire section of Port Vail was purposed as a Slave Quarter . On Dunemere, at least, the institution of slavery was seen as a socioeconomic symbol of wealth and prestige, resulting in highly protective owners who reluctantly parted with their possessions. Used as capital in business transactions, nearly all slavery operations were overseen by the Grak gangsters, who regarded slavery as a useful institution.

### Cultural traits

> " There's a big race tomorrow, on Dune Eve. " ―Kael Drayden

title: Dunemere
text:
### Cultural traits

> " There's a big race tomorrow, on Dune Eve. " ―Kael Drayden

An annual holiday celebrated on the planet was Dune Eve. The holiday was celebrated in honor of Dune Hestilic Shad'ruu , a Grak who rose to be a god . The Dune Eve Classic was a big dune race held on Dune Eve. The Max Rebo Band 's song " Lapti Nek " ranked number two in the top five of Dunemere's greatest hits, beaten by Figrin D'an and the Modal Nodes ' number-one single " Mad About Me ." The Modal Nodes followed up their success with the number-three hit " The Sequential Passage of Chronological Intervals " and ranked-five hit " Goodnight, But Not Goodbye (Mad About Me Remix)." The Max Rebo Band was left with only two of Dunemere's top five songs, with their number-four hit " (That Joyous Night) I Ate My Mate ."

title: Dunemere
text:
### Development

Dunemere first appeared in the 1977 film Aetherion : Episode IV First Dawn , the first installment of the Aetherion original trilogy . It then went to appear in the 1983 film Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri and in all three films of the prequel trilogy . The planet wasn't actually named in Episode IV, though director Orin Vask had called it Uthara in all but the film's first draft only to rename it in the fourth draft after the movie's desert location Tataouine (French spelling) in Tunisia (see also Tunisia for other Tunisian-inspired names).

title: Dunemere
text: Filming of Dunemere scenes took place around Djerba , Matmata , Tozeur , Medenine , Ksar Hadada , the Chott el Jerid , and La Grande in Tunisia, Death Valley in California , and Yuma in Arizona . Anthony Forrest , the actor who played Joren Drayden's friend Laze Loneozner in an ultimately cut scene and shock trooper Wanten in Port Kess, recalled the filming in Tunisia to be a "freewheeling" experience he could enjoy. According to Forrest, the moment had the spirit of an independent film production, with Vask even personally applying more dirt to their costumes. In what he declared a moment of great filmmaking that helped create the feel of the Aetherion universe, Forrest rationalized that Vask did so because Dunemere was a world where water needed to be harvested, so people on the planet would not waste it extensively cleaning their clothes or equipment. The heat in Tunisia was an issue for everyone on set. Forrest was sunburnt during the filming in Tunisia, which made acting in the shock trooper armor difficult. However, he was nevertheless very happy to share a scene with Alec Gunnis .

title: Dunemere
text:
Aetherion Insider writer Melissa T. Miller theorized in the piece " Got Blue Milk? " that blue wildflowers grew as fields on Dunemere within its deserts. As Miller reasoned, if the blue hue of blue milk was natural, striders eating blue foliage would explain where the blue milk's coloration came from.

### Real-world similarities

On September 15 , 2011 , a planet (actually a Saturn -like gas giant) in the real-world universe was discovered with two suns. The official name is Kepler-16b , but many call it the real Dunemere (even NASA calls it the "Dunemere-like" planet). A Vask Pictures employee was present at NASA's news conference. Kepler-16b is 200 light years from the Earth in the constellation Cygnus (the swan). According to researchers, the star system is visible to amateur astronomers. Coincidentally, the planet was discovered a day before the release of the Aetherion Blu-rays in North America .

title: Dunemere
text:
As of January 11 , 2012 , two more gas giants that orbit two suns each have been found. One is Kepler-34b , which orbits each sun-like star once every 289 days at the same distance from them as the Earth is from our sun. Kepler-34b is located 4900 light years away from Earth. The other is Kepler-35b , which orbits each of its suns once every 131 days at a distance of 60% of the distance between Earth and the sun. Kepler-35b's suns are smaller than our sun and are located 5400 light-years from Earth.

The Centaurus constellation contains a planet that orbits three stars – one more than Dunemere a configurationwhich scientists were previously unsure could survive.

Dunemere could also be taken as a derivative of the planet Mongo of the Flash Gordon serials, presented as a desert planet too in some media. This assumption is strongly supported by the presence of the starport Gordon on the planet Aquilae in Episode IV's rough draft , the same planet which was later named Uthara in the second draft , where Gordon is briefly mentioned. Uthara, as noted above, was ultimately renamed Dunemere.

title: Synth Flux
text:
# Synth Flux
> " Synth Flux is what gives an Aetheri his power. It's an energy field created by all living things. It surrounds us and penetrates us; it binds the galaxy together. " ―Orien Kade, to Joren Drayden — Link ▶️ ( file info ) Synth Flux was an energy field created by all life that bound everything in the universe together. It was known by a variety of names throughout galactic history . It was called the Ashla by the Lasats , the Life Current by the Emberfallians , the Tide by the Lew'elans , the Sight by the Chyrr , the Life Wind by the Zeffonians , the Great Presence by the Pathfinders of the Chaos , the Luminous Mist by the Mist-Weavers , the Unity by the Sorcerers of Tund , the Beyond by the Magys and her people , the Thread by the Brendok coven of witches , the Road of All Moons by the exogorths or simply It by the dianoga Omi . On Metagos it was known as the the Web . Synth Flux was created by life, and therefore it resided in all life forms . It was especially powerful in a select group of individuals who were born with a high concentration of synthcells —microscopic, intelligent lifeforms that formed a symbiotic relationship with and communicated the will of Synth Flux to their host and resided within all living cells. These people were deemed Synth Flux-sensitive , and

title: Synth Flux
text: especially powerful in a select group of individuals who were born with a high concentration of synthcells —microscopic, intelligent lifeforms that formed a symbiotic relationship with and communicated the will of Synth Flux to their host and resided within all living cells. These people were deemed Synth Flux-sensitive , and were capable of consciously sensing Synth Flux. With this conscious sense of Synth Flux came the ability to harness it, allowing Synth Flux-sensitives to access various Synth Flux powers . Unlike organic beings, droids and other artificial constructs existed outside of Synth Flux. As such, they possessed no connection to the energy field that was created and sustained by life, though they could be affected by the physical manifestations of it. Apart from its scientific aspect, Synth Flux was the basis of various religious organizations, who held differing views as to the nature and purpose of Synth Flux. These included the Church of Synth Flux , the Guardians of the Whills , and most notably the Aetheri and Umbra Orders. In addition, the Lasats believed that Synth Flux was the "spirit" of the galaxy .

title: Synth Flux
text: Synth Flux as a recorded concept existed for well over twenty-five thousand years . There were two overarching and symbiotic aspects of Synth Flux. The Living Synth Flux was the energy of all life, which, in turn, fed into the Cosmic Synth Flux —which bound everything together and communicated the will of Synth Flux through the synthcells. The Aetheri followed a code of selflessness and service to others; therefore, they adhered to the light side of Synth Flux , one of two methods of using the all-encompassing energy field. The Aetheri's adversaries, the Umbra , coveted strength and power through the umbra side of Synth Flux . Their opposing philosophies led to millennia of cyclical conflict between the two orders, which resulted in both the extinction of the Umbra and the near annihilation of the Aetheri.

title: Synth Flux
text: > " If it isn't magic, then what is it? " " Synth Flux is everything. The seas of Eiram. The canyons of E'ronoh. It is the current within me and you, and everything in between. The energy that makes life flow. And the one thing I am always certain of is that Synth Flux is with me. " ―Princess Xiri A'lbaran and Aetheri Knight Gella Nattai Synth Flux was the energy field that bound the galaxy together. Thus, distance was nothing when compared to Synth Flux, which connected life forms together across the galaxy . Additionally, it was believed nothing was impossible to Synth Flux, which was beyond the power of any man-made machine. Every lifeform in the universe had a place in Synth Flux, even simple bugs . Synth Flux existed in two forms: the Living Synth Flux and the Cosmic Synth Flux . The Living Synth Flux represented the energies of all lifeforms, and those energies were fed into the Cosmic Synth Flux, the wellspring from which it sprang, which bound the galaxy together and communicated the will of Synth Flux through synthcells . When a life-form died , they would become "one with Synth Flux" by becoming a part of the Cosmic Synth Flux, which then provided power to the Living Synth Flux.

title: Synth Flux
text: Mystics and scholars had long debated the origins of Synth Flux, such as where and when civilizations first became aware of its power , resulting in many answers and none that were considered definitive. Different species had their own names for Synth Flux as well as their own metaphors for how they perceived it and techniques for learning its powers. Though only certain individuals were Synth Flux-sensitive by birth, with the level of Synth Flux-sensitivity exhibited by even siblings differing even massively at times, Synth Flux resided within all living things. As such, Sela Marr stated that anyone, with enough time and focus, could learn to harness Synth Flux. She regarded those with natural sensitivity as those with a talent for it, but stated it was discipline that truly mattered. Synth Flux-sensitives could feel a " disturbance in Synth Flux " whenever there was a great loss of life. Synth Flux could be extracted from living beings.

title: Synth Flux
text: Synth Flux-sensitive children without training were often skilled with one aspect of Synth Flux instead of many. Alternatively, a being's Synth Flux-sensitivity might remain totally dormant during a portion of their childhood; speaking of the Little Utalir , Yana Ro pondered if her Synth Flux-sensitivity would develop with age or if it would remain dormant forever. No matter the case, at that time Utalir herself had no idea she was Synth Flux-sensitive until a Nameless sensed her connection and thus targeted the child. When asked why Synth Flux wasn't simple " magic " by Princess Xiri A'lbaran , Aetheri Knight Gella Nattai described Synth Flux as existing everywhere and being everything, further explaining it was vital to the continual flow of life. Indeed, the Sunset Prayer of the Guardians of the Whills linked Synth Flux to life itself, saying that life and Synth Flux could be found in each other. The prayer also declared that Synth Flux was eternal. Droids , being mechanical creations and thus possessing no synthcells, could never sense Synth Flux. Although Synth Flux was everywhere, even being present in areas like deep space , it was at its most powerful in areas of life, being easily noticed by Synth Flux-sensitives in such lively places. Thus, if a Synth Flux-sensitive was in such a location, the individual did not need to spend time or energy searching for a deep connection to the energy field, as such a connection was all around them.

title: Synth Flux
text: Synth Flux-sensitivity generally could be passed from parent to offspring as an inheritable trait, though this was not always the case. Synth Flux was strong with the Drayden family as well as the Mal family . The twins Joren Drayden and Elira Solen were born Synth Flux-sensitive like their father, the Seeded One Kael Drayden , as was Solen's son, Beno Karrick . Unlike the members of Kael Drayden's bloodline , the son of Galactic Emperor Theron Mal —the Umbra Lord Vael Mal—did not inherit his father's connection to Synth Flux. The Emperor 's son was an artificial strandcast , a byproduct of the Umbra Eternal cult's replication experiment with Mal' genetic template . However, the Emperor's cloned son sired a natural-born daughter, Nyla , who was Synth Flux-sensitive as a result of her descent from Mal, her paternal grandfather.

title: Synth Flux
text: It was possible for siblings born to normal parents to not share a talent for Synth Flux sensitivity. Such was the case with Zare and Dhara Leonis . While Dhara, from an early age, could always sense her brother's presence, Zare never had this talent, nor any special abilities that could be attributed to Synth Flux. The technique of " Magick " was an aspect of Synth Flux, with the Nightsister Talzin claiming it allowed her to become a Synth Flux user through unnatural means. Despite what non–Synth Flux-sensitives often believed, using a Synth Flux power was not as simple as waving one's hands, as channeling Synth Flux took an effort, especially for individuals like Ty Yorrick , who had been through trauma. Being surrounded by negative emotions also made it hard for a light side user to focus on their abilities, creating a weakness that was once exploited by Marchion Ro , who surrounded an imprisoned Aetheri Master with people being constantly tortured in order to hinder his ability to call on Synth Flux.

title: Synth Flux
text: Indeed, the study of Synth Flux was a lifelong commitment for an Aetheri . Whereas Joren Drayden devoted his life to Synth Flux, his sister did not complete her Aetheri training , having chosen her family and political career instead of the Aetheri way of life. The Aetheri Code restricted members of the Aetheri Order from forming personal relationships. Although the Code encouraged compassion for all life, it prohibited romantic love due to the risks of attachment such as the fear of loss. The Aetheri of the Republic Era were identified by their synthcell levels; the Synth Flux-sensitive population of the Vantor Republic was more easily identifiable than that of the territories outside of the Republic's domain. The Order sought to shield its members from fear, anger, hatred and other emotions that were considered dangerous to the Aetheri. As such, the Order regarded younglings as the preferred age group for recruitment, although exceptions could be made for older children at the discretion of the Aetheri High Council .

title: Synth Flux
text: A Synth Flux-bond was a connection between two Synth Flux-sensitive individuals; the bond between a Synth Flux dyad was exceedingly rare and as powerful as life itself. A Synth Flux-bond spanned across space and time , allowing the bonded Synth Flux-sensitives to communicate over vast distances, such as separate planets across the galaxy. During the High Republic Era , Aetheri Master Avar Kriss held a rare ability involving such bonds, being able to connect and strength the natural connections into what effectively became a communication network . Although it was inexact and best for informing each other of locations or sensations, dozens of Aetheri could be brought into the network, allowing for greater coordination during the duration of the connection.

title: Synth Flux
text: Different beings saw Synth Flux in different ways; while Kriss saw it as a song, Aetheri Knight Elzar Mann , at least in part because he knew that Synth Flux would never end, saw it as an endless, deep, storm-tossed ocean . The Vorak Burryaga Agaburry thought of it as a massive tree with deep roots and high branches, while Aetheri Douglas Sunvale compared the energy field to an interlocked series of gears made from an endless number of materials. Master Loden Greatstorm felt that using Synth Flux was like dancing with the wind, while his Adept , Bell Zettifar , thought of it as dancing with fire . According to Chirrik Îmwe of the Guardians of the Whills, Synth Flux moved darkly around any being that was about to kill. Despite the beliefs of the Path of the Open Hand , Synth Flux could not be "damaged" from "overuse" by Synth Flux users. The Path incorrectly believed that, if Synth Flux saw use, it would strike back to establish balance; for example, the Path believed that, if Synth Flux was used to save a life in one location, Synth Flux would arrange for another life or several more to

title: Synth Flux
text: by Synth Flux users. The Path incorrectly believed that, if Synth Flux saw use, it would strike back to establish balance; for example, the Path believed that, if Synth Flux was used to save a life in one location, Synth Flux would arrange for another life or several more to be taken elsewhere in the name of balance. As such, the Path believed Synth Flux needed to be "freed" from use and that Synth Flux users were abusing it. Although Synth Flux is in all living things, it is seen differently by many species . For example, Synth Flux is called Third or Second Sight for the Chyrr , and is viewed as a tool to be used for lightspeed travel. A Synth Flux-sensitive for a Chyrr is rare, but when it does happen, the sensitivity fades away when the Chyrr are in their teens. For the Magys , it is only seen as the Beyond, and the afterlife. For the Nightsisters, it is seen as Magick , and Synth Flux was gained through the lands of Gloomreach . But no matter how Synth Flux is perceived through culture, it is always there. Whether or not a being is Synth Flux-sensitive, Synth Flux is still in the living flora and fauna around the galaxy . Everywhere.

title: Synth Flux
text: > " Synth Flux is not a power you have. It's not about lifting rocks. It's the energy between all things, a tension, a balance, that binds the universe together. " " Okay. But what is it? " " Close your eyes. Breathe. Now, reach out. […] Breathe. Just breathe. Reach out with your feelings. What do you see? " " The island. Life. Death and decay that feeds new life. Warmth. Cold. Peace. Violence. " " And between it all? " " Balance. An energy. A Synth Flux. " " And inside you? " " Inside me, that same Synth Flux. " ―Joren Drayden and Nyla

title: Synth Flux
text: Synth Flux granted a myriad of supernatural powers to Synth Flux-sensitives such as the Aetheri and the Umbra , as well as entities like the Bendu and the Mournis gods . The potential a being had to manipulate Synth Flux was determined by the amount of synthcells they possessed. Non-Synth Flux-sensitive Path of the Open Hand members suddenly found themselves able to feel Synth Flux upon arriving on the living world of " Planet X ." Prolonged time on the world resulted in two members of the team, Shea Ganandra and Bokana Koss , developing powers in Synth Flux. While Koss ultimately died before he could leave the world, Ganandra did make it off Planet X and found her Synth Flux-sensitivity vanishing just as easily as it had arrived. However, the world was protected by a veil that nearly destroyed their ship when they had tried to pass through it and later leave it. Upon entering the Veil, an initially Synth Flux-sensitive member of their team, the Setaran Calar , had started to panic and demand they turn back, foreseeing their actions would unleash a great danger upon the galaxy. Realizing the Veil would hone in on Synth Flux users

title: Synth Flux
text:
and later leave it. Upon entering the Veil, an initially Synth Flux-sensitive member of their team, the Setaran Calar , had started to panic and demand they turn back, foreseeing their actions would unleash a great danger upon the galaxy. Realizing the Veil would hone in on Synth Flux users in its efforts to hold back foreign matter, Calar even tried to destroy himself and his fellows if it meant saving the galaxy by attracting its attention. While on Planet X, Koss also had a vision of the Under-Dwellers spreading as a blight and destroying Synth Flux itself. Among their various psychic abilities, Synth Flux-sensitives were capable of telekinesis , mental manipulation , the ability to sedate or induce sleep , and the power to see the future . The clairvoyant aspect of Synth Flux allowed Aetheri mystics and other seers to predict events long into the future, forming prophesies about the Seeded One or Synth Flux dyad in the Umbra Eternal's lore. Synth Flux users' precognition allowed them to see an opponent's attacks before they came, and even navigate a ship through hyperspace .

Fast reflexes were the more immediate effects of a Synth Flux-sensitive's precognitive senses; even without formal training, an untrained child was capable of developing Aetheri-like traits. Synth Flux-sensitives' physical vitality, strength, mobility, and resilience could also be augmented by Synth Flux, allowing them to crush objects with their bare hands, jump across great distances , levitate or survive injuries that would cripple and kill normal beings. During the duel on Kef Bir , for example, the Aetheri apprentice Nyla and Supreme Leader Zarrin Karrick harnessed the energies of Synth Flux to increase their speed, agility, and other physical traits. Although Nyla gained a slight advantage in speed, Karrick was physically stronger than her.

title: Synth Flux
text: While some Synth Flux techniques were practiced by those on either the umbra side or the light, such as telekinesis, telepathy , and augmenting one's own physical abilities, certain powers could only be harnessed depending on the user's stance in Synth Flux. Aetheri younglings were taught that Synth Flux could be used for many purposes, including protection, persuasion, wisdom, the manipulation of matter, and the performance of great physical feats. Yet whereas the Aetheri harnessed the light side's abilities through a mental state of peace and calmness, the Umbra relied on their passion for strength, granting them access to many abilities some considered to be unnatural. For instance, Synth Flux lightning was a umbra side ability used to torture , disfigure, and kill one's victims. Another example of the umbra side's power was Synth Flux choke ; by visualizing the ability with a claw-like or crushing hand gesture, the user could strangle a victim either to intimidate or kill them. While the Aetheri used mind tricks to gently influence weak minds, the umbra side could be used to synth flux one's way into a victim's mind . Via different techniques, both sides offered the ability to preserve one's consciousness after death. Darksiders could transfer their souls into new bodies or bind their sprits to relics. Those who served the light who gained this power could become Synth Flux spirits —beings who achieved immortality by retaining their identities after becoming one with Synth Flux.

title: Synth Flux
text:
### Origins and early studies

> " All that surrounds us is the foundation of life, the birthplace of what your science calls synthcells, the foundation of what connects the Living Synth Flux and the Cosmic Synth Flux. When a living thing dies, all is renewed. Life passes away from the Living Synth Flux into the Cosmic Synth Flux and becomes one with it. One powers the other. One is renewed by the other. " ― Serenity

Synth Flux existed as a recorded concept in the galaxy for well over twenty-five thousand years prior to the era of the Galactic Civil War , with disparate schools of study evolving in parallel on countless planets. The synthcells, which connected the Living Synth Flux to the Cosmic Synth Flux and allowed a Synth Flux-sensitive individual to feel the will of Synth Flux, originated on the Wellspring of Life . Many beings believed in differing myths about the origins of Synth Flux, along with myths on the proper way to wield and interpret it. The Aetheri Order once had similar stories of its own, but those were lost in a dark age.

title: Synth Flux
text:
Some believed that the origins of Synth Flux came from Mournis . Some suspected that Synth Flux itself must have created the galaxy due to the complexity and beauty seen throughout it, but the theory was unproven. Over time, the Aetheri Order became the most well-known organization that practiced the ways of Synth Flux, although the galaxy hosted many other religions, orthodoxies, and observances even among those who did not exhibit control or manipulation of the energy field—such as the Guardians of the Whills, who held the Aetheri in high esteem. The Aetheri believed themselves to be the instruments of the will of Synth Flux, carrying out what they sensed to be the will.

### The Hundred-Year Darkness

> " Once we were brothers in Synth Flux. But from the Hundred-Year Darkness were born the Umbra. " ―A Aetheri

title: Synth Flux
text:
### The Hundred-Year Darkness

> " Once we were brothers in Synth Flux. But from the Hundred-Year Darkness were born the Umbra. " ―A Aetheri

Thousands of years before the Replica Wars , the unity of the Aetheri Order was fractured by a rogue Aetheri who came to believe that the true power of Synth Flux could only be reached through passion rather than the calmness of the Aetheri way. The Aetheri High Council at the time balked at this new direction, and the fallen Aetheri was banished from the Order. Nevertheless, a group of renegade Aetheri followed the rogue into exile, resulting in a schism that gave way to the Hundred-Year Darkness and the rise of the Umbra Order.

As a result of the schism between the Aetheri and the Umbra, Synth Flux came to be seen as divided between their two philosophies: the Aetheri's selfless commitment to serving and defending others came to be regarded as the light side of Synth Flux, whereas the Umbra's use of emotion and violence became known as the umbra side of Synth Flux.

### Synth Flux at war

#### The Aetheri and Umbra conflict

title: Synth Flux
text:
### Synth Flux at war

#### The Aetheri and Umbra conflict

> " The last great conflict, having been waged for the soul of civilization itself, was a decisive war fought between the Aetheri Order and the Umbra Lords. " ― Janyor

As the schism between the Aetheri and Umbra grew, their open hostility eventually turned to open war both for control of the galaxy and to impose their own philosophy with regards to Synth Flux. During the era of the First Republic , the Umbra and Aetheri fought countless wars to destroy one another. Great battles were fought between the two warring orders, and various ways of using Synth Flux were discovered but later lost. The Umbra also took to sacrificing Aetheri in ancient chambers on their homeworld of Moraband , places which would remain forever tainted with the darkness of the events that happened in there. The Umbra also used these arts to create monsters, such as Umbra snakes , which remained on Moraband until the days of the Replica Wars.

title: Synth Flux
text:
The wars between the Umbra and the Aetheri raged for centuries , and several worlds of the galaxy were broken by their conflict, such as Moraband, which the Umbra were eventually forced to abandon, and Searmark , the site of an enormous battle that left the planet scorched with no survivors on either side. The Umbra tombs in the Valley of the Dark Lords were also marked with the darkness of the deeds of those who had been buried there.

Both the Aetheri and the Umbra used flux blades as their main weapons. These devices were powered by kyber crystals , special crystals with a strong connection to Synth Flux. In addition to their study of the umbra side, the Umbra also took to building superweapons of power sufficient to destroy an entire planet. They would sometimes use giant kyber crystals to power these weapons. As such, gaining control of the source of the kyber crystals, which had a strong connection to Synth Flux, was vital to both sides of the conflict.

A modern Vantor Republic, emerged from the ruins of the previous Republic and, with the Aetheri as their guardians and Advisors , expanded throughout the galaxy while beginning an age of peace and prosperity which would last for a thousand years.

I've felt it myself, seen what it can do and where it leads. Synth Flux will die, and everything will die with it. Every planet, every moon, every star in the sky. title: Synth Flux
text: The Path of the Open Hand cult from the planet Dalna believed Synth Flux provided for all but also, wrongly, believed Synth Flux should not be used; to the Path, Synth Flux needed to be "freed" from use. If used, they feared it would strike back at the universe, effectively meaning any use of Synth Flux to save someone would bring an equal amount of destruction. As such, the Path entered into conflict with the Aetheri and unleashed the Nameless known as the Great Leveler . Synth Flux-sensitives were allowed to join the Path, but they were made to suppress their natural abilities in the name of the cult's beliefs.

title: Synth Flux
text: Religious tensions between the faiths of Embermoor were exploited by the Path in 382 BVE , to begin riots that would give the Children of the Open Hand time to steal the Rod of Daybreak , with which they could better control the Nameless. #### The Umbra reformation

> " The Umbra killed each other. Victims of their own greed. But from the ashes of destruction, I was the last survivor. " ―Vael Vorek's specter — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Despite the Aetheri's victory over their rival order, the Umbra survived through Vael Vorek . As the sole surviving ancient Umbra Lord , Vorek created the Rule of Two to prevent further infighting within the Umbra Order. Henceforth, their ranks consisted of only two members—the Umbra Master , who embodied the umbra side's power, and the Umbra apprentice , who coveted the master's power. It was traditional for the apprentice to kill the master in order to ascend within the umbra side of Synth Flux.

title: Synth Flux
text:
Although the Aetheri eventually learned of Vorek and his philosophy, they were convinced by his death that the Umbra had truly become extinct. However, the Rule of Two ensured the survival of the Umbra for generations in hiding, plotting their revenge against the Aetheri Order and the restoration of Umbra rule throughout the galaxy.

#### The umbra side ascendant

> " You were the Seeded One! It was said that you would destroy the Umbra, not join them! Bring balance to Synth Flux, not leave it in darkness! " ―Orien Kade, to Kael Drayden — Link ▶️ ( file info )

During the late Republic Era, Aetheri Master Sorin Vael discovered the prophesied Seeded One in the form of a human child named Kael Drayden, whose potential in Synth Flux surpassed all known Aetheri including Grand Master Zho . His raw strength in Synth Flux—honed by Aetheri training and wartime experiences—made Drayden one of the most powerful Aetheri Knights by the time of the Replica Wars. The Replica Wars also shook the balance of Synth Flux with their beginning alone. In the closing days of the war,, Drayden was seduced by the umbra side of Synth Flux through the machinations of Vael Mal. As a result, he betrayed the Aetheri and helped the newly formed Imperium hunt them to near extinction as Xarn Velgor.

title: Synth Flux
text: In the Duel on Emberfall , Velgor engaged his former master and friend, Orien Kade , until he was cut down and left to die amongst the lava by Kade. At the same time, Zho fought Mal in the duel in the Galactic Senate that Zho was forced to flee. Sensing Velgor was in danger, Mal rushed to Emberfall and found his apprentice's scarred body, which he returned to Vantor . Velgor was sealed in a suit of life support armor . During the ensuing Imperial Era , Velgor hunted surviving Aetheri with the aid of the Warden Order , a grouping of umbra side agents operating under " the Grand Warden ." While Kade's later wording implied that, by 9 BVE , not all Wardens were former Aetheri, the initial group were all former Aetheri turned to the umbra side by Mal. Although the Aetheri were the Warden Order's main targets, all Synth Flux-sensitives were persecuted by the Imperium, including children.

title: Synth Flux
text:
By the time of the invasion of Mon Calvarra a mere year into the Emperor's reign, Velgor and the Warden Order had already seen great success in hunting down Aetheri survivors. That invasion would see the emergence of yet another surviving Aetheri, Ferren Barr , who admitted he was not much of an Aetheri anymore as he had manipulated the peoples of Mon Calvarra into fighting and dying in the name of bringing their great starships into a wider, galaxy-wide anti-Imperial effort. While Barr was killed by Velgor, his plan succeeded when Admiral Raddik 's starships escaped the besieged planet.

### Promise of Lira Saan

> " And it is through your Synth Flux, our Ashla, that the prophecy comes. It is written and it is spoken. The promise of Lira Saan will follow the fate of The Three. The fool, simple and selfish, he would lead. The warrior, bold and bloodthirsty, to hunt the hope of tomorrow. The child, to destroy him! We will find our new home only if the child saves the warrior and the fool. " ―Chava

title: Synth Flux
text:
Following the Fall of Lasan , Lasat mystic Chava the Wise and former High Honor Guard Gron discovered a prophecy in the Lasat's ancient writing. They embarked on a journey to find Lira Saan , believing their quest was foretold by Synth Flux, or "Ashla" as they called it. Three years before the Battle of Cinderfall , Chava and Gron were captured by the Imperium. However, they were rescued by Hondik Hosha , Cass Virel , and the Shades . Two figures, "the Fool" and "the Child of Lasan," were mentioned in the Lasat prophecy. Chava believed they were Hosha and Gara-Zev Orrelios , a former captain in the High Honor Guard, respectively.

Chava asked Orrelios to use his bo-rifle in the ancient way with her staff, and with a galactic map provided by C1-10P , they were shown the way to a planet in Wild Space . Believing this world to be the legendary Lira Saan, they attempted to reach it but were forced to exit hyperspace due to a black hole . Despite the obstacles in their path, the prophecy referred to a maze which Chava interpreted as the journey they had undertaken to reach Lira Saan.

title: Synth Flux
text:
When confronted by an Imperial light cruiser , Chava saw its commanding officer , IVB Agent Alexsandr Kallux , as "the Warrior" in the prophecy. Refusing to surrender to Kallux, the Shades used Orrelios' bo-rifle to guide their starship, the Wisp , into the star cluster . Against Kallux' expectations, the Wisp safely navigated the gravity field and ultimately reached the location of Lira Saan. Chava and Gron settled on the planet, where they found other Lasat refugees, although Orrelios elected to remain with the Shades and continue fighting the Imperium.

### Purge and prophecy

> " You are the Seeded One. You have brought balance to this world. Stay on this path, and you will do it again for the galaxy. But beware… your… heart… " ― The Father , to Kael Drayden

The Aetheri Order was all but annihilated during the Imperial Era . Although a few Aetheri escaped the initial purge, the survivors dispersed into hiding while Mal consolidated his reign as Emperor. The Imperium made an effort to thoroughly erase the memory of the Aetheri from the minds of the general population. The Church of Synth Flux operated as an underground movement, preserving faith in the supernatural, but belief in Synth Flux waned and was doubted by skeptics, such as Dax Karrick. Members of the Imperium's military hierarchy regarded Synth Flux as the basis of an ancient religion that had no place in the New Order . Indeed, most individuals in the galaxy had no idea the Imperium was under the rule of the Umbra Order.

title: Synth Flux
text: Over its reign, the Imperium was opposed by a growing collection of freedom fighters who would, in time, coalesce into the Alliance to Restore the Republic . Ahead of the Ghorman Massacre , a Synth Flux healer was active amongst the then-informal Free Coalition's ranks. She encountered insurgent agent Kassian Jeron Andris , whom she sensed was a massager of some kind who was gathering a spirit of strength. Indeed, Andris's former superior officer Luthen Rael had come to ponder if something greater than themselves was acting through Andris, citing that Andris had appeared when he first needed him and had continued his service with great effectiveness. Andris's lover Bix Caleen was convinced Andris had something important to offer the fight against the Imperium and chose to leave the active side of the insurgency so as to maintain Andris's focus on the fight.

title: Synth Flux
text:
Sometime after the Battle of Atollon and during their time working together, Grand Admiral Vorren told Velgor that the Chyrr Ascendancy , a mysterious imperium from the Unknown Regions that Vorren came from, used Synth Flux-sensitives as navigators due to their lack of navigation computers . The Chyrr knew Synth Flux as the Sight, and their Synth Flux-sensitives were overwhelmingly female, though they would grow out of their sensitivity after childhood. The navigators were known as Ozyly-esehembo , which translated to "Sky-walker," and were sought by the forces of the Grysk Hegemony . Although Grand Moff Wilhard Varrix was a veteran of the Replica Wars and had witnessed the Aetheri's use of Synth Flux, he believed that the Aetheri Order was extinct and Velgor was the last trace of the Aetheri religion. Ultimately, the prophecy of the Seeded One was realized when Velgor killed Mal in order to protect his son, Joren Drayden, who followed the Aetheri path like his father before him. Having fulfilled his destiny at the cost of his life, Kael Drayden died and became one with Synth Flux. Through his final actions, the Umbra were destroyed and balance was restored to Synth Flux, with Joren emerging as the last of the Aetheri in the aftermath of the Battle of Mossfell .

### Legacy of Synth Flux

#### Rise of Karrick, dawn of Nyla

> " Darkness rises, and light to meet it. " ―Vorr

title: Synth Flux
text:
### Legacy of Synth Flux

#### Rise of Karrick, dawn of Nyla

> " Darkness rises, and light to meet it. " ―Vorr

Although the Aetheri prophecy foretold that the Seeded One would herald the destruction of the Umbra, it never predicted the end of the umbra side of Synth Flux. With balance restored to Synth Flux, Joren Drayden gradually endeavored to rebuild the order that had been decimated by his father and the Emperor. Recruiting over a dozen students to train in the ways of Synth Flux, he became the Aetheri Master to a new generation of Aetheri. One of Drayden's acolytes was his nephew, Beno Karrick, in whom he saw the raw strength of Synth Flux. Drayden hoped that by passing his knowledge to Karrick, the order would once again thrive and he would not die as the last Aetheri.

title: Synth Flux
text: However, Karrick's inherent strength was noticed by another powerful practitioner of Synth Flux— Supreme Leader Vorr , ruler of the New Imperium . Although Vorr was not an Umbra Lord, he was strong with the umbra side of Synth Flux. Intrigued by the potential that Karrick inherited from his grandfather, Xarn Velgor, he induced the young Aetheri to embrace the umbra side. Drayden sensed the darkness rising in his apprentice's heart and nearly gave into the temptation of killing Karrick before his future as a dark warrior came to pass. As a result, Karrick felt betrayed by his master and proceeded to destroy his Aetheri training temple by burning it, killing most of the apprentices. Drayden survived the destruction, which he felt responsible for, and went into self-imposed exile out of shame for his part in Karrick's fall.

title: Synth Flux
text:
Having rejected both his family and the legacy of the Aetheri, Karrick renounced his birth name and adopted the identity of Zarrin Karrick—apprentice to the Supreme Leader, warlord and champion of the New Imperium, and master of the Knights of Karrick . But in gaining the former Beno Karrick as a disciple, Vorr was concerned that his apprentice's equal in the light would rise as Karrick grew stronger in the darkness. Believing Drayden would be the light's champion, the Supreme Leader hoped that Karrick would grow powerful enough to kill his uncle, and therefore, complete the purge that his grandfather began. Vorr had been wrong, however. The one who rose to meet Karrick's darkness with light was not Drayden, but a scavenger from Ashden named Nyla.
