During the events that led up to the Battle of Cinderfall, Zho noticed that with the Mirefall rains ended, it was time to migrate back to his lowland hut, and was grateful as his usual accommodation for the wet season reminded him too much of the Aetheri Sanctum and his failings. He reflected on how age had affected him and realized that he had become truly reliant on the walking stick he had originally adopted as an affectation for a joke played on his adepts. The Aetheri packed what little he owned and left but not before he checked for the Imperial probe droids which had once searched for him endlessly.

title: Zho
text:
As Zho descended farther downhill, however, he felt a presence. It was neither a probe droid nor one of the Imperium's ships but vibrations in Synth Flux from Orien Kade and what remained of Kael Drayden. A probe droid then appeared and Zho quickly took out a pot given to him by Kade. He used Synth Flux to smash it into the droid only to suddenly sense Kade's death at the hands of Xarn Velgor. With the Aetheri distracted, two more droids arrived but Zho crushed them both and continued on home. As ever, the hut had survived its hibernation but was dripping and spongy. Five days later, Zho had dried and cleaned the house. Each time he saw the shelf usually reserved for his pot, he reacted with some loneliness after destroying Orien's gift to him. Feeling his isolation, he reached out to the netherworld of Synth Flux to speak to Sorin Vael, but the spirit of Orien answered instead and requested that Drayden's child be trained. Having harbored regrets about not having taken the man's daughter as his apprentice, and assuaged that he had enough time left to teach another pupil, the Aetheri Master readily agreed until he found out that Kade was actually speaking of Kael's unfocused son instead. Nevertheless, Zho begrudgingly allowed Kade to direct the boy to him. As Zho ruminated on his decision afterwards, he returned to the "Cave of Evil" and was reassured that the site had no new fears to show him.

#### A phantom visitor

> " Zho had to know all of that. He could have killed me or let the planet do it for him. Instead…he chose to teach me. " ―The Archivist

title: Zho
text:
#### A phantom visitor

> " Zho had to know all of that. He could have killed me or let the planet do it for him. Instead…he chose to teach me. " ―The Archivist

Sometime later, a mysterious woman once known as Madelin Sun who became known as " The Archivist " arrived on Mirefall in search of Zho at the behest of Lady Vessa , the leader of the crime syndicate Carmine Dawn , who wanted Zho's help to take down the Umbra. When the Archivist was attacked by a monster after arriving on the planet, Zho used Synth Flux to save her from a distance and then led her into the umbra side cave in order to dissuade her from looking for him. Having a change of heart, she left the planet as Zho watched from afar. The Archivist returned to Vessa, lying and telling her that Zho was dead.

#### Haunted by Kade

> " The shadow that has fallen across the galaxy…my fault, it is. I have exiled myself here, not just for penance. I have removed myself from events…because without me, better off the galaxy is. " ―Zho to the spirit of Kade

title: Zho
text:
#### Haunted by Kade

> " The shadow that has fallen across the galaxy…my fault, it is. I have exiled myself here, not just for penance. I have removed myself from events…because without me, better off the galaxy is. " ―Zho to the spirit of Kade

Three years after agreeing to train Drayden, Kade contacted Zho, who at first ignored the late Aetheri Master's spirit. Kade urged Zho to see reason and acknowledge the growing darkness in the galaxy. Zho mused that the threat had become too powerful—too big—for him to defeat, to which Kade reminded Zho of the first lesson the latter would teach new Aetheri: "size matters not." Zho admitted that he had sensed Kade's demise and had been avoiding him on purpose, once again expressing a defeatist attitude to the situation at hand. Kade dismissed the notion, not believing it himself and saying he did not think Zho believed it either. Zho reflected on his own inability to stop Vael Mal and the fall of Kael Drayden, stating the galaxy was better off without him.

title: Zho
text: Zho later had a dream in which Bree Menaren , Zho's old pupil, taught and encouraged him to play the taratti . Zho, sensing something was amiss, turned to see the sky blocked out by a massive battle station. The Aetheri Master drew his flux blade to find himself facing an apparation of Kael Drayden as an Adept, his eyes glowing yellow, also encouraging Zho to play with the toy. Activating his weapon, Zho was confronted with a twisted vision of an undead Sorin Vael, who berated Zho for his ignorance before engaging him in a brief flux blade duel. Zho began to deny his claims, only to be annihilated by a blinding green light crashing down from the superweapon above.

title: Zho
text:
Zho woke from the nightmare to find Kade at his side. When Zho questioned the spirit's continued presence, Kade stated that he would remain until Zho agreed to hear him out and do as he asked. The elder Aetheri master, looking to get away from Kade, set out from his hut to find herbs for his soup. Kade followed, reminiscing about times past and reminding Zho about his making pastries when Kade was but a youngling. Not finding any herbs, Zho remarked he had made a wrong turn only to realize that he and Kade had arrived at the Cave of Evil—exactly where Zho needed to be, Kade opined, "from a certain point of view."

#### Entering the Cave of Evil

> " But what of you, old friend? Will you be ready when he comes? " " Ready to teach? Yes, I will. Ready to teach—and ready to learn. " ―The spirit of Orien Kade and Zho, after the latter went in the Cave of Evil

title: Zho
text:
> " But what of you, old friend? Will you be ready when he comes? " " Ready to teach? Yes, I will. Ready to teach—and ready to learn. " ―The spirit of Orien Kade and Zho, after the latter went in the Cave of Evil

Zho refused to go inside, believing that was what Kade wanted of him, to which Kade merely asked Zho if he thought that would be the right course of action. Zho noted that the location was stong in the umbra side and had nothing to prove, with Kade reasoning that his fellow master should therefore have nothing to fear. Zho dismissed the venture as a foolish waste of time but relented nonetheless.

title: Zho
text:
Entering the vergence, Zho was startled by a creature of Mirefall's wildlife, the Aetheri Master grumbling that he had become old and foolish. Zho was then confronted by a voice from the shadows—an apparation of Varek, his former apprentice. The illusion blamed Zho for his fall to the Umbra side, revealing his hand in the death of Yaddle and beginning to duel Zho. Zho then experienced a vision of High Republic Era Aetheri Keeve Trennis , who refused to help Zho and, like Varek, blamed him for her final fate.

Trennis used Synth Flux to push Zho into a mound of skulls, which a burning Kael Drayden claimed to be the Aetheri Master's failures—those who had died. Bael Solen, Lira Ondar, and Drevan Koss emerged from the grave, reminding Zho that they had looked to him for answers. Zho replied that he could not have known how things would ultimately turn out, only for a spectre of Vael Mal to cite the Aetheri Master as the greatest of his apprentices, blind and unaware. Mal noted there way no way back because of him, to which Zho began repeating the phrase and drowning in the pile of corpses.

title: Zho
text:
It was then that Bree appeared, reminding the Aetheri Master that there was no situation was entirely without hope—something he had learned from Zho himself. Bree elaborated that one could make as many mistakes as was required because, as Zho finished the thought for him, "the greatest teacher, failure is." Zho remembered the lessons of the Aetheri and struck down the remaining ghosts of his past.

Exiting the cave, Zho found Kade waiting for him. Zho answered an affirmative to the question on Kade's mind, agreeing to train the son of Kael Drayden. Removing Bree's taratti from his robe, Zho stated that he was ready to teach but also ready to learn.

#### Taking a new apprentice

> " Do, or do not. There is no try. " ―Zho to Joren Drayden — Link ▶️ ( file info )

title: Zho
text:
#### Taking a new apprentice

> " Do, or do not. There is no try. " ―Zho to Joren Drayden — Link ▶️ ( file info )

Soon thereafter, Joren Drayden, under guidance from the spirit of Kade, sought Zho in his Mirefall exile to receive Aetheri training. At the same time, Zho, stirred awake by the feeling of the umbra side and the memories of his trauma years ago, went to his storage area to find it empty. In an effort to find food, he made the arduous trek across the wild terrain of Mirefall. Eventually, Zho made it to a valley, full of colorful creatures, and another species in particular. Herds of these creatures ran through this valley, the best source of meat Zho had yet been able to find.

title: Zho
text: Years ago, Zho in his shame had decided to give up his flux blade, promising to never wield one again, taking a bow instead. To get what he came for, Zho readied his bow and took aim of one of the creatures, easily killing it with one shot of the bow. On his journey back, Zho began to feel the ground shift beneath his feet, beginning to crumble as Zho began to fall. At the last moment, Zho grabbed onto the side, reflecting on the similarities of this moment to his duel with Vael Mal many years ago. Zho's grip failed and he falls onto the ground below as boulders began to pile on top of him. Zho fell unconscious.

title: Zho
text: Zho began to dream, the dream of pain, suffering, anger, hate, and suddenly, he awoke once again. Realizing the predicament he was in, Zho began to laugh, laughing at his foolishness for allowing him to get into this situation. He began to doubt himself, thinking of how he was now trapped on Mirefall, but subsiding those feelings, knowing he was one of the last of the Aetheri. He reached out to Synth Flux and, in that moment, he realized that his shame, his hubris, his blindness, had all clouded his vision and realized his failings as an Aetheri. However, he knew that failure was the greatest lesson an Aetheri could learn, and understanding this brought him peace as he rejected allowing his shame to guide him any more. With this newfound peace, Zho reattuned to the light and used its power to move the boulders resting on top of him. With a newfound sense of responsibility and understanding, Zho began his journey home.

title: Zho
text:
Arriving back at his home, Zho began to cook a stew, when he began to hear a crashing in the trees surrounding his hut. A visitor had arrived. He walked out of his hut to discover this new visitor, realizing it was Drayden, the boy Kade had allowed to travel here to learn from him. As he stared at Drayden from the trees, he came to the realization that he would not be the last Aetheri, but only the instrument as to train the future.

Walking out, he decided to test the boy and did not reveal his true identity, instead promising to lead him to Zho. With Drayden growing annoyed while in Zho's hut as the Aetheri Master made rootleaf stew , Drayden's subsequent frustration and his age made the Aetheri doubtful as to whether it was a good idea to train the boy, but Kade's spirit managed to convince him to do so. Over the next few weeks, Zho trained the young Aetheri.

title: Zho
text:
Zho proceeded to tutor Drayden with a variety of exercises, including the telekinetic manipulation of objects in the area. As part of his training, he also sent Drayden into the umbra side cave in order to demonstrate the dangers of falling to the umbra side of Synth Flux. During his tenure with Zho, Drayden sensed that his friends were in danger in Aether Spire on the gas giant Mistral, and headed there to confront Xarn Velgor in spite of Zho's and Kade's persuasion to the contrary. Although Kade was distraught by Drayden's rushed departure, Zho reminded him that there was still another offspring of Kael Drayden —Elira Solen.

#### A disturbance in Synth Flux

Sometime later, the same mysterious woman helped activate the Fermata Vault , a mysterious artifact created by Vael Mornick . On her second attempt, Zho along with other Synth Flux users amongst the galaxy sensed the disturbances emanating from the cage.

#### Death

> " Joren... when gone am I, the last of the Aetheri, will you be. Joren... Synth Flux runs strong in your family. Pass on what you have learned. Joren... There... is... another... Sk-... Sky... walker... " ―Zho's last words, to Joren Drayden

title: Zho
text:
Drayden, having engaged in a duel with Velgor on Aether Spire, returned to Mirefall after a year. Zho, ill and very close to death, confirmed what Velgor had revealed to the young Aetheri on Mistral: that the Umbra Lord indeed was Kael Drayden, his father. He also warned him that with his training fully complete, his final task would be confronting Velgor again and defeating him, and cautioned Drayden not to underestimate Synth Flux powers of Galactic Emperor Vael Mal. Zho also said that when he dies, Joren will become the last of the Aetheri. Therefore, he wanted Joren to pass on what he had learned. With his last breath, Zho struggled to tell Joren of the existence of another member of the Drayden family. The old master died and his body disappeared as he became one with the light of Synth Flux. The Cave of Evil took advantage of the Aetheri Master's faltering presence and subsequent death to finally expand its influence once more, spreading a darkness across Mirefall.

### Postmortem and legacy

title: Zho
text:
### Postmortem and legacy

> " Heeded my words not, did you? Pass on what you have learned. Strength, mastery. But weakness… folly… failure, also. Yes, failure most of all. The greatest teacher, failure is. Joren… we are what they grow beyond. That is the true burden of all masters. " ―Zho's Synth Flux spirit, to Joren Drayden Thanks to the techniques passed on to him by Sorin Vael's spirit, Zho managed to retain his consciousness without a physical presence by becoming a Synth Flux spirit. Mere moments after his death, he was able to appear to Mal, who had felt his death in Synth Flux. Mal, who had been fantasizing about killing Zho himself in the past few minutes as well as inwardly celebrating his demise, was surprised by Zho's appearance, thinking the feat impossible. Putting on a show, he gloated on the fact that Zho was now dead and implying that Zho was there to witness Mal' final glory as he crushed the remnants of the Free Coalition and took Joren Drayden as his new apprentice. Zho stressed that Mal could not win, but Mal pointed out that he already had. Awaiting Zho's reply, Mal discovered that his specter had vanished.

title: Zho
text: Joren Drayden later used the training he received to confront Vael Mal and Xarn Velgor aboard the DS-2 Void Core II Mobile Battle Station over the forest moon Mossfell as part of an all-out attack on the station by the anti-Imperial Free Coalition , defeating Velgor and turning him back to the light side of Synth Flux, resulting in Mal' death at the hands of the redeemed Kael Drayden. As Kael died from his wounds, Zho and Kade appeared to him, smiling upon their redeemed friend. Zho then taught Kael the ability of retaining his consciousness after death. As the insurgents and Joren celebrated on the surface of the moon due to the demolition of the Void Core II and the deaths of Mal and Velgor, the ghosts of Kael, Kade, and Zho briefly appeared to Joren. After that, Kael asked Zho and Kade whether Joren would be alright, and Kade responded as Zho stood by. For the next years, Zho's spirit, alongside Orien and Kael, continued to guide Joren. Though it was rare, Zho also spoke to Elira offering her guidance and teachings of synth flux over the years of her life, teachings she would later pass on to Nyla.

title: Zho
text: Approximately five years after Zho's passing, the Ferrik bounty hunter Dinna Verrick took a member of Zho's species, Pip , to train under Sela Marr on the planet of Corvus . While with Verrick, Marr explained that she had only met one other member of Pip's species: Master Zho. Marr refused to train the Child but told Verrick that Pip could reach out to other Aetheri at the seeing stone on the planet of Tython . Thus, Joren Drayden learned of Pip and, after saving Verrick, Pip, and their allies from a platoon of Dark Troopers , took Pip as an apprentice. Thirty years after Zho's death, another Synth Flux sensitive, Nyla , heard Zho's voice describing Synth Flux during a vision she witnessed upon touching the flux blade that previously belonged to Joren and Kael Drayden.

title: Zho
text: Sometime later, and after Nyla had visited Joren on his hermit-island on Tidehollow , a disillusioned and self-loathing Drayden tried to burn down what few Aetheri artifacts and writings were left in hopes that it would rid the galaxy of the Aetheri once and for all, who, through him, had failed. Joren was surprised by the sudden appearance of Master Zho as a Synth Flux spirit, who not only did not seem to mind the ancient scripts burning up, but was the one to actually start the fire by causing lightning to strike the tree. In fact, unbeknownst to Joren, Nyla had already taken the Sacred Aetheri texts when she left. During their meeting, Zho pointed out that mistakes and failure were important lessons, if not the most important lesson, for an Aetheri Master. Ultimately, Zho helped Drayden come to terms with his failed training of Beno Karrick , and to realize that despite his fear of failing another student he could still be what Nyla needed. Inspiring Joren to face his past and forgive himself. This final, heartfelt meeting between the two friends led Joren to change his mind and help save the Coalition from certain defeat during the

title: Zho
text: to realize that despite his fear of failing another student he could still be what Nyla needed. Inspiring Joren to face his past and forgive himself. This final, heartfelt meeting between the two friends led Joren to change his mind and help save the Coalition from certain defeat during the Battle of Saltmark . During the Battle of Umbrale in 35 AVE , Zho's voice was heard by Nyla among the voices of many Aetheri of the past who aided her with destroying the resurrected Vael Mal. "Alone, never have you been," he told her, before telling Nyla to "rise in Synth Flux."

title: Zho
text: > " You knew Master Zho? " " Yes. He taught almost all of the younglings in the temple, at one point or another. " " Brenn described him to me. Small, green, and wrinkly with pointy ears. But he didn't know what he was really like. " " I'm not sure anyone did. He was wise, kind, but when I was young, he seemed happier. As the Replica War dragged on, he carried a great burden, a deep sorrow, as if he knew before anyone else that one time was ending, and another beginning. " ―Cass Virel and Sela Marr

title: Zho
text: Known for his wisdom, Zho had spent eight centuries training and tutoring generations of Aetheri. Zho was an ideal grandmaster. When he joined her Synth Flux-bond network, Aetheri Master Avar Kriss felt Zho's mind form its own part of the chorus of Synth Flux. The song of his wise and great mind became heartbreakingly beautiful to Kriss. Despite his appearance not making it seem like it would be so, his voice appeared to be made up of pure light, so Kriss considered him the epitome that people were not simply the crude matter of their bodies, a lesson that Zho would later pass on to Joren Drayden. He was reluctant to accept Kael Drayden or Joren Drayden for Aetheri training, considering them unfit. In both cases, however, he allowed Orien Kade to persuade him into accepting them as trainees.

title: Zho
text: Zho understood that nothing and no one was perfect, but that there was good or the potential for good everywhere and in everything. He urged his friend, Chancellor Kyong Greylark to continue fighting for good in the galaxy when she was uncertain, including her work establishing communications all the way to the Outer Reach. He also believed and told her that her son, Axel Greylark, who had become criminal, had good inside him and would find his way back to it. Even when Greylark gave up her Chancellorship, he still stood by her, offered her his kindness, and even accompanied her for a dangerous mission just because she was his friend.

title: Zho
text: There was a small garden in the Aetheri Sanctum where Zho often took to meditating, with the other Aetheri usually respecting the privacy of such moments. Indeed, Zho's favorite place to be was his own thoughts, being able to meditate and feel the calm Living Synth Flux flow throughout him. When Varek triggered a partial room collapse during his duel with Zho on Pyralis, the Aetheri, confronted with the choice of pursuing the fleeing Umbra or protecting the hurt Orien Kade and unconscious Kael Drayden from the falling debris, opting to save his comrades instead of going after Varek. However, when fellow Master Tor Vayne's fleet was destroyed by the Confederate superweapon Malignar , Zho forbade Kael Drayden and Sela Marr to conduct a search for Vayne, citing the danger posed by the Dissident vessel. Early in the Replica Wars, after learning he would be confronting Varek's apprentice Kessa Vray during his mission on Rugosa, Zho was disappointed to not be facing the Count himself, believing that he could end the bloodshed by meeting with Varek; Zho believed he could connect with his former Adept and redeem him to the light side of Synth Flux. Later in the war, however,

title: Zho
text: during his mission on Rugosa, Zho was disappointed to not be facing the Count himself, believing that he could end the bloodshed by meeting with Varek; Zho believed he could connect with his former Adept and redeem him to the light side of Synth Flux. Later in the war, however, Zho reluctantly agreed to a plan to assassinate Varek in the name of stopping the war. Orien Kade, after the plan's failure, would argue to his fellow councilmembers the mission had been a step too far into the dark. Adept Reath Silas believed that having Zho as a master would be "pretty fun" whilst discussing Zho's former apprentice Kantam Syra. Zho's favorite method of teaching was to ensure his students could figure things out for themselves. Even if all Zho did was wait for the student to catch up to speed, he found that they almost always realized what they needed. When Master Drevan Koss questioned whether Zho had sensed something or not, he waited until the younger Aetheri realized he was sensing nothing. Koss remained confused, forcing him to explain that the feeling of nothing needed to be caused by something. He disagreed with Koss's sentiment that "nothing" and "something" were always opposites, and he made sure to never be fully sure of himself, knowing there was more to learn. Koss also knew that, if he asked whether the Grand Master was afraid, he would turn the question back at him.

title: Zho
text: Zho remained calm even when insulted, such as when the mud dwellers called him a "weird little frog". During the Invasion of Ondara, Zho believed himself comfortably away from the umbra side, unaware of the growing power of Vael Mal, with the exception of what he knew he could not feel. Indeed, Zho concerned himself with trying to uncover the feelings that were hidden from his senses, which he eventually understood to be the umbra side. Zho was able to resist being tempted by the specter of the dead Umbra Lord Vael Vorek, who had appeared to him in a vision on the planet Moraband, recognizing that the spirit was a mere illusion and rejecting its call to the umbra side. However, he was quite concerned and worried about the danger and threat of the Nameless, which he secretly knew of quite well, opting to keep information about them out of the Aetheri Archives so that they would not be known and used against the Order.

title: Zho
text: Zho's teachings stuck with his students, even if at times they had to struggle to understand their true meaning. Upon hearing pilot Leox Gyasi explain why he had named his starship "the Vessel ," Silas was struck with the opinion that Gyasi sounded like what Zho's teachings would be like if the Aetheri Master took spice . As such, Silas decided his reasoning was either a very good or extremely bad sign. Despite barely knowing the Grand Master, Silas was greatly struck by his disappearance during the High Republic Era, with fellow Adept Ram Jomaram , despite having never even met Zho, agreeing and feeling the same. As he neared his death before the Battle of Mossfell commenced, Zho accepted his own mortality and imminent demise and died becoming one with Synth Flux. Zho's ears were expressive and would sometimes curl when he was expressing strong emotions like surprise. These ears were also highly sensitive and also sometimes would move to express his emotions. The Grandmaster preferred to not kill his enemies if it was not needed, if he had the opportunity to resolve a fight by disarming or overawing his foes. Zho opposed profanity, urging others to not use

title: Zho
text: ears were also highly sensitive and also sometimes would move to express his emotions. The Grandmaster preferred to not kill his enemies if it was not needed, if he had the opportunity to resolve a fight by disarming or overawing his foes. Zho opposed profanity, urging others to not use such language. Zho also had a sense of humor and curiosity, despite his age and wisdom. Part of the reason Zho kept up his sense of humor was that Aetheri Master Drevan Koss, even as a youngling, did not respond well to it. As such, he took teasing his fellow council member, once asking if he had arrived for a private discussion because he had embarrassing questions, which Koss denied instantly. Afterward, he elected to wait to speak, wanting Koss to begin the discussion and viewing it as him cracking as if he was under pressure. Koss also found Zho's behaviors distracting, yet he would always trust the older Aetheri's judgement and he himself described Zho as "hilarious". His sense of humor continued with others, as shown when he playfully rummaged through Joren's belongings when he first met him, fought Bolt-3 for a torch, and laughed gleefully when he supposedly set the ancient Aetheri texts on fire, and finding Joren's continued ignorance amusing, commenting that he had "missed him." Also when Kade told him about the planet Gelvaris missing from the archives during his class, he responded with, "Lost a planet, Master Kade has. How embarrassing. How embarrassing!" Being unable to destroy

title: Zho
text: ancient Aetheri texts on fire, and finding Joren's continued ignorance amusing, commenting that he had "missed him." Also when Kade told him about the planet Gelvaris missing from the archives during his class, he responded with, "Lost a planet, Master Kade has. How embarrassing. How embarrassing!" Being unable to destroy Vael Mal and bring down the Imperium made him sad. Zho was highly secretive about his homeworld and never revealed it to anyone. Despite his intensive Aetheri training and high status within the Order, he stated that he secretly had a dislike for ancient Aetheri texts. He had a distinctive and peculiar speech pattern: namely, he would rearrange words in his sentences, placing subject and object in front of the verb; for example, he would frame sentences like "Good relations with the Voraks, I have."

title: Zho
text:
### Flux blade combat

> " It is obvious that this contest cannot be decided by our knowledge of Synth Flux…but by our skills with a flux blade. " ―Varek, to Zho

Despite his small size and old age, Zho was an extremely accomplished flux blade duelist, wielding a short green-bladed flux blade. Zho used the Ataru blade form, boosting his body with Synth Flux to be able to perform the needed movements. Such was his mastery of this form that Zho could duel Mal and almost defeated the Umbra. Zho was a master of the Niman style of flux blade combat, retaining his skills with the form for his whole life.

Zho was extremely skilled in blast-deflection and proved more than capable of taking on multiple enemies at the same time and winning easily: he was able to single-handedly defeat without getting even a single shot to his person an entire army of droids that Vray sent as a test for King Katunko whether to accept the Aetheri or the Dissidents as an ally.

title: Zho
text:
The greatest display of Zho's skills with a flux blade was when he dueled the Umbra Lords Count Varek and Vael Mal. When he fought Varek, Zho maintained the upper hand through the duel, forcing Varek into the defensive, and would have defeated him had he not decided to flee. His duel with Mal, although initially well-matched, eventually began to turn into Zho's favor, forcing Mal to use Synth Flux to confront him.

### Synth Flux powers

> " The history of a soul, does Synth Flux permit me to understand. " ―Zho about his abilities ### Synth Flux powers

> " The history of a soul, does Synth Flux permit me to understand. " ―Zho about his abilities

Even despite his small size and old age, Zho was extremely powerful and accomplished in Synth Flux. with a connection to that power and knowledge of Synth Flux techniques that may well have surpassed that of any other Aetheri. Orien Kade considered Zho to be the most powerful Aetheri he ever knew. The Grandmaster was heralded as the greatest Aetheri of all time, at least until the fall of the Republic. Zho was utterly committed to the light side, but he also had a deep understanding of the umbra side as well as how both halves of Synth Flux interacted. The idea he was the greatest of the Aetheri went back centuries, at being held least to 232 BVE. The toll age took on Zho's body did not prevent him from still being strong in Synth Flux when Joren Drayden trained under him. Even in death, as a Synth Flux spirit, he had power over weather.

title: Zho
text: Zho was extremely skilled in telekinesis and all forms of it. When Avar Kriss worked with the other Aetheri to shove a sun-bursting explosive Avar Kriss found his level of power (which he lent via her Synth Flux Song) to be very grand, helpful, and impressive. When on a mission to free a child, Zho gripped two pirates who were holding the child and held them helpless, before making them punch each other and then threw them into the air. Then Zho defeated the rest of the pirates in the room when they attacked him. Zho used Synth Flux deflection against a Blue stone spear thrown at him by a member of the Mud dwellers , though holding the spear with Synth Flux was hard for Zho. Zho then levitated many boulders and rocks to catch the rest of the spears thrown at him and kept the rocks levitated for a whole conversation. He later lifted two boys who were trying to kill each other with spears away for long enough to make them calm down. Zho was unable to repel many of the Blue stones that were thrown at him with Synth Flux by the Rockhawkers , due to

title: Zho
text: a whole conversation. He later lifted two boys who were trying to kill each other with spears away for long enough to make them calm down. Zho was unable to repel many of the Blue stones that were thrown at him with Synth Flux by the Rockhawkers , due to how hard it was to affect with telekinesis and his unwillingness to harm the children he faced. Later, and having mastered Stonepower , Zho was able to casually blast the Rockhawkers who attacked him, subduing and disarming them without inflicting lasting harm. When facing Varek on the planet Pyralis, Zho demonstrated his superior telekinetic mastery by effortlessly repelling every metal piece and stone slab thrown by the very skilled Umbra Lord. During a confrontation with Confederate forces on the coral moon of Rugosa, Zho effortlessly pulled two droids to slash them with his flux blade, flung multiple pieces of the droid controlling one of the infantry high into the air and both opened the upper parts of another infantry tank, then sent it and the droid controlling it into the air. It was with ease that Zho raised and moved droids to fire upon their allies and slammed whole squads of droids down, without harming his own allies. After the droids were dealt with, Zho easily overpowered the powerful Umbra Assassin Kessa Vray with telekinesis, stopping her flux blade strike mid-way and disarming her with a simple gesture, and repulsed the many stones caused by Vray activating an explosion. If Zho had no desire to touch the ground, he could simply float in a mediative state.

title: Zho
text: Synth Flux barriers were a tool in Zho's skill set, as seen when he stopped a cloud of deadly gas. Zho could strike down his foes by hurling his blade at them, guiding the blow with his telekinetic skills. When he went to try to destroy the Umbra Emperor, Zho effortlessly defeated two Red Guards by knocking them into a wall. He was even able to breach the Emperor's defenses and blast Vael Mal himself through the air with a Synth Flux push and was able to stop and throw a Senate hoverpod Mal had thrown at him when they fought in the Senate building, an all the more impressive feat since it was thrown upwards against gravity. Later, on Mirefall, Zho used Synth Flux to throw a pot at an Imperial Probe Droid, destroying it. He then Synth Flux crushed two more of the robots before they could report his location. In order to teach Joren Drayden that anything was possible with Synth Flux, Zho levitated his student's sunken T-65B Vector starfighter out of a swamp of Mirefall and onto dry land with no visible strain.

title: Zho
text: With just a few days of training, Zho was able to learn how to use Stonepower and thus deflect Blue stones thrown at him. Zho could move a chunk three times his size--something unknown to his master, though Zho was then exhausted by doing so. Zho could also use Stonepower to stop strikes from giants of living stone , and with the aid of those he taught, call forth other giants to defeat the one he was fighting. Zho was capable of employing the power of Synth Flux lightning , to the point that he could make several arcs of energy lance out in different directions from only a single finger. Zho could manipulate flames with Synth Flux.

title: Zho
text: Aetheri Adept Bell Zettifar pondered whether Zho, after putting great focus into the effort, could use Synth Flux to stop gravity. In his duel with both Umbra Lords Count Varek and Vael Mal, Zho displayed great proficiency in Synth Flux Deflection , as he was able to easily stop and then redirect Varek's Synth Flux lightning attack with his bare hands and even managed to stop Mal' Synth Flux lightning attack using just his palms but was unable to deflect it completely: the energy eventually exploded and flung both of the combatants away from each other, ending the duel in a stalemate and causing Zho to escape. Zho could dampen or even negate the might of Synth Flux powers used to attack him by radiating a calming aura. Zho could employ Synth Flux to absorb volt pistol fire and negate the strikes of flux blades with his bare hands and channel the energy from volt pistols or lightning he absorbed into making his own attacks such as Synth Flux push and Synth Flux lightning more deadly.

title: Zho
text: His ability to use the combative applications of Synth Flux notwithstanding, Zho's incredibly strong connection to Synth Flux combined with his years of extensive study also granted him numerous supplementary abilities. Zho could enhance himself and seek out objects or persons he knew about regardless of the distance, and easily see though and/or destroy many Synth Flux illusions at once. During the trial of Daren Kelv , Zho revealed that he could uncover the alignment of a Synth Flux-user just by touching them; stating that Synth Flux had permitted him to read the history of a soul, able to easily sense that he had fallen to the Umbra side despite Vossa being proficient enough to hide it from many other Aetheri. Zho could detect the lies, emotional states, and thoughts of those he interacted with.

title: Zho
text: While physically isolated on Mirefall, Zho was able to see other Aetheri that were active in Synth Flux; he could not see one that had forsaken the ways of the Aetheri, with the exception of Velgor who was still exposed to his monitoring. Zho could detect living things and droids with Synth Flux and while on Mirefall he could sense all droids on the entire planet or the lack thereof. He could keep in mental contact with the Aetheri Temples across the galaxy, and telepathically converse with any Aetheri–even to the point of manipulating the experience to his desires–within them by accessing the World Between Worlds . Zho, still on Mirefall, was able to conjure an illusion of the Grand Warden (from when he was an Aetheri) to fight Brenn Aldric as a test and sight of worthiness. He also sensed that the place where Cass Virel and Brenn Aldric could be assured of a chance to fight the Umbra was Searmark, and so told Cass. When the Lorath Aetheri Sanctum was invaded, Zho sent illusions of Aetheri Sanctum Guards at the Wardens, subduing them for long enough for the living Aetheri present to flee.

title: Zho
text: With some effort, Zho could make himself and the powers he invoked impossible to detect with Synth Flux and go unnoticed by most. When two Blue stone spears were struck together, Zho sensed the disturbance this caused. He also sensed the killings that took place during Directive 66, the shock of which literarily staggered him, so forewarned by Synth Flux, Zho was able to destroy the Replicas soon sent to slay him on behalf of the Umbra. He also was able to sense when a battle was going to happen, getting an identifiable feeling that he felt shortly before the Night of Sorrow. Zho could use Synth Flux to see even in total darkness or when blinded. Additionally, Zho was able to use Synth Flux healing , even to the extent of healing himself and those around him while in battle with just a wave of his hand. Zho was also shown to be capable of experiencing Synth Flux visions and could invoke such insights at will for information up to three days into his personal future. However, he understood that Synth Flux prophecy was not absolute and that the future was always in motion. The Grandmaster could make great

title: Zho
text: also shown to be capable of experiencing Synth Flux visions and could invoke such insights at will for information up to three days into his personal future. However, he understood that Synth Flux prophecy was not absolute and that the future was always in motion. The Grandmaster could make great leaps with Synth Flux, to maneuver and dodge and charge. His visions led him to foresee the possible, and eventually actual, fall of the Aetheri in the Replica Wars and even his own death . Zho sometimes knew if he was probably going to die in a battle he fought in and could augment his physical abilities.

title: Zho
text:
He also was able to fully master the skill of maintaining consciousness after death , something that Sorin Vael was unable to do, allowing him to manifest a visible presence rather than simply being a disembodied voice. As a Synth Flux spirit, Zho was capable of manipulating weather to create lightning strikes. He was also shown to be capable of striking Joren Drayden with his walking stick, demonstrating an ability to interact with the living world in a physical sense despite both Zho and the stick being ostensibly non-corporeal.

### Other skills

Zho was also known to have a level of proficiency in piloting despite often leaving it to his soldiers, as when he was forced to travel alone by Sorin Vael, Zho displayed the ability to pilot Kael's personal interceptor comfortably and was able to avoid inflicting any damage on it until he returned to the Aetheri. Mal and Zho were equally matched during their duel in the Galactic Senate.

title: Zho
text:
According to Orien, Zho's thirst for knowledge was the grandmaster's greatest weapon. Zho could walk for hours without food or rest up a mountain/giant. Adept Reath Silas once reflected that he could feel Zho's wisdom and knowledge from even a kilometer away.

During the Replica Wars, Zho proved himself to be an exceptional strategist and leader, being a highly effective general. His abilities in those regard were displayed during a confrontation with Confederate forces on the coral moon of Rugosa: Zho was able to inspire hope into his troopers despite the overwhelming odds and was able to easily tactically defeat the army of droids, exploiting the weak-points of the infantry and tanks to systematically destroy them and at one point tricking one of the droids controlling the tanks into destroying the other tank.

Zho was a skilled diplomat. Although his cooking on Mirefall left much to be desired, Zho was skilled at baking, with Aetheri Master Torban Buck particularly enjoying Zho's pastry recipe.

title: Zho
text:
> " I am knowledgeable of many things. But I have never worn shoes! " ―Zho

Throughout his life, Zho wielded several flux blades. He made use of a training flux blade during his days as a youngling, with Zho later gifting the blade to the youngling Kai Brightstar. As a fully-fledged Aetheri, he owned several flux blades of a shoto -style, including one which he lost in a duel with Vael Mal at the end of the Replica Wars that was then destroyed in a public Imperial display. That flux blade had been the specific one which he had cherished, yet he did own at least one other. He kept that near identical flux blade with him on Mirefall but refused to use it.

title: Zho
text:
He was also known for using a cane. It began as a lesson, but really more of a joke, for his Adepts; he would limp into a room with the cane, then he would cast it aside and quickly use his speed in Synth Flux, only to finally grab the cane once more and hobble away. His intention was that the Adepts would then be left questioning whether or not he actually needed the cane. Nevertheless, as he grew older during his exile on Mirefall, he found he truly had come to need it.

As a Synth Flux ghost, he was able to manifest his staff and use it to strike living matter. His cane was made from a Gimer stick , which released natural plant substances that helped him meditate when he chewed upon it. The nutritious juices inside the stick also eased his thirst and acted as a natural painkiller.

title: Zho
text:
### The Original trilogy

> " The idea of using another person, perhaps an alien, for Joren to play off of came up during story meetings. Orin Vask and Leigh Brackett thought that the alien could be an Indian desert type, very childlike even though he's an old man. He at first should be repulsive and slimy but then should become kind and wise. He appears as a crazy little nitwit that goes around scurrying like a rat but ultimately teaches Joren a great deal about Synth Flux. " ― Laurent Bouzereau about Zho's development for Episode V The character of Zho made his first appearance in the 1980 film Aetherion : Episode V Rise of the Imperium , and subsequently appeared in Aetherion : Episode VI Return of the Aetheri , the closing installment of the original trilogy. He was also featured in all three episodes of the prequel trilogy, and multiple episodes of the Aetherion: The Replica Wars and Aetherion Insurgents animated television series. Zho also played a role in various Expanded Universe material now under the Aetherion Legends brand and thus non-canonical . In Orin Vask ' notes for the first chapter of the original trilogy Zho originally named as "Bunden Debannen" and nicknamed as "Buffy". During the development of the sequel, Vask, likening the character to "a little Dalai Lama ", decided to use an eastern sounding name and changed the character's name to "Minch Zho" in the resultant treatment before simply shortened it to "Zho" for the final film.

title: Zho
text: Much of the information and training that Zho gave to Joren on Mirefall was originally going to be given by Beno Kade , but due to Kade's death in First Dawn , Orin Vask conceived Zho to fulfill the role of Joren's teacher after Kade's death. Early concepts of Zho imagined him as a large alien before he was reimplemented as a tiny one, with various gnome– and elfin-like portrayals being created by the design team of Episode V. Once Zho's appearance was finalized, make-up and creatures supervisor Stuart Freeborn sculpted a detailed puppet, brought to life on screen by Frank Ozzik . Every time that Ozzik turned the puppet, the ears would do a little wiggle, which he did not like. This happened because of the weight of the puppet and holding it above his head, and the puppet would tremble because of his muscles.

title: Zho
text:
While Zho was largely depicted with the Ozzik-performed puppet in Rise of the Imperium , actor Deep Roy stepped in for long shots of Zho walking through the swamps. For these shots, Roy wore a detailed mask and full costume. Zho had additional play in the draft script for Return of the Aetheri : when Theron Mal strikes at Joren Drayden with Synth Flux lightning aboard Void Core II, Synth Flux ghost of Zho would have appeared alongside the ghost of Kade. Both Aetheri would have deflected the Emperor's lightning to protect Joren. Like Kael Drayden and Kade did in the draft, Zho also returned to life instead of remaining a ghost.

### The Prequel trilogy

title: Zho
text:
### The Prequel trilogy

> " I thought, 'I don't want to be matching to the puppet.' I adored the puppet in Imperium when I was 16 years old… But when it came time to do Attack of the Replicas , I felt that it would be really, really difficult, because we would have to match what they did with the puppet and interpret how that puppet movement would be put into a digital character running around. Orin [Vask] did say early on in briefing us that we'd see him full-body, he'd have to run and jump and fight. So I did know that, but I thought after learning what we learned on Waddu, Greeb, and Sebulba [in Episode I], I felt we could take on Zho. " ―Rob Coleman discussing creating a digital Zho for Episode II

title: Zho
text: A new model, younger in appearance, was built by Nick Dudman 's animatronics crew for the filming of Episode I, in which Zho also appeared as a CGI model for two shots' duration. In Episode II, Zho needed to be more agile than he was in the original trilogy and would have to fight during his duel with Varek, which was a creative risk for the film. Initially, Vask told Animation Director Rob Coleman that Zho would be featured as a puppet and the animators would create a digital version of him for his duel with Count Varek, but Coleman did not love the idea. He thought that it would be very difficult to match what was done for the Zho puppet in Rise of the Imperium and interpret how the puppet's movement would be put into a digital character. Early on in briefing, Vask told Coleman and his team that Zho would be seen full-body and he would have to run, jump, and fight. Coleman felt like he and his team could work on Zho after gaining knowledge and experience from working on Waddu , Greeb Mool , and Sebulba in Veiled Threat . The new goal was to

title: Zho
text: that Zho would be seen full-body and he would have to run, jump, and fight. Coleman felt like he and his team could work on Zho after gaining knowledge and experience from working on Waddu , Greeb Mool , and Sebulba in Veiled Threat . The new goal was to use a digital Zho for every scene and sequence that he appeared in. Designed specifically to not exceed Ozzik's puppetwork in realism, the animated version of Zho was accepted after Coleman's crew secretly developed animation tests using key scenes from Rise of the Imperium using the new technology, and these scenes were evaluated. Based on the strength of these animated tests, Coleman's crew was given permission to create a digital Zho, which was realized entirely through computer-generated imagery.

title: Zho
text: Creating a digital Zho terrified Coleman because of the backlash against Greeb, and he did not want to be known for "wrecking" Zho, but he was unwilling to back down from a challenge. Coleman's memory of seeing Zho in 1980 managed to keep him on target. Coleman studied the footage of Zho in Rise of the Imperium frame by frame and realized it was very limited. When creating the digital Zho, he wanted himself and his team to honor the range of motion he thought he saw in 1980. Coleman pitched that the digital Zho would do three talking shots while delivering memorable lines of dialogue, as well as three shots without talking to show the ability to convey a performance even when silent. Coleman worked on a closeup of Zho for the film in which Mal was speaking to Aetheri in his office, and Vask purposefully cut to Zho who was looking over his shoulder. This was meant to indicate that Zho did not trust Mal.

title: Zho
text: Coleman worked with Frank Ozzik in order to make sure that his digital Zho could be as faithful as possile. He came to know exactly what shape Ozzik's hand formed inside the puppet's head and learned how the shape affected expression. Coleman made sure that he did not go too far in terms of Zho's movement. After Ozzik saw the initial tests, he was very supportive and said he loved the restraint they did and that they matched what Ozzik had done before. At first, the digital character did not include the original detail of how Zho's ears wiggled everytime the puppet's head moved. This caused Zho to not appear old, which was considered to be a vital part of his character. Coleman's team added the detail in the digital character, and Zho now looked the correct age.

title: Zho
text: From the start of the creation of Zho and Count Varek's flux blade duel, most of the work would fall to Coleman's team. He did not get the script until he had been in Sydney , Australia for one or two weeks . The first draft described the fight as "'In a fight that defies description, Zho and Count Varek battle." For clarification, Coleman scheduled a meeting with Vask who told him he'd have to figure it out. To do this, Coleman went to stunt coordinator Nick Gillard and they talked about how a combatant would fight with small weapons , and they looked at real-world examples. Also, Ahmed Best , the actor who played Greeb, introduced Coleman to some anime and martial arts that he thought could be helpful. However, Coleman still was not sure how to depict Zho's speed and style in a fight. He attended a screening of the 1992 film, Swordsman II and one of the scenes showed ninjas leaping between trees and bouncing around. Coleman studied the action in the film, and this inspired him to give Zho the ability to jump around. While working on the duel, Coleman referred to Glen McIntosh 's dynamic

title: Zho
text: of the 1992 film, Swordsman II and one of the scenes showed ninjas leaping between trees and bouncing around. Coleman studied the action in the film, and this inspired him to give Zho the ability to jump around. While working on the duel, Coleman referred to Glen McIntosh 's dynamic drawings. In the duel, Vask wanted a shot of Zho pulling back his duster to reveal his flux blade as a reference to the iconic shot of the gunfighter at the O.K Corral . After finishing the duel, Vask and Coleman felt happy with it. Despite Coleman's concerns, Vask wanted Zho to jump, leap, and flip during the duel.

title: Zho
text:
Coleman worked on a shot that was called "The Widowmaker." In the shot, an animated Zho denounced Kade's sense of victory and said "Begun, this Replica War has." That line was approved and unapproved a couple of times. Also, Coleman received many notes telling him the line had to be sadder. When Coleman showed the shot to Vask, Vask said that the line was pathetic and sounded too sad. Vask said Zho should not sound sad, and should instead sound reflective, concerned, and upset over the inevitability of the Replica Wars.

For Episode III, the shot of Zho clinging to the Senate podium during his duel with Mal was animated by Tim Harrington . Coleman thought that his blocking was excellent, but Coleman was looking for more strain on Zho's face. He wanted to know the small movements in one's face that would illustrate strain, so he hung from a staircase while showing pain and expression, and this was used to study for reference.

### Animated television shows

title: Zho
text:
### Animated television shows

Zho's Aetherion: The Replica Wars and Aetherion Forces of Destiny incarnation was voiced by veteran Aetherion voice actor Tom Kane . During the Fury of the Umbra DVD press conference in 2005 , Ozzik initially mentioned that he was going to be involved in the Replica Wars series, but in a 2007 interview with Aintitcoolnews.com he eventually denied any involvement. In spite of this, Ozzik later returned to voice the character in Aetherion Insurgents . Piotr Michael provided the voice for Aetherion: Young Aetheri Adventures .

### The Sequel trilogy

> " Neal Scanlan and his team did a recreation of the Zho puppet. It's not only a puppet, it's an exact replica of the Imperium puppet. They found the original molds for it. They found the woman that painted the original eyes for Zho. Then Frank came and worked with them for a few weeks to get the puppet right. He did a lot of testing and a lot of adjusting with the puppet creators. It was amazing to watch the process. " ―Rian Johnson

title: Zho
text:
Ozzik continued to perform as Zho in all three films of the sequel trilogy : the 2015 film Aetherion : Episode VII Synth Flux Awakens , the 2017 film Aetherion : Episode VIII The Last Aetheri , and the 2019 film Aetherion : Episode IX The Rise of Drayden . In Synth Flux Awakens , Zho's voice was heard during Nyla's Synth Flux vision along with Orien Kade's. During the film's early development, Zho was originally going to have a bigger role, a decision that went far enough to ask Frank Ozzik to record some lines as Zho, although these recordings went unused when the character was cut from the film. The Last Aetheri director Rian Johnson praised the development process for Zho's appearance in the film.

### Discrepancies

The number of toes on Zho's feet has long been debated. In Aetherion: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know , Zho is given as having three toes at the front of each of his feet, and one at the back, comparing them with that of many birds.

### Non-canon content On October 29, 2014, for a Halloween-themed update, a costume of Zho was added to The Simza 4 for playable child Simza to wear in-game. The costume is purely cosmetic and offers no gameplay changes.

title: Korvane
text:
# Korvane

> "Every freighter in the galaxy has passed through Korvane at least once." — a Port Vey merchant

Korvane was a tidally locked rocky moon in the Korrathi system, the largest trade hub of the Inner Reach. Its single ocean of ammonia and nitrogen and its spaceport that never went dark made it the natural meeting place for merchants from a dozen systems.


The spaceport of Port Vey handled more freight per rotation than any other station in the Inner Reach. The port stood on the moon's terminator — the narrow belt of temperate air between the hemisphere of permanent day and the hemisphere of permanent night. Along the terminator ran dry docks, refineries and the famous Korrathi market, where Duskkin traders bartered spice and water for refined fuel.

title: Korvane
text: Korvane was settled by Korrathi prospectors in 712 BVE, who struck deposits of quadinar under the polar ice. The mining colony grew quickly: within a generation the moon had dry docks, a refinery and a permanent spaceport. During the Vantor Republic the moon became a hub for the grain convoys of the Commerce Combine, and its market was third in the Inner Reach for spice and fuel trade. After the fall of the Vantor Republic the Imperium garrisoned the moon and taxed every freighter that used its hyperrelay terminals. The Concordat returned the port to free trade in 11 AVE, and during the years of the Insurgency Korvane became one of the main refueling stops of the Free Coalition — it was here that Dax Karrick first haggled with a Concordat customs officer over the cargo manifest of the Corsair Wing.

title: Korvane
text:
In 15 AVE the orbital platform Vey Gate opened above Port Vey — the first orbital hub of the Inner Reach. Built by Calavane yards, Vey Gate handled customs and hyperrelay traffic for the whole Korrathi system, and its observation deck became the favorite view of visiting pilots.

The platform carried forty docking bays, a customs hall, a fuel depot and a lumen projector range that could render the entire Korrathi system at full scale. Vey Gate stayed Concordat property through the later wars, and only twice in recorded history did it ever close its lanes: during the siege of 19 AVE and the final blockade of the Korrathi system. In both cases the blockades broke within weeks, and the platform reopened as the region's first-call port. Maintenance of the Vey Gate hyperrelays was held, for most of its history, by the same Calavane yards that had built it.
